items.notes: One thousand one hundred and twelve subjects is among the largest samples in the review and is ample for the architecture; the problem lies in what the features contain rather than in how many there are.

The four-stage architecture, the GAMI-Net formulation, the atlas, the fused dimensionality, the baselines and the ablation design are all reported clearly. The phenotype field list, hyperparameters, imaging preprocessing and the resolution of the conflicting split and accuracy figures are not.
Two mutually inconsistent accuracy figures in the same paper, two mutually inconsistent split descriptions, a held-out subject count matching neither, and no confidence intervals on any estimate.
ABIDE-I is public and fully identified; no code is released and no preregistration exists.

No ethics statement in the retrieved text, which is conventional for secondary analysis of a public repository whose contributing sites obtained their own approvals. Funding and competing interests are not stated.

The abstract concedes that the partitioning scheme limits confidence and calls for validation under different schemes - the right instinct in kind. The target leakage, the site confound, the covariate-as-feature treatment and the internal inconsistencies are unaddressed.

Twenty autistic children from a single psychiatric hospital, required to have at least average non-verbal intelligence and the conversational competence to sustain a structured interview, 85% male, with no severity measure - so the sample is a cognitively able, verbal, predominantly male slice. The authors name sex ratio and severity range as limitations.

Community-recruited typically developing children with self-reported absence of psychiatric, motor, vision or physical disorder, and no autism screening instrument applied. No clinical comparison group, so the coordination difference cannot be shown to be autism-specific rather than a marker of atypical development generally.

Sex is matched (p = .413), but non-verbal IQ differs by 16 points at p = .015 and mean age by 15 months at p = .066, neither adjusted in the statistical or the classification analysis. Both are plausible drivers of motor coordination, and the age difference runs in the direction that would independently predict less mature coordination in the autistic group. A further uncontrolled factor is the interviewer, who supplies half the coherence signal and was presumably not blind to group.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Two of 23 comparison children were lost to technical problems before analysis, stated but not characterised. The 45 s minimum video length was applied and all 41 remaining participants met it, so no differential exclusion occurred at that stage - which is worth noting given that duration-based criteria elsewhere in this corpus have removed autistic participants preferentially.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: Multi-clinician DSM-IV consensus with escalation on disagreement is a reasonable clinical basis, but no standardised instrument, no reliability statistic, DSM-IV rather than DSM-5, no severity measure, and no screening of the comparison group.

The 57 derived features were constructed from coherences selected for statistical significance on the full sample; four classifiers were compared across two feature conditions with the maximum reported; and nesting of forward feature selection within the cross-validation is not stated.

Identical camera, sampling rate, side-view framing with both people equally placed, 80 cm seating distance, fixed camera position and stable lighting for every participant, with the same conversation protocol and appendix questions. The authors justify the validity of motion energy analysis directly from these acquisition conditions. A 45 s minimum duration criterion was applied uniformly.

Feature extraction and classification are automated and label-free once the regions of interest are drawn. But the regions of interest were drawn manually, and more importantly the interviewer - who contributes half the coherence signal - was a live participant presumably aware of each child's group, so differential elicitation cannot be excluded.
Leave-one-out cross-validation at participant level, described iteration by iteration, with one feature vector per child so within-participant leakage is structurally impossible.

The derived features underpinning the headline result were built from coherences chosen for significance on all 41 participants, so feature construction saw every held-out participant's diagnosis. Whether forward feature selection was nested inside the loop for the original-feature result is not stated.

The pseudo-pair surrogate null is an exemplary empirical chance level for the synchrony statistics - constructed by pairing children with adults who were never in the room - and is better than anything comparable in this corpus. But no chance baseline, permutation test or confidence interval accompanies any classification figure, and the entire improvement from 85.37% to 92.68% consists of three additional autistic children with specificity unchanged to the decimal.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Forty-one participants and 23 original plus 57 derived features. One participant is 2.4 accuracy points, and the authors name sample size as their first limitation.

Conversation protocol with appendix questions, seating distance, camera model and sampling rate, framing convention, region-of-interest procedure, minimum duration criterion, the principle and justification of motion energy analysis, all 23 time scales, the surrogate construction, four classifiers, the feature-selection cap, the leave-one-out scheme, the combinatorial derivation of the 57 features, and the exact composition of the three winning features are all specified. Software packages are not named.

Sensitivity and specificity are reported alongside accuracy - which is what makes visible that the whole improvement is a sensitivity gain of three children - and effect sizes and ROC curves are given. But no AUC values, no confusion matrices, and no confidence intervals on any classification figure.
No code, no data, no preregistration, and no software specification.

Declaration of Helsinki conformity, written informed consent approved by the local ethics committee and signed by caregivers, a separate declaration confirming Helsinki 2013 conformity and removal of identifying details, disclosure of the 200 CNY participant payment, and itemised funding from seven sources.

Three limitations compressed into one abstract sentence - sample size, sex ratio, severity range - with no dedicated section. Nothing about the significance-based feature construction, the classifier search, the IQ and age differences, or the discrepancy with the group's own null finding on these same recordings.

Sixty-four autistic participants with full clinical characterisation - full-scale IQ 81-91, SRS-2 85.53, Vineland-II composite 64.83, AQ 36.64 - so the sample is well described and spans a broader ability range than the high-functioning cohorts typical of this corpus. Co-occurring conditions were deliberately retained on explicit reasoning about clinical utility. The 62.5% female composition is unusual and unremarked.

Every comparison participant received the ADOS-2 and was confirmed non-spectrum against quoted cut-offs, which is stronger screening than any other study here provides. But three-quarters are college students selected for average grade point average, so the group is not a clinical comparison in the differential sense, and the 17 who came through the clinical pathway were selected precisely for having no psychiatric diagnosis.

Age differs significantly but by about a year; sex is not significantly different. The decisive uncontrolled factor is cognitive and educational level: measured at full-scale IQ 81-91 in the autistic group and not measured at all in the comparison group, where college grade point average was substituted - in a study whose outcome is grammatical complexity and variety of lexicogrammatical choice.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: All 135 participants appear in the analysis with no attrition reported, and the entire spoken output was used without length or duration criteria, so no differential exclusion by verbosity occurred. But no transcript-quality or exclusion accounting is given, and the seven-year recruitment window is not broken down by group.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: DSM-5 by neurodevelopmental specialists with ADOS-2 confirmation by a Western Psychological Services research-reliable administrator, plus SRS-2, Wechsler IQ, Vineland-II, AQ and PARS-TR; and ADOS-2 applied to the comparison group with published non-spectrum cut-offs quoted and group means reported. The only study in this review to instrument both groups with the gold standard.

Hyperparameters adopted from standard values and explicitly not searched; no feature selection; four configurations reported in full across two tasks and two annotation methods rather than the best being selected; model comparisons tested formally.

All language samples elicited by a certified ADOS-2 administrator following the Module 3 and 4 protocols, so the elicitation is as standardised as anything in this corpus. The entire spoken output was analysed without length requirements, avoiding a verbosity-based selection artefact. Annotation quality was quantified against manual annotation at F = 0.88 rather than assumed.

Classification is automated from transcripts. But manual annotation was performed by people who may have known participants' group membership, and the transcripts themselves come from sessions in which the examiner was assessing the participant for autism - so the elicitation was not blind even if the modelling was.

Participant-level leave-one-out cross-validation formally specified, with the automatic tag annotation model retrained inside each fold so that a fitted preprocessing component cannot leak information from held-out participants into their own annotations.
No feature selection occurs, and the one fitted preprocessing component - the Bi-LSTM annotator - is explicitly nested within the cross-validation loop.

Accuracy with 95% confidence intervals for all sixteen conditions, plus precision, sensitivity, specificity and AUC, and McNemar tests for pairwise model comparison with non-significance explicitly not read as equivalence. No majority-class baseline is stated, but the confidence intervals serve the same interpretive function against a 52.6% floor.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: One hundred and thirty-five participants is at the upper end for this corpus and the confidence intervals are correspondingly informative, but the authors name sample size as their principal limitation, describe the work as exploratory, and interpret their statistical comparisons with explicit reference to limited power.

Participant selection rationale, full diagnostic battery, ADOS-2 cut-offs applied to both groups, both elicitation tasks with their provenance, the annotation scheme with headings, functions and tag types, the transfer-comparison method, input construction for each model, all training hyperparameters with the statement that they were not searched, the fold-nested annotation procedure, and the full evaluation scheme are all specified. Software packages and seeds are not named.

Sixteen conditions with accuracy, 95% confidence intervals, precision, sensitivity, specificity and AUC, plus a McNemar comparison table with test statistics and p-values, and explicit power-aware interpretation of non-significant results. The most disciplined uncertainty reporting in the review after the population EHR study.

A data availability statement is provided and supplementary files carry the tag frequency comparisons, but the corpus itself is described in a prior publication rather than deposited, and no code is released.

Hirosaki University Committee on Medical Ethics approval with IRB numbers and their update history, information security guidelines followed, age-appropriate written consent including guardian consent for those under 20, and anonymisation with removal of identifiable utterances from transcripts - a privacy measure specific to spoken personal narrative. Funding itemised and competing interests declared as none.

A dedicated limitations section naming sample size repeatedly, describing the study as exploratory, identifying the weakest annotation category with concrete remedies, and interpreting non-significant statistical comparisons with reference to power. Not acknowledged: the unmeasured comparison-group IQ and the substitution of grade point average for cognitive testing, and the fact that the language samples come from the diagnostic sessions themselves.

No participants and no selection process; 1,468 photographs of unknown provenance in the autistic class, with the number of distinct children unknown and no demographic or clinical information available.
The contents of a 'non_autistic' directory, with no screening and no verification, drawn from a different source population than the autistic class.

Image provenance is confounded with the label by the dataset's construction, and the handcrafted feature set is composed of descriptors that respond directly to the imaging properties provenance determines. No analysis addresses this.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: No quality assessment of any kind - no resolution, compression, capture-condition or per-class image-property comparison.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: The label is the name of the folder an image was filed in.
Twenty model-condition combinations with the maximum reported, no hyperparameters, no prespecified operating point.
None is possible; photographs of unknown origin captured under unknown conditions, with the two classes drawn from different sources.
Feature extraction and classification are automated from image files.
No split, cross-validation or holdout is described anywhere, and the image-to-child mapping is unknown so partition integrity could not be established in any case.
Not assessable, since no evaluation partition exists relative to which preprocessing could be nested.
Twenty accuracy figures reported with no stated protocol for computing them, no confidence intervals, no confusion matrices, no AUC and no chance baseline despite a balanced design.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: 2,936 images of unknown provenance and unknown child count, with 3,315-dimensional feature vectors and no stated evaluation.

Feature extraction is narrated in step-by-step procedural detail with exact feature counts for all eight families, while the evaluation protocol - the one element that determines whether the results mean anything - is omitted entirely. No dataset identifier, hyperparameters, seed or code.

Precision, recall, F1 and accuracy for twenty combinations, but with precision, recall and F1 almost always identical to the percentage point and no confusion counts to verify them, no confidence intervals, no AUC, and no basis for interpreting what the figures estimate.
No code, no dataset identifier or version, no split specification, no preregistration.

No ethics approval, no consent, no funding declaration and no competing-interests statement, for a study built on photographs of identifiable children obtained without consent in which one class was assembled because those images appeared in autism contexts.
No limitations section and no constraint acknowledged anywhere.

No autistic participants at any point; adult volunteers producing instructed expressions, with no demographic reporting in this paper and a population decades older than the children the stated application concerns.
No autism-versus-non-autism contrast exists. A passing reference to an 'ASD-FE dataset' appears once in the results with no description, citation, size or characterisation anywhere in the methods.
Not applicable to a multi-class emotion task with no clinical groups. Four brightness variants were evaluated, which is a reasonable illumination-robustness check.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: The peak-frame selection rule for CK+ is stated explicitly and justified. No other exclusions or missingness are described, and class distributions are not reported.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: Instructed posed emotion labels from two established affective-computing corpora - sound for the task performed.

The preprocessing chain and quaternion optimiser formulation are specified, but the optimiser's own control parameters and the network's hyperparameters are not, and the number of emotion classes is stated inconsistently in three places.

Both corpora were collected under laboratory control, with KDEF geometrically standardised across all images - maximal standardisation, at the cost of representing none of the variation a deployed system would face.
Classification is fully automated with no human rater at inference.
No split, cross-validation scheme or partitioning unit is stated anywhere. CK+ supplies roughly 2.8 peak frames per individual and whether images of the same person span partitions is unknown.
Preprocessing is uniform and described; the metaheuristic optimiser is the tuning mechanism and the partition on which its fitness was evaluated is not stated.

Accuracy 99.8% with 100% recall and 94% specificity across six classes, reported without confusion matrices, class-wise results, a definition of multi-class specificity, confidence intervals, a chance baseline or the number of runs behind the means.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: CK+ supplies 327 peak frames from 118 individuals; KDEF's size is not stated, so the total training and evaluation volume cannot be determined.

Corpora, peak-frame rule, preprocessing chain and quaternion algebra are reported; no validation scheme, split, class distribution, optimiser configuration, network hyperparameters or run count is given.

Four point estimates and significance tests against three baselines, with no confusion matrices, class-wise breakdowns, intervals, chance baseline, or statement of the units over which the t-tests were computed.
Both corpora are established public resources; no availability statement, no code, no preregistration.
No statements given; secondary analysis of two consented public corpora conventionally requires none, but funding and competing interests are also absent.

No limitations section. The paper identifies in its introduction that staged emotions are easier to detect than spontaneous ones and that the field lacks spontaneous-stimulus work, without connecting either observation to its own design.

Ten autistic children from a single rehabilitation centre, with comorbidity excluded by criterion and functioning inferred from tablet use rather than measured. The group is said to span a range of severity but no score is given, so representativeness cannot be assessed. Twenty participants in total is the smallest sample among included studies.

Ten mainstream schoolchildren selected only on parent and teacher report of no neurodevelopmental disorder, recruited explicitly without assessment of pre-existing abilities, with no screening instrument and no clinical comparison group.

No developmental or cognitive measure for either group in a fine-motor study of 3-6 year olds; an autistic age standard deviation nearly ten times the comparison group's; the autistic children receiving psychomotor therapy at the recruiting centre while the comparison children were not; and table height adjusted by age, introducing a postural difference correlated with a variable whose spread differs between groups.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Three explicit and well-reasoned inclusion rules: recording begins only when the target image is dragged, incomplete drags are excluded, and only trajectories of 20-69 points are retained so that lengths are comparable. Generated trajectories under 20 points are also excluded in the simulation. No attrition is reported among the 20 children.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: ADOS-2-confirmed clinical diagnosis administered by professionals explicitly independent of the research team - a strength - but with no score reported and with comparison-group status resting on unstructured parent and teacher report.

Two prespecified feature sets compared directly, no feature selection, and preprocessing fixed a priori and specified in full. The unreported architecture is a reporting gap rather than a prespecification failure.

Identical game settings for every participant, one tablet model at a fixed 60-degree tilt, a fixed experimenter position, a single 20 Hz logging rate, and a task designed to minimise verbal and social demand so that motor behaviour is elicited without social confound. The one deviation is table height adjusted by child age.
Coordinates are logged automatically by the game software and modelling is fully automated; no human rating enters the pipeline, and the examiner gave no instructions that could differ by group.

Four-fold cross-validation over 738 trajectories from 20 children, with the validation set quoted in samples and no indication that folds respected child boundaries. Each validation trajectory has roughly 36 siblings from the same child, session and hand in training, and after rotation normalisation those siblings differ only in execution noise. No participant-level result is reported.
No feature selection occurs and the rotation normalisation is a deterministic geometric transform applied uniformly, so no fitted preprocessing component exists to leak.

Accuracy is reported as a fold-wise distribution rather than a point estimate, and ROC curves are given for both models - better than a bare number. But no sensitivity, specificity, precision, confusion matrix, AUC value, confidence interval or chance baseline appears anywhere.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Twenty children, the smallest sample among included studies, with the 738-trajectory count giving an appearance of data volume that 20 independent units do not support. The authors name sample size as their first limitation.

Exceptional on task, apparatus and preprocessing - exact recruitment dates, task geometry, tablet model and tilt, seating arrangement, sampling rate, all inclusion rules, the rotation normalisation in three numbered equations, the simulation range and the seven simplification rates. Silent on model architecture, training hyperparameters, seeds and whether folds were constructed by child.

Fold-wise accuracy distributions and ROC curves, plus correlations with p-values for the simulation analysis. But no class-conditional metrics, no AUC value, no confidence intervals and no participant-level figure.

The trajectory data are published in a public GitHub repository at a stated URL - the only open data release among included studies in this review, and one that makes the central claim independently checkable. No code or preregistration.

Approval by the Ethical Committee of Psychological Research of the Department of Humanities at the University of Naples Federico II, written parental informed consent, two named funders with an explicit no-role statement covering design, collection, analysis, publication decision and manuscript preparation, and a declaration of no competing interests.

Four limitations named with concrete remedies - sample size, single-device tracking, absence of longitudinal observation, and absence of complementary measures with a specific proposal to add ocular movement data. Not acknowledged: the trajectory-level partitioning, the absence of developmental assessment in either group, the differing age spread, or the psychomotor-therapy confound.
No sample size, demographics, recruitment route, eligibility criteria or setting reported. The only participant-level data shown are eleven variables for five illustrative individuals.
Undescribed. Individuals labelled 'Not detected' for a merged autism-and-SPD construct, with no screening, characterisation or count.

No covariate is known and none is controlled. The displayed data show the label tracking body temperature and heart rate abnormality, with no elicitation condition reported that would explain why those variables should differ by diagnosis.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: No data-quality, missingness or attrition information of any kind.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: None described, and the target merges two distinct conditions into one binary label so that a positive prediction would not identify which condition it refers to.
Label-dependent feature selection with no stated nesting; the selected subset never disclosed; nine model configurations compared with the proposed one reported best.
No task, stimulus, elicitation condition or equipment reported, so state-dependent variables such as emotion probability, heart rate and temperature have no interpretable measurement context.
Classification is presumably automated, but the derivation of the emotion probabilities is not described, so whether any human judgement entered the feature values cannot be determined.
Two inconsistent validation accounts, neither linked to the reported figures, with no stated unit of splitting and no participant count from which one could be inferred.
The fitness function uses inter- and intra-class similarity and therefore class labels, with no statement that selection was confined to training partitions.

Ten metrics reported to five decimal places with no denominator, no class distribution, no confusion matrix, no confidence interval and no chance baseline. Three different headline figures appear across abstract, conclusion and results table.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Not assessable - no sample size is reported anywhere in the paper.

The optimisation algorithm, network architecture and all ten metrics are specified mathematically and could be reimplemented; the data, participants, task, equipment and labelling are entirely absent. The paper specifies how to compute a result and not what it was computed on.
Five-decimal-place precision without a denominator, three mutually inconsistent headline figures, and no confusion matrix, confidence interval or class distribution.
No data, no code, no preregistration, and no statement on availability of any of these.

No ethics approval, ethics committee, consent statement, funding declaration or competing-interests statement, for a study reporting manual collection of heart rate, body temperature and facial data from human subjects.
No limitations section and no constraint acknowledged anywhere.

Self-selected screening-app users with positive rates far above population prevalence, no clinical ascertainment, and no reported demographic distribution despite age, gender and ethnicity being present as fields.
The comparison group is respondents whose summed item score fell below the cut-off - defined by the same arithmetic that defines the positive class.

Age is handled structurally by fitting a separate model per band, which is appropriate given that Q-CHAT-10 and AQ-10 are age-calibrated. No other covariate is examined, and registration metadata are entered as predictors without analysis.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Missing-value handling and categorical encoding are described, two fields were dropped on relevance grounds, and instance counts are reported completely for all four datasets.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: No clinical diagnosis for any respondent; the label is the summed item score thresholded at the instrument's cut-off, and therefore a function of the model's own inputs.

Preprocessing, feature retention and both architectures are specified, and the optimiser is chosen with a stated rationale. Search ranges and the partition on which the optimisation objective was evaluated are not reported.

Q-CHAT-10 and AQ-10 are standardised instruments administered through screening applications, so item collection is uniform - but the respondent differs between bands and the 'who completed the test' field is retained as a predictor.
Classification is fully automated from tabular data.
Participant-level splitting with tabulated partition sizes - sound in itself, and immaterial because the target is computable from the predictors on any partition.
Two features dropped a priori on relevance grounds rather than by data-driven selection, which is appropriate. The optimiser's evaluation partition is unstated.

Six metrics all reaching exactly 100% in four separate datasets - the signature of a degenerate task rather than converging evidence. Class distributions are reported so majority-class baselines are computable at 69%, 52%, 61% and 73%, but none is stated or compared against, and no confidence intervals are given.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Sample sizes range from 104 to 1,054 instances with 17 features, which would be adequate for the architecture on a genuine task; the adolescent test partition holds 21 instances.

Datasets, repositories, class distributions, split proportions with absolute sizes, feature counts, preprocessing chain, both architectures, the optimisation method with its justification, and all six metrics for both model versions across all four bands.

Six point estimates of exactly 100% per dataset, with no confidence intervals, no majority-class comparison despite the distributions being reported, and no consideration of what simultaneous perfection on six metrics indicates.
All four datasets are public and identified; the deployed web tool is illustrated; no code is released.
No ethics, consent, funding or competing-interest statement appears - the last being notable for a study whose output is a deployed public-facing diagnostic tool.
No limitations section. Critical attention is directed at prior work's sample sizes, narrow focus and hyperparameter practice; nothing is said about the present study's own constraints.

Approximately 99% of one municipality's five-year-old population, assessed in situ during routine examinations. Coverage is near-complete and self-selection is minimal; the sample represents the full trait distribution of that cohort rather than a recruited slice.

The comparison group is the remainder of the same population cohort below the SRS-2 cut-off - a within-population contrast rather than a recruited control group, which is the correct design for a screening question and is unique in this review alongside the population health-records study.

Age is controlled by design, every participant being five years old, which removes the confound that troubles every other motor study here; sex ratio does not differ and the SRS-2 cut-off is sex-specific. But no cognitive, developmental or motor-maturation measure was obtained, so at an age when postural control is still developing a general developmental explanation cannot be separated from an autistic-trait-specific one.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: No attrition is reported and all 126 participants appear in the analysis. But no signal-quality criterion is described for either the pressure or the pose stream, and no handling of OpenPose failure is reported - relevant because the study's discriminative features depend entirely on the estimated joint angles.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: A maternal-report SRS-2 total dichotomised at a published cut-off, with no clinical assessment, diagnostic instrument, second informant or reliability estimate for any participant. The authors acknowledge this and recommend integrating clinical evaluation.

Feature selection and hyperparameter optimisation performed jointly, reducing sixteen variables to three to five per model, with nesting relative to the cross-validation loop unstated; three variable sets compared on the same participants; no prespecified operating point.

One pressure sensor, one webcam model and resolution, a fixed 20 Hz synchronised acquisition, a documented physical configuration, and a standard clinical balance test administered identically to every child within a single routine examination programme. The task requires no verbal or social demand, so a motor measurement is obtained without social confound.
Feature extraction and classification are automated from sensor and pose data; the SRS-2 was completed by mothers independently of the balance testing and before it entered any analysis.

Leave-one-out cross-validation over participants, each contributing a single feature vector, so within-participant leakage is impossible. But the joint feature-selection and hyperparameter-optimisation step is described without reference to the folds, leaving the most consequential leakage question unresolved.

Three to five of sixteen variables plus a cost parameter selected per model by a procedure whose nesting within the cross-validation is nowhere stated. On 126 participants with 19 positives this alone would be sufficient to produce the reported perfect scores.

Accuracy, sensitivity and specificity all exactly 1.000 for two of three configurations, reported without a majority-class baseline against an 84.9% floor, without confidence intervals on a sensitivity estimated from 19 positives, and without comment on the implausibility of perfect separation in a behavioural measurement. Sensitivity and specificity are at least reported separately, which is essential at this prevalence.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Nineteen above-threshold participants for a model selecting three to five features from sixteen. The authors identify this directly, noting that with 'only around 20 above-threshold samples and highly imbalanced sample overall' they were constrained in their choice of validation scheme.

Population and sampling basis, inclusion criterion, instrument and cut-offs with their source, sensor and camera specifications, synchronised sampling rate, pose-estimation method with joints figured, all sixteen variables named and categorised, the three variable sets, the SVM kernel and cost parameter and the selected variables for each best model, the validation scheme and the statistical software with version. Supplementary materials give per-variable rationale and calculation. The nesting of feature selection is the one substantive omission.

Accuracy, sensitivity and specificity per variable set with the selected variables named; SHAP across all participants; and correlation of predicted probability with continuous SRS-2. But no confidence intervals, AUC, confusion matrix, chance baseline or positive predictive value - the last being directly computable and directly relevant given the population-based design.
Contributions stated to be included in the article and supplementary material, with further inquiries directed to the corresponding author. No code, no dataset deposit, no preregistration.

Nagasaki University Ethics Committee approval with number 22051204, Declaration of Helsinki conformity, and written informed consent from both the children and their guardians after a comprehensive explanation. Four funding sources itemised and competing interests declared as none.

Four limitations named, including the screening rather than diagnostic nature of the target with a recommendation to integrate clinical assessment, the small above-threshold sample, the single algorithm family, and the need for external validation - and, unusually, an explicit statement that the chosen validation scheme 'can produce optimistic performance estimates due to the small test set in each iteration' with a call for cautious interpretation. The nesting question is not addressed.

Images harvested from the internet by third parties. The number of distinct children is unknown; the paper's table labels 2,866 images as 'Total individuals'. No ascertainment process, no spectrum description, no clinical setting.

Controls are images from non-autism-related internet sources and frames from unrelated kindergarten videos. The comparison group differs from the index group in how it reached the internet, and possibly in nothing about the children themselves.

No demographic variable is available for either class, and the sex distribution is explicitly recorded as unspecified. Age, sex, ancestry and image-acquisition conditions are all free to differ systematically between classes and none can be tested.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Split sizes are reported precisely for both corpora, but the number of MTCNN face-detection failures is not given, no image-quality exclusion criteria are stated, and 28 test images were reassigned to training by a similarity rule.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: None exists. No diagnostic instrument, clinician judgement or medical record for any image; the label is image provenance. The paper nonetheless describes the positive class as diagnosed individuals.
Hyperparameters selected by a metaheuristic search over six ranges whose evaluation partition is unstated; no prespecified operating threshold; four model configurations compared on the same data.

Uncontrolled consumer photographs and video frames with unknown and class-correlated acquisition conditions. Preprocessing standardises geometry and pixel range but cannot standardise camera, lighting, pose, expression or compression.
Classification is fully automated from image data with no human rater involved at inference.

The best treatment of this issue in the facial-photograph branch: leakage was measured rather than assumed, found at 0.9714 maximum similarity, and addressed by perceptual-cluster splitting with a documented sweep and threshold. But perceptual similarity is a proxy for identity rather than a measurement of it, the reassignment step edits the test set using the model's own feature space, and none of it touches the provenance confound that determines what the labels mean.

The white shark search over learning rate, layer widths, batch size, depth and kernel size does not state which partition its fitness was computed on. Fitness is described as evaluated 'across folds' although no cross-validation scheme is defined elsewhere.

Confidence intervals of plus or minus 0.4 percentage points are reported on test sets as small as 68 images, where one image is worth 1.47 points and an exact binomial interval around 95% spans roughly 87% to 99%. No chance or trivial baseline; no positive predictive value at any realistic prevalence despite an assembled 1:1 ratio.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: A deep attention architecture with metaheuristic hyperparameter search trained on 951 images and evaluated on 68 in the video corpus. Image counts also overstate the effective sample, since the number of distinct children is unknown in both datasets.

Dataset URLs, preprocessing, exact split sizes, the leakage algorithm in pseudocode with thresholds and cluster sweep, the full training regime, hyperparameter bounds, hardware and software environment, and the metric definitions are all reported. The computational description is among the most complete in the corpus; what is missing is entirely on the human side.

A broad metric suite with curves and significance tests, and an internally consistent headline triple - but intervals narrower than a single test image, no chance baseline, no prevalence-adjusted predictive value, and no statement of how many runs underlie the reported means.
Both datasets public with URLs given; code on GitHub and archived on Zenodo with a DOI and a version tag. Among the strongest availability records in this review.

No ethics statement, no institutional approval and no consent statement anywhere in the paper, for a study trained on identifiable photographs and video frames of children scraped from personal websites, Facebook pages and YouTube. Funding, competing interests, author contributions and generative-AI use are all declared, so the omission is specific to human-subjects considerations.

Computational cost is named, the absence of clinical validation of the Grad-CAM heatmaps is stated in the authors' own voice with a concrete remedy, and the ablation admits that the paper's own multiscale contribution underperforms without the hyperparameter search. But the provenance confound, the absent reference standard, the missing demographics and the implausible intervals are all unmentioned, and the conclusion tells clinicians that the highlighted facial traits 'indicate the condition'.
Thirteen autistic boys with no ascertainment described, no severity characterisation, no cognitive or medication information, and an all-male sample.
Four typically developing children - the smallest comparison group in the review, and too small to characterise typical variation in any EEG measure or to support the reported specificity.

No age distribution by group across a 9-to-16 window in which EEG spectral characteristics change substantially; no medication record, although antiepileptics and antipsychotics alter EEG directly and are more common in autistic samples. Sex is fully controlled by the sample being all-male.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Recording at rest is described as minimising artefact, but no artefact rejection, epoch exclusion or channel interpolation procedure is reported, and the number of analysed segments is never given.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: No instrument, criteria, clinician or date for the autistic group, and no screening procedure for the comparison group.
Four architectures are specified with layer sizes and explicit activation equations, but the eleven features are not individually identified and no hyperparameters or training details are given.

A single acquisition chain applied identically to both groups, with montage, ground, reference, filter settings and sampling rate all specified - the most completely reported acquisition in the review.
Feature extraction and classification are fully automated from stored recordings.

No split, cross-validation scheme or partitioning unit is stated anywhere. With 17 participants the reported accuracies must be epoch-level, and with four controls a participant-disjoint arrangement is barely constructible.
Eleven features are extracted from stated domain families with no selection step described; whether extraction parameters were fitted on all data is not reported.

Five metrics reported for four architectures with no confidence intervals, no confusion matrices and no baseline - although the 13:4 participant ratio places a trivial all-autistic classifier at 76.5%.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Four neural architectures fitted on data from 17 children, four of them controls. The paper's own comparison table shows most of the branch operating at comparable scale.

The acquisition chain, group sizes and age ranges, feature domain families and all four architectures with layer equations are reported. No validation scheme, segment count, feature identity, hyperparameters or diagnostic procedure is given.

Accuracy, precision, recall, specificity and F1 for every architecture - including specificity, which is appropriate at this class ratio and more than several studies here provide. No intervals, confusion matrices or baseline.
The corpus is identified with its access URL and the provider is acknowledged by name; no code is released.

'For this type of study, statement of human rights is not required' and 'informed consent is not required', stated without qualification and without reference to the originating approvals, for EEG recordings of identifiable children obtained from another institution. Competing interests declared as none.
No limitations section. The conclusion states that the work 'underscores the efficacy of neural network in detecting Autism, advancing diagnostic tools'.

Twenty-three clinically diagnosed children scoring below CARS-2 30 were excluded, restricting the autistic group to at least moderate severity. The authors state that this may have produced selection bias toward more pronounced characteristics and that model performance may consequently be overestimated - the clearest self-identification of spectrum truncation in this review.

Kindergarten-recruited typically developing children, deliberately matched on age and sex with both tests reported - considerably better than the convenience controls typical of this corpus. But no non-autistic clinical comparison group exists, which the authors identify as the harder and more clinically relevant contrast, and the recruitment route differs systematically by group.

Age and sex matched and tested; comorbidity, neurological disease and psychotropic medication excluded by criterion. But no cognitive or language measure was obtained, although the strongest predictor is duration of socially directed speech, and age is matched at the mean without being adjusted for in a 1-to-6-year sample where four of five predictors are play-quantity measures and the group age variances differ (SD 9.9 against 13.5).

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: All 246 included children completed the task and contributed complete indicator vectors; the 23 exclusions are stated with their reason and occurred before analysis. No missing data or lost recordings are reported.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: DSM-5 best-estimate clinical diagnosis by senior child and adolescent psychiatrists, corroborated by CARS-2 with published psychometrics cited. Genuine clinical ascertainment, among the strongest in the review.

The task, toy set and coding scheme were fully prespecified and directional hypotheses stated in advance, including the confirmed prediction that repetitive behaviours would not differ. But the five model predictors were selected from 81 candidates post hoc and the operating cut-off chosen from the ROC curve.

Verbatim instruction reproduced in the paper including the examiner's constrained response rule, a fixed toy set with defined categories, a standard rapport-building preamble, and a 90-second duration applied identically to every child.

Diagnosis was established before and independently of the play task, but coder blinding to group is not stated - and with autistic children recruited from clinical services and controls from a kindergarten, group membership may be inferable from the recordings. This matters more here than in automated studies, since all 81 indicators pass through human judgement.

The unit of analysis is the child throughout with one vector each, so no within-participant leakage is possible. But there is no held-out set, no cross-validation and no external cohort - the model is fitted and evaluated on the same 246 children.

Five predictors selected from 81 candidates by group-difference testing, univariate regression and stepwise regression on the full sample, with performance reported on that same sample. A bootstrap was run but no optimism-corrected AUC is reported, and the stepwise criterion is unstated.

AUC with a confidence interval, sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, calibration curve and goodness-of-fit test - the fullest reporting in the behavioural branch. But the cut-off was chosen from the same ROC curve, and predictive values are quoted at the matched 50% prevalence with no recalculation for a screening base rate, which is the figure the paper's own screening proposal depends on.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: One hundred and twenty-three events for five final predictors is comfortable, but 81 candidates entered the selection process, which is where the optimism arises. The authors describe the sample as small for prediction-model development and call for more data.

Recruitment sources and window, full eligibility criteria, diagnostic procedure and threshold with the count excluded by it, matched demographics with tests, verbatim task instruction, toy categories, the coder training programme with experience range, duration and the inter-coder reliability check and its formula, all 19 behaviour definitions in a supplementary guide, and all 81 indicator definitions. Missing: coding and statistical software, stepwise criterion, bootstrap resample count.

AUC with interval, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, calibration curve, Hosmer-Lemeshow, density plots, and odds ratios with confidence intervals and p-values for every indicator at both stages. The gap is the absent optimism-corrected estimate rather than the presentation.

Anonymised data from the corresponding author on request, restricted by data protection and the consent text; the full coding guide is supplied as supplementary material, which is the more useful disclosure for replication. No code, no software named, no preregistration - though directional hypotheses were stated in the introduction.

Institutional ethics approval, Declaration of Helsinki conformity, and written informed consent from primary caregivers before the study. No funding received. Competing interests declared at the level of individual authors, with six of eleven declaring two patent applications arising from this research; four authors are affiliated with a commercial autism-services company, which is visible in the affiliations but not itself discussed.

Five limitations enumerated, including task brevity, sex imbalance, the CARS-2 severity restriction with its explicit consequence that performance may be overestimated, small sample for model development, and the absence of a non-autistic clinical comparison group. Selection optimism from choosing five predictors out of 81 is the notable omission.

Consecutive clinical recruitment from one hospital's services for both groups, but restricted to full-scale IQ above 85 and to verbally fluent adults suitable for ADOS-2 Module 4, with comorbidity excluded from both groups and severe positive symptoms from the schizophrenia group. The diagnostically ambiguous and comorbid cases the model targets are exactly those excluded.

The comparison group is another clinical population recruited from the same service and matched on age, sex and education - the design this review has repeatedly identified as missing across the corpus, and the only instance of it among included studies.

Age, sex and education matched and tested; the schizophrenia group extensively characterised on symptom severity, medication and illness course. But intelligence was measured with different instruments in each group - a reading-based premorbid estimate against a directly administered full-scale IQ - and the authors state that the groups therefore cannot be compared on it, which matters because several discriminating items concern conversational structure and content.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: All 90 participants completed both the diagnostic process and the ADOS-2, with no attrition, indeterminate results or missing item codes reported.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: Consensus DSM-5 diagnosis by several psychiatrists with extensive experience in both conditions, drawing on clinical interaction and full history, with ADOS-2 and ADI-R explicitly excluded from the process - deliberate independence from the index test, and the strongest reference-standard arrangement in the review for a study of this kind.

Both published algorithms were applied at their published cut-offs with no modification, which fully prespecifies the study's principal analysis. The six-item model, by contrast, was selected post hoc from 32 candidates on the full sample.

ADOS-2 Module 4 administered by research-certified psychiatrists following a published protocol of 15 prescribed activities over 40 to 60 minutes with published coding criteria for all 32 items - the most standardised behavioural measurement in the review.

Administrator blinding to the established diagnosis is nowhere stated, and both groups were recruited from the same service with diagnosis preceding assessment, so blinding is unlikely. Every index-test input is a clinician's ordinal judgement, and no within-study inter-rater reliability was computed at item level.
The unit is the participant throughout, each contributing one set of item codes, and the holdout split partitions participants. No form of within-participant leakage is possible.

Six items selected from 32 candidates on the full sample, with the apparent accuracy and AUC computed from that same sample and whether selection was repeated inside the training split unstated. The authors identify the resulting overfitting explicitly.

Both training and test accuracies reported (85.4% and 65.3%); AUC interpretive bands prespecified; DeLong's test for the paired ROC comparison; odds ratios with confidence intervals throughout; and the baseline is the instrument's own published algorithms on the same participants rather than a nominal chance line. The abstract nonetheless presents the apparent AUC of 0.938 without the held-out figure attached.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Six binary predictors selected from 32 candidates in a sample of 90. The authors state this directly: 'The model had six variables, which was a large number compared to the number of samples; hence, the AUC may have increased due to overfitting.' Sample size was justified against a comparable prior study rather than by power calculation.

Site, separate recruitment windows, full eligibility criteria for both groups, the diagnostic procedure with the explicit exclusion of ADOS-2 and ADI-R, the complete battery per group, the module with activity count and duration and both algorithms' cut-offs, the item dichotomisation rule with a worked psychometric justification, significance thresholds including a stricter alpha for correlations, and the statistical software with version. Missing: blinding, item-level reliability, and the holdout split proportions.

Sensitivity, specificity and explicit false-positive rates for both algorithms; AUCs against prespecified bands with DeLong's test; odds ratios with confidence intervals for every domain and item; non-zero proportions for all 32 items with tests; and both holdout accuracies. The one presentational fault is that the abstract carries the apparent AUC without the held-out figure.

Contributions stated to be in the article and supplementary material with further inquiries to the corresponding author. No code, no data deposit, no preregistration - though a sample size justification by reference to a prior comparable study is provided.

Medical Ethics Committee approval at Showa University School of Medicine, Declaration of Helsinki conformity, and written informed consent from the adult participants themselves rather than through proxies. No financial support of any kind and no competing interests declared.

Four limitations stated, including the incomparability of the two intelligence instruments and - the notable one - an explicit account of the holdout accuracy drop with overfitting named as the cause and external validation stated as the requirement. Blinding and item-level reliability are the omissions.

Convenience corpora collected for other purposes, one with no control group at all. Ages 4-18 with no distribution reported, no cognitive or language measure, and participant counts that cannot be reconciled between sections.

The four-class task includes dysphasia and PDD-NOS as non-autistic clinical comparison groups - a design almost absent from this review and its principal merit. But the binary comparison group was recorded in schools while the clinical groups were recorded in clinics, so the contrast confounds diagnosis with recording setting.

No age data by group in a corpus spanning 6-18 years, across which voice changes fundamentally; no language measure although one class is a language disorder; no control or normalisation for recording environment, which differs systematically by class. Sex is the one confounder taken seriously, through fairness testing, and the models fail that test substantially.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Complete partition tables are given for every class and every evaluation set. But no per-class participant counts, no account of excluded or unusable recordings, and no sample-duration statistics.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: Diagnoses inherited from source corpora with no procedure, instrument or criteria described, using pre-DSM-5 categories. The typically developing group is defined by absence of reported difficulties rather than by assessment.

Two architectures compared on identical folds with a separate development partition and a prespecified primary metric. Hyperparameters and the number of runs are not reported, and no uncertainty estimate accompanies any figure.

No recording equipment, sampling rate, acoustic condition or preprocessing chain reported for either corpus, and the two binary classes were recorded in different physical settings with no normalisation or channel compensation applied. No task or elicitation is described.
Classification is fully automated from audio; no human rater is involved at inference.

Speaker-disjoint splitting with the rationale stated explicitly, and a separate development partition - among the best-articulated splitting practice in the review. But the number of speakers per class is unknown, and speaker disjointness cannot address the class-level recording-setting confound.

Representations are learned; minority-class upsampling is applied to training only, with development and test distributions deliberately left unchanged 'to be representative of real-world' - a correct and explicitly reasoned choice that very few papers in this corpus make.

Unweighted average recall as primary metric, full metric suite across all partitions, confusion matrices, subgroup sensitivity and specificity, and benchmarking against a stated baseline and prior work on the same corpus - including a table showing the study's own four-class result below both. No confidence intervals or run-to-run variance.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Deep transformer models fine-tuned on 62 minutes of labelled audio, with the four-class test partition containing 26 samples per clinical class from an unstated and possibly very small number of children. The authors acknowledge that the test sets are small and 'not fully representative of the real-world'.

Complete partition tables, split proportions, splitting rule with rationale, both architectures with their pre-training corpora, the resampling policy, the metric, and the fairness procedure with formulae. Missing: code, hyperparameters, sample durations, recording conditions, per-class participant counts, age distributions, and any diagnostic procedure.

Every model reported on every partition with four metrics plus confusion matrices, and benchmarked against baseline and prior work - including where the study loses. But no confidence intervals, no variance across runs, and no significance testing, on margins as small as 0.7 points and test sets as small as 26 samples per class.
Neither corpus is openly available and no code is released. Contributions are stated to be in the article and supplementary material with inquiries to the corresponding author.

Approval attributed to the dataset administrations rather than a named research ethics committee, and consent stated as not required for participants or guardians - in a study of recorded child speech, and in a paper whose own introduction reflects at length on ethics committees as safeguards for exactly this kind of data. No funding and no competing interests declared.

Six limitations stated in detail, including the abandonment of the study's original younger-age aim, domain shift between corpora, class and gender imbalance with the fairness consequence spelled out, small test sets, and an explicit caution that the headline UAR must be interpreted against the corpus's specific characteristics. The clinic-versus-school recording confound is the significant omission.

A self-selected online advocacy community, English-only, on a platform skewed toward younger and higher-socioeconomic users, with no demographic information and no clinical ascertainment. The authors state the representativeness problem in these terms themselves.

A daily sample of general English-language Twitter, differing from the positive class in topic, community membership, posting motivation and sampling procedure as well as in putative autism status. The authors address only one contamination direction, bounding it at population prevalence.

No age, sex, ancestry or socioeconomic data for either group, and the #ActuallyAutistic community plausibly differs from a general platform sample on all of these. The one confound actively controlled is label-defining vocabulary, removed deliberately.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Corpus counts reported completely by group; the location field excluded with the reason given; a minimum-tweet threshold applied for the profile task and stated. Preprocessing is fully specified.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: Hashtag use plus profile keywords with no clinical validation, and an entirely unscreened control group. Stated as the first limitation and reflected accurately in the paper's own conclusion.

The preprocessing chain, keyword-removal list, representations, model families, splitting rules and selection procedure are all specified in advance and reported in full. Algorithm selection used cross-validation with a separately held test partition.

Text is naturally occurring so there is no elicitation to standardise, and preprocessing is applied uniformly. But the two classes' material was gathered by different sampling procedures, and heavy normalisation removes paralinguistic features that may carry signal.
Classification is fully automated from text; no human rater is involved at any stage of labelling or inference.

User-level splitting for both tasks with the rationale articulated - among the clearest statements of the principle in this review - plus separate validation and test partitions and a minimum-tweet threshold for the aggregated task.

The sixteen autism-related tokens that define the label were removed a priori on substantive grounds, closing the target-leakage route that would otherwise have made the task trivial. Algorithm selection used 5-fold cross-validation with the test partition held out.

Accuracy, AUC and F1 reported for both tasks on near-balanced classes, with no inflation in how they are described. But no confidence intervals despite a corpus that would support tight ones, no calibration, and no positive predictive value at population prevalence - the figure that would demonstrate why the authors' own restriction to cross-sectional use is correct.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: 6.5 million tweets from 188,596 users, far exceeding what the model families require. Sample size is the one dimension on which this study exceeds every other in the review.

Scraping tool, both search queries with date range, group-definition criteria, control sampling rate, the full preprocessing chain, the complete keyword-removal list, sentiment tool, representations, model families, splitting rules and proportions for both tasks, and all corpus counts. The pipeline is reconstructible even though the corpus deliberately is not.

Accuracy, AUC and F1 for both classifiers, reported consistently across abstract, results and conclusion with no inflation. Missing: confidence intervals, calibration, operating-point sensitivity and specificity, and predictive value at realistic prevalence.

Dataset and models deliberately destroyed after analysis and never shared outside the author team, for stated ethical reasons; code not mentioned. Unavailability is a considered decision rather than an omission, and is explained.

IRB approval 2023-00248 under expedited review, a separate data-governance determination, and measures taken beyond regulatory requirement including encrypted user IDs and anonymised mentions and email addresses. Consent is treated as the primary limitation rather than as satisfied by the public-data exemption, engaged with substantively through the literature, and acted upon by destroying the data and models. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text.

Five limitations with developed reasoning, a self-imposed restriction of legitimate use to population level, explicit enumeration of misuse scenarios, and a closing caution against building comparable models without consent and participatory design. The group-definition confound is the substantive omission.

Consecutive enrolment in an established longitudinal autism cohort over eleven years, ages 1.1-5.1 with no severity threshold applied, and a comparison group actively screened for neurological and psychiatric conditions and for first-degree family history.

Typically developing children matched on age and sex and assessed with the same ADOS protocol in the same setting - a better-matched comparison than any other included study on recording context. But no non-autistic clinical comparison group, so the harder discrimination is untested.

Sex matched exactly at 48 male and 32 female per group; age matched; the train-test split additionally matched on age, sex and ADOS module. Cognitive and language data are deferred to supplementary material rather than reported, and no sex-stratified analysis is run despite the sample uniquely supporting one.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: All 160 children contributed recordings and appear in the analysis; segment counts and total durations are reported for both partitions and both modalities. No losses reported. The 90% video-segment confidence filter is a post-hoc output selection whose effect on aggregate accuracy is not quantified.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: DSM-5 clinical criteria supported by gold-standard assessment in a clinical research cohort - substantively strong. But instruments are deferred to supplementary material, and independence from the ADOS recordings used as model input is not established.

Both architectures, segment lengths, aggregation rules and the three ensemble strategies are fully specified, with all tuning decisions confined to the training half's validation split. The decision tree's 60% threshold is reported explicitly.

Identical ADOS protocol and setting for both groups, audio normalised across microphones to a common format, video normalised to fixed-resolution skeletal renderings. Equipment varied across an eleven-year window but not by group.
Classification is fully automated from pose and audio with no human rater at inference; the interpretability analysis uses independently coded ADOS items.

Participant-level 50-50 split with each half matched on age, sex and ADOS module; segments nested strictly within participants so no within-participant leakage is possible despite tens of thousands of clips; validation carved from the training half only.

Segment lengths, MFCC count, batch size and epoch count all selected on the training half's validation partition, with the direction of observed overfitting reported. Test participants untouched throughout.

Complete six-metric table for all five model variants on a balanced test set, so chance is 50% and both operating extremes are reported. But no confidence intervals on 80 children, no positive predictive value at realistic prevalence in a paper framed around screening, and the abstract transposes precision with recall and specificity with sensitivity.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: Deep networks trained on 80 children and evaluated on 80. Segment counts are large but the effective sample is the participant count, and the ensemble's advantage over video alone corresponds to two test children.

Cohort, window, demographics, matching variables for groups and split, segment lengths with their empirical basis, audio normalisation and rationale, all acoustic features, complete architectures with layer sizes, dropout, optimiser, batch size and epochs, aggregation and filtering rules, all three ensemble strategies, and the full interpretability procedure with three importance metrics and a cross-modality normalisation model.

Six metrics for all five models in one table, including negative predictive value, and every ensemble variant presented rather than only the best. But no confidence intervals anywhere, and two transposition errors in the abstract that the results table does not share.

Training code for both networks on GitHub; a de-identified pose-estimation subsample on Zenodo with a DOI; raw recordings withheld with a correct and specific reason. A considered middle position that the study's own skeletal representation made possible.

University of Geneva Faculty of Medicine ethics approval, written parental consent for all children, and separate specific consent from the depicted child, their guardian and the examiner for publication of identifying images - a level of consent detail no other included study reports. Six funding sources itemised with grant numbers and a no-role statement; no competing interests.

The ensemble's failure to beat the individual modalities is named directly, and two more consequential interpretive cautions are volunteered in the discussion - that ambient non-vocal sound may have driven the audio classification, and that the examiner's prosody adapts to child severity so the model may be reading the adult. The reference-standard circularity, the absent confidence intervals and the absent predictive values are not addressed.
Children whose families chose to film and publish their stereotypies - a self-selected group biased toward visible presentation, with no demographic or clinical characterisation of any kind.

The non-autistic class is never described: no size, no source, no individual count. The data-distribution table lists SSBD as the sole database for all splits, contradicting the existence of a second class.

No age, sex or ancestry information for either class in a study that classifies faces, where apparent age and sex-linked morphology are known strong drivers and autism's four-to-one diagnostic sex ratio makes imbalance likely.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Two of 75 videos excluded for quality with the reason stated, and frames retained only where the face is observable - reported clearly, though the retention criterion could select differently across classes and total image counts are never given.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: Autism inferred from parental upload behaviour with an explicit statement of trust in the uploaders; no clinical assessment for any child. The non-autistic label has no stated basis.

Architectures and hyperparameters fully specified, with negative tuning results reported honestly and a separate validation partition maintained. But the input class composition is undefined and no operating threshold is prespecified.

Home videos on heterogeneous devices in uncontrolled conditions, with the authors themselves citing poor image and video quality. No normalisation applied, and the comparison images' acquisition conditions are entirely unknown.
Classification is automated from image data. The affect annotations were produced by five raters trained on a protocol under supervision, with inter-annotator agreement reported.

Subject-disjoint splitting implemented with the rationale stated and partitions reported by child and duration - materially better than the frame-level branch. But the guarantee covers only the SSBD half, and no splitting scheme can address a confound between image corpora.
Representations are learned; a separate validation partition is maintained; hyperparameters were taken from the original architecture paper with alternatives tried and reported as offering no gain.

No specificity, confusion matrix or confidence interval for the classification, and the chance baseline is undeterminable because class balance is described as balanced in one section and 'very imbalanced' in another. The 5-fold figure is a best-of-folds validation accuracy rather than a mean held-out estimate.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: A transformer classifier trained on 44 children and tested on 14, with the image counts never stated. The authors list dataset scarcity and small size as their first limitation.

Datasets, exclusions, annotation protocol, split proportions with per-child counts and durations, full architectures and hyperparameters, and metric definitions are all reported. The composition and source of the non-autistic class - the single fact needed to interpret the result - is not.

Accuracy, F1 and recall across three evaluation configurations, plus MSE and CCC for regression with a well-argued case for reporting both and a demonstrated instance of the two metrics ranking models oppositely. No intervals, no specificity, no confusion matrices.
'The authors do not have permission to share data.' The new arousal and valence annotations presented as a dataset contribution are therefore unavailable, and no code is released.

No ethics statement, no institutional approval and no consent statement anywhere, for work that crops faces from identifiable children's home videos and has five raters annotate their emotional states frame by frame. Funding and competing interests are declared.

Genuinely searching about the annotation layer - non-expert raters, reaction-time contamination of averaged labels, and no handling of disagreement, all volunteered - and the introduction cites a failed-replication warning about machine learning for autism diagnosis. Silent on the undocumented comparison class, the contradictory class balance, and the ethics of the source data.
Thirty male children at one residential special school, a setting selecting for higher support needs, with no age distribution or severity-group composition reported and no girls at all.
No comparison group exists; all analyses are between severity levels within an autistic sample whose class sizes are never stated.

No control for ambient temperature, exertion or capture setting in a study whose primary feature is skin temperature; no recording of current medication, which alters thermoregulation and correlates with severity by construction; no age-by-severity breakdown across a 5-to-15 range spanning major developmental change.

items.item_text: Handling of missing data and attrition
items.notes: Image counts are reported by capture setting with the number of students in each, but no exclusions, detection failures or unusable frames are described, and the 20 collected videos are never accounted for.

domain_2_data_collection_quality.domain_name: Behavioral Data Collection, Predictors and Reference Standard (PROBAST: predictors, outcome)

items.notes: No diagnostic ascertainment described, and the severity labels being predicted have no stated origin. The ABC is discussed as background but never reported as administered to these children.

The denoising pipeline and mood network are fully specified with hyperparameters and ablations; the three severity classifiers carrying the headline result have no reported hyperparameters or tuning procedure.

Emissivity is set and reported, which is good practice, but images span outdoor and indoor environments with no ambient compensation, no distance or angle control, and no environmental logging - so absolute skin-temperature readings are not comparable across settings.
Classification is automated, but the facial-mood ground truth for these thermal images must have been assigned by human raters whose identity, training and blinding are nowhere described.

An 80-20 image-level split over 1,500 images from 30 children with roughly 50 images each and no participant-level partitioning described. Severity is a fixed per-child attribute, so identifying the child recovers the label.

Mood-network dropout and batch normalisation were selected on validation accuracy and reported transparently with numeric tables. No feature selection or tuning procedure is described for the severity classifiers.

Class distribution across the three severity levels is never reported, so neither chance nor a majority-class baseline is determinable. No confidence intervals, no confusion matrices, no per-class breakdown and no specificity, and the ROC description conflates specificity with the false positive rate.

items.item_text: Sample size adequacy for the modelling
items.notes: A three-class severity model with an effective sample of 30 children, inflated fiftyfold by treating each image as an independent observation.

Collection site, camera and emissivity, image counts by setting, denoising pipeline, full network architecture and hyperparameters, two ablations and all metric formulae are reported.
