answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: The most thorough reference standard in the review alongside the joint-attention study, and the only one that applies a gold-standard instrument to both groups. Autism diagnosis followed DSM-5 criteria applied by experienced clinicians specialising in neurodevelopmental disorders, with ADOS-2 as the primary confirming instrument administered by someone holding research reliability certified through Western Psychological Services, and supported by a full battery: SRS-2, age-appropriate Wechsler IQ testing, Vineland-II, AQ and PARS-TR caregiver interview. What distinguishes it further is the comparison group. Every non-autistic participant received the ADOS-2 and was confirmed non-spectrum against the published cut-offs, which are quoted (6 or below on Module 3; combined communication and social interaction of 7 or below on Module 4), with group means reported separately for the clinically assessed and the recruited subgroups. Almost every other study in this corpus establishes comparison status by absence of a diagnosis or by parent report; this one administers the same instrument to both sides. The inclusion of co-occurring conditions in the autistic cohort is also a deliberate and well-argued choice rather than an oversight. Two qualifications remain: the diagnosing clinicians were not blind to anything and no inter-rater reliability is reported beyond the administrator's certification, and the language samples analysed come from the same ADOS-2 sessions that generated the labels.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Absent. The labels are the names of two subdirectories in a downloaded folder, and the methods section describes exactly this: features are extracted 'by traversing through the directory structure', with 'a label column added to denote the class label (autistic or non_autistic)'. No diagnosis, instrument, criterion, clinician or verification underlies either class. The quantity the models predict is therefore which folder an image was filed in, and given that the folders were populated from different parts of the internet, the reported accuracies are best read as measures of how distinguishable the two source collections are as image sets.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: None is required by the task as executed, since no autism classification is attempted - the labels are posed emotion categories, which are a strong ground truth for emotion recognition and carry no information about autism. The consequence for this review is that the study cannot contribute evidence on any of the diagnostic questions. Its relevance is instead to the review's treatment of how autism framing attaches to work containing no autism data: a reader relying on the title, abstract, keywords and conclusion would record this as an autism study, and it is not one.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: Solid for the autistic group and absent for the comparison group. Autism required a clinical diagnosis confirmed with the ADOS-2, and the paper states something few in this review do: the diagnoses were made 'by healthcare professionals and industry experts who were independent of our research laboratory and study'. Explicit independence between the diagnosing clinicians and the research team removes one route by which knowledge of the study could influence the reference standard, and is worth crediting. Against this, no ADOS-2 score of any kind is reported, so the severity range the autistic group is said to span cannot be characterised; comorbidity was excluded by criterion, narrowing the sample relative to the clinical population; and typically developing status rests entirely on parent and teacher report of no neurodevelopmental disorder, with no screening instrument administered and no assessment of abilities - so undetected autistic traits or developmental difficulty in the comparison group cannot be ruled out.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: None. The label is a binary 'Detected' or 'Not detected' for a combined 'autism and visual SPD' construct, with no diagnostic instrument, criterion, clinician, assessment or source described. Two features of the labelling deserve specific note. First, the target conflates two distinct conditions - autism and visual sensory processing disorder - into a single undifferentiated binary, so even if the label were valid it would not identify which condition a positive prediction refers to, and the paper nowhere addresses how a model trained on a merged label could support either diagnosis. Second, the dataset section asserts that 'a new dataset named AQ10 is developed based on autism screening performed in individuals and holds 20 features', which conflates a dataset with the AQ-10, an existing published autism screening questionnaire, and in any case none of the AQ-10 items appears among the eleven variables the paper actually shows. The quantity being predicted is therefore undefined.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None, and its absence is structural rather than incidental. The class variable in the UCI and Kaggle autism screening datasets is not a clinical diagnosis: it is computed by summing the A1 to A10 item responses and applying the instrument's published cut-off, so it is a screening outcome derived arithmetically from the same fields supplied to the model. The paper describes the scoring rule itself - 'each question is scored as either 0 or 1 based on the individual's response. Only responses that indicate autistic traits are given a score of 1' - without drawing the consequence. Two facts follow. No respondent in any of the four datasets is known to have undergone diagnostic assessment, so nothing here is validated against autism as clinically established. And because the label is a deterministic function of the modelled inputs, the classification task has no uncertainty in it: 100% on accuracy, precision, recall, F1, Matthews correlation coefficient and AUC across all four age bands simultaneously is the expected output of the arrangement, obtainable by a single summation and comparison, and no optimisation, architecture or validation scheme bears on it. This is the second study in the review resting on these datasets, and the pattern is identical in both.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: There is none in the diagnostic sense, and the study is explicit about this. Group membership rests entirely on maternal completion of the SRS-2 and application of published sex-specific screening cut-offs; no child received a clinical assessment, ADOS, ADI-R or diagnostic evaluation of any kind. The authors state the consequence directly, recommending that the method form 'part of a comprehensive assessment process that includes clinical evaluation and other standardized measures' and that 'integrating more robust diagnostic tools for ASD, such as clinical assessments or standardized behavioral tests, alongside the SRS-2, would improve the reliability of the screening process'. This places the study in a different category from the diagnostic studies charted elsewhere in this review: what is predicted is whether a mother's questionnaire responses about her child exceed a threshold, which is a legitimate screening target but not autism. Three specific consequences follow. Single-informant report carries known biases and no second informant or reliability statistic is available. A dichotomy imposed on a continuous scale creates borderline cases whose classification is arbitrary, which matters for a model reporting perfect separation. And the 19 above-threshold children are a screening-positive group of whom, at a population SRS-2 cut-off, a substantial proportion would not receive an autism diagnosis on assessment.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: There is none. No child in either corpus is known to the authors to have received a diagnostic assessment. In the Piosenka dataset the positive label means an image was found on a website or Facebook page with autism-related content; in the YTUIA dataset it means a video was collected into a corpus of self-stimulatory behaviour, half from YouTube and half from therapists and professional organisations. Neither carries a clinician judgement, a diagnostic instrument, a medical record or any documented ascertainment. The paper cites no reference standard, does not identify the absence as a limitation, and describes the positive class throughout as 'individuals diagnosed with ASD' - a description the data cannot support. The YTUIA positives at least depict a behaviour that is associated with autism, which places them a step above pure provenance labelling; but the modelling target is the face crop rather than the behaviour, so even that association does not transfer to what the model is trained on. This is the same reference-standard failure recorded for the other Piosenka-based papers in this review, and it bounds every figure the paper reports.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: None described. The 13 autistic participants are stated to be 'diagnosed with ASD' with no instrument, criteria, clinician qualification, setting or date, and no screening procedure is reported for the 4 comparison children. The labels derive from the originating corpus and this paper transmits none of its documentation. The consequence is the same as for several studies in this review: the quantity the models predict is a label of unknown provenance, and no reported figure can be located relative to any clinical standard.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: Among the stronger reference standards in this review. Diagnosis was made by senior child and adolescent psychiatrists as a best-estimate clinical judgement against DSM-5 criteria, corroborated by CARS-2 with the instrument's psychometric properties cited from the literature (internal consistency 0.93, meta-analytic alpha 0.90, sensitivity 88%, specificity 86%). The corroboration is real clinical assessment rather than a questionnaire threshold standing in for one, and it is applied by clinicians qualified to make it. Two qualifications matter. First, the CARS-2 floor of 30 was applied as an exclusion: 23 children with a clinical diagnosis but a score below 30 were removed from the study. This converts the reference standard from 'clinically diagnosed autism' into 'clinically diagnosed autism of at least moderate severity', truncating exactly the part of the spectrum on which a screening tool would be hardest and most useful. The authors state the consequence directly - selection bias toward more pronounced characteristics, with the model's performance therefore possibly overestimated - which is the correct inference and one that few papers here draw about their own inclusion rules. Second, whether the video coders knew each child's group is not stated, and because the autistic children were recruited from hospitals and intervention centres while controls came from a kindergarten, group membership may have been inferable from the recordings independently of any behaviour coded.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: The strongest reference standard in the review for the specific question at hand, and its strength lies in what was deliberately left out of it. Diagnoses in both groups were made under DSM-5 by consensus among several psychiatrists with extensive experience in both conditions, drawing on interactions during diagnostic assessment and on prior psychiatric and medical histories. The paper then states the crucial fact: 'ASD diagnosis was a good clinical estimate, as neither the ADOS-2 nor the Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R) was employed in the assessment process.' Because ADOS-2 items are the index test, any contribution of ADOS-2 to the diagnosis would have made the analysis circular - the model would be predicting a label partly derived from its own inputs, which is the failure this review has documented in the questionnaire-item studies where the class label is an arithmetic function of the modelled features. Here the separation is explicit and deliberate, and it is what makes the headline negative finding meaningful: when the ADOS-2 algorithm labels 45% to 52% of schizophrenia patients as autistic, that is a genuine disagreement with an independent clinical judgement rather than an artefact of shared information. Two qualifications. Best-estimate consensus diagnosis is the accepted standard in adult psychiatry but has no external criterion, so disagreement between algorithm and clinicians is evidence about the algorithm only if the clinicians are taken as correct. And whether the ADOS-2 administrators were blind to the established diagnosis is not stated, which matters more here than in an automated study because every item code is a clinician's judgement.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Absent as an independent element and inherited without description. De-Enigma children are stated to be 'diagnosed with ASD' and CPSD children to carry diagnoses of autism, dysphasia or PDD-NOS, but neither corpus's diagnostic process is described - no instrument, no criteria, no clinician qualification, no date. The typically developing group is characterised only by absence: 'no prior history of difficulties with learning, speech, hearing or general learning', which is a screening statement rather than an assessment. Two features compound this. The CPSD categories are pre-DSM-5, since PDD-NOS was eliminated as a diagnosis in 2013, so the labels encode a superseded nosology whose boundaries with autism were themselves contested - and the four-class task therefore asks a model to reproduce a distinction that the diagnostic system has since abandoned. And the atypical and typical children were recorded in different physical settings, clinic and school respectively, so the label is confounded with the circumstance of recording independently of whatever the diagnoses mean. The paper does not treat the reference standard as a topic at all.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: None, and the paper's handling of this is the most precise in the review. The positive label is use of #ActuallyAutistic plus autism-related keywords in the profile description - self-identification within an online community. The authors do not claim otherwise at any point: their own conclusion states that the models predict 'use of the #ActuallyAutistic hashtag, an imperfect proxy for self-reported autism', and their first limitation is that 'while we focused on individuals who self-identified as autistic, there is no clinical validation for their diagnosis'. They then reason about contamination in both directions. Users of the hashtag might be parents, caregivers or advocacy organisations rather than autistic people, which they judge rare 'due to the negative social connotations of using #ActuallyAutistic without a diagnosis' - an appeal to community norms rather than evidence, but an informed one, since the hashtag's function within the autism rights movement is precisely to mark first-person testimony. And autistic users who do not self-identify will contaminate the control group, which they bound at roughly the population prevalence, arguing that 'with autism having a prevalence rate of <3%, the model performance should not degrade by more than 3%' - a bound that assumes population prevalence transfers to Twitter's user base and that non-self-identifying autistic users write like non-autistic ones, neither of which is established. What the paper does not consider is that its label might be a design choice rather than a defect: undiagnosed self-identifying autistic adults are precisely the population an access-oriented screening tool would most want to reach, and treating their self-identification as noise assumes that clinical ascertainment is the only valid criterion in a study whose framing elsewhere questions exactly that assumption.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: Strong in substance and incompletely reported in one respect that matters. Autistic children met DSM-5 clinical criteria with the diagnosis 'further supported by employing gold standard diagnostic assessments', within an established longitudinal cohort staffed by a clinical psychiatry department - so this is genuine clinical ascertainment, not a questionnaire threshold or a dataset label, and it stands among the better reference standards in this review. The comparison group was actively screened rather than merely assumed typical: absence of known neurological or psychiatric conditions, and no first-degree relative with autism, which excludes the elevated-likelihood siblings who would otherwise blur the contrast. The unresolved issue is independence. The model's input is the ADOS recording, and 'gold standard diagnostic assessments' in a paediatric autism cohort ordinarily means ADOS, so the same session that supplied the model's training data may have contributed to the diagnostic label it is trained to predict. That is a circularity of the same family as the questionnaire studies excluded from this review, though far milder in degree - the model sees raw pose and audio rather than the clinician's coded items, so it must rediscover from signal what the clinician judged, rather than reproducing an arithmetic function of its inputs. Still, it means the label is not independent of the material, and the fix would be one sentence: another study in this review states explicitly that neither ADOS nor ADI-R entered its diagnostic process, which is exactly the statement needed here and is absent. The main text also defers the specific instruments to supplementary material, so a reader cannot check.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: None, and the paper's account of why is the most candid statement of provenance-based labelling in this review. SSBD videos were 'posted by parents/caregivers on YouTube', collected and annotated for stimming behaviour, and the authors reason: 'Therefore, and in the way the dataset is described, the data only concerns ASD children ... We are also confident in the reliability of the parents who uploaded these videos, and we, therefore, consider that the youngsters presented as the main subject of these videos are all autistic.' The autism label thus rests on two inferences - that a family posting a video of their child stimming implies a diagnosis, and that families are reliable reporters of that diagnosis - and on an explicitly stated act of trust. No clinical assessment, diagnostic instrument, medical record or clinician judgement exists for any child in the corpus. The comparison class is worse still: no basis whatever is offered for the non-autistic label, because the class itself is never described. Two structural consequences follow. Because the positive class comprises children whose families filmed and published their stereotypies, it is drawn from the visibly and severely affected end of the phenotype rather than from any representative spectrum. And because the paper elsewhere lists 'existing datasets are not necessarily trustworthy' as a limitation while simultaneously declaring confidence in these particular uploads, the two statements sit uneasily together.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: There is none for diagnosis and none stated for severity, and the second gap is the more damaging. All 30 children are described as autistic on the basis of attending a special school; no diagnostic instrument, clinician judgement or record is cited for any of them. The classification target is severity level 1, 2 or 3, and the origin of those labels is nowhere given - not in the dataset description, not in the methodology, not in the results. The Aberrant Behavior Checklist is discussed at length in the introduction as the 58-item instrument clinicians use to grade severity and guide dosage, and it is the obvious candidate, but the paper never states that it was administered to these children, by whom, when, or with what training. Two consequences follow. First, what the classifiers predict is simply unknown, so the 98.33% cannot be interpreted even setting aside the splitting problem. Second, the paper's central comparative claim becomes incoherent: it reports that the machine learning methods 'outperform the clinical ABC method' in classifying severity levels and presents a table comparing their accuracies. If the ABC supplied the labels, a model can at best reproduce it and cannot exceed it, and any apparent excess is measurement of the model's agreement with its own training signal; if some independent criterion existed against which both were scored, the paper does not say what it was. A claim to beat the clinical standard, in a paper proposing to adjust medication, requires the standard to be specified, and it is not.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: None. The autism label means an image was placed in the autistic subfolder of a Kaggle collection; the non-autistic label means an image was returned by a web search. No child in either class is known to have been assessed, no diagnostic instrument or clinician judgement is cited, and the paper does not identify the absence as a limitation - it reports the folder structure factually and moves on. This is the sixth study in the review resting on this corpus, and the position is unchanged: whatever separation the models achieve, it is a separation between two collections of internet images, and the paper supplies the description that makes this plain.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: Inherited from the source corpora and not transmitted. Children are designated autistic or typically developing by the original Eigsti and Nadig investigators, but this paper reports no diagnostic instrument, criteria, clinician qualification or assessment date. The labels are nonetheless in a different class from those in the web-scraped branches of this review: ASDBank and CHILDES are established research archives whose contributing studies performed documented clinical ascertainment, so the underlying labels are real diagnoses rather than folder membership or hashtag use. The specific weaknesses are that the paper does not tell the reader what those diagnoses rested on, and that the typically developing designation for the Warren and Kuczaj children means only that those corpora were collected from typically developing populations, without any screening described in this paper.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Inherited and undescribed for both corpora - no diagnostic instrument, criteria, clinician qualification or assessment date appears anywhere. The Gait Fullbody Dataset carries binary autistic and typically developing labels from its creators; DREAM carries a three-level label - non-spectrum, ASD and AUT - of which the non-spectrum class was discarded, following the prior study whose architecture this work extends. Discarding the non-spectrum group has a consequence the paper does not draw: the DREAM experiment is then a discrimination between two autism-related categories rather than between autism and non-autism, so its 70.19% is not comparable to the Gait dataset's autism-versus-typical task and the two figures cannot be read as measurements of the same thing. The reference-standard issue that most affects validity, however, is procedural rather than definitional. The methods state that in the Gait dataset each child performed ten walking trials and 'the most optimal trial was selected based on the disease and the doctor's recommendation'. Selecting which of a child's trials enters the dataset on the basis of that child's diagnosis is selection on the outcome: it means the 100 modelled samples are not a random sample of each child's walking but the trial a clinician judged most suitable given what the child was known to have. Whatever separation the models achieve is conditioned on that choice, and no splitting scheme downstream can undo it.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Among the stronger ascertainment procedures in this review and described with unusual completeness for a secondary analysis. The process ran in four stages: the Gilliam Autism Rating Scale, Second Edition completed by parents; a caregiver interview conducted against DSM-5 criteria; direct evaluation and observation of the child by two child clinical psychologists holding doctorates; and separate confirmation of the diagnosis by at least one child psychiatrist in a different setting. Independent confirmation by a second clinician working in a different setting is a real safeguard against single-assessor error and appears in almost no other study charted here. The authors also state plainly why ADOS was not administered - 'the official version of Autism Diagnostic Observational Schedule (ADOS) is not available for Farsi' - and repeat it in their limitations rather than leaving the omission unexplained. Two qualifications remain. The GARS-2 is a parental questionnaire, and its position at the front of the process means the pathway begins with parental report; and the typically developing group's status is not described as having been screened by any instrument.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: None. The 'Class/ASD' variable in this dataset is not a clinical diagnosis but a screening outcome, computed by summing the A1-A10 item responses and applying the AQ-10 cut-off. No respondent underwent diagnostic assessment, and no instrument, clinician or record is cited. The distinctive feature of this particular study is that the derivation is visible in its own methods: the paper prints the complete field list - 'A1 Score, A2 Score, A3 Score, A4 Score, A5 Score, A6 Score, A7 Score, A8 Score, A9 Score, A10 Score, age, gender, ethnicity, jundice, austim, contry of res, used app before, result, age desc, relation, Class/ASD' - which contains both the ten items, their sum ('result'), and the thresholded outcome ('Class/ASD'). The model is therefore asked to predict a variable that is a deterministic function of another variable it is given.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: None described. The 50 children are stated to be 'diagnosed with ASD' and nothing further is given - no instrument, no criteria, no clinician, no setting, no date - and no screening procedure is reported for the 50 comparison children. For a prospective study that designed its own acquisition protocol, recruited 100 families and recorded over 16 hours of video, this is a striking omission, and it contrasts sharply with the care taken over the technical description: the paper specifies the MediaPipe landmark counts, the composition of the 1,639-value feature vector, the dropout rate, the L2 coefficient and the early-stopping patience, while saying nothing at all about how autism was established in the children whose data those numbers describe. The consequence is that the label the model predicts is undefined, and the study's reported 85-90% cannot be located relative to any clinical standard.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: None for autism and none for gelotophobia, with the second absence being the more remarkable. The autism label reflects folder membership in a public image collection assembled partly from autism-related websites; no diagnostic instrument, clinician judgement or medical record is cited for any image, and the paper does not identify this as a limitation. For gelotophobia the position is stronger still: the ethics section states that the GELOPH<15> questionnaire 'was not directly administered to participants in this study; it was used solely as a reference from previously validated research' and that 'no direct contact with human participants occurred'. This directly contradicts the abstract, which says that in ambiguous cases 'the GELOPH<15> questionnaire, consisting of 15 items, was administered to confirm the diagnosis'. Taking the ethics statement as authoritative - as its specificity and its consistency with the study's design require - no person in this study was ever assessed for gelotophobia, so the system's gelotophobia outputs were never compared with anything. The conclusion nonetheless states that the study 'demonstrates the effectiveness of combining deep learning techniques with validated diagnostic tools for detecting gelotophobia'. This is the clearest instance in the review of a headline claim resting on no measurement whatever, and it is distinct in kind from the label-quality problems recorded elsewhere: those studies have bad ground truth, this component has none.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: None. The autism label reflects folder membership in a public collection whose positive class was harvested from autism-associated online content; no child is known to have received a diagnostic assessment, no instrument or clinician judgement is cited, and the paper does not identify the absence as a limitation. This is the eighth study in the review on this corpus family and the position is unchanged across all of them: whatever the models separate, they separate two collections of internet images.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: None. The autism labels reflect folder membership in a public collection whose positive class was assembled from autism-associated online content; no child is known to have received a diagnostic assessment, and no instrument, clinician judgement or record is cited anywhere. The paper describes the corpus as 'large, well-labelled public data promoting reproducibility', which conflates consistent labelling with valid labelling - the labels are consistent in that every image in the autistic folder carries the same tag, and they are not diagnoses. This is the ninth study in the review resting on this corpus family and the position is unchanged. The emotion labels are category assignments from the source corpus and are adequate for what they measure, though nothing establishes that they were assigned by raters familiar with autistic facial expression, which is the very phenomenon the paper says general-population models miss.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: None described for either source. For the Kaggle portion the labels are folder membership in a collection whose autistic class was harvested from autism-associated online content - the position documented across nine other studies in this review. For the Semarang autism-centre portion, children attending a clinical service would ordinarily carry clinical diagnoses, and this is the one point at which the study could have improved on its predecessors; but no instrument, criteria, clinician, assessment date or procedure is reported, and the paper's provenance sentence explicitly leaves the sources open, saying the data 'could come from a variety of places, such as clinics, past research, or relevant public statistics'. The opportunity to anchor part of the corpus in real diagnoses is therefore present and unrealised.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Not confirmed by this study. Labels are inherited wholesale from the figshare dataset. The presence of a CARS_Score field implies that the original collectors administered the Childhood Autism Rating Scale, but this paper reports no cut-off, no administrator qualification, no ADOS or ADI-R, no DSM or ICD criterion, and no statement of who made the diagnoses or when. The TD group's status as non-autistic is likewise asserted rather than evidenced - no screening instrument is named.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Not confirmed for any participant. This is the defining feature of the study: there is no clinical diagnosis anywhere in the pipeline. The label Class/ASD Traits is generated by the Q-CHAT-10 scoring function applied to the same ten items that supply the features. What is modelled is therefore a scoring rule, not a condition. The one screening instrument used is a caregiver checklist completed variously by parents, caregivers, medical staff or clinicians - and the field recording which of those it was was deleted during preprocessing as irrelevant, discarding the only available indicator of measurement heterogeneity.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: No diagnostic confirmation of any kind. The class labels are Kaggle folder names on images gathered from the open web. No clinical assessment, no instrument, no assessor, no date, and no record of who the children are. The paper does not mention this once, and instead treats the labels as ground truth adequate to support claims about automated ASD screening.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Well handled and honestly reported. Diagnoses were made by experienced physicians applying DSM-5 criteria together with CARS scores, and the paper states plainly why gold-standard instruments were not used: ADI-R and ADOS evaluations are not widely available in India. That candour about a real infrastructural constraint compares favourably with the many studies in this corpus that simply assert diagnosis or inherit labels from a download. What undermines it is the severity banding rather than the diagnosis: eligibility required CARS >=30, yet Table 3 assigns ten children to a Low class defined as CARS <=20 and ten more to a Mild class spanning 20 to 40, and a High class defined as CARS >60 when the scale's maximum is 60. The four equal groups cannot have been generated by the stated rule, and the actual CARS distribution is never shown.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: None. Labels are Kaggle folder names on photographs of unknown origin. No clinical assessment, instrument, criterion, assessor, date or provenance record exists for a single image, and the paper does not acknowledge the issue at any point - including in its ethics statement, which cites the dataset's public availability as the reason no ethical review was required.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Not described. Labels come as a binary field in the downloaded dataset (1 autistic, 0 non-autistic). No diagnostic instrument, criterion, assessor, setting or date is reported for either group, and the source dataset's own procedures are not summarised. The comparison group's non-autistic status is likewise asserted with no screening evidence.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: None. Group membership is determined by school: the autism group is the set of children attending a Special Elementary School, the comparison group the set attending a State Elementary School. No diagnostic instrument, criterion, assessor, date or record is reported for a single child, and the typically developing children were not screened with any instrument. The study's exclusion of intellectual disability, cerebral palsy and Down syndrome implies some clinical information was available, but its source is never described. School placement is a proxy for diagnosis that also carries administrative, geographic and socioeconomic structure into the label.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: None. The outcome is Class/ASD_Traits, the Q-CHAT-10 screening result, and no clinical diagnosis exists for any case. The paper describes this as 735 cases diagnosed with ASD, which overstates what the dataset contains: the ASD label here records that a caregiver's ten checklist answers summed above a cut-off, not that a clinician assessed the child. No assessor, criterion, instrument beyond Q-CHAT-10 or date is reported.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: None, and the paper states the label rule plainly enough that this is not in doubt: a 1 is scored for each Q-CHAT-10 item answered Always, Usually or Sometimes, and a total above 3 indicates the presence of potential ASD traits. That threshold is the outcome variable. No clinician, diagnostic instrument, criterion or assessment date exists for any record in either dataset, and the online questionnaire origin of the Saudi data means the respondents were not verified either.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: None. The outcome is the Class/ASD traits field, the Q-CHAT-10 screening result, applied to app-submitted responses with no clinical assessment, no clinician, no instrument beyond the checklist and no verification of who completed it. The paper's title and abstract are accurate about this - it predicts autism traits, not autism - and that accuracy distinguishes it from several neighbours in the corpus that describe the same label as a diagnosis.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: Self-reported but with real safeguards, and honestly characterised. Participants were asked about a clinically based diagnosis and about which professional made it; the 12 who reported self-diagnosis were excluded; and respondents were instructed to report only clinician-confirmed diagnoses and not diagnoses based on personal feelings of distress. The authors then name the residual uncertainty as a limitation and recommend clinician-based confirmation in future work. No diagnostic instrument was administered by the research team. Importantly, diagnosis is not the prediction target here - it is a covariate tested for incremental value - so the study's central claims do not rest on label accuracy in the way the rest of this corpus does.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: None. Labels are the folder assignment of a public image corpus. No clinical diagnosis, instrument, criterion, assessor or date exists for a single image, and unlike several of its neighbours the paper does not even describe the labelling process in passing. The comparison table's premise - that the models being compared share a common foundation because they use the same dataset - makes this the shared and unexamined weakness of the whole benchmark line.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: None. Labels are Kaggle folder names on photographs of unknown provenance. No clinical diagnosis, instrument, criterion, assessor or date exists for a single image. The paper opens by observing correctly that there is no medical screening or test like a blood test or scan for ASD and that diagnosis requires developmental history and behavioural assessment - and then treats folder labels on downloaded photographs as sufficient ground truth for a diagnostic classifier.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: None. The dependent variable is ASD_traits, a binary yes/no field in a Kaggle spreadsheet. No clinical assessment, diagnostic instrument administration, criterion, assessor or date exists for any case, and the originating collection procedure is not described at all. The paper nonetheless frames the task as ASD diagnosis throughout, titles itself Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics, and opens by criticising clinician-administered instruments for introducing variability and potential bias - a criticism made in favour of a label whose provenance is entirely unknown.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Clinically ascertained and honestly qualified. Diagnosis of ASD or DLD was made by a licensed, experienced team of clinicians following DSM-5 and international diagnostic manual guidelines, independently of this study and as a precondition of enrolment at an early intervention centre. Typically developing children are defined by the absence of such enrolment. The authors then add two caveats that few in this corpus offer: that their diagnostic tools could have been supplemented with further assessments but were the only ones available at the time, and that diagnoses at early ages are provisional and may evolve over time, so the findings should be interpreted with caution.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: None. Labels are inherited from a public image collection with no diagnostic instrument, criterion, assessor or date reported, and the originating study's diagnostic procedure is not summarised. The paper's opening argument is that conventional ASD assessment relies on subjective criteria and lacks objectivity - a criticism advanced in favour of a label whose ascertainment it never examines.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: None, and the paper states the substitute rule explicitly: if the Q-CHAT-10 score is higher than 3 then the class value is allocated as YES which implies ASD traits potential; if not, NO is allocated. The outcome is therefore a threshold on the sum of the ten checklist items that also constitute the feature set - the seventh instance of this structure in the review, after local_8253c2ec, local_a0d73248, local_8ff20c48, local_ed30e24c, local_b9de0d7f and local_14df790d. No clinician, instrument administration or diagnostic criterion enters at any point.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Clinically ascertained with documentation, and honestly bounded. Participants had to supply evidence of a formal clinical diagnosis such as a clinician's letter, or be drawn from databases where that evidence had been verified. The limitations section then names the two residual problems precisely: absence of a diagnosis does not exclude undiagnosed cases, and the PD and control participants belong to a generation in which autism diagnoses were not prevalent, so undiagnosed autistic people may sit in the comparison groups. That second observation is a genuine insight about ascertainment in older cohorts that appears nowhere else in this corpus.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: None, and the paper is explicit rather than silent about this. The abstract states that reliable severity stratification remains challenging due to the absence of explicit clinician-annotated severity labels; the methods then construct severity labels from the A1-A10 items themselves; and the scope paragraph states that because the severity labels are deterministically derived from the same behavioural attributes used as model inputs, the subsequent prediction task constitutes a structured function-approximation setting. The one external anchor is the weight calibration, in which domain weights were optimised to maximise agreement with independent expert assessments on a randomly sampled subset, achieving Cohen's kappa 0.72 (95% CI 0.69-0.76) - and the paper immediately qualifies this as supporting the internal consistency of the labeling heuristic while not implying external diagnostic validity. Neither the number of expert-labelled records, the identity or qualification of the experts, nor the instrument they used is reported.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: None. No diagnostic instrument administration, criterion, assessor or record is described for any dataset. The named sources - ASQ, CSBS, PEDS, M-CHAT and STAT - are developmental screening instruments, not diagnoses, and the paper does not describe how any label was assigned. One results passage categorises outcomes as yes (Y), random (R) - indicating a 50% probability of yes and a 50% probability of no - and not detected (N), which introduces a coin-flip category into what is presented as a diagnostic output.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: None, and not required by the task as executed - but required by the task as described. The videos are annotated for when a behaviour occurs, not for whether the child has a diagnosis; no clinical assessment, instrument or assessor exists for anyone in the dataset. The paper's title nonetheless places the work in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder and its abstract states that the approach facilitates quick, accurate and effective screening of ASD. Those claims do not follow from a four-way discrimination among arm flapping, head banging, spinning and other movement in videos of children who are all autistic.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Independent and clinician-made: diagnostic classification was conducted externally by qualified specialists (neuropaediatricians or clinical psychologists) prior to inclusion in the corpus, with the SCQ administered separately as a symptomatology measure. The label therefore predates and is unrelated to the gaze data - the property that separates this study from the checklist-threshold and folder-label branches of this review.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: None for either dataset. Dataset 1's target is a binary ASD-traits field with no diagnostic procedure described, and the dataset's own feature list includes the Autism Spectrum Quotient, Social Responsiveness Scale, Q-CHAT score and Childhood Autism Rating Scale - four instruments used to determine autism status, supplied as predictors of it. This is the same instrument-inclusion leakage documented in local_183eaef4, which used the same 1,985-record dataset and reached accuracy 1.0000. Dataset 2's four severity categories are asserted with no instrument named; clinical experts are said to have verified annotation consistency at Cohen's kappa 0.92, but what they were rating and against what standard is not stated.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Self-reported formal diagnosis by a registered clinician, with participants drawn from a national research register (NAR) rather than a convenience sample, and non-autistic participants reporting no autism diagnosis. Diagnosis therefore predates and is independent of the task data. The population is explicitly characterised as late-diagnosed, which the paper treats as a strength for the research question - it is precisely the group that existing screening instruments miss - rather than glossing over it.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: Not described. Labels are inherited from the public dataset with no diagnostic instrument, criterion, assessor or date reported, and the originating collection's ascertainment procedure is not summarised. This is the study's largest unforced omission, since two of its authors are clinicians - one at a psychiatric hospital and one at a clinical medicine school - and a paragraph characterising the source cohort would have been straightforward.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: None. Labels are annotations attached to a Roboflow dataset. No clinical diagnosis, instrument, criterion, assessor or date exists for a single image, and the originating collection is not described. The paper's introduction gives an accurate account of how ASD is actually diagnosed - paediatricians or psychologists using developmental history, behavioural observation and instruments including CARS for severity - and then treats platform annotations on downloaded photographs as an adequate substitute.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: None. Labels are the folder assignments of a public image corpus, with no clinical diagnosis, instrument, criterion, assessor or date for any image, and no description of how the collection was assembled. The introduction gives a conventional account of ASD as requiring thorough clinical testing and then treats folder labels as sufficient ground truth for a system offered as a diagnostic aid in clinical settings.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Inherited from the original collection and not independently established. The three-level grouping (typical, moderate, severe) is used as the classification target and the instrument behind the moderate/severe distinction is not named in the extracted text. What the paper does establish clearly is the provenance chain: ethics approval was obtained by the original collectors from their institutional review board before collection, guardian consent was given, and this study is a secondary analysis of de-identified public data.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Inherited from two peer-reviewed developmental-language studies, whose own diagnostic procedures are cited but not summarised. Governance is handled by reference to TalkBank's contribution requirements, which oblige contributing researchers to obtain informed consent from participants or guardians and the necessary ethical approvals before sharing. That is a reasonable basis for secondary analysis of a curated academic repository and is stated rather than assumed - a different situation from the web-scraped and platform-hosted collections elsewhere in this review.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: Clinical diagnosis is an inclusion criterion - children with a diagnosis form the ASD group and children without form the control group - but the diagnosing procedure, instrument and assessor are not described. The framing is honest about why this matters in context: the study's motivating problem is that a significant number of children with ASD in Brazilian early and primary education remain without an appropriate clinical diagnosis, which leaves educators without information to tailor teaching. The tool is proposed for exactly those undiagnosed children, and is trained on children whose diagnostic status is already known.

questions.question_text: Which cognitive, severity or related measures are reported?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Standardized developmental and language tests are mentioned as part of the cohort protocol but no cognitive, linguistic or adaptive scores are reported for the analysed sample. Comorbidities not described; other non-ASD language disorders explicitly absent from the sample.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Yes - IQ and mental age assessed with the Griffiths Mental Development Scales for all participants; ADOS Social/Communication and Stereotyped Behavior and Restricted Interests subscores reported for the 7 children who received ADOS. Comorbidities: participants were drug-naive with normal/corrected vision; other neurodevelopmental conditions were excluded from the design and flagged as future work.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: No cognitive, linguistic or adaptive-functioning measures reported. ASD participants are described as high-functioning and older than the low-functioning samples in prior work, but no IQ figures are given. Comorbidities are not described, and it is not stated whether ASD-ADHD co-occurrence was excluded - a material omission given the three-group design.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Nonverbal IQ measured with the Combined Raven Test (CRT-C2) for all participants and used to construct the ability-matched control group; AQ-Child reported for all three groups. No language or adaptive-functioning measures. Comorbid conditions are not described or excluded.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Yes, extensively: full-scale, verbal and performance IQ, Wechsler Memory Scale, Autism Quotient, Inventory of Interpersonal Problems, SCL-90 and Social Adjustment Scale reported for all groups. Comorbidity was actively excluded via SCL-90 screening, and the authors use verbal IQ, vocabulary subsection and WMS as covariates to show the semantic effect is not explained by structural language ability.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: A questionnaire on level of intellectual and social functioning and on prior mobile-device experience was administered to clinicians (autism group) and teachers (control group), but no scores are reported. IQ was explicitly not controlled - the authors state they 'were unable to exclude intelligence as a potential confounder' and mitigate by noting most children were clinician-classified as average (n=29) or high functioning (n=4), with only 2 low-functioning children contributing final data. Comorbidity is reported at the individual level (intellectual impairment in 4).

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Full-scale IQ measured with the Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence and reported for both groups (118.5 vs 119.8) and used as a matching variable - one of the few corpus studies to match and verify on IQ. No language or adaptive-functioning measures, no autism trait or severity scores (no AQ, ADOS or equivalent), and no comorbidity information.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: No cognitive, linguistic or adaptive-functioning measures are reported for any group. ASRS and AQ-10 are used only as control-admission gates and their scores are never reported for the ASD, ADHD or comorbid groups. Comorbidity, by contrast, is handled seriously - ADHD+ASD co-occurrence is a defined group and the subject of the second classification task, motivated by the observation that treatment differs across the three clinical groups.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Speech-language developmental level was annotated using the Stark Assessment of Early Vocal Development-Revised (SAEVD-R), recording whether each infant produced vocalisation types more complex than single canonical syllables - 4 ASD and 4 TD infants did, so the groups were comparable on this measure. No cognitive, adaptive or IQ measures are reported, and comorbid conditions are not described. Pacifier use during recording is noted for three infants, and one misclassified TD infant is flagged as having used one - an unusually granular disclosure of a potential acoustic confound.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Lexical abilities and academic grades are named as matching variables for the patient groups, but no scores are reported for any group and they are not used in modelling. All children are stated to have communicative verbal skills - an important inclusion constraint that excludes minimally verbal autistic children. Comorbidities are not described beyond the exclusion of learning disorders from the TD group.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, linguistic or adaptive-functioning measures are reported for either group, and no autism severity instrument underlies the 'mild category' description. The only functional criteria are physical - no history of lower-extremity injury and ability to walk independently. Comorbidities are not otherwise described.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic or adaptive measures for either group, and no autism severity instrument. Functioning level enters only as a post-hoc anecdote - two misclassified autistic children are described as 'high-functional in autism range' - which is used to explain errors rather than as measured data.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: The Gesell Developmental Scale (Chinese version) was administered to the ASD group, with adaptation, large motion, fine motion, language and personal-social subscores all reported - one of the fuller functional characterisations in the corpus. However the authors themselves list the absence of IQ and adaptive behaviour measures as their second limitation, and no GDS or other functional data were collected for the control group. Comorbidities are not described for the ASD group.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic or adaptive-functioning measures, no autism severity instrument, and no comorbidity information for any group. The reading materials are drawn from the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, so a standardised articulation instrument supplies the stimuli, but it is not scored as an assessment. The authors note narratively that 'some non-verbal children may not able to finish the reading test' but no verbal-ability data exist.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Years of formal education reported for both groups; web-use frequency assessed for all participants (all daily users); familiarity with each of the six stimulus websites surveyed to rule out over-familiarity confounds. No IQ, language or adaptive-functioning measures, and no autism severity score for the autistic group. Comorbidity handled only by excluding formally diagnosed intellectual disability, which bounds the sample to high-functioning adults.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Full Scale IQ measured by WISC-IV for both groups and used as a matching variable; executive function assessed in both groups by the Tower of London test with no significant difference (TD 29.35 +/- 3.54, ASD 29.35 +/- 2.80, t38 = 0, p = 0.999); handedness assessed by the Edinburgh Handedness Inventory (all but two children right-handed). Comorbidity is handled by explicit exclusion of pharmacological treatment, dyslexia, epilepsy and any other neurological or psychiatric condition. This is unusually thorough functional characterisation for a computer-vision paper.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Intelligence measured with the Wechsler Scales for all participants, with group means reported (109.4 and 112.3) and a minimum threshold of 85 applied as an inclusion criterion - so IQ is both measured and controlled by restriction and matching. Vision was normal or corrected-to-normal and neurological conditions excluded for all subjects. No language or adaptive measures, and ADOS-2 severity scores are not reported despite the instrument being administered.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Non-verbal IQ assessed by Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices and used as an inclusion criterion (average ability), so cognitive level is controlled by restriction rather than by matching or covariate adjustment. No language or adaptive-functioning measures and no autism severity instrument. Comorbidity is handled by exclusion: ADHD, mental retardation and schizophrenia ruled out for the ASD group; controls reported no physical or mental disorders.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Full-scale, verbal and non-verbal IQ measured with the WASI-II for both groups and used as matching variables with all comparisons tested. ADOS-2 Calibrated Severity Scores (overall, social affect, restricted and repetitive behaviour) and SCQ lifetime scores reported for both groups with group comparisons. All participants were native English speakers. Comorbid conditions are not described.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: IQ score range (58-137) reported for the ASD group only, with no mean, SD or control comparison, and not used as a covariate despite the authors' own introduction noting that eye-tracking results 'can be impacted by sample size, age, developmental level and IQ'. No language or adaptive measures. Comorbidities not described for the ASD group; controls screened by exclusion of psychiatric history, developmental delay and special education.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: MCHAT total scores and ADOS subscores (social affect, restricted and repetitive behaviour, composite) reported for the assessed subset. Additional health and social indicators are reported that no other corpus study collects: preterm birth, stunted growth, family income band, urban/semiurban/rural residence, and religion. Stunting information is missing for the entire TD cohort, which prevents its use as a covariate. No IQ, language or adaptive-functioning scores.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic, adaptive or severity measures, and no comorbidity information - consistent with the complete absence of participant metadata in the source dataset as used here.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic or adaptive measures, no severity instrument, and no comorbidity information. Mental age is used for matching but its values are not given. The one clinically relevant characteristic reported is that all ASD-group children were undergoing intervention and trained on similar tasks almost daily - which the authors correctly identify as a confound affecting their behaviour toward the robot.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic, adaptive or severity measures for either group. The workflow specifies that a therapist collects patient information and medical history in the pre-analysis phase, so such data are presumably gathered, but none is reported or used.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: IQ matching is claimed but no IQ values are reported for either group, and no language, adaptive-functioning or autism-trait measures are given. Comorbidities are not described. This is unusually sparse given that the paper is otherwise meticulous about its analysis.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: No cognitive, linguistic or adaptive measures are reported for either group, and no comorbidity information. CARS is the only clinical instrument, reported as a sample-level mean and median with a box-plot distribution.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Extensive neuropsychological examination is stated to have supplemented the diagnostic interviews for the autistic group, but no scores are reported and none are used in analysis. No IQ, language or adaptive measures for either group, no autism severity instrument, and no comorbidity information.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Planned and comprehensive. The Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire, the ESSENCE Questionnaire and the Adaptive Behavior Assessment System-3 or Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales-II are all administered to parents of children in the autistic and other-neurodevelopmental-disorder cohorts. That combination gives a behavioural-difficulty measure, a neurodevelopmental symptom-breadth measure and an adaptive-functioning measure alongside the diagnostic label, which is the apparatus needed to ask whether the instrument's output tracks severity or only category - the analysis this review has repeatedly found missing in completed studies whose data would have supported it.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic, adaptive or severity measures, and no comorbidity information - consistent with the absence of participant metadata in the challenge dataset as used here.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic, adaptive or severity measures and no comorbidity information for any participant.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any participant.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic, adaptive or severity measures and no comorbidity information.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure was obtained.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Comprehensive by corpus standards. Gesell Developmental Scale developmental quotients across five domains (adaptive, gross motor, fine motor, language, personal-social) for all participants; CSBS-DP with three factor scores and total, CARS, and ABC for symptom severity in the high-risk group. All were used analytically - correlated against behavioural indicators - not merely tabulated. The requirement that the mother be the primary caregiver is also a stated inclusion criterion for both groups, controlling a variable that matters for a mother-infant interaction paradigm.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: IQ is reported for all four subgroups and used as a matching variable with statistical verification, and handedness is also matched. No language, adaptive-functioning or autism-severity measures are reported, and no comorbidity information. IQ means of 122-126 indicate a sample well above population average.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental quotient, language, adaptive functioning, symptom severity or comorbidity measure is reported for either group. Severity grading is named only as future work.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: No cognitive, linguistic, adaptive or autism-severity measures are reported. Anthropometrics (height, body mass) are measured and reported for both groups, which is the relevant covariate set for postural biomechanics. Comorbidity is handled by explicit exclusion of neurological disorders other than ASD, chronic medical disorders, visual impairments and physical impairments affecting balance - a well-targeted exclusion list that removes the most plausible competing explanations for balance differences.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: None reported. No cognitive, linguistic, adaptive or severity measures for either group, and no comorbidity information.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Extensive. Full-scale and index IQ measured with WISC-V and used as an inclusion criterion; general motor ability measured with the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-2 explicitly to separate imitation-specific from general motor differences; ADOS-2 and SRS-2 administered and used quantitatively in correlational analyses of symptom severity. Full inclusion and exclusion criteria are deferred to a supplement. This is among the fullest functional characterisations in the corpus.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: K-CARS, SRS and SCQ were administered and could have supported severity analysis, but no severity, cognitive, language or adaptive scores are reported and no severity-stratified result is given. The five-category vocalisation labelling (single syllable, canonical babbling, non-syllabic babbling, first word, atypical voice) functions as a developmental-stage descriptor and is the only developmental characterisation reported, given per group as proportions of total vocalisation time.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental, language, adaptive or severity measure is reported, and no comorbidity information. Nor are the anthropometric variables that directly determine gait phase durations - height, leg length, body mass - which for a gait study is a substantive omission independent of clinical characterisation.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: ADOS total, SA and RRB scores are the severity characterisation and are used analytically throughout, including a separate correlation analysis per subscale. No IQ, language, adaptive or cognitive measures are reported, which matters because ADOS module assignment already encodes language capacity and so the cohort spans a language range that is not otherwise quantified. Comorbid language and developmental delays are present in 10 children and identified as such but not scored.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: Intellectual disability and reading disorder were formal exclusions, and three control participants were excluded for school dyslexia referrals, so reading ability is controlled at the eligibility level for a task that depends on reading. Vision not correctable by glasses or lenses was also excluded. No IQ, AQ score (for the autistic group), symptom severity or adaptive functioning measure is reported; functional level is characterised by employment, housing and education instead, which is arguably more informative for an adult cohort though not comparable across studies.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental quotient, language, adaptive functioning or symptom severity measure is reported for either group, and no comorbidity information. Grading severity is named only as future work.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None reported, and their absence is explicitly acknowledged as a limitation. ADOS-2 and ADI-R were administered and yield severity indices in social affect and restricted/repetitive behaviour domains, but no scores appear and no severity-stratified analysis is performed. No IQ, cognitive, language or adaptive measure, and no motor comorbidity screening despite the outcome being motor.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental quotient, language, adaptive or symptom severity measure is reported, and no comorbidity information. The six behaviour scores function as a within-protocol profile but are not related to any external severity measure.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: The most complete clinical characterisation in the corpus for a subset of participants: ADOS severity (autism symptom severity), SRS total (reciprocal social behaviour), Vineland-3 ABC across communication, daily living skills and socialisation (adaptive functioning), and Stanford-Binet IQ for the full cohort. Critically, these are not merely tabulated but used as regression targets, which is what allows the paper's central negative finding - that eye-tracking features predict IQ but not autism severity or adaptive functioning.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: None reported. PEP-3 yields developmental scores that could have supported severity or functioning analyses, but no scores appear and no stratification is performed. This is a substantive gap given the paper's own explanation for inconsistent EEG findings in the literature - that 'autism can be divided into low function and high function according to behavioral ability' and that heterogeneity is why 'using only EEG evaluation may be insufficient'. Having advanced that argument, the study is unable to test it in its own data.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Complete. SCQ, SRS-2 total and Stanford-Binet ABIQ for every participant in both groups, plus itemised comorbid psychological conditions and current medications for those who completed the survey. Uniquely in this corpus, the medication data are reported at drug level rather than as a summary count, which matters because several of the drugs listed - methylphenidate, guanfacine, aripiprazole - have documented effects on attention and eye movement.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: ADOS scores for 35 participants, Autism-Spectrum Quotient for all participants in both groups, and Wortschatztest verbal intelligence as an inclusion screen. The ADOS data are used substantively: the classifier's predicted class probability correlates with ADOS score at rs = 0.48, p < 0.0001, establishing that the model's output tracks symptom severity and not merely group membership. No full-scale IQ, adaptive functioning or comorbidity scores are reported.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental, language, adaptive or severity measure, and no comorbidity information. Given the paper's opening claim that autism symptoms 'range from completely debilitating to manageable', the absence of any severity characterisation means nothing can be said about where on that range the classified sample sits.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: CARS severity category only, as minimal or mild. No CARS total scores, no IQ, no language or adaptive measures, and no comorbidity information.
