The two performance measures the model consumes - joint attention and imitation success rates - are themselves clinically meaningful and are tabulated per child, but they are the model's input rather than an independent characterisation.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: CARS scores for both groups, reported as ranges and a group mean. The autistic range of 33-45 spans mild-to-moderate through severe on standard CARS bands, so the sample covers meaningful severity variation - but this is never exploited. No severity-stratified analysis is performed, no relationship between CARS score and classifier output is examined, and no IQ, language or adaptive measure appears. Given that the discriminative signal is in anticipatory gaze during joint attention, which plausibly varies with severity, relating classifier confidence to CARS would have been a straightforward and valuable analysis.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: AQ total scores for the preliminary sample only, with the five subscale domains described but never analysed. No severity, IQ, language, adaptive or comorbidity measure for the diagnosed test participants, and no AQ administered to them - so it is not possible to establish whether the diagnosed group would even have scored above the study's own trait threshold.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: The most complete cognitive characterisation in the corpus. Combined Raven's Test for nonverbal and PPVT-R for verbal mental intelligence, plus SCQ, administered to all three groups with means and standard deviations tabulated and all pairwise comparisons tested. These are not merely reported but used structurally - they define the functioning subgroups, they establish that the high-functioning and typically developing groups are matched on both intelligence measures, and they support the interpretation that visual-orienting performance tracks cognitive level. No adaptive functioning or comorbidity measures.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental, language, adaptive or severity measure, and no comorbidity information for either group.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental, language, adaptive or severity measure, and no comorbidity information for either group.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Strong for a severity study. CARS for all participants with group ranges and means; Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales and the Repetitive Behavior Scale-Revised administered 'when possible'. The Vineland result is used substantively - significantly lower adaptive functioning in the severe group corroborates the CARS-based split from an independent instrument, which is the correct way to validate a severity dichotomy. The absence of IQ is acknowledged as a limitation and proposed as a future model feature.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Nonverbal IQ via Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices for both groups, with at least average intelligence required for inclusion in the autistic group. No autism severity measure of any kind, which the authors state candidly: severity 'was not specifically measured in our study' and the sample 'could be viewed as representing individuals with minor severity'. No language, adaptive functioning or comorbidity scores. The IQ data are reported but, unusually, the significant group difference they reveal is not carried into the analysis.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental, language, adaptive or severity measure, and no comorbidity information for any of the three groups.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: CARS for severity and ECSP for social communication, both in French versions, administered to both groups by psychologists. CARS is used analytically in the correlation analysis rather than merely tabulated. ECSP is reported but not used, and its near-identical group means at what appears to be a ceiling limit its informativeness. No IQ, adaptive functioning or comorbidity measures, and ADI-R and ADOS-G scores were inaccessible.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Among the better-characterised samples in the corpus: CARS for all participants, plus WISC intelligence, Repetitive Behavior Scale and Vineland adaptive behaviour for autistic participants where obtainable, all deposited per participant. The limitation is that none of these measures is used analytically - there is no severity-stratified analysis, no relation between CARS or IQ and classifier output, and no examination of whether comorbidity status affects classification, despite comorbid participants having been deliberately retained.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: ADOS-2 and ADI-R administered but with no scores reported and no severity-stratified analysis. No IQ, cognitive, adaptive or language measures, and the authors identify the absence of IQ and cognitive matching as a limitation requiring attention in future work. The only functional indicator available is the choice of ADOS-2 module 1.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Nonverbal IQ via Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices, used both as an inclusion criterion and, importantly, as a covariate in the feature-discrimination models. No autism severity measure, which the authors acknowledge in calling for future samples with 'different behavioral presentations'. No language or adaptive functioning measures.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: None used. CARS is mentioned as having been applied in the source study but no scores are reported, no severity stratification is performed, and no cognitive, language or adaptive measures appear. Since the source dataset's accompanying publication reports CARS and ECSP scores, the omission is a choice of this reanalysis rather than a constraint of the data.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: ADOS total scores individually reported for all 26 participants with the module used, plus ICD-10 diagnostic subtype and comorbid diagnoses per child. Severity is used analytically rather than descriptively - correlated against all four kinematic outcomes - which is what produces the paper's key dissociation. The acknowledged gap is intellectual functioning: no IQ or developmental level was measured, and the authors state that future research 'will have to evaluate intellectual disability, which is an important source of inter-subject variability in ASD that seems to impact motor planning and coordination'.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: CARS2 is used as an eligibility range rather than as a per-child variable, so no severity gradient is available for analysis - a missed opportunity, since relating attention trajectories to baseline severity across six children in a seven-week course would have been the natural individualisation question and the data existed to ask it. The study's own outcome measure, the automated attention score, functions as a repeated within-child measure and is used that way: its whole design rationale is that assessment could be 'repeated more frequently to trace the severity and development of symptoms'. That is a severity-tracking argument, and it is the clearest statement in this review of why continuous behavioural measurement might matter clinically for reasons other than diagnosis.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, language or adaptive measure. Family history of cognitive disability is collected as a predictor rather than as a characterisation.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: The most complete clinical characterisation of any speech study in the corpus. ADOS-2 Social Affect, Restricted and Repetitive Behavior, total and Calibrated Severity Scores; SRS total t-scores; WISC-IV short-form full-scale IQ from Information, Block Design and Vocabulary subtests; and the Children's Communication Checklist-2 yielding both a General Communication Composite and a Social Interaction Difference Index designed so that more negative values indicate autism. All are reported with group means and p-values, and the ADOS-2 CSS, SRS, GCC and SIDI are used analytically as correlates of the selected voice features, with partial Spearman coefficients adjusted for IQ.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: None. No IQ, language, adaptive functioning, comorbidity or medication information for either group, and no exclusions described. Nor is there any severity measure, so the model's outputs cannot be related to any clinical gradient.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: None. No IQ, adaptive functioning, language measure, comorbidity or medication information, and no exclusion criteria. Consequently nothing links model output to any clinical gradient, and the frequently cited possibility that IQ rather than diagnosis drives gaze differences cannot be examined.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Comprehensive and, unusually, used analytically rather than descriptively. ADOS calibrated severity scores for total, social affect and restricted/repetitive behaviour; VABS-II Adaptive Behavior Composite with communication, socialisation, daily-living and motor subdomains; and a Best Estimate IQ constructed to combine 'the most representative cognitive functioning measures for each child', since instruments varied with age and with each child's ability to attend demanding tasks - a pragmatic solution to a real problem in toddler cognitive assessment, and one that is documented rather than glossed. All three feed the validation analyses. Comorbidities are not described for the autistic group.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Partial. IQ was assessed with the Leiter-3, a nonverbal intelligence test appropriate for this population and administered in its original form for the assessment, but reported only as a range per group. Comorbidity was handled by exclusion rather than measurement: 'no existing comorbidities' was an inclusion criterion, no specific comorbidity was reported, and all participants were required to have normal vision and no sensory or motor deficit - the last a genuinely relevant control for a study whose outcome is a fine-motor measure, and one that also narrows the sample away from the substantial proportion of autistic children who do have motor impairment. No adaptive functioning measure, no language level, and no ADOS severity scores despite the instrument being used for diagnosis. Medication is not reported, though ongoing psychomotor and speech therapy is.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: No cognitive, language or adaptive measure of any kind for either group - a significant omission in 3-to-6-year-olds, where developmental level varies enormously and both resting EEG spectral power and social gaze allocation are strongly age- and ability-dependent. No comorbidity information and no exclusions described. Four symptom instruments (ABC, SCQ, SRS, CABS) were administered to the autistic group and three to the comparison group, and their scores are tabulated, so a severity gradient exists in the data; it is used only to characterise the sample and is never related to the model's continuous output, missing the opportunity to test whether the classifier's confidence tracks symptom level - the analysis that would have provided clinical anchoring.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: IQ was measured for every child using an age-appropriate instrument - Korean WPPSI-IV for older children, Korean Bayley Scales-II for younger - and combined into a best-estimate figure, which is the right approach for a sample spanning 24 to 72 months. The result is the study's central confound rather than a control. Comorbidity was handled by exclusion and the exclusions are mechanistically reasoned: because joint attention depends on 'perception, attention, and motor coordination', children were required to have normal or corrected vision and normal hearing and were excluded for pharmacological treatment, developmental coordination disorder, ADHD, and any other neurological or psychiatric condition. This is a more thoughtfully constructed exclusion set than most in the corpus, since each element removes a plausible non-autism cause of failing the specific target behaviour. No adaptive functioning or language measure is reported.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None whatsoever. No IQ, developmental quotient, language level, adaptive functioning measure, severity score, comorbidity list or medication information for either group. This is the most complete absence of clinical characterisation among the studies in this corpus that nonetheless report high accuracy, and it compounds the recruitment asymmetry: with children drawn from special education schools versus regular kindergartens and no cognitive measure taken, there is no way to determine whether the classifier separates autism or separates developmental level.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Nothing. No IQ, language, adaptive functioning, comorbidity, medication or severity data, and no exclusions described. Consequently there is no possibility of relating model output to any clinical gradient, and no way to assess whether developmental level rather than diagnosis distinguishes the classes.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Comprehensive and used analytically rather than descriptively. Full-scale IQ was measured in both groups and reported with range and test statistic; the AQ was administered to both groups; and ADOS-2 Overall Calibrated Severity Scores derived by the Hus and Lord algorithm were obtained for the autistic group with a full range of 3 to 10, meaning the sample spans the severity spectrum rather than clustering at one end. Severity was then correlated against all four gaze features, with the finding that none reached significance - a negative result that matters, since it means the gaze measures that do differentiate groups on average do not index how autistic an individual is. Comorbidity handling is deliberate and unusual: depression, anxiety and ADHD were permitted rather than excluded on the grounds that they are common in autism, with only moderate-to-severe depression (BDI-II >= 25) and antipsychotic medication ruled out. The authors then list this inclusiveness among their own limitations, noting it leaves open how much comorbidity contributed to the findings - a rare instance of a design decision being defended and then flagged as a threat in the same paper.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive or severity measure for either group, and no comorbidity or medication information. This matters more than usual for a speech study, since expressive language level directly determines what a child produces in a 90-second game and would be expected to differ between a median-5-year-old autistic group and a median-9.5-year-old comparison group on both developmental and diagnostic grounds. Nothing in the data allows that to be examined, and no exclusion criteria of any kind are described.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Complete and used analytically throughout. IQ was estimated from a three-subtest WISC-IV short form (Information, Block Design, Vocabulary) with the Sattler and Dumont formula, and the authors note honestly that separate verbal and non-verbal estimates cannot be derived from this short form. The Children's Communication Checklist-2 was completed by parents, with its structure described in detail - ten subscales, the first four averaged into a Structural Language scale and four more into a Pragmatic scale, with the last two measuring behaviours characteristic of autism. ADOS-2 Social Affect and Restricted and Repetitive Behavior scores were computed under the Gotham et al. algorithm. Three objective language-output indices were additionally computed from the task itself: total c-units, total words and activity time. All of these then serve as predictors in the misclassification analysis, which is the paper's most original contribution - they are not merely descriptive but are the variables through which the complementarity of the two modalities is established.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Comprehensive for the autistic group and absent for the comparison group. ADOS-2 Toddler Module calibrated severity scores average 7.56 +/- 1.67 across a range of 2-10, so the sample spans the severity spectrum. The Mullen Scales of Early Learning provide an Early Learning Composite of 63.64 +/- 10.17 alongside Expressive Language (T = 28.08), Receptive Language (T = 23.14), Fine Motor (T = 34.11) and Visual Reception (T = 33.94) T-scores - all substantially below average, indicating a group with considerable developmental delay, and the Fine Motor score is directly relevant since the outcome is a motor measure. The Mullen composite is used analytically, correlated against all three head movement measures. Because no Mullen data exist for the neurotypical group, the cognitive difference between groups cannot be estimated or adjusted, and the authors list this among their limitations: 'The autistic and neurotypical group differed in cognitive ability and, thus, it is not clear the degree to which differences in cognition contributed to our findings.' Comorbidity is not otherwise characterised, and the 12 children with non-autism diagnoses were removed.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: IQ was measured in every participant, but with different instruments by language group: the WASI, WAIS-III/IV or WISC-IV for English participants and the TONI-4 for Cantonese participants. The TONI-4 is a nonverbal reasoning measure while the Wechsler scales yield full-scale IQ incorporating verbal subtests, so the two sets of scores are not interchangeable and cross-language comparison of cognitive level is not possible. Within each language group the comparison participants score higher (111.03 versus 104.13 in English; 115.08 versus 108.54 in Cantonese). ADOS-2 calibrated severity scores are reported for both autistic groups (7.02 English, 6.00 Cantonese) with full ranges spanning 3-9.5 and 3-10, so both samples cover the severity spectrum. No language ability measure was administered, and the authors identify this as a limitation that matters specifically for their outcome: 'future studies should employ more comprehensive assessments of language abilities for group matching, since baseline language ability may covary with age and autism severity, influencing prosody and pitch in particular'. No adaptive functioning or comorbidity data.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Both verbal and non-verbal IQ measured in every participant using age-appropriate Wechsler scales - the WISC-R for those aged 6.0-16.11 and the WAIS for those older - with means, standard deviations, ranges and t-tests reported for both. Reporting verbal and non-verbal IQ separately is appropriate and uncommon, and matters directly for a narrative-language outcome. Non-verbal IQ of 80 or above was an inclusion criterion, so the sample is confined to participants without intellectual disability, which the authors identify as limiting generalisation: 'our study included only fluently speaking participants with ASD with no intellectual disability and might not apply to everyone on the autism spectrum'. ADOS-2 overall and SCQ overall scores characterise severity in both groups. No adaptive functioning or language-specific standardised measure was administered, and no comorbidity information is reported beyond the idiopathic-autism inclusion requirement.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Developmental level was measured properly, with the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Third Edition - an age-appropriate instrument covering 1 to 42 months, cited with its psychometric properties - administered to both groups and reported separately for cognition and language. That both groups were assessed is a genuine strength relative to studies here that measure cognition in the autistic group only or not at all. The problem is that the resulting data are used descriptively and never analytically: the 20-point cognitive gap and 34-point language gap are tabulated and then absent from every subsequent analysis, with no covariate adjustment, no matched subsample, and no mention in the discussion or limitations. No autism severity instrument was administered, so the model's outputs cannot be related to a severity gradient and the false-negative analysis the authors themselves call for - assessing 'the symptom profiles of false-negative children' - is not possible with the data collected. No comorbidity or medication information beyond the exclusion criteria.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: CARS scores were obtained for the autistic groups only and only for children aged 2 and over, at 32.3 +/- 1.5 in toddlers and 33.0 +/- 2.1 in preschoolers - both close to the cut-off of 30, so the samples sit at the milder end of the CARS range with narrow standard deviations, which limits the severity gradient available for correlation. The severity data are nonetheless used analytically, in a multiple regression of fixation time percentage on CARS with age and gender as covariates across all autistic children, returning no significant association on any area of interest (p values from 0.13 to 0.99). That null is reported without qualification and is important: it means the gaze measures separate the groups on average without tracking how autistic an individual child is, which converges with the same finding in the Keles adult study and bears on whether such measures could serve as severity or outcome measures rather than only as classifiers. No cognitive, language or adaptive measure was collected for either group, and no comorbidity or medication information.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Extensive on comorbidity and severity, absent on cognition. Specialists recorded all comorbid conditions, tabulated across fifteen diagnostic categories with frequencies, and then cross-tabulated against Device output - showing for instance that children with phonological disorder were classified indeterminate 82.4% of the time while those with intellectual disability received a positive output 66.7% of the time. DSM-5 support-level severity was recorded separately for social communication and restricted repetitive behaviour domains in every autism-positive child, using the maximum where site and reviewing specialists differed, and broken down by output: of 121 with scores, 5 were Level 1, 51 Level 2 and 65 Level 3, with the Device classifying 44 of 65 Level 3 children positive against 1 of 5 Level 1 children. That gradient is the clearest evidence in the paper of what the abstention mechanism is doing - declining on milder and more ambiguous presentations. No IQ or developmental quotient was obtained, and the reason given is sound: 'a large portion of participants were below the age threshold where non-verbal cognitive abilities can be reliably tested with traditional measures of intelligence'. The authors nonetheless flag that 'appropriately powered follow-up studies are needed to confirm Device performance across a range of intellectual levels'.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: None whatsoever - no cognitive, language, adaptive, severity or comorbidity measure for either group. The absence is particularly consequential here because the outcome is narrative speech elicited from a picture sequence: expressive language level determines how much a child says, how fluently, and with what syntactic complexity, all of which shape the acoustic signal, and it would be expected to differ between a group recruited from speech and language therapy services and a community comparison group. Nothing in the data permits this to be examined, and the paper does not raise it.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive, severity, comorbidity or medication information for either group, and no exclusions described. Nothing therefore relates model output to any clinical dimension, and the possibility that the classifier separates developmental level rather than diagnosis cannot be examined.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive, severity or comorbidity measure for either group. Nothing therefore relates the gaze findings to any clinical dimension, and with an age span of 2 to 15 years and no developmental measure, neither age nor ability can be separated from diagnosis as an explanation for the observed differences.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: None used. CARS-based severity exists in the source data and is referenced in the literature review, but no cognitive, language, adaptive, severity or comorbidity measure enters the analysis, and no exclusions are described. Consequently nothing relates model output to any clinical dimension, and the paper's speculation that 'ML models could quantify heterogeneities in ASD symptoms, allowing for accurate ASD severity grading using ET data' is untested despite the severity data being available in the source.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: None analysed. No cognitive, language, adaptive or severity measure was obtained for either group, and no comorbidity data are reported despite the diagnostic menu having captured alternative labels and despite therapy type having been collected. The absence matters for the specific construct at issue: response latency in an emotion-enactment task depends on receptive language, processing speed and motor planning, none of which is measured, and the sample spans ages 3 to 12 with no age reported by group. The authors list co-occurring diagnoses among the dimensions they cannot examine at this sample size.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive, severity, comorbidity or medication information for either group, and no exclusion criteria. One relevant observation is made in passing and is important: 'the quality of children's word pronunciation was poor because some ASD children can't pronounce normally, or it's difficult for them to pronounce as required, finally, less than 1/3 of the data was usable'. That establishes that expressive speech ability varied substantially within the autistic group and that data loss was driven by it, but no measure of that ability was collected and the retention rate is not reported separately by group.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: ADOS raw scores are reported for both groups and are the dependent variable, so severity is characterised more centrally here than anywhere else in the corpus. Nothing else is measured: no IQ, developmental quotient, language level, adaptive functioning or comorbidity data for either group. The omission is consequential for interpretation because the sample is explicitly a young and largely non-fluent one, so expressive language ability varies widely and is not quantified. Since the predictors are acoustic properties of speech and the outcome is a clinical score that itself weights communication heavily, an unmeasured language-ability variable sits between the two and could account for a substantial part of the reported correlation without any autism-specific acoustic signal being involved.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: No independent severity instrument was administered, but the study's own observational scale carries graded 0-5 severity ratings for interest in the robot and for additional movements at each defined position, so a within-study severity dimension exists. The authors use the group differences on these subscales to argue that the findings 'support the initial ASD diagnoses by showing that autistic symptoms are present in children diagnosed with ASD' - which is a convergent-validity argument for the measurement rather than a severity analysis, and is a reasonable use of the data. No relationship between turn-taking indicators and any severity score is examined.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Cognitive ability: Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices in both groups, non-verbal only, used both as an eligibility gate (IQ >= 70) and as a reported demographic. Language: a qualitative judgement by a speech-language psychologist that the child could sustain average verbal communication - no standardised score. Severity: none. No ADOS calibrated severity score, CARS, SRS, ADI-R algorithm score or any other symptom-quantification instrument was obtained, which is a direct consequence of the stated lack of access to ADOS/ADI-R. The study therefore cannot relate its gaze-entropy features to symptom severity, cannot report where on the spectrum its 19 children sit, and cannot test whether misclassified children were the less severely affected ones. Combined with the exclusion of children with severe symptoms and of those with IQ below 70, the analysed autistic sample is a narrow, cognitively able, verbal slice of the population.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, developmental, adaptive, language or motor assessment was administered to any participant, and no autism severity measure was obtained. This is a substantive omission for two reasons specific to this design. First, the task is a fine and gross motor task performed by 3-6 year olds, and the extracted features - jolt counts, acceleration energy, tilt rates, spatial extent of movement - are all motor-competence-sensitive; without a developmental or motor measure it is impossible to separate an autism-specific play signature from a general developmental-level difference, particularly since the authors themselves observe that 'the TD children played with more energy and they moved the car in a wider area compared to the other two groups'. Second, the discussion rests its case for multimodality on within-spectrum heterogeneity - 'children with ASD may be at different parts of the ASD spectrum' - which is precisely the variable the study does not measure, so the claim cannot be tested against the data and the model cannot be checked for whether it succeeds only on more severely affected children.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Cognitive ability was measured in every participant with the Leiter-3 International Performance Scale, a non-verbal instrument appropriate for this population, and reported as a per-group range (ASD 59-109, TD 74-110) with the six autistic children in the 59-70 band identified. No means, SDs or statistical comparison are given. Autism severity was not measured or reported at all: ADOS-2 was administered for diagnosis but no severity, comparison or algorithm score is carried into the paper, so the position of these 30 children on the spectrum is unknown, no analysis relates model output to symptom severity, and it cannot be checked whether the model succeeds preferentially on more affected children. No language, adaptive-functioning or motor-competence measure was obtained, the last being a notable gap in a study whose entire signal is motor. There is also a structural entanglement peculiar to this design: the Leiter-3 serves simultaneously as the cognitive measure and, in tablet form, as the experimental task, so the kinematic features are recorded while children perform the very test used to characterise their cognitive ability, and only trials they completed correctly are analysed. Cognitive ability is therefore not an independent covariate here - it conditions which trajectories exist in the dataset.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: No cognitive, language, adaptive or global severity measure was administered or reported. The only quantitative symptom measure in the study is the response-to-name score itself, and it is genuinely informative: Table 2 shows that 17 of the 30 children failed to respond after all five calls, with the remainder distributed across the lower scores. That distribution is a symptom-severity profile for one ADOS-2 item, and it is reported honestly. But it is also the paper's undoing statistically, because a majority of children and a larger majority of the 109 calls fall into the single 'no response' category, and no chance-corrected agreement statistic is computed against that floor. Beyond this item, nothing: no ADOS-2 calibrated severity score despite ADOS-2 having been administered in full to every child, no developmental quotient, no language measure beyond the coarse module assignment, and no motor assessment - the last being relevant since the system's primary signal is torso rotation and children in this age and module range vary widely in postural control.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: No cognitive, language, adaptive or severity instrument was administered to any participant in either group. The autistic sample is described only as having 'high-performance autism disorder', a label with no accompanying score, cut-off or source, and the conclusion leans on it interpretively - arguing that accuracy above 73% is 'desirable given the status of children with high-performance autism disorder', i.e. that the task is intrinsically harder in a less impaired sample. That is a reasonable argument but it cannot be evaluated, because no measure of functioning or severity exists to place the sample on any scale, nor to check whether the misclassified children were the less affected ones. Two informal proxies appear in the inclusion criteria - a therapist's judgement of the child's face perception, and the capacity to sit and attend at a computer - and both operate as gates rather than as measurements. The absence of IQ is particularly consequential here because the index task is a visual matching task drawn from the same family as nonverbal reasoning tests: any group difference in fixation distribution over candidate figures could as easily reflect differences in matching strategy or task comprehension as differences in social attention, and there is no covariate with which to separate them.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Cognitive ability was measured properly: WASI-II full-scale and verbal IQ estimates were obtained for the whole sample and compared between groups, with no significant difference. This is the correct handling and it removes the single most pervasive confound in this literature. Language ability is indexed by verbal IQ and by the requirement that all participants be native and fluent English speakers, which matters for a task whose entire stimulus is spontaneous conversation. Autism severity, however, is not reported. ADOS-2 Module 4 was administered as part of the diagnostic process, so calibrated severity scores were almost certainly available, yet none appears - so it is impossible to say where the 15 autistic adults sit on the spectrum, whether the 45% the model failed to detect were the less severely affected, or whether the four participants that humans misjudged but the model caught differed systematically in severity. That last question is the one the paper's own error-overlap analysis makes most interesting, and severity data would have gone a long way towards answering it. No adaptive-functioning, comorbidity or motor measure is reported either.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, developmental, language, adaptive or severity measure was administered to any of the 333 children, and no autism severity score of any kind is reported. Three consequences follow that the paper does not address. First, the autistic sample cannot be positioned on the spectrum, so it is unknown whether the model's performance would hold in a less clearly affected group - a particular concern given that the discussion itself observes that adding subjects makes 'more unclear and atypical cases' appear. Second, the paradigm demands six minutes of sustained attention to a screen from 3-6 year olds, and the ability to comply is developmentally graded; without a cognitive measure it is impossible to separate an autism-specific viewing signature from a general attentional or developmental one, and the authors' own explanation of why specificity is lowest in 3-4 year olds - younger children 'find it difficult to focus on the screen the entire time, resulting in meaningless fixations that fall on the gray mask' - shows that this is not hypothetical. Third, the conclusion proposes that dynamic viewing patterns 'can also be employed to quantitatively assess subjects' ASD risk', but with no severity instrument in the study there is nothing against which such a continuous risk score could be calibrated or validated.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive or severity measure exists, and none could exist given the data source. This matters more than in most studies here because language is the entire modality: a paper classifying people by their writing reports no lexical, syntactic, readability or pragmatic measure of that writing, and no characterisation of how the two corpora differ. Severity appears only in the introduction, where Asperger syndrome is described as 'the one that is labelled as severity 1' and is included among the search keywords, but no severity information is extracted, used or reported. The absence has a specific analytical cost: because self-disclosure of autism on social media is likely to be associated with particular parts of the spectrum - verbally fluent, self-aware, digitally engaged, often diagnosed later in life - the sample is drawn from a narrow and self-selected slice of the autistic population, and nothing in the study characterises which slice.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Partial, and better than most here on severity while silent on cognition. ADOS-Toddler total scores were obtained for the diagnosed children and are reported as a group mean of 7.64 +/- 1.69, giving a genuine quantitative severity index - the study is one of relatively few in this corpus where such a score exists at all. But it is used only descriptively. No analysis relates integrated entropy to ADOS-T score, so the question that would most strengthen the biomarker claim - whether facial-dynamics complexity tracks symptom severity within the autistic group, rather than merely separating groups - is not asked. The tight standard deviation (1.69) also indicates a fairly homogeneous severity range, which limits what such an analysis could have shown and constrains generalisation to more or less affected children. No cognitive, developmental or language measure was administered to either group, which matters for a paradigm requiring 17-36 month olds to attend to a screen for several minutes: developmental level governs sustained attention, and the paper's own 40% valid-data threshold removes children who looked away too much, so cognitive and attentional capacity silently shapes who is analysed. The authors partly address this by verifying that missing-data percentage does not differ significantly between groups and by entering it as an ANCOVA covariate, which is a good empirical substitute for a developmental measure but not a replacement for one.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Rich on symptom severity and empty on cognition - an unusual combination in this corpus, where the reverse is more common. Severity and phenotype are measured with four or five instruments per dataset. Adults: SRS-2 total raw score (control 55.2 +/- 20.9, ASD 73.3 +/- 36.0 - note the very large SD in the autistic group, indicating wide variation in social-communication severity), ADOS-2 (46.5 +/- 11.9), PANSS for the schizophrenia group (67.1 +/- 13.0), and Kikuchi's Scale of Social Skills 18-item (control 64.7 +/- 11.0, ASD 45.3 +/- 9.46, Sz 59.1 +/- 9.14, so the autistic group scores lowest on self-reported social skill). Children: SRS-2 (control 19.2 +/- 11.5, ASD 74.7 +/- 26.9 - a very wide separation), ADHD-RS and CBCL. SRS-2 was deliberately not administered to the schizophrenia group because it has not been validated in that population, an omission explained rather than glossed. Against this, no IQ or developmental measure was obtained for anyone. The authors state the limitation squarely: participants were recruited without intellectual difficulties but 'we did not obtain any actual IQ values', so the study 'does not adequately take into account the influence of intellectual level', and the sample comprises 'only a small number of mild (high-functioning) cases'. Two consequences follow. Because the FEIT is a cognitive task with a correct answer, intellectual level plausibly affects both recognition accuracy and viewing strategy. And because SRS-2 was used to select which controls were retained, a severity-related variable enters the sampling as well as the description. Notably, no analysis relates any of these severity scores to model output, so the rich phenotyping is used descriptively rather than analytically.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive-function or autism-severity measure exists for any participant, and none could exist given the data source. This is a substantive gap for a study whose modality is language production: the dataset consists of hundreds of thousands of communicative acts, and the paper reports descriptively that autistic users produced a considerably higher number of unique words than most other diagnostic groups, but no linguistic or communicative competence measure is derived, validated or used. The conclusion identifies the gap without naming it as one, proposing future work on 'how usage patterns can be used to predict quantitative traits of clinical relevance (such as adaptive skills and the severity of the autism presentation)'. Two consequences follow. There is no way to characterise where on the spectrum the 81 autistic users sit, and since they are people who need a speech-generating device they are by construction from the minimally verbal end - a population systematically under-represented in the rest of this corpus, which is a genuine strength of the dataset that the absence of any severity measure prevents the study from exploiting. And the number of unique words used, which the paper reports as evidence of the app's usefulness, is equally readable as a proxy for expressive language level, unmeasured and uncontrolled, and plausibly one of the features the classifier exploits.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Unusually complete on both cognition and severity, and among the best in this review. Cognitive functioning was assessed in every participant using an age-appropriate and ability-appropriate instrument - the Korean Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development, Second Edition, or the Korean Wechsler Preschool and Primary Scale of Intelligence, Fourth Edition - and a best-estimate IQ derived, reported separately from verbal IQ and stratified by age band. Severity is measured twice over: K-ADOS-2 calibrated severity scores are reported for total, social affect and restricted-repetitive domains with medians and ranges, and K-CARS-2 total scores are reported by age band for both groups. Module distribution is given, establishing that the autism sample is predominantly preverbal or single-word. What this permits, and what almost no other study in the corpus can do, is a genuine severity-prediction analysis rather than a binary one - and the study takes it up, reporting AUROCs of 84.2-90.3% for a three-class severity task. Two caveats attach. The severity target is the caregiver-completed K-CARS-2 rather than the clinician-administered K-ADOS-2, which is the weaker of the two instruments the study holds. And the three classes include non-autism, so the severity model is not discriminating within the spectrum but performing a graded version of the detection task - which means its 90.3% AUROC is not evidence that the system can grade severity among autistic children, and no within-autism-only result is reported.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive or severity measure appears, and none could, since no participants were assessed by these authors. The absence has a specific analytical cost in this design: the scanpath is a picture of where a child looked during an unreported task, and how much a child looks at all - the number of fixations, the spatial extent covered - varies with attention, developmental level and task compliance. Without any measure of those, a difference in the visual density or spread of the plotted trajectory cannot be separated from a difference in social attention. Since the models are given only the drawing, this is precisely the ambiguity that an interpretability analysis would have addressed, and none is performed.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: No external cognitive, language or severity measure exists, and the absence is more consequential here than in most studies because language is simultaneously the modality, the feature set and the plausible confound. The study computes mean length of utterance in morphemes and number of distinct word roots - both standard expressive-language indices used clinically to characterise developmental level - and uses them as classifier inputs, with the second identified by SHAP as the dominant predictor. In a sample where the autistic group extends down to 12 months and the comparison group does not go below 3 years, that finding is compatible with the model having learned a developmental-language gradient rather than an autism-specific one. Nothing in the analysis distinguishes the two, because no independent measure of language level exists to adjust for. Severity is likewise absent and is named as future work. The gap also blocks the more interesting question the feature set was built to answer: whether pragmatic atypicality - echolalia, poor discourse coherence, failure to initiate questions - is present over and above general language level, which is the clinically meaningful version of the claim.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, language, adaptive or severity measure is reported for any participant. The absence is more consequential here than in most studies because the paper's opening claim is explicitly about clinical gradation: 'in children with ASD, these patterns change with intellectual and social impairments, suggesting that patterns of social attention provide indices of clinically meaningful variation in ASD'. That is a claim about the relationship between looking patterns and intellectual and symptom severity, and the study collects no data with which to examine it. What it substitutes is demographic stratification - age and sex - which are sources of variation in autism but are not the clinically meaningful ones the abstract invokes. The result is a study framed around parsing heterogeneity that measures none of the clinical variables by which heterogeneity is defined, and which therefore cannot distinguish a scan-path difference that indexes symptom severity from one that indexes being a twelve-year-old rather than a three-year-old.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: CARS scores are available and reported at the sample level - mean 32.97, median 34.50 - which makes this the only reuse of this dataset in the corpus to carry any severity information at all. That is a genuine asset and it is entirely unused: no analysis relates CARS to model output, no within-autism severity gradient is examined, and no check is made on whether misclassified images belong to less severely affected children. The omission is more conspicuous because the paper's own introduction sets up exactly this question, noting that 'an atypical preference for geometric images can serve as an early indicator of a specific subtype of autism spectrum disorder, which is linked to more severe symptoms', and that comorbid ADHD alters fixation durations on faces. Both observations invite a severity or subtype analysis on data the study already holds. No cognitive, language or adaptive measure is available for any participant.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: No autism severity measure exists in the records, and no cognitive, language or adaptive standardised score is available - the well-baby protocol records milestone attainment as pass or fail rather than scaled scores. What the study does have, and uses well, is a proxy for general developmental concern that sits outside the model: referral for extensive developmental assessment due to developmental delay. Because this variable was deliberately excluded from the feature set, it functions as an independent check, and children flagged high risk proved 3.29 times more likely to have been referred (95% CI 3.18-3.39). That is a genuinely informative use of an available clinical variable and it partially answers the question of what the false positives are: many are children whom clinicians independently identified as developmentally concerning. The absence of severity data nonetheless means nothing can be said about which autistic children the model detects - whether the 75% captured differ in presentation from the 25% missed, and whether the model is better at flagging children with co-occurring language or motor delay than those with a more isolated social presentation. Given that four of the seven top milestone predictors are language milestones, the second possibility is live and untested.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: None, and none is possible. No severity, cognitive, language or adaptive information exists for any image, so nothing can be said about which autistic children the model would detect. The study's proposal - a mobile application for families - would be applied to individual children about whom the model has no information beyond a photograph, and no analysis addresses how the system would behave across the range of presentations, ages, ethnicities or image qualities it would encounter.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: Present in more detail than anywhere else in this review - ADOS total and communication subscale, ADOS-Gotham severity, ADI-R social and verbal domain totals, SRS raw total - and used exclusively as predictors. No analysis relates the model's output probability to any severity score, which is precisely the validation this review has repeatedly found missing where the data would support it and which this dataset would support better than any other. A study holding both a continuous severity measure and a model probability, and choosing to feed the first into the second rather than to correlate them, forgoes the one analysis that could have distinguished a graded biological signal from a reproduction of the clinical judgement.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Non-verbal cognitive ability was measured with Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices in both groups and functions both as an eligibility gate (at least average non-verbal intelligence) and as a reported demographic, where it emerges as the one significant group difference. No autism severity measure of any kind was obtained, and no language or adaptive measure is reported. The consequence is specific to this study's construct: the introduction states that interpersonal coordination 'has been found to be closely correlated with social cognition and autistic traits', so a severity or trait measure would have allowed the central question to be asked dimensionally - whether coordination scales with autistic traits within the group - rather than only categorically. The authors name the absence of severity variation as a limitation, which is an acknowledgement that the sample is narrow rather than that the measure is missing. As with the companion paper on this cohort, the requirement of at least average non-verbal intelligence and of conversational competence means the autistic sample is a cognitively able, verbal slice of the population.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Extensive for the autistic group and absent for the comparison group. Available and reported: ADOS-2 Module 3 (6.93 +/- 1.38) and Module 4 (11.42 +/- 3.55) totals; SRS-2 total 85.53 +/- 9.00, indicating substantial social-communication difficulty; AQ 36.64 +/- 8.04, above the usual screening threshold; Vineland-II adaptive composite 64.83 +/- 22.53, well below the normative mean and with a very wide spread; PARS-TR 13.54 +/- 6.27 for preschool items and 24.30 +/- 11.49 for adolescent and adult items; and full-scale IQ from WISC-IV (81.22 +/- 14.42) or WAIS-III (91.33 +/- 20.12). Taken together these characterise a sample with average-to-borderline cognitive ability, marked adaptive-functioning impairment and clear social-communication difficulty - a genuinely informative clinical picture, and one that positions this cohort quite differently from the high-functioning verbal samples that dominate the rest of the review. Two things are not done with this material. None of it is related to model output, so the natural questions - whether linguistic distinctiveness scales with SRS-2 or AQ score, whether misclassified participants have lower ADOS-2 totals - are unasked despite the data being in hand. And no equivalent measure exists for the comparison group, so the severity information cannot be used to characterise the contrast, only one side of it.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: None, and none is possible. No severity, cognitive, language or adaptive information exists for any image.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists, and none could, since no clinical population was studied.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: None for either group. No IQ, developmental quotient, language, adaptive or severity measure was obtained, and the paper says so implicitly by describing the autistic group's functioning as inferred from their ability to use a tablet. The absence has two specific costs in this design. Because the outcome is fine motor kinematics in 3-6 year olds and neither group was assessed developmentally, the difference between groups cannot be attributed to autism rather than to general developmental level - and the autistic group's much wider age spread makes this more rather than less pressing. And because the autistic group is described as covering 'a range of symptom severity levels within the spectrum' without any score, the natural question of whether the model's confidence tracks severity cannot be asked, even though the study's simulation methodology is well suited to it.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, language or adaptive measure exists, and the binary target does not distinguish autism from sensory processing disorder, let alone grade either.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None used as an outcome, although one is present. The 'result' field in these datasets is the summed A1-A10 score - a continuous screening total that could have supported a graded analysis - and it is retained as a model input rather than examined as a severity dimension. No cognitive, adaptive, language or clinical measure exists for any respondent.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: The SRS-2 total score is the study's only clinical measure, and it serves three roles - defining the groups, characterising them (69.79 +/- 23.66 against 31.24 +/- 11.48), and, most valuably, functioning as a continuous validity check. The authors correlate SRS-2 total with the model's predicted probability of high-trait membership for each of the three variable sets and report a positive relationship in every case. This is the analysis most studies in this corpus fail to perform even when the data are available: it tests whether the model's output tracks the underlying trait dimension or merely reproduces the imposed dichotomy, and a positive continuous relationship is evidence for the former. The authors also identify the natural extension, stating that they 'intend to consider developing a continuous SRS score prediction model as a next step' - which would convert a screening classifier into a trait-estimation instrument. No cognitive, language, adaptive or motor-development measure was obtained for any child.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, severity, adaptive or language measure exists for any image in either corpus, and none could, given how the data were assembled. The introduction cites literature relating intercanthal distance and facial midline height to autism severity, which would make a severity analysis the natural test of whether the model has learned anything morphological - but no severity data exist to run it against, and the point is not raised.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any participant, so no gradient analysis is possible and the models' outputs can be related only to group membership.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: CARS-2 total is the only clinical measure and it does three jobs: it corroborates diagnosis, it gates inclusion at a score of 30, and it characterises the groups (median 37.0, IQR 33.5-41.5 against 15.0, IQR 15.0-15.5; Z = -13.90, p < 0.001). What it is not used for is the analysis that the data would support and that this review has repeatedly found missing: relating CARS-2 to the model's predicted probability. That correlation would test whether the nomogram tracks a continuous severity dimension or only the group boundary, and it is a stronger validity check than any of the internal statistics reported. No cognitive, adaptive or language measure was obtained for either group, and no developmental level was recorded - which, in a study whose predictors are quantities of object play across ages 1 to 6, leaves developmental maturity as an unmeasured competitor to the autism explanation.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: The most thorough severity characterisation in the review, and it is used to answer a question rather than to describe the sample. The Autism Spectrum Quotient was administered to both groups as a self-report measure of autistic traits. The schizophrenia group additionally received PANSS across all four scales, DIEPSS, antipsychotic dosage in chlorpromazine equivalents, age at onset and duration of illness. These measures then carry the study's explanatory finding. All ADOS-2 domains and totals from both algorithms correlated positively with the PANSS negative scale in the schizophrenia group, with strong correlations for the original algorithm's social domain and the revised algorithm's total. Schizophrenia participants meeting the autism cut-offs had substantially higher negative-scale scores than those who did not - 27.61 against 18.36 on the original algorithm (p < 0.001) and 26.29 against 18.37 on the revised - while the positive and general psychopathology scales did not differ. And logistic regression entering all variables that differed between cut-off-positive and cut-off-negative subgroups found that cut-off positivity was predicted by the PANSS negative scale score alone. The conclusion is specific and important: what the ADOS-2 detects in adults with schizophrenia is negative-symptom severity, not autism. This is the kind of construct-validity analysis that this review has repeatedly found missing from studies whose severity data would have supported it, performed here on the group where it matters most.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, language or adaptive measure is available in either corpus as used here. De-Enigma carries additional annotations for emotion, autistic behaviour and non-verbal vocalisation type, which the authors explicitly set aside as outside their focus - and among these, the autistic-behaviour annotation would have permitted exactly the severity-gradient analysis this review has repeatedly found missing. The four-class diagnosis task partially substitutes for a severity measure by requiring differentiation among clinical categories rather than only from typical development, which is more informative than any single-group severity correlation would have been.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any user, and none could without linking to clinical records. The corpus retains rich behavioural metadata - account age, friend and follower counts, reply, retweet and like counts, posting source, timestamps - which the authors note could support network or statistical analysis but deliberately do not use. Some of these would function as crude proxies for social engagement and could have supported a gradient analysis of the kind this review has repeatedly found missing; the paper's decision not to pursue them is consistent with its overall restraint about extracting more from the data than it collected consent for.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: ADOS-2 item scores across all 27 items are available and are used analytically rather than descriptively, which is the study's most valuable methodological choice on this axis. Rather than reporting group means and moving on, the authors fit random regression forests with the 27 items as predictors and each network's prediction confidence as the outcome, then calibrate a third model so that the two modalities' importance estimates can be compared on a common scale. This asks - and partly answers - the question this review has repeatedly found unasked: what is the model actually responding to, expressed in clinical terms. The answer for the video model is a coherent nonverbal social-communication cluster (initiation of joint attention, quality of social overtures, unusual eye contact, pointing gestures). The answer for the audio model is not a vocal cluster at all (showing behaviour, pointing gesture, unusual sensory exploration, hand mannerisms), which the authors read as evidence that ambient non-vocal sound contributed to classification. No cognitive or adaptive severity measure is reported in the main text.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists. The study's own contribution on this axis is a new continuous affect layer - arousal and valence values for SSBD frames, produced by five trained annotators using continuous rating software with a mouse, keyboard or joystick, on a 0 to 5 scale, normalised to the -1 to 1 range for comparability with published work, with the per-frame values averaged across raters and an inter-annotator correlation matrix reported. This is a genuine measurement contribution and the authors subject it to the sharpest self-criticism in the paper: the annotators 'are not experts in affect and emotion estimation. Therefore, it is impossible to confirm that the information gathered is accurate'; averaging 'is subject to the annotators' reaction times', so that an inattentive rater's lag propagates into the label; and simple averaging 'does not deal with disagreements either'. The stated ambition of automated severity-level assessment, which would 'alert clinicians and parents when aggravation occurs', is not realised - affect level is not severity, and no severity data exist to validate against. The annotations themselves are not released, since the authors do not have permission to share data.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: The three-level severity grade is the study's only clinical variable, it is the classification target, and its derivation is unstated - so the study has a severity measure in the sense that it predicts one, and none in the sense that it validates against anything documented. No cognitive, adaptive, language or behavioural instrument is reported as administered, and no continuous score is available against which the predicted probability could be correlated. This is the more striking because the study's own rationale is a severity-measurement argument, and a good one: the ABC takes about 15 minutes and 'does not capture the full range of daily behavioral variations in children', so a measure that samples continuously across a school day would in principle capture something a single sitting cannot. That argument is the strongest case for continuous behavioural monitoring anywhere in this review. But the study cannot demonstrate it, because it trains against labels that must themselves have come from a brief assessment of exactly the kind it criticises, and it never examines whether its predictions vary within a child across the day - which is the analysis its own thesis calls for and which its four-setting, multi-image-per-child data would support.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any image, and none is possible from a web-assembled corpus.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists independently of the modelled features - and this absence is the study's central interpretive problem rather than a routine gap. Mean length of utterance is the single most important predictor in both feature-importance analyses, and MLU is one of the oldest and best-established indices of expressive language development in child language research. Autistic children in this age range frequently have language delay, so a model whose leading feature is MLU may be detecting delayed expressive language rather than autism. Distinguishing the two requires an independent measure of language ability, which the archived transcripts do not supply here and which the paper does not seek. The point is sharpened by the paper's own demographic analysis: it reports that MLU is 'the only feature that consistently significantly increased with age', so the top predictor is simultaneously a developmental index and a diagnostic one, in a sample whose age composition by diagnostic group is not reported.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: None used. The Gait Fullbody Dataset includes a subset of nine children with severe symptoms, and the paper's methodology section states that the architecture is proposed 'for ASD detection and severity assessment' - but no severity analysis is performed, no result for the severe subset is reported, and severity appears nowhere in the results. DREAM's three-level labelling likewise encodes a gradient that is collapsed by discarding one class. No cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for either corpus.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: GARS-2 was administered to every autistic child as the first step of the diagnostic process, so a quantified severity measure exists in the source data - and no score is reported, no group summary is given, and no analysis relates severity to any acoustic feature or to the model's output. That is the analysis this review has repeatedly found missing where the data would support it, and here the data plainly do: correlating jitter, shimmer or harmonics-to-noise ratio with GARS-2 total would test whether the acoustic differences track autistic trait severity or only group membership, and would distinguish a graded biological signal from a categorical artefact. No cognitive, language or adaptive measure is available for either group.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: None used as an outcome. The 'result' field is the summed AQ-10 score - a continuous screening total that could have supported a graded analysis - and it appears among the predictors rather than as a severity dimension. No cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure is reported for either group, so no gradient analysis is possible and the model's output cannot be related to anything other than group membership. The protocol includes conversational prompts, so verbal ability was engaged in producing the data without being measured.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any image. The GELOPH<15>, which would have supplied a continuous gelotophobia score, was not administered to anyone.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any image.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any image in either corpus.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: None. No severity, cognitive, adaptive or language measure exists for any image.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: CARS_Score is present in the data but is never reported as a participant characteristic - no mean, no range, no distribution by group. Instead it is consumed as a model input feature. No IQ, developmental quotient, adaptive-behaviour, language or comorbidity measure is reported for any participant.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental quotient, adaptive behaviour, language level or ASD severity measure. Q-CHAT-10 score is present but is the label's source. Comorbid neurological conditions were an exclusion criterion, so no comorbidity data exist.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, adaptive, language or severity measure - none is derivable from a photograph, and none is discussed as missing.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: CARS is the only reported measure, and it is the label rather than a covariate. The Gesell Developmental Scale is named but never reported. No IQ, adaptive-behaviour, language or comorbidity data.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, adaptive, language or severity measure, and none obtainable from photographs.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: None. No IQ, adaptive behaviour, language, severity or comorbidity measure of any kind.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: None. No IQ, developmental, adaptive or language measure, and no autism severity instrument. Intellectual disability appears only as an exclusion criterion.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, developmental, adaptive, language or severity measure is available in the dataset or reported.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: No validated cognitive, adaptive, language or severity measure. The Q-CHAT-10 total is repurposed as a severity index in Phase II, binning children into five severity levels. Q-CHAT-10 is a binary screening instrument with a single cut-off; it was neither designed nor validated to grade severity, and using its total as a severity scale is an unsupported extension that Phase II then rests on entirely.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: None. No cognitive, adaptive, language or severity instrument. The Qchat-10-Score total appears as a predictor in two feature subsets rather than as a participant characteristic.
