answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: The stated goal is to overcome the failure of 2D face scans and eye tracking to capture subtle facial asymmetries by performing 3D facial landmark localisation with a CNN plus active shape appearance model, encoding inter-landmark geometry as a Euclidean graph, and classifying with Randomized-Trees-guided XGBoost. Headline findings at 500 epochs: accuracy 0.985, precision 0.975, recall 0.987, F1 0.925, AUC 0.98, detection accuracy 0.99, miss rate and fall-out both 0.07, and landmark localisation error 0.9 mm. The central problem is that the premise and the data do not meet: the entire methodological argument is about depth information that 3D scans obtain and 2D images lack, while the actual input is a Kaggle folder of 2D web photographs processed with Dlib's 2D 68-point detector at 224x224. A localisation error quoted in millimetres cannot be established from such images at all, since they carry no scale reference and no metric ground truth.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: The stated goal is to replace largely manual, unscalable eye-tracking analysis with an automated scanpath-based method that classifies autism severity into four levels, and to characterise how gaze features vary across those levels using DTW and MultiMatch similarity. Headline findings: CNN-RNN with features (x, d, y) reaches accuracy 97.00%, recall 98.24%, F1 97.04%, against GRU 92%, 2-LSTM 92%, XGBoost 80.25% and RFC 80.80%. The more interesting finding is the feature ablation: velocity contributes least, and the authors conclude that it is the continuous attention process, as opposed to the transition phases, that reflects atypical visual behaviour - with differences concentrated in attention duration and vertical gaze distribution.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: The stated goal is to distinguish facial images of individuals with ASD from normal controls with an ensemble pipeline: Gabor filtering, MobileNetV2 feature extraction, an ensemble of LSTM, deep belief network and hybrid-kernel extreme learning machine, and Crested Porcupine Optimizer hyperparameter selection. Headline findings: average accuracy 96.43%, precision 96.44%, recall 96.43%, F-score 96.43% and G-measure 96.43% at 1,000 epochs, against literature-quoted comparators between 89.55% and 92.64%. The Gabor ablation - the paper's one genuinely executed experiment - gives 96.43% with filtering against 92.80% without, at less than half the training time.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: The stated goal is a secure, privacy-preserving ASD diagnostic framework combining multimodal kinematic and eye-movement data, deep neural networks, federated learning with FedAvg, and SHAP-based explanation, evaluated in two scenarios (all features versus SHAP-selected features) across three clients and three rounds. The reported headline is that L_General gives the best results with an accuracy of 99.99% and F1 of 99.99%, described as flawless classification performance. The substantive finding, once the tables are read, is different and more interesting: performance is wildly unstable. Across the four feature subsets and three clients, accuracies in the all-features scenario range from 0.01 to 0.88, and SHAP-based feature selection helps some client-subset combinations and badly hurts others (Client 2 on K_General rises from 0.22 to 0.66 while Client 2 on K_Attention falls from 0.55 to 0.33). The paper reports this variability but attributes it to data heterogeneity rather than to the estimator's variance at n=9.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: The stated goal is to address the limited variation and representativeness of existing autism facial-image datasets by building a new dataset with broader variation in facial characteristics, lighting and social context, and to refine a CNN classifier on it. Headline findings: accuracy 0.90, precision 0.92, recall 0.88, F1 0.90 on 102 test images, with 47 and 45 correct classifications against 4 false positives and 6 false negatives. The conclusion attributes the result principally to the choice of a 1:1 aspect ratio and 224x224 image size, which is a claim about preprocessing conventions rather than about autism.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: The stated goal is to improve early ASD detection for toddlers aged 12-36 months by combining chi-square feature selection with six machine learning classifiers, SVM-SMOTE balancing, Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation and SHAP explanation, claimed as the first study to combine all four. Headline findings: chi-square selection improved every classifier (DT 0.938 to 0.969, KNN 0.959 to 0.973, LGBM 0.976 to 0.980, ET 0.986 to 0.990, MLP 0.993 to 0.997), and SVM reached 1.000 on accuracy, precision, recall and F1 both before and after selection, with all 292 test cases classified correctly - zero false positives and zero false negatives, reported as 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity and as confirming suitability for reliable clinical screening applications.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Two goals. Phase I: identify ASD from merged toddler screening data using seven classifiers plus a proposed RF-XG voting ensemble, under three feature-selection schemes. Phase II: recommend an appropriate teaching method for each child from their physical, verbal and behavioural performance. Headline findings: RF-XG reaches 0.94 on original features, 0.92 with Bi-Directional Elimination, 0.98 with Boruta and 0.99 with ML-based feature selection; 10-fold cross-validation averages 0.986; and Phase II predicts the teaching-method label at 0.9917. The comparison table separately claims 99.99%, a number that appears in none of the results tables and exceeds every figure the study actually reports.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: The stated goal is to identify a minimal feature subset for ASD trait screening in toddlers through systematic feature selection and hyperparameter tuning, and to map Q1-Q10 and the Q-CHAT total onto DSM-5 behavioural domains. Headline findings: using Q1-Q10 alone (a 41% feature reduction) gives the best performance across all classifiers, with the LR-KNN ensemble at accuracy 0.99, precision 1.00, specificity 1.00 and MCC 0.98, followed by ANN 0.98, LR 0.97 and KNN 0.94. Q9, Q6 and Q5 rank consistently highest across chi-squared, tree-importance and correlation methods; Q8 and Q10 lowest.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: The stated goal is to evaluate whether machine learning on self-reported camouflaging behaviours can predict dimensional autistic traits and anxiety/depression symptoms, and whether knowing a person's gender or autism diagnosis improves that prediction. Headline findings: correlations between true and predicted scores of R=.85 for Aloofness, .82 for Pragmatics and .75 for Rigidity (strong by the pre-specified Colton criterion), against .58 for Depression and .54 for Anxiety (moderate); and adding gender and/or diagnosis changes R by at most .03, from which the authors conclude that this information is already implicit in the camouflaging items. The stated implication is a possible screening aid for people whose autistic traits are masked or subthreshold and whose diagnosis is unclear or not yet established, regardless of gender identity.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: The stated goal is to overcome the limitations of prior facial-image ASD classifiers - computational cost, pose sensitivity, poor generalisation across demographics - with HyVit-ASD, a hybrid combining a pre-trained ResNet convolutional block, a pre-trained ViT with a custom residual ReAttention mechanism, and an Attention-Based Augmentation Layer. Headline findings: test accuracy 91%, sensitivity 94%, specificity 88%, AUC 95.67%, F-measure 90.99%, G-mean 90.95%, fall-out 0.12, miss rate 0.06, against six models the authors fitted (71-80% validation accuracy) and five literature figures on the same corpus (68-90%).

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: The stated goal is to make facial-image ASD screening robust to poor image quality by adding a deblurring stage and a joint denoising-classification network with metaheuristic parameter tuning. Headline findings: accuracy 96.94%, precision 97.28%, recall 96.62%, F-measure 96.95%, against five literature figures between 92.0% and 96.63%; and, for the deblurring stage, 91.22% blur removed with PSNR 32.75 dB and SSIM 0.96 against Deepblur, Wiener filtering and blind deconvolution.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: The stated goal is to combine explainable AI with a rigorous, clinically guided preprocessing pipeline to make ML-based ASD diagnosis both accurate and interpretable, and to provide practical R-based guidelines for non-expert clinicians. Headline findings: under 10-fold cross-validation the neural network reached accuracy, precision, recall and F1 of exactly 1.0000, with GBM and XGBoost at 0.9984 and logistic regression at 0.9858; Wilcoxon and Friedman tests confirmed significant differences between models; and PFI, LIME and SHAP all identified the A1-A10 behavioural items as dominant with demographic variables contributing little.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: The stated aim is to apply explainable machine learning to eye-tracking data from a social attention task in children with ASD, DLD and typical development, to assess classification accuracy across all group combinations and to identify which variables best differentiate the groups. Headline findings: F1 0.912 for DLD versus TD, 0.88 for pooled ASD+DLD versus TD, 0.86 for ASD versus TD, and 0.63 for ASD versus DLD; broad social versus non-social areas of interest carried the signal while finer decompositions by facial region and emotion did not improve accuracy; naive Bayes and logistic model trees performed best; and mean duration of visits to objects emerged as a candidate disorder-specific marker.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: The stated goal is to automate ASD categorisation from eye-tracking data using deep learning, in response to the cost, delay and subjectivity of conventional assessment. Headline findings: MobileNet reached 100% accuracy with perfect precision, recall and F1 for both classes and ROC 100%; VGG19 92%; DenseNet169 78%; the proposed model is ranked above three prior studies on the same dataset (87%, 90%, 79%). The paper attributes its advantage explicitly to preprocessing - our model achieved high accuracy because we have used a different preprocessing approach from improving dataset.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: The stated goal is a hybrid deep-learning method for ASD detection in three stages: Yeo-Johnson transformation to remove noise and artefacts, DeSEHO (Double Exponential Smoothing integrated into the Elk Herd Optimizer) for feature selection, and MEResNeXt (Moments Embedding Network combined with ResNeXt) for classification. Headline findings: accuracy 95.3%, sensitivity 96.5%, specificity 94.8%, described as performing better than traditional models.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Two aims, one confirmatory and one applied. First, to test directly whether autistic and parkinsonian movement resemble each other - a comparison previously possible only by juxtaposing separate studies with different designs and demographics. Second, to assess whether kinematic features can classify clinical versus non-clinical status and, within the clinical groups, ASD versus PD. Findings: autistic participants differed from both PD and controls in speed modulation and sub-movements, and from PD in reaction time; classification reached a best mean test accuracy of 0.73 for clinical versus non-clinical and 0.93 for ASD versus PD, in both cases from kinematics combined with questionnaires; and, most importantly, no kinematic feature was found to be similar between ASD and PD while also differing from controls. The anecdotal likeness between autistic and parkinsonian movement is not supported.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: The stated goal is a single-stage framework performing joint screening-level ASD identification and four-level ordinal severity stratification, under an explicitly controlled labelling paradigm, with a bidirectional LSTM as representation learner and a chaotic optimiser for training stability. Headline findings: accuracy 99.10% for toddlers, 97.10% children, 98.50% adolescents and 98.10% adults with AUROC above 0.99, a 3-6 point gain over the authors' own baselines (SVM 0.911, logistic regression 0.902, random forest 0.928, MLP 0.944, unidirectional LSTM 0.932). The framing of these results is the study's distinguishing feature: they are presented as evidence of the model's effectiveness in approximating a deterministic behavioural severity-scoring function rather than independent clinical diagnostic performance.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: The stated goal is a machine-unlearning-integrated explainable AI framework for early ASD and brain-disability detection in newborns, motivated by a genuinely important argument: once a newborn's data is used in training, most models provide no mechanism to remove it if parents withdraw consent, which raises ethical and legal problems under GDPR and HIPAA. Headline findings: a 23% reduction in error rates, reduced false positives, accuracy improved to 98%, and reduced processing time. The results are described as simulation results.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: The stated goal is to classify four behaviour categories - arm flapping, spinning, head banging and normal behaviour - from naturalistic, unstructured video, using a CNN-GRU architecture, in order to help clinicians monitor behavioural trends. Headline findings: CNN-GRU reaches k-fold accuracy 0.9294 +/- 0.0038 and validation accuracy 0.96, outperforming MobileNet (0.9193), 3D-CNN+LSTM (0.8912), EfficientNet-B7 (0.8808) and VGG16, with paired t-tests significant against all four at a corrected threshold of 0.0125. Per class, the two clearly distinct repetitive behaviours (arm flapping, head banging) reach F1 0.98 while spinning and normal behaviour reach 0.94 and 0.93.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: The stated goal is to investigate eye-tracking-based ASD detection during audio-visual storytelling using traditional but explainable machine learning, and to identify which gaze features and which phases of speech carry discriminative information. Headline findings: best performance 64.1% F1 and 64.5% AUC (logistic regression, audio-visual speech phase); around 55% F1 in the speech phase across both modalities; a statistically significant advantage for audio-visual over audio-only stimuli in the pre-speech phase but not during or after speech; and convergent feature-importance and SHAP evidence that mouth fixation time and revisits across facial areas of interest are the most informative features. The abstract states in its second-to-last sentence that performance remains modest.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: The stated goal is an ensemble framework that is both accurate and interpretable enough for clinicians to trust, evaluated on a behavioural dataset and a multimodal one. Headline findings: 97.6% accuracy on behavioural data from a regularised neural network (ROC-AUC 0.998) and 98.2% on multimodal data, with all other models above 93%; and an ablation showing accuracy rising from 89.40% (no feature selection, no resampling) through feature selection, SMOTE and ensemble fusion to 97.60% with neural-network regularisation.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: The stated goal is to test whether online performance-based measures can predict adult autism diagnosis, whether they add to the most widely used screening questionnaire, and which behavioural variables carry the predictive signal. Headline findings on the age- and gender-matched sample: objective task measures alone reach 74% accuracy (sensitivity 69.2%, specificity 79.2%, F1 73.5%); the AQ alone reaches 83%; the two combined reach 92%. On the unmatched full sample the objective measures reach 81.8%, which the paper states is inflated by including age and gender as features. A label-randomised control performs at chance. Several variables with no significant group difference under Bonferroni correction nevertheless contributed predictive value in combination.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: The stated goal is a hybrid ensemble integrating bagging, boosting and stacking that operates directly on raw scanpath features rather than on scanpath images, so as to reduce preprocessing overhead and improve interpretability for real-time screening. Headline findings: the stacking ensemble reached accuracy 0.9600 (SD 0.0800), precision 0.9750, recall 0.9500 and F1 0.9524, above every base learner (AdaBoost 0.9267, KNN 0.8867, random forest 0.8533, decision tree 0.8200, gradient boosting 0.7800), and comparable to image-based deep learning models on the same dataset at a fraction of the preprocessing cost.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: The stated goal is real-time ASD screening from facial images using object detection, with YOLOv8n compared against YOLOv9c to identify the more effective solution. Headline findings: YOLOv8n reached precision 91.95%, recall 92.77%, F1 92.36% and mAP@0.5 94.76%, against YOLOv9c at 91.29%, 90.29%, 90.79% and 93.32%; YOLOv8n showed higher true-positive rates for both classes with fewer misclassifications into the Background class; and, in an out-of-distribution probe, YOLOv8n rejected non-human inputs while YOLOv9c classified a dog as Autistic and a leaf as Nonautistic.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: The stated goal is a computationally efficient, privacy-preserving and optimised framework for ASD detection from facial images, combining Gaussian Gabor filtering, fused deep features from VGG16, DenseNet-121 and XceptionNet, a wavelet neural network classifier tuned by the chimp optimisation algorithm, and Grad-CAM++ for visual interpretation. Headline findings: average accuracy 98.42% with precision 98.40%, recall 98.42%, F-measure 98.41% and AUC 98.42% in the 30% testing phase, against quoted comparators from 92.10% to 97.76%.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: The stated goal is objective classification of three ASD severity levels from 3D motor features, identification of the contributing motor biomarkers through SHAP, and evaluation across multiple validation strategies. Headline findings: 84.6 +/- 10.9% accuracy under 5-fold cross-validation and 86.4% on the held-out sets; 100% on the severe class (4 of 4) with a 95% confidence interval of 39.8% to 100.0%; and wrist movements, knee trajectories and elbow-to-foot distances as the leading biomarkers. The abstract itself states that the severe-class result is a methodological proof-of-concept rather than clinical validation because the severe features were synthetically generated.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: The stated goal is to test whether privacy-preserving machine learning on speech transcripts can screen for ASD, on the argument that structured text avoids identifiable biometric data such as raw audio or video. Headline findings: ROC-AUC 0.93 on Nadig and 0.87 on Eigsti binary with logistic regression, approximately 0.96 on the merged data with TabNet, accuracy above 86% on both binary datasets, and a four-feature model reproducing nearly the same 86%. The result the authors themselves flag as important is the three-class Eigsti task, where the best ROC-AUC falls to 0.71.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: The stated goal is a serious-game tablet application combining inclusive-design requirements with machine learning, to give educators a playful, non-invasive ASD screening aid usable inside the school day. Headline findings: random forest reached 96% accuracy, MLP, deep MLP and SVM 94%, KNN 90%, logistic regression 82% and naive Bayes lower, with learning curves showing training accuracy above validation accuracy and no abrupt decline.

questions.question_text: What is the study setting and the provenance of the data?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Clinic setting (videotaped ADOS assessments). Existing data: a subset of the ongoing Canadian Infant Sibling Study database, analysed retrospectively.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Clinical/laboratory setting at an Italian research hospital. Newly collected data (ASD group recruited over 18 months; controls via pediatricians and kindergartens); no existing dataset used.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: Clinic setting - a child and adolescent psychiatry outpatient department. Newly collected application-log data; stimuli drawn from the existing public Cohn-Kanade facial-expression database.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Laboratory eye-tracking setting. Existing data - the study is an explicitly secondary machine-learning analysis of the eye-movement dataset collected for Yi et al. (2016), which had analysed it with a conventional area-of-interest approach.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Clinic/research setting - an academic outpatient developmental neuropsychiatry program plus advertisement and advocacy-group recruitment, with instruments delivered through a computer-based program. Newly collected data; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Applied real-world settings - specialist therapeutic centres for the autism group and standard kindergartens for the controls, explicitly chosen over a university laboratory because laboratory motion-capture paradigms with reflective markers 'under the watchful gaze of curious scientists' are difficult for autistic children and may invalidate the data. Newly collected data; commercially available games were adapted with logging code.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Laboratory setting at the University of Manchester. Existing data - the study is an explicitly secondary machine-learning re-analysis of an imitation experiment previously analysed with mean-based statistics on only five kinematic parameters. Its contribution is analytic rather than new collection, though it does newly release the dataset.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: A controlled recording setting with a screen and Kinect camera, with clinical recruitment via an NHS Asperger and ADHD service. Newly collected data - the study contributes the KOMAA dataset and no existing dataset is used.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Laboratory setting - a closed recording room with ceiling-mounted cameras, deliberately arranged so parents would play as they would at home and with study personnel absent during recording. Existing data: retrospective analysis of recordings collected within the EASE (Early Autism Sweden) longitudinal high-risk sibling study.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Mixed clinic and school setting - patients recruited in two Paris university child and adolescent psychiatry departments, controls from elementary schools. Existing dataset: the Child Pathological and Emotional Speech Database (CPESD), used entirely as secondary data; no new collection.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Laboratory setting - a dedicated human motion gait analysis laboratory with force plates embedded in an instrumented walkway. Data were newly collected within a larger institutional research project but are reused here from the authors' earlier published work, so this paper is a secondary analysis of an in-house dataset rather than a new collection.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Clinic setting - the Center for Treatment of Autistic Disorders (Tehran Autism), with the robot placed in a cage and cameras positioned overhead and beside it. Newly recorded interaction data, but building directly on an existing robot-screening platform and protocol from the same research group.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Clinic setting for testing (a dark, soundproof room with fixed viewing geometry) with clinical recruitment from a hospital outpatient ward and control recruitment from a kindergarten in the same city. Newly collected data; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Home setting, and uniquely so in this corpus - devices were mailed to families and all collection occurred inside children's homes with no professional supervision, deliberately to emulate real deployment of child-specific smart devices. Newly collected data; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Laboratory setting with a controlled eye tracker and fixed viewing distance. Existing data - the eye-tracking corpus was originally collected to investigate web-searching difficulties experienced by autistic users, and the authors are explicit that 'the data used in this study was not collected with this objective in mind', treating this as a limitation on achievable accuracy.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Laboratory setting - a quiet room with fixed table and chair geometry and a standardised start posture - with clinical recruitment from a hospital child neuropsychiatry unit and control recruitment from primary schools. Newly collected data, released as the first public video dataset of ASD/TD gestures.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Laboratory setting with a chinrest, fixed viewing distance and periodic data-quality monitoring. The data were collected by the authors across two experiments, with Experiment 1 data also used in a separate publication on information extraction - disclosed transparently on the grounds that 'recruiting ASD subjects and validating their diagnoses is extremely costly'.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Clinical recruitment (hospital child psychiatry department) with laboratory-style testing on a desktop LeapMotion apparatus. Newly collected data; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Clinic/research setting at a hospital autism centre. Newly collected data; the design deliberately departs from the field's reliance on ADOS-derived or highly structured speech samples in favour of naturalistic conversation with a non-expert partner.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Mixed clinic and community setting - recruitment spanned university clinics, websites, registries, local advertising and the 2015 Minnesota State Fair, with testing at more than one location using different displays and different eye trackers. Newly collected data; the face stimuli come from the existing Cohn-Kanade database.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Home setting for data capture - parents recorded brief videos on mobile phones - combined with clinical setting for diagnosis and recruitment at a Dhaka children's hospital, and remote US-based rating. Newly collected data. The design deliberately exploits Bangladesh's 95% mobile phone subscription rate as the deployment substrate.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Setting not reported - this is entirely secondary analysis of an existing benchmark dataset (Saliency4ASD, IEEE ICME 2019 Grand Challenge), with no data collection by the authors and no description of the original acquisition conditions.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Laboratory setting - a purpose-built examination and observation suite with a two-way mirror, fixed camera position and overhead microphone, with a therapist in the room and a second therapist plus robot operator behind the mirror. Newly collected session data; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Intended clinical setting - autism centres or hospitals in Saudi Arabia, with a therapist-operated workflow. Newly collected data, though nothing about the collection setting, session structure or conditions is described.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Laboratory setting at a UK university. Newly collected data using motion tracking; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Laboratory setting - a quiet university room with white barriers to reduce visual distraction, children seated alone or on a parent's lap at approximately 60 cm. Newly collected data, with the resulting image dataset released publicly on Figshare and described in more detail in an earlier publication by the same group.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Laboratory setting with standardised lighting and fixed camera and seating geometry, but with naturalistic unscripted conversation content. The data come from an existing study on interpersonal coordination in dyadic interactions by the same group, so this is a secondary analysis for classification purposes.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Two sites, Glasgow and Gothenburg, with recruitment through NHS Greater Glasgow and Clyde Specialist Children's Services, other specialist children's centres, nurseries and schools, and via two streams for the clinical cohorts - children receiving a positive diagnosis following an NHS clinic assessment, and children already diagnosed. Multi-site international recruitment is itself a design feature aimed at the pilot's acknowledged weakness, that a sample drawn from 'a small number of specialist day-care centres in Poland' is 'prone to selection bias and site-specific effects'. The assessment is intended for use 'in the home, clinic or classroom', so the deployment envelope is broad and the trial's setting is the referral pathway rather than a research laboratory. The residual limitation, not stated, is that recruitment through specialist services and existing diagnoses means predictive value at population prevalence will still not be directly estimable.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Setting not reported - entirely secondary analysis of the Saliency4ASD benchmark. The source dataset used a Tobii T120 eye tracker with a 17-inch monitor, but no room, distance, calibration or session details are given.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Home setting - videos recorded by parents during the child's daily activities and submitted through a commercial remote assessment platform. Existing data: the NODA corpus was collected and expert-annotated by Behavior Imaging and provided to the authors, so this is secondary analysis of industry data. A manually annotated children's pose dataset was newly created by the authors for retraining the pose estimator.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: An in-clinic setup with the therapist, the robot and a caregiver all present in the room, the caregiver instructed not to help the child perform the task. The multi-person setting is what necessitates one of the pipeline's design decisions - face recognition is used specifically to 'differentiate the child's face from other faces detected and found in the scene', since a system measuring a child's gaze in a room containing two adults must first establish which face is the child's. That is a practical requirement of clinical deployment which laboratory single-subject setups do not encounter, and its explicit handling is a strength.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Setting not reported - entirely secondary analysis of the Saliency4ASD benchmark, with no description of the original acquisition conditions, viewing durations, eye tracker or calibration.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: An integrative kindergarten in Wroclaw, named in the acknowledgements. Assessing children in their own everyday setting, with a portable robot brought to them, is the deployment scenario the work envisages, so the pilot data were collected under the conditions in which the method would be used. Integrative kindergartens in Poland enrol autistic and typically developing children together, which is also the setting that would make the group's stated next step - comparison against typically developing peers - straightforward to arrange without changing anything else about the protocol.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Outpatient clinic of the Child Mental Health Research Center, Nanjing Brain Hospital Affiliated to Nanjing Medical University, with typically developing controls recruited from the Nanjing area over the same period (December 2017 onward). Prospectively registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry as ChiCTR-OPC-17011995.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Laboratory setting at a UK university. The data come from an experimental protocol previously published by the same group, so this is a machine-learning analysis of an existing behavioural dataset rather than a new collection.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: Testing was conducted in quiet classrooms at two cooperating institutions - Amy Education School in Zhengzhou for the typically developing group and Guangzhou Children's Care Center for the autistic group. System requirements were developed through repeated consultation with physicians at Hubei Maternal and Child Health Hospital, Wuhan Children's Hospital and Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center, including direct observation of how they administer the diagnostic scales.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Laboratory setting - a biomechanics laboratory with force-plate instrumentation. Newly collected data; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Laboratory setting with robots on a table and children standing or seated around it. Newly collected data from a user study; no existing dataset used.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Research centre setting at a neurodevelopmental research institute, with community and school recruitment. Data were collected as part of a wider study of imitation skills in autism, so this is a focused analysis within a larger programme rather than a standalone collection.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: Retrospective secondary analysis of audio extracted from video recordings of clinical autism diagnostic sessions conducted at Seoul National University Bundang Hospital between 2016 and 2018, under IRB approval for use of fully anonymized data from an existing study. Recording conditions are reported: two clinical rooms of stated dimensions with ambient noise around 40 dB.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Not stated. Author affiliations span Ulster University (Northern Ireland), Bangor University (Wales) and the University of Colombo (Sri Lanka), but no collection site, recruitment route, period or setting is identified, and no ethics approval or consent statement appears.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: The National Autism Research Center of Israel in Beersheba, a collaboration between Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and Soroka University Medical Center. Recording used a fixed setup in a dedicated ADOS room - an AKG CHM99 microphone 1-2 m from the child feeding a TASCAM US-16x08 interface at 44.1 kHz, downsampled to 16 kHz. Funded by the Israel Science Foundation (grant 961/14) and the BGU Research Authority, with the centre itself funded by the Israeli Ministry of Science and Technology.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: A quiet room at the University of Wolverhampton with only researcher and participant present. Autistic participants recruited through a UK autism charity and the university's Enabling Centre; controls by snowball sampling in the Birmingham area. Ethical approval obtained from the University of Wolverhampton Ethics Committee before collection began.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: A therapy room with at most two people present besides the child. Autistic participants came from the Children Rehabilitation Center at Shaanxi Rehabilitation Hospital, Xi'an; typically developing participants from mainstream Xi'an schools. Funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the China Postdoctoral Science Foundation and the Natural Science Foundation of Shaanxi Province.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: A three-surface CAVE of 4 x 4 x 3 m at the Institute for Research and Innovation in Bioengineering, Polytechnic University of Valencia. Autistic participants came from Red Cenit, a Valencia cognitive development centre; controls were recruited by a management company through family mailings. Funded by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Industry and Competitiveness ('Immersive virtual environment for the evaluation and training of children with autism spectrum disorder: T Room'), the Generalitat Valenciana REBRAND project, and ERDF Valencian Community funds.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: A standardised low-cost room setup deployed at the collaborating Third Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University, Guangzhou, with a fixed seating layout for child, clinician and parent and a single camera positioned to record the child's frontal face. Funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China, the Key Research and Development Program of Jiangsu Province, the Six Talent Peaks project and a Guangzhou municipal livelihood science and technology plan.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: Laboratory eye-tracking at Seattle Children's Research Institute and Yale University, with acquisition protocols aligned to a published multi-site standard and a delivery system providing embedded 5-point calibrations and the ability to insert video breaks for behavioural management. Funded by NIH awards K01 MH104739, R21 MH103550 and R03 MH092618, an NSF Expedition in Socially Assistive Robotics, and a Simons Foundation award.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: A shielded room for EEG recording and a separate eye-tracking station, with autistic children recruited clinically and typically developing children from a local kindergarten. Funded by the National Natural Science Foundation of China and the National Key Research and Development Program of China.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: In-lab at Stanford University, with families recruited between 25 February 2015 and 26 January 2016 through the Autism and Developmental Disabilities Research Registry, referrals to the Autism and Developmental Disabilities Clinic, the Developmental Behavioral Unit of Lucile Packard Children's Hospital, and academic presentations. Funded by NIH grants 1R01EB025025-01 and 1R21HD091500-01 plus multiple foundation and Stanford programme grants. The senior author declares founding Cognoa, a company building digital child-health solutions.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: A quiet laboratory with constant lighting at Humboldt-Universitat zu Berlin, with participants recruited through the autism outpatient clinic of Charite Universitatsmedizin Berlin. The experimenter left the room before the task began, so the participant was alone with the screen. Ethics approval from the Charite ethics committee, Helsinki conformity, written informed consent from all participants and separate consent for figure publication.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: Not stated. No collection site, period, recruitment route or ethics approval appears, because the data are secondary and their origin is never identified. All modelling was performed in Microsoft Azure Machine Learning Studio.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: The Autism Resource Center, Islamabad, with the study approved by the centre's autism specialist and director board and parental consent obtained. Two robots were placed in an arc approximately 1 m from the child, who sat for the joint attention module and stood for imitation, with a Kinect behind the robots. The authors state that the participant setting is illustrated 'to make the intervention replicable'. No external funding was received.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Laboratory eye tracking with participants recruited through the Department of Psychiatry at the University of Sao Paulo's School of Medicine, in collaboration with the School of Arts, Sciences and Humanities and the bioinformatics postgraduate programme. Funded by CNPq, FAPESP/INCT-MACC, CAPES and PRONAS/PCD. No ethics approval statement appears.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: Laboratory sessions at Tsinghua University's Shenzhen International Graduate School, with diagnosed participants recruited through the Shenzhen Autism Society. Funded by Shenzhen Humanities and Social Sciences Key Research Bases, the Guangdong Natural Science Foundation, the National Philosophy and Social Sciences Foundation of China and a Tsinghua SIGS foundation. IRB approval from the Department of Psychology, Tsinghua University (No. THUDP20) covering both experiments.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Laboratory testing at Peking University, with autistic participants recruited from a preschool specialised for autistic children in Beijing. Funded by multiple National Natural Science Foundation of China grants, an NSFC/DFG collaborative research centre, a Guangdong key project on autism diagnosis and treatment tools, and a Beijing municipal science and technology grant. No conflicts of interest declared.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Autistic participants were recruited from the Shanghai Putuo District Zhanyi Children Cultivation Service Center; no setting is stated for the comparison group and no laboratory conditions, lighting or viewing distance are described. Acknowledged support from two university research teams at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Shanghai University of Engineering Science. The first author is affiliated with a Shanghai high school.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: EEG recorded in a shielded room and eye tracking conducted subsequently; ethics approval indicates Beijing Normal University while the analysis was conducted at Wuhan University's School of Computer Science. No recruitment route, period or clinical setting is described.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: The Psychiatry Institute of the University of Sao Paulo School of Medicine, with acknowledgement to the Autism Spectrum Disorder Program of the Clinics Hospital (PROTEA-HC). Funded by CAPES and the Brazilian National Program to Support Health Care for Persons with Disabilities. Ethics approval from the School of Medicine research ethics board under protocol 17556019.8.0000.0068.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: A laboratory dyadic setup at Shenzhen University with participants seated 80 cm from the interviewer, autistic children recruited from Shenzhen Kangning Hospital's Child Psychiatry Department and comparison children from local schools. Funded by seven Shenzhen and Guangdong municipal, medical-discipline and provincial research programmes. No conflicts declared.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: Recording in an unspecified 'noise free location' using consumer audio editing software on a laptop, at two engineering colleges in Tamil Nadu. No recruitment route, clinical setting or collection period is described, and no funding or ethics information appears.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: A quiet room at the University of Picardy Jules Verne with white barriers to reduce visual distraction, in an interdisciplinary collaboration between psychology and artificial intelligence research units. Children were recruited regionally, with autistic participants diagnosed at multidisciplinary specialty clinics. Supported by a university research quality bonus; no conflicts declared.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Laboratory eye tracking with autistic participants recruited from the Psychiatry Institute of the University of Sao Paulo School of Medicine, in collaboration between computing, psychiatry and bioinformatics units. Ethics approval from the University of Sao Paulo under protocol 57185516.9.0000.5390.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: A three-wall CAVE of 4 x 4 x 3 m at the Institute for Research and Innovation in Bioengineering, Polytechnic University of Valencia, with autistic participants from the Red Cenit Neurocognitive Development Center and comparison children recruited by a management company. Funded by the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Industry and Competitiveness project 'Immersive Virtual Environment for the Evaluation and Training of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder: T Room'.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: A laboratory dyadic setup at Shenzhen University with the child seated 80 cm from a 33-year-old female interviewer blinded to group membership and required to behave and speak identically across participants; autistic children recruited from a local psychiatric hospital, comparison children from nearby communities. Funded by seven Shenzhen and Guangdong municipal, medical-discipline and provincial programmes.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: No data collection. The source data were gathered from schools in Hauts-de-France; all analysis here was performed in Google Colaboratory using scikit-learn, by authors at institutions in Bangladesh and Australia.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Laboratory motion capture at the University of Ferrara and the Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia's Center for Translational Neurophysiology of Speech and Communication, with autistic children recruited from a local outpatient neurodevelopmental clinic and comparison children from a local kindergarten. Funded by two Italian Ministry of Health young-researcher grants and an EU H2020 project. No competing interests declared.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: An autism rehabilitation centre, with participants recruited from Al Ain Hospital - a clinical service setting, and the same setting in which the system would be deployed. That alignment between study setting and intended use setting is shared by only a few studies in this review. The clinical framing is specific: the authors note that assessment is typically performed at enrolment and repeated during long-term therapy, and that if it 'could be repeated more frequently to trace the severity and development of symptoms, then therapists could implement more efficacious diagnostic and therapeutic options' - so the setting defines the problem, which is the cost in expert time of repeated assessment.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: The Child Psychiatry Department at Mayo Hospital Lahore, described as the only government-run child psychiatry department in Pakistan and seeing on average two patients daily, together with a private school for autistic children in Lahore. Questionnaires were administered on paper at the school and via Google Forms otherwise. No setting is described for the comparison group.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: Oregon Health and Science University, with participants recruited by community outreach and referral from OHSU specialised clinics into a neuroimaging study, and speech extracted from videotaped ADOS-2 administrations conducted as part of that study's screening. IRB approval from OHSU.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Not reported. The eye-tracking sessions belong to the Saliency4ASD collection and the authors describe neither the room, the tracker, the viewing distance, nor the country. The only settings named are the two Italian universities where the analysis was performed. For a study whose entire signal is fixation duration, the absence of the acquisition sampling rate and calibration procedure is a substantive reproducibility gap rather than a formality.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Not reported for the data collection - the setting belongs to the Saliency4ASD source study. The acquisition conditions are partially restated: Tobii T120 eye tracker, 17-inch monitor, each image presented at original full resolution for 3 seconds. This is more than the companion paper on the same data provides but still omits room conditions, viewing distance, calibration procedure and sampling rate, all of which matter for a signal whose dominant discriminator turns out to be total fixation duration.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: University of Geneva, Switzerland, within an ongoing longitudinal study of early autism development. The assessments were not staged for this analysis - they are the cohort's routine clinical ADOS sessions, conducted 'in several different rooms', by 'different examiners', and 'filmed with different camera systems'. That heterogeneity is the study's most under-appreciated methodological asset: where other work in this corpus achieves high accuracy under a single fixed acquisition setup and therefore cannot distinguish diagnostic signal from site signature, here the acquisition varies within both classes, so camera, room and examiner cannot serve as proxies for group. The authors report classification robustness to this variability explicitly in supplementary analysis and treat it as evidence for generalisability rather than as noise to be apologised for.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Naples, Italy, across two different settings by group: autistic children at the Neapolisanit S.R.L. Rehabilitation Center, which provided 'the clinical ward for the experimentation' and where those children also receive ongoing psychomotor and speech therapy; comparison children at a primary school. The physical arrangement is specified precisely and identically for both - child seated at a table 65-70 cm high adjusted for age, experimenter opposite, tablet within 20 cm of the table edge - which controls posture and reach geometry, the most obvious physical determinants of drag kinematics. What is not controlled is the setting asymmetry itself. Recruiting cases from a therapy centre and comparisons from a school means group membership is entangled with familiarity with clinical assessment and with prior therapeutic exposure to fine-motor practice, either of which could shift drag dynamics independently of diagnosis.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Beijing, China. Comparison children were recruited from a local kindergarten; the autistic children came from a school site whose identity is not given and where the authors report limited access to reliable diagnostic information. Both recordings took place under controlled conditions - EEG in a quiet room with the child in an armchair usually accompanied by a caregiver, eye tracking at a fixed ~60 cm viewing distance following a five-point calibration that had to pass with small error vectors before proceeding. Recruiting the two groups from different institutional settings is a structural feature the paper does not discuss, and it carries a specific risk for the eye-tracking modality here: the stimulus is Tiger Qiao Hu, a widely broadcast Chinese children's programme, so prior familiarity with the characters could differ systematically between children in a mainstream kindergarten and children in a special-education setting, and familiarity affects where a viewer looks.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Seoul, South Korea. The clinical group came from the Child and Adolescent Psychiatry Division of Seoul National University Hospital and the comparison group from preschools - a recruitment asymmetry of the kind that elsewhere in this corpus introduces setting confounds, but mitigated here because the paradigm itself is identical for both groups and highly constrained: same quiet room arrangement, same height-adjustable chair, same 70 cm toy placement, same 45-degree examiner offset, same ten toys, same 30-second waits. The paper also states that videos 'were acquired at different locations with various background noises' and treats the model's robustness across them as evidence for generalisability - which the train-on-segmented, test-on-raw result supports more directly than the assertion alone would.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: China, with the two groups drawn from different institutional settings - special education schools for the autistic children and regular kindergartens for the comparison children. Recording conditions are described only obliquely and only in the limitations, where the authors note that 'the recording environments are changing' and that 'across-day variability exists in recording conditions'. That acknowledgement is candid but incomplete: if recording conditions varied across days and the two groups were recruited from different institutions, sessions may have been clustered by group, in which case environmental variation is partially confounded with diagnosis. The paper does not report whether recordings were interleaved across groups.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Not reported. The recordings belong to the source dataset and the paper describes neither the room, the country, the recruitment route nor the acquisition protocol. The only setting information is the hardware on which the experiments were computed - an AMD Ryzen 7 2700X with 16 GB RAM, a GTX 1050 Ti and a 250 GB SSD - which is specified more precisely than anything about the children.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Two independent sites - Caltech and Indiana University - using 'otherwise identical eye trackers and video stimuli', with the two-site design adopted explicitly 'to optimize generalizability'. Recruitment was through flyers distributed at outpatient treatment programmes, community support groups and community locations including college campuses and YMCAs, so the sample is community-recruited rather than clinic-referred - which matters for representativeness, though the authors note the sample 'is not representative of ASD in general'. Site membership is carried through the analysis and displayed in every figure by marker shape, so site effects remain visible rather than being pooled away. This is the only multi-site study in the corpus.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Participants' own homes, with no researcher present, no controlled acoustics and no equipment standardisation - the design's defining property and its explicit purpose. The authors' argument is twofold and both parts are worth noting. Logistically, prior speech studies used directional microphone arrays or multiple wireless microphones at a hospital, which 'pos[es] significant barriers to the widespread availability of automatic diagnosis tools', reinforced by the observation that 83.86% of American counties have no autism diagnostic resources at all and that the delay from first consultation to diagnosis averages over two years. Behaviourally, the authors argue that 'interacting with unknown adults in foreign environments could be stressful and possibly affect the behavior of children with autism, thus leading to observations that are not generalizable to the real world' - a validity argument for home recording rather than merely a convenience one. The consequence embraced rather than lamented is heterogeneous audio quality, which the paper treats as fidelity to deployment conditions.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Oregon Health & Science University, with participants recruited through community outreach and referral from OHSU specialty clinics into an fMRI study - so the sample is a research cohort rather than a consecutive clinical series. Recording arrangements are described precisely and with their rationale: 'The microphone was suspended in a cage and placed on a table approximately 3 feet from where the child sat. This allowed the recording to accurately capture the child's language, even if, as is common in ADOS Module 3 administrations, the child sometimes moved around the room before being reminded to sit down.' That sentence does two things few papers here manage - it specifies the acquisition geometry and it explains the specific behaviour the geometry was designed to accommodate. The authors nonetheless flag microphone quality and placement as insufficiently controlled and recommend tightening it in future work to reduce reliance on denoising.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Four Duke pediatric primary care clinics during routine well-child checkups - the only truly point-of-care setting in the corpus. The description of environmental control is unusually honest: a quiet room with few distractions was identified at each clinic, but 'although it was quiet and without a lot of distraction, it was not otherwise controlled as in a laboratory setting', with the four rooms noted as similar in size, lighting and presence of distractions. The social arrangement is specified in detail and matters for the measurement: the caregiver held the child on their lap with no instructions on how to do so, sat quietly, and was asked not to guide the child's behaviour or give instructions, while siblings and the administering assistant stayed behind both caregiver and child to reduce distraction. The tablet sat on a tripod approximately 60 cm in front of the child. That the caregiver's holding is uninstructed is a deliberate choice for ecological validity and an uncontrolled source of variance for a measure of postural movement.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Two sites in different countries with different recruitment routes - a research setting in the United States, where participants came from an established family-genetic study of autism, and community recruitment in Hong Kong through social media, schools, autism organisations and employment programmes. The recording setting itself is described minimally: pages presented on a computer monitor with narration audio recorded, and no information about room, microphone, distance or recording equipment in either site. For a study whose primary features are the amplitude envelope and its spectral structure, the absence of any acoustic-recording specification is a genuine reproducibility gap, and it is compounded by the two-site design: if recording conditions differed systematically between the United States and Hong Kong, that difference would be absorbed into the envelope features. The combined-language model would be sensitive to this, though the fact that rhythm classification succeeds within each language separately - where recording conditions are presumably homogeneous - substantially mitigates the concern.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Poland, with participants contacted through a university clinic, diagnostic or therapeutic centres, or schools, and assessed as part of a research evaluation. The narratives themselves come from ADOS-2 administrations conducted by research-reliable clinicians, so the elicitation context is a standardised clinical assessment rather than a naturalistic setting. This has the same double edge noted in the OHSU studies: the standardisation makes narratives comparable across participants and the data are a by-product of an assessment already being conducted, but the assessment is specifically designed to elicit autism-related behaviour, so performance may not transfer to spontaneous narration. The authors raise the related point about narrative context, citing evidence that 'participants with ASD exhibit lower performance in less structured tasks (i.e., narratives of personal experiences, conversation) than more structured picture book tasks' - which implies, though the authors do not draw the inference explicitly, that a less structured elicitation might yield stronger rather than weaker classification.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: A purpose-built eye-tracking laboratory at a university research centre for children with special needs, with lighting described as optimised for tracking. The acquisition arrangement is described with the care a toddler paradigm requires: children sat approximately 60 cm from the screen either alone or on a parent's lap, screen distance and height adjusted individually, a researcher accompanying each parent-child pair throughout, a five-point calibration using a crying cartoon as the attention-catching target, and calibration repeated for each child until deviation in both x and y fell below one degree. Repeating calibration to a stated tolerance rather than accepting the first attempt is a discipline few studies here report. The setting is a controlled laboratory rather than a clinic or home, which the authors implicitly acknowledge as a limitation of the field when they call for 'less intrusive screening instruments that do not require tightly controlled environments' - a requirement their own paradigm does not yet meet.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: A hospital-based child mental health and rehabilitation centre in Shenzhen, with testing conducted in 'a dark and soundproof room' at a fixed 65 cm viewing distance with the child's centre of vision aligned to the monitor centre. This is a tightly controlled laboratory environment rather than a point-of-care setting, which suits the measurement but limits the deployment claim - a dark soundproof room with a calibrated remote tracker is not a paediatric waiting area. The recruitment asymmetry is present but mitigated: autistic children came from the hospital's rehabilitation centre while comparison children came either from a local kindergarten or from routine check-ups at the same hospital's outpatient ward, so a proportion of the comparison group was recruited within the same institution.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Fourteen sites across six US states, recruiting children 'representing a population of patients that HCPs would see in their primary care practice' - so the sampling frame is the referral population the tool is intended for, not a research cohort. The participating clinicians are equally representative: 15 physicians trained in general pediatrics or family medicine, spanning 1 to 38 years of post-residency experience, and explicitly 'not recruited on the basis of any special interest or experience of ASD diagnosis, beyond what was delivered as part of their standard training'. That last detail matters more than it might appear: a diagnostic aid evaluated only with enthusiastic autism-interested clinicians would not establish that ordinary primary care physicians can use it. Thirteen point nine percent of clinician assessments were conducted by telemedicine rather than in person, with 'no evidence of performance degradation' when done remotely - an incidental finding produced by the COVID-19 disruption that speaks directly to rural and low-access deployment.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Two entirely different settings, and this is the study's defining problem. Autistic children were recorded in June 2019 by a designated speech therapist, in the room where they usually play, during a session that 'started with activities generally done during the treatment session so the child would act in the most spontaneous way', with 'a video camera placed on a tree-legged support'. Comparison children were recorded later by their own parents at home on the parents' phones, because 'due to the COVID-19 pandemic, it was impossible to collect the data in situ'. The clinical setting was designed carefully for the autistic children's comfort, which is good practice for eliciting natural speech and simultaneously guarantees a fixed, distant, uncontrolled microphone position in a room with unknown reverberation. A parent holding a phone produces a close-miked, low-noise, high-signal recording. Since the paper's entire yield is acoustic, the recording chain is not a nuisance variable but a direct competitor for every reported effect.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Not reported. The paper describes neither the room, the country, the recruitment route, the eye tracker nor the acquisition protocol for the source recordings. The only settings named are the four institutions where the analysis was carried out and the hardware on which it ran - a fifth-generation i5 processor with 8 GB RAM and a 4 GB GPU, specified more precisely than anything about the children.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Participants' own homes with no researcher present, no environmental control and no equipment standardisation - and the paper's positioning depends on this. The related-work section is unusually specific in critiquing prior computer-vision studies on precisely this point, noting that Hashemi and Chang 'controlled the room lighting and distance of the camera from the participant's face' and concluding that 'the ability of these techniques to translate to natural nonclinical environments and unstructured tasks remains to be explored'. The consequences are then reported rather than hidden: 'excessive camera movement and poor lighting conditions rendered some frames in our data set too blurry for use', and 'other adults or siblings would often join in gameplay, resulting in multiple faces in the frame'. Roughly 43% of frames were discarded by the automated quality filters. This is the most uncontrolled acquisition setting in the corpus and the paper treats that as its subject rather than as noise.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Not reported for the data collection. The literature review states, summarising the source publication, that recordings used 'an SMI RED series mobile eye tracker' while participants 'watched a series of videos to stimulate eye movement across the screen', but nothing about the room, country, recruitment or protocol is restated in the methods. The only settings named are the two analysing institutions and the compute environments - Microsoft Azure Machine Learning Studio Classic, Google Colaboratory, and a specified Dell laptop.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Participants' own homes with no researcher present, no equipment provision and no environmental control - 'this study was conducted remotely' - which is the design's entire point. The equity argument is developed at length and with specifics rather than as a gesture: prevalence is similar in rural (0.9%) and urban (1.0%) areas but rural communities face limited access to identification and intervention services; up to 80% of US counties lack sufficient diagnostic resources; and existing questionnaire-based screening 'require[s] literacy and perform[s] worse with non-white and lower education caregivers', so digitising those questionnaires 'risks exacerbating current disparities'. The proposed alternative - deriving signal from behaviour rather than from caregiver report - would in principle be insensitive to caregiver literacy, though the game itself still requires a smartphone, internet access and English.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: China, with collection organised through Anhui Medical University, the Anhui Autism Association and special education schools. The recording environment is not described in text at all - a figure is referenced showing the collection setup, but no room, distance, microphone or channel configuration is stated. This gap is not merely a reporting deficiency here but a methodological one, because time-frequency ICA is a multichannel technique: it requires at least two observation channels to separate sources, and which two signals constitute those channels determines entirely what the unmixing matrix represents. Without the recording configuration the paper's central feature construction cannot be reconstructed or evaluated.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: The ADOS examination room at a national autism research centre, with recording conditions described honestly rather than idealised: a single microphone 1-2 metres from the child, in an environment with 'background noise, reverberation, and overlapping speech', and with both child and therapist free to move during the session. The resulting average signal-to-noise ratio of child speech is reported as 12 +/- 5 dB and named as a limitation. The authors position this deliberately against better-equipped prior work, noting that another group 'applied a diarization method for speech signals using four microphones, including a beamforming algorithm that improved their recordings' SNR' and that 'even though our proposed diarization methods achieved higher DER values, we used only one distant microphone recorded in a noisy environment'. Accepting worse acquisition in exchange for deployability in an ordinary clinic room is a defensible trade and is argued as such.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: The kindergartens the children attended, with a maximum of three children assessed per visit. Both groups were assessed in the same settings under the same protocol, which removes the clinic-versus-school recruitment asymmetry that this review has documented as a confound across the photograph, audio and thermal branches. Bringing a portable robot to a child's own nursery is also the deployment scenario the work envisages, so the data were collected under the conditions in which the method would be used - a property shared with only a few studies in this corpus, notably the population-based one-legged-standing study and the routine-examination work.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
