answers.answer: Single site in Shenzhen, China. Autistic children were recruited from a first-class mental health centre (Shenzhen Kangning Hospital / Shenzhen Mental Health Center, the affiliation of the child-psychiatry co-author); TD children came from nearby communities. The recording setting is a controlled but not screen-based one: a face-to-face structured conversation with an interviewer at a fixed 80 cm distance, with the child wearing eye-tracking glasses. This is a clinic-adjacent laboratory setting, not a naturalistic home or classroom setting and not a primary-care setting, so the recruitment path guarantees a spectrum-narrow, already-diagnosed autistic sample facing an unselected community control group - the classic case-control geometry whose accuracy does not transfer to a screening population.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Single site: an autism centre in Tehran, Iran. Children played in a 3 x 4 m room at the centre for 3-5 minutes, alone or accompanied by a parent or therapist, with a child psychologist from the centre supervising. This creates a gap between the study as conducted and the study as framed: the paper's central argument is for a home-based IoT device usable 'at homes, daycares, or clinics' in natural settings without expert involvement, and it repeatedly criticises fMRI, EEG and robot-based approaches for requiring specialised centres - yet all the reported data were collected at a specialised centre under psychologist supervision. The recruitment geometry is also the standard case-control one: an already-identified autistic group from a service setting against a typically developing comparison group, at 61% autism prevalence, which is roughly 60 times the population base rate the device is proposed to screen at.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Two sites in Campania, Italy, and the pairing is itself a confound. Autistic children came from the Neapolisanit S.R.L. Rehabilitation Center, which is also the employer of two of the four authors, and were undergoing psychomotor and speech therapy there. Typically developing children came from a mainstream primary school. Testing conditions were standardised across both groups - the same tablet, a table 65-70 cm high with the tablet within 20 cm of the edge, the examiner seated opposite, the same instruction protocol - so the acquisition chain does not differ by group in the way it does in some other studies in this corpus. But the recruitment geometry is the classic case-control one at 50% prevalence, and it carries a specific extra risk here: the autistic group's ongoing psychomotor therapy is an intervention directed precisely at the motor system whose kinematics constitute the study's entire feature set. Whether that therapy makes autistic movement more or less like typical movement, it makes the two groups differ in motor training history as well as in diagnosis.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Single site: the Department of Developmental and Behavioral Pediatrics, The First Hospital of Jilin University, Changchun, with engineering from Jilin University's School of Communication Engineering. The setting is the study's most distinctive feature and is used deliberately rather than incidentally. Recording took place during actual ADOS-2 screening sessions rather than in a purpose-built experiment, with four fixed cameras installed in the assessment room and the clinical protocol left untouched: the clinician stands where the protocol requires, calls in a natural tone, repeats and reinforces as the manual specifies, and an unspecified and varying number of parents may be present. The authors argue explicitly that this yields 'less laboratory control, more realistic child response, and a flexible number of accompanying parents', and they are right that this is the correct target distribution for a tool meant to sit inside a clinic. It also creates the engineering problem the pipeline is built to solve - the scene contains multiple adults, so person re-identification is needed simply to know which skeleton belongs to the child. The countervailing point is that the sample is a referred clinical series at a tertiary hospital with 29 of 30 children already autistic, which is the opposite of the community screening population the conclusion invokes when it proposes deployment 'in remote areas with underdeveloped medical care'.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Single-city, two-source recruitment in Tehran, with testing centralised at one laboratory. Autistic children came from the Daily Rehabilitation Clinic for Children with Special Disorders, a specialist service affiliated to the Family Institute of Shahid Beheshti University; comparison children came from Namjoo public elementary school. All eye tracking took place on one stationary system at the Faculty of Education and Psychology, Shahid Beheshti University, so unlike some studies in this corpus the acquisition chain is identical for both groups and no equipment confound arises. The recruitment geometry is nonetheless the standard clinic-versus-school case-control arrangement at 50% prevalence, and here it is compounded by asymmetric filtering: the autistic group faced five inclusion criteria and two exclusion criteria that removed 20% of those approached, while no criteria at all are stated for the school-recruited comparison group. The children who could not tolerate sitting at the computer or could not be calibrated - plausibly those with greater sensory or attentional difficulty - are precisely those absent from the analysed autistic sample.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Single site: the Center for Autism Research at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, with the University of Pennsylvania. This is a specialist research centre, and both arms of the study reflect that - the participants are a research-registry sample assessed by Clinical Best Estimate on site, and the 19 raters are the centre's own doctoral clinicians and BA-level staff. The rater sample is therefore an unusually strong human benchmark (these are people who assess autistic adults professionally) and simultaneously a narrow one (they share an institution, a training culture and, plausibly, prior exposure to similar video material). The recording setting is a laboratory room with a floor-standing dual-camera device between the two conversation partners, and the paradigm is a semi-structured assessment rather than a clinical encounter. The recruitment geometry is case-control at 35.7% prevalence with deliberately clear-cut controls, which the authors flag as the key generalisation limit. Against that, the paradigm itself is deliberately designed for scalability outside such settings: the conversation partner is a non-clinician, the interaction lasts three minutes, and the only equipment is a camera - which is the basis for the claim that this could serve as a screening procedure.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Multi-centre, and deliberately so: children were recruited from multiple hospitals and schools in Shaanxi and Fujian provinces, chosen because 'medical conditions are relatively poor' there. This is one of only a few studies in this corpus with genuine site diversity, and the framing is consistent throughout - the paper's entire motivation is that screening in remote and low-income areas is understudied, and the design constraints follow from that premise rather than being retrofitted to it. Recording took place in a therapy room with the child 0.5 m from the monitor and at most two other people present, the mother and one researcher, which is a realistic community-clinic arrangement rather than a laboratory. The counterweight is the usual one: recruitment pairs hospital- or rehabilitation-identified autistic children against school-recruited comparison children at 42% prevalence, so the geometry remains case-control and the accuracy does not transfer to a community screening population. The authors do not compute what their operating point would mean at population prevalence, which for a proposed universal screening tool is the omission that matters most.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: There is no setting in the usual sense. No participants were recruited, contacted, assessed or informed; the study consists of harvesting five years of public posts from 252 identifiable Twitter accounts through the developer API and classifying them offline. The research group is at Universidad de Leon in Spain, and the compute is a single desktop workstation. Two features of this design deserve comment for the review. It is the only study in the corpus with no acquisition protocol at all, which means it is free of every acquisition confound that troubles the video and audio studies here - no equipment differences, no examiner effects, no laboratory artificiality - and simultaneously free of every control those protocols provide, since nothing about who wrote what, when, why, or to whom is known or standardised. And it is the only study here whose data subjects are neither aware of nor consenting to their participation, on a topic they disclosed publicly about themselves, which raises governance questions the paper does not engage with at all.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Four paediatric primary care clinics in the Duke Children's Primary Care network, with data captured during routine well-child visits. This is the study's most consequential design property and it addresses the corpus's most pervasive external-validity problem. Because recruitment is by clinic attendance rather than by diagnostic status, the sample is not a set of specialist-clinic cases contrasted with community controls but a screening cohort in which autism is identified prospectively at 9.2% prevalence. The measurement is embedded in the visit rather than added to it: the child sits on the caregiver's lap, an iPad is placed at 60 cm, and the movies play for a few minutes while the front camera records. Practical constraints of the setting are reported honestly as exclusion criteria - the child was too upset, the caregiver had no time or needed to mind siblings, consent could not be given in English or Spanish - which is a realistic account of what limits deployment in primary care and is more informative than a laboratory study's silence on the same issues. The one respect in which the setting is not fully representative is socioeconomic: 82.8% of caregivers held a college degree, which is far above the US population and reflects the catchment of an academic health system.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Single-country, clinic-linked laboratory testing in Nara and Osaka, Japan, with participants recruited through the psychiatry department of Nara Medical University School of Medicine and Osaka Psychiatric Medical Center and tested on equipment at the Nara Institute of Science and Technology. The setting is a controlled screen-based assessment at a fixed 65 cm viewing distance rather than a naturalistic or point-of-care one, and no deployment scenario is proposed. Recruitment geometry is the standard clinical case-control arrangement, with the important qualification that both clinical groups come from psychiatric services and both are contrasted against the same actively screened control group, which is what makes the parallel comparison meaningful. One setting-related feature is unaddressed: the FEIT is a Western instrument and the participants are Japanese, so every trial involves other-race face processing, in a task whose entire outcome is where on a face the participant looks. Cross-cultural differences in face-scanning are well documented and the paper does not mention them.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: There is no research setting: the data are telemetry from a free commercial iPad app used by people at home and in daily life across at least three continents over two and a half years, transmitted automatically to a backend server. This is the most naturalistic dataset in the corpus by a wide margin, and the authors are right that it represents a kind of scale that conventional autism research cannot reach - approximately 200 new users per month even at the end of the app's life, and around 1,800 in the busiest month. The corresponding losses are total. Nothing about the context of any interaction is known: whether the user was communicating with a person or exploring the interface, whether a therapist was present, whether the device was being used for its intended purpose, whether the account holder was the person using the screen. The logs were not designed for research and the authors say so plainly - collected 'for developers' debugging purposes and general system usage statistics', with 'little attention... given to the data structure and representation during the app development'. So the study inherits both the reach of consumer telemetry and its complete absence of experimental control, and it is candid about the latter in a way that makes the work easier to appraise.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Multi-site in the sense that participants were drawn from across South Korea - Seoul, other metropolitan cities and self-governing provinces in equal-ish thirds - but recruitment channels differ completely by group. Autistic children came exclusively from the Child Psychiatry Outpatient Clinic of Seoul National University Hospital, described as receiving referrals of children at high risk of autism from throughout the country; comparison children came from day care centres. This is the standard case-control geometry, and here it is compounded by the deliberate selection of clinically distinct groups. The testing environment itself is standardised and low-tech - a quiet room, a height-adjustable chair, a table, a single consumer camera on a front-facing tripod - and this is presented as a feature, since the protocol is designed to be replicable without specialised equipment, calibration or trained raters. The claim that the setup is 'amenable to computer vision and DL and applicable to a wide range of neuropsychiatric conditions' is credible on the acquisition side; what it does not address is that the model was trained on children drawn from the extreme ends of a clinical distribution.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: There is no study setting: all work was performed on Google Colab using a downloaded public dataset, at Vellore Institute of Technology in India, on images collected elsewhere. No children were recruited, tested, observed or consented for this work. This matters for how the study should be weighted in the review: it contributes no new evidence about autistic children and no new data, and its value lies entirely in being an additional independent modelling attempt on a dataset that several other included studies also use - which makes it a comparison point rather than a primary source.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: No study setting: this is a computational reanalysis conducted at IIIT Delhi on transcripts collected years earlier in North American research laboratories. The three source settings are described only briefly and differ substantially - 30-minute free play sessions in one corpus, roughly 10 minutes of parent-child play in another, and natural mother-child interaction with 12-26 month olds in the third. That heterogeneity is the study's central unexamined problem, because it is not random with respect to the label: one corpus supplies autistic children exclusively. Any systematic difference between the corpora - transcription conventions, how disfluency and unintelligibility were marked, who the partner was, how long the session ran, what era the recording belongs to - is therefore partially aligned with diagnosis. Length-dependent features are normalised over conversation length, which handles the most obvious component, but transcription and partner effects are not addressable by normalisation and are not discussed.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: Described only as a naturalistic study with a battery of eye-tracking video stimuli; no site, room, equipment or procedure is given in the retrieved text. The authorship spans seven United States institutions including the Yale Child Study Center and Seattle Children's Research Institute, and the paper notes that its paradigm 'share similarities with recent studies of autism biomarker Consortium for Clinical Trials (ABC-CT)', which locates the work within a serious clinical-research programme even though the report itself supplies no setting detail. The recruitment geometry cannot be assessed because recruitment is not described.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: No study setting: a computational reanalysis at two universities in Amman, Jordan, of images collected in France. The source acquisition setting is described in more detail than in the other reuses of this dataset and is worth recording, because it bears on what the scan-paths represent: a quiet room at university premises, physical white barriers erected to reduce visual distraction, the child seated alone or on a parent's lap approximately 60 cm from the screen, and all interaction conducted in French, the participants' first language. Typically developing children came from schools in the Hauts-de-France region and autistic children from specialised clinics - the standard clinic-versus-school case-control geometry, inherited rather than chosen.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: The Israeli national well-baby surveillance programme, Tipat Halav, operating across 503 Ministry of Health clinics and covering 75% of the population, with the remaining quarter followed by two health maintenance organisations under identical national guidelines. Services span immunisation, growth monitoring, developmental surveillance and risk detection for mother and child, delivered by nurses with specific maternal and child health training alongside a developmental paediatrician, across approximately eleven visits from birth to age six. This is the only study in the review whose setting is the deployment setting: there is no recruitment, no research protocol, no laboratory and no case-control geometry, and the model is trained on exactly the data that would be available at the moment of use. The equity implication is drawn out explicitly - because the surveillance system is universal and free, a model built on it inherits multi-cultural representativeness that a recruited cohort could not, which the authors contrast with 'disparities in healthcare screening resources and in provider awareness' as barriers to detection. The counterweight is that the model's transferability depends on a health system that most countries do not have, and the authors say so, calling for cross-cultural validation covering 'the expression of signs, parental recognition, interpretation, and reporting levels'.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: No study setting exists. Images were downloaded from Kaggle and processed in Google Colab. The absence of a setting is not incidental: because the photographs were captured by unknown people, with unknown devices, in unknown circumstances, for unknown purposes, there is no acquisition chain to standardise and no way to establish that the two classes were photographed comparably. Every other study in this review that uses cameras controls the device, the distance, the lighting or at least the protocol; this one controls nothing, and the two classes are known to come from different sources.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: No study setting; ABIDE-I aggregates 17 sites internationally. Multi-site aggregation is the dataset's principal strength and its principal hazard: it provides scale and population diversity, and it introduces systematic between-site differences in scanner hardware, field strength, pulse sequence, head coil and recruitment practice that are well documented to support above-chance autism classification on their own. The paper label-encodes SITE_ID during preprocessing, so site information is available to the model, and reports no site-stratified evaluation, no leave-one-site-out validation and no harmonisation procedure. Within-site case-control recruitment is nonetheless a real advantage over the internet-scraped corpora charted elsewhere in this review, since autistic and control participants at each site were recruited and scanned under comparable local conditions.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Single site in Shenzhen, with autistic children enrolled from a first-class psychiatric hospital and typically developing children recruited from local communities - the standard clinic-versus-community case-control geometry. Recording took place in a controlled setting with a fixed camera and stable lighting, which the authors note is a precondition for motion energy analysis to be valid. Participants were paid 200 CNY. The setting is the same as the companion paper on this cohort. What distinguishes the acquisition from most video studies in this review is its minimalism: a single consumer camcorder positioned to the side with both people framed equally, no markers, no sensors and no calibration, which is the basis for the claim that the approach is 'economic, contactless, and calibration-free' and could be deployed without specialist equipment.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Hirosaki University's Department of Neuropsychiatry, with natural language processing collaboration at Tohoku University. Language samples were drawn from ADOS-2 administrations conducted by a research-reliable administrator, so the recording setting is the standardised diagnostic assessment itself. Recruitment ran from September 2013 to October 2020, combining prospective enrolment with retrospective examination of diagnostic records under the same ethical framework. The recruitment geometry is the study's weak point relative to its reference standard: autistic participants come through a university neuropsychiatry clinic while three-quarters of the comparison group are college students recruited for the study, so clinical status, educational setting and probably cognitive level all co-vary with group. The 17 clinically assessed comparison participants partially mitigate this by coming through the same clinical pathway, but they are under a quarter of that group.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: No study setting. Work was performed on a downloaded Kaggle dataset at two universities in Visakhapatnam, India, with no contact with any participant and no acquisition of any kind.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: No study setting. Both corpora were collected under laboratory conditions by their original creators, with KDEF in particular geometrically standardised so that eyes and lips fall at fixed image coordinates across all images. That standardisation is the opposite of the conditions the paper's motivating application would face - an autistic child in spontaneous distress, filmed at whatever angle and distance the situation allows - and the mismatch is not discussed. The one robustness check reported, evaluation across four brightness variants of KDEF, addresses illumination but not pose, spontaneity, age or population.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: Two recruitment sites in the Naples area with a familiar asymmetry: autistic children from the Neapolisanit S.R.L. Rehabilitation Center, which is also a co-author affiliation and where the children were receiving psychomotor and speech therapy, and comparison children from a mainstream pre-primary and primary school. The testing arrangement is described in unusual physical detail - table height 45-60 cm adjusted to the child's age, experimenter seated to the child's right at about 30 cm, a 12.3-inch tablet raised and tilted at approximately 60 degrees to give a full view of the game - and this level of specification is a genuine reproducibility asset. One element of it is also a small confound: adjusting table height by age introduces a systematic postural difference correlated with a variable whose spread differs sharply between groups. The wider recruitment geometry is the standard clinic-versus-school case-control arrangement, compounded here by the autistic group receiving active motor therapy at the recruiting site.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: Not reported. No site, clinic, laboratory, school or other setting is named, and the data collection is described only as manual. The authors are at engineering departments in Pune, India, with no clinical affiliation listed.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: No study setting. The four datasets aggregate responses submitted through autism screening applications, collected by third parties and deposited publicly. The absence of a setting is consequential for the deployment claim rather than for the analysis: the proposed tool is intended for 'clinical and at-home use', so the population that would use it is the general public, while the datasets consist of people who had already sought out an autism screening app - a self-selected group with an above-population base rate, which is visible in the class distributions (69% positive among toddlers, 61% among adolescents).

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: A local preschool in Sazacho, Nagasaki Prefecture, during the pupils' routine medical examinations, capturing approximately 99% of the town's five-year-olds. Three features of this setting distinguish it from the recruitment geometry of almost every other study in this review. There is no case-control contrast: both groups come from the same population and differ only in where their SRS-2 score falls, so the spectrum-truncation problem that inflates diagnostic studies does not arise. The measurement is embedded in an examination the children were attending anyway, so it imposes no additional burden and the participation rate is near-total, eliminating the self-selection that affects recruited samples. And the setting is exactly the deployment setting the paper proposes - preschool screening before elementary education - so the data were collected under the conditions in which the method would be used. The corresponding limitation is geographic narrowness: a single small municipality, which the authors identify when calling for validation on datasets from different regions or institutions.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: No study setting exists. Both corpora are secondary web collections assembled by third parties, and the computational work was done on Google Colab. This matters more here than in most secondary-data studies in this review, because the setting is precisely what generates the labels: the Piosenka positive class is defined by having been found on autism-related websites and Facebook pages, and the YTUIA classes are defined by being drawn from a self-stimulatory-behaviour video corpus versus unrelated kindergarten videos. In a study where the data collection setting differs systematically between classes and no other ascertainment exists, the setting is the confound rather than a background detail.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: No primary collection. Recordings were made by the originating group under controlled laboratory conditions with participants at rest, described as ensuring artefact-free and reliable data. Both groups were recorded on the same equipment under the same protocol, so the acquisition asymmetry that undermines several branches of this review - clinic against school, autism websites against general internet - does not arise here. That is a genuine structural advantage of purpose-built physiological corpora over the assembled behavioural ones.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: A playroom, with the child seated at a table and an instructor beside them, preceded by 5-10 minutes of rapport building with warm-up toys that were then removed. The recruitment settings differ by group: autistic children from a hospital and autism intervention service centres in Beijing, comparison children from a local kindergarten. That asymmetry is the default arrangement across this literature and it carries two consequences the paper does not discuss. Children recruited through intervention services have by definition been identified and are receiving support, so they differ from a screening population in ways beyond diagnosis. And because the recording context is not identical across groups, an unblinded coder could plausibly infer group membership from the video independently of the behaviours being scored - a risk that matters here more than in automated studies, since every indicator originates in a human judgement.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: Outpatient and inpatient services of a single university psychiatric hospital in central Tokyo, with both groups drawn from the same institution. This removes the recruitment asymmetry that affects nearly every case-control study in this review, where the autistic group comes from clinical services and the comparison group from schools, kindergartens or community advertising - an asymmetry that introduces differences in ascertainment, motivation and setting alongside the diagnostic difference of interest. Here both groups are patients of the same service, assessed in the same place by the same certified administrators. The setting is also the deployment setting: a differential-diagnosis aid for autism versus schizophrenia would be used in exactly this kind of adult psychiatric service. The corresponding limitation is a single site in one country with one clinical culture, and the two groups were recruited in non-overlapping windows about two years apart, which the paper does not discuss.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: No primary collection, and the setting structure of the evaluation corpus is the study's central unexamined problem. The CPSD description states that 'recordings of all subjects were captured in their typical environment, i.e clinic for the LIC subjects and elementary, secondary, and high school for the TD subjects'. The atypical classes were therefore recorded in clinical rooms and the typical class in schools, so reverberation, background noise, microphone type and placement, examiner presence and recording protocol all covary perfectly with the binary label - and the entire binary result is trained and tested on this corpus. No acoustic normalisation, channel compensation or noise handling is reported that would mitigate it. The paper does discuss setting as a limitation, but the setting difference it examines is the one between its two corpora (De-Enigma at home, CPSD in laboratory conditions), which affects pre-training rather than the labelled contrast; the within-CPSD clinic-versus-school structure, which is the confound that directly threatens the headline, is never mentioned. This is a clean instance of a pattern the review has documented across modalities - a class label that is inseparable from the circumstances under which the two classes were recorded - arising here in audio rather than in images.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: No study setting exists in the ordinary sense - the data are public posts scraped from Twitter using snscrape, a library chosen because it avoids the need for platform API keys. The absence of a setting is the point: the data are naturally occurring, produced without observation effects, at a scale no laboratory could approach, at essentially zero collection cost. The corresponding costs are equally structural. Nobody knew they were being studied. The two classes were assembled by different procedures - full timeline harvesting for the autism group, daily sampling for controls - so the corpora differ in composition independently of authorship. The platform's user base is skewed by age, language, geography and socioeconomic status in ways the authors acknowledge. And the positive class is defined by membership in a community organised around a topic, so the contrast is between a self-advocacy discourse and general platform conversation rather than between two comparably situated populations.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: Clinical research assessment sessions in the Geneva Autism Cohort, with both groups undergoing the same ADOS protocol in the same setting. This is the single most important design property of the study for the purposes of this synthesis. Across the video, audio and photograph branches charted here, the recurring failure is that the two classes are recorded under systematically different conditions - clinic against school, autism-advocacy websites against general internet, home videos of stereotypy against kindergarten footage - so that acquisition context is a perfect proxy for the label and no amount of downstream methodological care can separate them. Here the context is common to both classes by construction: same room, same protocol, same examiner role, same equipment. Whatever the models are detecting, it is not the difference between being in a clinic and being at school. The residual acquisition concern is temporal rather than group-related: recordings span eleven years, and audio was explicitly normalised 'to homogenize the audio format from different microphones used for ADOS recordings', so equipment changed over that period - but there is no reason to expect equipment drift to align with diagnosis.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: No study setting exists. The autism data are home videos filmed by families on unspecified devices in unconstrained conditions and uploaded to YouTube; the comparison images have no stated origin at all. The paper is unusually thoughtful about setting as a variable, opening its dataset section with an explicit taxonomy - a controlled environment is one where 'researchers have a lot of control over factors that can affect the data being collected' and adjust them 'to reduce potential sources of error or bias', while an uncontrolled environment is one where 'data are obtained under natural or actual settings' without manipulation - and it categorises its four corpora accordingly, arguing that spanning both 'helps to understand a model's behavior'. That analysis is carried through rigorously for the affect task, where the drop from 98.4% on CK+ to 62.2% on AffectNet is precisely the controlled-versus-uncontrolled contrast made visible. It is not carried through for the autism task, where the same reasoning would ask whether the positive and negative images were acquired under comparable conditions - and where the paper's silence about the negative class means the question cannot even be posed.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: A residential special school in Chennai, with images captured across four naturalistic contexts during the school day - outdoor play, classroom, dining area and veranda. This is genuinely ecological data collection, and multi-context sampling within an ordinary day is exactly what a continuous-monitoring argument requires; very few studies in this review collect behavioural data in the settings where children actually spend their time. The same feature creates the study's central measurement hazard, and it is specific to this modality. Skin temperature is determined substantially by ambient temperature, solar radiation, airflow and physical exertion, all of which differ sharply between an outdoor playground in Tamil Nadu and an indoor dining hall. No ambient compensation, environmental logging or per-setting normalisation is described, and the image counts by setting (500, 600, 200, 200) come from different and overlapping groups of children (10, 12, 4, 4) whose severity levels are not reported. If severity is unevenly distributed across capture settings - which with 4 children in two of them is likely - then the thermal environment is confounded with the label, and the confound would survive any splitting scheme. A per-setting stratified analysis would have addressed this directly and is not performed.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: No study setting exists. The corpus is a third-party Kaggle assembly, and its two classes were built by different procedures - an autism-labelled collection on one side, general web search on the other. As with the other studies on this corpus charted in this review, the collection route is the confound rather than a background detail, because it is the only documented respect in which the two image populations are known to differ.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: No study setting; four archived corpora with different recording protocols. The heterogeneity is presented as a strength - two data banks used 'to better represent the population and make the detection model systems more reliable' - and it is a defensible position against the single-corpus practice the paper criticises. It also creates a partial provenance confound that goes unexamined. The autistic children come only from Eigsti and Nadig; the typically developing children come from those two plus Warren and Kuczaj, which contain no autistic children at all. For that supplemented fraction, corpus of origin is perfectly correlated with class, and the corpora differ in ways that bear directly on the features: session lengths of 30 minutes, 10 minutes, unspecified and 30 minutes respectively; a structured cleanup period in one and not the others; and different investigator roles, which matters because half the features are ratios of the child's output to the investigator's. The paper addresses the transcription-convention side of cross-corpus variation in detail and does not address the protocol side.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: No study setting. The Gait Fullbody Dataset records walking trials captured by Kinect v2, and DREAM was collected during robot-assisted therapy sessions with Kinect v1. The paper documents the sensor difference carefully - Kinect v2 detects 25 joints, Kinect v1 detects 20, and DREAM omits the lower body leaving 10 - which is exactly the kind of acquisition detail that determines cross-corpus comparability and that most secondary-analysis studies in this review omit. It does not, however, examine the settings themselves: what the children were doing during DREAM sessions, how a robot's presence shapes movement, or whether the walking protocol was standardised in distance, speed or footwear. Within each corpus, both classes were recorded under the same conditions, so the acquisition confound that affects the photograph and clinic-versus-school audio studies charted elsewhere in this review does not arise here - a genuine structural advantage of using purpose-built research corpora.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: The recording settings are reported group by group and their distribution is the study's most consequential unexamined feature. For the autistic children, 87.10% of recordings came from autism centres and 12.90% from homes; for the typically developing children, 54.84% came from health centres and 45.16% from homes. The paper describes this variety as deliberate - 'a variety of devices and recording locations ... were used to avoid bias and increase generalizability' - but variety across a study is not the same as balance across groups, and here almost nine in ten autistic recordings come from one type of setting while the comparison recordings are split between two others. Jitter, shimmer and harmonics-to-noise ratio are all sensitive to reverberation, background noise and microphone distance, and harmonics-to-noise ratio in particular is a direct measure of the ratio of periodic to aperiodic energy, so ambient noise depresses it mechanically. The strongest statistical finding in the paper (HNR, p < 0.0001) is therefore in the direction that a noisier recording environment would produce. Partial standardisation was applied - a common WAV format at 16-bit and 44.1 kHz, a 25 cm microphone distance instruction, exclusion of recordings not made in quiet conditions - which mitigates but cannot remove the imbalance, and no per-setting stratified analysis is reported although the data to run one plainly exist.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: No study setting. The data are screening-app submissions aggregated on Kaggle by a third party, from respondents who sought out an autism screening tool - a self-selected population whose positive rate reflects help-seeking rather than prevalence.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: A controlled recording environment with standardised lighting, using a single webcam, with both groups recorded under the same protocol. That last point matters and is one of the study's real strengths: across the photograph, video-frame, thermal and clinic-versus-school audio branches, this review has repeatedly found the two classes recorded under systematically different conditions, so that acquisition context proxies for the label. Here the setting, lighting, camera, resolution, frame rate and task sequence are common to both groups, and the landmark representation additionally discards appearance and background before modelling. Whatever the study is detecting, it is not the difference between two recording environments. What is not stated is where the recordings took place, how children were recruited to each group, or whether the examiner differed between groups.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: No study setting. The corpus is a public assembly described as drawn 'from platforms such as Kaggle and ASD-related websites', which is the construction principle this review has documented across the facial-image branch: the autistic class harvested from autism-associated online content, the comparison class from elsewhere, with the result that collection route is the one documented difference between the two populations of images. Nothing in the paper's design addresses this, and no per-source analysis is possible from what is reported.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: No study setting. The corpus is a public Kaggle assembly of children's photographs harvested from the internet, with the two classes drawn from different kinds of online source - the construction principle documented across this review's facial-image branch, in which collection route is the one respect in which the two image populations are known to differ.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: No study setting. Both corpora are public Kaggle assemblies, with the autism images drawn from internet sources by a third party. The paper's stated reason for choosing Kaggle - 'large, well-labelled public data promoting reproducibility in work' - is a genuine consideration and explains why this corpus has attracted at least nine independent analyses, but it addresses reproducibility of the computation rather than validity of the labels.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: Two settings, imperfectly distinguished. Part of the corpus is the Kaggle collection, which has no setting - the images were harvested from internet sources by a third party. Part comes from an autism centre in Semarang, which is a clinical service setting and the same kind of environment in which the proposed edge-deployed tool would run. The mixture is potentially valuable and is undermined by the absence of any breakdown: without knowing how many images came from each source and how they distribute across the two classes, a reader cannot tell whether the clinic data broadens the corpus or introduces a setting confound aligned with the label. A source-held-out analysis would have answered this directly and is not attempted.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Data collection setting is described second-hand: a dedicated experimental room, participant seated about 60 cm from a 17-inch display, session length about five minutes, stimulus order varied between participants, infrared reflection tracking. The country, clinic type, recruitment channel and date of the original collection are not stated. The analysis itself was run on a desktop workstation.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Several rehabilitation centres across Pakistan, with responses collected on paper and via Google Forms into a Google Sheet. The authors are candid about the context: there is no proper reporting and tracking of ASD cases in the country, and the data had to be recorded from scratch. Neither the number of centres, their names, their catchment, nor the collection dates are given, so site cannot be treated as a variable and the pooled sample cannot be characterised.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: No study setting. Images were downloaded; computation ran on a Windows 10 desktop with 8 GB RAM and an Intel i3 CPU. That configuration is worth recording because it is not plausible hardware for training a CNN, a shape model and a graph network for 500 epochs on 2,020 images, and no training time is reported.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: A single special school (Dakshinya Autistic School, Guntur) supplying participants, with ethics oversight from Government Medical College, Guntur, and analysis at VIT-AP University. Recording used a five-point calibration then passive viewing. Setting is described adequately for the acquisition but the recording room, examiner and session conditions are not characterised, and there is no discussion of whether recording conditions varied across severity groups.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: No setting. Images were downloaded from Kaggle on 22 November 2024; the compute environment is not described at all, and the only timing information is an unlabelled training-time column (10.5 versus 26.0) in the Gabor ablation table.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: None described. No acquisition setting, no laboratory, no clinic, no country of origin for the data. The federated clients are simulated - the paper says they represent independent clients such as hospitals or personal devices, but all three run on the authors' own partition of one 44-row file, so no distributed data actually exists.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: Reported in more detail than any other study in this corpus. A 7x7 m room with a 2x2 m capture area, black curtains over the windows, air conditioning at 25-27 degrees C, controlled humidity, fixed room lighting, sessions restricted to 09:00-12:00 to limit lighting and temperature variation, a fixed one-metre subject-to-camera distance, a tripod-mounted camera, and a stated acclimation period before capture. The two groups were photographed at different institutions, however - a special school and a state school - and the paper does not report whether the studio setup was physically identical at both sites or whether the same operator ran both. Given how completely the acquisition is otherwise specified, this is the one variable that matters most and is left open.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: No study setting. A single-author secondary analysis of a downloaded file; no computing environment or runtime is described.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: No study setting. Two downloaded or pre-existing questionnaire datasets, analysed in Python. No computing environment, runtime or data-handling arrangement is described.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: No setting. A single-author secondary analysis of a downloaded file; no computing environment or runtime is described.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: An online REDCap survey hosted at Fundacion Publica Galega de Medicina Xenomica, disseminated through autism associations, institutions, federations, clinical units, research networks and social media, within a broader project validating the CAT-Q for the Spanish population. Recruitment channel is stated and its selection consequences are analysed in the limitations rather than left implicit.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: No study setting. Images were obtained from a public repository; training used CUDA acceleration with no hardware, runtime or environment described.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: No study setting. Images downloaded from Kaggle; experiments run in MATLAB R2021a with no hardware, runtime or environment described.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: No study setting. A downloaded Kaggle file analysed in R. The authorship is notable for this corpus - it includes practising paediatric and psychiatric clinicians from a university hospital, and their input is credited with guiding the feature-selection step.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Early childhood intervention centres in the province of Cordoba supplied both clinical groups; testing used a screen-based eye tracker below a 15-inch laptop, with nine-point calibration. The clinical recruitment route is stated, though the room, examiner and whether TD children were tested under identical conditions are not described.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: No study setting. Images downloaded from an unnamed public repository; the compute environment is tabulated but not quoted in the extracted text. Critically, the acquisition setting of the original data - the viewing task, the stimuli, the eye tracker, the session structure - is nowhere summarised, so a reader cannot say what behaviour the scanpaths record.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: No study setting. A downloaded dataset analysed in Python; no hardware, runtime or environment is described.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Home-based testing on a supplied tablet over two days no more than three days apart, following an online screening form, questionnaire battery and reasoning task. The PD group completed the tasks before their first dopaminergic dose each morning. Home administration is presented as an advantage for scalability - the protocol could be run in community settings without laboratory kinematic equipment - and its cost is acknowledged in the limitations, where stylus resistance and the tablet's sampling and spatial resolution are named as possible suppressors of group differences.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: No study setting. Public datasets harmonised and analysed computationally; no environment, hardware or runtime is described.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: No study setting. Datasets are said to have been processed in different computing laboratories; a testbed with 32 GB RAM and 2 TB storage is named for timing measurements. The paper states that the work involved no hospital deployments while also claiming, in its contributions list, past experience implementing the system in clinical settings and that the framework can effectively validate itself in real-world clinical implementations.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: No study setting - the defining property of the data is precisely that there is none. The videos are unstructured home recordings made by families in everyday environments, which is the source of both the design's principal strength (ecological validity, behaviours observed rather than reported) and its principal uncontrolled variance (camera, framing, lighting, distance and activity all vary by video and are perfectly confounded with the child).

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: The BeGaze corpus was collected in a Spanish research setting with children viewing pre-recorded storytelling clips on screen with AOIs defined over the narrator's face. The bilingual Castilian/Valencian environment of the recorded participants is treated as a methodological factor in its own right rather than left unmentioned.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: No setting is described for either dataset. Dataset 1 is a public download; Dataset 2's 100 original clinical samples have no stated collection site, country, institution or period, which is difficult to reconcile with the claim that an Institutional Review Board granted approval for their collection.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Entirely online, in Dutch, via the Neurotask platform, on participants' own devices - which the paper presents as the point rather than a compromise, arguing that online performance-based measures offer a marriage of more objective data types with the accessibility of surveys, against neuroimaging approaches that are costly, time-consuming and require laboratory attendance. The battery is described as briefer than a typical movie.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: No study setting. A public dataset analysed computationally, with no compute environment, runtime or hardware described - which sits awkwardly with a contribution framed around computational efficiency and real-time deployment, since no timing measurement supports it.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: No setting. Images exported from Roboflow and models trained with the Ultralytics framework; no hardware, runtime or environment is described, which is a notable gap in a paper whose central claim is real-time deployability.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: No setting. A downloaded dataset analysed in Python 3.6.5 on a desktop with an i5-8600K, 16 GB RAM and a GeForce GTX 1050 Ti - a configuration reported in unusual detail for a study whose stated contribution includes computational efficiency, though no runtime or inference-time measurement accompanies it.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: The original recordings were made in a controlled laboratory environment for the typical and moderate groups and in clinical settings for the severe group. The reason for that difference is reported and is substantive: Kinect V2 could not be deployed in controlled conditions for children with severe autism, so only phone video was obtained. That is a real, generalisable observation about who this class of technology can and cannot measure, and it is stated plainly rather than worked around silently.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: No setting of the authors' own. The source recordings were 30-minute free-play sessions (Eigsti) and parent-child interactions at three time points over a year (Nadig), both naturalistic language-sampling protocols from developmental research rather than screening paradigms.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: A specialised educational service setting within Brazilian full-day schools, with the games administered by a trained education professional during the child's normal activities and guardians not present. This is the only study in the charted corpus whose data were collected in the setting where the resulting tool would actually be used, and the choice is argued: full-day schools provide a convenient setting, the professional's existing daily relationship with the children was leveraged, and the application was incorporated into planned educational demands.

questions.question_text: What task or paradigm is used to elicit the behaviour?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: ADOS Module 1 semi-structured assessment (24-52 min), designed for preverbal children; vocalisations manually segmented/labelled into speech, babble, cry, squeal, laugh, other, then automatically re-segmented by energy thresholding.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: A structured reach-grasp-drop task: grasp a 6-cm ball from a support and drop it into a 7-cm hole in a transparent box, 10 trials per child (5 per hand, counterbalanced), demonstrated non-verbally by the experimenter with individually varying practice trials.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: A computerised emotion-recognition task: 40 facial-expression images shown up to a certain expression strength, with the participant answering 'What is the emotion of this person?'. Response correctness and latency were logged. Participants were recruited from outpatient referrals and randomly assigned to sessions.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: A face recognition memory task: three study blocks in which the child memorises one Chinese and one Caucasian face (3 s each), each followed by three test blocks with two target and two foil faces shown until response. Stimuli were grey-scale, front-view, with hair and ears removed by an elliptical mask.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: A single structured elicitation prompt: describe four personally important individuals using 10 positive and 10 negative sentences each, then rate the strength of each description from 0 to 10. The authors explicitly note this prompted format is a design choice - it standardises the assay but does not probe free language generation.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Two tablet games, each with a 2-minute guided training phase and a 5-minute unassisted test phase. 'Sharing': tap a food item to slice it into four, then drag pieces onto four cartoon children's plates, with characters reacting positively or negatively, plus non-task distractor objects. 'Creativity': choose a toy or animal shape, swipe to fill in its dotted outline, then select a colour and paint freely with no rules. The experimenter demonstrated verbally and gesturally during training but did not intervene during testing; the clinician or teacher was present and intervened only for challenging behaviour, in which case data were omitted.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: A voluntary imitation task: participants observed a video clip of a demonstrator's hand performing a two-movement sequence and then copied it, cued by an exclamation mark after a fixation cross and a still hand image. Eight conditions crossed target presence (pointing to visible targets vs no apparent targets) with speed (48 vs 58 beats per minute) and trajectory (15 cm flat, 10 cm short, or 15 cm curved/elevated). Four blocks (two Target, two No-Target) with speed and trajectory randomised within block; 8 analysed trials per condition, plus 32 filler trials specifically included to stop participants' behaviour becoming repetitive and stereotyped.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: A computer-mediated version of the Strange Stories task: 12 short stories displayed on screen and simultaneously read aloud by a pre-recorded voice, each followed by 2-3 questions answered aloud. The design deliberately simulates a human interviewer while removing the interviewer, so that the stimulus is identical across participants. Video was manually segmented into the 12 story periods for feature aggregation.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: A semi-standardised free-play parent-child interaction on a mat with toys, 12 minutes per infant, with parents instructed to play as at home. No task demands were placed on the infant. Vocalisations were then manually segmented by vocal breathing groups using Noldus Observer XT, with vegetative sounds excluded, and annotated for developmental complexity against SAEVD-R by an annotator blinded to group membership.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Spontaneous speech recordings designed to induce three emotional valence categories (positive, neutral, negative). The elicitation procedure itself is not described in this paper - no prompts, stimuli, interlocutor or session structure are given, only the valence categories and the resulting utterance counts. Recordings were segmented into 6380 utterances by an unspecified procedure.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Straight barefoot walking along a 6.5-metre walkway at self-determined speed, with the two force plates positioned so that one foot strikes each. Trials were accepted only on a clean foot strike on each plate. Only a single left-limb stance phase from one selected valid trial per participant was analysed - an extremely small behavioral sample per child, and the selection criterion for which valid trial to use is not stated.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: A fixed 190-second scenario of interaction with RoboParrot, beginning with a greeting from the robot followed by several communication actions designed to motivate the child to engage further. The robot speaks, blinks, sings, laughs and moves slightly, and is teleoperated from a tablet. Parents accompanied their child but were instructed not to get involved. The child is free to move within the space in front of the robot; there is no task instruction to the child.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Passive viewing, deliberately minimal: five-point calibration, then eye-position correction on a dynamic pink rabbit, then a single 10-second muted video of a young Asian female mouthing the English alphabet. The brevity is the explicit design contribution - the authors argue that with young children the paradigm must be short as well as informative, since keeping such subjects focused on a monitor for long periods is difficult. The stimulus is muted, so the speaking face provides visual mouth motion without audio.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Two complementary protocols. Structured: four gamified exercises activated by child or parent - picture description of social scenarios (9 pictures), word reading (5 lists of 10-11 words), sentence reading (2 sentences) and story reading (2 ~100-word stories), with materials drawn from the Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation and reproduced in full in the appendix. Unstructured: a monitoring mode that continuously listens and begins recording on voice-activity detection, capturing everyday communication. Crucially the paper documents real-world protocol failure honestly, reproducing a transcript in which a parent prompts and speaks over the child throughout a word-reading test, and designing error-robust features (irrelevant-word and repeated-word ratios) in response.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Two contrasting tasks over the same six web page screenshots. Browsing: up to two minutes per page, free to read or ignore anything, moving on when ready. Searching: 30 seconds per page to answer two questions posed verbally by the researcher, with the answer read aloud - the full set of twelve questions is published in a table. Pages were presented in randomised order per participant and the two tasks were counterbalanced. Pages spanned three ViCRAM-rated visual complexity levels, giving a designed manipulation of stimulus complexity.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: A highly standardised reach-to-grasp protocol: fixed start posture with pincer grip on a marked point, a water-filled bottle of specified dimensions at 44 cm from the child's midline, and four intention conditions (grasp-to-place, grasp-to-pour, pass-to-place, pass-to-pour) with target objects at specified distances. 12 consecutive grasps per condition (48 total), initiated at natural speed after an auditory tone, with 2 practice trials before each block, pseudo-randomised block order, and a 2-minute pause between blocks to avoid fatigue. Crucially, video is trimmed at the moment of contact, so only the pre-grasp reaching phase is analysed - testing the neuroscientific claim that intention is encoded in the earliest stages of a motor act.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Five face-perception tasks spanning emotion recognition, a non-social perceptual judgement (brow versus lip width), free viewing, age estimation and a social evaluation ('nice' or not), across 60 trials per subject. Stimuli were 60 FACES database photographs balanced by sex and across three age bands, each shown once per subject with one randomly chosen expression from six to avoid familiarity effects and face-emotion confounds. Notably the study deliberately used images of the entire head with varying facial-feature locations, criticising the field's usual practice of using cropped images with standardised feature positions as 'somewhat unrealistic' - and solved the resulting AOI problem with automatic landmark detection.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: A deliberately inverted task design: participants perform one-dimensional oscillatory hand movement 'as complex as possible', with the experimenter demonstrating the contrast between simple periodic oscillation (mono amplitude and frequency) and complex unpredictable oscillation (variant amplitude and frequency), followed by practice trials until the requirement was understood. Three 60-second trials with the subdominant hand held behind the back, breaks of 2-5 minutes between trials, and trial reinitiation if the hand left the recording zone or movement stopped. The design is the paper's key idea - restrictedness is measured as failure to comply with an instruction to be variable.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: A 5-minute unstructured 'get-to-know-you' conversation with a novel young adult confederate blind to diagnostic status and assigned by availability. No conversational prompts were given to either speaker. Recordings were made with a device placed between the speakers carrying two opposed HD cameras and four directional microphones. Transcription used a rigorous protocol: two junior annotators (one segmenting pause groups, one transcribing words) plus a senior annotator with at least six months' experience reviewing and correcting every file, with all annotators having completed at least 10 hours of Quick Transcription training modified for clinical ASD interviews and having achieved over 90% agreement with a gold-standard transcript before independent work.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: The Dynamic Affect Recognition Evaluation task: silent videos of a face transitioning slowly from neutral into one of six emotions, with the participant pressing the spacebar upon recognition and then selecting the emotion from six labels. Two practice trials (two choices) preceded twelve test trials (six choices), with practice videos not reused. Videos lasted 19-33 seconds. The design yields both a behavioural measure (how quickly recognition occurs, and whether it is correct) and a gaze measure over the same stimulus - which is what enables the accuracy-versus-latency dissociation.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Parents submitted brief unstructured videos, quality-screened against three content criteria: capturing the child's face and hands, involving social interaction or attempts at it, and involving interaction between the child and a toy or object. All 159 submitted videos passed quality inspection. Nine clinically untrained, non-Bengali-speaking US raters then answered 31 multiple-choice questions per video after a one-hour training session, with quality control comparing a 10-video subset against gold-standard scores agreed by two experienced clinical research coordinators.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Free viewing of 2D natural scene images, per the source dataset. No task instruction, viewing duration, stimulus presentation details or calibration procedure is described, since none of it was performed by these authors. The analysis pipeline adds its own processing tasks - YOLO object detection and SDSP saliency estimation over each stimulus image.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Four ADOS-derived tasks, each performed exactly once as in ADOS: response to name call (positive if eye contact detected), joint attention (transferring attention to a second robot that activates its lights, verified by eye contact), play request (eliciting vocalisations and eye contact coordinated with hand and body gestures to test simultaneous multi-channel communication), and functional imitation with real objects - a toy frog and a cup - which the authors distinguish from the simple motoric imitation used in comparable work. In every task the robot first performs an action intended to provoke a child response. A therapist placed objects into the robot's hand and triggered demonstrations via head tactile sensors, specifically to eliminate failed grasps and guarantee the imitation always occurred.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Stated only at the highest level: Arabic visual stimuli 'that closely align with the existing English language visual stimuli' of a cited prior study, with data collection following recommendations from the same source. The results section states videos were used as stimuli. No stimulus inventory, count, duration, presentation order, calibration procedure or region-of-interest definition is given, so the elicitation protocol cannot be reconstructed or repeated.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: A deliberately minimal task: point between two 8 mm stickers 30 cm apart on a table with the index finger, as quickly and accurately as possible, for 10 seconds, repeated with the dominant and non-dominant hand. The brevity and simplicity are the point - the paper tests whether a task this short can carry diagnostic signal, in contrast to the longer imitation and gameplay protocols elsewhere in the corpus.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Passive video viewing lasting about 5 minutes on average, with scenarios deliberately varied in content and length to allow ocular activity to be analysed from different perspectives. Stimuli were designed to attract children (colourful balloons, cartoons) with elements whose position changes during the experiment, and some videos featured a human presenter speaking in French who attempts to direct the child's attention to visible or invisible elements. Additional SMI Experiment Center stimuli spanned static and dynamic naturalistic scenes with and without receptive language, joint attention stimuli, static faces or objects, and cartoons. A five-point calibration with subsequent verification procedures preceded recording.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Five 5-minute dyadic social interaction tasks - an ice-breaker, two debating tasks, a meal-planning task and a roleplay - with dyads composed as TD-TD, ASD-ASD or mixed. The ice-breaker task was abandoned entirely because one mixed dyad did not understand the instructions, reducing 145 videos to 116. Recording used a fixed high-definition camera 320 cm from chairs placed 60 cm apart under standardised artificial lighting. Two regions of interest per participant (head; body including legs) were drawn manually, and grayscale change within them produced two continuous movement time series per person.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Two commercially available children's cartoon games from the Duckie Deck series, engineered with bespoke code to capture touch-screen and inertial sensor data, played for five minutes each.
