This is the most deployable paradigm in the review and the protocol states its properties exactly: the method 'required no professional training to deploy, no verbal instructions were required to engage the child, and only limited supervision was necessary. The result of the assessment was purely statistical; no subjective coding was required.' Four consequences follow that no other included paradigm achieves together. There is no examiner, so examiner variability is eliminated rather than merely controlled. There is no verbal demand, so the assessment reaches pre-verbal and minimally verbal children whom the language-based measures in this review cannot assess. There is no human rating anywhere in the chain, so inter-rater reliability is not a consideration. And the apparatus is a consumer tablet running a children's game, so ten minutes in a nursery or a living room produces the data. Against this, what the child is doing is playing a game rather than interacting socially, so the construct measured is motor control rather than reciprocity - which the protocol presents as a deliberate choice.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Free viewing of 300 natural images, each shown at original full resolution for 3 seconds. The paper adds a computational task of its own: generating a synthetic 'typical viewer' scanpath for every image using STAR-FC, a multi-saccade generator that fixates centrally, applies a retinal transform with anisotropic blurring, combines peripheral low-level and central high-level conspicuity streams into a priority map with inhibition of return, and iterates.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Unstructured everyday home activity, categorised as play alone, play with others, meal time, and parents' concerns, with videos ranging from 2 to 10 minutes. The episode construction rule is explained and justified: 8 seconds before and 2 seconds after each expert time stamp, 'because physicians usually labeled a typical or atypical time stamp after they observed the behavior for a while, and a 10-second window could approximately record the behavior in full'. This is a thoughtful accommodation of how human annotation actually occurs.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: A joint-attention protocol using 'look at, point and speak' stimuli to direct the child's attention toward objects in the room, delivered first by the therapist alone and subsequently by the robot alone. The construct is decomposed into the three standard subtypes - initiation of joint attention, responding to joint attention bids, and initiation of request behaviour - which is a level of construct specification that few studies in this review match, and the within-session mediator transition makes the design a within-subject manipulation: the same child receives the same bid type from a human and then from a robot, so the mediator is the variable and the child is their own control. That is what makes a six-child study capable of producing an interpretable pattern at all. The design's weakness is that the transition is not counterbalanced - therapist always precedes robot - so the group difference in initiation toward the robot is confounded with order, with accumulated fatigue, and with the novelty effect that the paper elsewhere says it intends to leverage.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Image viewing with gaze recording, per the source dataset; no task instruction, duration or presentation detail is given. The analysis pipeline adds a computational stage: SalGAN generates a reference saliency map representing where a general-population observer would look, and 225x225 patches are cropped from that map at each fixation location, so the model sees not where the child looked in absolute terms but what the predicted saliency landscape looked like at each fixated point.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: Two interactive games with the NAO robot, 'Touch me' and 'Dance with me', preceded by a dialogue phase in which a multiple-choice voice menu encouraged the child to choose a game or request a demonstration. Three properties of this paradigm bear on the review. The elicitation is delivered by a machine, so the social partner's behaviour is identical for every child - a form of standardisation no human examiner can supply, and one that removes examiner variability from a construct (reciprocal interaction) where the examiner is half the dyad. The voice-menu opening gives the child a choice of activity, which is a design decision oriented to engagement rather than to experimental control and is consistent with the group's later commitment to scenarios attractive to children. And the two games differ in a way the group's 2022 paper makes explicit: one uses a stationary robot issuing instructions, the other a moving robot inviting imitation, so that the same physical behaviour has different meanings in each. Here that structure is used to define the two conditions of the within-subject contrast - instructed against spontaneous - which is the paradigm's payoff.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: A two-episode still-face paradigm: 2 minutes of normal mother-infant interaction under fixed instructions, then 1 minute in which the mother holds a neutral, unresponsive face. The classic reunion episode was omitted, following the common two-episode variant. The design logic is that the still-face episode manufactures a controlled social challenge - all of the mother's social signals vanish at once - and the paper's central empirical claim is that this challenge is more diagnostically informative than ordinary interaction, since the SF episode beat the FF episode for every classifier and only SF behaviours correlated with symptom severity.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Movement imitation with style manipulation: participants watched a video of a hand movement sequence pointing between four locations and then imitated it, with only movements between two designated locations analysed. Three movement styles were used - elevated amplitude, fast-direct, and direct - crossed with two instruction blocks, a general instruction block and an attention instruction block that directed attention to movement style. The elevated condition is the theoretically critical one, since imitating an unusually elevated trajectory requires adopting a movement style outside one's habitual repertoire.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: Prompted facial expression imitation. The system randomly displays one of seven expressions (angry, disgust, fear, happy, sad, surprise, neutral) and prompts the child by picture and sound to reproduce it, presenting the same expression three times, with elicitation aids such as cartoon smiling faces, children's songs and animations for situational simulation. The design is explicitly modelled on how physicians administer the diagnostic scales - 'The doctor observes the tester's reaction to determine whether the tester is autistic after requesting the tester to make the corresponding expression' - and the paper justifies the choice by itemising the expression-related items in the CABS, ABC and CARS scales.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Quiet standing balance, barefoot on two feet with arms relaxed, for 20 seconds, under randomised eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions, with three acceptable trials per condition. The 20-second duration is justified explicitly against the practical difficulty of keeping autistic children still for longer, citing evidence that 15 seconds gives acceptable construct and concurrent validity in children. Foot placement was deliberately left unconstrained 'to enable participants to adopt a natural stance to more closely reflect any strategy they might use to maintain balance in their natural environment' - an ecological-validity choice made at the cost of some standardisation. Trial acceptability criteria are stated explicitly, and environmental distraction was minimised by keeping investigators and guardians quiet.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: A sensory maze scenario in which two robots - a small humanoid and an iPod-based mobile robot - walk around a maze to find stations and interact with sensory stimuli at each. The activity was designed to include multiple opportunities for robot-initiated conversation, encouraging active participation from the child in a joint sensory experience. Children's movement was deliberately unrestricted and no obtrusive sensors were worn, which the authors identify as the design's key advantage for generalisation to naturalistic settings.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Whole-body imitation of dance-like movements performed by a young woman on a large TV screen, deliberately without music or sound. Sequences comprised 14-18 individual movement types selected to be 'relatively unfamiliar (e.g., moving arms up and down like a puppeteer)', to lack an end goal, and to require moving multiple limbs simultaneously - chosen on the basis of prior research showing that autistic imitation difficulties are most pronounced for meaningless, goal-less actions. A brief training phase preceded testing. Of 14 collected trials at varying speeds, only the 4 at 100% speed are analysed to avoid confounding by speed, comprising two sequences each presented twice, which is what enables the test-retest analysis.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: No experimental task at all - and this is a deliberate methodological position rather than an omission. Audio comes from the clinical diagnostic procedure itself, so what the models see is the same behaviour a clinician sees, recorded in situ with clinician speech, parent speech, toy noise and chair scraping all present. The cost is that infant-only segments must be isolated by hand and that the recording contains no controlled elicitation; the benefit is ecological validity and the possibility of retrofitting to sessions already being recorded.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Overground walking trials with lower-limb marker placement - a minimum of five per subject, each containing a variable number of gait cycles, with the analysis restricted to the five-trial common minimum so that every subject contributes equally. Restricting to a common trial count is a deliberate balancing decision at the subject level, and is the only such control the design applies.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: The ADOS-2 assessment itself, with no additional or purpose-built task. This is the design's central choice and its main practical strength: the data are generated by a procedure clinics already perform, so deployment requires only recording rather than a new protocol, and the model's target and its input come from the same session. The cost is that the input is contaminated with clinician, parent and environmental sound, which is why manual speaker labelling was necessary; and that module assignment varies by child, so the speech elicited is not identical across participants.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: Real web pages under three task types drawn from a published hierarchy of information needs - browse (no goal), search (locate one element), synthesis (locate two elements and infer a third). Study 1 used six pages spanning low, medium and high visual complexity; Study 2 selected eight from the Alexa top 100 after removing duplicates, non-English pages, search engines and pages requiring authentication, then scoring visual complexity with the ViCRAM tool and randomly selecting four low- and four high-complexity home pages. The rationale for web pages is ecological: they offer mixed textual and visual stimuli organised for a semantic purpose, permitting multiple search strategies, and browsing is 'a highly familiar and naturalistic task' whose data could in principle be captured without laboratory equipment. Time limits were manipulated deliberately across studies to separate strategy differences from duration differences.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: Free viewing of 82 static images across four categories - facial images, social scenarios, animated characters and synthetic patterns - each shown for 3 seconds with a 1-second mask between images to suppress carry-over, at 0.5 m from a 1920 x 1080 monitor with no instruction beyond observing. The design choice is deliberate and argued: eye-tracking protocols for this population 'usually consider the limited attention of children with ASD, with each set of experiments lasting less than 10 minutes', and the paper contrasts its short protocol against comparators requiring 10 minutes or 10-45 minutes. Note that 82 images at 4 seconds each implies roughly 5.5 minutes of presentation, against the 'approximately 2.5 minutes for recording eye movement' claimed in the comparison - an unexplained discrepancy.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Avatar imitation in a projected virtual city street, under three cumulative sensory conditions - visual (waving), visual-auditory (dancing to a disco track), and visual-auditory-olfactory (biting a buttered muffin with a butter scent released by a wireless diffuser). The design is the most theoretically motivated stimulus escalation in the corpus: the sensory ladder follows the autism sensory literature directly, adding modalities to which autistic children are reported hypersensitive (visual, auditory) before one to which they are reported hyposensitive (olfactory), on the hypothesis that sensory load provokes repetitive behaviour. The imitation framing is also apt, since imitation deficits are independently documented. Order was fixed rather than counterbalanced, deliberately, to avoid sensory overload - a defensible clinical choice that the authors correctly flag as a methodological cost.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: A purpose-designed protocol modelled on ADOS and organised around distinct humour mechanisms: greeting smile with the child's name, praise words, hide and seek, hints of tickling, actual tickling, and a parent-delivered greeting smile. Each stimulus opens with a scripted keyword phrase, which is what makes automatic temporal segmentation possible - the ASR system detects the phrase and thereby locates the response window, so protocol design and pipeline design are co-dependent by construction. Stimuli are repeated up to three times if the child does not respond, and children who do not complete every step contribute missing scores that are mean-imputed.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: Six passive-viewing paradigms totalling 109 stimuli, each designed by clinical psychologists 'to characterize features known to be atypical or impaired in individuals with ASD' and each targeting a distinct construct: social motivation and shared play (Activity Monitoring), primitive social preference (Biomotion), sensitivity to social overtures (Dyadic Bids), naturalistic scene viewing (Dynamic Scenes), automaticity of information-seeking from others (Social Referencing), and interest in and comprehension of others' intentions (Theory of Mind). Passive viewing with no instruction is a deliberate design decision justified by the observation that autistic individuals are differentially affected by verbal instruction, so implicit-attention paradigms generalise better across ability and age. Stimuli were presented in counterbalanced orders.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: Two distinct paradigms in one session. Resting-state EEG for about 6 minutes with eyes open, with the child kept as still and quiet as possible. Then passive viewing of face photographs - a young girl of the child's own race or of another race, each type presented 6 times for 10 seconds in random order, with a dynamic kitten and sound between trials to re-engage attention and no response required. The own-race/other-race manipulation is uncommon in this literature and yields a directly interpretable comparison; the attention-recapturing interstimulus is a practical design detail for this age group that few papers describe.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Emotion recognition under competing attentional demand - a face at centre flanked by two validated high-autism-interest nonsocial distractors, so that gaze allocation and emotion identification are measured in the same trial. The paper's rationale for combining them is theoretical rather than opportunistic: emotion recognition and social attention 'have mostly been studied in isolation' and both have been proposed separately as diagnostic indicators, so the authors 'hypothesized that they are deeply linked and studied them together'. The three-trial structure with feedback in trial 2 only is designed to emulate the Superpower Glass intervention, and it produces an unanticipated result - discrimination was best in trial 1, before any feedback or task adaptation.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: The Simulated Interaction Task - the corpus's most carefully constructed elicitation paradigm. A prerecorded actress conducts a small-talk conversation about food preferences and dinner preparation, structured into neutral, positive and negative segments of 24-26 seconds each, alternating between her speaking and the participant answering while she displays empathic listening (nodding, social smiling). The design reasoning is stated in unusual detail: food preferences were chosen because they elicit positive and negative emotion quickly without personal or sensitive content, and because response lengths vary less than for topics such as favourite films, which aids standardisation. To generate natural behaviour, the actress actually conversed with the film director during shooting rather than reading to camera. Naturalness was supported by informing participants the actress's part was prerecorded, by instructing and rehearsing three-to-four-sentence answers, and by opening with a practice exchange. Crucially, the actress's own behaviour was then verified with the same OpenFace pipeline, confirming she expressed more disgust and less joy when discussing disliked food and smiled more when listening than speaking - so the stimulus is quantified rather than assumed.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: The gap/overlap paradigm, which is a well-chosen task for this question even though the paper does not explain why: extinguishing the fixation point before target onset (gap) versus leaving it visible (overlap) separates attentional disengagement from saccade execution, and the paper correctly reports that overlap latencies were substantially longer than gap latencies, confirming the manipulation worked in the source data. Each participant completed one block of 30 gap trials and one block of overlap trials. The paradigm is described but not motivated, and the gap-minus-overlap difference that gives it its diagnostic interest is never analysed as such.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: Two modules of an existing multi-robot intervention, each targeting a core impairment. The joint attention module escalates cues in a least-to-most hierarchy - visual (cyclic eye colour change, blinking), then visual plus speech, then visual plus speech plus motion - which is drawn from established prompting practice and allows the level of support required to be read off the cue level at which the child responds. The imitation module is contingent rather than scripted: the child must fixate one of the two robots for five seconds to activate it, then imitates four movements. Using two robots is a deliberate design choice presented as 'representing a triad human communication scenario', on the reasoning that dyadic robot interaction does not exercise the same social configuration as everyday multi-party interaction.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Three purpose-built 10-second joint attention videos at 1920 x 1080, forming a graded series: in video A only the therapist's eyes move; in video B the gaze shifts toward an object of interest; in video C the hand points to the object. Each is segmented at the points where the set of relevant regions changes, giving nine analysed segments in total. The design is unusually well matched to the construct - joint attention involves coordinated mutual engagement with a third entity, so a stimulus that isolates gaze-only, gaze-to-object and gaze-plus-point conditions decomposes the paradigm into its components, and the segment-level ensemble then reveals which components carry information.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: A single Unity3D virtual scene - a couple in a garden with their dog - containing three semantic regions: human figures as social stimuli, an animal, and landscape. Free viewing for 15-20 seconds with no instruction. The design rationale is explicit and worth recording: previous Chinese eye-tracking work used 'merely a face on the computer screen', whereas static or isolated social presentations may fail to reveal group differences because 'for static images or those which present social information in isolation, social attention is normal in autism'. The 15-20 second exposure is by some margin the shortest stimulus in the corpus, which suits deployment but yields few gaze points per participant.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: A gamified visual-orienting task with a graded social-content manipulation - arrow, pointing finger, cartoon animal gaze, human gaze - crossed with four directions across 160 trials, using 160 distinct cue pictures and 640 distinct object pictures so that no stimulus repeats. The task requires not just an orienting saccade but sustained fixation on the target for 1000 ms to earn a reward, a design choice the authors justify from piloting: autistic children 'might occasionally choose one target, but then change their mind and fixate on another', so the long fixation window gives them the opportunity to revise. The 4000 ms trial limit was likewise set by piloting because 'some children with ASD would lose their attention during a trial'. The authors also flag that this attention-sustaining phase distinguishes their paradigm from conventional visual-orienting tasks and 'arguably contributes to the poor performance of children with ASD' - an unusually self-aware statement about what their own task measures.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: A six-minute point-light biological motion animation constructed from human skeletal figures with body keypoints, showing three behaviours in sequence: figures walking forward from distant to near, walking upside-down, and clapping hands. The stimulus choice is well motivated from the literature - typical viewers have 'a strong visual sensitivity to biological movement', autistic children show 'abnormal gaze towards scattered light points or rotating aperture', and have 'a lower tendency to immobilize biological moving objects'. Using abstract point-light figures rather than faces or naturalistic video isolates biological motion perception from face processing, which is a cleaner manipulation than most gaze studies in this corpus attempt. The upside-down walking condition in particular is the standard inversion control for biological motion, though the paper does not analyse it as such.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: The broadest gaze battery in the corpus - seven distinct tests targeting own-race unfamiliar faces (twice), other-race unfamiliar faces, joint attention, gaze following (twice) and social interaction, each photograph type presented six times for 10 seconds. This design permits the informative negative finding that joint attention was the least discriminative gaze feature (t = -0.79, non-significant) while unfamiliar own-race face viewing was the most discriminative - the opposite of what much of this corpus assumes. Resting EEG precedes the gaze battery rather than being recorded concurrently, which is why the cross-modal covariances the paper reports are between asynchronously acquired signals.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: The geometric-versus-social preference paradigm - nine videos totalling 54 seconds at 30 fps and 1920 x 1080, with social scenes of children playing or doing yoga on one side of the screen competing against randomly varying fractals on the other. The paradigm is chosen for reasons of clinical reach rather than theoretical richness, and the reasons are stated: it 'has the advantage of being short and does not require audio, it can be used in nonverbal and at any age'. This matters for a severity study, since a paradigm requiring verbal instruction or sustained compliance would systematically exclude the severe end of the range being measured.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: A structured four-session conversation with a single blinded interviewer, each session designed to probe a different aspect of interaction: general questions for familiarisation, hobby sharing to test whether a self-selected topic changes gaze, yes-no questions to elicit head nodding or shaking, and question raising to examine initiative. The full question list is published, which makes the protocol reproducible in a way that most naturalistic-interaction studies are not. The design's key property is that the number of exchanges is fixed while the time taken is free, which is exactly what makes session length an interpretable behavioural measure rather than an artefact - and it is that measure which proved most discriminative.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: Sustained phonation of the vowel /ah/, chosen explicitly against the alternative of connected or spontaneous speech. This is a defensible methodological position for voice-quality analysis - it holds linguistic content constant and isolates phonatory function - but it is a severe constraint for autism specifically, since the acoustic differences documented in autistic speech concern prosody, intonation contour and pragmatic use of voice, all of which are eliminated by a sustained vowel. The paper's own introduction describes autistic speech as 'machine-like monotonic or sing-song', properties that cannot manifest in an isolated sustained vowel, so the task may not be capable of capturing the phenomenon it is aimed at.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: A composite battery assembled from several existing psychological protocols and described at unusual protocol-level detail: three 58-second joint attention initiation videos plus 18 matched 5-second photographs, opening with a hand-waving cartoon attention grabber before a woman greets the child and then looks, verbalises and points toward a target either present in or absent from the child's visual field; twelve 4-second gaze-following videos separating head-plus-eye shifts from eye-only shifts; static actor-plus-object photographs; and five minutes of cartoon scenes whose characters' emotional expressions are contingent or non-contingent on the preceding scene. Stimuli were counterbalanced and interleaved with a two-second central crosshair. The variety - dynamic versus static, human versus cartoon, human versus object - is deliberate, allowing 'analysis of the ocular activity of participants from different perspectives', and it is what produces multiple scanpath images per child.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: The biological-versus-geometric preference paradigm rendered as nine sequential 6-second clips totalling 54 seconds, with the screen split between children interacting and fractal movement, and with side and ordering varied to prevent conditioning. Two protocol details matter: calibration was repeated once on failure and the participant excluded after a second failure, and only subjects with more than 80% of total video time successfully captured were retained - a quantified data-quality gate. Where a child had to sit on an adult's lap, the adult wore a blindfold 'in order to avoid influencing the signals acquired', which is a control against caregiver gaze cueing that no other study in the corpus reports.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: The most elaborate elicitation paradigm in the corpus: a 24-minute 45-second multisensory virtual mall with 16 scripted scenes and synchronised visual, auditory and olfactory channels. The scenes are designed to sample distinct social demands - an avatar greeting the child and asking their name, peekaboo through shop displays, a choice offered between an apple and a lollipop, explicit joint-attention bids where the avatar indicates three times verbally and by gesture that the child should look left, an emotional display of disgust at a trash can, and a startling event where a train nearly runs over the avatar. Two design decisions deserve note: forest scenes with relaxing music were inserted at the start and between stores specifically 'to avoid cognitive and sensory overload', and scene order was counterbalanced across participants. This is elicitation designed around the population's sensory needs rather than only around the constructs being measured.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Ten yes-no questions with an explicit verbal instruction to nod or shake the head while answering, drawn from the third of four chronologically arranged conversational sessions. The instruction is what makes the study possible - it ensures the target behaviour occurs in every participant, so kinematics can be compared on matched gestures rather than confounded with whether the gesture happened. The authors recognise the cost and state it: prior findings of reduced head gesture use in autism may hold only in spontaneous contexts, so 'our task may not a good one to reveal an ASD vs. TD difference in terms of head nodding/shaking frequency', and future work should examine unintentional gesture use.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: Not described. The paper does not report what the children were looking at, how long the stimuli lasted, or how scanpaths were rendered into images - all of which are documented in the source publication and all of which bear on what the classifiers are learning. A reader of this paper alone cannot tell whether the images encode gaze position only or, as in the source, gaze velocity through colour gradient.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Reaching for and grasping a felt-tip pen to complete a printed figure - a task chosen because it is ecological and needs no explanation to a preschooler, with pen orientation varied across four positions specifically to prevent stereotyped movement. Forty trials per child across eight blocks in two sessions, with block order randomised and free choice of hand and grip. The design decisions are all in service of the mechanistic question: enough trials to estimate trial-to-trial variability and to fit trial-wise PCA, enough orientation variation to require genuine motor parameter selection rather than a rehearsed movement, and enough naturalness that task comprehension is not a confound.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: A semi-autonomous adaptive scenario in 13 sections, delivered by a NAO robot with a mobile phone mounted on a purpose-built chest holder that displays facial expressions through an Emotions Selector application, presenting emotional cues and soliciting emotional responses. The paradigm's distinctive property is that it is closed-loop: the scenario adapts across sessions according to each child's attention score history, so the measurement feeds back into the intervention. No other study in this review implements that loop - the rest measure behaviour and stop. The engineering description is also careful in a way that matters practically: the chest mount was designed so that the added weight 'barely affects the center of mass of the robot body, hence the changes in the moment of inertia are negligible', preserving the robot's balance and its built-in interactive behaviours, which is the kind of detail that determines whether a modified platform actually works in a clinic. What is not reported is the session duration or the content of the 13 sections, so the paradigm cannot be reproduced from the paper.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: No behavioural task and no observation of any kind. All data are caregiver responses to a 21-item questionnaire, most of it retrospective - the age at which a child first walked or spoke, whether they rocked in a crib as a baby, whether they were ever thought deaf, and maternal behaviours during a pregnancy that occurred years earlier. Recall accuracy for such items is known to be limited and to differ systematically between parents of diagnosed and undiagnosed children, since a diagnosis reframes recollection of early development. The paper does not address recall bias.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: Four conversational ADOS-2 Module 3 tasks, chosen on an explicit criterion - they occur in the second half of the administration, 'do not require objects, books or images, and are purely conversational', so speech is elicited without competing manipulative demands. The design's central practical virtue is that no new protocol is required at all: the speech already exists in every videotaped ADOS-2, so the measure is retrofittable to routine assessment. The task-by-task comparison then produces a directly actionable finding - the friends and marriage conversation alone matches or exceeds all four combined, so a shorter sampling context suffices, and the authors note it 'could be selected in circumstances where reducing the false positive rate is required'.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Free viewing of 400 natural images from mixed categories, inherited from the benchmark. No instruction, response or trial structure is described. The paradigm is the most passive in the corpus - the child looks at pictures and nothing is asked of them - which is an advantage for feasibility in young or minimally verbal children and a disadvantage for interpretability, since there is no task performance against which viewing behaviour can be referenced. The best/worst image analysis shows how much the paradigm's yield depends on stimulus choice: three of the five best-performing images depict children, which the authors suggest 'might have moved the attention of the young participants', implying that stimulus curation rather than model capacity sets the ceiling.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Free viewing of natural images for 3 seconds each, with no instruction, response or interaction. The paradigm is entirely inherited, and the paper's contribution lies in representation and architecture rather than task design. The 3-second window is worth noting against the finding that total scanpath duration is the dominant discriminator: within a fixed 3-second presentation, total scanpath duration is determined by how much of the window the tracker recorded valid fixations for, so the discriminating quantity is partly a function of tracking quality and compliance rather than of viewing strategy - a data-quality-as-signal pattern that recurs across this corpus and that the paper does not consider.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: The ADOS assessment itself, filmed end to end and averaging 42 minutes - not a purpose-built task. Only Modules Toddler, 1 and 2 were used, on the stated grounds that these are conducted while moving around a room with attractive toys and demand less language, whereas Modules 3 and 4 are table-based and discussion-heavy. The paradigm's key property is that it requires no new protocol, instrumentation or examiner training: any clinic that already videotapes ADOS sessions holds the raw material. Against that, it inherits a structural feature the paper does not examine - the ADOS is an interactive assessment in which a trained examiner actively presses for social behaviours and adapts to the child's responses, so the recorded scene is a joint product of child and clinician, and the video contains the examiner and frequently a caregiver as well.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: A digital reimplementation of the Leiter-3 nonverbal intelligence battery, built in Unity and C#, playing 'exactly the same tasks of the Leiter-3, presented in the same order' under the original administration rules, with the examiner advancing subtests at the standard error threshold. Five subtests span figure-ground, figure completion, classification analogies, sequential order and visual patterns, with two to eight draggable cards and placeholders per item and distractors present, ascending in complexity. Three features of the design deserve note. The paradigm is entirely dual-purpose: the child takes a cognitive assessment they would take anyway and the motor data are a by-product, so there is no added task burden and the approach is retrofittable to any clinic already using the Leiter-3. The nonverbal character of the instrument makes it usable across language levels, which matters for autism specifically. And the cognitive-load control is carefully reasoned - only the first five items of each subtest were analysed 'since all participants correctly performed at least the first five items', so kinematic differences cannot be attributed to some children struggling with the cognitive demand, and the demonstration item FG1 was excluded because the examiner may have moved cards during it. The five one-hot task-identity variables then give the network explicit information about which cognitive context each movement came from.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Two paradigms with complementary demands, both requiring nothing of the child. EEG is eyes-open resting state for at least five minutes, so there is no task at all and no compliance requirement beyond sitting - the caregiver may be present. Eye tracking uses two ~30-second clips of a dynamic social interaction between a child and an adult, presented in random order, with an attention-grabbing animated kitten between trials, and 'no response was required from the children'. This is a well-judged design for the 3-6 age band: neither component depends on language, instruction-following or motor response, which is precisely what limits most computational paradigms in preschoolers. The eight areas of interest are the analytically substantive choice, distinguishing adult from child and, within each, eyes from mouth from body, plus a dedicated joint-attention region - a scheme built to test specific published claims about social attention. That the resulting 96 features are then fed undifferentiated into an autoencoder, with no analysis of which AOIs mattered, wastes the design's discriminative structure.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: The most carefully constructed elicitation paradigm in the corpus, and the design reasoning is unusually visible. It adapts Mundy's Early Social Communication Scales, a validated manual for eliciting and scoring joint-attention behaviours, together with behaviour-extraction techniques from applied behaviour analysis. Three geometric decisions are justified explicitly. The toy sits 70 cm away on the midline, out of reach, because a nearer toy means the child 'would simply pick up the toy and play with it without making any effort to interact with the examiner' - so the design forces the social bid rather than merely permitting it. The examiner is offset such that seeing their face requires an approximately 45-degree head turn or a substantial gaze shift, which makes the target behaviour large enough to register in 2D video from a front-facing camera. And the examiner provides no verbal instruction and simply waits, so any initiation is spontaneous rather than prompted. The toys are standardised in size (3x5x3 cm) and drawn from ADOS-2 and ESCS guidelines, with pseudo-randomised order and a substitution rule if the child shows no interest. Ten seconds from toy placement defines the analysis window. The whole session takes about 10 minutes. The one unexamined element is that the examiner responds contingently - turning to the toy once the child initiates - so the examiner's behaviour is a function of the child's, and the paper does not state whether the examiner is in frame or whether the model could be reading their response rather than the child's initiation.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: A single 40-second video clip designed so that social and non-social content compete within the same display - social being comedians with happy expressions, funny actions and laughter, non-social being backgrounds and two spinning wheels. The selection procedure is documented and is the more careful part of the design: ten candidate clips were rated by three graduate students in special education on valence and arousal, mean positions on the arousal-valence plane were computed, and the clip with the highest mean positive arousal was chosen. That grounds the stimulus in an explicit affective criterion rather than in the experimenters' intuition, though three raters is a thin basis and the raters were adults rating their own emotions rather than children's. The paradigm's strength is that one stimulus simultaneously probes three constructs - where the child looks (social versus non-social competition), whether the child mirrors the displayed expression (imitation), and the concurrent EEG response - so the three modalities are genuinely commensurate. Its limitation is duration: 40 seconds is the shortest observation window in the corpus, and with a single clip there is no test-retest or within-child replication.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Described in a single clause: participants 'were shown different videos containing stimulating scenarios for the movement of the eye in the entire screen'. No stimulus content, category, duration, number, order or instruction is given, and no response was apparently required. The only substantive remark about the paradigm appears in the discussion, where the authors note that 'the short duration of the video scenarios' limits the information in each image and that 'more extended scenarios should be allowed to obtain images with more information in both classes' - which is an observation about image density rather than about behavioural sampling, and it inadvertently identifies the study's core interpretive problem: the quantity being classified is how much of the plot is filled in, not what the child looked at.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Free viewing of two episodes of a commercial television sitcom, chosen on an argued rationale rather than by convenience. The authors state that naturalistic video was selected over 'much more impoverished and artificial stimuli typically employed in earlier studies (such as cropped photographs of grayscale faces)' because movies deliver 'high participant engagement, and reducing confounds to data quality including sleepiness and motion artifacts', and because the same stimuli had proved effective in the group's prior neuroimaging work. Two distinct episodes were used specifically to test whether within-individual reliability holds across stimuli rather than merely across time, which is the stronger test. Three design controls attach to the stimulus. Prior familiarity with each episode was measured on a nine-point scale, participants split into familiar and unfamiliar, and every reported result verified not to differ between them. Gaze during the social-comprehension question pauses in Episode B was excluded. And the analysis showed that gaze to faces differed substantially between the two episodes (Cohen's d 1.15 in the autistic group, 1.70 in controls) while the between-group differences remained stable - establishing that the group effect is a property of the participants rather than of the particular video, which is precisely the confound that stimulus-specific studies elsewhere in this corpus cannot exclude.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Ninety-second sessions of the Guess What? mobile game, structured as either charades - acting out emotions, characters, sports, chores or objects - or a quiz on colours, shapes, numbers and word spellings. The child follows the gameplay while the parent mediates, holding the smartphone against their own forehead with the front-facing camera on the child. Three properties matter. The interaction partner is the child's own parent rather than a clinician or a stranger, which is what makes the elicited speech naturalistic. The session is extremely short, and the total corpus is only 115.5 minutes across 58 children, which the authors turn into a positive by noting that so little data still yielded workable accuracy. And the task structure is only semi-standardised: families choose between two game types and the resulting speech differs accordingly, so the linguistic and prosodic demands are not equated across children - a source of variation the paper does not examine, and one that could interact with age given that a median-5-year-old and a median-9.5-year-old will engage very differently with a spelling quiz.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: A single ADOS-2 Module 3 conversational task, chosen on three stated criteria that jointly amount to a principled sampling argument: it occurs in the second half of the assessment after the warm-up period, so the child is acclimatised; it 'consistently yields the most c-units of all ADOS tasks', so the sample is maximally dense; and it 'has a high standardization of conversational questions, leading to good comparability between participants', using pre-established open-ended interview questions. Two independent prior analyses from this group had converged on this task as the most discriminative. The paradigm's practical strength is that it requires no new protocol - the recording already exists in any videotaped ADOS - and its analytic strength is that all 158 participants completed the identical task, so between-participant differences are not confounded with differences in what was asked. The corresponding limitation is stated by the authors themselves: 'ADOS administration focuses on eliciting autistic features, thus it is possible that our results are overestimated compared to what would be obtained with more naturalistic conversational samples'.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Seven brief movies totalling about five minutes, split four social and three nonsocial by explicit design, each described with its duration and content. The social movies feature actors smiling, frowning, gesturing and using limited verbal expression; the nonsocial movies feature bubbles moving randomly, a mechanical toy puppy and a puppy appearing at screen positions in a fixed right-right-left pattern. The social/nonsocial split is the analytic instrument rather than a background feature: it enables the within-group contrast that produces the paper's most informative result, and it permits the group-by-content interaction test that adjudicates against Martin and colleagues' interpretation. The paradigm requires nothing of the child beyond sitting and watching, which is what makes it viable at 17 months in a clinic waiting room, and the near-equivalent attention rates of 95% and 93% across groups indicate that it holds toddlers' attention in both groups - an important equivalence, since differential attention would otherwise confound any movement measure. One movie, Mechanical-Puppy, showed no significant group difference on any of the three measures, and this is reported consistently rather than omitted.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Narration of Frog, Where Are You?, a 24-page wordless picture book, presented one page at a time on a monitor with no examples given. The choice is the study's enabling methodological decision. Because the book contains no words, the identical stimulus can be administered in any language without translation, and it elicits connected spontaneous narrative rather than repetition, reading or single-word production - so the speech is naturalistic while the content is controlled across participants and across languages. The task has a long history in narrative discourse research in autism and in cross-linguistic work, which the authors cite. Twenty utterances per participant, segmented at natural pauses, were selected for analysis. The analytic level is deliberately the utterance rather than the syllable, on the grounds that 'the utterance is associated with the intonational phrase, the most fundamental unit of prosody argued to be universal across all languages' - the linguistic argument that makes English and Cantonese commensurable, since syllable-level units (final-syllable excursion in English, sentence-final particles in Cantonese) are language-specific and had been the focus of the group's prior work in each language separately.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: The ADOS-2 Telling a Story from a Book task using Tuesday by David Wiesner, a 15-page wordless picture book in which frogs float on lily pads and fly over a town at night. The choice is substantively motivated: the book presents 'unreal and humorous situations, and several mental and emotional states of the characters', so producing a coherent narrative requires inference about characters' internal states, causal linking of unusual events, and management of a fantastical premise - exactly the pragmatic demands the narrative literature identifies as difficult in autism. Being wordless, it supplies no linguistic scaffolding, so the entire narrative is the participant's construction. The resulting samples are short: on average 22 sentences, 323 tokens and 4 minutes 24 seconds, with participants producing utterances for a mean of 13.6 of 15 pages. That brevity is the practical constraint on the whole study - a few hundred words per person is a thin basis for a 15,360-dimensional representation - and the paper's honest performance figures should be read against it.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: A paired preferential-viewing paradigm with social and non-social content presented simultaneously on either side of a central dividing line, six pairs in total, each a 16-second video preceded by a 2-second central red fixation dot, with the 2-second segments excluded from analysis and left-right position counterbalanced. The design's distinctive feature is treating the non-social competitor as an experimental variable rather than a fixed choice. Two competitor classes were used, both selected on empirical rather than theoretical grounds - toys 'selected because many young children with ASD highly preferred these toys during their free play activities at the university-based research center', and spinning animations chosen because 'many young children with ASD's parents report that their children are highly interested in screen time compared to playtime and reading together'. The social videos were deliberately naturalistic, filmed in a playroom with a colourful carpet, shelves and toys, 'to observe how children view a natural environment' - which raises the competitive demand, since the social scene itself contains objects. The comparison then answers a design question the rest of the eye-tracking literature leaves implicit: which competitor best exposes the attentional bias. The answer, that animations beat toys, is directly usable by anyone constructing such a paradigm.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Five short paradigms totalling roughly 40 seconds, each pairing a social element against a non-social competitor within a single display, and each with a stated theoretical rationale drawn from a specific prior literature. The design's strongest feature is its use of position-switched replicates: both the biological motion and the face-versus-dot paradigms were presented twice with left and right positions swapped and the fixation percentages averaged, which controls for any lateral gaze bias - a source of artefact that most paired-display studies in this corpus do not address. The paradigms also span a graded range of social content, from a full face with moving mouth, through point-light biological motion, to a still infant face, against competitors ranging from an abstract moving dot to an electric fan to clipart animals - which is what makes the age-specific ranking analysis informative, since it identifies which level of social content carries signal at which age. The brevity is a practical virtue for 18-month-olds and a limitation for reliability: a 5-second still-image trial yields one fixation percentage per child with no within-child replication from which stability could be estimated.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Three mutually blinded inputs, deliberately mirroring the components of a standard evaluation: 'use of multimodular Device inputs is consistent with current guidelines and recommendations for an evaluation of ASD that include having both caregiver and clinician input, as well as a structured observation of the child'. The video component is the element that distinguishes it from a questionnaire battery, and the rationale given is behavioural rather than technical - clinicians assess 'within a time-constrained clinical encounter where the child may not display behavior characteristic of that seen in the home environment or may become newly behaviorally reactive due to change in environment', so caregiver-recorded home video supplies observation of the child in their ordinary setting. The practical constraints are modest and reported: two videos of 1.5 to 5 minutes, with in-app guidance on framing and lighting; a caregiver questionnaire taking a median 4 minutes 56 seconds; and a clinician questionnaire taking about 10 minutes after a 30-minute visit. Age-banded questionnaire versions differ slightly to reflect developmental trajectories, with the classifier trained to perform equivalently across both.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Semi-spontaneous narrative from a six-picture sequence depicting a birthday party, from a commercially available storytelling toy, chosen as 'easily interpretable by neurotypical children of different ages'. This is a reasonable elicitation - picture-sequence narration is the standard paradigm in the narrative literature, it produces connected spontaneous speech rather than repetition or reading, and holding the task constant across groups is what the authors correctly identify as the one thing they did preserve when the recording arrangements diverged. Two limitations follow from the design's reuse. The autistic recordings were collected for a different study, on discourse and storytelling, so the elicitation was optimised for qualitative narrative analysis rather than acoustic measurement - which is precisely why the original comparison recordings from that project were unusable. And recording durations, utterance counts and speech quantity are not reported for either group, so it is not known whether the two groups produced comparable amounts of speech, which bears on the stability of every averaged acoustic functional.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Entirely absent. Unlike Gaspar and colleagues on the same dataset, who at least state that participants 'were shown different videos containing stimulating scenarios for the movement of the eye in the entire screen', this paper reproduces nothing at all about what was viewed, for how long, or under what conditions. The reader is given no basis on which to judge what behaviour the scanpaths represent. Since the analysis proceeds by treating the resulting plot as a texture image, the absence is internally consistent with the method - the pipeline does not require knowing what generated the trace - but it means the study cannot connect its result to any behavioural construct, and the paper accordingly makes no attempt to.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Ninety-second charades within a mobile game, with the child acting out prompts - emotions, sports, animals, chores - while the parent guesses, and the phone held on the parent's forehead with the front camera facing the child. The design achieves something specific: because the parent must watch the child to guess, the game creates a genuine dyadic social interaction in which the child's gaze toward the parent's face is functionally motivated, rather than a passive viewing task. The authors describe this as supplying 'inherent structure' in camera position, child location and interaction type while leaving the child free of hardware. The corresponding weakness is that the phone is mounted on a moving head, so the coordinate frame in which gaze is measured drifts continuously - which is why the resulting regions cannot be mapped to facial features. The prompts also vary between videos, so the elicited behaviour is not held constant across children.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Not described. The methods section begins from the images and never states what the children viewed. The literature review's one-line summary of the source study is the only information available, and it is not carried into the analysis or used to interpret any result. The limitations section does return to the acquisition question with a substantive recommendation - 'the clinician must ensure that the child is staring at the eye tracker throughout the trials and that the recording environment is free from any distractions that may impact the child's attention' - which correctly identifies attention and environmental control as determinants of data quality, but this is offered as guidance for future collection rather than as a characterisation of the data analysed.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: A 90-second charades game in which the parent holds the phone against their forehead displaying a prompt they cannot see, the child acts it out, and the parent guesses and labels the outcome by tilting the phone. The prompts analysed are 17 CAFE facial-emotion photographs spanning anger, fear, sadness, happiness, surprise, disgust and neutrality, so the task requires the child to recognise an emotion and enact it recognisably to another person - a compound demand the authors characterise carefully as 'a complex interaction between child performance and parent interpretation', functioning as 'a proxy for emotion recognition' that 'likely captures components of theory of mind, metacognition and many other phenomena, as well'. The design's strength is that the parent's guessing behaviour makes the child's enactment functionally consequential rather than performed for a camera. Its corresponding weakness, which the authors state, is that the parent is inside the measurement loop: they set the end of every timed interval and they generate every accuracy label.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Elicited single-word production, with words constituting 95% of the corpus and phrases and sentences the remainder, each analysed sample trimmed to exactly one second at 48 kHz - a duration chosen because it 'not only ensured the integrity of the speech signal but also reduced the computational effort'. No prompt list, elicitation script, examiner instruction or session structure is described. Single-word production is the most constrained speech paradigm in the corpus, which has one methodological advantage - lexical content can in principle be held constant across children, removing a source of acoustic variation - and one significant cost, that prosodic, pragmatic and conversational features cannot be measured at all, so the study cannot address the prosodic constructs that motivate most speech work in autism. Whether lexical content was in fact matched between groups is not stated.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: No purpose-built task - the speech analysed is whatever the child produced during a standard 45-minute ADOS-2 administration. This is the design's principal translational strength: any clinic already recording ADOS sessions holds the raw material, no additional child burden is imposed, and the sampling context is by construction the one in which the reference score is generated. The corresponding limitation is the one the review has noted for other ADOS-derived studies: the assessment is designed to elicit autism-related behaviour, so acoustic differences observed within it may not generalise to spontaneous conversation. The paper does not raise this. A second, more specific constraint is imposed downstream: the severity model requires at least 20 seconds of child speech comprising at least 50 vocalisations, so children who spoke less than this could not be analysed - and in a cohort described as mostly not verbally fluent, that threshold plausibly excludes a meaningful proportion, though the number is not given.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Two purpose-designed five-minute dyadic games preceded by a five-minute familiarisation session, and the paradigm is the study's principal output. Its design merits recording in detail. 'Touch me' uses a stationary robot issuing voice commands; 'Dance with me' uses a moving robot inviting imitation. The two are constructed to dissociate routes to the same observable behaviour, and the authors state the logic explicitly: in 'Dance with me' a child touching the robot 'cannot be classified as a response to the robot's voice command. If at all, this is a phase of some kind of imitation process', while 'the Touch me scenario precludes the emergence of spontaneous child reactions because the NAO robot in this case was not moving'. Designing two conditions so that a single behaviour can be attributed to command-response in one and imitation in the other is a level of construct care that almost nothing else in this review matches - most included studies collect a behavioural stream and ask what separates the groups, whereas this one asks what a given behaviour would mean and builds the paradigm to answer it. Four further properties make the paradigm well suited to the review's concerns: it is short, it requires no verbal response, it is delivered identically to every child by a machine rather than a person - removing examiner variability, which the authors note gives 'predictable and reliable situations' - and it is portable to a kindergarten.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: The paradigm is a structured dyadic conversation, notable in this corpus for being live and social rather than screen-based. Four topic sessions were arranged - Generic question, Hobby sharing, Yes-no question, Question raising - but only the first was analysed, for two stated reasons: gaze behaviour is topic-sensitive so pooling sessions would make segments heterogeneous and harder to classify, and the first session was the longest, yielding the most segments. The six questions of that session are published in an appendix. Two design features deserve credit. Head-mounted rather than remote tracking was chosen deliberately so that head movement is unconstrained and gaze in the scene-camera frame reflects eye-in-socket movement. And the participants were kept naive: they were not told the glasses recorded gaze, were not instructed to keep still, and post-experiment questioning confirmed none had guessed - a control against reactive gaze that most eye-tracking studies in this corpus do not report. The countervailing weakness is that the interviewer is a live human whose own behaviour is not standardised or measured, and who was presumably not blind to group; anything the interviewer did differently with the two groups is baked into the child's gaze.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Three to five minutes of unstructured free play with a toy car in a small room. This is one of the least constrained paradigms in the corpus and that is largely a virtue - there is no script, no examiner prompt, no screen, no wearable, and the electronics are hidden inside the car body specifically so the child is not distracted by them, so what is measured is spontaneous object play. The cost of that freedom is that nothing is standardised: session length varies by up to 67% between children, the presence of a parent or therapist in the room varies and is not recorded, whether anyone interacted with or encouraged the child is not stated, and the floor surface, lighting and available space beyond the room dimensions are not described. Because several features are ratios normalised by total or interactive playtime, some of this variability is absorbed, but the absolute features (jolt count, wheel turn rate, energy) are not obviously duration-invariant. The four-state decomposition is the paradigm's real contribution: by defining not-playing, wheels-only, floor and air play through the joint accelerometer/encoder signature, the authors turn an unstructured session into an interpretable behavioural budget.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: A tablet reimplementation, built in Unity and C#, of five subtests of the Leiter-3 Cognitive Battery, administered following the original test's instruction procedure with the examiner switching between subtests as the manual prescribes. Each scene shows up to five draggable cards at the bottom and up to eight placeholders at the top that capture cards dragged nearby, with distracting stimuli and image detail increasing across five difficulty levels; each child completed 25 tasks, five per level. Instructions were delivered by pointing and gesture without vocal aid, after which the child worked unaided. The design has real strengths: it is a standardised, clinically meaningful task rather than an ad hoc game, it varies difficulty systematically, and it captures fine motor behaviour as a by-product of a cognitive assessment the child would plausibly undergo anyway - which is the most translationally attractive property of the whole approach, since it means no additional testing burden. Two design decisions constrain interpretation. A task counted as complete when all cards had been placed regardless of correctness, but only correctly performed tasks were analysed 'to avoid the noise of the cognitive mistakes for the classification process'. This conditions the analysed sample on cognitive success and, if the groups differ in error rate - which is likely given the IQ ranges and six autistic children below the TD floor - removes trials differentially by group, changing what the retained trajectories represent. No error rates per group are reported, so the size of this effect cannot be assessed. And features are averaged to task level, so within-task temporal structure and trial-to-trial variability, both plausibly informative about motor control, are discarded before modelling.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: The ADOS-2 response-to-name press, executed as the manual prescribes and left unmodified. The child sits at a table absorbed in toys; the clinician stands behind and to one side and calls the child's name in a natural voice; if the child turns and makes eye contact the item ends, otherwise the call is repeated up to three times at roughly 3 s intervals; then up to two reinforced calls follow, delivered with a changed tone or by a parent. Scoring runs 0 (responds to the first call) through 5 (no response after all five). Two properties make this paradigm unusually well suited to automation. It has a precise onset - the moment the name is spoken - which the ASR component recovers automatically and which the authors correctly identify as removing a source of manual-annotation error; and it has a precise, short response window of 3 s fixed by the protocol itself. Two properties make it hard. The clinically defined response is 'turn and face the implementer with eye contact rather than glance to the side', which is a conjunction of orientation and gaze that no single sensor captures, and which the cascade approximates rather than measures - eye contact per se is never assessed, only head yaw and whether a face was detected by the rear camera. And the caller's position varies between left and right rear, which is why two rear cameras are required and why the head-pose channel depends on the child turning towards whichever camera happens to be behind the caller.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: A two-stage computer game built specifically for this study, informed by picture-exchange approaches in which cards depicting facial expressions convey concepts non-verbally. Stage S1 (face recognition): three photographs of Japanese women are displayed in a row beside a target figure, and the child must identify which candidate matches the target. Stage S2 (expression matching): the same women are shown with happy, sad and surprised expressions, with 'happy' as the target. All stimuli come from the JAFFE database. Children were familiarised with example images first, and conditions were checked as suitable before the full run of 240 game images. The design has clear merits - it is engaging rather than passive, it has an objectively correct answer on every trial so gaze can be interpreted against task demands, and it targets a behaviour (facial expression processing) with strong theoretical links to autism. Three features constrain what it can show. The stimuli are other-race for this sample, and the other-race face effect is a documented modulator of both face-processing performance and gaze distribution - the paper cites this literature but not in relation to its own design. Only static images are used, so no dynamic or interactive social content is present. And the analysis discards trial structure entirely: fixations are pooled into region counts and durations, so whether the child looked at the correct candidate, in what order, or how their strategy evolved across 240 trials is not represented, even though the single-child illustration in Fig. 7 shows exactly that kind of trial-level reasoning being informative.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: The Contextual Assessment of Social Skills, slightly modified - a semi-structured assessment of conversational ability designed to mimic a real-life first-time encounter. Each participant held two 3-minute face-to-face conversations with two different confederates: an interested condition, in which the confederate engaged verbally and non-verbally, and a bored condition, in which the confederate signalled disengagement through one-word answers, few follow-up questions, neutral affect and reduced eye contact and gesture. Only the interested condition is analysed here. The confederate protocol is specified to an unusual degree: 10 confederates (3 male, 7 female, all native English speakers, undergraduate or BA-level research staff), blind to diagnostic status and unaware of the dependent variables, trained to speak no more than 50% of the time, to wait 10 s before initiating and 5 s before re-initiating after a pause, and otherwise to converse naturally; the prompt given to both parties is quoted verbatim. That combination - a live, unscripted, genuinely social task with a standardised and blinded partner - is close to the ideal for this literature, since it preserves naturalism without letting the partner's behaviour vary with what they believe about the participant. Two design choices constrain the result. Audio was discarded from both the AI and human conditions, so speech content, prosody and turn-taking timing - all diagnostically informative and all captured on the recording - are excluded by design in order to make the human-AI comparison fair. And only the participant's video enters the model, an approach the authors name explicitly as monadic and identify as a limitation: 'even if the context of the conversation is dyadic, our AI-based analysis is not dyadic since it discards the information from the confederate'. The bored condition, which would test whether the coordination signature survives a change in the partner's behaviour, was collected and left unanalysed.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Passive free viewing of 82 static images, presented in two sessions of roughly three minutes each with each image shown for 3 s and a 0.5 s grey mask between images, with the only instruction being to observe. Four stimulus categories were chosen 'according to the behavioural characteristics of children with ASD': facial images, social scenarios, animated characters and synthetic patterns. Three properties make this among the better-designed paradigms in the corpus. It is short and undemanding by explicit design, because the authors treat children's limited sustained attention as a constraint on the method rather than as a nuisance. It varies stimulus type systematically, which permits the study's most practically useful analysis - a ranking of all 82 images by discriminative power, showing facial images strongest (499.59) and animated characters weakest (356.27), and demonstrating that dropping to the best 60 images costs no accuracy while dropping to a random 60 costs a great deal. That result is a concrete contribution to protocol design that most eye-tracking studies here are not positioned to make.
