And the grey mask, introduced as a simple inter-stimulus interval, turns out to carry signal, since fixations landing on it are one of the three factors the authors identify as driving model scores. That last point is also the paradigm's weakness: dwelling on a blank grey screen is at least as much a measure of disengagement from the task as of atypical social attention, and the paper's own observation that 3-4 year olds in the comparison group generate 'meaningless fixations that fall on the gray mask' concedes that the same behaviour arises from ordinary inattention.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: None. This is the only included study with no elicitation paradigm: the behavioural sample is whatever 252 people chose to post on Twitter over five years, unconstrained in topic, audience, purpose, length or timing. The consequence that matters most is topic confounding, and it goes unaddressed throughout. The autistic group was assembled by searching biographies for autism-related keywords including 'ActuallyAutistic', a hashtag whose function is to mark autistic people's own commentary on autism; people who identify that way in their profile will frequently tweet about autism, disability, sensory experience, diagnosis, accommodation and advocacy. No preprocessing step removed autism-related vocabulary from the tweets, no topic model or lexical analysis was run, and no ablation tested whether the classifier still works with such terms masked. So the most parsimonious explanation of the 84.3% figure - that BERT is detecting subject matter rather than communication style - is neither tested nor mentioned. The paper's own framing invites this reading, since its introduction speaks of identifying 'linguistic patterns, emotional expressions, and communication styles', which is a style hypothesis, while its method offers nothing that could separate style from topic.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Six short movies, each under 90 seconds, presented on a tablet during the clinic visit, with the social/non-social split used as an internal control rather than as incidental variety. The four social movies feature human actors making eye contact, smiling, gesturing, reciting nursery rhymes and behaving comically - Blowing Bubbles (64 s), Spinning Top (53 s), Rhymes and Toys (49 s) and Make Me Laugh (56 s) - and two of them deliberately include both successful and failed attempts, which creates natural moments for affective response. The two non-social movies show dynamic toys or animations: Mechanical Puppy (25 s) and Dog in Grass Right-Right-Left (40 s), the latter using a structured spatial sequence. The design has three strengths worth carrying into the synthesis. It is short, passive and requires nothing of the child, so it can be administered opportunistically to 17-36 month olds in a clinic room. The social/non-social contrast provides a within-subject test of whether the measured signal is specific to social content, and the answer - large effects for social movies, medium effects for non-social - is more informative than a single accuracy figure, because it shows the complexity difference is amplified by social content but not created by it. And the environment is controlled in a low-tech way that suits the setting: caregiver holds the child, tablet at a fixed 60 cm, everyone else stands behind the pair to reduce distraction. The limitation is that passive viewing elicits a narrower behavioural range than interaction, and the authors identify live interpersonal interaction as the natural next step.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: The Facial Emotion Identification Test, a validated instrument that uses morphing to generate expressions at varying intensity, including deliberately weak ones - which is central to the paper's argument, since the finding it converges on concerns subtle rather than prototypical expressions. Each trial: a one-second central fixation cross, then a face for 5 seconds, then a verbal response naming the emotion. Adults saw 21 images (three each of happiness, sadness, fear, anger, surprise, disgust, neutral) and children 32 (eight each of happiness, sadness, anger, surprise), all in random order. Three properties make this among the better paradigms in the corpus. It has an objectively correct answer on every trial, so task performance and gaze behaviour are separately measurable - and the result is striking: FEIT scores were essentially identical across groups (adults 15.5, 14.5 and 14.3 out of 21 for controls, autism and schizophrenia; children 22.1 and 22.2 out of 32), meaning the groups recognised the emotions equally well while looking at the faces differently. Any gaze difference therefore cannot be attributed to differential task success. The stimulus set is systematically structured by emotion, which is what makes per-image weighting meaningful and interpretable rather than an arbitrary ensemble. And the one-second fixation cross standardises the starting gaze position across trials and participants, so scan-path measures begin from a common origin. The paradigm's limitations are the short trial (5 seconds, giving at most 600 gaze samples), the static stimuli, and the copyright restriction that prevents the images being reproduced or shared.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: None, and its absence defines what the study can and cannot show. There is no task, protocol, prompt, stimulus or elicitation; the behavioural sample is whatever thousands of people chose to do with a communication app over two and a half years. This yields ecological validity that no laboratory paradigm can match - these are real communicative acts serving real needs, not responses to a screen in a clinic - but it also means the behaviour is confounded with everything that varies between users: how the app was configured, who set it up, what vocabulary was loaded, what the user was trying to say, how much support they had, and how long they had owned the device. One design consequence is handled well and is worth recording: the app was fully customisable, so different users operate on different icon arrangements, and the authors correctly reject spatial modelling on this basis - 'between participant or between group analyses are difficult due to the customizability of the app which allows different participants to all potentially create a different base (i.e. set of icons) upon which they operate'. That is a clear-sighted rejection of a representation that would have appeared informative while measuring only how each user had arranged their own screen. The windowing scheme is the substitute for a trial structure, and its trade-off is stated explicitly: longer windows capture more cohesive patterns but produce fewer pseudo-samples and discard short sessions, shorter windows produce more samples but distort the patterns.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: The strongest paradigm in this review, judged by the fit between construct, task and measurement. Three tasks were designed by adapting the Early Social Communication Scales manual of Mundy et al. together with validated behaviour-extraction techniques, each targeting one theoretically distinct form of joint attention: initiation, which indexes a child's motivation to share attention and manifests as triadic gaze shifting between object and partner; low-level response, following an indication to a nearby object; and high-level response, following an indication to an object across the room, requiring the child to turn. The decomposition is not arbitrary - it maps onto an established taxonomy with different developmental and clinical significance, and the study's most interesting result is that the three tasks behave differently, with initiation alone carrying severity information. Three further design features deserve credit. The whole protocol takes a single 10-minute session with one consumer camera in a quiet room, so the paradigm is genuinely deployable. Repetition is built in (up to ten IJA trials, five per RJA task), and the authors monitored engagement across repetitions with a purpose-built compliance score analysed by two-way mixed ANOVA, concluding that both groups habituate and recommending that future models be trained on the first five to ten repetitions - a protocol-optimisation finding derived from data rather than assumed. The countervailing concern arises from that same compliance analysis: autistic children showed early disengagement specifically at the start of RJA tasks, so an unknown portion of what the RJA detection models separate is willingness to attend to the examiner at all rather than joint attention per se. The authors raise this as a limitation for severity modelling but not for detection.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: Not reported. The paper never states what the children were looking at when the gaze data were recorded, how long the recording lasted, what the display or eye tracker were, or how the scanpaths were rendered into images. It describes only the general definitions of fixation, blink and saccade from the source experiment, and states that the source study 'provides these visualised scanpath images which is used in the work as a biomarker'. So the study models a representation of a behaviour elicited by an unknown task. Two consequences follow for interpretation. Nothing can be said about whether the discriminative signal is social - the whole rationale offered in the introduction concerns looking at eyes and mouths, but if the stimuli were not faces that rationale does not apply. And the rendering choices that turned gaze coordinates into pictures - line width, colour, marker size, axis scaling, whether fixation duration is encoded as circle radius - are properties of the source dataset that determine what a convolutional network can extract, and none is described.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: Three different paradigms pooled as though equivalent. Eigsti recorded 30-minute free play sessions; Nadig recorded approximately 10 minutes of parent-child free play; Flusberg recorded natural mother-child interaction in infants and toddlers. The conversation partner is not held constant and the paper's own terminology drifts - the echolalia feature is defined by repetition of bigrams 'originally spoken by the therapist', the discourse-coherence feature is described as similarity 'between BERT embeddings of consecutive sentences of therapist and child', SHAP results refer to 'trainer-child (t-c) discourse', and the corpus descriptions say the partner was a parent or the mother. Whoever the partner was, they are a live participant whose own language shapes every child-partner feature, and pragmatic behaviour in a child differs systematically with whether the interlocutor is a parent or a clinician. Since child-partner discourse coherence ranks among the top contributing features, this is not a peripheral concern. The countervailing strength is the paradigm's ecological character: these are unstructured natural conversations rather than elicited tasks, so the pragmatic behaviours the features target - taking initiative, building on statements, sustaining a topic - had a genuine opportunity to occur.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: The best-designed stimulus battery in this corpus, and described with a care that the rest of the methods does not match. Four tasks were chosen on three explicit criteria - strong construct performance, demonstrated between-group discrimination, and relation to autism symptoms in prior work with school-aged children. Activity Monitoring shows two actresses using child-directed speech and directing gaze to each other or to the activity between them, with clusters of colourful but irrelevant toys as deliberate distractors. Dyadic Bid is the most carefully constructed: an actor periodically addresses the camera while the two non-speaking actors either look silently at the viewer - included both as a control, to ensure the participant is not merely following a face that looks at them, and as a competing-face distractor - or look down with subtle hand movements, included as a foil controlling for the salience of the speaker's mouth movements. Social Referencing films escalating stressful episodes with distinct escalation, critical-event and resolution phases, such as a balloon inflated until it bursts. Theory of Mind implements a naturalistic false-belief scenario in which an antagonist repeatedly relocates objects unbeknown to a protagonist. Building explicit controls and foils into the stimuli rather than relying on post-hoc statistical adjustment is the kind of design reasoning that most studies here omit entirely. Against this, exposure to individual clips was extremely uneven - Table 6 shows clips viewed 92, 90, 62, 61 or 60 times alongside eighteen clips viewed exactly once - so the effective stimulus set is much smaller than the 43 clips listed, and participants did not all see the same material.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: Inherited and described at second hand, but more informatively than by the other reuses. Children watched videos built to attract them - colourful balloons, animated characters, elements whose position changed during the study - and some videos included a live host who spoke to the child and attempted to direct attention towards both visible and hidden elements. That last detail matters for interpretation: a live host issuing verbal direction makes the task partly a joint-attention and instruction-following probe rather than pure free viewing, so the resulting scan-paths reflect responsiveness to social direction as well as spontaneous visual preference. What is not stated in this paper is how many videos each child saw, how long they lasted, how a session was segmented into the roughly nine scan-paths per child, or how gaze coordinates were rendered into images - the last being the determinant of what a convolutional network can extract from the drawing.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: There is no experimental paradigm; the behavioural data are generated by routine clinical practice. The surveillance protocol nonetheless functions as a structured behavioural assessment: 60 age-related milestones across gross motor, fine motor, language and personal-social domains, based in part on the Denver Developmental Screening Test, with 38 assessed up to 24 months and between four and nine checked at each of nine age bins from six weeks to six years, results recorded per milestone, plus systematic elicitation of parental concerns about development and hearing at each visit. Two features distinguish this from the elicitation paradigms elsewhere in the review. It is universal and repeated - every child in the population is assessed roughly eleven times by a trained nurse over six years, at zero marginal cost to the research - which is a scale of behavioural observation no research protocol can approach. And it is unoptimised for the task: the milestones were chosen for general developmental surveillance, not for autism detection, so the model works with whatever the protocol happens to record. The authors identify this as a limitation and name specific candidate red flags that fall outside it - head lag at three months, raising hands to be picked up at six months, nodding at twelve months - which is a concrete and testable proposal for improving the instrument rather than the algorithm.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: None. There is no task, protocol or elicitation - the images are photographs. This matters for the review's framing because a facial-photograph classifier is not measuring behaviour at all: it is measuring appearance. The paper's own premise makes this explicit, grounding the approach in claimed morphological differences in the upper face and mid-face rather than in anything the child does. The attached expression recognition module, trained on AffectNet, does concern behaviour, but AffectNet contains adult and general-population faces annotated for emotion and has no autism labels, so that module says nothing about autism and is never linked to the classification result.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: None. Structural MRI requires no task, and the phenotype fields are administrative records of assessments conducted before and independently of the modelling. This is the defining structural difference between this study and the rest of the review: every included study that measures behaviour must decide what to ask a person to do, and that decision shapes what can be detected - a point the free-play study demonstrates empirically when its 90-second protocol fails to elicit restricted and repetitive behaviour at all. Here there is nothing to elicit, and the corresponding cost is that nothing about the person's behaviour is observed either.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: A structured face-to-face conversation with an interviewer seated 80 cm away, filmed from the side by a fixed camera so that child and adult occupy equal halves of the frame - a framing choice that matters because the analysis requires movement time series from both people at comparable spatial resolution. The conversation had four sessions and only the first was analysed, being the longest and serving to familiarise the two people with each other, with its questions published in an appendix. Only videos longer than 45 s were retained, to give a sufficient frequency range and stable wavelet estimates; all 41 qualified. The paradigm has three properties that suit the construct particularly well. It is genuinely interactive with a live partner, so spontaneous coordination has an opportunity to occur, unlike the screen-based paradigms that dominate this review. It is unscripted in its motor content, so the movement being measured is whatever the conversation produced rather than a prescribed action. And because both parties are recorded, the measurement is symmetric - the same procedure yields the adult's time series as the child's, which is what makes a dyadic measure possible at all. The countervailing weakness is that the interviewer is a live human whose own movement is half the signal and who was presumably not blind to group, so any systematic difference in how the interviewer behaved with the two groups enters the coherence directly and cannot be separated from the child's contribution.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Two tasks, both taken from ADOS-2 Modules 3 and 4 as administered rather than constructed for the study: interview responses and picture-book story recounting. The choice has one clear advantage and one clear cost. The advantage is standardisation - the same certified administrator elicited both from every participant under a protocol designed to sample social communication, so the elicitation is as comparable across participants as anything in this review. The cost is that the speech analysed was produced during the diagnostic session itself, so the examiner's behaviour toward each participant is part of the context and is unobserved, and the language sample is not independent of the encounter that produced the label. The paper is explicit about what it does with the material: the entire spoken output is evaluated 'without setting specific requirements for text length, speaking duration, or word count', and the analysis addresses 'patterns of lexicogrammar selection from participants' responses' rather than the dynamics of interaction - so turn-taking, latency and interactional contingency are outside scope by design. The contrast between the two tasks is the most valuable feature of the paradigm and is exploited properly: interview is dialogic and socially demanding, picture-book recounting is monologic and scaffolded by the stimulus, and the consistent superiority of interview transcripts across all four models and both annotation methods is a within-study replication of the paper's theoretical claim.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: None. There is no task, protocol or elicitation - the data are photographs. The framing gap is worth stating plainly: the title announces 'Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection' and the introduction argues that 'facial expressions and emotional expressions can help in early detection and diagnosis of ASD', but no expression is labelled, detected, elicited or analysed anywhere in the paper. The features extracted are generic image descriptors, and the classification target is the image's folder. The word 'emotion' does not recur in the method, results or conclusion. So the study measures no behaviour at all while describing itself as behavioural, which places it further outside this review's modality scope than the companion study on the same dataset, that one at least having attached a genuine facial-expression module trained on AffectNet.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: Instructed posed expression production, as designed into both corpora. This is the canonical easy case for facial expression recognition: prototypical, maximally intense, produced deliberately, and captured at the peak frame - CK+ explicitly uses 'the peak frame of each sequence' because 'it includes the greatest information relating to emotions'. Selecting peak frames maximises separability and is standard practice for benchmarking, but it removes precisely the subtlety the paper claims to address. The paradigm gap is therefore twofold: posed rather than spontaneous, and peak rather than continuous.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: A purpose-built drag-and-drop game, and the design reasoning behind it is the paradigm's most valuable feature. The child drags an image from the screen centre to a target at one of eight positions spaced 45 degrees apart while avoiding distractors, with the settings panel allowing category, scene count and distractor number to be varied - all held constant here. Three design decisions address problems that recur throughout this review. No verbal instructions were given: the examiner deliberately withheld them so the child could work out the game's logic independently, and the two support mechanisms provided - a video tutorial triggered by the play button and a vibration cue on the image to be moved - were introduced explicitly 'to avoid stressful social situations and improve engagement and autonomy'. Designing the elicitation to minimise social demand, in a study measuring motor rather than social behaviour, removes a confound that several other studies here carry unexamined. The eight-target arrangement at fixed angular spacing then makes rotation normalisation possible, so trajectories to different targets become comparable - a design choice that pays off directly in the analysis. And recording is restricted to completed drags from image to target, with incomplete drags and stray touches excluded, so the measured behaviour is well defined. The costs are that session duration varied between children without being modelled, and that a single session per child leaves no within-child stability estimate.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: None described. The paper does not state what the individuals were doing when their facial expressions, heart rate and body temperature were recorded - whether they were viewing stimuli, engaged in a task, at rest, or in any other condition. This matters directly for the variables measured: emotion probabilities, heart rate and body temperature are all state-dependent, so without knowing the eliciting condition their values are uninterpretable, and any systematic difference in condition between the two label groups would be indistinguishable from a group effect.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None. Respondents completed a ten-item screening questionnaire, answered by a parent, relative or health professional in the toddler and child bands and by the person themselves in the adult band. The distinction from the observational paradigms elsewhere in this review is total: nothing was elicited, observed or measured, and the record contains one person's answers to questions about another person's characteristics.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: The one-legged standing test, administered on a pressure sensor with the child facing the experimenter and multiple trials conducted. Four properties make it well suited to the purpose. It is a standard clinical balance assessment with an established literature, so the construct is not invented for the study. It is brief and requires no verbal instruction beyond the request to stand on one leg, no stimulus, no screen and no social interaction - so a motor measurement is obtained without the social demand that confounds several other motor studies in this review. It was already part of the routine medical examination, which is what made near-complete population coverage feasible. And the authors identify a specific analytic target within it that most balance studies overlook: the transition from two-legged to one-legged standing, which they treat as 'a feed-forward process that is necessary to achieve the one-legged standing outcome' and therefore as informative about anticipatory postural control rather than only about steady-state sway. Limitations of the paradigm are that a single brief task samples a narrow slice of balance ability - the authors call for 'a broader range of balance cues' - and that no test-retest data exist, so the stability of the measures within a child is unknown.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: None. No task, paradigm or elicitation procedure exists in either corpus. The children in the Piosenka images were photographed for reasons unrelated to any study, and the YTUIA videos were recorded by families and organisations for their own purposes. This has a specific analytic consequence the paper does not draw: the introduction motivates the work through evidence about facial expression dynamics - that autistic infants 'exhibit more complex facial expressions than their typically developing classmates, particularly in the eyebrows and lips' - but nothing in an uncontrolled still photograph or an isolated video frame holds expression, pose, gaze, emotional context or elicitation constant, so a difference in expression between classes cannot be distinguished from a difference in the circumstances under which the two classes of image were taken.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: None, by design. The EEG was recorded 'during participants' relaxed states to ensure artifact-free data', so no task was administered, no stimulus presented and no behaviour elicited. This is the defining difference between the electrophysiological branch and the behavioural studies charted elsewhere in this review, and it cuts both ways. Resting-state acquisition is maximally undemanding - it requires no cooperation with instructions, no verbal ability and no social engagement, which is why it reaches participants that task-based paradigms cannot - and it also means there is no behavioural or cognitive event to which any observed difference can be anchored. A group difference in resting spectral power is a difference in ambient neural state, interpretable only against a physiological literature, whereas a group difference in gaze during a social scene or in utterance length during play is interpretable directly.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: A 90-second free play episode with a fixed toy set spanning miniature or representational toys, cause-and-effect toys and construction toys, preceded by 5-10 minutes of rapport building. The instruction is reproduced verbatim in the paper and is tightly specified: allow the child to explore and play independently for 90 seconds; do not initiate any conversation or interaction; respond appropriately and neutrally if the child initiates - if the child hands the examiner a toy, smile and say thank you but start no new conversation. This is a well-designed paradigm for its purpose. It is genuinely brief, it places almost no demand on the child, it requires no screen or instrumentation, and the examiner's role is constrained precisely enough to be reproducible. The authors state its cost in the same terms as its benefit: 1.5 minutes of child time and 10-15 minutes of coder time, against a session too short to elicit repetitive behaviours or to give the child an opportunity to initiate social interaction. Both halves of that trade-off are confirmed in the results - the play and communication indicators separate the groups while the restricted-repetitive indicators are degenerate - and the authors' proposed fix, lengthening the session and building in opportunities for initiation, follows directly.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: ADOS-2 Module 4 - 15 standardised interactive activities over 40 to 60 minutes, administered by research-certified psychiatrists, with behaviour rated on 32 items against published criteria. Module 4 is the version for verbally fluent adolescents and adults. This is the most rigorously standardised behavioural paradigm anywhere in this review: the activities are prescribed, the coding criteria are published and detailed, administrators require formal certification, and the instrument's psychometrics are established in the literature (the paper cites sensitivity 89.6 and specificity 82.2 for the algorithms in their validation populations, figures that refer to autism against non-autism rather than against schizophrenia). Two properties of the paradigm are directly relevant to the review's synthesis. It is designed around social presses - the examiner actively creates situations that require reciprocity, so it samples behaviour under demand rather than passively - which is why it elicits far more of the phenotype in an hour than the 90-second free-play or 3-minute video paradigms charted elsewhere. And its cost is the mirror image of the automated approaches: an hour of certified clinician time per participant, which is exactly the bottleneck those approaches exist to relieve. This study is therefore useful as a reference point for what a full-cost, fully standardised behavioural assessment achieves - and the answer, for the autism-versus-schizophrenia question, is an AUC of about 0.56.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Not described, for either corpus, and the omission is more damaging here than in most studies because the paper's substantive claim is prosodic. The motivating account is that autistic speech is monotonous, 'lacking the typical variations in pitch, intonation, and expressive elements' - but prosody is determined as much by what a speaker is doing as by who they are. Spontaneous conversation, responding to an adult's questions, reading aloud, repeating modelled utterances and playing all produce systematically different intonation contours. Nothing is stated about what the children in either corpus were doing when recorded, whether an adult or a robot was present, what was said to them, or whether the elicitation differed between the clinic-recorded atypical children and the school-recorded typical ones. De-Enigma was collected within a robot-assisted autism education project, so its vocalisations arise from a specific and unusual interactive context that is not characterised at all. Without a task description, a prosodic difference between groups cannot be attributed to speaker characteristics rather than to what each group was asked to do.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: None, and this is the study's chief methodological attraction. There is no elicitation, no examiner, no instruction and no observation effect - people wrote what they wanted to write, at their own pace, over nine years. Against the 90-second free-play sample, the 3-minute video and the 40-minute standardised assessment charted elsewhere in this review, a user's full Twitter timeline is an enormous and ecologically valid behavioural record. What the absence of a paradigm removes is any control over what the two groups were writing about, and here the comparison is unfavourable: because the positive class was selected by participation in a hashtag community, its members were writing about autism, diagnosis, accommodation, sensory experience and ableism far more than a background sample would. Removing the explicit autism keyword list attenuates but cannot eliminate this, since topic pervades vocabulary, syntax and stance well beyond a list of sixteen terms. Naturalistic data therefore buys freedom from task effects at the price of losing any guarantee that the two samples are doing the same thing.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: The ADOS, a semi-structured 40-60 minute assessment comprising free play and activities modelled on everyday play, administered identically to both groups, with average session lengths of about 46 minutes in each partition. The authors set out the paradigm choice as a considered trade-off rather than a default, and their statement of it is the clearest in this review: automating social-symptom measurement has usually required 'over-standardization ... at the expense of less ecological feature presentation', whereas the ADOS activities 'are specifically designed to be representative of naturalistic interactions, with a high amount of prompts aiming at eliciting communication and reciprocal exchanges in a restricted time period'. That formulation identifies exactly what a good behavioural paradigm needs - dense elicitation of the target behaviour within a bounded time, without collapsing into a single narrow construct - and it sits usefully between the two poles this review has charted. At one pole, the 90-second free-play study demonstrated empirically that a brief sample cannot reach restricted and repetitive behaviour at all; at the other, response-to-name and screen-based paradigms deliver a clean readout of one construct. Forty-six minutes of ADOS spans the phenotype, and the interpretability analysis confirms it - the models' confidence relates to joint attention, social overtures, eye contact, pointing, showing, sensory exploration and hand mannerisms, which is most of the diagnostic space. The cost is that the paradigm requires a trained ADOS examiner, so it does not remove the expert bottleneck that motivates the field, and the authors' proposal that this could eventually move to home settings without specialised equipment is aspirational rather than demonstrated.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: None for the autism data; the children were filmed by their families for their own purposes. For the affect layer the paper does define a paradigm, and describes it carefully: five annotators, all trained on the software and the protocol beforehand, watched the videos and gave instantaneous ratings of arousal and valence between 0 and 5 using a mouse, keyboard or joystick, with the authors present throughout to ensure the protocol was followed and with worked examples supplied. Ratings were averaged across annotators per frame and normalised to the -1 to 1 range used in the affect literature. The absence of a paradigm on the data side has a specific consequence the study half-recognises: what a child is doing when filmed determines their expression, and in SSBD every autistic child is by construction engaged in a stereotypy while the comparison children are doing something unknown - so the classifier and the affect model are both operating across an uncontrolled difference in activity as well as any difference in the children.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: None, by design. Images were captured during ordinary school activities with no instruction, elicitation or standardisation, which is the correct choice for a framework whose entire argument is that brief structured assessments miss daily variation. The cost is that nothing is held constant: a child running outdoors, sitting in a classroom and eating a meal differ in exertion, posture, distance from the camera, head angle and thermal environment, and all of these affect both the measured skin temperature and the appearance of the face to a mood classifier. The paper does not report distance to subject, viewing angle, or whether images within a setting were taken in a single session. What is missing is the analysis that this data structure uniquely enables and that the study's own thesis demands: whether a child's predicted state varies across the day and across contexts, which would be evidence of continuous behavioural measurement rather than of static classification. Instead the design collapses multiple images per child into a single per-child severity label, which discards precisely the temporal variation the framework exists to capture.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: None. No task, elicitation or standardisation exists. The children were photographed by whoever took the pictures, for their own purposes, under uncontrolled conditions. This matters for the paper's premise in a specific way: the motivating literature concerns craniofacial morphometry - measurements that require controlled pose, distance and camera geometry to be meaningful - and none of those is available in web-sourced photographs, so even if the morphometric claims were correct the data could not test them.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: Play-based spontaneous speech, but not one paradigm - four. Eigsti recorded 30-minute play sessions, Nadig 10-minute free play followed by a cleanup period, Warren toy play of unspecified duration and Kuczaj 30-minute spontaneous speech samples. Spontaneous play speech is a good elicitation context for the constructs of interest: it produces enough utterances to estimate MLU stably, it imposes minimal demand, and it captures conversational turn-taking with an adult, which the ratio features exploit. The heterogeneity is handled only partly. The paper normalises the three count-based features as ratios to the investigator specifically 'to normalize for different transcript lengths', which is the right instinct and addresses the most obvious threat. It does not address that a 10-minute free-play session with a cleanup period and a 30-minute spontaneous speech sample differ in more than length - in topic structure, in how much the adult initiates, and in what kinds of utterance are elicited - or that one corpus's session duration is simply unknown.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Walking trials in one corpus and robot-assisted therapy sessions in the other, neither described in detail. The gait paradigm is well chosen for the review's purposes: walking requires no verbal ability, imposes no social demand, is producible by very young children, and yields a motor signal that can be measured objectively - which the paper argues explicitly, noting that diagnosis 'often requires speech-based tests' but 'at the early detection stage, many young children may not yet be able to speak'. That argument identifies a real gap in the assessment landscape, since the language-based measures charted elsewhere in this review are inapplicable to precisely the youngest and least verbal children for whom early detection matters most. Two things weaken the execution. Only one of ten walking trials per child is retained, and that trial was chosen with knowledge of the diagnosis, so within-child variability - which is itself a candidate marker in motor studies - is discarded by a non-blind procedure. And in DREAM the recorded movements arise from therapy interaction with only upper-body joints available, so the gait construct that motivates the paper is not measurable in the second dataset at all.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: None, by the nature of the behaviour - cries were captured opportunistically when they occurred. That is appropriate and unavoidable, and the paper handles the resulting variability better than most: it excluded pain-associated cries, retained 'only pure crying sounds' with segments containing other vocalisations or non-empty-mouth cries eliminated, and recorded the eliciting cause for each cry. Reporting the cause distribution is genuinely good practice and appears nowhere else in this review. It also reveals a further imbalance: complaint or discomfort accounted for 74.20% of autistic and 67.75% of typically developing cries, with sleepiness, hunger and anxiety making up the remainder at 25.80% and 32.25%. Cry acoustics vary with what prompted the cry, so aetiology is a third variable covarying with class alongside age and setting, and it is not adjusted for.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: None. Respondents answered ten AQ-10 statements about themselves. Nothing was observed, elicited or measured.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: A purpose-designed structured interaction protocol of 8 to 10 minutes per child, comprising simple games, gesture imitation exercises and short conversational prompts, explicitly intended 'to elicit both social and motor behaviors'. This is among the better-judged paradigms in the review. It is short enough to be practical in a clinic or school, it actively elicits the target behaviours rather than waiting for them to occur, and it spans the social and motor domains within one session - which matters because a study charted elsewhere here demonstrated empirically that a 90-second free-play sample cannot reach the restricted and repetitive dimension at all. The gesture-imitation component is a targeted elicitation of motor imitation, a construct with an established clinical literature in autism, and its inclusion means the protocol probes something specific rather than sampling behaviour generically. Against this, the tasks are described only in outline: no script, no item list, no ordering, no statement of whether the examiner's prompts were standardised, and no report of how children who declined a task were handled. The protocol is therefore reproducible in spirit and not in detail.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: None, and its absence is more damaging for the gelotophobia component than for any other study in this review. Gelotophobia is a fear about how other people's laughter is intended - a dispositional appraisal, elicited only when laughter is present and directed at the person. The images here were taken in unknown contexts with no laughter, no social interaction and no ridicule, so the condition the model is asked to detect has no eliciting circumstance anywhere in the data. The GELOPH<15> exists precisely because the construct is an internal state accessible through self-report rather than through observation, and the paper cites it as validated while proposing to bypass it with a still photograph. For the autism component the paradigm absence carries the usual cost: expression, pose, gaze and emotional context all vary freely and none is held constant across the two classes.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: None. The children were photographed in unknown circumstances for purposes unrelated to any study. This matters for the study's own premise, since the morphometric literature it invokes - intercanthal distance, mid-face height, philtrum length - depends on controlled pose, distance and camera geometry, none of which is available in web-sourced photographs. Even if the morphometric claims were correct, the data could not test them.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: None. The children were photographed outside any study, in unknown circumstances. This is a specific problem for the emotion task, which the paper does not raise: an emotion label attached to a photograph taken for unknown reasons has no eliciting condition, so what the child was feeling, whether the expression was posed or spontaneous, and what prompted it are all unknown - and the paper's own argument is that autistic facial expression differs from the neurotypical patterns on which such labels are usually based, which makes the labelling process itself the thing most in need of scrutiny.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: None. The photographs were taken outside any study, in unknown circumstances, for both portions of the corpus. The paper's description of what the network extracts - face shape, expression and skin texture - underlines the consequence: with no task and no controlled acquisition, expression at the captured instant is free to vary with why the photograph was taken, and skin texture with the camera that took it.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Free viewing of mixed static and dynamic stimuli. Dynamic content comprised short videos with engaging elements such as cartoon characters and balloons designed to attract children's attention; static content comprised images of faces, objects and scenes. No areas of interest are defined, no fixation or saccade extraction is performed, and no social-versus-nonsocial contrast is computed - the abstract's framing as social attention tasks is inherited from the dataset description rather than operationalised in the analysis.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: There is no task or paradigm. The instrument is the ten-item Quantitative Checklist for Autism in Toddlers (Q-CHAT-10) of Allison et al., reproduced in full in Table 2, plus seven auxiliary variables. Behaviour is entirely caregiver-reported and retrospective.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Static photographs, no stimulus, no interaction, no session. The construct measured is facial morphology, though the abstract describes the target as ASD-related behaviours and the keyword list includes eye tracking, which appears nowhere in the method.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Passive viewing of a ten-second silent movie in which a young Asian woman articulates the English letters, chosen on the reasoning - well argued from the prior literature reviewed - that a speaking face is a more discriminating stimulus than a static one, since gaze duration on inner facial features is reduced specifically while the face is speaking. The stimulus choice is one of the better-motivated in the corpus. Against that, the workflow section describes classifying autism severity from a 2-min ET video, which contradicts the ten-second stimulus and is never reconciled.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Static photographs with no stimulus, interaction or session. The construct is facial morphology and texture, justified by the premise that developmental problems affecting face features are often associated with fundamental brain disorders.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Not reported. Features are said to be extracted per instructional segment, and the eye-movement subsets are labelled General and Attention, but no task, stimulus, instruction, session length or protocol is described anywhere in the article. A reader cannot say what the participants were doing when the kinematic and gaze data were recorded.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: Posed expression photography: each child produced flat, smiling and sad expressions on instruction, five photographs each. The paper states outright that the process focuses solely on the final classification between Normal and Autism without independently assessing the individual expressions. That is a striking design decision - the expression manipulation is the only behavioural content in the study, it was deliberately elicited, and it is then discarded as a variable. A per-expression analysis would have distinguished a model reading facial morphology from one reading expression production, which is precisely the question the design was built to answer.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. The instrument is the ten-item Q-CHAT-10 caregiver checklist, completed retrospectively about a toddler; the paper does not reproduce the items but names three of them via the SHAP results.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: No task or paradigm - an online caregiver questionnaire. Phase II claims to assess children's physical, verbal and behavioural performance, and this claim is unsupported at the most basic level: the dataset contains ten checklist items and a handful of demographic fields, and no physical, verbal or behavioural performance measure of any kind.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. The instrument is the ten-item Quantitative Checklist for Autism in Toddlers, administered through a screening app on a five-point frequency scale from never to always, collapsed to binary. Table 1 maps each question to its behavioural construct - response to name, eye contact, finger pointing and so on - which is more transparency about the instrument than most of the branch offers.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: No task or paradigm - a self-report battery completed in one sitting: the 25-item CAT-Q-ES (Likert 1-7) as predictors, and the 36-item BAPQ, the PHQ-9 and the GAD-7 as outcomes. This is the design's central methodological feature and its principal limitation, discussed under RQ4.5.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Static photographs. The rationale nonetheless refers repeatedly to movement - the ReAttention mechanism is justified as capturing fine-grained local features critical for ASD biomarkers such as asymmetric facial movements, and as amplifying regions including eye gaze and mouth movements. None of these is present in a still image, so the architecture's stated motivation describes a modality the study does not use.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Static photographs with no stimulus, interaction or session. The construct measured is facial appearance, framed as a diagnostic route parallel to behavioural analysis.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Tabular records combining AQ-10 item responses, four instrument scores, comorbidity flags and demographics, with a rater field recording whether a family member, healthcare professional or other person completed the assessment. The rater field is retained as a predictor rather than analysed as a source of measurement heterogeneity.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: The eye-tracking paired preferences paradigm: social and non-social images presented side by side, with faces displaying happiness, anger and neutral expressions paired against objects, following established designs (Sasson and Touchstone; Vacas et al.). This is a purpose-built social-attention task drawn from the developmental literature rather than a repurposed video or free-viewing sequence, and the choice is justified by reference to the metrics - fixation duration, fixation count, latency to first fixation - shown to be sensitive to gaze differences across neurodevelopmental conditions.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: Not reported. The paradigm behind the scanpaths is never described. This matters more than usual for a scanpath dataset, because the geometry of a scanpath image is jointly determined by the child and by the stimulus, and without knowing the stimulus set one cannot tell whether the classifier is reading gaze behaviour or stimulus identity.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: No task or paradigm - a caregiver checklist. The article does not reproduce or discuss a single Q-CHAT-10 item, so no behaviour is named anywhere in it.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: A Shapes Tracing Task with four shapes chosen to span the angular-frequency spectrum (clover, petals, ellipse, rounded square) plus a Reaction Time Task, both stylus-based. The shape design is deliberate and yields a methodological result the review should record: the ellipse was the least useful shape for distinguishing groups, and the authors point out that most drawing tasks in the literature index only elliptical or spiral movements, recommending that future studies span the full angular-frequency range. That is a concrete, actionable finding about task design derived from data.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: No task or paradigm - screening checklists completed by caregivers or self-report. The paper offers a substantive argument for its architecture choice that deserves recording: although the A1-A10 items are collected in a static format, their ordering is said to be non-arbitrary, with each question progressively evaluating social reciprocity, which is why a bidirectional sequence model is applied. The argument is stated but not tested - no experiment permutes item order to see whether the claimed sequential structure carries any signal.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Developmental screening instruments and archived imaging. The most concrete behavioural description concerns CSBS items on communication via eye movements (straight, upward, leftward, downward) and repetitive hand and finger movements, recorded as binary responses over 30-second monitoring windows.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: No imposed task. Naturalistic recordings of children engaged in everyday activities, with behaviour episodes delimited by the SSBD annotations of start and finish times. This is the most ecologically valid data source in the charted corpus - no laboratory, no stimulus, no instruction, and behaviours that occurred spontaneously in the child's own environment.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: A well-designed and unusually informative paradigm. Children watched a professional storyteller narrating short children's stories with the face clearly visible, then answered comprehension questions. Six stories were used, three audio-only and three audio-visual, counterbalanced across participants, and each instance was segmented into pre-speech, speech and post-speech phases. This yields a factorial design in which modality and temporal phase can be varied independently, and it is the only study in the charted corpus that manipulates the stimulus systematically rather than presenting a single fixed stimulus set. The paper also notes what it did not control - that the data were not stratified by story content - and then tests that concern directly in a per-story analysis.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: No task or paradigm for either dataset. Dataset 2's modality descriptions imply that facial images, 10-30 second voice recordings, body-keypoint motion and wearable physiological signals were captured simultaneously with synchronisation errors below 100 ms, which requires a structured session protocol - none is described.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: A battery of online tasks spanning three neuropsychological domains - multisensory perception, emotion recognition and executive function - reused from three prior published experiments with overlapping participants, yielding 54 dependent variables. The design rationale is stated clearly: because autism is heterogeneous, differences in any one neuropsychological domain are inconsistently detected, so the study looks across domains rather than within one.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: Not reported. The viewing task, stimuli, eye tracker and session structure of the originating collection are nowhere summarised, so a reader cannot say what the participants were looking at when the scanpaths were recorded. For a scanpath analysis this matters, because scanpath geometry is jointly determined by the viewer and the stimulus, and without knowing the stimulus set one cannot exclude stimulus identity as a source of the signal.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Static photographs. The construct is facial morphology, with the backbone described as extracting facial symmetry, eye spacing, philtrum width and face shape - a list of dysmorphology features that would require calibrated measurement rather than a detection head trained on uncalibrated web images.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: No task or paradigm. Static photographs with no stimulus, interaction or session; the construct is facial morphology and expression.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Gait and full-body movement recorded with 25 Kinect V2 joint points at X, Y and Z coordinates, from which the dataset creators pre-calculated 463 features: inter-joint Euclidean distances, range-of-motion metrics, gait parameters (speed, step length, cycle time) and temporal characteristics. The severe-ASD group was recorded on a Samsung Note 9 in clinical settings, and the paper explains why extracting the same 463 features from that video was technically impossible - missing 3D coordinates, depth information and time-series data.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Naturalistic language sampling rather than a designed classification task, which is a strength - the speech is spontaneous interaction, not an elicited response to a stimulus. The features derived from it are conversational as well as lexical: Mean Length of Turn Ratio measures the child's turn length relative to the adult's, capturing conversational participation rather than isolated production.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: Three classical games on a tablet, purpose-designed around executive functions - planning, cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, working memory and performance monitoring - with the theoretical grounding cited to Pennington and Ozonoff and to Hill. The paradigm is genuinely constructed for the question rather than repurposed, and the games' accessibility and usability requirements were derived from a prior review stage documented in the methodology flowchart.

questions.question_text: Is the design longitudinal, and how are ethics and consent handled?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Underlying cohort is longitudinal (from 6 months, reassessed every 3-12 months, diagnosis at 36 months) but the analysis is cross-sectional at the 18-month visit. Data are highly sensitive (video/audio of identifiable toddlers); the paper describes no anonymization, consent or data-protection procedure.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Cross-sectional - a single ~15-minute session per child. Data are marker-based 3D kinematics rather than video or audio, so less directly identifying; informed written consent from legal guardians and institutional ethics-board approval under the Declaration of Helsinki are reported, but no anonymization or data-protection procedure is described.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session; no session duration or number of sessions reported. Data are behavioral logs (correctness and millisecond latencies), not identifiable media, so sensitivity is low. Ethics approval (Marmara University Medical Faculty Ethical Advisory Board, protocol 09.2014.0194) and signed parental consent are reported; no anonymization or data-protection procedure is described.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Cross-sectional single session. Data are gaze coordinates, low in identifiability; face stimuli are third-party images. This paper carries no ethics, consent or data-protection statement - procedures are deferred to the source publication - and no anonymization is described. Longitudinal follow-up is named as future work, not performed.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, one session; no time scale or follow-up reported, and the authors state that the clinical importance of the findings will depend on future longitudinal data. The material is highly sensitive - free-text descriptions of participants' own family members and friends, including negative characteristics - and two full description sets are reproduced verbatim in Table 2. Written informed consent was obtained before enrollment and the New York State Psychiatric Institute / Columbia University IRB approved all procedures; no text anonymization or de-identification procedure is described.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single ~14-minute session per child with no follow-up. Data are touch coordinates and inertial signals - low identifiability, no video or audio. Written informed parental consent, Declaration of Helsinki compliance and University of Strathclyde Ethics Committee approval are reported. However, the data pipeline transmits gameplay data over the web to Microsoft Azure cloud storage operated in connection with a commercial company; the paper documents this as architecture but never as a privacy, anonymization or data-protection question.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session; no longitudinal component. The data are numeric hand-position kinematics, not identifiable media, so sensitivity is low - and the released dataset is inherently de-identified. Consent and ethics are reported more completely than anywhere else in the corpus so far: written information provided at least 48 hours in advance, an explicit opportunity to ask questions, written consent, and approval of the study, the consent procedure and the use of data by both the University of Manchester and NHS research ethics committees.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single ~12-minute recording per participant with no follow-up. The data are highly sensitive - identifiable RGB facial video plus depth and recorded voice responses from clinically diagnosed adults. Despite this, and despite announcing the resulting database as a contribution to the research community, the paper contains no ethics-approval statement, no participant consent statement, and no anonymization, access-control or data-protection provision. Only funding bodies are acknowledged.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: The parent study is longitudinal - infants recorded at 10 months with diagnostic outcome at 3 years, a 26-month prospective interval - but the acoustic analysis itself is cross-sectional at the single 10-month recording. Data are highly sensitive: audio-video of identifiable infants and their parents in intimate play interaction. Ethical review board approval at the participating centres is stated in a single footnote; there is no consent statement, no anonymization or de-identification procedure, and no data-protection or access-control provision despite the media type.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; nearly 12 hours of audio in total but no per-child session duration, number of sessions or follow-up. The data are identifiable child speech recordings from a clinical population. This paper contains no ethics approval, no consent statement and no anonymization or data-protection provision, deferring entirely to the source corpus citations - a notable gap for a paper published at a digital health venue. A competing-interests declaration is present (none declared), which makes the absence of an ethics statement more conspicuous.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single walking session with no follow-up and no repeated measurement. The data are numeric force-plate traces rather than identifiable media, so privacy risk is minimal. Ethics approval is reported at the level of the parent project (Research Ethics Committee of Universiti Teknologi MARA), but no participant or parental consent statement and no anonymization or data-protection procedure is described.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 190-second session per child with no repeat or follow-up. The data are highly sensitive - continuous video of identifiable young children from two angles, including a close-range facial camera, plus a published photograph of a child interacting with the robot. There is no ethics approval statement, no parental consent statement, and no anonymization or data-protection provision anywhere in the paper. Only the funding council and recruiting clinic are acknowledged.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 10-second measurement per child with no follow-up. The data are fixation durations on predefined regions - among the least identifiable data types in the corpus. Ethics approval from the hospital research committee is reported with explicit reference to the 1964 Helsinki Declaration and its amendments, informed consent was obtained from parents of all participants, and a conflict-of-interest disclosure is given for one author. Ethics and consent reporting is essentially complete.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Longitudinal in collection (17 months, April 2016 to September 2017) but cross-sectional in analysis - all of a subject's recordings are averaged into one feature vector, so no temporal or developmental modelling is performed despite the long span. The data are among the most sensitive in the corpus: 890 hours of passive in-home audio from children's bedrooms, inevitably capturing parents and other household members. Two protections are described - HIPAA-compliant encryption (Sookasa over Dropbox) for cloud storage, and parent-controlled activation/deactivation of monitoring mode 'for privacy considerations'. But there is no ethics approval statement, no IRB reference, no parental or child consent statement, and no consideration of consent for third parties recorded incidentally.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session with no follow-up. Gaze data over public web pages carry low re-identification risk, which is part of why the data can be released openly. Full ethical approval was obtained from the University of Wolverhampton Faculty of Arts Ethics Committee before collection, all participants signed consent forms after being familiarised with the purpose and procedure, and participants were debriefed. Uniquely in this corpus, the authors also flag prospective ethical risk in the discussion, warning that future profiling of conditions from web-searching behaviour 'will raise ethical considerations which should not be treated lightly'.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single ~30-minute session per child with no follow-up. Video of identifiable children is inherently sensitive, though the analysis pipeline applies Gaussian smoothing to suppress appearance and the released clips show only a lateral view of a reaching arm. Ethics approval from the local committee (ASL3 Genovese) under the Helsinki Declaration is reported, and parents gave written informed consent after a detailed study description. No anonymization or data-protection statement accompanies the public dataset release, which is a gap given that the dataset is posted openly.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; two experiments in a laboratory session series with no follow-up. The data are gaze coordinates over third-party stimulus faces, so re-identification risk is minimal and the public release is correspondingly low-risk. Consent handling is exemplary: ethics approval from the named Faculty Research Ethics Committee, written consent from adult subjects or from guardians of underage subjects, and additionally oral consent obtained from the underage subjects themselves - a two-tier assent procedure that only one other study in this corpus matches.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; three 60-second trials in a single session with no follow-up. Data are numeric hand-position traces, not identifiable media. Written informed consent was signed by caregivers, the study conformed to the Declaration of Helsinki, and it followed the ethical guidelines of Shenzhen University. No anonymization procedure is described, and none is materially required for this data type.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 5-minute conversation per child with no follow-up. The data are highly sensitive - audio and video of identifiable children in unscripted personal conversation, plus verbatim transcripts. Ethics reporting is complete and among the best in the corpus: IRB approval and oversight from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, written parental informed consent, and verbal assent from the children themselves. No anonymization or retention procedure for the recordings is described.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single ~10-minute session with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates and button-press latencies over third-party stimulus faces, so participant-identifiable content is minimal. Institutional Review Board approval from the University of Minnesota is reported for all recruitment. No participant or parental consent statement, no anonymization procedure and no competing-interests declaration appear.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single short video per child with no follow-up. The data are among the most sensitive in the corpus - identifiable home video of very young children, transmitted internationally and viewed by nine non-clinical raters in another country. Governance is reported reasonably fully: dual ethical clearance from the Bangladesh Institute of Child Health / Dhaka Shishu Children's Hospital and the Stanford IRB, consent obtained in Bengali, secure transmission, and a HIPAA-compliant rating platform. What is absent is any retention, deletion or re-use policy, and any discussion of the ethics of routing identifiable child video to non-clinical raters abroad.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single scanpath per subject per image with no temporal or longitudinal component. The data are fixation coordinates over public stimulus images, with subject identifiers already randomised by the dataset providers, so re-identification risk is minimal. No ethics approval, consent or data-protection statement appears - understandable for secondary use of a released challenge dataset but not acknowledged as such anywhere in the paper.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session per child, with repeated sessions deliberately avoided to prevent learned behaviours. The data are video and audio of identifiable preschool children, recorded both by the robot's onboard camera and by a high-definition camera concealed behind a two-way mirror - among the most privacy-sensitive arrangements in the corpus. There is no ethics approval statement, no parental consent statement and no anonymization or data-protection provision anywhere in the paper. The only privacy-adjacent measure is that transcripts shared with the expert assessors omitted child identification.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; no session duration, number of sessions or follow-up is reported. Gaze fixation durations are low-sensitivity data, but the described workflow has a therapist collect patient information and medical history at the pre-analysis stage, which is identifiable clinical data. No ethics approval, no parental consent statement, and no anonymization or data-protection provision appears anywhere - a serious omission for a system designed for clinical deployment with children.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
