answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session of a few seconds of task data per hand, with no follow-up. Data are numeric 3D position traces, not identifiable media, so sensitivity is low. Ethics approval from the University of Manchester research ethics committee is reported with the specific reference number (2017-2541-4204); no consent statement or anonymization procedure is separately described.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single approximately 5-minute session per child with no follow-up. The data are gaze coordinates rendered into abstract images, so identifiability is low and the public release is correspondingly low-risk. Consent handling is reported carefully: both informed consent from parents and assent from the children themselves were confirmed for all cases, and procedures followed institutional and/or national research committee ethical standards and the 1964 Helsinki declaration with later amendments.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; four analysed 5-minute interactions per dyad in a single session with no follow-up. The data are video of identifiable adults in extended conversation - among the most sensitive in the corpus. Handling is the most careful encountered: written informed consent under the Declaration of Helsinki, local ethics committee approval, 50 Euro compensation, debriefing, and an explicit data availability statement refusing sharing because the data are 'identifiable patient data from a sample that did not consent to their data being shared in any form'. That is a substantive privacy-protective decision rather than an unexplained absence.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Prospective and cross-sectional at the level of the index test, with each child assessed once, and prospective in the trial sense that the algorithm is fixed before any evaluation data are collected. Ethics approval was obtained from the West of Scotland Research Ethics Service Committee 3 and the University of Strathclyde Ethics Committee. The competing-interest handling is the most thorough in this review and is worth recording in full: the academic authors sit on the trial steering and management committees and declare no financial interest in the product or in the funding company, while two coauthors are board members of Harimata sp. z o.o., which intends to commercialise the technology, and hold options vesting in it. The funding is a subcontract from that company under a Horizon 2020 SME Instrument grant. A commercially sponsored diagnostic evaluation in which the analysis is blinded to the developers, the academic investigators hold no equity, and the governance structure is stated, is exactly what this review has found missing elsewhere - most notably in the commercially funded cry-analysis study, whose disclosure is comparably complete but whose design provides none of these separations.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; 3 seconds of viewing per image with no temporal or longitudinal component. The data are fixation coordinates over public stimulus images, so re-identification risk is minimal. No ethics approval, consent or data-provenance statement appears - understandable for secondary use of a released challenge dataset, but not acknowledged as such.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; single videos per session with no longitudinal modelling, though the platform is designed for ongoing remote assessment. The data are the most privacy-sensitive in the corpus - parent-recorded video inside family homes capturing children during play and meals, routed through a commercial company to an academic laboratory. There is no ethics approval statement, no parental consent statement, no anonymization procedure and no data-protection or retention provision anywhere in the paper.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional with a single session per child, and no follow-up. Parental consent is reported for all volunteers; no ethics committee approval appears in the retrieved text, which is an omission for a study recording video of three-year-olds. Funding and competing interests are not stated.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; single-session viewing per the source dataset, with no temporal or longitudinal component. Data are fixation coordinates over public stimulus images, so re-identification risk is minimal. No ethics approval, consent or provenance statement appears - common for secondary benchmark use but not acknowledged as such.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: Cross-sectional pilot, single session per child, with no follow-up or test-retest. Ethics reporting is brief but complete on the essentials: approval of the committee of research ethics was obtained to carry out the experiment, and informed consent was obtained from the children's parents. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text; the participating kindergarten is acknowledged by name.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Prospective longitudinal in the essential respect: behavioural measurement at 8-23 months, diagnostic outcome at 24 months. The behavioural measurement itself is a single cross-sectional session. Data are video of identifiable infants with their mothers - among the most sensitive material in the corpus. Governance is correspondingly well reported: named ethics approval (2017-KY089-01), written guardian consent, specific consent for publication of potentially identifiable images or data, and prospective trial registration.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session with no follow-up. Data are numeric kinematic and gaze traces, not identifiable media. Ethics and consent details are not restated in this paper, being referred to the source protocol publication - a reporting gap even if the underlying governance was presumably adequate.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session per child with no follow-up. Data are facial images of identifiable children including a clinically diagnosed group, stored server-side in a SQL Server database and with collection photographs reproduced in the paper. Governance reporting is the weakest in the corpus: parents were informed of the purpose of data collection, but no ethics committee approval, no written consent procedure, no anonymization and no retention or access policy is described - which is a serious omission for a system whose stated deployment path is public download by app or web page.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single laboratory session totalling roughly two minutes of recorded standing per child, with no follow-up. The data are numeric force-plate traces, not identifiable media, so privacy risk is minimal. Institutional Review Board approval of the study protocol is reported, eligibility was screened by telephone with legal guardians, and informed consent was obtained from legal guardians on arrival at the laboratory. No child assent statement is reported.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session per child averaging roughly 9-11 minutes, with no repeated sessions or follow-up. The data are video recordings of identifiable children, and a figure showing children interacting with the robots is published. Institutional Review Board approval is reported with a specific protocol number (GW IRB#111540), but there is no parental consent statement, no child assent statement, and no anonymization, retention or data-protection provision.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; two-day visits with repeated trials within session, and no longitudinal follow-up - though repeated trials within session provide the test-retest estimate. Data are depth-camera recordings reduced to skeletal joint coordinates, so identifiability is moderate rather than high. Ethics governance is complete: Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine IRB approval prior to commencement, written informed consent from all legal guardians, verbal assent from all children, and $100 compensation.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: Cross-sectional per infant, with a definite final diagnosis recorded about a month after the initial examination. Data are clinical audio of infants, and the governance reporting is exemplary by corpus standards: two IRB approval numbers, explicit statement that analysis used fully anonymized retrospective data, and - unusually - the paper treats infant anonymity as a first-order constraint shaping what data can ever exist in this field, which is the stated motivation for the small-data method it develops.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single capture session per subject with no follow-up. Data are numeric marker trajectories and event timings, so low sensitivity in themselves, but no ethics approval, consent procedure or data governance statement appears anywhere in the paper. Since ages are never reported, it cannot even be determined whether the participants were adults or children.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: Cross-sectional - a single ADOS session per child, averaging 41.6 +/- 12.4 minutes. Longitudinal follow-up is named as necessary future work precisely because the intended application (tracking severity change over time and after treatment) requires it. Data are full audio of clinical sessions including parent and clinician speech - among the most sensitive material in the corpus - yet no ethics approval, consent procedure or anonymization statement appears in the extracted text, while funding and acknowledgements are reported in detail.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; one session per participant per study, with nine participants contributing to both. Data are gaze coordinates plus demographic questionnaire responses. Governance is properly reported - prior ethics committee approval, signed consent forms, debriefing - and the authors go further than compliance by naming ethics as an open research question for any future move to naturalistic recording.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session per child with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates over image stimuli. No ethics committee approval, parental consent procedure, anonymization or data governance statement appears anywhere in the paper, despite participants being children as young as 1.8 years recruited through a clinical rehabilitation service.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 14-minute session with three 2-minute-40-second conditions each preceded by a 2-minute baseline, no follow-up. Data are depth video of identifiable children reduced to joint coordinates. Governance is properly reported: written information and written consent from family caregivers, approval by the Ethical Committee of the Polytechnic University of Valencia, and conformity with institutional and national committee standards and the 1964 Helsinki Declaration.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session per child with no follow-up. Data are frontal video and audio of identifiable toddlers with a parent and clinician present - among the most sensitive material in the corpus. Governance reporting is a single clause in the acknowledgements referring to participants' consent; no ethics committee approval, formal consent procedure, anonymisation or retention policy is stated, and no data availability statement is given.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session per child with no follow-up, though the motivating application - monitoring treatment response and predicting later outcomes - is inherently longitudinal and the paper acknowledges much work remains before eye tracking can serve it. Data are gaze recordings with linked clinical scores. Governance is fully reported: IRB approval from both Yale University and Seattle Children's Research Institute covering experiments, acquisition and analysis.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session per child with no follow-up. Data are EEG traces and gaze coordinates over face photographs, low in identifiability. Governance reporting is complete: conducted according to the Declaration of Helsinki, approved by the ethics committee of Beijing Normal University, with parental informed consent obtained before participation, and a data availability statement offering the data on request.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; one 20-minute session per child with no follow-up, though the stated goal of continuous phenotyping is inherently longitudinal. Data include eye and world video of identifiable children with extensive manual annotation by independent labellers. Governance is reported: written informed consent from both parents and children under an approved Stanford IRB protocol. The conflict of interest is declared.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; one session per participant with no follow-up, though the stated applications include monitoring disorder course and treatment outcome. Data are video and audio of identifiable adults. Governance is complete and includes an unusual element - explicit separate consent from individuals appearing in published figures - and the data availability statement withholds the dataset specifically 'due to privacy restrictions of the video data' while making it available on reasonable request. The discussion also engages the downstream consequences of deployment, noting that 'especially screenings and unsupervised feedback might result in more individuals seeking care and lead to higher costs for the health system' and that 'it is warranted to carefully define the area of use and evaluate benefits, costs, and risks' - one of very few papers in the corpus to consider system-level effects of its own tool.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. No ethics approval, consent procedure, anonymisation statement, data governance policy or data provenance is reported anywhere. Since the dataset is neither named nor cited, it cannot be established under what approvals the original collection took place or whether this reuse was authorised - a governance gap that is qualitatively different from simply failing to report approval for one's own collection.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: Longitudinal in structure - 9 sessions per training child over 9 weeks and about 6 per test child over 6 weeks - but the longitudinal dimension is not analysed. Sessions are treated as independent observations rather than as repeated measures within child, and no change over time in joint attention or imitation is examined despite the data being an intervention series. Data are video and depth recordings of identifiable young children, with a photograph of a child with the robots published. Governance is reported at centre level (autism specialist and director board approval, signed parental consent) but no institutional review board is named and no data-handling policy appears.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single viewing session per participant with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates over purpose-recorded video of a therapist. No ethics committee approval, parental consent procedure, anonymisation or data governance statement appears anywhere in the paper, despite participants aged from 3 years recruited through a university psychiatry department - the most conspicuous reporting gap in an otherwise clinically careful study.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; one brief exposure per participant with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates within a synthetic scene, plus questionnaire scores and demographics - low sensitivity. Governance is properly reported: IRB approval with a reference number for both experiments and explicit attention to participant safety, which matters here because the authors note that some autistic participants rejected the VR headset.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 15-minute session per child with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates over picture stimuli. Governance is fully reported: Helsinki conformity, named ethics committee approval at Peking University, written parental consent obtained before the experiment, and separate personal approval for publication of the photographs used as human-gaze cues. The experimenter was blind to functioning subgroup - 'the experimenter did not know a priori whether a child with ASD belonged to the LFA group or the HFA group' - which is a rare and worthwhile control.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single six-minute session per child with no follow-up. Data are numeric eye and head deviation angles. No ethics committee approval, parental consent procedure, anonymisation or data governance statement appears anywhere, despite the sample including children as young as two recruited through a service centre for children with developmental needs.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single visit per child comprising sequential EEG and eye-tracking sessions, with no follow-up. Data are EEG traces and gaze fixation summaries. Governance is reported: conducted according to the Declaration of Helsinki, approved by the ethics committee of Beijing Normal University, with written informed consent provided.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 54-second viewing session per participant with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates over video stimuli. Governance is properly reported: research ethics board approval with a full protocol number and Helsinki conformity. Clinical stability over the preceding three months was required for inclusion.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; one conversation per child with no follow-up. Data are first-person scene video from head-mounted glasses plus two external camera feeds of identifiable children in dyadic interaction. Governance is partially reported - Helsinki principles, Shenzhen University ethical guidelines, and written caregiver consent - but no ethics committee approval number is given. Participants were deliberately not told the glasses recorded gaze, with a post-experiment interview confirming none had realised; this is methodologically well motivated for behavioural naturalness but the deception is not discussed as an ethical consideration.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; multiple phonations per child in a single session with no follow-up. Data are voice recordings of identifiable children with clinical diagnoses. No ethics committee approval, parental consent procedure, anonymisation statement or data-handling policy appears anywhere in the paper - a complete absence rather than a partial omission, and one that matters given the population.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single session of approximately 10 minutes per child with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates rendered as abstract scanpath images and released openly. Governance is fully reported and its regulatory basis explained: informed written consent from parents or guardians after explanation of objectives, tasks and the right to withdraw; assent from every child; parents permitted to remain in the room; Helsinki conformity; and an explicit statement that ethics committee authorisation was not required under French recommendations for psychological research. Explaining why approval was unnecessary, rather than simply omitting the matter, is better practice than the silence found in much of the corpus.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 54-second viewing session per participant with no follow-up. Data are gaze coordinates over video stimuli. Governance is complete and detailed: named ethics committee approval with full protocol number, informed consent from participants or legal guardians, Helsinki conformity, and separately obtained consent for publication of identifying images from the individuals appearing in the stimulus videos - the last being a consideration almost never addressed elsewhere in this corpus.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single 24-minute session per child with no follow-up. Data are first-person video of identifiable children moving through a monitored environment. Governance is properly reported: informed consent from relatives after explanation of objectives and procedure, separate explicit consent to video recording of the child, ethics committee approval at the Polytechnic University of Valencia, and Helsinki conformity. A researcher remained present to monitor the child but 'attempted to intervene as little as possible (only in situations of device failure or cybersickness)' - the only mention of cybersickness in the corpus and a real consideration for immersive paradigms with children.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single conversational session per child with no follow-up. Data are frontal and side video of identifiable children. Governance is partially reported - Helsinki conformity and written caregiver informed consent, with payment of 200 CNY disclosed - but no ethics committee approval or reference number is given.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of publicly released images. No ethics statement appears, which is largely defensible for reuse of open data, though the paper does not discuss the terms of that reuse. The Figshare repository is cited with its URL, and the originating study is credited.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; two sessions per child with no follow-up. Data are numeric marker trajectories, with per-participant clinical data published in tabular form but no identifiers. Governance is complete: written informed consent from parents or legal guardians, Helsinki-compliant design, and local ethical committee approval with a full reference number.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: Longitudinal in design - a seven-week course of sessions per child, with 34 sessions contributing to the agreement analysis - which distinguishes it from the almost uniformly cross-sectional remainder of this review. Repeated measurement within children is the study's methodological point rather than an incidental feature. Ethics reporting is complete: approval by the Social Sciences Research Ethical Committee of UAE University and by Al Ain Hospital, with signed parental consent letters. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text. Attrition is substantial and unexplained: 6 of 11 children completed the long-term study.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; a single questionnaire per family with no follow-up, though the items ask retrospectively about the perinatal period and early childhood. Data include maternal substance use, antidepressant use and miscarriage history - sensitive material about identifiable families collected partly through a commercial web form. No ethics committee approval, consent procedure, anonymisation policy or data-handling statement appears anywhere in the paper.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; one ADOS-2 administration per participant with no follow-up, though the stated application as a treatment outcome measure would require longitudinal demonstration that the measures capture change, which the authors identify explicitly. Data are audio from videotaped clinical assessments. Governance is reported: informed written consent or assent from all participants and their parents, who also had to be fluent in English, and IRB review and approval at OHSU.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of a released benchmark; no follow-up. No ethics statement, consent statement or IRB approval appears anywhere - a defensible position for public challenge data, but the paper never states that position, nor does it point to where the original approvals were obtained. A competing-interests declaration is present, though it declares only a domain-based conflict.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis; no follow-up. No ethics, consent or IRB statement anywhere, despite acknowledged NIMH funding (R01MH121344-01) and a full competing-interests declaration - so the omission is not a matter of the paper lacking front-matter sections. Data are public challenge material, which mitigates but does not remove the expectation of a statement about the source approvals.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Cross-sectional analysis of data acquired within a longitudinal cohort; no longitudinal modelling is performed here, though the parent study follows children over time and the authors position the measure as suitable for tracking development. Ethics are reported in full: approval by the Ethics Committee of the Faculty of Medicine of Geneva University, methods stated to conform to that institution's guidelines and regulations, informed written consent obtained from a parent or legal guardian for every child, and separate explicit consent for publication of identifying images from both the adults and the guardian of the child appearing in Figure 1. The privacy engineering is stronger still: reducing video to skeletons on a black background was adopted partly 'to ensure de-identification of the persons involved', so the analytic representation is itself the anonymisation - among the few instances in this corpus where sensitive video data are handled by design rather than by assurance.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, one session per child, no follow-up, though the authors state a future aim of applying the method to younger children. Ethics are reported: approval by the Ethical Committee of Psychological Research of the Department of Humanities, University of Naples Federico II, with written informed consent from legal guardians obtained before the study. The data are coordinate streams rather than video or audio, so re-identification risk is intrinsically low, and a data availability statement commits to sharing raw data 'without undue reservation'.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up. Ethics approval from the School of Psychology Research Ethics Committee of Beijing Normal University, with informed consent obtained from all children with parental permission before enrollment. Funding sources are itemised (NSFC grants 62003228 and 61761166003, a Beijing Municipal Education Commission project, and a National Key R&D programme grant). No data availability statement, no data sharing plan and no discussion of how the EEG and gaze recordings are stored or protected - though both modalities are lower-identifiability than the video and audio data used elsewhere in this corpus.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up. Ethics are reported in full for a conference paper: approval by the Yonsei University IRB under number 4-2021-0845, conduct in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, and written informed consent from parents 'after receiving a detailed description of the study'. The data are identifiable video of young children, and although semantic segmentation removes background it retains faces; two children appear in published figures identified by participant codes. No data availability statement, no code release and no description of how the video corpus is stored or protected.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up. Ethics reporting is complete and specific: approval by the Institutional Review Board of Pingdingshan University under protocol code 068 dated 20 October 2020, conduct in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, and informed consent from all subjects involved. A data availability statement commits to sharing 'from the corresponding author on reasonable request'. Facial video of identifiable preschoolers is collected and no statement about its storage, retention or de-identification appears.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of a public dataset; no follow-up. No ethics statement, consent statement or IRB approval appears anywhere, and no pointer is given to where the source dataset's approvals were obtained - an omission that is common for benchmark reuse in this corpus but is not acknowledged here either. A competing-interests declaration and a CRediT contribution statement are both present, so the absence of an ethics statement is not a matter of missing front matter.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Cross-sectional with two measurement blocks on the same day separated by a break, drawn from a larger study that also included extensive behavioural assessment and neuroimaging. The authors identify the temporal limitation themselves as their second main limitation: 'we collected only two [blocks], both close in time and for similar (but distinct) video episodes', and argue that longer-term longitudinal data with dense state measures such as sleepiness and mood would be needed to distinguish measurement error from genuine state-dependent within-individual change. No ethics or consent statement appears in the extracted text, though the study is embedded in an established multi-site research programme. Copyright constraints on the sitcom prevented reproducing stimulus frames, and a royalty-free substitute image was used for the segmentation figure.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, with data accumulated opportunistically over four years from 2018 to 2021 rather than in a defined recruitment window; no follow-up. Parental consent to share each recording is built into the app flow - families view the video after each session and choose whether to send it - which is a stronger form of ongoing consent than a single upfront authorisation, though no IRB approval statement appears in the extracted text. Privacy is treated substantively rather than as boilerplate, with a dedicated Discussion subsection arguing that the models' small size permits on-device inference and privacy-preserving federated learning, motivated explicitly by autism's stigmatisation and by parents who want a diagnostic signal but are unwilling to share video. A senior author declares founding Cognoa, a company developing digital paediatric health solutions.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; one assessment per participant, with the intended application being longitudinal outcome measurement rather than cross-sectional classification. The authors are explicit that the reliability evidence needed for that application does not yet exist: 'we do not yet know the reliability (test-retest) and short-term stability of the measures we generated from transcripts and audio recordings', though they state they are currently undertaking those studies. This is an important self-limitation, since an outcome measure without demonstrated test-retest stability cannot distinguish treatment effect from measurement noise. Ethics reporting is complete: IRB review and approval at OHSU, with informed written consent or assent obtained from all participants and their parents at the initial visit. A data availability statement offers de-identified data on request and gives a public GitHub URL for the analysis code.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Cross-sectional in analysis but embedded in a prospective screening pathway, with diagnosis ascertained after app administration at a mean interval of 0.7 months (range -0.1 to 5.9). No longitudinal follow-up of the measures themselves, and the authors identify the developmental course of head movement differences as a future direction. Ethics reporting is complete and specific: written informed consent from caregivers and approval by the Duke University Health System Institutional Review Board under two named protocol numbers. Conflicts of interest are declared at length and are substantial: five authors developed technology related to the app which has been licensed, with both they and Duke University benefiting financially; the senior clinical author sits on four scientific advisory boards, consults for three companies including Apple and receives book royalties; both senior authors have invention disclosures and patent applications registered with Duke's licensing office; and the senior engineering author is affiliated with Apple, with a note that the work was done before and independently of that affiliation. The disclosure is exemplary in its completeness, and the commercial interest in the app is relevant context for a paper reporting the app's discriminative performance.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, one narration per participant, no follow-up. Ethics reporting is adequate but generic: informed assent and consent from all participants and guardians as applicable, approval by each institution's ethics committee, and conformity with the Declaration of Helsinki, without naming the committees or protocol numbers. Data sharing is a genuine strength and rare in this corpus - 'The minimal dataset and analytic scripts are available from the OSF database' with a working URL, so the analysis is independently verifiable even though raw audio is not shared, which is the appropriate handling of identifiable speech. A competing interest is declared: one author owns a startup company supported by a Hong Kong government technology scheme, with a statement that the reported research is not associated with it.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, one narration per participant, no follow-up. Ethics reporting is complete and unusually granular on consent, which was obtained separately from three parties as applicable: parents of participants under 16, parents of participants aged 16 and older, and the participants themselves - a structure that respects the assent of older adolescents and adults alongside parental consent. Approval came from the Faculty of Psychology, University of Warsaw Research Ethics Committee, with Declaration of Helsinki conformity stated. Data are withheld from public deposit on an explicit and appropriate privacy rationale - narrative transcripts of identifiable clinical assessments 'containing information that could compromise the privacy of the research participants' - with availability on request from the named authors. No competing interests, with Polish National Science Centre and University of Warsaw funding declared.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up. The most conspicuous reporting omission in the paper is ethical: no ethics committee approval, protocol number, consent or assent statement appears anywhere in the extracted text, despite the participants being toddlers with clinical diagnoses recruited through hospitals and clinics. Funding by the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey is acknowledged and a conflict-of-interest declaration is present, so the absence is not a matter of missing front matter. Against this, data sharing is handled well: an open practices statement provides a URL at which 'the study data for all machine learning experiments are available', which is more than most studies here offer and which would in principle allow the sample-size discrepancy to be resolved externally.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Cross-sectional with two age cohorts sampled independently rather than followed longitudinally - so the developmental claim rests on a cross-sectional age contrast, which the design cannot distinguish from cohort effects, though this is a standard and reasonable compromise. Ethics reporting is complete: approval by the Ethics Committee of Shenzhen Maternity and Child Healthcare Hospital, written informed consent from legal guardians, and separate written consent obtained specifically for publication of potentially identifiable images or data. Partial overlap with a prior publication by the same group is disclosed rather than concealed: 'A portion of preschool data using paradigm (video clip) data had been used in a previous study... However, this study used more comprehensive paradigms and the findings presented in this study have never been published before.' Raw data are offered on request.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Prospective and prospectively registered (NCT04151290) before initiation, conducted August 2019 to June 2020, with each child assessed once by the Device and once by specialists. Ethics reporting is complete and specific: centralised IRB review by IntegReview under protocol number Q170886, approved 19 July 2019, with the subsequent acquisition by Advarra noted, and informed consent from all caregivers. The COVID-19 disruption is disclosed in detail rather than smoothed over - the date of the national emergency, the number of sites closed (9 of 14), the reduced availability of those remaining, the estimate that 100 specialist visits could not be completed, the 97 that were completed afterwards, and the estimated drop-out rate absent the pandemic (26.2%). Data are withheld from public release on patient-sensitivity grounds but offered to qualified researchers under a data-sharing agreement, with the full protocol public on ClinicalTrials.gov. The code is proprietary and not available.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, one recording per child, with the two groups recorded at different times separated by the onset of the pandemic. Ethical reporting is incomplete: written consent from caregivers is stated for the autistic group, but no consent statement appears for the comparison group and no ethics committee approval is reported for either. Data are not shared. The analysis code, however, is publicly released on GitHub, which is rare in this corpus and materially improves verifiability of the computational steps even though the recordings themselves are unavailable.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of a public dataset; no follow-up. No ethics statement, consent statement or IRB approval appears anywhere, and no pointer is given to where the source dataset's approvals were obtained. A data availability statement supplies the figshare URL for the source images with an access date, funding is acknowledged from the Najran University Scientific Research Deanship under a named grant, and a conflict-of-interest declaration is present - so the absence of an ethics statement is not a matter of missing front matter but of the section not being written.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, with videos accumulated opportunistically as families played and chose to share; no follow-up. Ethics approval from the Stanford IRB under a named eProtocol number, with parental consent to share each recording built into the app flow. Privacy is treated as a design constraint rather than a compliance step, and is one of the paper's three stated contributions: annotation was performed entirely computationally so that no human annotator ever viewed the footage, and the discussion explicitly contrasts this with prior manual-annotation work that 'may compromise the privacy of participants by providing annotators with access to video footage'. The senior author declares founding Cognoa and a co-author declares part-time consulting for the same company.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of a public dataset; no follow-up. No ethics statement, consent statement or IRB approval appears anywhere, and no pointer is given to the source dataset's approvals - an omission that is common for benchmark reuse in this corpus but is not acknowledged. Funding is not declared in the extracted text. The dataset is described throughout as publicly available but no URL or accession is given in the extracted portion.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, with data accumulated opportunistically across nearly four years as families played and shared. Stanford Institutional Review Board approval is stated, though without a protocol number, and recruitment channels are named. The privacy position is a genuine design property rather than a claim: because the analysis uses only four event fields per trial - start time, end time, correct flag, skip flag - no imagery, audio or identifiable content is involved at all, which the authors present as enabling screening 'in a privacy-preserved manner' and contrast with computer-vision approaches where 'privacy concerns are at the forefront'. Among the three GuessWhat studies in this corpus, this is the only one whose modality raises no confidentiality question.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, with recordings accumulated over roughly two years and no follow-up. No ethics committee approval, consent statement or institutional review is mentioned anywhere, despite the study having purpose-collected approximately 7,000 speech recordings from more than 140 children recruited through special education schools and an autism association. Funding from two Anhui provincial science programmes is acknowledged. The dataset is presented as a contribution, with the authors noting that 'currently, there is no available public speech dataset for ASD children, which creates a big obstacle for related research', but no release, access route or sharing commitment is offered.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, one recorded session per child, with no follow-up and no test-retest assessment of the severity estimate's stability. The absence of any ethics, consent or institutional review statement is the most conspicuous reporting gap: the study analyses audio recordings of clinical diagnostic assessments involving young children, their parents and clinicians, manually labelled by researchers, and no approval is mentioned in the extracted text. Funding from the Israel Ministry of Science and Technology is acknowledged with a grant number. No data availability statement and no code release.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session per child, with no follow-up or test-retest - the last being a real gap for a five-minute protocol proposed as a diagnostic aid, since the stability of a six-year-old's engagement with a novel robot across occasions is unknown and is exactly what a supplementary assessment tool would need. Ethics reporting is complete and specific: approval from the local research ethics committee at the University of Lower Silesia; legal guardians acquainted with the research aims and procedures; and signed consent forms covering both participation and, separately, the filming of the study. Separate consent for video recording is reported by very few studies in this review. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Cross-sectional; no longitudinal component, no follow-up, no repeat testing, no test-retest reliability for the entropy features. Ethics reporting is the weakest element of the paper: the retrieved full text contains no institutional review board statement, no Declaration of Helsinki statement, and no description of parental consent or child assent, despite the study involving minors, a clinical population, and a deliberate withholding of the device's true purpose from participants. The parent study (Zhao et al., 2021c) may carry the approval, but a secondary analysis reusing identifiable behavioural recordings should restate it. What is declared is a conflict-of-interest statement (none) and a detailed funding list of eight grants.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up, no test-retest reliability for any feature - which matters for a device intended for repeated home use. Ethics reporting is unusual and problematic. Consent is handled well: parents were informed of the study, its goals, the procedure and their rights, informed consent was obtained in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, a child psychologist supervised, and data were stored under anonymous participant IDs without names or personal information. But formal ethics review was not obtained and the Institutional Review Board Statement argues that it was not needed: the proposal was accepted by the University of Tehran's School of ECE 'considering the privacy of participants and non-intrusiveness of the screening nature of the work', and the authors assert that 'this is a non-intrusive screening that does not require ethics approval as long as the privacy of the participants is considered', supplemented by the autism centre's own guidelines. A departmental engineering-school sign-off plus site guidelines is not equivalent to ethics-committee review of research on 3-6 year old children with developmental disabilities, and the non-intrusiveness of the measurement does not remove the need for review of recruitment, consent and data handling in a vulnerable population.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up, no test-retest reliability for any kinematic feature - which matters for a proposal to use feature values as clinical thresholds, since a threshold is only useful if the measurement is stable within a child across occasions. Ethics reporting is complete and appropriate: the study was reviewed and approved by the Ethical Committee of Psychological Research of the Department of Humanities, University of Naples Federico II, and written informed consent was obtained from participants' legal guardians. The conflict-of-interest statement discloses that two authors were employed by Neapolisanit S.R.L., the rehabilitation centre from which the autistic participants were recruited - a material disclosure, correctly made. Funding is not reported.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Cross-sectional single session with no follow-up and no test-retest assessment. Since the pipeline is proposed as a clinical scoring aid, the absence of any repeat measurement means nothing is known about whether the same child assessed twice would receive the same automated score. Ethics reporting is minimal but present in both required elements: 'these experiments have passed an ethical review', with no committee, institution or approval number named, and informed consent obtained from the children's parents before each session. A privacy measure is also implemented and disclosed - participants' faces are mosaicked in the published figures, with the authors noting that this may obscure the facial joints they wish to illustrate - and the data are declared confidential rather than released. For video recorded on preschool children with disabilities during clinical assessment, the consent and privacy handling is appropriate; the ethics statement is thinner than the norm and would not satisfy most journals' current reporting requirements.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up, no test-retest reliability. Ethics reporting is the strongest element of the paper's governance: approval was obtained from the Research Ethics Committee of Islamic Azad University, Tehran Science and Research Branch, with the approval identifier IR.IAU.SRB.REC.1401.152 stated in a dedicated Ethics subsection and repeated in the declarations - a named committee and a verifiable reference number, which most reports in this corpus do not provide. Consent is handled less completely: parental consent appears as an inclusion criterion for the autistic group only, with no consent statement for the school-recruited comparison children and no mention of child assent. Funding (none received) and competing interests (none) are declared.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session per participant, no follow-up and no test-retest assessment of the coordination features. Ethics governance is well handled: the study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, and consent was evidently granular rather than blanket, since two of the 44 enrolled participants were excluded specifically because of 'their lack of consent for this particular set of experiments' - a per-experiment consent regime that is a positive marker of data governance in a study involving identifiable facial video. Confederates were blinded to diagnostic status. The human raters were not blinded in the ordinary sense - they were told that every participant was either a confirmed autism case or a deliberately recruited clear control - which is appropriate for calibrating a benchmark but does mean their task was easier than a real screening decision. Funding from four NIH grants is fully itemised. No competing-interests statement appears in the retrieved text, which is a gap given that the work develops a potential clinical tool.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up, and no test-retest reliability - which is a real gap for a tool proposed for repeated community screening. The nearest thing to a temporal analysis is Fig. 8, which tracks how the sample and the classification results evolved across the four quarters of 2021, showing 2-4 misclassified cases in an initial 40-child phase and stable results thereafter; this is a development log rather than a validation, but it is unusually transparent about how the model matured alongside the dataset. Ethics reporting is complete for approval and thin for consent: the study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Northwestern Polytechnical University under protocol 202002032, with all procedures conducted in accordance with the latest revision of the Declaration of Helsinki - a named committee and a protocol number, better than most reports here - but no parental consent or child assent statement appears, despite the participants being 3-6 year olds. Funding from three National Natural Science Foundation of China grants is itemised. No competing-interests statement appears.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: Cross-sectional in analysis though the data span five years, with no temporal modelling: tweets from 2017 and 2022 are pooled and classified independently, so nothing is learned about stability or change over time, and no test-retest or within-user consistency is examined. Ethics is the study's most serious deficiency and is entirely absent. There is no institutional review board approval, no ethics committee, no research-ethics statement, no consent, and no discussion of the ethics of the enterprise. The data are health-related disclosures made by identifiable individuals about themselves, harvested without their knowledge and used to train a classifier whose stated purpose is to identify people who may be autistic. The only privacy measure described is the redaction of username, location and date of birth from two example biographies reproduced as a figure, done 'in compliance with Twitter's policies' - a platform-terms consideration rather than a research-ethics one. The paper does not consider whether the autistic Twitter community, which is organised and vocal, would regard such a classifier as acceptable; whether a model that infers autism from public text could be used against the people it identifies; or whether public availability implies availability for this purpose. Given that several of the search keywords are terms this community coined for itself, the omission is conspicuous.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up, and no test-retest reliability of the entropy measure - which matters for a biomarker proposed for treatment monitoring, since sensitivity to change requires knowing the measurement's stability. Governance is exemplary by the standards of this corpus. The study was approved by the Duke University Health System Institutional Review Board under two protocol numbers (Pro00085434, Pro00085435), written informed consent was obtained from caregivers or legal guardians, and inability to consent in English or Spanish is disclosed as an exclusion criterion rather than passed over. Funding from eight sources including four NIH grants and four technology companies is itemised, with an explicit statement that 'the funders had no direct role in the study design, data analysis, decision to publish, or preparation of the manuscript'. The competing-interests statement is the longest in this corpus and is unusually forthcoming: several authors developed technology licensed to Apple and have benefited financially, one is CEO of a company and holds a granted patent plus three applications alongside numerous advisory and consulting relationships, and another was affiliated with Apple at publication. Crucially, a structural mitigation is described rather than merely asserted: 'Data analysis for this project is constantly independently reviewed by Scott Compton, who has no conflict of interest related to this work', and Compton is a named co-author. Given the commercial stakes attached to a tablet-based autism screening app, an independent analysis reviewer is the right safeguard and is worth noting as a practice other groups could adopt.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session per participant, no follow-up and no test-retest reliability for any gaze feature. The two datasets are age-stratified rather than longitudinal - adults and children are separate samples, not the same people at two ages - although the introduction motivates the design partly by an interest in 'the developmental trajectory in processing emotional stimuli in neurodevelopmental conditions', and the parallel analysis does permit a cautious comparison across age groups, which the discussion makes: anger is highly weighted in both the adult and child autism models, suggesting a possible common specificity. Ethics reporting is complete for approval and consent: the data collection was approved by ethics committees at both Nara Medical University and Nara Institute of Science and Technology, the procedure was explained at the start of recording and informed consent obtained, and the formal ethics statement records written informed consent from participants' legal guardian or next of kin. Funding from a single CREST grant is stated, and competing interests are declared as none.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: Longitudinal in data span and cross-sectional in analysis: usage covers January 2012 to May 2014 with per-month user and event counts charted, but the classification treats windows as exchangeable and models nothing about change over time. This is a striking missed opportunity, since AAC usage is expected to develop as a user learns the system and, in the acquired-condition groups, may decline with disease progression - and the conclusion identifies 'the stability of predictions over time' as future work. Ethics is the study's most serious deficiency and is entirely absent. There is no institutional review board approval, no ethics committee, no research-ethics statement and no consent process for research use of the telemetry, which was gathered automatically for debugging from a commercial product. The only safeguard reported is that 'all the recorded data were encrypted and de-identified', and the only choice offered to users concerned the optional survey. The population includes 75 users aged 10 or under and a further 20 aged 11-18 among survey respondents alone, plus an unknown number among the roughly 5,192 unlabelled users, and every one of them is a person with a communication impairment whose attempts to speak are the data. Retrospective research use of consumer telemetry from disabled children, without consent or ethical review and without any discussion of either, is a governance gap that a four-page conference format does not excuse. No competing-interests statement appears despite three commercial or industry-lab affiliations among the authors and the app itself having been a commercial product.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Prospective and cross-sectional: children were enrolled and assessed over an eleven-month window, but each contributed a single 10-minute session with no follow-up, no repeat testing and no test-retest reliability for the model's output - a gap for a system proposed as a severity-assessment tool, since severity assessment implies sensitivity to change. The nearest thing to a temporal analysis is the within-session compliance study across repeated trials, which is genuinely informative about habituation but says nothing about stability across days. Governance is complete and well documented. The study was approved by the Yonsei University Health System Institutional Review Board, caregivers gave written informed consent, and the report follows the STARD reporting guideline for diagnostic accuracy studies - one of very few studies in this corpus to adopt a formal reporting standard, and the reason its participant table, flow accounting and confidence intervals are as complete as they are. Funding is from a Korean government physician-scientist training programme with an explicit no-role statement. The competing-interests disclosure is material and full: two authors hold issued patents on the method and apparatus for diagnosing developmental disability and its severity in toddlers based on joint attention, a third has a patent pending, two report non-financial support from LumanLab Inc, one is affiliated to that company, and the acknowledgements thank LumanLab's administrative, regulatory and data management staff. So the method is patented by its developers and a commercial entity participated in data management - disclosed properly, but without any independent-analysis safeguard of the kind reported by the Duke group elsewhere in this corpus.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: Cross-sectional by inheritance; the study performs no temporal analysis and could not. No ethics statement of any kind appears, which for a secondary analysis of published de-identified images is defensible in substance but is still a reporting omission - the source dataset's approvals are not referenced. No funding statement and no competing-interests declaration appear either. The paper is a four-to-six page conference contribution and these omissions are typical of that format, but they are omissions nonetheless.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional by inheritance, with one session per child and no temporal analysis. The pooling of corpora spanning 12 months to 8 years creates something that looks like developmental range but is not a developmental design, since age is confounded with corpus and with label. No ethics statement appears, which is defensible for a secondary analysis of a public research corpus but is still an omission - the CHILDES databank operates under its own conditions of use and no reference to the source studies' approvals is made. Funding from an Indian government start-up research grant with partial industry-linked centre support is acknowledged; no competing-interests statement is provided.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: Cross-sectional with no follow-up and no test-retest assessment. The study is nonetheless the most thorough in this corpus on within-trial temporal structure: gaze is analysed in successive non-overlapping 3-second windows across the first 15 seconds, and separately in 1-second sub-windows, revealing that discrimination is highest in the first three seconds (76.3%) and declines steadily thereafter (71.7%, 69.3%, 71.0%, 70.2%). That is a substantive finding about when social attention differentiates, and it has a practical implication the paper does not draw out - that a shorter protocol may lose little. No ethics approval, consent statement, or competing-interests declaration appears in the retrieved text, which for a study of children including infants is a significant reporting omission whatever the underlying governance. Funding from an NIH K01 award and a Simons Foundation grant is stated.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: Cross-sectional by inheritance, with no temporal analysis. Ethics is handled by reference to the source study: procedures 'were conducted following the ethical standards set by the institutional and/or national research committee, as well as in compliance with the 1964 Helsinki Declaration and its subsequent amendments'. Citing the originating study's ethical basis is appropriate practice for a secondary analysis and is more than most dataset-reuse papers in this corpus do. No funding statement and no competing-interests declaration appear in the retrieved text.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Genuinely longitudinal in structure and, by the standards of this review, exemplary in its handling of time. Predictors are drawn only from measurements taken up to 24 months and the outcome only from diagnoses recorded after 24 months, an ordering imposed deliberately 'to develop a model that minimizes data leakage from diagnosis to predictors'. Mean age at recorded diagnosis was 37.5 months (SD 13.3), so the model predicts on average more than a year ahead of the clinical event. Follow-up varies by birth cohort, and the authors address this both by noting the smaller autism proportion among 2019 births and by fitting a sensitivity model excluding that year. Within-child longitudinal structure is nonetheless collapsed - milestones are binarised to ever-passed versus only-failed - which the authors name as their first limitation and as a target for future work. Governance is complete: Ministry of Health Helsinki committee approval with number and date, consent waived on anonymisation grounds, extraction and anonymisation performed by dedicated Ministry personnel, access only through a secure platform, funding stated, and no competing interests declared.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: Cross-sectional in the trivial sense that photographs have no time dimension. There is no ethics statement, no consent, and no discussion of either. This is the most serious governance failure in the review, and it is worth stating precisely why. The dataset consists of identifiable photographs of children, obtained without their knowledge or their families' consent, in which one class was collected specifically because those images appeared in autism contexts - so the dataset itself asserts a health status about identifiable minors. Training on that dataset propagates the assertion; publishing a mobile application built on it would extend the assertion to new children photographed by whoever downloads it. None of this is acknowledged. No funding statement and no competing-interests declaration appear either.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: Cross-sectional analysis of a cross-sectional repository, with no longitudinal element - although ABIDE-I's phenotype records include age at scan across a wide range, so age is present as a covariate rather than as a design dimension. No ethics statement appears in the retrieved text; ABIDE-I contributing sites obtained their own approvals and consents, and secondary analysis of the public release conventionally proceeds without fresh approval. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up and no test-retest reliability for the coherence measures. The temporal dimension that is analysed is within-conversation frequency rather than change over time: cross wavelet analysis decomposes coordination across 23 time scales from 0.1 to 10 s, which is a genuine and well-motivated use of temporal structure and locates the group difference specifically at the faster scales. Ethics reporting is complete: the protocol conformed to the Declaration of Helsinki, written informed consent was approved by the local ethics committee and signed by caregivers, and a separate declaration confirms Helsinki 2013 conformity, consent, and removal of identifying details. Participants were paid 200 CNY, which is disclosed. Funding from seven Chinese sources is itemised.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional in analysis, though the corpus was assembled over seven years, with prospective recruitment and retrospective record examination running concurrently. No follow-up, no repeat sampling and no test-retest assessment of the linguistic measures - which matters for an instrument proposed as a diagnostic aid, since stability across occasions is unestablished. Ethics reporting is complete and specific: approval by the Hirosaki University Committee on Medical Ethics under IRB 2013-142, subsequently updated to 2018-168 with the previous number 2015-055 also given; the committee's information security guidelines followed; written consent from participants aged 20 and above and from both participants and guardians for those 19 and under; and anonymisation by alphanumeric identifier with identifiable utterances removed from transcripts. The last of these is a specific privacy measure appropriate to a corpus of personal spoken narratives and is not standard practice in this corpus. Funding from two JSPS KAKENHI grants is itemised and competing interests are declared as none.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Cross-sectional in the trivial sense. No ethics statement, consent, funding declaration or competing-interests statement appears anywhere. As with the companion study, the dataset consists of identifiable photographs of children obtained without their families' knowledge, with one class assembled specifically because those images appeared in autism contexts - so the collection asserts a health status about identifiable minors, and training and publishing on it propagates that assertion. None of this is acknowledged.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element. No ethics statement appears, which is conventional for secondary use of two established consented affective-computing corpora. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session per child, with recruitment compressed into five weeks. No follow-up and no test-retest reliability for any kinematic measure - which the authors identify as a limitation and address directly, recommending that 'the sample should be expanded and observed longitudinally'. Governance is complete: approval by the Ethical Committee of Psychological Research of the Department of Humanities at the University of Naples Federico II, written informed consent from parents of all participants described as guaranteeing full understanding, funding from two named sources with an explicit statement that the funders had no role in design, data collection, analysis, publication decision or manuscript preparation, and a declaration of no competing interests. The data are deposited in a public GitHub repository, which is the only open data release among the included studies in this review.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: Cross-sectional as far as can be determined; no temporal structure is described. There is no ethics approval statement, no ethics committee, no consent statement and no governance description of any kind, for a study that reports manual collection of physiological measurements - heart rate and body temperature - and facial data from human subjects. This is the most complete governance absence among included studies that involve primary data collection. No funding or competing-interests statement appears either.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of public repositories, with no longitudinal element. No ethics statement, consent statement, funding declaration or competing-interest declaration appears in the retrieved text. Secondary use of public tabular repositories conventionally requires no fresh approval; the absence of a competing-interest statement is more notable given that the study's output is a deployed public-facing diagnostic tool.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up and no test-retest reliability. The absence of repeat measurement is a real gap for a proposed screening instrument, since a threshold decision on a single brief balance trial requires knowing how stable that trial is within a child. Ethics reporting is complete: approval by the Ethics Committee of Nagasaki University under number 22051204, procedures conducted in accordance with institutional and national standards and the 1964 Declaration of Helsinki and its amendments, and written informed consent obtained from both the children and their guardians after a comprehensive explanation - the participants section specifies 'all subjects and their guardians provided written informed consent', so assent as well as parental consent. Funding from two JSPS Grants-in-Aid, JST MIRAI and JST CREST is itemised, and competing interests are declared as none.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: Cross-sectional and retrospective, with no longitudinal element and no repeat measurement. The ethics reporting is the notable gap: the paper contains no ethics statement, no institutional review board approval and no consent statement of any kind - a full-text search returns no occurrence of 'ethic' or 'consent'. Analysis of public datasets frequently proceeds without fresh approval, and PeerJ's declaration structure elicited funding, competing-interests, author-contribution and data-availability statements from these authors, so the omission is specific to human-subjects considerations. The data are identifiable photographs and video frames of children, harvested from personal websites, Facebook pages and YouTube, whose families posted them to seek support or raise awareness and did not consent to their use as training data for an autism classifier. The paper's conclusion envisages clinical deployment of a model built on that material without touching the question. Funding from King Faisal University grant KFU250488 is declared with a no-role statement, competing interests are declared as none, and the authors disclose that generative AI was used to correct the English.
