answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element. The ethics declarations read in full: 'For this type of study, statement of human rights is not required' and 'For this type of study, informed consent is not required.' The data are EEG recordings of identifiable children obtained from another institution's research group with permission, so the declaration concerns secondary use rather than the original collection - but the paper does not distinguish the two, gives no reference to the originating approvals, and states the exemption in absolute terms. The data provider is acknowledged by name with the corpus URL, and competing interests are declared as none.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: Cross-sectional with a single session, no follow-up and no test-retest. The absence of repeat measurement matters for a proposed screening instrument built on a 90-second sample of a young child's behaviour, since day-to-day variation in a toddler's play is substantial and unquantified here. Ethics reporting is complete: approval by the institute's ethics committee (anonymised in this version for blind review), conformity with the 1964 Declaration of Helsinki, and written informed consent from primary caregivers before the study began. The competing-interest declaration is more informative than most and deserves recording: six of the eleven authors declare two patent applications arising from this research (202310300588.1 and 202310315701.3) while five declare none, and four authors are affiliated with ALSOLIFE, a Beijing autism-services company, alongside the Peking University Sixth Hospital group. The paper states it received no funding of any kind. The patents are declared without their claims being described, which is the relevant detail when the paper proposes the coding scheme and model as a deployable clinical tool.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional with a single assessment session per participant and no follow-up, though the schizophrenia group's clinical characterisation includes age at onset and duration of illness, giving a longitudinal dimension to the covariates if not to the design. No test-retest data. Ethics reporting is complete: approval by the Medical Ethics Committee of Showa University School of Medicine, conduct in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki and with local legislation and institutional requirements, and written informed consent from the participants themselves - who, being adults with measured IQ above 85, consented on their own behalf rather than through proxies, which is true of very few studies in this review. The authors declare no financial support of any kind and no competing interests, and acknowledge a named colleague for teaching them ADOS-2 administration and an editing service for language.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element and no repeat measurement. The ethics reporting is the thinnest of any included study that reports any at all: approval is attributed to 'The Child Pathological Speech Database and De-Engima Project administrations' - the dataset custodians rather than a named research ethics committee - and written informed consent was 'not required from the participants or the participants' legal guardians/next of kin in accordance with the national legislation and institutional requirements'. The contrast with the paper's own introduction is worth noting, since that section reflects specifically on research ethics committees and institutional review boards as safeguards for child data and presents transfer learning as a response to the difficulty of obtaining such data - the topic is raised seriously in the argument and handled formulaically in the declaration. The study received no funding and declares no competing interests, and author contributions are itemised.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional in analysis but drawing on nine years of longitudinal record, since users' full timelines from 2014 to 2022 were collected - a temporal depth no other included study approaches. That depth is used only descriptively, to show a rising trend in autism-related discussion, and no within-user temporal modelling is attempted. Ethics reporting is by a distance the most thorough in this review. The study holds University of Hawaii Institutional Review Board approval 2023-00248 under expedited review and passed a separate institutional data governance review that deemed it exempt 'due to the inherently public nature of the study data'. The authors then describe measures 'not required by the Institutional Review Board': encrypting user IDs to reduce reidentification risk, and anonymising user mentions and personal information such as email addresses within tweet text. They engage with the consent question substantively rather than resting on the public-data exemption, citing survey evidence that 84% of users were not or only slightly concerned about university research use while observing that 'this leaves a considerable portion of the population who remains concerned', and noting that privacy policies are 'long, with complex legal terms that the users may fail to understand or authorize'. They call for large-scale consent procedures and a regulatory framework for social media data mining. And they act: 'the data set and the model that we built using those data have been deleted. When the data set did exist, it was never shared outside of the original authors.' Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: The classification analysis is cross-sectional, but the participants are drawn from a longitudinal cohort explicitly established to study early development in autism, and the recruitment window spans eleven years - the longest in this review. No longitudinal modelling or follow-up outcome is reported here. Ethics reporting is complete and in one respect exceeds every other included study: approval by the Ethics Committee of the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Geneva; written informed consent from a parent or legal guardian for all children; and separately, specific consent obtained from the child depicted in a figure, from their legal guardian and from the examiner for publication of identifying images in an open-access article. That last item is a detail no other paper here reports, and it stands in sharp contrast to the studies charted nearby that train on identifiable photographs of children scraped from support pages without any ethics statement at all. Six funding sources are itemised with grant numbers and a no-role statement, and competing interests are declared as none.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element, despite the stated goal being a longitudinal monitoring platform. There is no ethics statement, no institutional review board reference and no consent statement anywhere in the paper - a full-text search returns no occurrence of the word. The data are identifiable home videos of children, published by their families for reasons of their own, from which faces were cropped and then annotated frame by frame for emotional state by five raters in order to build an autism classifier. Whether families posting a video of their child's stimming for a community of other parents thereby consent to its use as autism training data, and whether a child depicted at two or three years old has any interest in the matter, are questions the paper does not raise. The one place the authors do discuss the trustworthiness of their data concerns label accuracy rather than the ethics of use. Funding under the Malaysia-France Bilateral Research Grant IF040-2021 is declared, competing interests are declared as none, and the data availability statement reads in full: 'The authors do not have permission to share data' - which means the annotations offered as the paper's dataset contribution cannot be obtained.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Cross-sectional despite being framed as continuous monitoring - no child is followed over time, no repeat measurement is analysed, and the 20 videos collected 'for real-time testing to assess the algorithm's performance in dynamic settings' are mentioned once and never reported on. Longitudinal study appears only as future work. The ethics position is the most serious in this review and is stated in five words: 'Ethical Approval. Not required.' There is no institutional review board reference, no ethics committee, no consent statement and no assent statement anywhere in the paper. The participants are 30 disabled children aged 5 to 15, resident at a named special school whose full postal address is printed in the article, thermally photographed during play, lessons and meals, in a study whose declared purpose is to automate adjustment of their psychiatric medication. Who authorised the imaging, whether guardians consented, and whether the children were told what was happening are all unaddressed. This exceeds the ethics gaps recorded elsewhere in this review for the web-scraping studies, because the data here were collected prospectively and in person from a dependent institutionalised population rather than harvested from material families had already made public. The study declares no funding; competing interests are not stated; and the data - identifiable thermal images of these children - are offered to anyone who asks.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element. The retrieved text terminates within the discussion section before the declarations, so ethics, funding, data-availability and competing-interest statements could not be assessed from what was available. What can be said is that the paper contains no discussion anywhere in its main text of the ethics of the underlying material - identifiable photographs of children aged 2 to 14, collected from the internet without their families' knowledge or consent, one class specifically from autism-related sources. The introduction does raise the ethical hazards of autism identification in general terms, naming labelling, effects on self-esteem and social relationships, and overdiagnosis, which is more than the rest of this branch offers; it does not extend that concern to the provenance of its own training data.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of archived transcripts, one session per child, with no follow-up. The ethics position is stated briefly and is defensible: 'The data used in this research is from a publicly available database. The information was gathered with informed consent. This research will not involve any personal information.' Unlike the web-scraping and institutional-imaging studies charted elsewhere in this review, the underlying material was collected for research purposes with consent obtained at source and archived under a governance framework designed for reuse, so a secondary analysis of it raises materially different questions from harvesting children's photographs from support pages or thermally imaging pupils at a special school. Funding and competing interests are not stated.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element. No ethics statement appears, which is conventional for analysis of two public corpora collected under their originators' governance. The paper does address a related concern substantively, and its argument deserves recording: it notes that prior eye-tracking work 'raised concerns about ensuring anonymity' and identifies 'the issue of privacy protection associated with gaze data', then positions skeleton representation as the answer. Joint coordinates carry no face, appearance, clothing, room or lighting information, so a skeleton corpus is inherently less identifying than the video or photograph corpora that dominate this branch. That is a real privacy property of the modality, argued as a motivation rather than noted as a side effect, and it aligns with the same reasoning that led the Geneva group charted elsewhere in this review to render pose as skeleton-on-black and to release a de-identified pose subsample when raw video could not be shared. Funding from the University of Aizu Competitive Research Fund is declared, competing interests are declared as none, and both datasets are identified with public locations.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element, though the paper argues that the modality would support one - cry 'allows for longitudinal assessment, enabling researchers to track developmental changes over time', which is a real advantage of a signal that can be captured repeatedly at home at no cost. Ethics reporting is complete for the original collection: approval by the ethics committee of Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences and Health Services in Tehran, with 'comprehensive informed consent ... acquired from the parents or legal guardians' before enrolment, specified as covering objectives, procedures and possible advantages and risks. The competing-interest declaration is the fullest in this review and is itemised by individual: two authors are employed by Zoundream AG, a commercial infant-cry-analysis company, one of them being a co-founder holding stock; a third received compensation as a member of its scientific advisory board; the fourth declares none; and the company funded the research alongside four public and quasi-public funders. Naming employment, founder status, equity and advisory compensation separately is exactly what a commercially sponsored diagnostic-technology study should do, and it allows a reader to weigh the translational claims accordingly.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of a public tabular repository, with no longitudinal element. No ethics, consent, funding or competing-interest statement appears in the retrieved text; secondary use of a public tabular dataset conventionally requires no fresh approval.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session per child, with no follow-up or test-retest. The ethics position is the study's most serious reporting failure. There is no institutional review board reference, no ethics committee, no consent statement and no assent statement anywhere in the paper - a full-text search returns no occurrence of the word 'consent'. The only appearance of ethics is in the data availability statement, which cites 'privacy and ethical considerations' as grounds for withholding the data, so the authors evidently regard the material as ethically sensitive while documenting no approval for having collected it. This is a prospective study that recruited 100 children including 50 autistic children and recorded more than 16 hours of video of them, so unlike several other studies in this review the omission cannot be attributed to secondary-data status. Competing interests are declared as none; funding is not stated in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary image analysis with no longitudinal element. The ethics reporting is better than most of this branch and deserves credit: approval by the Faculty of Computers and Information Research Ethics Committee with a stated approval code (2024 01 004), conformity to the Declaration of Helsinki, and explicit reference to 'ethical standards regarding data privacy and the responsible use of AI in health-related research'. Very few studies in the facial-image branch obtain or report any approval at all. Two features of the statement are nonetheless questionable. It describes the images as coming from 'a publicly available, anonymized dataset on Kaggle, ensuring no personally identifiable information was used' - but a photograph of a face is among the most directly identifying data types that exists, and the same study processes those photographs with a face-recognition library whose purpose is to establish identity from them; calling such a corpus anonymised misstates what it is. And the claim that 'no direct contact with human participants occurred' is accurate and is precisely what makes the gelotophobia component unevaluable, since it means no one was ever assessed for the condition the system claims to detect. The study declares no funding and no competing interests, and supplies the GELOPH<15> as a supplementary appendix.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element. No ethics or consent statement appears anywhere in the paper, in work whose training data are identifiable photographs of children collected from the internet without their families' knowledge. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis with no longitudinal element. No ethics or consent statement appears anywhere, for work whose training data are identifiable photographs of children collected from the internet without their families' knowledge. Funding and competing interests are not stated in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary and clinic-sourced analysis with no longitudinal element. No ethics or consent statement appears anywhere in the paper. This is a more serious omission than for the purely Kaggle-based studies charted elsewhere in this review: part of the corpus consists of facial photographs of children attending an autism centre in Semarang, so identifiable images of clinically attending children were obtained and used with no reported institutional approval and no consent process. Funding and competing interests are not stated.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, no follow-up. Ethics reporting is absent entirely - no approval statement, no committee, no consent statement, and the word ethic does not appear in the article. This is a study of clinically labelled disabled children published in a medical journal with a full data-availability statement and no ethics statement of any kind. Only the public status of the source dataset is offered, which addresses data access, not the ethics of the analysis or of the diagnostic claim being made.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, no follow-up. Ethics reporting is among the better examples in this corpus in form: Declaration of Helsinki compliance, named committee, protocol number BUIC/H11/SE/46113 with an approval date of 3 April 2023, informed parental consent as an inclusion criterion, and exclusion of children with comorbid neurological disorders. The reviewing body is a Software Engineering Department ethical review committee rather than a clinical or psychological board, which is a mismatch given that the study collects health data on disabled children and advertises a diagnostic use.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics reporting is absent: the declarations section contains only a conflict-of-interest line. There is no approval, no consent statement, and no consideration of the fact that the corpus consists of photographs of identifiable children scraped from the web and redistributed with an autism label attached. The limitations section does raise a genuine ethical point - that false positives cause unnecessary family stress and false negatives delay intervention - which makes the silence on image provenance more conspicuous rather than less.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session, no follow-up. Ethics is a genuine strength: approval from the Government Medical College Guntur Ethics Committee with a stated decision reference (IRB-2024-0057), written parental informed consent before participation, and separate written consent for publication of participants' details and any accompanying images. That second, publication-specific consent places this study at the responsible end of the review's ethics gradient, alongside local_7d7f1fcc and well away from studies that report no ethics statement at all.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics is handled by explicit exemption: the study did not involve direct experiments on humans or the use of human tissue samples, and publicly available Kaggle datasets were used instead. That reasoning treats identifiable photographs of children - carrying a disability label that no clinician assigned - as outside the scope of human-subjects consideration entirely. It is the clearest statement in the corpus of the assumption that makes this branch of the literature possible, and it is stated as a formal declaration rather than in passing.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. Ethics reporting is absent - no approval, no consent, no exemption statement, and the word ethic does not appear in the article. This absence is the paper's most consequential internal contradiction: the entire contribution is framed as a privacy-and-security advance for sensitive health data, invoking GDPR and HIPAA, yet the study reuses identifiable behavioural recordings of 44 people without stating any ethical basis for doing so. Federated learning here protects data from a hypothetical future adversary while the actual governance question - whether these 44 people agreed to this - is never raised.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session. Ethics reporting is solid: an ethics code number is given (036/EA/FK/2025, Faculty of Medicine), parents signed a consent form before collection, and children were accompanied by their teachers throughout - a safeguarding measure that no other study in this corpus mentions. What is missing is consent for publication of images, since sample photographs of identifiable children appear in Figures 3 and 6, and any statement about the dataset's future distribution, even though building a shareable dataset is presented as the study's primary contribution.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. There is no ethics or consent statement for this study. The single occurrence of the word ethical is in the XAI section, which argues that interpretability is needed in healthcare for clinical adoption, risk reduction, ethical compliance, informed consent and patient engagement - the paper names informed consent as a value that explainable AI supports, while providing no consent or governance statement for its own reuse of 1,054 toddlers' screening records.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. There is no ethics statement, no consent statement and no data-governance statement anywhere in the article. That absence is more consequential here than in most of this corpus, because the output is not a screening probability but a specific educational placement recommendation for individual children, offered to educators as a basis for decisions affecting their learning and development.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. The ethics statement is the notable feature: the dataset was collected via an ASD test screening application, with no direct human interaction, with responses submitted by parents and other stakeholders, ensuring ethical approval for research purposes. Absence of contact between researcher and participant is presented as itself supplying ethical approval. No committee, protocol number, consent statement or data-governance arrangement appears, and no consideration is given to whether app users agreed to research reuse of their children's screening responses.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single administration. Ethics reporting is complete: Declaration of Helsinki, approval by the Ethics Committee of the University of Santiago de Compostela with the code USC 26/2023, informed consent presented in the survey's first section before participation, and participant anonymity preserved throughout collection. Beyond procedural ethics, the discussion contains a substantive ethical analysis absent from every other study charted here - it warns against reinforcing stigma and pathologising adaptive social strategies, insists that algorithmic models should never replace clinical evaluation, and requires that clinicians apply them within a personalised-medicine approach respecting patient autonomy and daily-life context.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics reporting is absent entirely - no approval, no consent, no exemption claim, and no mention of where photographs of identifiable children came from or under what terms they may be reused. The paper does note, in summarising prior work, that web-based screening tools raise privacy concerns, so the category is available to it and simply not applied to its own data.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. There is no ethics statement, no consent statement and no exemption claim, and no consideration of where photographs of identifiable children came from or under what terms they may be reused, deblurred, denoised and redistributed in figures - the paper reproduces sample faces at five processing stages in Figure 3.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. Ethics is formally addressed and formally waived: ethical review and approval were waived due to the use of publicly available data without any identifiable information, and patient consent was waived because the dataset is widely accepted and publicly available, has been used in numerous research studies establishing a general consensus regarding its use for research purposes, and has been de-identified. The reasoning is at least stated, which distinguishes it from the many charted studies with no ethics statement at all; but the specific argument - that prior reuse establishes a consensus legitimising further reuse - is a citation-count justification for a governance question, and it is offered for a dataset whose own collection consent is never established.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Cross-sectional, single session. Ethics reporting is complete and specific: approval by the Research Ethics Committee of Cordoba dated 02/08/2019 with reference number 4393, conducted per the Declaration of Helsinki and local legislation, with families informed of the study's purpose and procedures and written informed consent obtained from legal guardians. The discussion adds an ethically relevant scientific caveat - that early diagnoses are provisional - which bears directly on how the labels should be read.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. There is no ethics statement, consent statement or exemption claim anywhere in the article, and no consideration of the provenance or consent basis of the underlying eye-tracking recordings of children.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. Ethical approval and informed consent are both declared Not Applicable, without reasoning - the paper does not invoke the public-data exemption that comparable studies at least state, and offers nothing in its place. A related reporting anomaly: the article has a single author, Saloni Rai, whose CRediT contribution is listed only as Data curation, yet the author statements read All authors have made substantial contributions to conception and design and the acknowledgements thank the co-authors of this manuscript for their valuable and constructive suggestions.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Cross-sectional with two testing days; no longitudinal follow-up, which the authors identify as limiting their ability to know whether autistic participants later develop PD. Ethics reporting is complete: two Research Ethics Committee approval numbers (ERN_18-1800B and ERN_16-0281AP5), Declaration of Helsinki compliance, fully informed consent, and payment of GBP 10 per hour - remuneration being reported at all is uncommon in this corpus and is relevant to the ethics of research participation.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. Ethical approval and consent to participate are both declared not applicable, with the reasoning stated in full: no direct experimentation with human participants, and all analyses conducted on publicly available, fully anonymised, open-access de-identified datasets from Kaggle and UCI. The declaration is at least reasoned rather than blank. What it does not address is whether the original respondents consented to research reuse - the same gap present across this branch.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics and consent are declared unnecessary on the stated ground that the work involved no hospital deployments, and the same passage claims that the datasets were fully identified and processed with strict subject-level partitioning, with fully authorised controlled access, audit logging and standard encryption. Fully identified is the opposite of de-identified and appears in a sentence listing privacy safeguards, so it is presumably an error - but it is the operative word in the article's only statement about the identifiability of newborn data. The irony is structural rather than incidental: the paper's entire motivation is that models must be able to forget a newborn's data when parents withdraw consent, and it obtains no consent and no ethical review for its own use of that data.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. There is no ethics statement, consent statement or exemption claim anywhere in the article. The omission is more pointed than in the questionnaire studies because the paper itself describes the data's provenance: parents and caretakers posted their videos on websites that are accessible to the public, and the dataset consists of URLs to 75 YouTube videos of identifiable autistic children. Whether a parent posting a home video to YouTube thereby consents to its use as machine learning training data is exactly the question the study needed to address and does not raise.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics reporting is complete for the corpus: approval by the Ethics Committee of the Universitat de Valencia, conduct in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, and informed consent from the legal guardians of all participants. Funding is fully itemised across six grants.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics is claimed only for Dataset 2, in a short paragraph stating that all participant data were anonymised, written consent was obtained from caregivers, and IRB approval was granted for data collection and analysis, with secure storage, encryption and restricted access. No committee, protocol number, institution or country accompanies any of this, and no ethics statement covers Dataset 1 at all. Given that Dataset 2 is otherwise entirely unsourced, the ethics paragraph is the only evidence offered that its 100 clinical samples exist as described.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics reporting is complete: ethical committee approval from the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam with reference VCWE-2020-041R1, compliance with the Netherlands Code of Conduct for Research Integrity and the revised Declaration of Helsinki, and informed consent from all participants prior to the experiments. Data governance is also handled properly - the register data are restricted for privacy reasons, and the procedure for requesting access through a research proposal and Data Sharing Agreement is documented.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. Ethics is declared not required, with reasoning given: the dataset is publicly available, was released in anonymised form by its creators, contains no identifiable personal information, and no new data were collected. The declaration is at least argued rather than blank, and the paper additionally discloses that one author is an editorial board member of the journal and was excluded from the editorial decision - a disclosure no other charted study makes.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. Ethics is not obtained but is genuinely reasoned about, which distinguishes this study from most of its branch: the authors note that the data comprise only de-identified facial images with no personally identifiable information, state that according to Roboflow dataset sharing policies it is understood that the curators obtained adequate consent and ethical clearance before publication, confirm that no personal or clinical collection took place, and - unusually - write explicitly that given the child's facial data aspect, there is ethical sensitivity. That last sentence is the only acknowledgement anywhere in the fifteen-study facial-image branch that photographing and labelling children's faces raises a question at all. Its weakness is the inference immediately preceding it: consent is presumed from a hosting platform's sharing policy rather than verified.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: Cross-sectional. The ethics declaration is factually wrong rather than merely permissive: this article does not contain any studies with human participants performed by any of the authors, stated for an analysis of 2,940 photographs of children, with consent to participate and consent to publish both marked not applicable. It is paired with a data-availability statement asserting that no datasets were generated or analysed during the current study, in an article whose results section reports a full metric grid computed on a 2,940-image dataset. Together the two declarations describe a paper that did not use any data, which is the opposite of what the article reports. The framing also claims the framework is privacy-preserving, with no privacy mechanism of any kind described.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Cross-sectional secondary analysis. Ethics is documented at both levels - institutional review board approval obtained by the original collectors before data collection, guardian written informed consent, and a secondary analysis of publicly available de-identified data in accordance with local legislation and institutional requirements. Both repository locations are given. This is complete provenance reporting for a secondary analysis and is among the best in the corpus.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Cross-sectional analysis of longitudinally collected data. Ethics rests on TalkBank's stated requirement that contributors obtain informed consent and ethical approval before sharing, which the paper cites explicitly. The privacy argument is the paper's organising claim and it is stated with appropriate qualification: the authors acknowledge that they have not implemented explicit cryptographic privacy measures such as differential privacy or encryption, and claim only that text-based inputs inherently avoid identifiable biometric data. That qualification, placed in the abstract, is more careful than the unqualified privacy-preserving claims made elsewhere in this corpus.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: Cross-sectional analysis of three months of collection. Consent is documented at both levels - guardians signed an Informed Consent Form as the precondition for each child's participation, and the administering professional signed a Free and Informed Consent Form after training - though no ethics committee reference appears in the extracted text. The paper also contains an ethical discussion that no other study in this corpus offers: it states that the ethical implications of early screening in educational settings must be considered, including the risk of stigmatisation and the responsible use of the generated information; that screening should be understood as an initial support for identifying warning signs and guiding the search for specialised clinical evaluation, not as a definitive diagnosis; and that use of the tool should be accompanied by appropriate training for education professionals to reduce misinterpretations and promote an inclusive and respectful approach to differences. For a tool intended to be operated by teachers on undiagnosed children, that is the right set of concerns and it is stated without prompting.

questions.question_text: What equipment, software and tools are used?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Hardware: video recording of ADOS sessions (audio at 44 kHz, downsampled to 16 kHz). Software: VoiceSauce (UCLA SPAP Laboratory), in-house MATLAB scripts, DTREG for classifier training and evaluation.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Hardware: SMART D optoelectronic system (BTS Bioengineering) with eight infrared cameras at 60 Hz, sub-0.2 mm accuracy; 1-cm passive markers on wrists, hand dorsum, ball and box. Software: MATLAB R2013b with the biolearning toolbox, fifth-order Butterworth 8-Hz low-pass filter, self-written segmentation and parameter-estimation code.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: A custom application displaying Cohn-Kanade images and logging responses and latencies; the platform, display hardware and timing precision are not specified. The acknowledgements credit an eye tracker (ITU Computer Engineering Kullab) and sensors (tazi Machine Learning Solutions), but neither contributes data to the reported analysis.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Hardware: Tobii T60 remote eye tracker, 60 Hz binocular. Software: Tobii Studio for acquisition; MATLAB for K-means quantisation, SVM training and ROC/AUC computation.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: No sensing hardware - data are typed/recorded sentences collected through a computer-based self-report program (platform unspecified). Software: standard NLP tokenisation, latent semantic indexing, and MATLAB with statistics and bioinformatics toolboxes for classification, ROC/AUC and network analysis.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Hardware: iPad mini (Apple) running iOS 7.0, positioned on a 65 cm children's table within 10 cm of the edge so that sensor readings reflect touch forces rather than device movement; tri-axial accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer sampled via iOS Core Motion at 10 Hz; standard iOS touch-event acquisition. Software: two Duckie Deck commercial children's games wrapped in a bespoke app that sequenced and time-boxed the games and disabled the home button; gzip/JSON transfer to Microsoft Azure Table Storage; a bespoke cloud-side feature-computation engine.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Hardware: Polhemus Liberty electromagnetic motion sensor attached to the index finger of the dominant hand, sampling 3D position at 120 Hz; video presentation of stimulus clips. Software: MATLAB for filtering (120 Hz Butterworth), movement segmentation (10% of peak velocity over six consecutive samples) and parameter extraction; LIBSVM for SVM training with grid search over C and gamma; Weka for the standard-attribute-evaluator comparison.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: Hardware: Microsoft Kinect 2.0 RGBD sensor capturing high-resolution colour and depth; a computer screen with speakers for stimulus delivery. Software: Kinect v2 library for animation units and 3D head pose; a modified deep CNN facial-action-unit detector (the Jaiswal & Valstar architecture with the BLSTM removed); custom landmark-centroid head-speed computation; SVM with RBF kernel and greedy forward feature selection.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Hardware: Panasonic HC-V700 camcorders ceiling-mounted in the room corners so infant behaviour could be captured continuously regardless of orientation; audio extracted from one camera as single-channel 44.1 kHz AAC. Software: Noldus Observer XT for video coding and segmentation; openSMILE (audEERING) for eGeMAPS extraction; Weka with sequential minimal optimisation for SVM training; TensorFlow with the Adam optimiser for the BLSTM.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: No acquisition hardware is described - microphone, recording format, sampling rate and environment are all absent. Software: openSMILE for eGeMAPS and ComParE extraction, selected explicitly 'for transparency and reproducibility'; GAN generator and discriminator as feed-forward networks trained with SGD (mini-batch 128, LeakyReLU, batch normalisation, tanh output, binary cross-entropy); linear-kernel SVM for classification. The deep-learning framework is not named.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Hardware: two independent Advanced Mechanical Technology Inc. force plates embedded consecutively in a 6.5 m walkway, recording medial-lateral, anterior-posterior and vertical forces at 1000 Hz. Software: second-order low-pass Butterworth filter with 30 Hz cut-off; IBM SPSS Statistics v21 for stepwise discriminant analysis; MATLAB R2015a Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox and Neural Network Toolbox for SVM and ANN classification.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Hardware: RoboParrot, a parrot-like social robot with speech, blinking, singing, laughing and limited movement, teleoperated by tablet and placed inside a cage; two cameras, one beside the robot for facial expression and one overhead for global movement. Software: motion detection or manual tagging for initial child detection; Kernelized Correlation Filter tracking, chosen after comparison against MIL, Boosting and TLD trackers; custom grid partitioning, cosine similarity, and classifiers. No specific software packages or versions are named.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Hardware: SMI RED250 portable eye tracker sampling at 250 Hz with 0.03 degree spatial resolution; 22-inch widescreen LCD at 1024x768; fixed 65 cm eye-to-monitor distance; dark soundproof room. Software: BeGaze for gaze data analysis; SPSS 22.0 for statistics, group comparisons and the SVM discriminant analysis.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Hardware: Apple iPod Touch with an iRig Mic Cast external microphone (chosen to ensure data quality), sent to each family. Software: a custom iOS app implementing the four gamified tests and the monitoring mode with voice-activity-triggered recording and automatic cloud upload; Sookasa for HIPAA-compliant encrypted Dropbox storage; COVAREP for acoustic feature extraction; Google Cloud Speech-to-Text for ASR; LIWC for linguistic analysis; a custom self-adaptive SVM voice-activity segmentation using per-recording energy percentiles to handle varying background noise.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Hardware: Gazepoint GP3 video-based eye tracker at 60 Hz with 0.5-1 degree of visual angle accuracy, a 19-inch LCD monitor, and an integrated sensor controlling viewing distance at approximately 65 cm; nine-point calibration. Software: Gazepoint software for capture; the extended VIPS (Vision-Based Page Segmentation) algorithm for page-specific AOI definition; the ViCRAM tool for rating page visual complexity; R for logistic regression and cross-validation.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Hardware: Vicon VUE video camera at 1280x720 and 100 frames per second, lateral viewpoint; height-adjustable chair and a table of specified dimensions; a plastic bottle, box and glass of specified dimensions. Software: pre-trained GoogLeNet for CNN features; a custom LSTM with soft spatial attention; dense trajectories with HOG and HOF descriptors and VLAD encoding for the baseline. Deep-learning framework and training hyperparameters are not named.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Hardware: SMI RED250 Mobile remote eye tracker at 250 Hz with 0.4 degree accuracy; 15-inch Dell Precision M4800 at 1280x720; chinrest at 65 cm; 5-point calibration with 4-point validation and automated periodic quality checks prompting repositioning. Software: C# experimental program; SMI event detector (60 ms minimum fixation, 50 degrees/s velocity threshold); Wolfram Mathematica 11.3 for the facial landmark detector and LightGBM; MATLAB (van der Maaten's original code) for t-SNE; R for the Cramer test.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Hardware: LeapMotion hand-tracking device connected to a Lenovo Legion R720-15IKBN computer, with a physical rig of two sticks and a string defining a 60 cm movement zone and a mat for comfortable hand positioning. Software: MATLAB R2017b for signal processing (piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation, second-order 5 Hz low-pass Butterworth filter, differentiation) and machine learning; SPSS 17.0 for statistical comparison.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Hardware: a 'Biosensor' recording device placed on a table between the two speakers, with two HD video cameras facing opposite directions to capture both participants simultaneously and four embedded directional microphones. Software: sox for format conversion; openSMILE with the ComParE13 configuration (25 ms window, 10 ms step) for acoustic low-level descriptors; XTrans for time-aligned orthographic transcription; base R, qdap and LIWC plus a custom author script for text features; scikit-learn (SimpleImputer, PCA, GradientBoostingClassifier) in Python.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Hardware: two Tobii Pro eye trackers - the TX300 at 300 Hz for all ASD subjects and six controls, and the X2-60 at 60 Hz for the remaining controls - with Tobii Studio 3.3.2; two display configurations (19-inch 1680x1050 and 27-inch 1920x1080) depending on collection site; viewing distance approximately 65 cm (camera range 50-70 cm); 9-point calibration with error below 0.5 degrees for every subject. Software: OpenFace pre-trained on LFW for face features, Viola-Jones for face detection, scikit-learn for random forests.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Hardware: parents' own mobile phones for video capture - deliberately, since the deployment argument rests on mobile ubiquity. Software: a secure HIPAA-compliant web rating platform; Python 3.6.7 with pandas 0.23.4, scikit-learn 0.20.0 for models, hyperopt 0.1.1 for hyperparameter tuning, shap 0.24.0 for Shapley values, and matplotlib 3.0.1. Version numbers are given throughout, which is better practice than corpus norm.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: No acquisition hardware, since no data were collected. Software: YOLO (You Only Look Once) for object detection, chosen to segment images into object and non-object regions; SDSP (saliency detection by combining simple priors) for saliency, chosen for low computational complexity; mean-shift clustering with a Gaussian kernel and a distance/scale threshold of 100 for region-of-interest extraction; MATLAB TreeBagger for the random forest.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Hardware: two NAO humanoid robots, one facing the child with its back to the two-way mirror and one on the floor to its left with lights off except during the joint attention task; a high-definition camera behind the two-way mirror; an overhead microphone in the examination room; the robot's onboard camera. Software: hierarchical POMDP models solved with the SARSOP point-based solver, with protocol and task controllers and the operator interface running on a remote computer.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Hardware: Tobii X120 remote eye tracker. That is the only technical specification given - no monitor, viewing distance, sampling rate, calibration procedure, or analysis software, library or platform is named. The literature review names WEKA and MATLAB as tools used by other researchers, but the paper never states what it used itself.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Hardware: Polhemus Fastrak electromagnetic motion tracker with a single sensor on the distal phalange of the index finger, sampling X, Y and Z at 120 Hz; two 8 mm red target stickers on a table. Software: scikit-learn for SVM and grid search, scikit-rebate for ReliefF; outlier handling following the Van Selst and Jolicoeur non-recursive procedure.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Hardware: SMI Red-m remote screen-based eye tracker at 250 Hz mounted below a 17-inch monitor at 1280x1024, with the child approximately 60 cm away; physical white barriers around the setup. Software: SMI Experiment Center for stimulus presentation; Python with Matplotlib for scanpath rendering; Keras for image augmentation and neural network training; scikit-learn for PCA and conventional classifiers; Azure ML Studio hosting the models as web services with an ASP.NET and JavaScript front end for the demonstration application.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Hardware: Panasonic DV C Pro HD P2 high-definition video camera on a tripod at a fixed 320 cm distance, chairs 60 cm apart, standardised artificial lighting. Software: Motion Energy Analysis following the Ramseyer and Tschacher pipeline; the rMEA R package for smoothing, scaling and lagged cross-correlation; NeuroMiner for PCA, SVM training and nested cross-validation. Notably no wearable sensors are used, which the authors flag as an advantage given hypersensitivity in autism.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: An Apple iPad and two children's games. The sensing is entirely built in - capacitive touch screen for contact kinematics, triaxial accelerometer and gyroscope for device movement - so nothing is purchased, worn, calibrated or maintained beyond a consumer tablet. Set against the eye trackers, depth cameras, thermal cameras, EEG amplifiers, force plates and MRI scanners charted elsewhere in this review, this is the lowest equipment barrier of any instrumented approach here, and it is the reason the protocol can propose deployment 'in the home, clinic or classroom'.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: No acquisition hardware used by these authors; the source data came from a Tobii T120 eye tracker with a 17-inch monitor. Analysis: STAR-FC for synthetic scanpath generation; dynamic time warping for alignment; ResNet-18 pretrained backbones; PyTorch on a Titan XP GPU. Notably the hyperparameters are reported in full for all three models - layer counts, neuron counts, activations, dropout, optimiser, learning rate, batch size, epochs and trainable parameter counts - which is better than corpus norm.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Hardware: parents' own recording devices (unspecified) at 30 fps. Software: Behavior Imaging's NODA platform for collection and expert annotation; 2D Mask R-CNN with a ResNet base, region proposal network and RoI Align, extended with a keypoint estimation head, retrained on manually annotated child poses using a semi-automatic annotation tool the authors describe as enabling researchers to build their own annotated datasets; particle filter for keypoint imputation; a modified PoTion generator; a convolutional classifier; Inception V3 for the baseline.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: The most architecturally developed measurement infrastructure in the review. An unstructured, scalable network of RGBD sensors runs on ROS, with each camera node performing face detection, recognition, segmentation, tracking, landmark detection, head pose and gaze estimation locally, publishing results as nav_msgs/Odometry messages; a fusion node on the most powerful workstation combines all navigation messages, computes the visual focus of attention through a Hidden Markov Model, and publishes it as a timestamped message naming the attention target. The components are open source and cited with repositories - Dlib for CNN face detection and ResNet face recognition, OpenFace for CLNF landmarks and gaze - with the specific integration modification described (making the neural model an attribute of the ROS node class and evaluating it in each topic callback). Two design consequences matter for the review. Multi-camera fusion addresses occlusion directly, which is the binding practical constraint on gaze measurement in a room with a moving child, an adult and a robot - and the paper reports encountering exactly that, with 'occlusion by hair, hands and the robot' detected. And the architecture is scalable and unstructured by design, meaning cameras can be added without reconfiguration, which is what would make deployment across differently shaped clinic rooms feasible.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: No acquisition hardware. Software: the SalGAN generator pretrained on SALICON (referenced to a public GitHub implementation) for saliency prediction; custom shallow CNNs in two variants with full layer specifications given in a table; a two-layer LSTM of length 40 with max-pooling; batch normalisation and dropout. Training on an NVIDIA P100 GPU with 16GB memory, Adam optimiser, learning rate 1e-5, momentum 0.9, batch size 8, 30 epochs.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: A NAO humanoid robot from Aldebaran Robotics - 57 cm tall, 5.4 kg - with its SDK and desktop applications for authoring animations, behaviours and dialogues, plus video recording. The paper notes the availability of ASK NAO (Autism Solutions for Kids), a commercial application pack 'inspired by commonly practiced special education teaching methods (ABA, PECS, TEACCH, DENVER, SCERTS)', which is a useful observation for the review: the platform already carries an autism-specific software ecosystem built around established educational approaches, so robot-mediated assessment can be layered onto infrastructure that exists in practice rather than requiring a purpose-built device. The equipment cost remains high relative to the webcam-and-toys protocols charted elsewhere here, and what it buys is exact reproducibility of the social partner.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Video recording in a designated observation room; The Observer XT 12 behavioural observation and coding system; Python with scikit-learn (SVC, GaussianNB, RandomForestClassifier). Clinical instrumentation: M-CHAT, Gesell Developmental Scale, CSBS-DP, CARS, ABC, ADI-R, ADOS. No custom hardware and no automated behavioural sensing.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Hardware: motion tracking and eye tracking apparatus, with specific models deferred to the source protocol publication; a screen for video stimulus presentation. Software: implementations of SVM-RBF, four feature selection algorithms, nested cross-validation, and the authors' novel bagging and wrapped t-test variants; Kuncheva's index for stability quantification.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: High-definition cameras; client applications for computers and smartphones; a four-layer architecture (application, communication, application server with firewall, database server); SQL Server; HDF5 feature files; JSON over TCP; VGG-19 and ResNet-18. Public training corpora: FER2013 (35,887 images at 48x48, seven expressions) and CK+ (593 sequences from 123 people at 640x480, 69% female, including African American, Asian and South American subjects). A specified non-functional requirement - end-to-end response under 5 seconds - is one of the few deployment constraints stated anywhere in this corpus.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Hardware: a Kistler force plate sampling centre-of-pressure at 60 Hz; standard anthropometric measurement of height and body mass. Software: MATLAB R2020a with the Machine Learning Toolbox for classification and performance evaluation; a fourth-order low-pass Butterworth filter with a 10 Hz cutoff selected by residual analysis; sample entropy computed with sequence length 2 and matching tolerance 0.15 times the COP standard deviation.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Hardware: two robots (a small humanoid and an iPod-based mobile robot) in a sensory maze setup on a table; video recording equipment (unspecified). Software: OpenPose for upper-body tracking and facial keypoint extraction; Laban movement analysis for deriving weight, space and time movement-intent features; a custom 1D CNN with specified layer structure and dropout rate; random forest and k-nearest neighbour comparators. No frameworks, versions or hyperparameters beyond the dropout rate and layer counts are given.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Hardware: two Microsoft Kinect Xbox depth cameras at 30 frames per second positioned in front of and behind the child, requiring no sensors or special clothing - an explicit design advantage for this population; a large TV screen for stimulus display. Software: iPi Motion Capture Software for extracting 20 joint coordinates from depth recordings; a custom dynamic time warping and metric learning pipeline with equations supplied in a supplement; SVM for classification.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: 48 kHz stereo recording downsampled and downmixed to 16 kHz mono; openSMILE for the 88 eGeMAPS parameters at 25 ms frames with 10 ms overlap; TensorFlow; t-SNE. Model components: a 88-70-54-70-88 stacked auto-encoder with an auxiliary softmax head on the latent layer, and a BLSTM with eight cells matched to prior work for comparability.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Vicon infrared motion tracking system sampling at 250 Hz for marker capture and gait event detection; the scikit-learn Python library for L2 normalisation, the four classifiers, grid search, 10-fold cross-validation and the four reported metrics. No custom software and no bespoke instrumentation.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: AKG CHM99 microphone at 1-2 m; TASCAM US-16x08 sound card; 44.1 kHz downsampled to 16 kHz; in-house GUI software for manual speaker interval labelling; PRAAT for pitch and formant analysis; custom code for energy, ZCR, spectral slope, jitter and conversational features; deep models with RMSProp and MSE loss. No commercial analysis system - the paper argues explicitly against LENA on the grounds that it is not open source, so 'it is not possible to further develop the LENA algorithms nor assess their utility in estimating ASD severity'.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: Gazepoint GP3 at 60 Hz with 0.5-1 degree accuracy, right eye, roughly 65 cm with sensor-controlled distance and nine-point calibration; 19-inch and 17-inch LCD monitors; Gazepoint's position-variance fixation algorithm; extended VIPS for page segmentation into hierarchical elements, using the fifth level (or deeper where a task could be completed by fixating a single element); ViCRAM for visual complexity; R for classification. The eye tracker is deliberately a low-cost consumer-grade device, consistent with the paper's argument that gaze hardware is already commodity technology.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: SciEye 2.0 eye tracker at 140 Hz; 1920 x 1080 monitor at 0.5 m; a pretrained two-stream CNN taken from prior published work rather than trained here; LIBSVM; a saliency pipeline incorporating Itti et al.'s conspicuity maps, Oliva-Torralba saliency, a trained horizon-line detector and face, person and car object detectors. Sampling rate, viewing distance, presentation timing and image dimensions are all specified; calibration procedure, data loss rate and fixation-detection algorithm are not.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: CAVE with three ceiling ultra-short-throw projectors (100-degree image from 55 cm) and a Logitech Z906 5.1 sound system; Olorama Technology wireless scent diffuser with 12 UDP-triggered channels and programmable fan control of duration and intensity; Intel RealSense D435 depth camera with SDK 2.0; OpenPose for 25-joint pose estimation on an Nvidia GTX1060; MATLAB R2016a with LIBSVM. The scent delivery hardware is unique in this corpus and is what makes the olfactory condition possible.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: A single camera at 24 FPS and a microphone in a fixed layout, explicitly framed as low-cost. Software: Kaldi with an AISHELL-2-trained Mandarin ASR model; OpenCV-DNN face detector chosen for robustness on small toddler faces; a custom 2D-3D CNN built from ResNet-18 and pretrained 3D-ResNet-18 components; standard classifiers for the final decision. Standardising the physical setup is treated as a contribution in its own right.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: SR EyeLink 1000 Plus at 500 Hz binocular; Samsung SyncMaster 2233RZ 22-inch at 60 Hz, 1680 x 1050; 650 mm viewing distance; Neurobehavioral Systems Presentation with embedded calibration and behavioural management; Dynamic Programming on Distance Dispersion fixation identification; expert frame-level ROI annotation; PyTorch, sklearn and pyglmnet in Python 3.6. Quality control is quantified - 95% trimmed mean calibration error of 0.751 visual degrees - which almost no other eye-tracking study in this corpus reports.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: 128-channel HydroCel Sensor Net (Electrical Geodesics) at 1000 Hz, with 62 electrodes selected and re-referenced to linked ears; Tobii TX300 at 300 Hz with a five-point calibration required to pass with small error vectors before the experiment proceeded, at roughly 60 cm; MATLAB R2016a with EEGLAB for preprocessing and pwelch for spectral estimation.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Deliberately low-cost and open-hardware derived: Google Glass with a custom 3D-printed prism mount holding a Microsoft LifeCam HD-6000 webcam whose infrared filter was removed and whose indicator LEDs were replaced with infrared emitters, adapted from the open-source Pupil Project, at about US $35 for the add-on. Multiple mount variants were printed so the best eye view could be chosen per participant. Stimuli came from the CAFE dataset of child faces, balanced across five racial groups and by gender and emotion within each trial - the most carefully balanced stimulus set in the corpus.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: Deliberately minimal: a standard computer with a camera and microphone, which the paper contrasts against comparators using 'high-cost apparatus, not suited for large-scale testing'. Analysis used OpenFace for action units, landmarks and gaze with a trained confidence network, Librosa for MFCCs and energy, Parselmouth Praat scripts for fundamental frequency, jitter and shimmer, and scikit-learn. The preparatory study used facial EMG over zygomaticus major, corrugator supercilii and levator labii to establish which action units to target.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: Microsoft Azure Machine Learning Studio for the entire pipeline - data ingestion, column selection, missing-value cleaning, filter-based feature selection, train/validation splitting, model training and evaluation - with a screenshot of the workflow reproduced as a figure. No eye-tracking hardware is identified. The paper notes that the Studio limited its ability to tune the model, being unable to 'adjust the number of nodes, leaves, and depth', which is an unusual admission that the tooling constrained the science.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: Two NAO humanoid robots with the Naoqi SDK, using the ALGazeDetection module of NaoqiPeoplesPerception to determine whether the child is looking at the robot and to compute eye-contact delay and duration; a Microsoft Kinect for real-time skeletal joint tracking to score imitation against the robot's action. The measurement is therefore fully automated within the intervention itself, requiring no separate assessment session - which is the practical strength of the approach.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Tobii Pro TX300 with a removable 23-inch monitor, up to 300 Hz sampling and head-movement tolerance to 50 cm/s, at 50-70 cm viewing distance; Python with scikit-learn including GridSearchCV and SMOTE implementations. The 300 Hz sampling against video frame rate yields approximately ten gaze records per frame, which is what makes fine-grained trajectory features and the anticipation measure feasible.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: HTC Vive with an embedded aGlass infrared eye-tracking module, gaze coordinates delivered in a normalised unit square through the Unity console; Unity3D for scene construction and recording scripts; scikit-learn with GridSearchCV. The authors report the hardware's limitations candidly, stating that 'the stability and accuracy of aGlass are not high enough' and that they observed rejection of VR among autistic participants - two practical findings that bear directly on whether this modality is deployable with the target population.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Tobii X120 at 120 Hz; a 25.5 x 34 cm display at 1024 x 768 viewed from approximately 60 cm; five-point calibration accepted only when mean visual angle error fell below 1 degree at all five points; Psychtoolbox on MATLAB for stimulus presentation; SPSS 20 for statistics. The calibration acceptance criterion is stated quantitatively, which few eye-tracking studies in this corpus do.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Tobii 4C eye tracker, which records head as well as eye movement - the feature that makes the head-eye co-movement hypothesis testable and distinguishes this setup from the gaze-only trackers used elsewhere in the corpus; a 29WK500-P monitor; and the biological motion animation from prior published work. Sampling at 0.02-second intervals (50 Hz). No calibration procedure, viewing distance or data-quality criteria are described.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: 128-channel HydroCel Sensor Net (Electrical Geodesics) sampled at 256 Hz in a shielded room; eye tracking at 300 Hz with five-point calibration required to pass with small error vectors; EEGLAB for ICA-based artefact removal. Notably, only 8 of 128 electrodes (F3, F4, T3, C3, C4, T4, O1, O2) were retained, justified solely as being 'in order to reduce computational overhead' - a substantial discard of spatial information for a stated engineering rather than scientific reason.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Tobii Pro TX300 at 300 Hz with stated processing latency of 1-3.3 ms; 23-inch screen at 50-70 cm; Tobii Pro Studio; five-point calibration with animated figures at the corners and centre; MATLAB 8.5 R2015a with mexopencv for the attention model; RStudio for statistics. Data quality was enforced as an exclusion criterion - participants with an eye-tracking record rate below 80% were excluded, which is a stricter and more explicit quality gate than most of the corpus applies.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Tobii Pro Glasses 2 head-mounted eye tracker at 50 Hz with Tobii Pro Lab for dynamic-stimulus analysis, plus two video cameras at 25 and 30 Hz. Two practical details are unusual and worth recording: an accuracy test was performed at the end of any conversation in which the participant had moved the glasses, and the authors report verifying that the device 'was reliably accurate even if the glasses were moved by participants during the conversation'. They nonetheless flag head-mounted tracking as a limitation, noting that autistic individuals 'are more sensitive to wearing devices' and recommending contactless, calibration-free alternatives.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: Audio Editor 2016 on a laptop recording PCM mono WAV at 16-bit resolution in a stated noise-free location; MATLAB on an i5 processor for all processing; LIBSVM for the SVM comparator. The recording chain is consumer-grade, which the paper does not treat as a limitation despite its own observation that 'the noise parameters depend on the voice recording environment. Hence the values of parameters also vary accordingly'. The stated sampling rate of '24,000 kHz' is a transcription error for 24 kHz.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: SMI RED250 remote eye tracker at 250 Hz - among the highest sampling rates in the corpus, and material here because the authors attribute conflicting literature findings on saccade dynamics partly to trackers running at 60 Hz and 24 Hz; a 17-inch monitor at 1280 x 1024 viewed from about 60 cm; SMI Experiment Center; five-point calibration followed by verification procedures. Analysis in Python with Matplotlib, OpenCV and Keras on a Tesla K80, with the Minerva R package for the MIC computation, and Azure ML hosting the deployed demonstration model.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Tobii Pro TX300 with five-point calibration and a documented failure and exclusion policy; monitor viewed from 50-70 cm; MATLAB 2015a; Saliency Toolbox for Itti-model features; a gist-descriptor mixture of linear regressions for horizon detection; face and person detectors; optical flow for motion estimation.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: A three-wall CAVE with three ultrashort-throw projectors, Logitech Z906 5.1 audio and a wireless Olorama olfactory system regulating odour presence and intensity; Tobii Pro Glasses 2 with a scene camera, two cameras per eye using a 3D eye model, and an accelerometer and gyroscope allowing head and eye movement to be separated so that head motion does not contaminate gaze data - a technical requirement for free movement that screen-based trackers cannot meet. Glasses were fitted and calibrated in an adjacent room, with researchers verifying both correct operation and that 'the subject did not reject them' before the child entered the CAVE. Analysis in R 3.6.1.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Two consumer cameras, a Samsung HMX-F90 at 25 Hz and a Logitech C270 at 30 Hz, with only the frontal Logitech feed used for head pose; OpenFace 2.0; MATLAB 2017b.
