The equipment argument is worth noting: the whole pipeline runs from an ordinary webcam and open-source software, which underpins the authors' claim that head pose tracking suits early screening because it is 'constraint-free' and requires no worn devices or task compliance.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: scikit-learn in Python on Google Colaboratory. No hardware, hyperparameters, random seeds or software versions are reported.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Qualisys optoelectronic motion capture with three infrared cameras at 200 Hz - the highest-fidelity motion measurement in the corpus - with ten passive markers on the upper limbs and one on the sternum, low-pass filtered at 10 Hz with a third-order Butterworth filter. Marker labelling was verified by offline visual inspection, and the movement onset and offset criteria were themselves validated by visual inspection of individual trials. The robustness analysis using only the ulnar marker is a direct response to the practical constraint that autistic children may not tolerate a full marker set.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: An Aldebaran/SoftBank NAO robot with a custom-designed chest mount holding a mobile phone, the phone camera configured as an IP camera through a mobile application, and Haar cascade classifiers performing face and ear detection at approximately 1 Hz. The design point worth recording is that the sensing is the robot's own - the camera that measures the child is mounted on the thing the child is attending to - so the measurement apparatus and the social stimulus are the same object. That is more elegant than the arrangements charted elsewhere in this review, where a separate camera observes a child interacting with something else, and it means the face-detection geometry directly encodes orientation toward the robot. The cost is that the measure is only as good as the assumption behind it, and a low-frame-rate Haar cascade detecting a face is a coarse proxy for attending.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Paper questionnaires and Google Forms for collection; Python with scikit-learn for encoding, feature selection and classification. No hardware, versions, seeds or hyperparameters are reported.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: No dedicated recording equipment - the analysis reuses videotape from ADOS-2 administrations, which is what makes it deployable without protocol change. Analytically it rests on the authors' own time-varying harmonic model, developed to correct two specific failures of standard pitch detection algorithms: octave errors that estimate pitch at half or double its true value, and insufficient time-frequency resolution to capture the fine pitch and amplitude perturbation characteristic of disordered speech. The model is fitted by maximum a posteriori estimation to prevent overfitting from model complexity, and had been previously validated on Parkinson's disease and clinical depression.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment is described - the eye tracker, its sampling rate, calibration and stimulus presentation are all properties of the source dataset and are not restated. Analysis tools are named specifically: YOLO with a stated architecture (9 convolutional plus 2 fully connected layers) trained on COCO for object detection; SDSP for saliency, with the selection rationale given as low computational complexity relative to Itti-Koch, GBVS, BMS, Salicon, SalGAN and SAM-ResNet; mean-shift clustering with an explicitly stated distance threshold of 100; and MATLAB's TreeBagger with tuned minLS, numPTS and numTree.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Acquisition: Tobii T120 with a 17-inch monitor, restated from the source collection. Analysis: STAR-FC, described in enough detail to follow - central initial fixation, retinal transform giving anisotropic blurring, a conspicuity map fusing a low-level peripheral stream with a high-level deep-learned central stream, and a priority map incorporating inhibition of return - together with ImageNet-pretrained ResNet18 and ResNet50, a 5-layer LSTM, DTW, Hausdorff and Frechet distance implementations, and PyTorch. Every optimiser setting, learning rate, weight decay, batch size, dropout rate and epoch count is specified for each of the five architectures.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Deliberately minimal on the acquisition side. OpenPose 'uses a simple 2D camera input not requiring any external markers or sensors, thus allowing the retrospective analysis of videos' and is 'immune to variations in resolutions and setting' - so no motion capture suits, markers, depth sensors or calibrated rigs, and existing archives become usable. Analytically: OpenPose COCO model with 18 keypoints (13 body, 5 facial); VGG16 pretrained on ImageNet; a 512-unit LSTM; rmsprop with categorical cross-entropy; training on the Geneva Baobab HPC cluster across RTX 2080Ti, Titan X and Quadro P1000 GPUs; GraphPad Prism v.8 and SPSS v.25 for statistics, both with URLs. The contrast with the marker-based and depth-camera motor studies elsewhere in this corpus is the point - equivalent or better accuracy from ordinary video.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Deliberately commodity hardware: an Android 6.0 tablet with a 9.6-inch 1280x800 screen at 60 Hz refresh, dimensions given to the millimetre, with touch sampling at 40 Hz - so 40 coordinate pairs per second. No motion capture, markers, depth cameras or wearable sensors, which is the study's practical argument: the same measurement in the optical motion-tracking literature it cites requires a laboratory. Software is bespoke (Unity, C#), analysis uses RStudio with the traj package with its two source citations, and the Leiter-3 materials were supplied by Stoelting Co. The 40 Hz sampling rate is a meaningful constraint that goes unremarked: it bounds how finely acceleration - the feature family the importance analysis identifies as most discriminative - can be estimated from a differenced coordinate stream.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Specified in detail on the acquisition side, which is a strength. EEG: Electrical Geodesics 128-channel Ag/AgCl passive electrode net, 1000 Hz sampling, at least five minutes, Cz online reference, impedances verified below 50 kOhm via Net Station, downsampling to 250 Hz, 50 Hz notch, 0.5-45 Hz band-pass, 4-second non-overlapping epochs, a cited automated artifact detector covering eye movements, blinks, line noise, breathing, muscle, abrupt slopes and outliers, supplementary visual inspection, a 200 microvolt bad-channel threshold with neighbour interpolation, and 62 of 128 electrodes retained across ten regions. Eye tracking: Tobii TX300 at 300 Hz, 1024x768 display, ~60 cm viewing distance, five-point calibration gated on small error vectors, Tobii fixation filter, linear interpolation of gaps up to 100 ms, binocular averaging, and a >70% screen-looking-time inclusion threshold. Modelling uses the publicly available DeepLearnToolbox, cited with its GitHub URL - so the learning machinery, at least, is reproducible off the shelf.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Acquisition is a single consumer camera - a Sony DSC-RX100 IV at 1920x1080 and 30 fps, front-facing - with no depth sensor, marker, wearable or eye tracker, which is the practical argument for the approach: the same behaviour is measured elsewhere with eye-tracking hardware or motion capture. Physical setup is specified to the centimetre (70 cm toy distance, 3x5x3 cm toys, 45-degree examiner offset, height-adjustable chair with the child's right elbow and wrist on the table). Modelling uses ImageNet-pretrained VGG-16 with the last convolutional layer retained for its spatial structure, a two-layer 512-dimensional LSTM, a soft attention module, and a classifier head of 512-unit FC, ReLU, dropout 0.5 and a 512-to-2 FC layer. Semantic segmentation isolates the foreground human, though the segmentation method itself is not named.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Three consumer-grade sensors, which is the practical argument of the paper: a Tobii eye tracker (model not specified), an unspecified video camera, and an Emotiv EPOC+ 14-channel wireless headset with all electrode positions named (AF3, F7, F3, FC5, T7, P7, O1, O2, P8, T8, FC6, F4, F8, AF4, referenced to P3 and P4). The EPOC+ is a consumer device with saline electrodes and no impedance control, applied here to children aged 3-6; the paper cites its noninvasiveness, low cost and high temporal resolution as advantages and does not discuss its known signal-quality limitations. Preprocessing is stated (0.2-45 Hz band, epoching, removal of epochs containing blinks, eye movement or muscle activity, FFT band power) but the number of surviving epochs per group is not reported - the differential-data-quality question that Han et al. at least quantified for their comparable design.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment beyond a single mention of the SMI RED screen-based eye tracker used for the source recordings, with no sampling rate, calibration procedure or viewing geometry. Analysis tools are specified in more detail: Lanczos interpolation for resizing (with the justification that it 'provides the best properties for preserving details'), the ITU-R 601-2 luma transform for grayscale conversion at 8-bit depth, contrast stretching with the normalisation equation given, the KELM formulation with its Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse solution and RBF kernel, and the full GPC update equations with their physical parameters. The asymmetry is characteristic: every step of the image pipeline is documented and nothing about the measurement is.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Tobii TX300 at 300 Hz with 0.4-degree spatial resolution on a movable 23-inch 1920x1080 monitor at approximately 65 cm. Calibration discipline is the most rigorous in the corpus and is reported with its failure handling: a nine-point calibration followed by a nine-point validation quantifying error at all nine locations spanning the full screen, with results displayed immediately to the experimenter, who would adjust the screen or participant and repeat if any point exceeded 1.5 degrees of error - and the procedure repeated before each of the three parts of Episode A. The authors also report, against their own interest, that 'a computer error resulted in the loss of the validation data, so further quantitative assessment of validation accuracy is not possible', and that 12 participants were recorded at 120 Hz rather than 300 Hz 'because of a user error', noting that downsampling to the 24 Hz video frame rate compensated for the difference. Reporting both errors is a form of candour absent elsewhere in this corpus. Feature extraction used Detectron2 with DensePose and InsightFace with RetinaFace, and clustering used scikit-learn.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Deliberately none beyond what families already own: participants' own smartphones, with no model, microphone or sampling-rate constraint, held against the parent's forehead during play. This is the study's contribution and its cost. The benefit is that the recordings carry the acoustic heterogeneity of real deployment - varying room acoustics, distances, device microphones, background noise - so a model that works here has already survived conditions that laboratory studies control away. The cost is that none of that variation is characterised: no distribution of device types, recording levels, signal-to-noise ratios or sampling rates is reported, so it cannot be determined whether any acoustic property covaries with group. Given that the two groups were recruited through the same app but differ in age and sex, a systematic difference in, say, microphone distance for younger children is plausible and unexamined. Analysis tools are named precisely: Librosa, scikit-learn, Keras with Visualkeras, and the facebook/wav2vec2-base checkpoint.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Acquisition is minimal and reusable - a single suspended microphone three feet from the child during a routine ADOS administration - which is what makes the measures retrofittable to existing clinical archives. The analytic pipeline is where the equipment complexity sits: a harmonic model of speech with model-based jitter and shimmer estimation, adopted because 'standard methods for calculating jitter and shimmer are sensitive to the pitch estimation'; a pretrained fully automated deep-neural-network denoiser applied before feature extraction; and R for all statistical analysis with code released. The denoising step warrants attention because its necessity is stated unusually starkly: 'Recordings from both groups contain similar, ubiquitous noise not caused by participants. If denoising is not performed, the acoustic features mainly represent the noise instead of participants and the classifier cannot distinguish between groups.' Applying the denoiser identically to both groups is the correct control, and stating that raw acoustics were noise-dominated is candid, but it means the entire voice result is conditional on a black-box preprocessing step whose interaction with group-specific vocal characteristics is, as the authors concede, unknown.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Deliberately minimal and entirely commodity: an iOS tablet on a tripod, using its own front-facing camera, running a purpose-built app. No external camera, depth sensor, marker, wearable or motion capture. That is what permits administration in a primary-care room by a non-specialist assistant with a caregiver holding the child. The analytic chain is specified in detail - face detection with human-supervised tracking to ensure only the participant's face is followed, 49 2D facial landmarks, head pose angles relative to the tablet, an automatic gaze estimation algorithm, and Python with pingouin for all statistics. Two engineering decisions deserve note because they neutralise obvious confounds. Landmark displacement is normalised by a one-second running average of inter-eye distance, which removes the effect of the child moving closer to or further from the camera - a variance source that would otherwise dominate in a lap-held toddler. And the sample-entropy tolerance uses the population-wide standard deviation rather than each participant's own, chosen explicitly so that 'this choice defined a distance threshold r consistent across participants', which prevents children with more variable movement from being scored on a correspondingly wider tolerance and hence appearing artificially regular.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Essentially nothing on the acquisition side - no microphone, recording device, sampling rate, room or distance is specified for either site, which for a study built on amplitude-envelope spectra is the most consequential reporting omission. Analysis tools are named: the MATLAB Audio Toolbox together with scripts from four prior published studies for the envelope spectrum, intrinsic mode function and temporal modulation spectrum extraction, with further technical detail relegated to supplementary material. The intonation pipeline extracts time-normalised f0 contours at 20 points per utterance. Principal component analysis and a linear-kernel SVM complete the chain. The reliance on published scripts rather than bespoke implementations, together with the OSF deposit of the analysis code, makes the computational half of the pipeline substantially more reproducible than the acquisition half.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: No specialised acquisition equipment - narratives were video recorded during ADOS-2 sessions already being conducted. The methodological weight sits on transcription, which is described more carefully than in any other study here: two experienced transcribers worked independently and blind to diagnosis, following the Codes for Human Analysis of Transcripts convention, achieving word-level reliability averaging 91%; one trained transcriber then compared the two transcripts word for word and resolved discrepancies by reference to the video. Reporting an actual reliability figure for transcription is unique in this corpus - MacFarlane and colleagues describe extensive transcriber training and consistency checks but state explicitly that they have no reliability results. Computational tools are named precisely: the Polish ELMo from ELMoForManyLangs pre-trained on 20 million words from Wikipedia and Common Crawl, at default settings; Universal Sentence Encoder large v3; XGBoost with default settings; scikit-learn NuSVC; and TensorFlow 2, with package URLs given in footnotes.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Fully specified and appropriate to the age group. An SMI RED250 remote eye tracker at 250 Hz - remote rather than head-mounted, which is necessary for toddlers - mounted below a 17-inch LCD at 1680x1050 resolution, with stimuli presented via SMI Experiment Suite and data collected and stored in Experiment Center 3.6. Viewing distance approximately 60 cm with both distance and screen height individually adjusted, five-point calibration with a crying cartoon target repeated until x and y deviation fell below one degree, and a researcher present with each parent-child pair. Areas of interest were drawn in BeGaze, and all analysis performed in WEKA. Reporting the calibration tolerance and the repeat-until-criterion rule is important for a study whose features are all derived from gaze position, and it is done here where most studies in the corpus simply state that calibration was performed.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: An SMI RED250 remote tracker at 250 Hz with 0.03 degree spatial resolution, viewing a 22-inch LCD at 1024x768 from 65 cm in a dark, soundproof room, with the child's centre of vision aligned to the screen centre. Calibration used five points with a dynamic pink rabbit as the target, and - importantly - 'those who failed to follow the dynamic pink rabbit fixation did not continue in the experiment', so calibration failure was an exclusion rather than a tolerated source of noise. A second quality step used Gaze Replay path playback before analysis 'to exclude the subjects whose fixation point deviates from the screen to reduce systematic errors'. Both steps are good practice for a toddler paradigm and both are likely to remove children differentially by group, since compliance with a calibration target and sustained on-screen looking are themselves plausibly reduced in autism - yet no exclusion counts are given for either step in either group, which is the most consequential reporting omission in the paper. Fixation detection thresholds are stated (duration above 100 ms, displacement below one degree) and analysis used BeGaze and R-studio 3.5.2.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Consumer smartphones for caregivers plus web portals for clinicians and analysts - no specialised hardware. The substantive resource requirement is human: video analysts must hold at least a master's degree in psychology, occupational therapy, physical therapy, speech-language pathology, special education or a related field with specific autism training, and have at least five years of professional or clinical experience with autistic children. They receive standardised training, must pass certification on previously unseen videos meeting minimum PPV, NPV and abstention-rate guarantees, and undergo ongoing performance review during the study. This is the element that most complicates the scalability claim, and the authors identify it themselves as a research priority: 'improving the scalability of the video component of the Device by decreasing reliance on human video analysts in subsequent generations of the algorithm'. The Device also requires smartphone access, which the authors note 'not all low-income American families may have', and functions only in English, with Mandarin and Spanish versions in development.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: The acquisition equipment is the study's decisive variable and is reported with enough candour to be evaluated. Autistic group: a video camera on a three-legged support, at an unspecified distance, in a therapy playroom. Comparison group: parents' own phones, model unspecified, at home. No sampling rates, microphone specifications, distances or room characteristics are given for either. The analysis chain is by contrast well specified - openSMILE 2.1 with eGeMAPS, chosen over ComParE because 6,376 features 'vastly outnumbers the sample size', and over GeMAPS for its psychological grounding - with Python, scikit-learn and Jupyter, and public code. The authors' own recommendation for future work is the correct diagnosis of what went wrong: 'it would be necessary that all the participants wear [a microphone] simultaneously from their mouths to ensure that all the variations are due to the actual speech production'.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment is described at any point. The analysis chain is specified in unusual mathematical detail: the average filter with its 5x5 window and neighbour-averaging equation, the Laplacian operator, the subtraction combining them, the active contour formulation including the level-set function, the energy terms, the Heaviside and Dirac delta smoothing functions, the sign convention determining whether the contour shrinks or expands, and the stopping criterion comparing successive masks. Morphological operations are named, LBP is given with its neighbourhood size and feature count, and the CNN training options are tabulated with optimiser, mini-batch size, epochs, learning rate, validation frequency and execution environment for both networks. The asymmetry is total: every arithmetic step is documented and nothing about the measurement is.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: No specialised hardware at all - participants' own phones, with no model, camera specification, resolution or frame rate reported. The analytic chain uses two off-the-shelf systems applied without task-specific training: Amazon Rekognition for 30 facial landmarks and bounding boxes, and OpenFace for gaze direction. Both are used as noisy annotators with explicit quality gates - frames with zero or more than two faces removed, and frames with OpenFace gaze confidence below 75% removed - and the authors are appropriately cautious about what survives, stating that 'we expected the final annotations to be of high quality, but the presence of some noise and incorrect labels was to be expected'. Using general-purpose vision tools as automated annotators rather than training bespoke models is what makes the privacy-preserving claim credible and the pipeline reproducible, and it is a deliberate architectural choice rather than a convenience.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment is described beyond a literature-review mention of the source study's SMI RED tracker. The analytic environment is specified in unusual detail for a computational paper: Microsoft Azure Machine Learning Studio Classic for the conventional models, Google Colaboratory for the neural network, and a Dell XPS 15 9500 with an Intel i7-10750H at 2.60 GHz with six cores. Model hyperparameters are stated - binary cross-entropy loss, 50 epochs, batch size 16, learning rate 0.001 with Adam - along with the full convolutional architecture layer by layer with filter counts, kernel sizes, pooling dimensions and output feature dimensions.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: None beyond a smartphone the family already owns - iOS or Android, with internet access, and no model, sensor or specification requirement, because the data are event timestamps rather than recordings. This is the most minimal data-collection footprint in the review and it is the paper's principal translational argument: a screening signal derived from four fields per trial imposes no bandwidth cost for video upload, no storage burden, no annotation pipeline and no privacy exposure. Analysis used Python with scikit-learn and XGBoost, with hyperparameter grids tabulated for all four classifier families.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: The most consequential reporting gap in the paper. No microphone, recording device, sampling arrangement beyond the 48 kHz rate, room, distance or channel count is described; a photograph is referenced in place of a methods description. This matters because the entire analysis rests on a two-input two-output convolutive mixing model, and the paper's own equations describe the two observation channels ambiguously. Equation 1 sets up a general M-receiver model, which implies multiple microphones. Equation 2 then simplifies to two channels and states that 'x(n) are the ASD children's speech signal and the normal children's speech signal, respectively' - which describes not two microphones recording one speaker but one recording from each group. Under that reading each ICA would operate on a paired autistic and comparison utterance, and the resulting unmixing matrix would depend on the pairing, which requires the labels. The analytic chain is otherwise well specified: STFT with window 512 and offset 256 giving 256 frequency sequences, negative entropy as the independence criterion with the definition given, a fixed-point update rule, and permutation sorting with amplitude compensation before reconstruction.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: Fully specified and deliberately minimal: a single AKG CHM99 microphone at 1-2 metres, 44.1 kHz downsampled to 16 kHz, in the ADOS room. Reporting the microphone model, its distance, the sampling and downsampling rates, the mean session duration and the achieved signal-to-noise ratio is more complete acquisition reporting than most speech studies in this corpus provide, and it matters here because the paper's central claim - that automatic diarization matches manual annotation - depends on the audio being genuinely difficult. Analysis tools are named specifically: the Brno University of Technology x-vector system with its window size and rate, the dscore tool with a 0.25-second collar, and RMSprop with random-search tuning under five-fold cross-validation, with the selected batch size, epoch count and learning rate tabulated separately for each of the three segmentation conditions.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: A NAO humanoid robot operated remotely by an experimenter through its standard graphical interface, plus video recording. NAO's onboard sensing is not used for measurement at any point, so the robot is a standardised stimulus rather than an instrument - which is the study's defining methodological characteristic and the reason it contains no automated measurement. The equipment cost is nonetheless the highest of the elicitation devices in this review after MRI and thermal imaging: a NAO is a research-grade humanoid platform costing several thousand euros, against the webcam-and-toys protocols charted elsewhere. What it buys is exact reproducibility of the social partner's behaviour, which no human examiner can provide, and the authors identify this as the point.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Tobii Pro Glasses 2 head-mounted eye tracker sampling at 50 Hz, with an integrated 1920 x 1080 scene camera; gaze coordinates exported in pixels by Tobii Pro Lab. Cognitive assessment by Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices. Analysis tooling is not named - no MATLAB, Python, R, scikit-learn or LIBSVM is identified, and the SVM implementation, kernel and hyperparameters are unspecified. Calibration was one-point at the interlocutor's body position within Tobii's recommended 0.5-1.5 m working distance, verified qualitatively by checking that the live-view gaze marker overlapped named targets; no numeric accuracy or precision criterion was applied, and no per-participant tracking-ratio statistic is reported beyond the rule that segments with >30% loss were discarded.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Well documented at the hardware level, undocumented at the software level. Hardware: an ESP8266 NodeMCU IoT board streaming sensor data over Wi-Fi by UDP; an ADXL345 MEMS triaxial accelerometer; two Hall-effect magnetic shaft encoders mounted on the front and rear wheels; battery power; all electronics concealed inside the car. Firmware is built on the Arduino ecosystem explicitly to simplify future development, and an ROS package was written so the car can be integrated into other screening systems - a genuine and unusual contribution to reusability. Software for analysis: nothing is named - no Python, MATLAB, scikit-learn or equivalent, no SVM implementation or regularisation parameter, no MLP architecture or augmentation method, no random forest settings. Two acquisition parameters that a replicator would need are also missing: the sampling rate of the accelerometer and encoders, and any accounting of packet loss, which is a real concern because UDP was chosen precisely for throughput over reliability and offers no delivery guarantee.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Hardware and capture: an Android 6.0 tablet, 241.9 x 149.5 x 8.5 mm with a 9.6 inch 1280 x 800 screen at 60 Hz refresh, running custom software written in Unity and C# that logged finger position at 40 Hz. Cognitive assessment: Leiter-3 International Performance Scale. Feature extraction: RStudio with the traj package, citing Leffondree et al. (2004) and Sylvestre et al. (2006) - a specific, checkable toolchain. Modelling software is not named at all: no TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras or equivalent, and no architecture details beyond 'a simple multilayer perceptron' predictor with a tanh intermediate layer and softmax output. The imbalance in the Methods is conspicuous - roughly two pages explain what a feed-forward neural network and backpropagation are, at textbook level, while the actual network used in the experiments has no stated layer sizes, learning rate, optimiser, batch size or epoch count.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Capture: four Hikvision RGB cameras with 2.8 mm lenses mounted at a common height of 1.44 m, recording 1280 x 720 at 25 fps, of which three are used - C1 at the child's left front for body pose and C3/C4 at left and right rear for head pose, the pair being necessary because the clinician may stand on either side. Audio is captured alongside and converted to 16 kHz 16-bit PCM for the speech service. Software stack, all named and all off-the-shelf except for retraining: iFlytek (HKUST Xunfei) real-time speech transcription, a deep fully-convolutional ASR that returns timestamped text and thereby locates each name call; YOLOv3 for person detection, deliberately retrained on more than 1,700 images from the study's own 30 subjects rather than using COCO weights, on accuracy grounds; HRNet for top-down 2-D pose estimation, chosen for its high-resolution feature maintenance and repeated multi-scale fusion; OSNet person re-identification to associate detections across frames and assign a stable ID, without which the child's skeleton could not be distinguished from the clinician's and the parents'; OpenFace for face detection, landmarks and 3-D head Euler angles. Implementation in Python and PyTorch. What is missing is any calibration: the cameras' geometry is fixed and stated but no intrinsic or extrinsic calibration is performed, and the shoulder rotation angle is computed directly in 2-D image coordinates, so a given physical torso rotation maps to different measured angles depending on where the child is seated and how they are oriented with respect to C1.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Stimuli: the Japanese Female Facial Expression (JAFFE) database, presented at 1024 x 768. Capture: a stationary eye-tracking system at Shahid Beheshti University, depicted in a photograph but never identified - no manufacturer, model, sampling rate, spatial accuracy or precision figure appears anywhere in the paper, which is a significant omission because every feature is a fixation count or duration and fixation detection depends directly on sampling rate and on the detection algorithm's parameters, neither of which is stated. Analysis: MATLAB R2020b, using fixation detail output (start, duration, end, X, Y) and the Neural Network facilities for the MLP. Calibration was performed and used as a gate, with failure to calibrate an explicit exclusion criterion, but the protocol, point count and accuracy threshold are not described. Out-of-range samples were retained by enlarging the analysis space beyond the stimulus and labelling the surplus 'OUT', which is a pragmatic choice but implies non-trivial tracking error that is never quantified.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Recording used a purpose-built in-house device with two 1080p cameras at 30 fps mounted back to back on a floor stand between the participant and the confederate, so both parties are captured simultaneously from a fixed and identical geometry. Cognitive assessment used the WASI-II. Diagnosis used ADOS-2 Module 4. The analysis stack is the study's technical core and is described precisely: 3DI, a 3D morphable model fitting method chosen for two specific properties - it learns facial identity from multiple frames, so identity bias can be modelled and explained away rather than left to contaminate the expression signal, and it accepts camera parameters as input, which the authors state is critical for decoupling expression from head pose. The default PCA expression basis was replaced with a purpose-built basis of 60 localised components; 7 corresponding to nose and cheek were discarded, leaving 53 expression dimensions plus 3 rotation angles. Classification used a linear SVM at default C. The decision to reject Facial Action Coding System units is argued rather than assumed: the analysis needs continuous intensities for cross-correlation, automated AU detectors supply intensity for only a small number of AUs, and adding AUs would inflate a feature space that already grows quadratically in the number of time series.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: A SciEye 2.0 eye tracker sampling at 140 Hz, using infrared illumination with corneal and retinal reflection, feeding a 1920 x 1080 monitor on which 1040 x 780 images were centred; the child sat 0.5 m away. The device's own preprocessing is specified numerically and is a genuine reporting strength: gaze points separated by less than 0.02 in normalised coordinates were merged, and merged points shorter than 0.1 s deleted, to suppress noise. No calibration procedure is described, which is the notable gap in an otherwise well-specified acquisition chain. On the analysis side: SLIC superpixel segmentation, a deep autoencoder trained layer-wise then fine-tuned globally with a cross-entropy reconstruction loss on 10,000 MS COCO images, and an LSTM with fully connected and regression heads trained by backpropagation through time, with the full gate equations reproduced. Otsu's maximum between-class variance method supplies the decision thresholds. Two baselines were reimplemented for comparison rather than merely cited - a fixation-count histogram with SVM, and stacked deep features of up to 10 fixations with SVM - which is more effort than most papers here expend on their comparators. Software frameworks and hardware for training are not named.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: Data collection used a Python script against the Twitter developer API, exporting to CSV. Analysis ran in two Jupyter notebooks under Python 3.9 on a single workstation (Intel Core i7-9700K at 3.60 GHz, 32 GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080). The models are named with their selected hyperparameters - decision tree (max depth 9, min samples leaf 2, min samples split 4), XGBoost (colsample_bytree 0.8, gamma 5, max depth 5, min child weight 1, subsample 0.8), k-nearest neighbours with k = 1 - and the deep model is identified precisely as BERT-base-multilingual-cased, used without tuning by deliberate design. GridSearchCV is named as the search tool. What is conspicuously missing is the representation layer for the three classical models: the paper states that natural language processing techniques were combined with the models but never says how text became numbers - no tokenisation, no bag of words, no TF-IDF, no n-gram range, no embedding - so it is not possible to say what the decision tree, XGBoost and k-nearest neighbours were actually fitted to, which makes their comparison against BERT uninterpretable as a claim about model families.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: An ordinary consumer iPad with its front-facing camera at 30 frames per second, running a purpose-built application - no research-grade sensor, no eye tracker, no wearable, no additional hardware. That choice is the point: the entire measurement chain is a device already present in most homes and clinics, which is what makes the scalability claim credible rather than aspirational. Analysis components are all published and cited: a face detection algorithm, a low-dimensional facial embedding used to identify and track the child's face specifically among those of caregiver, siblings and clinical staff, a 49-point landmark detector, and the group's own pose-invariant affect estimator, itself previously validated against human frame-by-frame coding of 136,450 frames with an intraclass correlation of 0.9. Statistical work used Python with pingouin (Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon, ANCOVA), scipy (Spearman) and scikit-learn (logistic regression), each named at function level. The one component with a stated weakness is the perception layer: the landmark and affect algorithms were trained primarily on adults, which the authors list as a limitation while noting their prior validation in toddlers.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: A Tobii Pro Fusion eye tracker sampling at 120 Hz, with participants seated approximately 65 cm from a 1920 x 1080 display. Fixation and saccade classification used Tobii Pro Lab version 1.145 with its attention filter and the I-VT velocity-threshold algorithm, with the threshold stated explicitly at 100 degrees per second - a level of specificity about event detection that most eye-tracking papers in this corpus omit entirely, and one that matters because fixation counts are meaningless without it. Areas of interest were drawn on the eyes (extending up to the eyebrows), nose and mouth, and were redrawn for each image because mouth size varies with expression, which prevents a systematic bias in mouth-region measurement across emotions. Scan-path length was computed in Python with an algorithm published as pseudocode that segments rather than bridges invalid samples. Modelling used PyTorch with fully tabulated architectures. Clinical instruments: ADOS-2, PANSS, SRS-2, Kikuchi's Scale of Social Skills 18-item, ADHD-RS and CBCL. No calibration procedure is described.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: FreeSpeech, an iPad speech-generating AAC application commercially available on the Apple iTunes store from January 2012 to May 2014, with a customisable programmable interface supporting user-modifiable icon arrangement, sentence generation and mapping to synthesised or recorded voices. The app logged all key presses, their timings and other on-screen events and transmitted them automatically to a secure backend on internet connection. No research instrument, sensor or assessment tool was used at any point - the entire measurement apparatus is a consumer application's debug logging. Analysis software, frameworks, library versions and compute are not named anywhere, and neither are the architectures or training settings of the stacked autoencoders and deep belief networks that produce the headline result. The asymmetry is notable: the data-collection platform is described in useful detail while the modelling that generates the paper's claim is described only by algorithm name.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Deliberately minimal. A single Sony DSC-RX100 IV consumer digital camera recording 1920 x 1080 at 30 frames per second from a fixed front-facing viewpoint, a height-adjustable chair and a table in a quiet room. No eye tracker, no depth sensor, no wearable, no markers, no calibration. This is a direct response to the authors' own criticism of prior work for requiring 'specialized and expensive equipment, calibration, trained personnel', and it is what makes the scalability argument credible. Clinical instruments are all named in their Korean validated versions with citations: K-CARS-2, K-ADOS-2, Korean Bayley-II and K-WPPSI-IV. Analysis software is specified to the version number - Python 3.6.8, SciPy 1.4.1, Statsmodels 0.11.1, scikit-learn 0.23.2, Seaborn 0.11.0, Matplotlib 3.3.1 - which is rare in this corpus and is good practice. What the main text does not provide is the network's layer configuration, training hyperparameters or augmentation, though an architecture diagram and training/validation performance appear in supplementary material.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: Google Colab and TensorFlow; InceptionV3 pretrained on ImageNet. That is the entirety of the apparatus, because no data were collected. The eye tracker, display, stimuli and recording software that produced the underlying gaze data are not named, so a reader cannot evaluate the measurement chain at all - a striking situation for a study whose stated contribution is to use eye tracking as a biomarker. The description of InceptionV3's architectural innovations (factorised convolutions, asymmetric factorisation, auxiliary classifiers, efficient grid size reduction) is detailed and accurate but is standard exposition rather than anything specific to this application.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: An entirely software-based pipeline, well specified for its scale. CLAN, the standard CHILDES analysis toolkit, supplied the morphosyntactic baseline features. L2SCA, an established second-language syntactic complexity analyser, supplied the 23 syntactic complexity measures. BERT embeddings with cosine similarity supplied the two discourse-coherence measures. TF-IDF vectors supplied the unexpected-word count. An AutoML tool was used to compare classifier families, and SHAP for attribution and for feature elimination. Using off-the-shelf, community-standard tools throughout is appropriate and makes the pipeline reconstructible in outline, though the specific BERT variant is not named and no code is released. Notably absent, given publication at ICASSP and repeated reference to 'speech signals' and 'speech features', is any acoustic analysis: the study operates entirely on transcripts, and the prosodic properties the introduction cites from prior work - increased pitch range and variability in autistic children - are not measured.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: Not reported. The paper describes no eye tracker, sampling rate, display, viewing distance, calibration procedure or recording software - a striking gap in a study whose entire input is eye-tracking data and which computes gaze velocity, a quantity whose meaning depends directly on sampling rate. What is specified is the downstream rendering: scan-paths are drawn on a black background at 1680 x 1050, resized to 100 x 100 and converted to greyscale, with velocity encoded as colour in the final experiments through a stated threshold mapping. Modelling used DNN and CNN architectures shown only as a figure.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: Acquisition equipment is inherited and specified: SMI Experiment Center Software with a Red-m remote eye tracker sampling at 250 Hz, producing images at 640 x 480. That is a high sampling rate and a named commercial system, which is more than several primary studies in this corpus provide about their own equipment. The analysis stack is given in full: Python 3.6.8 with Keras on TensorFlow, OpenCV, scikit-learn and Matplotlib, running on an Intel Core i7 tenth-generation machine with 16 GB RAM and an NVIDIA GeForce MX230. No calibration procedure, tracking-quality criterion or rendering specification is available.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: None in the instrumental sense - the study uses no sensor, device or measurement apparatus of its own. Data were extracted and anonymised by the TIMNA project, the Israel Ministry of Health's Big Data Platform, and accessed by researchers through a dedicated secured Ministry platform, with a public URL given for the access route. Analysis used gradient boosting with logistic regression, random forest and naive Bayes comparators and SHAP for attribution; no software package or version is named, which is the one specification gap in an otherwise thoroughly reported methods section. The absence of equipment is the point: the entire input is data that a nurse enters during an ordinary visit, which is why this is the only study in the review whose measurement cost at deployment is zero.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: Software only: Google Colab with TensorFlow and Keras, three ImageNet-pretrained networks for classification, YOLOv8 variants for expression recognition. No acquisition equipment exists because no data were collected. The imaging characteristics of the source photographs - resolution, sensor, compression, colour profile - are unknown and unexamined, which is precisely the information needed to assess whether the classes are separable on grounds unrelated to the children.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: MRI scanners at 17 sites, with the heterogeneity that implies, and the Harvard-Oxford atlas for parcellation. The equipment requirement is the highest in the review by a wide margin: structural MRI needs a scanner, a radiographer, and in young autistic children frequently sedation or extensive desensitisation, which is precisely the barrier that the behavioural approaches charted elsewhere exist to avoid. The paper's motivating argument - that ADOS and ADI-R are 'largely impossible in low-resource environments' - sits awkwardly with a proposed alternative requiring an MRI scanner and the same two instruments as input.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: A single fixed Samsung HMX-F90 camcorder sampling at 25 Hz, positioned to the side with both participants framed equally. Raven's Advanced Progressive Matrices for cognitive assessment. The analytical apparatus is the substance: motion energy analysis converts video to movement time series by counting pixel changes between consecutive frames within manually drawn regions of interest, and the authors justify its validity from the acquisition conditions - because the camera is fixed and the lighting stable, 'the sole factor that could lead to pixel changes between image frames was the human movement' - and cite evidence that motion energy analysis achieves reliability comparable to motion tracking and computer vision. Cross wavelet analysis then computes coherence between the two series across 23 time scales. No software package or version is named for either step, which is the one specification gap. The equipment minimalism is the point: nothing beyond a consumer camcorder is required, and no calibration, marker placement or sensor attachment is involved.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: No instrumentation - the data are transcribed ADOS-2 sessions. The apparatus is analytical and is specified adequately: logistic regression on normalised tag frequencies; Bi-LSTM models with 300-dimensional word and hidden vectors trained with Adam at learning rate 0.001, batch size 32, for 50 epochs; and a separate Bi-LSTM sequence labeller for automatic annotation. The most consequential methodological statement concerns what was not done: the hyperparameters 'were adopted from commonly used values and not explored, as preliminary experiments determined that the impact of the search for hyperparameters' was limited. Declining to search hyperparameters on a 135-participant dataset removes a source of optimism that most studies in this corpus exploit heavily, and doing so deliberately and saying so is exceptional. No software package or version is named, which is the one specification gap.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: None. Pretrained VGG16, ResNet and Inception networks used as fixed feature extractors with fully connected layers excluded, and five classical classifiers. No hardware, software package, version or hyperparameter is reported. The imaging characteristics of the source photographs - the properties that differ between the two source collections and that HOG, LBP, PHASH and SIFT are designed to capture - are neither reported nor examined.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment. Preprocessing is described in reasonable detail - grayscale conversion, resizing to 120x110 for a Gabor filter stage and 100x100 for the convolutional network, intensity normalisation, histogram equalisation, face detection with realignment, and landmark or local binary pattern feature extraction. The two-resolution arrangement for the two processing stages is a specific and reproducible detail.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: A 12.3-inch Dell Latitude tablet running purpose-built software written in Unity 2D and C#, logging finger x and y coordinates at 20 Hz with asynchronous programming used for storage so that recording did not degrade game performance. No sensor, marker, camera or wearable is involved. The 20 Hz sampling rate is modest - one sample every 50 ms - and bounds what can be said about rapid acceleration changes, though it is adequate for the trajectory-shape features the study models. No analysis software or framework is named, and the neural network architectures are not specified in the retrieved text, which is the one substantive gap in an otherwise well-documented apparatus.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: Not reported. No camera, facial expression recognition software, heart rate monitor, thermometer or any other instrument is named, and no computational environment or framework is specified. The optimisation algorithm and network are described mathematically but nothing is said about their implementation.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None. The data were collected through mobile and web screening applications by third parties, and the analysis is tabular. The equipment argument is the whole basis of the deployment claim - a screening questionnaire needs nothing but a phone - and it is genuinely the lowest barrier of any approach in this review. What the low barrier delivers here is the ability to re-administer an existing instrument through a neural network.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Deliberately modest and fully specified. A 48 cm square LL pressure sensor from NEWCOM Inc. captured plantar pressure distribution; a Logitech c615n webcam at 640 x 480 and 30 fps, placed in front of the child, captured full-body images; the two streams were acquired synchronously at 20 Hz, and the physical configuration of participant, experimenter, camera and sensor is documented in a figure. Joint angles at ten body points were estimated from the video using OpenPose. Statistical analysis used SPSS 27.0. The equipment choice matters for the translational claim: a consumer webcam plus a single pressure mat, with open-source pose estimation, is deployable in a preschool examination room, which is the setting the paper targets. What is not reported is any calibration, signal-quality criterion or handling of pose-estimation failure - relevant because OpenPose accuracy on 640 x 480 video of a five-year-old at unspecified distance is not guaranteed and the study's proposed features depend entirely on the joint angles it produces.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment exists. Computation used an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU on Google Colab under Python 3.8 with 12 GB RAM and 16 GB GPU memory, batch sizes between 32 and 128. MTCNN performed face detection on the video frames, followed by alignment, cropping and resizing; pixel values were normalised to [0, 1]. A pretrained ResNet-50 supplied the feature space for the leakage analysis. Because the images come from unknown consumer cameras and phones under unknown conditions, every acquisition variable that a purpose-built study would control - focal length, sensor, resolution, illumination, distance, compression - varies freely and, critically, may vary systematically with class, since the two classes were harvested from different kinds of online source.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: The most completely specified acquisition chain in the review. A g.tec EEG cap with 16 Ag/AgCl electrodes, a g.tec GAMMAbox and g.tec USBamp, driven by BCI2000; electrodes at FP1, FP2, F7, F3, Fz, F4, F8, T3, C4, Cz, C3, T5, Pz, O1, Oz and O2 under the international 10-20 system; AFz as ground and the right earlobe as reference; bandpass 0.1-60 Hz with a 60 Hz notch; digitised at 256 Hz. Montage, ground, reference, filter settings and sampling rate are all given, which is more acquisition detail than most behavioural studies in this review report for their own instruments and is exactly what would be needed to replicate the recording. The corresponding practical point is that this apparatus - a research EEG amplifier, a gel cap, a trained operator and a cooperative child who will sit still - is at the opposite end of the deployment spectrum from the webcam-and-toys protocols charted elsewhere, and the review's synthesis should note that the electrophysiological branch shares the behavioural branch's motivation while requiring the equipment that motivation exists to avoid.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: Minimal and deliberately so: a video camera in a playroom and a fixed set of physical toys. No sensor, screen, wearable or eye tracker is involved. That is the design's practical argument - the equipment barrier to using this protocol in a clinic or kindergarten anywhere is a camera and a box of toys, which is lower than for any other included study except the population health-records analysis. The cost is transferred to the analysis: 10-15 minutes of trained-coder time per 90-second video, which is where the scalability constraint now sits, and which is why the authors describe the coding scheme as 'a feeding database with low granularity for automatic behavior recognition through machine learning in the future'. Neither the coding software nor the statistical software is named.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: None. The instrument, a trained administrator and a scoring sheet are the entire apparatus; analysis used SPSS 29.0. The absence of equipment is worth stating explicitly in a review otherwise populated by eye trackers, pressure sensors, motion capture, webcams and wearables, because it inverts the usual cost structure. Nothing needs to be bought, calibrated or maintained, and nothing can fail to acquire - but the assessment consumes 40 to 60 minutes of a psychiatrist who holds research certification in the instrument, plus scoring time. Every automated approach in this corpus is, in effect, an attempt to move cost from that clinician to a device. This study measures what the clinician-borne version delivers on a question the automated work has not attempted.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: None reported, which is itself a finding. For a speech study, no microphone, sampling rate, channel configuration, recording environment specification or preprocessing chain is given for either corpus. Sample durations are not stated; the reported totals imply mean sample lengths of roughly 1.3 seconds in De-Enigma and 2.2 seconds in CPSD, which are short for prosodic analysis. Computation used two pre-trained model families - a discriminative fine-tuning architecture and Wav2Vec 2.0 with quantisation removed feeding a BLSTM classifier - but no hardware, framework or hyperparameter detail is provided. The absence of acoustic condition reporting is directly connected to the study's principal vulnerability: with the two classes recorded in different physical settings, the properties of the recording chain are exactly what a reader would need to judge whether the signal is speech or room.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: No instrumentation. snscrape for collection, better-profanity for masking swear words, VADER for lexicon-based sentiment, word2vec and TF-IDF for representation, and an attention-based bidirectional LSTM for user-level classification. The equipment cost of this study is zero and its collection cost is a scraping script - which is precisely why the ethical analysis matters more here than anywhere else in this review. Every other included study is bounded by what a research team can afford to collect from consenting participants; this one is bounded only by what a platform will serve, and the authors' response is to build the model, measure it, describe what it would enable, and destroy it.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: Standard ADOS session recording equipment, unspecified and heterogeneous across the eleven-year window - which the authors handle by normalising audio to a 2-channel 44 kHz 192 kbps format explicitly 'to homogenize the audio format from different microphones', matched to the parameters of the Urban8K benchmark corpus. Analysis used OpenPose for pose estimation, ImageNet-pretrained VGG16 for video features and Librosa for acoustic features. The equipment story matters for the translational claim: nothing here is specialised. No eye tracker, no motion capture, no wearable, no force plate - a camera and a microphone in a room where an assessment was happening anyway. That places the study alongside the one-legged-standing and free-play studies charted here as instrumentation that a clinic could actually deploy, and unlike them it captures 46 minutes of dense social interaction rather than 90 seconds. The bottleneck it does not remove is the ADOS examiner.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment; the videos were 'shot using various devices in unrestricted natural settings' by families. Analysis used a Haar cascade for frame selection and face cropping, and three architectures whose configurations are reported in useful detail - a Perceiver with the LAMB optimiser at learning rate 0.001 updated every three epochs, weight decay 0.0001, dropout 0.0001, eight transformer blocks of twelve heads with four cross-attention repetitions, patch size 4 and a 256x256 latent array; a CNN-WGAN trained with Wasserstein loss; and an ImageNet-pretrained Inception v3 taken from the Keras applications with top layers excluded. Continuous annotation used dedicated rating software accepting mouse, keyboard or joystick input. The heterogeneity of the source recording devices is acknowledged as a limitation - 'the unconstrained environment and conditions of acquisition and the bad images and videos quality' - but no normalisation, resolution criterion or channel compensation is described that would address it.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: A FLIR USB thermal imaging camera calibrated at an emissivity of 0.98, with analysis in MATLAB 2023a on a Dual-Core E5700. Reporting the emissivity value is good practice and is more acquisition detail than most studies in this review provide. The choice of modality is also well argued on grounds that matter for this corpus: thermal imaging needs no external illumination, is unaffected by lighting conditions, and - the point worth carrying into the synthesis - is 'not affected by ... skin tone', which is a sensor-level answer to the demographic fragility that this review has documented repeatedly in visible-spectrum facial analysis. What is missing is everything needed to interpret an absolute temperature reading: camera model, spatial resolution, noise-equivalent temperature difference, distance to subject, and ambient temperature and humidity at each capture. For a study whose primary feature is skin temperature and whose images span outdoor and indoor settings, the absence of ambient logging is not a minor reporting gap but a limit on what the measurement means.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment. Analysis used three ImageNet-pretrained networks on 224x224x3 images with categorical cross-entropy, the SGD optimiser and a 25-epoch cap. Because the images come from unknown cameras under unknown conditions, every acquisition variable is free to vary and, critically, may vary systematically with class given that the two folders were assembled by different routes.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: No instrumentation. Stanford's Stanza NLP package parsed sentences and tokens; scikit-learn supplied five classical models and the multilayer perceptron; Keras supplied the convolutional network. The computational cost is trivial and the input is text that already exists in a public archive, so this is among the least resource-intensive designs in the review - which is also its limitation, since it inherits whatever the original recordings and transcriptions captured and can add nothing.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Microsoft Kinect v2 for the Gait Fullbody Dataset, giving 25 three-dimensional joint coordinates, and Kinect v1 for DREAM, giving 20 joints of which 10 upper-body positions are recorded. The paper explains the difference and its consequence for comparability, with a figure contrasting the two joint layouts. Kinect-class depth sensing is consumer hardware, which matters for the deployment argument: skeleton capture requires no markers, no wearables, no calibration by the family and no clinical instrumentation, and produces data that cannot identify the child by appearance. Analysis used Python 3.10 with nine named packages at stated versions on an RTX 3090 with 48 GB RAM, trained with SGD at learning rate 0.001 and batch size 12 - a fuller software and hardware specification than almost any other study in this review provides.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Sony UX560 and UX512F voice recorders for 74.2% of recordings and smartphones running a custom recording application for the remaining 25.80%, all captured in WAV at 16-bit and 44.1 kHz specifically 'to ensure consistency across devices', with parents and trained voice collectors instructed to record in quiet environments at approximately 25 cm from the child's mouth. Praat performed acoustic analysis. The equipment story is the strongest part of the translational argument: a smartphone recording of a cry costs nothing, requires no clinic visit, no specialist operator, no cooperation from the child and no language ability, and can be repeated indefinitely at home - which is why the authors propose 'continuous remote monitoring'. Two device classes with different microphones nonetheless introduce acoustic variation that no level normalisation or channel compensation is reported to address, and the device mix by group is not stated.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: None. Data collection was by a screening application operated by third parties, and the analysis is tabular.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: A single webcam recording at 1920x1080 and 30 frames per second under standardised lighting, with MediaPipe face mesh, pose and hands performing landmark extraction. The equipment requirement is the lowest of any instrumented study in this review apart from the free-play video work: one consumer camera and open-source software, with no eye tracker, depth sensor, force plate, wearable or thermal camera. That makes the proposed application in 'clinical and educational contexts' credible as an equipment matter, and it means the 1,639-parameter feature vector is obtainable anywhere a laptop and a room are available. What is missing is the acquisition detail that determines whether landmark coordinates are comparable across sessions: camera distance and angle, the child's seated or standing position, and any per-session calibration. No landmark-detection failure rate is reported, which matters because MediaPipe hand tracking fails intermittently when hands leave frame or overlap, and class-correlated missingness would be indistinguishable from a class-correlated behavioural difference.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment. Analysis used an Intel Core i7-11800H with 16 GB RAM under Windows 10, with Python 3.9.7, scikit-learn 0.24.2, TensorFlow 2.9.2 and DeepFace 0.0.93, plus PyTorch for the multilayer perceptron and CUDA for acceleration. Versioning every library is good practice and makes the computational pipeline reproducible. The consequential detail is the choice of DeepFace as the feature extractor: it is a face-recognition and emotion-classification library trained on adult neurotypical face corpora for identity verification and basic-emotion classification, and it is applied here without fine-tuning to children's faces for a diagnostic task. A study charted elsewhere in this review showed directly that an affect model trained on neurotypical faces performs poorly on autistic children and improves markedly when fine-tuned on autistic data; that finding applies to the emotion half of the pipeline here and is not cited or addressed.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment. Analysis ran in Jupyter Notebook on TensorFlow 2.10.0 with an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 Ti Max-Q - a laptop GPU. Reporting the hardware is a small but genuine transparency, and it substantiates the accessibility argument the conclusion makes: this pipeline requires a consumer laptop and a public dataset, which is why the branch is so heavily populated.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment. Training ran on CPU-based hardware, which the authors identify as a limitation that 'limited more profound tuning and real-time optimization' - an honest disclosure, and one that also indicates how low the computational barrier to this branch is.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: No acquisition equipment is described. The architectural argument is explicitly about deployment hardware: MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0 were chosen 'because they are fast and have small models', using depthwise separable convolutions and compound scaling so that inference is quick enough for 'devices with limited processing power, like mobile phones or edge devices used in clinical settings'. That is a coherent design rationale for a low-resource context and connects the architecture choice to the stated Indonesian setting, where the paper notes national statistics are scarce.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: SMI RED mobile eye tracker at 60 Hz with a 17-inch stimulus display, participant at ~60 cm. Compute: 7th-generation Intel Core i7, 8 GB RAM, 16 GB GPU. Software is described only as a suitable computational framework for neural network training - no library, no version, no seed. Calibration procedure, data-quality thresholds and drift handling are not described, which matters because Tracking_Ratio (a data-quality index) is one of the retained features.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: No instrumentation - Google Forms for capture, CSV export. Modelling used the TPOT library (10 generations, population 100, remaining parameters default) with scikit-learn estimators. No versions, no hardware, no seed. The full best-pipeline parameter set is given in Table 4, which is more than most papers in this corpus supply.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: OpenCV and Dlib for landmark detection, Python for the pipeline, XGBoost for classification; Windows 10, 8 GB RAM, Intel i3, no GPU. Training settings: Adam, learning rate 0.001 chosen by grid search over [0.0001, 0.01], batch size 32, 500 epochs, 224x224 input, rotation and scaling augmentation. No versions, no seed, no runtime.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: SMI RED250 portable eye tracker at 250 Hz, 1024x768 display, stated spatial resolution 0.05, five-point calibration, with calibration drift correction applied in preprocessing. Fixation/saccade segmentation by dispersion-threshold and velocity-threshold algorithms. Classification implemented in MATLAB on Windows 10 with an Intel Core i5 and 4 GB RAM; frame segmentation in Python. The hardware is implausibly modest for the described deep models and no training time is given.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: None for acquisition. Processing components named: Gabor filter bank, MTCNN face detection, median filter, Z-score colour normalisation, bicubic interpolation, MobileNetV2, LSTM, DBN built from restricted Boltzmann machines, hybrid-kernel ELM, Crested Porcupine Optimizer. No software, versions, seed, hardware or runtime environment is given, and the target image resolution is left as the literal placeholder (X, Y pixels).

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation is named, because the data were downloaded and the source acquisition is not summarised. Computational components: a shallow DNN with dense layers, ReLU and dropout (Local Model 1), a five-hidden-layer DNN described as multi-class although the task is binary (Local Model 2), FedAvg aggregation, XGBoost with SHAP for feature ranking, MinMaxScaler. No library, version, seed, hardware or runtime.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: Canon EOS M-100 on a tripod, 256 GB storage, ISO 800, f/5.6, 1/25 s, 6000x4000 capture cropped to 1:1 and resized to 224x224. Room instrumentation includes a 17-inch LCD screen and speakers, listed for video viewing although no video task is described. Analysis software is not named; only the Keras ImageDataGenerator augmentation block is printed. Several environmental parameters conflict between the narrative and Table I: lighting 30 W versus 22 W, humidity 40-45% versus 50-60%, acclimation 10-15 minutes versus 3 minutes.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: None for acquisition. Analytical components: label encoding, MinMaxScaler, SVM-SMOTE, chi-square selection, six scikit-learn-family classifiers, Bayesian optimisation and SHAP. No library, version, seed, hardware or runtime is reported.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: No instrumentation. Python with scikit-learn for modelling; numpy is named specifically as the library used to create the Phase II teaching-method column. No versions, seed, hardware or runtime.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: No instrumentation. Analytical components: StandardScaler, one-hot and label encoding, SelectKBest with chi-squared, RF and Extra Trees importance, Pearson and Spearman correlation, variance inflation factor, Kruskal-Wallis tests, logistic regression, KNN, a feed-forward ANN and an LR-KNN ensemble. No library names, versions, seed or hardware.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: REDCap for capture, with validated data entry, audit trails for tracking data manipulation and export, and automated export procedures. Modelling used fifty regressors implemented in Python, R, Matlab and Octave, with the package and hyperparameter tuning grid for each listed in a supplementary appendix.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation. Modelling used PyTorch with a torchvision pre-trained ResNet and a ViT-base transformer, AdamW at learning rate 1e-5 with weight decay 1e-2, cross-entropy loss and CUDA. No versions, seed, epoch count, batch size or hardware.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
