answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation. Implementation in MATLAB R2021a. No toolbox versions, hardware, runtime, seed or code. The proposed pipeline's components - DeepDeblur, DOCNN and the Fire Hawk Optimizer - are described by loss functions and a notation table rather than by any reproducible configuration.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: No instrumentation. R with caret 6.0.94, iml for SHAP and permutation importance, lime for LIME, glmnet and class for two of the models. The paper devotes an entire subsection to arguing that R is accessible to non-expert clinicians and offers practical guidelines for its use - a genuine attempt at translation - and then does not release the script that would make those guidelines operational.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Tobii X2-30 remote eye tracker at 30 Hz on a 15-inch laptop screen with Tobii Studio and nine-point calibration using an animated target. The stated spatial accuracy of 36 degrees is a typographic error for 0.36 degrees - as printed the figure would exceed the visual angle of the entire display. The modelling software is not named, and no hyperparameters, tuning procedure or seed is reported for any algorithm, which is the main reporting gap in an otherwise well-specified study.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation described. Modelling used ImageNet-pretrained MobileNet, VGG19 and DenseNet169 backbones with custom heads, Keras ImageDataGenerator for augmentation, RMSprop or Adam at learning rate 0.0001, batch sizes 16 (training) and 32 (validation), and 100 epochs. Parameter tables per model are provided and are more complete than most in this corpus.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation. Implementation in Python with no library, version, seed or hardware. Method components: Yeo-Johnson transformation, the Elk Herd Optimizer with double exponential smoothing, the Moments Embedding Network and ResNeXt.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Samsung Galaxy Tab A7 with a 10.4-inch 2000x1200 touchscreen and stylus; tasks programmed in PsychoPy and delivered via Pavlovia (PsychoJS 2021.1.4); MaRs-IB on Gorilla. Analysis in R Studio 2022.07.2 (matching), MATLAB 2022a with fitlme (mixed models) and JASP 0.17.2.1 (Bayesian analyses and classification). Every package is named with a version.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: No instrumentation. Analytical components: BiLSTM, a chaotic optimiser (expanded inconsistently as Chaotic Grey Ball Optimizer in the abstract and Chaotic Gradient-Based Optimizer in the methods), SHAP, and standard preprocessing. No software, version, seed or hardware is named in the extracted text.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation. Model components: ResNet-50 (50 layers) or InceptionV3 (48 layers) at 224x224 input, Adam at learning rate 0.003 (described as increasing), batch size 64, 150 epochs, binary cross-entropy; unlearning and retraining times of 3.2 s and 5.6 s per partition; an inter-modality correlation threshold of 0.65. A testbed with 32 GB RAM and 2 TB storage is named.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: No controlled acquisition equipment - the recordings are consumer video of unknown origin. Python OpenCV was used for frame extraction. Region-of-interest detection and cropping were applied to remove background objects, which is the appropriate response to uncontrolled framing. No deep learning framework, version, seed or hardware is named.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Screen-based eye tracking with predefined AOIs over eyes, nose and mouth; the device model is not named, which is the study's one notable acquisition-reporting gap. Analysis used Scikit-learn, XGBoost and PyTorch on an Intel i7 desktop with 16 GB RAM and no GPU, a configuration the authors highlight deliberately as evidence that the pipeline is deployable without specialised hardware.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: For Dataset 2, vision-based pose estimation and wearable sensors are named without models; ResNet50, VGG16 and MobileNetV2 supply image features at 224x224 with ImageNet normalisation; audio features include MFCC, spectral, temporal, rhythmic and voice-quality measures such as jitter, shimmer and harmonics-to-noise ratio. No software, version, seed or compute environment is given anywhere.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Participants' own devices, with tasks programmed and delivered online through Neurotask. Analysis in Python with scikit-learn's RandomForest and GridSearchCV, with the script deposited on OSF.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation is described. Modelling components: decision tree, random forest, KNN (k=3), AdaBoost, gradient boosting and a stacking meta-learner. No software, version, seed or hardware.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation. Roboflow supplied preprocessing (640x640 resize, RGB conversion, normalisation) and augmentation (horizontal flipping and transformations for illumination, expression and pose variation) at export; training used the Ultralytics YOLO framework for 50 epochs. No learning rate, batch size, optimiser, seed or hardware.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: No acquisition instrumentation. Compute fully specified (Python 3.6.5, i5-8600K, 16 GB RAM, GTX 1050 Ti 4 GB, 250 GB SSD, 1 TB HDD). Training settings: ReLU, learning rate 0.01, dropout 0.5, 50 epochs, batch size 5 - though the accuracy and loss curves are described over 25 epochs, which does not match.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Microsoft Kinect V2 capturing 25 joints in three dimensions in real time for the typical and moderate groups; a Samsung Note 9 phone camera for the nine severe-ASD children. The analysis software, versions and seed are not reported.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: None for acquisition; transcripts retrieved through TalkBank APIs. Modelling used logistic regression, random forest and TabNet with grid-searched hyperparameters; no software, version or seed is named.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: A tablet running the study's own serious-game application. Modelling used seven standard algorithms with grid-searched hyperparameters; no software, version, seed or compute environment is named.

questions.question_text: How reproducible is the study (data sharing, code, parameters, seeds)?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: No dataset access statement; the Infant Sibling Database is a restricted clinical cohort. No code availability, no seeds, no hyperparameter table; feature set and classifier settings are described narratively only. Not reproducible as reported.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release; the SVM pipeline is cited to prior work (Salvatore et al. 2013) and the feature set and validation scheme are described in enough detail to re-implement in principle, but no hyperparameters beyond 'linear kernel', no seeds and no released data. Not reproducible as reported.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: No data availability statement, no code release, no hyperparameters (beyond ReliefF k=10), no seeds, and - critically - no statement of the validation scheme. The Cohn-Kanade stimulus set is public, but the collected participant data are not. Not reproducible as reported.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: No data availability statement, no code release, no seeds. The pipeline (K-means quantisation, histogram normalisation, RBF-SVM, LOO with participant-level score averaging, threshold selection) is described in enough detail to re-implement in principle, and K values and the optimal threshold (0.3255) are reported - better than most contemporaries - but the underlying dataset is not accessible. Not reproducible in practice.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release; several methodological details (the NLP pipeline, the connectivity normalisation) are deferred to Supporting Information rather than the main text. LSI, the three classifiers and the 10-fold scheme are named but hyperparameters, seeds and the fold-level treatment of LSI are not specified. Not reproducible as reported, although the elicitation protocol itself is trivially repeatable.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release - unsurprising given the commercial affiliation and stated commercialisation ambition. Reproducibility support is nonetheless comparatively good: the full 262-feature list is provided in a supplemental table, algorithm hyperparameters are given (RGF 500 trees, L2=sL2=1.0, square loss; ET and RF 5000 trees), the correlation-based feature reduction threshold (r>0.9) is stated, the cross-validation scheme is fully specified, and classification thresholds (0.50 and 0.55) are reported explicitly rather than optimised silently. The games are commercially available. Method-reproducible, data-irreproducible.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: The best reproducibility profile in the corpus so far. The dataset is released as Supporting Information (S1_File.xlsx) under CC-BY with an explicit data availability statement and an invitation to other researchers; the full 20-parameter definition table is published; the sampling rate, filter, segmentation threshold and trial structure are specified; the SVM library and grid-search procedure are named; and the entire pipeline is benchmarked in Weka, a public tool, against nine named standard evaluators. No code is released and random seeds are not reported, but the analysis is reconstructible from the released data.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: Weak. The KOMAA dataset is announced as a contribution but no access conditions, licence, repository or contact route is stated - so a dataset presented as a community resource is in practice unavailable. No code release. Feature construction is described in good detail (histogram bin counts, AU list, angle ranges, smoothing window, normalisation) and would be re-implementable, but SVM hyperparameters, the feature-selection stopping criterion and the final feature-vector dimensionality are not given, and nothing states whether feature selection was nested in the cross-validation. Not reproducible as reported.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release, but reproducibility of the method is comparatively strong: the feature set is a published open standard (eGeMAPS) extracted with an open-source tool (openSMILE), both classifiers use widely available toolkits (Weka, TensorFlow), the SVM complexity grid is stated, the BLSTM architecture search outcome (one layer, eight cells), time step (10 ms), optimiser and early-stopping rule are given, the exact cross-validation partitions are published per subject in Table 1, and the optimised per-fold decision thresholds are listed. This is among the most re-implementable pipelines in the corpus; only the cohort recordings are unavailable.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Mixed. Strong on the modelling side: the feature sets are published open standards extracted with an open-source toolkit chosen for reproducibility, full network architectures are specified (layer counts, hidden units, activations, normalisation, objective, optimiser, batch size), the SVM complexity parameter is stated to be tuned on validation, and partition sizes are given. Weak on the data side: CPESD access conditions are never stated, the elicitation protocol and recording setup are absent, no code is released, no random seeds are reported, and the exact child-to-partition assignment is not published, so the child-independent split cannot be reproduced.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: No data availability statement, no code release and no random seeds. Method reporting is otherwise good: the full 20-feature definition table, the complete SWDA p-value distribution for every feature, the SWDA entry and removal criteria, the sampling rate and filter settings, the SVM kernel types with their C and gamma grids, the polynomial degree range, and the ANN architecture and training function are all specified. The pipeline is re-implementable in principle but the analysis cannot be reproduced without the data.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Poor. No data availability statement, no code, no software versions, no hyperparameters (the Gaussian SVM kernel width and the KNN k are never given), no random seeds, and no specification of how the 4x4 grid maps onto physical space. Table 1, which holds the per-group presence ratios, is not recoverable as values. The method is describable in principle - grid occupancy, cosine similarity, standard classifiers - but no quantitative result other than the accuracies and p-values can be extracted from the paper.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release. Method reporting is nonetheless strong: eye-tracker model, sampling rate, spatial resolution, screen resolution, viewing distance, calibration procedure, stimulus content and duration, the full AOI definitions and the ratio definitions are all specified, as are the cross-validation folds and the permutation counts. The analysis is re-implementable in principle on comparable data; the specific SVM kernel and regularisation settings are not given.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release. Method reporting is otherwise strong: all toolkits are named and are standard (COVAREP, LIWC, Google Cloud Speech-to-Text), feature dimensions are tabulated per source and per type totalling 1330, the missing-data encoding (-1 padding rather than interpolation) is stated, normalisation is described, the grid-search ranges for epochs and learning rate are given, and the complete reading and picture stimulus materials are reproduced in an appendix. The pipeline is re-implementable; the corpus is not accessible.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: The best in the corpus. An explicit 'Open Data' section states that the eye-tracking data, code, and materials are available at a named GitHub repository, and the abstract states the gaze data, R code, visual stimuli and task descriptions are 'made freely available for replication purposes'. Full replicability is listed as one of the paper's three stated contributions. Beyond the release, the paper publishes the complete search question set, the AOI definition methods, the eye tracker specifications, viewing distance, calibration procedure, cross-validation scheme, and confidence intervals for every configuration, and directs readers to the repository for results of page combinations not shown in the paper.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Mixed but above corpus average. The dataset is publicly released at a stated URL - the only video dataset released in this corpus - and the experimental protocol is specified in exhaustive physical detail (table dimensions, object weights and positions, start posture, trial counts, block structure, camera settings, trimming rule). The model architecture is described concretely (GoogLeNet last conv layer, 7x7x1024 features, 7x7 attention map, 128-dim LSTM hidden state, 16-dim FC layer, 15-frame clips). What is missing: no code release, no training hyperparameters (learning rate, optimiser, epochs, regularisation), no random seeds, and no statement of how the model handles the 15-frame clip splitting at test time beyond averaging.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: The strongest reproducibility profile in the corpus alongside Yaneva et al. Data and code are both released as supplementary information. The method is documented exhaustively: eye tracker specifications, calibration and validation procedure, fixation detection thresholds, the 68+8 AOI construction and why the extra 8 frame points were added, the 50 ms character-repetition encoding, the substitution matrix construction with its distance and group logic and its [-1,+1] rescaling, the length normalisation rationale, the t-SNE implementation used, the LightGBM hyperparameters, the class priors, and the subject-level fold constraint. The authors also report that manipulating t-SNE settings and LightGBM defaults produced no qualitative change - an informal robustness check.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: The dataset availability is stated explicitly and negatively - 'The dataset is not made publicly available' - which is at least transparent, and rarer in this corpus than silence. No code release. Method reporting is otherwise strong: apparatus, movement-zone geometry, trial structure and durations, interpolation and filter settings, noise thresholds for each kinematic quantity, the 101-bin histogram construction, the Shannon entropy and range equations, the two-stage feature-selection procedure with its p<0.1 threshold, the five classifiers with the k values tested, and the software versions. Re-implementable in principle; not reproducible without the data.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release, which is a real gap for a corpus this valuable. Method reporting is otherwise strong: the openSMILE configuration and window/step sizes, the full list of 44 low-level descriptors, the exact feature arithmetic (44 x 2 speakers x 4 functionals = 352), the six text-feature groups totalling 272, the voiceless-frame exclusion rule, the pitch normalisation formula with the 5th-percentile baseline, the correlation threshold (p<0.025), the number of components retained (10), the classifier, the libraries, and the annotation training and reliability criteria are all specified. The pipeline is re-implementable; the conversations are not accessible.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release. Method reporting is otherwise detailed: eye tracker models and sampling rates, calibration procedure and error tolerance, display specifications, viewing distance, stimulus source and resolution, trial counts, feature definitions and dimensionalities, the exact OpenFace layer used (inception-4a, 640 channels at 6x6), the Gaussian kernel for fixation density maps (sigma=15 pixels), balanced class weighting, and the cross-validation scheme. The pipeline is re-implementable in principle; the data are not accessible.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: No data availability statement and no code release. Method reporting is otherwise strong: all software packages with exact versions, the rater-weighting softmax formulation, the Shapley local-accuracy property and its ensemble extension, the elastic-net loss with its two hyperparameters and the grid-search procedure, the balanced class weighting, the three-fold cross-validation split sizes, and demographic breakdowns for both training and test sets. Full mathematical detail is deferred to a multimedia appendix. The pipeline is re-implementable in principle; the videos, being identifiable child media, could not reasonably be released.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Mixed. The source dataset is a public benchmark with an organiser-defined train/test split, which is the strongest form of comparability in this corpus - results are directly comparable against other challenge entrants. The feature set is fully enumerated in a table with definitions and the saliency feature is given as an explicit equation, the ROI clustering threshold (100) and centre-proximity radius (100 pixels) are stated, and the classifier and tree count (128) are named. But no code is released, no random seeds are given, no software versions are specified, and the object-detection and saliency models are named without configuration details.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: No data or code release. The model specification is however documented in unusual detail: the state factorisation, the belief-space partitioning scheme (16 partitions over the condition simplex, 3 each over engagement and verbal activity), the full 3x16 observation probability matrix for the condition states, the 2x3 matrices for engagement and verbal activity, the centroid-based procedure for deriving those probabilities, the confidence-scaling equation with its chosen value of 0.8, the reward-shaping rules, and the solver used. The model is therefore reimplementable; the sessions are not reproducible, and the clinician survey that supplied the underlying observation rates is not documented.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Effectively nil. No data availability statement, no code, no software or versions, no SVM kernel or hyperparameters, no ROI definitions, no feature-vector dimensionality, no stimulus materials, no sample sizes, and no random seeds. Neither the experiment nor the analysis could be reproduced from the paper. The only reproducibility-supporting detail is the eye tracker model and a pointer to the prior study whose stimuli and data-collection recommendations were adapted.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: No data or code release and no random seeds, but the analytic pipeline is described in enough detail to reimplement: the full 20-measure table, the accuracy-feature definitions, the outlier-removal procedure and its citation, z-score normalisation, the four feature-selection methods with their parameters (ReliefF K=23, top 10 features for the filter methods), the SVM kernel and grid-searched parameters, the named libraries, the nested cross-validation structure with 10 folds repeated 100 times, and the 1000-permutation significance test. Analytically this is one of the more reproducible descriptions in the corpus; empirically it is not reproducible without the data.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Unusually strong on data, weaker on process. The 547-image dataset with metadata is publicly released on Figshare with the explicit intention that others reuse it, and a working demonstration application is deployed at a stated URL. The rendering procedure is described in reproducible detail - the colour-gradient encoding of velocity, acceleration and jerk, the one-quarter-diagonal cap, the vertical mirroring, the 200-point threshold and how it was chosen, the 100x100 rescaling, the grayscale luminance equation, and the PCA reduction to 50 components. What is missing: no code release, no random seeds, no statement of how cross-validation folds were partitioned, no augmentation transformation parameters beyond 'rotation, shearing', and no per-group demographics.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Data sharing is refused on explicit consent grounds and no code is released, but the analysis is described in unusual procedural detail: the MEA pipeline and its source, the region-of-interest definitions, the cross-correlation window length (60 s), lag range (plus or minus 5 s) and step size (0.04 s), the non-overlapping window rule, the resulting feature counts (1004 lagged cross-correlations, 4016 features per participant), the PCA variance threshold (80%) and its placement inside the inner fold, the feature scaling range, the full nested cross-validation structure (10 folds x 5 permutations outer, 5-by-5 inner), and the eight C values searched. The named open-source tools (rMEA, NeuroMiner) further support re-implementation.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: The most complete protocol reporting in the corpus. Specified: the design and its STARD basis; the trial registration number and its pre-results status; both sites with participant allocation broken down by cohort and site in a table; inclusion and exclusion criteria for all three groups in a second table, including the exclusion of subclinical or secondary autism expressions from the comparison-disorder group; the age window; both recruitment streams; the games, their source and their duration; the sensor modalities; the third-party algorithm with its provenance in a published pilot; the questionnaire battery for the clinical cohorts; primary and secondary outcomes; the sample size justification with explicit power figures; both ethics approvals; the funding source with grant number; an itemised competing-interest statement distinguishing academic from commercial authors; and author contributions naming who performed the sample size calculations and who conducted technical development. What cannot be reported is any result.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Mixed but above average for a workshop paper. The source dataset is a public benchmark with an organiser-defined blind test set, so results are comparable against other entrants. All three model architectures are specified in reproducible detail including trainable parameter counts, and the augmentation regime is fully described (colour jitter, up to 20-pixel location jitter, duration scaling in [0.75, 1.25], random Gaussian sigma in [0.1, 2], horizontal flips, with affine transforms deliberately excluded to avoid pushing fixations out of frame). What is missing: no code release, no random seeds, no participant counts, no STAR-FC configuration details, and no statement of how the 240/60 image split was drawn.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Mixed. The authors state that 'the code for our proposed method will be released in our website', which is a commitment rather than a completed release. The representation is described in reproducible detail - 15 named keypoints, Gaussian kernel size 12x12 with variance 1.0, the three-colour body-region scheme, intensity ramping across the episode, 256x256x3 output, the 8-seconds-before and 2-seconds-after episode rule, and 30 fps giving up to 301 frames. Dataset statistics are tabulated per set. What is missing: no participant information, no train/test split specification, no classifier hyperparameters, no random seeds, and no access route for the video corpus, which is commercially held.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: Strong for the system and thin for the study. Reported: the complete vision pipeline stage by stage; the open-source libraries with repository URLs and the modification required to run their neural models inside ROS nodes; the inter-node message types; the HMM-based visual-focus-of-attention estimation; the two-channel bidirectional architecture linking robot and web client; the therapist-facing application's role in controlling and registering each protocol step; the joint-attention protocol with its three subtypes and stimulus types; the mediator sequence; the tagged behaviour categories; participant numbers, ages, sex composition and parental consent; and the occlusion failures encountered. Not reported: ethics approval, session duration, the risk factors defining the index group, any screening of the comparison group, the number of cameras used, and any quantitative behavioural result. A reader could rebuild the system from published components and could not reproduce the study.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Reasonable for a four-page challenge entry. The source dataset is a public benchmark with an organiser-defined blind test set. The CNN architectures are fully tabulated (layer type, channel count, kernel size, stride), the patch size (225, a=112), LSTM length (40), zero-padding rules, optimiser, learning rate, momentum, batch size, epochs and model-selection criterion are all specified, and the SalGAN implementation is linked to a public repository. What is missing: no code release for the authors' own model, no random seeds, no participant information, and no statement of how many scanpaths entered training and validation.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: Adequate for a short conference paper and incomplete on participants. Reported: both games, the voice-menu dialogue opening, the robot platform with physical specifications and software environment, the professional backgrounds of the competent raters, the questionnaire-based coding procedure, the normalisation of behaviour counts to proportions of behaviours required in each game, the statistical test with statistic and p-value, ethics approval, parental consent, and the participating kindergarten by name. Not reported in the retrieved text: sample size, ages, sex, diagnostic ascertainment, the questionnaire items themselves, and inter-rater reliability - the last being a real gap given that the competent-raters technique is the study's measurement instrument, and one the group closed in its 2022 follow-up by reporting Kendall's W and subscale alpha.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Above corpus average. A data availability statement exists, trial registration is prospective, ethics approval is named with its reference number, inter-coder reliability is quantified per behaviour, the behavioural coding definitions are stated in full, the classifier library and functions are named, and the validation scheme is described precisely enough to reproduce. What is missing: hyperparameters (SVM kernel and C, forest size), any code release, participant-level data despite the availability statement, and reconciliation between the headline accuracies and the confusion matrix.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: No data or code release stated. Method reporting is strong on the analytic side - the full 20-parameter kinematic definition list, the feature structure across conditions and blocks, the four baseline selectors, the three developed variants with their operating rules (100 subsamples of size n/2 for bagging; t-statistic adjustment up or down at a 50% accuracy threshold with termination at Kuncheva's index of 1 across 100 consecutive iterations for the wrapped t-test), the nested cross-validation structure with feature selection inside each of ten folds, and the classifier. Weak on the experimental side, where apparatus, protocol details and diagnostic ascertainment are all deferred to a prior publication.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: Poor. The system architecture, network topology, module decomposition, data formats and interface flow are described in detail, but nothing needed to reproduce the machine learning is given: no training procedure, no train/validation/test split, no hyperparameters, no epochs, no augmentation, no accuracy on the source expression datasets, and no description of how the VGG-19 and ResNet-18 outputs were 'synthesised'. No code and no data are released. The clinical evaluation reports per-child recognition rates in full, which is welcome, but no statistical test accompanies them.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: No data or code release. Method reporting is otherwise strong: force plate manufacturer and sampling rate, filter order and cutoff with the selection method, all six COP variable definitions, sample entropy parameters, the outlier check and its criterion, trial acceptability criteria, the ANOVA design, the cross-validation scheme, the metric formulas with the positive class defined, the software version, and classifier parameters supplied in an appendix. Confusion matrices for all classifiers are also provided in an appendix. The analysis is re-implementable in principle on comparable force-plate data.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Weak, as expected for a two-page report. No data or code release, no software versions, no CNN training hyperparameters (optimiser, learning rate, epochs, batch size), no random seeds, no KNN k value or random forest configuration, and no specification of how the 80/20 split was drawn. The feature construction is described at a level that would allow approximate reimplementation - OpenPose, 68 facial keypoints from nose and eyes, three Laban features over a 1-second moving window, 71 features total - and the CNN architecture is sketched, but nothing could be reproduced quantitatively.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: No data or code release is stated in the extracted text, and substantial methodological detail - the CAMI equations, parameter learning formula, parameter values, full inclusion and exclusion criteria, study setup, and supplementary ten-fold replication - is deferred to a supplement. What is in the main text is precise: the five-step algorithm is described in sequence, joint importance estimation is explained, the three features are defined, the cross-validation scheme and its rationale are given, and the software and hardware are named. The approach would be reimplementable with the supplement.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: Good on architecture and preprocessing, thin on training detail. Reported: layer dimensions, auxiliary output formulation with equations, frame length and overlap, five-frame grouping, normalisation fitted on training data only, batch normalisation, ReLU, dropout, ADAM, early stopping with 100-epoch patience, best-model checkpointing, and the utterance decision rule (mean frame-wise class index above 0.5). Not reported: learning rate, batch size, dropout rate, auto-encoder pretraining schedule, the relative weighting of reconstruction and auxiliary losses in the joint objective, and whether SVM hyperparameters were tuned. No code and, by design, no data.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Mixed. The feature definitions are exemplary - all eight are named explicitly by their event pairs (RS-LS, LS-RS, LO-LS, RO-RS, LS-LO, RS-RO, LS-LS, RS-RS), mapped to their gait phases, with the sampling rate and the frame-difference computation stated, so the feature set is fully reproducible. The dataset construction is also precisely specified, down to the cycle and trial counts in each condition. Everything else is missing: no grid-search ranges or selected hyperparameters for any classifier, no random seed, no code or data release, no ethics statement, and no participant characteristics whatsoever.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: Among the best in the corpus for method reporting. All 60 features are enumerated individually with their computation; the segmentation algorithm is given with its equations and every threshold (40 ms frames at 10 ms rate, baseline as modal energy within +/- 20 s, onset at 90% above baseline held 50 ms, offset at 10% above baseline held 50 ms, 110 ms and 3 s duration bounds, under 1.5% excluded); the PRAAT voicing threshold is stated as 0.45; all six model architectures are specified layer by layer with epochs, batch sizes and dropout; the hyperparameter search grid is given (batch size from {4,8,16} or {32,64}, learning rate from {1e-5, 5e-5, 1e-4, 5e-4}); and the balanced-split acceptance criteria are stated numerically. Missing: code and data release, ethics documentation, and the selected hyperparameter values are relegated to a table that did not survive extraction.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: The best in the corpus. Data, code, materials, page screenshots, task questions, confusion matrices, comparisons against other classifiers, and full results for every data split and page configuration are all deposited at a public repository, and releasing data is stated as an explicit objective of the paper. Apparatus, calibration, viewing distance, fixation algorithm, AOI construction and split procedure are all specified in the text, and results carry 95% confidence intervals. The one gap in the paper itself is that Tables I and II - demographics and the feature list - are the two most reference-critical tables and neither survived text extraction here, though both are presumably in the deposited materials.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: Mixed. The model is described in enough detail to reimplement - patch sizes (79 x 79 centre, 158 x 158 surround resized to 79 x 79), the full 33-dimensional saliency breakdown with dimension counts per component, the multi-scale piece construction for k = 1 to 5 with the scoring equations, the aggregation formula, the thresholding method and the toolbox used. Stimulus timing, count, categories and apparatus are given. Missing: SVM kernel and hyperparameters, calibration and data-quality procedures, the identity of the CNN's pretraining data, any code or data release, any ethics documentation, and an account of the four recruited children who do not appear in the experiments.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Good on apparatus and pipeline, thin on results provenance. Reported: CAVE dimensions and projector specification, viewing distance, condition durations and baselines, camera model and SDK, OpenPose joint indices with their anatomical mapping, the 0.5 confidence cutoff, the displacement computation, PCA variance threshold, SVM kernel and search grid, the LOSO normalisation scheme, the nested RFE with correlation bias reduction, the optimisation criterion, and the software versions. Missing: any data or code release; ADOS-2 and ADI-R scores; frame rate of the depth camera; the proportion of joints discarded by the confidence threshold; an explanation for the two autistic children apparently absent from the analysis; and any account of how the 24 reported models relate to the number actually run.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: Good on architecture, thin on protocol provenance. Reported: the full network architecture layer by layer for both branches with feature map dimensions, the 7-frame clip length and 224 x 224 input size, the 24 FPS and 20-second default window (about 480 frames per stimulus), the 0.9 smile decision threshold with its rationale, the ASR training corpus, the mean-imputation rule for missing stimuli, and the leave-one-out evaluation. Missing: decision tree hyperparameters, the smile-count threshold for stimulus scoring, group-wise demographics, ethics documentation, and any data or code release. A typographical error in the stimulus scoring description states that the score is marked 0 in both branches of the threshold test.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: Among the best in the corpus. Reported: all six paradigms with their construct rationale, stimulus counts, durations and per-stimulus feature counts with standard deviations; the eye tracker, monitor, refresh rate, resolution, viewing distance, calibration scheme and measured calibration error; the fixation identification algorithm; the ROI annotation scheme including the non-overlap rule and composite variables; the imputation method; the network architecture, layer sizes, activation, bias handling, learning rate schedule, epochs and batch sizes; the optimisation algorithm; and the identity of every comparator method. Code is open sourced on GitHub and the data and processing pipeline are offered on request. Missing: group-wise demographics, the diagnostic decision procedure, and the specific 11 stimuli that constituted the best sparse subset.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: Good on signal processing, absent on evaluation. Fully reported: electrode count and selection, sampling rates, referencing scheme, filter bands, downsampling, notch filtering, ICA artefact removal, visual rejection, epoch length, Welch parameters (eight segments, 50% overlap, Hamming window), the five frequency bands with their boundaries, the eight AOIs, the fixation-proportion index definition, the 60 ms fixation threshold, viewing distance, calibration procedure, stimulus counts and durations, and the interstimulus attention device. Entirely absent: any statement of how the classifier was trained and evaluated - no split, no folds, no repetition - together with SVM hyperparameters, the identity of the 32 selected features, and any code release.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Very good, with implementation detail deferred to a supplementary appendix rather than omitted. Reported in the paper: recruitment window and channels, all inclusion and exclusion criteria for both groups, every excluded participant with the reason, hardware construction and cost, screen size, resolution and viewing distance, stimulus source and balancing, image counts per trial, display durations, feedback modality and timing, the calibration validation device, the four-calibration scheme with per-calibration polynomial regression, the four-way gaze coding scheme, all four feature blocks with their dimensionalities, the classifier and its rationale, the cross-validation scheme, the shuffling test with iteration count and convergence checking, and a full 60-cell ablation grid. Pupil tracking algorithms, inter-labeller reliability and outlier exclusion criteria are in Multimedia Appendix 1. Not released: data or code.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: Among the best in the corpus. Reported: all recruitment, inclusion and exclusion criteria; the full SIT structure with segment durations and the reasoning behind topic choice; the actress's verified non-verbal behaviour; frame- and participant-level tracking confidence thresholds (0.75 confidence, 90% of frames) with actual achieved tracking rates (99% of frames, mean confidence 0.99, no group difference at p = 0.97); feature construction at both primary and secondary levels with counts per modality; the classifier, ensemble size and full hyperparameter grids; the nested cross-validation scheme with an explicit statement about the absence of repeated measures; the expert rating protocol; and all statistical tests with effect sizes. Analysis code is public on GitHub, and the SIT instrument was scheduled for open release from 2024 under a Creative Commons licence at a named repository. Video data are withheld for privacy but available on request.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: Poor. The workflow diagram and the named Azure modules make the pipeline order legible - which is how the feature-selection leakage becomes visible - but almost nothing else is reproducible. Not reported: the dataset's identity or citation, k for the k-fold cross-validation, any hyperparameters, the random seed, the identity of three of the six retained features, performance figures for any comparator algorithm, the AUC value behind the plotted ROC curve, and any statistic supporting any descriptive claim. No code and no data.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: Mixed. Well reported: the two intervention modules with their specific cues and actions, the physical setup with distances, the sensors and SDK modules used, the binning thresholds for both observable variables, the session and week counts for training and testing, and a per-child table of age, sex, autism type and mean performance. Poorly reported or absent: CARS scores and band definitions, how the HMM parameters were estimated from the 72 training sessions, the basis for the transition probabilities quoted, per-child test results, any code or data, and any statement of institutional ethics approval. The printed transition probabilities do not sum to valid distributions, and the posterior formula assumes conditional independence between joint attention and imitation without stating or justifying that assumption.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Strong on the feature and modelling pipeline, absent on governance and descriptive results. Fully reported: all 15 features with their definitions and which were newly devised; the floating region identification procedure including specialist demarcation of the first frame and automated propagation; segment boundaries with frame counts; the missing-value imputation rule with its constant; Min-Max normalisation; the SMOTE variants and random forest hyperparameter grids; all three ensemble strategies with their threshold ranges; and the 10-fold cross-validation. Absent: any ethics or consent statement; any group-level descriptive statistics for the features; the identity of the selected hyperparameters; data or code release; and any account of missing or excluded data.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: Mixed. Reported: the scene contents, exposure duration, headset and tracking module, the K-means region segmentation procedure, all eleven features with definitions, the seven base models with the specific hyperparameters tuned for each and the rationale for PCA before logistic regression and naive Bayes, both ensemble combination rules, the 70/30 split with threefold cross-validated GridSearchCV, and full metric tables for both experiments. Not reported: the outlier criterion and the stage at which mean imputation was applied relative to the split, the selected hyperparameter values, the number of gaze points per participant, any calibration or data-quality statistics, the diagnostic basis of the test participants, and any code. Data are available on request.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Excellent. Reported: full stimulus inventory with picture counts, dimensions, resolution and spatial separation; the exact instruction wording; trial timing with the empirical rationale for both the 1000 ms fixation requirement and the 4000 ms limit; calibration procedure and acceptance threshold; fixation definition (50-pixel radius, 100 ms); all four areas of interest; per-group trial exclusion rates; the local-versus-global coordinate handling for randomly positioned regions; all 68 features enumerated by type and count; the classifier with its k values and the external source used to fix them; the cross-validation scheme; and complete confusion matrices with per-class sensitivity, specificity and AUC for both the three-class and binary problems. Missing only: data or code release, and the authors' own choice not to report feature importances, which follows from their no-selection stance.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Mixed. Well specified: the three behavioural hypotheses, the six-region screen division, the rule mapping eye deviation angle to gaze region, the head-eye co-movement criterion, the clap-prediction rule, the complete 43-feature inventory with naming convention, the stage and sub-stage structure, the sampling period, both hyperparameter values, and the three classifiers with their mathematical definitions. Not specified: any diagnostic instrument; ethics approval; calibration procedure, viewing distance or data-quality thresholds; the value of k for KNN; how epsilon and tau were chosen; participant ages beyond ranges; and any data or code release. The complete absence of a diagnostic basis alongside a full derivation of the SVM kernel function is a striking imbalance of reporting effort.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: Mixed. Well specified: EEG preprocessing chain with filter band, sampling rate, referencing, ICA artefact removal, electrode selection and 4-second non-overlapping epochs; the seven eye-tracking tests with their purposes and presentation schedule; the 60 ms fixation threshold; the fourteen features by name; both comparator architectures including ResNet18 channel configuration; and complete t-statistics for every feature. Not specified: any diagnostic instrument; participant ages, sexes or matching statistics; the unit of the 8:2 split; the covariance threshold used to build the adjacency matrix; GCN layer configuration, training hyperparameters or random seed; and the random forest configuration used for gaze feature selection. No code, and a data availability statement that points to the article itself.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Good. Reported: full stimulus specification with duration, frame rate and resolution; viewing distance, screen size and calibration procedure; the exclusion criteria including the 80% record-rate threshold; all 27 candidate features itemised by level; the frame preprocessing chain including edge removal, resizing, transition-frame deletion and the 33%-difference grouping rule that reduced 1,590 frames to 135; both pixel-sampling strategies with counts; the complete neural network architecture, activation functions, training algorithm, learning rate and stopping criteria; the 0.75 binarisation threshold; the 20-frame decision rule and how it was chosen; the cross-validation scheme with its subject-level unit; and the statistical tests with normality checking. Missing: whether ReliefF was nested within folds, the identity of the selected features beyond their counts by category, any data or code release, and reconciliation of the inconsistent performance figures.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Strong. Reported: full question list for all four sessions; interviewer age, sex, blinding and consistency requirement; seating distance; both camera models with sampling rates; eye tracker model and rate; the four areas of interest; the real-world mapping procedure with human verification and manual correction; the velocity-threshold fixation definition with its 30 deg/s and 60 ms parameters; the fixation-percentage computation; all 21 features; the forward selection procedure described step by step; the leave-one-out scheme; and a table giving accuracy, sensitivity and specificity at every feature count from 1 to 21. Missing: ethics approval number, data or code release, and classifier hyperparameters. The interviewer-consistency check by image differencing is itself reported with its test statistic.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: Detailed on signal processing, absent on everything else. Fully specified: pre-emphasis, framing and windowing with 30 ms Hamming windows; the RASTA-PLP computation given as a seven-step procedure; MFCC parameters including window length, shift, coefficient count and dynamic features; RASTA-PLP order and window overlap; the network architecture, activation functions, training algorithm, learning rate, momentum, epoch count and target error; the hidden-neuron selection procedure; and the partition ratios. Absent: diagnostic instruments, group ages, ethics approval, recruitment, how samples were elicited or how many per child, whether the partition respected speaker boundaries, any group-level acoustic statistics, and any code or data.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: Good. Reported: the full stimulus battery with per-protocol durations, counts and content; recording geometry, calibration and verification; the three-step visualisation procedure including the mirroring correction and the velocity bound at a quarter of the screen diagonal; the empirical selection of the 200-point drawing threshold with the tested alternatives and their outcomes; image cropping and rescaling to 256 x 256; the augmentation factor and resulting sample count; the CNN layer composition; the three-fold cross-validation under both splitting regimes with the participant-level procedure described step by step; training epochs and hardware; and the MIC method with its rationale and software. Missing: CNN hyperparameters beyond layer counts, filter sizes, the repository link for the released dataset, and ADI-R and ADOS-G scores which were inaccessible.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Very good. Reported: stimulus construction with clip counts, durations, resolution and counterbalancing; positioning, calibration procedure and the two-failure exclusion rule; the 80% capture-rate inclusion threshold; the blindfold control for lap-seated children; frame preprocessing including edge removal, resizing to 200 x 350 and transition-frame deletion; the optical-flow aggregation threshold of 0.33 with its empirical derivation and an explicit note that it is video-specific and 'should be reviewed' for different stimuli; the 5 x 5 Gaussian smoothing kernel; the 350-positive and 350-random-negative pixel sampling; all 28 candidate features with their sources; the full network specification including loss, optimiser, learning rate and stopping criteria; the vote-based classification rule; and the subject-level cross-validation with the 50 held-out diagnosis frames. Missing: group-wise ages, whether genetic algorithm selection was nested within folds, and any code or eye-tracking data release.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: Strong on protocol, weaker on results provenance. Reported: every scene with its content and duration; CAVE dimensions, projector, audio and olfactory hardware; child positioning; the counterbalancing and the sensory-overload interludes; the calibration and acceptance procedure; the eye tracker's head-motion compensation; the hierarchical area-of-interest structure; all five feature families with construction rules including the difference features; the normality testing and choice between t-test and Mann-Whitney; the step backward wrapper with its ten-feature cap; the repeated cross-validation scheme; and six metrics with standard deviations for all ten datasets. Missing: participant sex, ADOS-2 and ADI-R scores, the identity of the selected features in the winning models (deferred to a supplementary table), any data or code release, and reconciliation of how many total model fits the reported maxima were selected from.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Good. Reported: seating distance, both cameras with sampling rates and their distinct purposes, the full ten-question list in an appendix, the instruction given to participants, interviewer blinding and consistency requirement, OpenFace version with published per-axis accuracy figures and the rationale for choosing it, per-group tracking failure rates, spline interpolation for smoothing, the exact definitions and computation of both features including the velocity-integration procedure and the per-minute normalisation with its rationale, the blind double-coding of gesture occurrence with Spearman reliabilities, the mixed-effects model specification with all fixed and random terms and the likelihood ratio testing approach, the exhaustive feature-combination rationale, all five classifiers, and leave-one-out cross-validation. Missing: ethics approval number, group-wise demographics in the extracted text, classifier hyperparameters, and any data or code release.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: Poor for a computational paper. Reported: the source dataset with its repository link and originating citation, the preprocessing chain (greyscale, brightness increase, resize to 128 x 128), the number of clusters, the nine classifier names, ten-fold cross-validation, the eight evaluation metrics, and a complete 45-row results table. The k-means algorithm is set out in full mathematical detail, which is unnecessary for a standard method. Not reported: how many images or children fall in each cluster and their class balance; any hyperparameter for any classifier; the random seed; the rationale for choosing four clusters; whether images from a child were kept together; and any code. The mathematical exposition of k-means occupies more space than the entire account of how the classifiers were configured.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Excellent. Reported: task geometry with all distances, stimulus dimensions, block structure and randomisation; camera count, sampling rate, filter type and cutoff; marker placement anatomy; the five-segment kinematic model with all nine joint angles and their derivation including the pronosupination computation; movement onset and offset criteria with their thresholds and durations; PCA preprocessing including time-normalisation to 200 points and per-trial z-scoring with its stated rationale; the justification for retaining three components; the full ANOVA model with both factors; permutation testing for non-normal outcomes with iteration count; all 17 classifier features defined individually in a table; the SVM kernel and full hyperparameter grid; the leave-one-subject-out procedure including how normalisation was applied across the split; and per-participant clinical data. Supplementary material covers pronosupination derivation, trial-count robustness, feature-restricted robustness and per-participant feature importance. Missing only: data or code release, and IQ measures.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: Strong on the system and incomplete on the study. Reported: eligibility criteria including the CARS2 band and the verbal-response requirement, mean age with standard deviation, recruitment site, both ethics approvals, the parental consent procedure, the robot and the custom chest-mount with its mass-distribution justification, the phone-as-IP-camera configuration, the detector types, all three scoring rules with their exact constants (+5, -1, +15 and a linear latency function), the 1 Hz update rate, the 13-section scenario structure, the adaptive personalisation mechanism, the number of sessions in the agreement analysis and the exact number of mismatches, and a practical failure mode with its fix. Not reported: session duration, the content of the 13 sections, why 5 of 11 children did not continue, the therapist rating procedure and its reliability, funding and competing interests. A reader could rebuild the scoring system and could not reproduce the study.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Poor. Reported: the full 21-item questionnaire with each item's type and wording, the encoding scheme, the three feature-selection methods with their parameters, the nine algorithms with brief descriptions, the 80/20 split ratio, a complete 27-cell accuracy table, and confusion matrices for all nine algorithms under one selection scheme. Absent: any diagnostic instrument, ethics approval, group demographics, recruitment source for the comparison group, the identity of features retained by any selection method, all hyperparameters, the random seed, sensitivity and specificity values despite being said to have been computed, and any data or code. The questionnaire itself is the one element documented well enough to be reused.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: Very good. Reported: the four ADOS-2 tasks with the criterion for their selection; the full three-level analysis cascade with frame length, frame rate, silence detection, voiced-unvoiced separation, the Markov smoothness constraint and Viterbi decoding; the summarisation statistics and the decision to summarise voiced and unvoiced regions separately; all feature families with their rationale; the classifier, kernel, regularisation and scaling; the cross-validation structure with explicit statement of how test folds were held blind; the undersampling procedure with its convergence criterion; the confidence interval computation; the RFECV method; the IQ-matched subsample construction; and the complete exclusion criteria list. Missing: SVM hyperparameter values, whether RFECV was nested within folds, data or code release, and the number of speech segments or total audio duration per participant.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Mixed, and split cleanly along the boundary between what the authors did and what they inherited. Their own pipeline is reproducible in fine detail: all 30 features are individually named and defined in a table, the saliency-weight feature is given as an equation, the object-region rule (YOLO top-3 by confidence, remainder as non-object) is explicit, the clustering threshold is 100, the heatmap threshold is 0.1 with the source cited, the centre-proximity radius is 100 pixels, all 23 candidate classifiers are tabulated with their accuracies, and the selected hyperparameters and OOB error are stated. What is inherited is absent entirely: participant ages, sexes, diagnostic procedures, acquisition hardware, viewing durations. No code release is mentioned. The net effect is that the model could be re-implemented but the result could not be clinically interpreted.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: The best-reported study in the eye-tracking group and among the best in the corpus for the parts under the authors' control. All preprocessing is specified: coordinate normalisation by image dimensions, duration normalisation by division by 5000, zero-padding to 33 fixations, the discarding of STAR-FC's always-central first point, Gaussian spreading with sigma = 20 versus 30-pixel replication, augmentation by up to 20-pixel fixation shifts and duration scaling in [0.8, 1.2], colour jitter and horizontal flip, and the explicit decision to exclude affine transforms because they could push fixations outside the image. Every architecture is given layer by layer with all training hyperparameters. Tables 4 and 9 go further than any other paper here by tabulating the exact delta between the published challenge submission and the improved version - preprocessing, layer count, inputs, learning rate, regularisation, epochs, dropout and batch size - which makes the source of the improvement auditable rather than asserted. What is missing: no code release, and none of the participant-level or diagnostic information, which is inherited.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Strong on the pipeline, with one class of omission. Reported: OpenPose model variant and keypoint count; background removal; the decision to compute feature vectors from image output rather than raw coordinates, with the stated purpose of invariance to rigid-body and affine transformation; downsampling from 696x554 to 320x240; 5-second segmentation with the selection justified by validation loss against 10 and 15 seconds; full VGG16 layer geometry; LSTM size and both dropout rates; optimiser, loss, batch size, epochs and the 80-20 internal split; the least-validation-loss checkpointing rule; the 0.5 threshold on averaged ASD probability; the sliding-window procedure with its 20-second start and 20-second step; every Bonferroni-corrected significance threshold; and the PLS-C decomposition with its 1000 permutations and 1000 bootstrap resamples. Video-level statistics are tabulated (68/68/101 videos, 47.8/48.7/50.0 hours, ~505 segments per video). Missing: no code or model weights release, no data availability statement in the extracted text, no random seeds, and - the substantive gap - no statement of how many people appear per frame or whether any person-selection was applied to OpenPose's multi-person output, which is exactly the detail needed to know whose movement the classifier is reading.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Good on instrumentation and modelling, thin on data structure. Reported: tablet model, screen size, resolution, refresh rate and sampling frequency; the seating geometry; the task battery with its five domains, item structure and administration rule; the definition of a finite trajectory; all twelve features with formal definitions including the STH ratio and the DC/sdDC interpretation; the traj package with citations; feature standardisation; the full network specification (17-5-2, tanh, softmax, Adam, learning rate 0.01, Xavier initialisation, sparse categorical cross-entropy, 500 epochs); the grid-search range for hidden units and the criterion for choosing five; the cross-validation scheme; and the feature-removal procedure with its source. Missing or ambiguous: the number of trajectories per child, the aggregation from 25 tasks to 1,500 samples is stated but the fold-assignment rule is described only as random 'regardless' of subject composition, so the reader must infer that subjects span folds; no code release; no random seeds; and no participant-level performance breakdown that would allow the segment-versus-subject question to be resolved from the reported numbers. A data availability statement is present.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Strong on signal processing and network architecture, absent on selection procedure and data structure. Fully reported: every EEG acquisition and preprocessing parameter, every eye-tracking acquisition parameter, all three feature families with their band definitions, region groupings, MSE scale ranges and the seven graph metrics; the AOI scheme and the six per-AOI statistics with the arithmetic yielding 96 features; the normalisation formula together with the explicit statement that it is fitted on training data and applied to test; all three SDAE layer geometries; noise level, both learning rates, both iteration counts and the optimiser; the cross-validation scheme with its subject-independence and stratification; and the toolbox with its URL. Not reported: how the network geometries, noise level and learning rates were chosen, and whether that selection used the reporting folds; how many children were screened out by the >70% looking-time rule; whether any EEG recordings were excluded entirely; any group means or effect sizes for any feature; random seeds; and any data or code release beyond the third-party toolbox.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Good on protocol and architecture, thin on training procedure. Fully specified: the elicitation protocol with all distances, timings, toy specifications and examiner rules; camera model, resolution and frame rate; clip trimming rule (from toy placement, 10 seconds, 300 frames); the discard criterion for corrupted acquisitions; final clip counts by group (484 and 434 of 918); the exact composition of all four partitions by group and by clip count; the full network specification layer by layer; the attention formulation; and the difference in preprocessing between test sets. Not reported: optimiser, learning rate, batch size, epochs, loss function, any regularisation beyond the single dropout layer, the semantic segmentation method, random seeds, or any statement of how architecture or hyperparameters were selected. No code or data release. For a conference paper the protocol reporting is exemplary and the training reporting is incomplete.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Uneven, with the mathematics fully specified and the empirical procedure underdocumented. Reported in detail: the K-means loss function, assignment rule, centroid update and convergence criterion; the attribute-weighting formula for naive Bayes with its zero-avoidance property; the two-level fusion architecture; all 14 EEG electrode positions; the filter cut-offs and the five band definitions; the complete t-test table with F, t, p, mean difference and standard error for all 30 region-band combinations; the stimulus selection procedure; and both best and average accuracy for every modality-classifier pair. Not reported: the Tobii model, the camera specification, the sampling rates of any device, the number of EEG epochs retained per child or per group, the final chosen value of K, the CNN architecture and training details beyond a reference to prior work, any hyperparameters for random forest, SVM or KNN, and the order in which feature selection and cross-validation were performed - which has to be inferred from the text's sequence and is the study's decisive ambiguity.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Reproducible as an algorithm, not as a study. Fully specified: the three augmentation operations and the resulting 1300% expansion; the resize target, interpolation kernel, colour transform and bit depth; the normalisation equation; the CSV structure of 785 columns; the KELM equations; the GPC pseudo-code with all four operations and their parameter values; the internal parameters of all five comparator optimisers in a table; the multilayer perceptron's architecture, activation, optimiser and learning rate; the search space for C and gamma; population size, dimension and iteration count; the number of independent runs; and the compute hardware. Entirely absent: any train/test split or cross-validation protocol, the sizes of any partition, the criterion by which the optimiser's fitness was evaluated relative to reported performance, any participant-level information, and any code release. The single most important methodological fact - how performance was estimated on data not used to fit or tune the model - is not stated at any point in the paper.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Among the most reproducibly reported studies in the corpus. Specified: recruitment channels; both sites' diagnostic criteria including the exact ADOS-2 algorithm, cutoff and tolerance; the complete flow from 183 recruited to 153 analysed with reasons and counts at each step; eye tracker model, sampling rate, resolution, monitor size, viewing distance, calibration and validation protocol with its error threshold and repetition rule; both recording errors; stimulus identity, duration and part structure; the familiarity questionnaire and its cut-point; the complete area-of-interest construction including the specific models used, the merging of 24 DensePose parts into three, and the geometric rule for deriving eye and mouth regions from five keypoints; detection rates across all 61,724 frames; the manual verification of automatic segmentation; the downsampling to video frame rate, the 1-degree gaze disk and the maximum-overlap assignment rule; the normalisation of area-specific gaze by successful on-screen frames with its stated rationale; heatmap construction with Gaussian width, bin duration and the leave-one-out reference rule; the bootstrap, permutation and sampling procedures with their 10,000 iteration counts; classifier, held-out sizes and cross-validation repetitions; the mixture-model initialisation and its robustness checks; and the FDR correction. What is missing from the extracted text is an ethics statement, a data availability statement and any mention of code release.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Good on modelling, thin on data. Reported: the app, the two game types, the 90-second session length, the recording arrangement, the manual splicing criterion (segments containing no voice but the child's), clip counts by class, the mean of 1.32 videos and 14.7 clips per child, the fold composition table, the child-disjoint fold constraint with its rationale, the complete random forest feature list and all six hyperparameters, the CNN's layer structure, regularisation penalty, epoch count and exact parameter count, the wav2vec checkpoint and fine-tuning step count, the alternative models tried and rejected, and the total 115.5 minutes of audio. Not reported: any acoustic property of the recordings, the group-specific age ranges or means, any splicing reliability check or inter-splicer agreement, clip durations, the criterion for how many clips were taken per child, any data or code release, and random seeds. The manual splicing step is the least reproducible element - it is a human judgement applied to every clip, performed by unspecified people to an unspecified standard, and the authors identify its non-scalability as a limitation without addressing its consistency.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Among the best in the corpus.
