Reported: the complete participant flow from 289 screened to 158 analysed with a reason and count at every step; the full exclusion criteria list; the diagnostic procedure at each stage; the ADOS module, administrator training level and task selection with rationale; microphone type, placement distance and its justification; the transcription protocol, unit definition, disfluency notation, blinding of transcribers to diagnosis and IQ, consensus resolution procedure and biannual consistency checks; the three-module audio pipeline; the precise definition of all seven language measures and all ten voice measures; the SVM kernel, the soft-margin constant for each of the three models, feature normalisation, and the fact that non-linear SVMs and formal tuning were also run and reported in supplementary material; the cross-validation scheme with its citation-backed justification and its 10-fold robustness check; the DeLong test for AUC comparison; the mSVM-RFE procedure with an explicit note that 10-fold was used because the software could not run under leave-one-out; and the statistical tests for every comparison. Analysis code is publicly released and de-identified data offered on request. What is missing, and acknowledged: transcription reliability statistics, despite the training and consistency checks; and the effect of the denoiser.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Among the most completely reported studies in the corpus. Specified: recruitment setting and inclusion and exclusion criteria; the full screen-and-refer diagnostic pathway with M-CHAT-R/F cut-points; instrument names and administrator qualifications; the demographic table with race, ethnicity, caregiver education and statistical tests; all seven movies with durations and content descriptions; the physical setup including tripod distance, caregiver instructions and positioning of other people; the landmark count and pose angles; the |yaw| < 20 degree attention criterion with its theoretical justification and the additional gaze-based confirmation; the inter-eye normalisation with its rationale; the 10-frame smoothing window; the complete multiscale entropy formulation with the coarse-graining equation, the sample entropy definition, m = 2, r = 0.15 sigma, the use of population-wide sigma with its rationale, integration across the first 10 scales, and the missing-data handling; the 40% data-quality threshold with its justification and the resulting per-movie sample sizes shown in every figure; every statistical test with its Python function; the classifier, kernel, cross-validation scheme and confidence-interval method; and the model-comparison criterion. Missing: no data or code release, no random seeds, and no reporting of how many of the 457 were excluded per movie in aggregate, though per-movie counts are given.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Split sharply between the computational and the empirical. Fully specified or deposited: the two feature classes with their theoretical motivation, the counts (8,640 rhythm features, 400 intonation features), the utterance selection rule and count, the analytic level with its linguistic justification, the classifier and kernel with an argument for the choice, the nested structure of dimensionality reduction and hyperparameter tuning within cross-validation, the permutation testing with 5,001 iterations, and the analysis scripts on OSF. Not specified: any recording equipment or acoustic condition; the reason 22 English autistic and 6 English comparison participants were dropped between recruitment and analysis; how the 20 utterances per participant were selected from the full narrative; who performed transcription and segmentation, with what training or reliability; the number of principal components retained; and the SVM hyperparameter ranges searched. The supplementary file carries the post-hoc confound analysis, the technical feature-extraction detail and a supplementary demonstration that the rhythm features do contain systematic cross-linguistic differences - the last being an important internal check that the combined-language rhythm result is not simply detecting language.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Good on the computational pipeline and the language sample, thinner on the participants. Reported: inclusion and exclusion criteria for both groups; the ADOS-2 task and the specific book; the transcription protocol with its convention, blinding, reliability figure and discrepancy resolution; descriptive statistics of the transcripts (sentences, tokens, duration, pages narrated); all three representation schemes with their vector dimensions and the 15% missing-page rate; every encoder with its version, pre-training corpus and settings; the classifier families with the dense layer's full hyperparameter grid; the leave-one-out scheme; and package URLs. A footnote even records that recurrent classifiers were tried and performed substantially worse. Not reported: sex composition despite matching being claimed; how the narrative was divided into page-level subsets, described only as done manually and acknowledged as 'sometimes ambiguous, especially when a participant skips one of the pages'; the number of trials or seeds; and any AUC, confidence interval or significance test. Data are available on request rather than deposited, for stated privacy reasons; no code release.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Strong on acquisition and stimulus design, weak on the analytic sample and the modelling. Reported in full: recruitment sources; inclusion and exclusion criteria for both groups; the complete stimulus structure with durations, pairing, counterbalancing and the rationale for each non-social class; tracker model, sampling rate, monitor, resolution, viewing distance, calibration procedure and tolerance; all thirteen features with definitions for the less familiar ones; the three feature-selection algorithms with their selections tabulated feature by feature and area by area for both datasets; all 24 classifier-by-selection-by-dataset results with seven metrics each; a worked decision tree with split thresholds; group mean looking times per area of interest per stimulus set; and a public data URL. Not reported: how many participants entered the classification analyses and how the balanced subset was formed; any hyperparameters for any of the four classifiers; standard deviations for age or Bayley scores; the number of participants excluded for tracking failure; ethics approval; and how feature selection was nested within cross-validation beyond the assertion that only training data were used.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Strong on statistics and stimuli, weak on flow and on the classifier. Fully reported: recruitment sources and screening instruments for both groups; the diagnostic basis with its acknowledged limitation; demographics per cohort with tests; every paradigm with duration, content, area-of-interest definition and rationale; the position-switching and averaging procedure; tracker model, sampling rate, spatial resolution, monitor, resolution, viewing distance, room conditions and calibration procedure with its exclusion rule; fixation detection thresholds; the complete statistical model including covariates, variance assumption testing, the weighted least squares substitution, post-hoc correction method and the multivariate-t adjustment for interaction contrasts; means and standard deviations for all ten areas in all four groups; F statistics and p values for all three ANCOVA effects on all ten areas; Cohen's d for every contrast; and the leave-one-out procedure. Not reported: exclusion counts at either quality-control step; the SVM kernel, hyperparameters or implementation; the reconciliation between 78 and 74 preschoolers; and any code. Raw data are offered on request.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Reporting is at regulatory-trial standard and exceeds every other study in the corpus. Fully specified: trial registration number and protocol availability; IRB name, protocol number and approval date; site count and states; recruitment population; clinician qualifications and experience distribution; participant flow with reasons at each stage and COVID-19 impact quantified; baseline demographics for both completers and all enrolled across age, sex, race and ethnicity, education and income; the complete list of behavioural constructs probed by the questionnaires; item counts per input per age band; video duration requirements and caregiver guidance; video analyst qualification, training and certification requirements; the reference standard procedure including the blinding and adjudication structure; specialist qualifications; the certainty rating scale; median completion times for two of three inputs with the third's estimation method disclosed; the confusion matrix against a three-level standard; performance across every demographic stratum with intervals; severity and comorbidity breakdowns by output; the statistical software, packages and interval method; and the abstention threshold-setting procedure including the FDA-agreed PPV and NPV floors. Not available: the algorithm itself, the feature weights, and the code, all proprietary; and the specific standardised instruments the specialists used are described generically rather than named.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Uneven. Fully reported: the elicitation stimulus with its source; both recording arrangements including their divergence and its cause; the feature set with its version, the rationale for choosing it over two alternatives, and a complete table of all extracted feature families with definitions; the selection test; all 16 selected features with group means, standard deviations, outlier counts and exact p-values; the four classifiers; the split proportions and resulting sample sizes; the cross-validation scheme; the number of runs; both best-model and ten-run mean performance; and public code. Not reported: participant age means or tests; any cognitive, language or severity measure; the diagnostic procedure beyond one clause; recording durations, distances, sampling rates or device models; any classifier hyperparameters; comparison-group consent or ethics approval for either group; and any characterisation of speech quantity per child.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Reproducible as an image-processing pipeline, not as a study. Fully specified: all filtering, segmentation and morphological steps with equations; LBP neighbourhood and feature count; the 216-dimensional concatenated vector; the network architectures with layer counts; both CNNs' complete training hyperparameters; the augmentation operations and the resulting counts before and after; the exact split into 350 training, 88 validation and 109 test images with per-class breakdowns; the evaluation formulae; and the compute hardware. Not reported: anything about the participants beyond counts and sex; the stimuli; the eye tracker; the diagnostic procedure; the final chosen contour parameters; whether the split was stratified or randomised and with what seed; and any code. The data availability statement points to the public source images.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Good on pipeline, weak on participants. Fully reported: the app, game format, 90-second limit and recording arrangement; video and frame counts before and after filtering, broken down by group; both annotation tools with their outputs and the exact exclusion rules including the 75% confidence threshold; the gaze coordinate convention with its sign meanings; the 4x4 discretisation; the graph construction and normalisation for the transition analysis; the permutation test specification with 100,000 permutations and both Bonferroni thresholds; the sliding-window parameterisation with the ranges explored; the LSTM architecture, optimiser, learning rate, batch size and loss function; the three-way split with per-group video counts and the child-level constraint; and the metric choice with its rationale. Not reported: group-specific ages; any statistical comparison of demographics; the diagnostic elicitation; phone models or video specifications; the number of children excluded at any stage; and any data or code release.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Reproducible as a pipeline, silent on the data. Fully reported: greyscale conversion with its channel weighting; resizing to 100x100 and flattening to 10,000 elements; the resulting array dimensions; the number of principal components retained in each condition; the complete convolutional architecture with all layer dimensions; the hyperparameters and the tuning procedure; the 70:30 split with exact image counts; the five-fold cross-validation; the augmentation rotations and the resulting class counts; the mini-batch construction and its leave-one-out protocol; the compute platforms and hardware; and full performance tables for every model in every condition. Not reported: participant demographics, diagnostic procedure, stimulus, acquisition protocol, the criterion by which one image per child was selected for the mini batch, random seeds, ethics approval, or any code.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Strong on modelling, weak on participants, with one substantive ambiguity. Fully reported: the game mechanics including the tilt-labelling convention; the four event fields recorded; the rationale for restricting to CAFE prompts; both feature definitions with their formulae; the complete preprocessing sequence with its ordering, the three-standard-deviation outlier rule, k = 3 for imputation, and SMOTE; the explicit statement that preprocessing occurs within each split; the nested cross-validation structure with outer and inner fold counts and the seven repetitions; the selection criterion of AU-ROC in the inner loop; hyperparameter grids for all four classifiers; the deliberate bias of the search space toward regularisation; and all sixteen performance figures across two feature conditions. Not reported: group-specific ages; any demographic comparison; the therapy information collected as a diagnostic check; whether a child contributing multiple sessions supplies multiple rows to the dataset; the IRB protocol number; and any data or code release. The unit-of-analysis ambiguity is the most consequential gap given the paper's otherwise careful leakage handling.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Mathematically detailed and empirically opaque. Fully specified: the convolutive mixing model, the frequency-domain formulation, the negative-entropy independence criterion with its definition, the fixed-point update equation, the STFT window and offset, the resulting number of frequency sequences, the three feature constructions and the SVM kernel with its cross-validated parameter search. Not reported: recording equipment or channel configuration; participant ages, sexes, diagnoses or severity; the elicitation protocol or prompt set; whether lexical content was matched between groups; the CNN architecture, depth, training regime or any hyperparameter; how the 1,017 analysed recordings map to children; the retention rate by group; the criterion for selecting the 126th frequency sequence beyond it performing best; ethics approval; and any data or code release.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: Good within the constraints of a four-page conference paper, with one systematic deferral. Reported: microphone model, distance, sampling and downsampling rates, session duration, signal-to-noise ratio; the six manual labelling categories; both diarization feature sets with dimensionality and, for x-vectors, window size and rate; the shared network structure with its dual softmax and Viterbi post-processing; the vocalisation splitting including the treatment of segments over 3 seconds; the 100x48 matrix construction with its 10-vocalisation sampling rule; the optimiser and per-condition hyperparameters; the diarization error decomposition with its collar and the rationale for ignoring silence errors; the split construction with its four matched distributional moments and 50 repetitions; and the total detected duration under each segmentation condition. Deferred to a prior publication: the identity of the 48 features beyond four examples, the vocalisation separation method, and the CNN architecture details. Absent: ethics approval, data or code release, and the number of children excluded by the 20-second threshold.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Strong for an observational study. Reported: participant numbers, ages with mean and standard deviation, sex composition by group, the diagnostic source and the disciplinary composition of the diagnosing team, the kindergarten setting and the maximum of three children per visit, the two-session structure with familiarisation and both games and their durations, the robot and its remote operation, the number and professional background of the raters, both reliability statistics with their p-value, the statistical tests used, and - most usefully - the complete observational scale with its rating definitions published in an appendix. Publishing the instrument is what makes the paradigm reusable and is the single most valuable disclosure a study of this design can make. Not reported: rater blinding, the diagnostic instruments behind the kindergarten records, funding and competing interests.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Split. The experimental side is highly reproducible: the conversation protocol and its six questions are published, the 80 cm distance and 50 Hz sampling are given, the segmentation arithmetic is written out index by index, the binning is exact (10 px bins giving 192 x-bins, 108 y-bins and 20,736 x-y blocks), the Shannon entropy formula is stated, and the 30% data-loss rule is cited to its source. The computational side is not: no code, no data, no preregistration, no SVM kernel or regularisation parameter, no random seed, no scaling procedure, no statement of how many segments existed at each window length in numbers rather than a bar chart, and no specification of the grid of thresholds searched. A reader could re-run the experiment on new children but could not reproduce the reported numbers from the authors' data.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Mixed, with an unusual profile: this is one of the few studies in the corpus where the physical apparatus is more reproducible than the analysis. A reader could rebuild the car from the part numbers given and would have the ROS interface and Arduino firmware ecosystem described. Both feature tables are complete, listing all 44 baseline acceleration features with their symbols and all 10 new features with their definitions, and the final selected subset is named feature by feature. The four play states are defined operationally. Room size and session duration are given. Data are available on request. Against this: no code repository, no sampling rate, no model hyperparameters for any of the three algorithms, no random seed or fold assignment, no statement of whether feature selection was refit inside each fold, and no diagnostic criteria - so the labels themselves could not be reproduced. There is also an internal reference error, with the text pointing to 'Table 4' for the results that appear in Table 5.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Split, in the same pattern as several engineering-led studies in this corpus. Reproducible: the tablet specification, the 40 Hz sampling, the seating and table geometry, the five Leiter-3 subtests and 25-task structure, the definition of a trajectory (first tap to finger lift), all 12 features with their formulas or plain definitions in Table 1, the extraction package, and the three-term VAE loss written out in full with the equal weighting stated. Not reproducible: the network architecture and every training hyperparameter, the fold assignment procedure, random seeds, the Monte Carlo perturbation's sampling distribution parameters beyond 'N(mu_fi, sigma_fi)', and any code. Raw data are offered on request without undue reservation, which is a genuine commitment though weaker than deposition. The paper also reports no participant-level accuracy despite plotting participant-level latent means, so the single most useful number for a reader wanting to compare against other studies is absent.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Strong on specification, absent on artefacts. Every decision constant is stated numerically - the 3 s response window, the 90 degree and 20 degree shoulder thresholds, the 10-frame (0.4 s) and 8-frame duration thresholds - and the angle computation is written out as three equations from the shoulder vector through the arccosine to the degree conversion. The camera rig, frame rate, resolution, focal length and mounting height are given, as are the roles of each camera, the clinical protocol and its full scoring rule, the exact third-party models used, and the size of the custom detection training set. A competent group could rebuild the system from the paper. What cannot be reproduced is any number in it: the data are declared confidential, the retrained YOLOv3 weights and the 1,700-image annotations are not released, no code is available, and the ASR component is a commercial service whose behaviour may change. There is also no preregistration and no independent evaluation of the perception components (detection, tracking, landmark) in isolation, so their error rates on this population are unknown and are folded silently into the end-to-end figure.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Split between a well-specified experiment and an under-specified model. Reproducible: the game's two stages and objectives, the JAFFE stimulus source, the 240-image protocol, the stimulus resolution and the region segmentation with its named zones, the 18-feature definition as fixation count and fixation time per region, the MATLAB version, the training algorithm (scaled conjugate gradient backpropagation) and the activation functions (tanh hidden, sigmoid output), and the ethics approval identifier. Not reproducible: the eye tracker itself, the fixation-detection parameters, the MLP's hidden-layer count and node counts, the learning rate and iteration count that were 'optimised' by MSE, the random split and seed, and the code. Data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. The single most consequential reporting gap is not technical but presentational: because the abstract and conclusion quote the pooled total rather than the test column, a reader who does not open the tables will take away a figure roughly 15 points higher than the study's own held-out result.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Among the best-specified methods in this corpus, with the usual artefact gap. Reproducible from the text: the CASS protocol including confederate selection, training rules, timing constraints and the verbatim prompt; the camera hardware, resolution, frame rate and placement; the choice of 3DI with its stated rationale; the construction of the 60-component localised basis and the principled exclusion of nose and cheek components; the exact windowed cross-correlation scheme, including 50% window overlap, forward-lag-only convention and the explicit note that the pair (i,j) is therefore not equivalent to (j,i); the derivation of the 6,272 feature count; the SVM kernel and the fixed C = 1; the single tuned hyperparameter and its four candidate values; and the nested 10-fold cross-validation repeated 100 times with shuffling. The human-rating protocol is equally complete - head-and-neck crops, side-by-side layout, audio removed, randomised order, one viewing per video, no revisiting, completed in one to three sessions. Not available: code, data, the modified expression basis, preregistration, and the Table 1 demographics in the retrieved text. As a workshop paper (CEUR/ACM IUI joint proceedings) it is also shorter than a journal article, which accounts for some of the compression.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Strong on method, absent on artefacts, with an unusual amount of parameter transparency. Reproducible from the text: the complete stimulus protocol including image count, categories, display and mask durations, session structure and viewing distance; the eye tracker, its sampling rate and its exact noise-suppression rule; the superpixel step; the autoencoder's external training corpus, loss function and two-stage training strategy; the full LSTM equations; the feature concatenation; the weak-supervision label assignment; the aggregation and Otsu thresholding; and a sensitivity table spanning hidden units, fully connected size, epochs, mini-batch size, learning rate and the minLength lower bound. The finding that the resized superpixel bounding box outperforms a centred patch is reported as a negative result, which is rare and useful. Not available: code, data, the 82-image stimulus set, the specific final architecture dimensions, and - most importantly - the diagnostic procedure that generated the labels. Ten supplementary figures and three supplementary tables exist but were not retrieved. As an IEEE TBME paper the reporting standard is engineering-first, which shows in the asymmetry between an exhaustively specified pipeline and an unspecified clinical protocol.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: Partial, and unusually asymmetric. The data-collection procedure is described well enough to repeat in principle: the six search keywords are listed, the three manual exclusion rules (organisations, advocates, family members) are stated with examples, the four cleaning steps are enumerated, the date range is given, and the tweet counts before and after cleaning are reported. Model configuration is also specified, with selected hyperparameters for all three classical models, the exact BERT checkpoint, the split ratio and the compute hardware. Against this: how the 31 comparison users were chosen is never stated, which alone prevents reconstruction of the dataset; the text representation for the classical models is undescribed; BERT's fine-tuning regime (epochs, learning rate, batch size, maximum sequence length) is not given; no random seed is reported for a study whose single result rests on one random split; and neither code nor data is available. The data could not straightforwardly be shared in any case, since they consist of identifiable individuals' posts, which is a reason to have addressed data governance rather than a reason to omit it.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: The strongest methods reporting encountered in this review. Reproducible from the text: the full recruitment and screening pathway, all five exclusion criteria, the seating and device arrangement with the 60 cm distance, all six movies with durations and content, the 30 fps capture, the complete preprocessing chain including the affine canonical-face normalisation, the 15 Hz low-pass cut-off with its physiological justification (260 ms to produce an expression, 150-250 ms for a valid one), the removal of non-attending intervals, the entropy parameters m = 2 and r = 0.15 sigma with their literature sources and a supplementary sensitivity analysis, the exact rule for handling missing data inside the entropy computation with a worked numerical example, the 40% validity threshold and its consequence for per-movie sample size, the 20-scale integration window, the affect-energy definition with its 10-frame moving average, and every statistical test named down to the Python function. Two methodological contributions are presented as such rather than buried: the modification of multiscale entropy to handle partially missing time series without concatenation artefacts, and its normalisation to permit across-subject comparison - the latter accompanied by the pointed footnote that despite MSE's popularity in health research 'this problem has never been addressed before, and often authors report lower MSE for data that is clearly more complex and vice-versa'. Not available: code, data, the movies, and the decision-tree configuration. Five supplementary appendices hold further analyses, including the developmental-delay comparison and the head-motion work.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Among the best-specified studies in the review. Reproducible from the text: the full instrument battery per group, the FEIT protocol with image counts per emotion and exact trial timing, the eye tracker and sampling rate, the viewing distance, the I-VT algorithm with its velocity threshold, the area-of-interest definitions and the per-image redrawing rule, both trial-exclusion rules with the resulting per-emotion trial counts listed exactly, the scan-path computation as pseudocode, both model architectures in a table giving neuron counts and kernel sizes and channel counts, the optimiser, loss function, epoch cap and early-stopping patience, the heat-map construction including the Gaussian sigma and the 34 x 34 centre-cropped downscaling, the three-step strategy adopted specifically because the dataset is small, and the nested leave-one-participant-out scheme with its 8:2 inner split. Statistical procedures are equally explicit, including Welch's t-test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Not available: code, and the FEIT images, which are under copyright and could not even be reproduced as figures. Raw data are offered on request without undue reservation.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: Partial and uneven. Reproducible in principle: the app's identity and deployment window, the user and event counts, the 12.6% exclusion rule for insufficient events, the survey response numbers, the four-category pseudo-semantic identifier scheme with its non-overlapping ID ranges and the count of 69 unique keys and events, the definitions of sequential, temporal and spectral modelling, the window sizes swept, the classifier inventory, and the repetition and bootstrap counts for both cross-validation schemes. Not reproducible: the unit of cross-validation, which is never stated and determines whether the results mean anything; the k-means configuration, how pseudo-labels were assigned and whether any were checked; the stacked autoencoder and deep belief network architectures and training regimes; the survey instrument; any hyperparameter, seed, code or data. The dataset is telemetry from a discontinued commercial app held by a third-party foundation and is not described as available. Internal consistency is also weak, with three different participant totals recoverable from the text and tables.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Among the best in this review on protocol and reporting, incomplete on the model. Fully specified in the main text: recruitment sources and dates, enrolment and exclusion criteria, the staged screening and diagnostic pathway with every instrument named in its validated Korean version, the theoretical source and operational definitions of the three joint attention constructs, the camera model, resolution and frame rate, the exact input tensor dimensions for each task (224 x 224 x 300 for IJA, 224 x 224 x 150 for RJA), the cross-validation scheme with its grouping unit stated explicitly, the classification threshold, the confidence-interval method, and every software package with version. Supplementary materials carry the enrolment flow diagram, the task procedures and acquisition setup, the compliance metric definition, the architecture diagram, training and validation performance, age-stratified results, and all Grad-CAM, attention-plot and cluster-map figures. STARD adherence and a data sharing statement are declared. What is missing is the model itself in reproducible detail - layer sizes, optimiser, learning rate, epochs, augmentation - and any code release. Given that the method is patented, the absence of code is unsurprising but does mean the central artefact cannot be independently checked.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: Adequate for the modelling, absent for the data. Reproducible: the source dataset is cited and public; the split counts are given exactly (382/108/57); the preprocessing is fully specified including the RGBA-to-RGB conversion, the 100x100 resize, the greyscale luminance formula, the 299x299 resize for InceptionV3 and the [-1, 1] normalisation; the custom CNN is tabulated layer by layer with kernel counts, sizes and output dimensions at each of five levels; the extraction point in InceptionV3 is named; and the MLP hidden layer sizes, optimiser, learning rate, loss, batch size and epoch count are all given. Not reproducible: the specific train/validation/test split, the random seed, and the mapping from images to children - which is the one piece of information needed to determine whether the evaluation is participant-disjoint. There is also a transcription error in the greyscale formula, where the blue coefficient is given as 0.144 rather than the standard 0.114.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: Better than most conference papers of this length. Reproducible: the three source corpora are public, named and cited with their participant counts and age ranges; every one of the 77 features is named with a definition in a two-column table, including the exact construction of the BERT-cosine coherence measures and the TF-IDF basis of unexpected words; the normalisation of count features over conversation length is stated; the tools are named; the reduction from 77 to 63 features and its SHAP basis is described; the classifier family, kernel and the grid-search-with-5-fold-CV procedure for C and gamma are given; and both the six-classifier comparison and the seven-configuration feature ablation are reported with four metrics each. Not available: code, the split or seed, the identity of the 63 retained features, the per-corpus composition of the training and test sets, the BERT variant, and the AutoML configuration. The stated 90:10 split is also inconsistent with the reported accuracies, all of which are exact multiples of 1/17.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: Sharply uneven. The stimulus design, the per-clip view counts, the rendering resolution and downsampling, the temporal windowing scheme, the velocity formula and colour mapping, the dropout and epoch settings, the split ratios and the image counts for every one of fourteen experimental tables are all specified precisely - so the analysis pipeline is largely reconstructible. Almost everything about the data is not: no eye tracker or acquisition parameters, no diagnostic procedure, no demographics beyond age band and sex, no ethics or consent statement, no mapping from images to participants, no augmentation parameters, no seeds or split specifications, and no code or data. The mapping from images to participants is the single most consequential omission, because without it a reader cannot verify whether any evaluation in the paper is subject-disjoint - and nothing in the text suggests any of them is.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: Extensively reported on the computational side and unverifiable on the numerical side. Reproducible from the text: the public source dataset with participant statistics, stimulus description, eye tracker and native image size; the full preprocessing chain from 640 x 480 colour through 100 x 100 greyscale to a flattened one-dimensional vector, with figures; the complete hyperparameter grids for kernel size, stride, pooling, batch size, optimiser and architecture, each reporting accuracy for every cell; the winning configuration in full; and the software and hardware. Not reproducible: code, the cross-validation implementation and seed, the image-to-child mapping - the one fact needed to assess whether any evaluation is participant-disjoint - and, most seriously, the headline numbers themselves, since the reported accuracy cannot be derived from the reported sensitivity and specificity at the stated class sizes.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Among the best-reported studies in the review, constrained only by data-access restrictions. Fully specified: the cohort definition with birth-year window and minimum follow-up requirement; the two-stage case-ascertainment procedure with counts by route and the acronym-collision and family-member checks; the comparison-group definition with its exclusion logic and the explicit reasoning for excluding Down syndrome but retaining other autism-associated aetiologies; the surveillance protocol with milestone counts by domain and age bin and its Denver Developmental Screening Test basis; the milestone binarisation rule with its stated rationale and its stated cost; the reduction from 100 to 59 features on clinical-relevance grounds; the modelling method, cross-validation scheme and Youden-threshold definition; full confusion counts for four comparator methods; and the SHAP fold-stability analysis. Five supplementary tables and figures carry the complete 100-feature list, training performance by fold, performance at multiple thresholds, and boys-only and no-2019 sensitivity models. The data cannot be released publicly for privacy reasons but a formal request route with a URL is provided. Code is not available and no software is named.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: Reported in outline and internally inconsistent in detail. Available: the dataset composition, the three architectures, the appended layer configuration (1,024 neurons, ReLU, L2 at 0.015, dropout 0.4, softmax output), the RMSprop optimiser, batch size 80, 100-epoch cap with early stopping at patience ten, the augmentation list, and the platform. Unavailable: the Kaggle dataset identifier or version, code, the split assignment or seed, and the image-to-child mapping. Two mutually inconsistent input sizes are given (96 x 96 in the dataset section, 224 x 224 x 3 in the transfer learning section) without reconciliation. The confusion matrix sums to 280 images while the stated validation and test partitions contain 200 and 100. And the order of augmentation relative to partitioning - the single most important procedural fact for interpreting the result - is left ambiguous by the text's ordering of subsections.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: Reported: the dataset with subject and site counts, the four-stage architecture with each component's role and rationale, the Harvard-Oxford atlas, the GAMI-Net formulation as an explicit equation, the 32-dimensional fused latent space, the four baseline comparators, the ablation design, and SHAP and t-SNE analyses with ranked contributions. Not reported: the complete phenotype field list, hyperparameters, imaging preprocessing beyond parcellation, any resolution of the conflicting 70:30 and 20% split descriptions or of the 99.40% versus 96.4% accuracy figures, quality-control exclusions, code, funding and competing interests. The architectural description is detailed enough to reimplement; the experimental description is not detailed enough to reproduce the numbers.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Well specified on protocol and analysis, absent on artefacts. Reproducible: the conversation structure with appendix questions, the 80 cm seating distance, the camera model and sampling rate, the side-view equal-framing convention, the region-of-interest drawing procedure, the 45 s minimum duration criterion, the principle and justification of motion energy analysis, the full list of 23 time scales from 0.1 to 10 s, the pseudo-pair surrogate construction, the four classifiers, the forward feature selection procedure with its fifteen-feature early-stopping cap, the leave-one-out scheme described iteration by iteration, the enumeration of how the 57 derived features were formed (15 + 20 + 15 + 6 + 1 combinations), and the exact composition of the three winning derived features. Not available: code, data, software packages, and any statement of whether forward feature selection was nested within the leave-one-out loop - which for the original-feature result is the one procedural fact a reader would most want.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Strong on conceptual and procedural specification, weaker on artefacts. Reproducible from the text: the participant selection rationale with its critical-period justification, the full diagnostic battery, the ADOS-2 non-spectrum cut-offs applied to the comparison group with observed means, the two elicitation tasks and their ADOS-2 provenance, the Systemic Functional Linguistics annotation scheme with its lexicogrammatical headings, linguistic functions and tag types tabulated at category level, the transfer-comparison method by which the Japanese system network was built, the input construction for each of the four models, all training hyperparameters with the statement that they were not searched, the leave-one-out procedure with the annotation model retrained within each fold, and the evaluation metrics with confidence intervals and McNemar comparisons. Supplementary files carry the tag frequency comparisons. Not available: code, the corpus itself (described in a prior publication rather than deposited), the specific software stack, and any random seed. The annotation scheme's full tag inventory is summarised rather than exhaustively listed in the main text.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Curiously uneven. The feature-extraction pipeline is described at unusual procedural length, narrating library imports, directory traversal, per-image processing, DataFrame construction, label-column addition, merging and CSV export, with exact feature counts tabulated for all eight families. The evaluation is described not at all. A reader is given enough to reconstruct how a 3,315-dimensional feature vector was built and nothing whatever about how the reported accuracies were computed. Also absent: the Kaggle dataset identifier and version, any classifier hyperparameters, any seed, and code.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: Partial. Reported: both corpora by name, CK+'s 327 sequences from 118 individuals, the peak-frame selection rule, the full preprocessing chain with both working resolutions, the quaternion algebra underpinning the optimiser given as explicit Hamilton relations, the three baseline comparators, and t-values and p-values for the comparisons. Not reported: KDEF's sample size, class distributions for either corpus, any train-test split or cross-validation scheme, the swarm optimiser's own population size and iteration count, the network's hyperparameters, how many runs contributed to the reported means, over what units the t-tests were computed, code, funding and competing interests. The mathematical apparatus is documented and the experimental protocol is not.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: Among the strongest in this review, and uniquely so on data. Reproducible from the text: exact recruitment dates, inclusion criteria for both groups, the game platform and task geometry with eight targets at 45-degree spacing, the settings panel contents and the statement that identical settings were used for all participants, the tablet model and its 60-degree tilt, the table-height range and experimenter position, the 20 Hz sampling rate, all three data-inclusion rules including the 20-69 point trajectory-length window, the rotation normalisation written out across three numbered equations with the atan2 construction and the angle-range mapping, both feature sets, the four-fold cross-validation with its 110-sample validation size, the acceleration-variation range for the simulation, and the seven trajectory-simplification rates. The trajectory data are published on GitHub at a stated URL - the only open data release among included studies here, and one that makes the central claim independently checkable. Not reported: the network architectures, training hyperparameters, seeds, and, critically, whether cross-validation folds were constructed by child or by trajectory.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: Sharply divided and instructively so. The computational contribution is documented in detail: the density-factor update equation, the threshold rule switching between artificial bee colony and honey badger updates at alpha = 0.5, the network composition, and all ten evaluation metrics written out as numbered equations with their standard definitions. A reader could reimplement the algorithm. Nothing about the data is available: no sample size, no participants, no collection procedure, no equipment, no task, no label provenance, no code and no dataset. The paper specifies exactly how a number was computed and not at all what it was computed on, which is the inverse of the profile this review has found in the clinically led studies.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Strong on the computational protocol and empty on provenance. Reported: all four datasets with their repositories and instance counts; class distributions for every band; the 80/20 split with absolute partition sizes for all four (843/211, 233/59, 83/21, 563/141); the feature counts before and after dropping two fields; the preprocessing chain of feature selection, categorical encoding and missing-value handling; the baseline and optimised architectures; the Tree-structured Parzen Estimator with an explicit justification for preferring it to grid search; and all six metrics for baseline and optimised models in all four bands. Not reported: search ranges for the optimisation, the partition on which its objective was evaluated, code, and any account of how the class variable in these datasets is derived - which is the one piece of provenance that determines what the results mean.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Well reported. Available from the text: the population, its 99% coverage and the single-age inclusion criterion; the SRS-2 with its sex-specific cut-offs and their published source; the pressure sensor make and size; the webcam model, resolution and frame rate; the 20 Hz synchronised acquisition; OpenPose with its ten joints figured; all sixteen variables named and grouped into three categories; the composition of the three variable sets; the SVM kernel and the cost parameter for each best model; the named variables selected by each model; the leave-one-out scheme; and the statistical software with version. Supplementary materials carry the rationale and calculation method for each explanatory variable and further detail on model construction and evaluation. Not available: code, the dataset, and - the one gap that affects interpretation - whether the joint feature-selection and hyperparameter-optimisation procedure was performed inside or outside the cross-validation loop.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: Better than most of this branch on the computational side and empty on the human side. Fully reported: both dataset URLs, the preprocessing pipeline, the final split sizes for both corpora, the leakage-detection procedure in pseudocode with its cosine thresholds, cluster sweep from 30 to 150 and reassignment rule, the training regime including early stopping with patience 5, checkpointing on best validation loss and learning-rate reduction by a factor of 0.1 on a plateau of 3, the hyperparameter search bounds, the white shark configuration, the hardware and software environment, and the full metric suite with McNemar and paired t-tests. Code is on GitHub and archived on Zenodo with a DOI, which places this paper in the minority of the corpus that permits computational replication. Not reported: the number of distinct individuals behind either image count, any demographic composition, which data partition the hyperparameter fitness was evaluated on, the number of runs behind the reported means, and how the confidence intervals were computed. The stated search dimension of 3 is also inconsistent with the six hyperparameter ranges tabulated.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: Sharply divided. Fully reported: the data source with its URL and a named acknowledgement of the provider, both group sizes and age ranges, the complete electrode montage with ground and reference positions, the filter settings and sampling rate, the recording condition, the count of features and their domain families, all four network architectures with layer sizes and activation functions given as explicit equations, and five performance metrics for each model. Entirely absent: any train-test split, cross-validation scheme or partitioning unit; the number of EEG segments analysed and how they distribute across the 17 participants; the identity of the eleven features; hyperparameters; and any account of how autism was ascertained. A reader could replicate the recording and the architectures and could not evaluate or reproduce the result.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: Strong on the human protocol and thin on the computational one. Fully reported: recruitment sources and window, inclusion and exclusion criteria, the diagnostic procedure and CARS-2 threshold with the count excluded by it, group demographics with matching statistics, the verbatim task instruction including the examiner's response rule, the rapport-building preamble, the toy categories with definitions, the coder training programme - three coders with 3 months to 11 years of relevant experience, one month of training under the manual's authors with weekly review meetings, and an inter-coder consistency check in which all three independently coded the same 30 children, reaching 83.7-91.7% with the reliability formula given - the definitions of all 19 behaviours in a supplementary coding guide, all 81 indicators with definitions, and the complete univariate and multivariate regression output with odds ratios, confidence intervals and p-values. This is enough for another group to run the protocol. Not reported: the coding software, the statistical software, the stepwise selection criterion, the number of bootstrap resamples, and the optimism-corrected AUC that the bootstrap should have produced. Data are available from the corresponding author on request only, with the restriction attributed to data protection and the consent text.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: Strong on the clinical protocol, silent on computation. Reported: the site, the separate recruitment windows, full inclusion and exclusion criteria for each group, the diagnostic procedure with the explicit statement that ADOS-2 and ADI-R were excluded from it, the complete battery administered to each group, the ADOS-2 module with its activity count, duration, item count and both algorithms' cut-offs, the item dichotomisation rule with the psychometric argument for it and a worked example, the non-zero proportions for all 32 items with chi-square tests, the complete regression output including odds ratios and confidence intervals for every domain and every retained item, the prespecified AUC interpretive bands, DeLong's test for the paired ROC comparison, both training and test accuracies from holdout validation, the significance thresholds including a stricter alpha of 0.01 for correlations, the sample size justification by reference to a prior comparable study, and the statistical software with version. Not reported: administrator blinding, within-study inter-rater reliability at item level, the holdout split proportion and whether the split was repeated, and code. Data are available from the corresponding author on request.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Reported: both corpora with their sources and project pages, sample and duration totals, complete partition tables giving class counts for training, development, test, female and male sets under both tasks, the 70/15/15 split proportions, the speaker-disjoint splitting rule with its stated rationale, the two architectures and their pre-training corpora, the decision to upsample the minority class in training while leaving development and test distributions intact, unweighted average recall as the primary metric, the equalised-odds procedure with its sensitivity and specificity formulae, confusion matrices for every model and partition, and comparison tables against a baseline and against published results on the same dataset. Not reported: code, hyperparameters, sample durations, recording equipment and conditions, the number of children per diagnostic class, age distributions by group, any diagnostic procedure for either corpus, and the number of runs behind each figure. Neither corpus is openly available. The partition tables are the strongest element - they let a reader compute the class balance of every evaluation set, which is what makes the fairness results interpretable and what reveals that the gender test sets differ in composition from the mixed-gender set.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: Deliberately partial, with the incompleteness explained rather than concealed. Fully reported: the scraping library, both search queries with their date range, the profile-keyword criterion defining the autism group, the 1,000-per-day sampling rate for controls, the complete preprocessing chain from profanity masking through tokenisation, stop-word removal, stemming and lemmatisation to padding, the full sixteen-item list of removed autism-related keywords, the sentiment tool and the censored-versus-uncensored comparison, the representation methods and model families, the 5-fold cross-validation used for algorithm selection, the 85:15 user-level split for tweet classification with a further 85:15 training-validation division, the 80:20 user split and five-tweet minimum for profile classification, and all corpus counts by group. Not available: the dataset and the trained models, both destroyed, and the code, which is not mentioned. The pipeline is therefore reconstructible and the corpus is not - which is the outcome the authors intend, since re-creating the corpus is the act they argue should not be undertaken without consent.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: Among the strongest reproducibility records in the review, and the only one combining published code with a partial data release. Reported in full: the cohort and its eleven-year recruitment window, group sizes with age and sex, the matching variables for the groups and separately for the train-test split, the exact 50-50 participant split with 40-40 composition per half and the 80-20 internal training-validation division, segment lengths for both modalities with the empirical basis for choosing them, the audio normalisation format and its stated rationale, all five acoustic feature families and the 150-MFCC selection, complete architectures for both networks including LSTM units, dense layer sizes, dropout rate, loss function, optimiser, batch size and epoch count with the observation that larger values overfit, the segment aggregation rule and the 90% confidence filter, all three ensemble strategies including the decision tree's 60% threshold, a complete six-metric table for all five models, and the full interpretability procedure with its three importance metrics and cross-modality normalisation model. Training code for both networks is published on GitHub, and a de-identified subsample of pose-estimation videos is deposited on Zenodo with a DOI. What is unavailable is the raw recordings, and the reason given is correct - they 'contain identifiable features such as faces and voices of participants, and as such cannot be shared integrally'. Cognitive and diagnostic-instrument detail is deferred to supplementary material, and no confidence intervals are given.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: Strong on procedure and empty at the one point that matters most. Well reported: all four datasets with their properties and their categorisation as controlled or uncontrolled, the two SSBD exclusions and the face-observability criterion for frame retention, the annotation protocol with the rater count, training, scale, software modality and supervision, the normalisation equation and the inter-annotator correlation matrix, the split proportions for every dataset, the subject-disjointness rule with per-split child counts and video durations, the complete Perceiver hyperparameter configuration and the evidence that alternatives were tried without gain, the Inception v3 provenance and layer handling, and formal definitions of every metric. Absent: the composition, source and size of the non-autistic image class; the total number of images in any split; code; and the new annotations, which cannot be shared. The first of these is disabling - a reader cannot determine what the classifier's 74.5% is a discrimination between, and the paper's own data-distribution table, which lists SSBD as the sole database across all three splits, is inconsistent with a second class existing at all.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Sharply divided between the signal-processing work, which is well documented, and the clinical work, which is not. Reported: the collection site by name and postal address, the camera and its emissivity setting, image counts by capture context with the number of students in each, age range and sex, the denoising pipeline with PSNR and SSIM evaluation against alternatives, the DN-FME architecture with its eleven convolutional and three dense layers, kernel sizes, parameter count and input resolution, the complete hyperparameter table, two ablation tables with numeric results, the three severity classifiers, the AUC values, all metric formulae and the computation-time comparison. Not reported: the origin of the severity labels; the origin of the facial-mood labels, which someone must have assigned to thermal images of these children and which the paper never mentions; the class distribution across severity levels; whether the 80-20 split respected participants; hyperparameters for the three classifiers; ambient conditions; results from the 20 videos; code; and any ethics or consent arrangements. A reader could reimplement the denoising and the mood network and could not reconstruct or evaluate the severity result at all.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Adequate on the computational side and empty on the human side. Reported: the corpus with class counts and stated age range, the four augmentation parameters with their values, the 80/10/10 split, the image dimensions, the three architectures, the loss, optimiser and epoch cap, complete per-class precision, recall, F1 and support, confusion matrices, and training and validation curves with specific accuracy and loss trajectories. Not reported: the number of distinct children, any demographic composition, whether the split respected individuals, the composition of the evaluation partition in a form reconcilable with the stated split, hyperparameters beyond the epoch cap, and code. The stated claim of a facial-feature importance analysis has no corresponding section.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: Good for a short conference paper, and notably strong on the preprocessing that determines whether cross-corpus features are comparable. Reported: all four source corpora by name with recording protocols where known, the deliberate exclusion of developmentally delayed children, group sizes, the age range, all six features with both their child-alone and ratio definitions and the reason ratios were used, the NLP package, the token-cleaning rules in detail - symbols removed, bracketed and parenthesised tokens removed as unspoken, 'xxx' and '@<letters>' special-form markers stripped because they are used inconsistently across datasets, '&=' tokens removed as non-speech sounds - the seven models with their library provenance, the convolutional architecture layer by layer, the 75/25 split, the 50 repeated splits with the stability criterion that justified that number, and all five metrics with ROC variability bands. Not reported: age and sex composition by diagnostic group, the source corpora's diagnostic procedures, which features were removed before the headline accuracies, and code.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Among the more reproducible computational records in the corpus. Reported: both datasets with public access locations, one with a Dryad DOI and access date; sensor models, joint counts and the difference between the two Kinect generations with a figure; sample counts for both corpora; the exclusion of the non-spectrum class; the complete software stack with version numbers for nine packages; the hardware; optimiser, learning rate and batch size; the epoch schedule with the reason for its extension; the cross-validation scheme with fold sizes and repetition counts stated separately for each dataset, including why DREAM was run three times rather than five; mean, maximum, minimum and standard deviation for every architecture on both datasets; and the specific configuration flag needed to enable Skepxels in the inherited codebase. Not reported: whether DREAM splitting respected participants, any demographic composition, per-class counts for DREAM, sensitivity and specificity, and the authors' own code.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Strong on the human and acoustic protocol, incomplete on the modelling. Reported: the source corpus with citation and public availability, group sizes with exactly matched sex composition, mean ages, the four-stage diagnostic procedure with instruments and clinician qualifications and the stated reason ADOS was unavailable, recorder models and their proportions, the audio format and sampling rate with the rationale, the 25 cm distance instruction, the recording-setting distribution by group, the cry-cause distribution by group, the exclusion rules for pain cries and impure segments, per-child cry yields with standard deviations, the acoustic software and the definitions of the perturbation measures, and the network architecture with layer counts, kernel size, channel count, dropout, augmentation methods, optimiser, cyclic learning-rate bounds, batch size and epoch count. Not reported: any test partition, the split proportions, whether splitting respected participants, the number of cry instances per partition, and code. A reader could reproduce the acoustic analysis and could not evaluate the classification result.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: Partial. Reported: the dataset source, its 704 rows and 21 fields with every field name printed verbatim, the preprocessing stage of cleaning and missing-value handling, a feature-engineering stage guided by exploratory data analysis, the 5-fold cross-validation scheme, the Random Forest classifier and the Bayesian optimisation method. Not reported: which features survived the engineering stage - the single fact needed to determine whether 'result' entered the model - together with the class distribution, hyperparameter search ranges, any metric beyond accuracy, and code. Printing the full field list is nonetheless a useful piece of transparency, since it is what makes the leakage identifiable.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: Sharply divided. The technical protocol is documented well: task types, session duration, total video volume, resolution, frame rate, lighting standardisation, the three MediaPipe models with their landmark counts (468 face, 33 pose, 21 per hand), the composition of the 1,639-value vector with per-component counts, the definitions of the mouth aspect ratio and of motion energy as mean Euclidean landmark displacement between consecutive frames, the complete validation strategy with fold count, stratification rule, subject-independence, early-stopping patience of 10, dropout of 0.5, L2 coefficient of 0.001 and batch shuffling, the network architecture layer by layer with unit counts and activations, the loss function and optimiser, and the metric set with paired t-tests across folds. The human protocol is not documented at all: no recruitment source, no diagnostic procedure, no age distribution by group, no ethics approval and no consent process. A reader could rebuild the pipeline and could not evaluate, replicate or ethically justify the study that produced the data.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: Mixed. Reported: corpus size, class balance and Kaggle location; the split proportions with absolute counts (2,653 training, 279 testing); 100,352 features per image; the library stack with version numbers; the hardware; the classifier family; the cross-validation scheme; a numbered ethics approval; and the GELOPH<15> instrument itself as a supplementary file. Not reported: the number of distinct children in the corpus, any demographic composition, whether splitting respected individuals, any diagnostic ascertainment for either target, hyperparameters for any model, per-class metrics or confusion matrices, and code. A reader could reconstruct the computational pipeline and could not evaluate what it was applied to.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Reported: the corpus with its size and source, all five feature extractors by name, the logistic-regression classifier, the three preprocessing configurations with illustrative sample images, the augmentation parameters with explicit numeric ranges and an explanation of what each does, the software with version, and the hardware. Not reported: class distribution, the number of distinct children, any train-test split or validation arrangement, whether augmentation was applied only to the training partition, hyperparameters, any metric beyond accuracy and a confusion-matrix figure, ethics arrangements, funding and code. The preprocessing description is the most thorough element and is genuinely reusable.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: Better than most of this branch on protocol. Reported: both corpora with their source, the exact partition sizes for both tasks (2,526/280/80 and 703/130), the stratified random sampling procedure with its stated purpose of preserving class proportions, the image quality-filtering criterion requiring a frontal face with eyes, nose and mouth visible, the preprocessing steps, both architectures with their constituent networks and layer types, the baseline comparators, a full six-metric set for each task, confusion matrices, the explicit statement that only one split was used and why, and the training hardware. Not reported: class counts within each partition, the number of distinct children, hyperparameters, code, ethics arrangements, funding and competing interests.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: Adequate on the pipeline and deficient on the corpus. Reported: total image count and exact class balance, both sources by name, the 80:20 split ratio, the preprocessing and augmentation operations (resizing, normalisation, rotation, flipping, contrast adjustment), all five ensemble pairings with their constituent architectures, both combination rules, the softmax-plus-threshold decision structure, four metrics for each pairing, learning curves for each, and a comparison table against prior work. Not reported: the proportion of images from each source and their distribution across classes, the number of distinct children, whether augmentation preceded splitting, hyperparameters, per-class error breakdowns, ethics arrangements, funding and code.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Partial and, on the decisive points, poor. Reproducible: the source dataset is openly archived on figshare with a resolvable URL, and the preprocessing sequence is narrated step by step. Not reproducible: no code, no software or version names, no random seed, no complete hyperparameter specification, no statement of the mutual-information threshold or scores that produced exactly 16 features, no per-fold row counts, and no per-child row counts. A reader cannot verify whether the 16 selected features are the same ones the mutual-information ranking would yield on their machine, nor reconstruct the folds.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Mixed, with one notable strength. The authors manually rebuilt the TPOT-selected pipeline using the exact reported parameters to verify that the automated result was reproducible - a deliberate replication step that almost no other study in this corpus performs, and the paper's best methodological instinct. Against that: the dataset is not deposited, no code is released, no library versions or random seed are given, the single 80/20 split is unseeded, the participant counts do not reconcile, and two different accuracies (78% and 0.83) appear for the same experiment.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: Low. Positives: the source dataset is publicly linked, the split ratio is stated, and the main optimisation settings are listed. Negatives dominate: no code, no seed, no software versions, no architectural specification sufficient to rebuild CNN-ASAM or the GECN, no landmark count, no XGBoost parameters, no identification of which 200 test images produced the headline numbers, and a Table 1 whose annotations have no reconstructible source. Independent replication is impossible in principle, not merely inconvenient.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Mixed. The acquisition protocol is reported in enough detail to be repeated - device, sampling rate, calibration procedure, stimulus, display parameters, eligibility criteria - and the four feature sets and their ablation are fully specified, so the study's most interesting result could be re-tested. Everything downstream is opaque: no code, no seed, no MATLAB version, no convolutional architecture, no epoch count, no fold count for the cross-validation that is repeatedly asserted but never reported, and no access route for the 4,000-image dataset the paper announces as a contribution for researchers and developers to leverage. A further reproducibility concern is the literature review, which contains a run of citations on building energy consumption, distributed generation, solar-equipped neighbourhoods and electric vehicles - and the abbreviation list correspondingly defines DB as Design builder, DG as Distributed generation and ICME as Integrated Computational Materials Engineering. These belong to a different paper and indicate that portions of the manuscript were assembled rather than written for this study.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: Very low. Some preprocessing choices are specified with real precision - rotation range -15 to 15 degrees, horizontal flips, random crops to 10%, brightness 0.8 to 1.2, inverse-frequency class weights, Z-score channel normalisation - and the source dataset is properly cited with an access date. Everything needed to actually rebuild the system is missing: no code, no libraries, no seed, no image size, no layer configuration, no ensemble combination rule, no CPO search space or budget, no split specification, and a stated sample size that the reported confusion matrices contradict.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Very low, and internally contradictory on a basic point. The preprocessing section states that each feature is preserved in its original, continuous form without normalization and then, one paragraph later, that the MinMax scaler was employed for scaling and the dataset normalised; the pseudocode also calls MinMaxScaler. The dataset is described as openly available on Mendeley but is given no name, DOI or URL, and the formal data-availability statement instead says the data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. Code is available on demand only. No split ratio, no seed, no client partition rule, no layer widths, no learning rate, no epochs. The paper also refers to Pearson correlation analysis by the abbreviation PCA, which elsewhere denotes principal component analysis.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: The most sharply divided reproducibility profile in the corpus. The data side is exemplary: room dimensions, temperature, humidity, lighting, session hours, camera body, ISO, aperture, exposure, capture and output resolution, subject distance, curtain arrangement, expression protocol, per-child photograph counts and the verbatim augmentation configuration are all published, so another laboratory could recreate the acquisition closely. The model side is empty: no architecture, no layer specification, no optimiser, no learning rate, no batch size, no epoch count, no seed, no code, and no deposit for the dataset that the paper exists to introduce. The internal contradictions between narrative and Table I further undercut the acquisition detail, and the survival of stunted child in the workflow description indicates text carried over from an unrelated manuscript.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: The strongest reporting in this review's questionnaire branch, with one structural gap. The dataset is public and cited; the preprocessing sequence is given step by step in order; the split proportions and the exact test-set composition (292 cases: 148 ASD, 144 non-ASD) are stated; and Table I lists every tuned hyperparameter for all six classifiers to four significant figures, including C = 635.2340 and alpha = 0.0002816. Against that: no code, no seed, no versions, and - most consequentially - the number of features chi-square retained is never given, the selected features are never listed, and whether selection was fitted inside or outside the split is never stated.
