Nothing is said about the image-level split on a dataset with repeated images per child, about the 55-image test set, about the absence of any description of the underlying task, or about the fact that three architectures trained on the same data under the same protocol span 78% to 100%.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: Two sentences, both concerning the model rather than the study: the reliance on the Yeo-Johnson transformation for noise removal may not be sufficient for all types of data, and the complexity of the model may lead to overfitting, especially with smaller datasets. Notably, the article contains an extensive limitations apparatus pointed at other people's work - Table 1 tabulates the advantages and disadvantages of each prior study, and the related-work section names constraints for several of them - while none of that scrutiny reaches the circular label, the unreported sample size, the absent validation protocol or the Not Applicable ethics declaration.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: A genuinely analytical limitations section with five distinct items, each carrying a mechanism: diagnosis-based grouping cannot exclude undiagnosed cases; the PD and control groups come from a generation in which autism diagnoses were not prevalent, so undiagnosed autistic people may be present in them; stylus resistance and tablet sampling and spatial resolution may have suppressed group differences relative to motion tracking; kinematic features are context-dependent and the results may be task-specific; and the autistic sample was older than those in the existing kinematic literature, so apparent contradictions with prior findings may be age effects. Two further issues go unstated: the classification test partitions contain roughly 13 to 19 participants, and the discriminatory feature sets were selected using group-difference tests computed on all participants.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: This is the study's defining characteristic and the reason it matters to the review. The scope restriction is not confined to a closing limitations paragraph but is stated in the abstract, the contributions list, the labelling section, the training section and the results discussion. Its clearest formulation is in section 3.3: because the severity labels are deterministically derived from the same behavioural attributes used as model inputs, the subsequent prediction task constitutes a structured function-approximation setting; accordingly, high classification performance should be interpreted as evidence of the proposed model's ability to learn stable and interpretable behavioural scoring functions, rather than as proof of clinical diagnostic accuracy. It further states that the labelling kappa supports internal consistency while not implying external diagnostic validity, that SHAP results carry no causal or diagnostic attribution, that performance gains are methodological improvements rather than evidence of clinical diagnostic superiority, and that the datasets are behaviourally constrained. What remains unstated: that the domain weights were calibrated on the full dataset before cross-validation, that SHAP-based feature pruning requires a fitted model and was likewise performed on the full data, that no class counts are reported, and that the ablation credits SHAP with a 0.002 accuracy gain when SHAP is a post-hoc explanation method that cannot alter a model's predictions.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: Two sentences, both about deployment: the framework depends on the availability and quality of multimodal datasets, which may vary across clinical settings, and repeated unlearning operations can incur overhead at scale. Neither addresses the evidence. Unmentioned: the contradictory sample sizes, the three different age ranges, the absence of any diagnostic label description, the absence of any numeric result table for the headline accuracy, the majority-class baseline implied by the reported class ratio, and the fact that the experiments are described as simulations.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: The paper announces that it will discuss its weaknesses, and the only self-directed remarks concern the data - that SSBD is the sole freely available dataset of its kind, that it is somewhat helpful but does not fully meet the study's conditions, and that no existing dataset does. Against that, a full column of Table 1 assigns a specific limitation to each of eleven prior studies (did not describe the pre-processing and model development steps; need to improve results; implemented a basic CNN model that performs binary classification and was tested on a small dataset). Unmentioned for this study: that folds are formed over clips from 75 videos with no video-level or child-level grouping; that the number of distinct children is unknown; that there is no non-autistic comparison group behind a screening claim; that no ethics statement accompanies the reuse of identifiable children's home videos; and that per-class counts and the chance level are unreported.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: A dedicated limitations section naming three constraints - small sample for specific modality/phase pairings limiting generalisation and increasing overfitting risk; the context-specific storytelling task potentially not transferring to other situations; and predefined AOIs and fixed time intervals limiting analytic granularity - plus a separate section on cultural and linguistic constraints addressing the Castilian/Valencian bilingual environment, and a further section (7.3) that positions the work explicitly against clinical viability benchmarks. The self-assessment is distributed through the discussion rather than confined to a closing paragraph, and it is accurate. The one limitation not raised is the substantial receptive-vocabulary difference between groups, which is measured, reported, and then not adjusted for in a task built on comprehending narrated stories.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: No limitations section appears in the extracted text. A comparison table instead assigns a named limitation to each of roughly fifteen prior studies (few participants, results may not apply widely; tested only in lab settings, not in daily life situations; works best only on similar data, not tested in real-world settings). None of that scrutiny is turned inward. Unmentioned: that four autism instruments sit in Dataset 1's feature set alongside the autism label; that Dataset 2's split partitions augmented copies rather than original samples; that Dataset 2's test partition holds 40 samples against 4,220 features; that Dataset 2 contains no non-ASD class, so its 98.2% is four-class severity rather than detection; that the 63.28% majority-class baseline on Dataset 1 is never stated; and that Dataset 2 has no provenance.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Distributed through the discussion rather than isolated, and unusually incisive. The paper states that the unmatched sample's higher accuracy is inflated by including age and gender as features and that the matched estimate should be preferred; that the feature ranking may not generalise across participant ages; and that the work represents initial efforts with limits on what can be concluded. Its most valuable limitation, though, is directed outward and applies to a large part of this review's corpus: it notes that studies reporting higher accuracy did so either by using the AQ-10 items to predict whether participants fell above or below an AQ cut-off score rather than whether they received an official diagnosis, or by using groups that were not balanced on demographic features included as predictors - and that this risks sampling biases inflating performance, which the authors accounted for through their matched analysis. That is a precise, published statement of the two mechanisms this review has documented across the questionnaire branch.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: Stated plainly and correctly, in the discussion rather than in a boilerplate paragraph: although the framework achieved high accuracy, it was evaluated on a single small-scale dataset of 28 participants, which limits the statistical generalizability of the findings, so the reported results should be interpreted as a proof-of-concept demonstration pending validation on larger and more diverse populations. That is the right reading of a 28-person study and it is offered without hedging. What is not raised: that the fold-wise standard deviations (0.08 on accuracy, 0.095 on F1) are large precisely because each fold holds five or six people; that no demographic, task or diagnostic information about the source cohort is reported; and that the within-subject resampling step is not located relative to the split.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: None for this study. The literature table (Table 2) is unusually thorough in the opposite direction, assigning each of roughly ten prior works a named weakness - limited dataset diversity and challenges generalizing to real-world conditions; overfitting risk with limited data; overfitting in small datasets and poor generalization; low model interpretability and high training time; small and limited dataset, lack of clinical validation, no multimodal analysis. Every one of those applies to the present study and none is claimed by it. Unmentioned: the absent class counts and split ratios, the unstated number of distinct children, the impossible mAP relationship, and the fact that a model trained to detect autism from a face assigned a class label to a dog.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: One stated limitation, and it is the right one: the dataset lacks demographic information, expression patterns and facial morphology vary across demographic factors, and their influence on classification and feature learning therefore cannot be examined - with future work directed at demographically different datasets to assess fairness and generalisability. Within the facial-image branch this is the clearest statement of the problem that undermines all sixteen of its members. What is not stated: that the labels have no diagnostic basis, that the split is at the image level on a corpus that repeats individuals, that the testing-phase accuracy exceeds the training-phase accuracy, that the epoch counts disagree, and that the ethics and data-availability declarations contradict the article's own contents.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: The most thorough and self-critical limitations discussion in the charted corpus, and the only one in which the paper's own headline result is dismantled by its author. The severe-class analysis is described as the most critical limitation of the study; the reason no real data exist is explained; the synthetic-generation method is named; and the consequence is stated in full - that the reported 100% reflects the model's ability to distinguish between real moderate ASD motor data and an artificially constructed distribution, not between true clinical severity levels. The author further notes that the extremely wide confidence interval indicates high statistical uncertainty and that a single misclassification would reduce recall to 75%, sets a minimum target of 20 to 50 real severe-ASD cases for future work, and states that the two test sets are reserved subsets from the same data distribution rather than independent external validation. The one limitation not raised is the provenance of the severity labels themselves.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Substantive and mostly well aimed. Stated: the small size and limited diversity of the corpora, particularly the narrow 3-6 year age range; the absence of prosodic information - pitch, rhythm, intonation - which text cannot represent and which is indicative of atypical speech in autism, an honest acknowledgement that the privacy advantage carries an information cost; the risk of overfitting given 48 and 38 participants, addressed by a quantified train-validation comparison; and the markedly lower performance on the three-class task, read as showing that features specific to developmental delay are needed to reduce misdiagnosis risk. Not stated: that the ASD and TD groups in the Nadig corpus differ in mean age by roughly two years and that age is one of the four features the paper identifies as carrying the signal.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: One of the fullest threats-to-validity sections in the corpus, with six distinct items: small sample size as a major constraint on generalisation given the variability among individuals with ASD; convenience sampling as a source of selection bias restricting profile diversity and compromising external validity; the restriction of scope to ASD signs alone, with each exclusion criterion enumerated and justified; overfitting risk from the reduced sample; the absence of longitudinal data, with repeated collections recommended; and the ethical implications of school-based screening including stigmatisation risk. The one thing not identified is the thing that governs the result: that 640 sessions come from 12 children and are partitioned by session. The paper instead argues in the opposite direction, stating that the high accuracy observed in the models and the robust metrics reinforce the low likelihood of overfitting - which reads a symptom as reassurance.

questions.question_text: Which future directions do the authors state?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Include toddlers with other non-ASD language development disorders to test specificity; extend the acoustic analysis to the 9- and 12-month assessments.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Replicate in a larger sample with a truly held-out dataset; extend to females, high-functioning children and adults; also train against chronological-age-matched controls; collect full ADOS to correlate kinematics with clinical severity; add other neurodevelopmental conditions to test ASD specificity; guide follow-up neuroimaging or genetic work on the identified phenotype.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: None proposed. The conclusion summarises results only and states no open questions or future directions.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Validate and replicate on larger samples; run longitudinal high-risk-infant studies to test whether infant face-processing predicts later symptom severity; refine the algorithm and determine the minimum number of eye-movement features needed for clinical use; extend to other stimuli (social and non-social) and other tasks; and combine face-scanning with brain activity, skin conductance, speech, motion, body gestures and facial expressions in a multimodal risk measure. The paper is an early and explicit call for multimodal ASD prediction.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Apply the method to freely generated rather than prompted verbal material; adopt more theory-driven models to improve sensitivity and specificity; incorporate word ordering and phrase-level correlations; recruit more women with ASD; develop analyses that separate structural-language, social-language and compensatory mechanisms so interventions can be tailored; conduct longitudinal studies to establish clinical importance; combine with functional neuroimaging to test neural correlates of semantic similarity; and build real-time clinical visualisation of where a patient's descriptions sit in semantic space.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Test differentiation between ASD and other developmental psychopathologies (developmental coordination disorder, ADHD) - framed as 'the ultimate clinical question'; substantiate with a larger, more generalised population and test whether the algorithms transfer or need retraining; apply the paradigm to younger, not-yet-diagnosed children; couple gameplay with other psychometric tests, with the face-forward camera for social-intelligence and emotional-reaction measures, and with sensorised toys; and shift toward individual functional assessment rather than broad diagnostic categorisation.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Expand to more complex, full-body motor functions; train on larger groups to improve generalisation across ASC heterogeneity; compare against developmental coordination disorder and ADHD to test whether motor profiles are shared or distinct; investigate motor subgroups within autism and their implications for daily living and therapy; and design future imitation experiments around actions dissimilar to the observer's existing repertoire, since that is what maximised group differences here - a concrete, actionable design recommendation rather than a generic call for more data.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: None proposed. The conclusion asserts high potential for facial expressions to predict ADHD, ASD 'and other neurodevelopmental disorders' but sets out no specific research programme, no validation plan and no open questions - unusual even by the standards of a short conference paper.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Larger and more fine-grained studies; systematic comparison of alternative acoustic feature sets; alternative feature pre-processing such as bag-of-words representations; and other deep learning architectures. The authors also sketch the intended deployment scenario - early preventative judgements from vocalisations captured during routine paediatric examinations in the first year of life - which frames the eventual clinical target rather than a research step.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Apply the GAN-based system to other health tasks such as depression detection; extend GAN representation learning to other behavioural signals including video descriptors and to physiological signals such as electrocardiogram and electrodermal activity; and compare and combine GAN-based feature learning with alternative unsupervised representation-learning approaches such as bag-of-words. All the proposed directions are methodological rather than clinical - no validation, replication or population-extension work is proposed.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Two directions only: deeper exploration of kinematic and kinetic gait parameters beyond ground reaction forces, and evaluation on a larger dataset. No proposals for external validation, for comparison against other motor-affected conditions, or for addressing the demographic and methodological gaps.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Test on more children for higher accuracy and confidence; study child-parent interaction during screening sessions; develop a more robust protocol to cut image-processing cost and complexity; exploit the front camera for facial emotion and other features; and integrate with other intelligent screening approaches. The last of these follows directly from their own finding that the method misclassifies shy typically developing children, so it is a limitation-driven rather than generic proposal.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Larger-sample validation; extension to other populations, particularly young infants, where early detection would matter most; determination of whether the effect is age-group specific; direct head-to-head comparison of this short paradigm against established longer paradigms; and combination of the short paradigm with other paradigms. The authors also state a general principle rather than a research step - that current ASD biomarkers including eye tracking are supplementary and not replacements for clinical assessment.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Develop a speaker diarization algorithm suited to everyday monitoring conditions, named as important future work because the absence of diarization degrades both acoustic and linguistic analysis; incorporate age and gender to enable age- and gender-dependent fine-grained inference; and extend beyond screening to evaluating intervention effectiveness and tracking child development over time.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Design tasks specifically intended to amplify visual-processing differences between groups, since the present stimuli were repurposed; explore capturing the same differences without an eye tracker at all, using operation logs, mouse clicks, task accuracy and miss rate, so that screening could run on ordinary hardware; develop a serious game for large-scale accessible screening; extend the gaze-classifier approach to other conditions with visual attention differences such as dementia, schizophrenia and ADHD; and confront the ethical implications of profiling for clinical conditions from web behaviour.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Exploit the intention labels already in the dataset to test whether intention classification itself is altered in ASD, which could provide an additional diagnostic cue; and refine the spatial attention model to more finely inspect the kinematic discriminants in the gestures. Both are concrete and grounded in the existing data rather than generic calls for larger samples.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: No autism-specific future work is proposed. The methodological conclusion is that the technique 'could be used in other problems in which one needs to compare two sets of eye movement sequences in terms of their temporal features', positioning the contribution as a general tool for eye-movement research rather than an autism screening development.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Extend classification from ASD-versus-TD to ASD-versus-other-conditions, specifically ADHD; apply machine learning to adjacent problems such as engagement evaluation; integrate genetic, neurological, psychological and kinematic features toward automated objective diagnosis, while acknowledging the open problem of selecting relevant features from a very large pool; and develop ways to quantify higher-level restricted and repetitive behaviour such as circumscribed interest, which accelerometer and Kinect approaches to stereotyped movement cannot capture.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Engineer features that directly capture semantic and pragmatic appropriateness turn by turn, since that is what human raters used and the model lacked; enlarge the dataset to improve performance and enable real-world deployment; and test whether longer conversations (10 rather than 5 minutes) and designated topics improve performance. All three are grounded in specific observed shortfalls rather than generic.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Extend to more subjects across a wider span of developmental ages; build a multimodal classifier incorporating demographic information, autonomic nervous system measures, functional MRI and other methodologies; and apply the same paradigm to schizophrenia and ADHD, which also show altered gaze patterns in visual tasks - a differential-diagnosis direction that addresses the specificity question left open by ASD-versus-TD designs.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Expand to larger samples across Bangladesh and other low-resource settings; recruit raters who share the children's linguistic and sociocultural background, hypothesised to close the performance gap with US results; accumulate a large annotated video corpus so that convolutional and recurrent networks can learn features directly from raw video and audio rather than from human annotations; and use location-tagged videos to generate epidemiological prevalence estimates that could inform policy and resource allocation - a public-health framing of future work that is unique in this corpus.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Incorporate object semantics - the type of object fixated rather than merely whether a fixation fell on an object - motivated by evidence that ASD subjects look at the mouth rather than the eye region of faces; and study in depth which areas of fixation coverage ASD subjects miss, on the argument that what fails to attract attention may be as diagnostic as what attracts it. The discussion additionally implies, without stating it as a formal direction, that features must be adapted by participant age.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Run more clinical sessions to obtain data on child engagement and verbal activity during robot-administered tasks, which would enable richer reward models, permit evaluation of the robot's task-selection policy, and allow belief-based classification to be compared against conventional classifiers that currently cannot be trained for lack of data; continue developing social cue detection toward full autonomy; increase the number of protocol tasks; and investigate whether children behave differently when diagnostic tasks are administered by a robot rather than a human examiner - a question that bears directly on whether robot-administered protocols measure the same construct as clinician-administered ones.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Replicate with larger datasets to validate the machine-learning performance, and apply and compare other classification techniques against SVM. Both are generic; no specific validation design, population extension or deployment study is proposed.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Extend the approach to kinematic data from more complex movement imitation tasks, with preliminary results described as promising - which is exactly what the same group's 2020 Scientific Reports paper in this corpus goes on to do; and validate the models on newly collected independent data to establish robustness, directly addressing the absence of external validation.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: No dedicated future-work section. The limitations imply that longer video scenarios should be tested, and the conclusion suggests the scanpath-visualisation approach may generalise to comparable diagnostic problems and to other psychological disorders. No proposals for participant-level validation, larger or independent samples, or addressing the demographic reporting gaps.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Apply the trained algorithm to a completely new and larger dataset, and test transdiagnostic specificity across different psychiatric disturbances; combine multiple non-verbal communication parameters with clinical data such as questionnaires to improve prediction and detect cross-domain associations; extend to eye-gaze and facial expression; and move toward fully automated computer-vision pose and gaze estimation to remove the manual region-of-interest step - while cautioning that such tools' validity against standard motion capture is not yet demonstrated and that they vary in susceptibility to tracking failure and in the video types they support.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Completion of recruitment and comparison of the blinded classifications against medical diagnosis, with dissemination through peer-reviewed publication and conferences. For the review, the protocol's value is that it specifies in advance what a credible answer would look like, which makes any eventual result interpretable in a way that retrospective studies cannot be.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: None proposed. The paper closes by noting the validation-to-test performance gap and its possible causes without setting out future work, consistent with its four-page challenge-entry format.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Combine RGB and audio modalities alongside pose to improve accuracy; and develop a 3D-trajectory version of the PoTion representation to add spatial information to the pipeline. Both are technical extensions; no validation, population-characterisation or participant-level evaluation work is proposed, despite these being the study's principal gaps.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: Extension of the framework to the other behavioural features the paper names as within its reach - 'eye contact, stereotyped movements of the head, concentration and excessive interest in objects or events' - and continued development of the reasoning module that closes the loop between measurement and robot behaviour. The steps the study most needs are counterbalancing the mediator order, establishing diagnostic status for both groups, validating the automated attention estimates against human coding, and a sample capable of supporting a statistical claim.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Investigate and integrate attention mechanisms into the architecture; explore incorporating additional image features; and - notably - 'a thorough investigation on the differences in the scanpaths between ASD and TD children will also be conducted', an explicit acknowledgement that the model was built and evaluated without establishing what behavioural difference it is exploiting.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: Three directions, two of them named as limitations and one as an engineering output. Compare autistic children's robot interaction against that of typically developing children - subsequently done. Observe interactions with children who have other developmental disorders, to address the differential-diagnosis problem the paper identifies as the hardest. And apply the collected user requirements and evaluation criteria to robot design, which the paper treats as a research product in its own right.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Expand the sample, especially the N-ASD group, to verify the model on children who resolve off the spectrum; make identifying N-ASD from ASD an explicit objective; develop more effective machine-learning models; repeat the analysis under controlled physiological and psychological ages to address the age-matching problem; and develop the still-face paradigm into a convenient, objective and standardised self-screening mode usable at home.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Not set out as a discrete future-work section in the extracted text. The introduction's framing implies the priority - the paper notes that adult diagnostic instruments 'have only been validated for use with children', that with adults 'clinicians rarely rely on standardised diagnostic methods making diagnosis less accurate, more subjective and lengthier', and that researching adult diagnostic criteria is listed among the top ten priorities by a UK autism research charity. The work positions itself as contributing quantitative tests to supplement current qualitative ones in that under-served context.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: Test the system in a large number of cooperating hospitals; collect far more facial expression data from both typically developing and autistic children and build a dedicated children's facial expression database, since existing databases are built mainly from adults and children have rounder faces, larger eyes and less prominent bones that make their features harder to recognise; extend the system to recognise physical movement so autism can be assessed from multiple perspectives; and add severity grading into severe, moderate and mild.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Increase the sample size and analyse more postural control data and features, with the expectation of better classification performance. No proposals for external validation, comparison against other developmental conditions, or clinical deployment are made.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Increase participant numbers and add repeated interaction sessions, which the authors expect will grow the dataset rapidly and may then favour the CNN over simpler classifiers; incorporate physiological, eye gaze and vocal data to represent ASD behaviours more comprehensively and improve network reliability; and extend the approach to other naturalistic interactions such as play at home, where much larger datasets could be obtained - a direction the authors argue is enabled specifically by the absence of obtrusive sensors and movement restriction.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Improve scalability by exploring capture technologies beyond Kinect, whose motion-tracking imperfections currently require time-consuming manual processing. The authors also frame CAMI as a candidate biomarker 'for defining biologically meaningful ASC subtypes and guiding intervention', and note it can 'track performance during interventions designed to improve social-communicative function through imitation training' - positioning it as a measurement instrument for intervention research rather than only a diagnostic tool.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: Increase the volume of infant speech data; refine the acoustic features and the auto-encoder architecture; adopt deeper and more current model structures, since the authors expect the auto-encoder's redistributed feature map to pay off more in complex models than in the deliberately small BLSTM used here; extend the approach to children aged 3-4 who can produce several sentences, adding linguistic features to acoustic ones; and generalise beyond autism to the detection of developmental delay.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Include objective measures of intra-subject gait variance directly in the feature vectors, on the basis of the observed greater variability in autistic subjects; pair variance reduction with synthetic data generation for the minority class to counter the imbalance that averaging exacerbates and the overfitting seen in the SVM; and examine more generally when the loss of dataset size outweighs the gain from reduced variance.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: Incorporate automatic speaker diarization to remove the manual annotation step and enable a fully automated system; extend from clinic recordings to long home recordings of the kind LENA collects; adopt a longitudinal design testing which speech features are informative at which developmental periods; and reassess the anomalous finding that more severely affected children responded faster rather than slower.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: Develop a serious game that captures visual processing differences without a dedicated eye tracker; move to behavioural data collected in natural environments; test whether aggregating more simple Search tasks beats designing more complex ones, since complexity did not help; and apply the approach to other conditions with atypical attention patterns - dementia, schizophrenia, ADHD. The authors frame three prerequisites: what makes a good discriminating task, how to record outside the laboratory, and how to do so ethically.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: Larger-scale replication with attention to class balance; extension from binary identification to severity scoring; protocol improvements to hold children's attention and increase the proportion of valid data; incorporation of fixation duration, which the authors observe 'most identification models have ignored'; replacement of fixed-length piece encoding with recurrent networks able to consume variable-length scanpaths directly; and transfer of the framework to other recognition tasks including other diseases, gender and age.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Larger samples permitting a held-out test set and better coverage of autism's heterogeneity; comparison groups with other neurodevelopmental conditions involving movement impairment - ADHD and intellectual disability are named - specifically so that 'taking also into account different neurodevelopment conditions could improve the specificity of the classifiers for ASD rather than for neurodevelopment disorders in general'; matching on IQ, cognitive ability and motor comorbidity; and counterbalanced stimulus orders stratified by functioning level.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: Fuse scores and features from multiple complementary automated protocols - response to name and joint attention are named as the natural partners - to move from a single-aspect indicator to a composite screen, and address the distinction between spontaneous and socially responsive smiling that accounts for most remaining scoring error.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: Extend group sparsity to bi-level, hierarchical, tree-structured and overlapping group definitions so that paradigms can be organised into nested subgroups; replace expert-annotated event windows with data-driven identification of the informative time periods within stimuli; expand the sample to characterise heterogeneity, since limited power constrains severity prediction; design stimuli specifically for predicting ADOS, SRS and Vineland rather than reusing paradigms built for group separation, and develop modelling techniques suited to those outcomes; and test the robustness of selected stimuli on larger unseen data.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: Recruit younger children, aged two years or under, to address the clinical need for earlier diagnosis; and extract additional features from both EEG and eye tracking, since 'multi-modal, multi-feature fusion will likely improve classification accuracy further'.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Move acquisition into the home, with four named prerequisites: large-scale in-home data acquisition, augmented reality platforms with robust native eye tracking, game design for at-home analysis platforms, and clearly defined measurable experimental parameters. Extend feasibility testing to younger children. Balance cohorts for age and gender. And solve a human-computer interaction problem the authors state precisely - producing 'appropriate user interfaces and games that homogenize use in ways so as to lower the natural variability of measurement', since follow-up Superpower Glass studies showed heterogeneity in less-restricted collection. They also note that later generations of the system dropped the eye tracker entirely because of bulkiness and calibration issues, and expect native gaze tracking in commercial AR devices to resolve this.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: Compare SIT behaviour against a live face-to-face condition with the same topic and script to validate the simulation; make the actress's responses adaptive to participants' answer lengths; provide interaction partners matched on gender, age or ethnic background since similarity enhances mimicry; add automated camera and microphone checks and evaluate accuracy in home settings, since self-administration often diminishes accuracy; use state-of-the-art eye tracking to establish whether gaze carries information in this paradigm; and test sensitivity and specificity in larger clinical samples spanning other psychiatric conditions, since social interaction deficits are common to psychosis, depression, bipolar disorder and substance use disorders.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: Retain more than six input features, since filtering may have discarded useful signal; move the model out of Azure ML Studio to permit tuning of node count, leaf count and tree depth; and expand beyond 108 participants for a more diverse and robust classifier better able to handle edge cases.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: None stated. The conclusion asserts the model's usefulness without identifying required replication, larger samples, per-child validation, or the reconciliation of its own tables.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Enlarge the dataset so that class balance can be achieved with real rather than synthetic samples; automate region-of-interest identification to remove the therapist from the loop and speed the method; and explore alternative machine learning approaches including genetic algorithms for meta-classifier construction. The authors also note the approach generalises to any joint attention video provided a therapist marks the first and last frame of each region.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: Improve the accuracy and stability of the eye-tracking hardware and address VR acceptability among autistic participants; enlarge both samples to reduce small-sample bias; involve a specialist psychologist in scene construction since social stimuli do not automatically discriminate; and design multiple scenes and select the most discriminative.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Test dynamic directional cues; establish whether the method distinguishes autism from attention deficits, given that the attention-sustaining phase may be doing much of the work; recruit balanced numbers of girls and boys to test sex-specific performance; and treat base-rate constraints seriously when comparing automated classification against clinical diagnosis.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Collect more samples to permit meaningful comparison against existing diagnostic methods, and establish whether the clap-prediction feature is genuinely diagnostic given its weak observed correlation.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: None stated beyond the general remark that the approach 'holds potentials in the applications when concerning fusing much more data sources'.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Test the method with different visual inputs to validate which features are genuinely relevant rather than paradigm-specific; extend the age range beyond 3-16 given that autism is lifelong; enlarge the sample and address the sex imbalance; and incorporate intelligence quotient as an additional model feature.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Validate on a larger autistic sample varying in severity with balanced sex ratio; include other clinical conditions such as developmental delay and ADHD; recruit younger children, citing a meta-analytic mean diagnosis age of 60.48 months overall and 43.18 months among children aged 10 or under; develop contactless calibration-free gaze recording, citing recent webcam-plus-computer-vision work whose accuracy was comparable to manual coding; generate richer gaze features including fixation counts, entropy, revisits and oculomotor performance; and combine eye tracking with kinematic, EEG and neuroimaging data.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: None stated.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: A larger cohort spanning different ages with analysis of socio-cognitive and cognitive profiles alongside gaze; autism-specific data augmentation methods; longer video scenarios for richer gaze representation; adaptation of more recent deep network methodologies; and, more broadly, transfer of the approach to other neurodevelopmental disorders. The authors also identify the field-level need for a benchmark dataset, which their own open release partly addresses.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Continue building the dataset toward public release, with the observation that assembling eye-tracking signals alongside expert clinical evaluation 'is not a trivial task'; evaluate further machine learning techniques and additional features; and extend from case-control comparison to discrimination between two disorders, specifically naming autism versus ADHD - the differential question the corpus almost never addresses.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: Larger samples with testing on an independent dataset; treatment of sociodemographics, IQ and cognitive ability as moderators; refinement of areas of interest to include eyes and mouth, and adoption of a bottom-up data-driven definition rather than predefined macro-areas; development of a portable system with integrated remote eye tracking to replace glasses that young children may reject and a CAVE that is prohibitively expensive to assemble; and inclusion of other neurodevelopmental conditions such as ADHD to sharpen discrimination and characterise severity gradations.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Larger and more behaviourally varied samples given autism's heterogeneity; investigation of unintentional rather than instructed head nodding and shaking, to test whether reduced gesture use appears only in spontaneous contexts; and extension to younger children, with the argument that constraint-free computer vision is particularly suited to early screening since data can be collected in natural settings without worn devices or task instructions.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: None stated.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Measure intellectual disability as a source of inter-subject variability affecting motor planning and coordination; include developmental coordination disorder and ADHD comparison groups to test whether impaired synergies represent 'a common pathogenetic mechanism for these conditions' rather than an autism-specific marker; and extend the synergy framework to speech and language, on the argument that 'speech and language coordination share key similarity with upper limb action' and that language difficulties are common in autism.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: The authors propose sharing assessment data 'locally, within the same team or clinic, or globally as integrated clinical dataset sharable by professionals in different places through interoperable systems', and continued development of semi-autonomous adaptive robots that recognise behavioural cues and respond accordingly. The steps the study most needs are a control condition to separate intervention effect from familiarisation, an account of attrition, a chance-corrected agreement statistic with clustering adjustment, and reliability data for the therapist ratings.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Expand the dataset; build a mobile application for clinicians; maintain historical records and raise mental health awareness; and strengthen trait correlations with more data. The authors add two cautions that function as recommendations - that the model requires professional supervision in use, and that the dataset is local and should not be transferred to other populations without consultation.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: Compare voice-only against language-only analysis on the same participants and test whether combining them helps, building on the group's parallel work applying natural language processing to ADOS-2 transcripts from this same sample; develop these measures as treatment outcome measures given 'a recognized dearth of outcome measures available for treatment research in autism', which requires longitudinal demonstration of sensitivity to change; and extend to preverbal toddlers at risk and to young children with minimal or no language, where the authors note identification of atypical voice patterns 'might enhance diagnostic procedures'.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Two directions, both specific. Condition the feature set on participant age, given the age-dependence documented in the Discussion - though this requires demographic metadata the benchmark does not supply. And invert the analytic target by studying the regions of an image that autistic viewers fail to cover rather than those they fixate, on the reasoning that this 'might provide an insight on what does not attract the attention of a person with ASD'. The second is a genuinely different framing from the rest of the eye-tracking literature in this corpus, which almost uniformly models where gaze goes rather than where it does not.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: One explicit direction: produce explainable features by mapping the learned representations back to interpretable scanpath properties, which the authors state is 'left for future studies'. One implicit: enlarge the participant pool, since small subject count is their own explanation for the anomalous scanpath-only result. Neither is elaborated, and notably the paper does not propose participant-wise partitioning, which is the direct remedy for the mechanism it identifies.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Two concrete and well-motivated directions. Add a spatio-temporal attention mechanism 'to allow knowledge on the specific elements in space and time used to inform the diagnosis process in the network' - which, if it also resolved which person's skeleton drives the decision, would address the study's main unexamined confound. And perform fine-grained annotation along the non-verbal continuum for the behaviours that contributed most, specifically 'the precise annotation of the incidence of communicative gestures, shared affective states, atypical social overtures', to establish what the network learned and to build a measure more sensitive than a 3- or 4-point clinical scale. The broader agenda is finer-grained digital phenotyping able to process data 'at the spatio-temporal resolution that is off limits to human coding', to uncover manifestations not previously evidenced and to define subtypes for more precise clinical action.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Four directions, three of them named by the authors and one clearly implied. Replicate on a larger sample and determine whether the trained model transfers without retraining - a transfer question rather than a sample-size platitude. Control IQ explicitly as an independent variable rather than relying on task selection to suppress its influence. Include other neurodevelopmental conditions - ADHD, developmental coordination disorder, intellectual disability - to establish whether the signature is autism-specific rather than a general marker of atypical development; the authors give the mechanistic reason, that sensory integration dysfunction is not autism-specific. And extend the method to younger children, where earlier identification would matter most, which is where the motor-precursor literature they review predicts the signal should already be present.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Two directions, both about model efficiency rather than about validity. Replace the three-model pipeline with convolutional or attention architectures to reduce computational cost; and, more interestingly, develop fusion that can operate 'even especially in the absence of one modality during the model training', which would address the practical barrier that the current design requires both an EEG net and an eye tracker for every child - a genuine obstacle to the scalability the paper claims. A third, briefer aim is to explore additional autism-related features via advanced signal processing. Absent from the agenda: external validation, direct diagnostic confirmation, developmental-level control, or any analysis of which features drive the result.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Two directions, both well chosen. Replicate with IQ-matched cohorts - which follows directly from the acknowledged confound and is the single analysis that would establish whether the result is about autism or about developmental level. And extend from binary classification to continuous prediction of social-function deficit severity, to serve 'as an objective assessment tool that can be used in conjunction with currently available symptom severity measurement questionnaires and clinical scales'. The second is well supported by data already in hand, since ADOS-2 calibrated severity scores, CARS totals and human-rated IJA scores were all collected and none was related to model output; the severity-regression analysis is available in this dataset and simply was not run.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Two directions, both modest. Enlarge the sample to improve accuracy and stability. And address non-stationarity by 'adopting detection models over time' given the across-day variability in recording conditions - which points toward domain adaptation and is a sensible response to the consumer-EEG constraint the study operates under. Absent from the agenda: any proposal to strengthen diagnostic ascertainment, to measure developmental level, to recruit comparison children from comparable settings, or to validate on an external cohort.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Two lines are proposed, neither addressing the study's weaknesses. First, 'the enhancement and democratization of eye-tracking technologies' - an infrastructure aim rather than a research one. Second, improving the classifier 'by incorporating multi-class information such as medical records or clinical evaluations', which would move the work toward the multimodal designs elsewhere in this corpus but would require exactly the clinical data this study does not have. Notably absent: any proposal to validate at participant level, to obtain participant metadata, to test on an independent cohort, or to separate augmentation from evaluation.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: The agenda follows directly from the findings and is unusually specific. Scale up via internet-based (WebGazer) and smartphone-based eye tracking to obtain the sample sizes needed to identify subtypes, which the authors argue is now feasible and is made more so by their own finding that 2-minute epochs suffice. Collect longitudinal data with dense state-dependent measures - sleepiness, mood - to separate measurement error from genuine within-individual variation across weeks or years, and to assess intervention efficacy while revealing what an intervention changes ('gaze to faces but not to other features might change throughout training'). Design stimuli with specifically chosen visual features to maximise within-individual reliability and between-individual differences, which 'possibly... could also improve the classification analyses'. And integrate with neuroimaging and genetics, on the reasoning that systematic gaze differences 'would be expected to translate to differences also in evoked BOLD-fMRI activations' and 'may be an endophenotype reflecting substantial genetic effects'. The through-line is that establishing individual-level reliability was a prerequisite for all of these, which is the paper's framing of its own contribution.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Five directions, with the most substantive being technical. Collect more data across a wider selection of both groups, argued from the observation that 115.5 minutes already sufficed. Replace manual splicing with automatic blind source separation - the authors are realistic about this, calling it 'an exceptionally challenging task' while noting it is 'possibly a necessary hurdle to overcome to develop widely available and consistently effective autism machine learning diagnosis resources', which correctly identifies the bottleneck for any home-recording pipeline where parents and children speak simultaneously. Explore wearable collection through devices such as Google Glass, building on the group's prior work delivering social cues through wearables. Add crowdsourced human annotation of audio features. And combine audio with computer-vision quantification of hand stimming, upper-limb movement and eye contact toward an interpretable multimodal system. Notably absent: any proposal to verify diagnoses, to match on age, or to characterise what acoustically distinguishes the groups.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Seven directions, each traceable to a stated limitation. Extend to adults and younger children, and to lower-IQ and minimally verbal participants who cannot complete Module 3. Test each component feature systematically to establish individual predictive power. Determine which voice features drive the voice model's false positives, with a specific and testable hypothesis - 'it could be that loudness is a general non-specific feature of young children interviewed on sensitive topics (as those covered by the Friends task) in an unfamiliar setting; if so, removal of these non-contributory features might improve the classification performance of voice-only models'. Control microphone quality and placement to reduce dependence on denoising. Establish test-retest reliability and short-term stability, which are prerequisites for the intended outcome-measure application. Sample naturalistic conversation outside the clinic, 'aiming at minimizing interference by strangers and capturing naturally occurring conversations in the ecological niche of the participants'. And replace manual transcription with automatic speech recognition, with the explicit caveat that 'future studies based on ASR transcription will need to re-evaluate performance of the models relying on ALMs' - recognising that ASR errors would propagate into disfluency and maze measures that depend on precise transcription.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Three directions, each following from a stated limitation. Explore the developmental course of head movement differences and 'elucidate their nature and neurobiological basis', with several concrete hypotheses already advanced - that the movements modulate sensory information generally rather than social perception specifically, that they reflect postural control difficulties that increase with sensory demand, or that like some repetitive behaviours they serve a regulatory function when stimuli are arousing. Extend the computer vision beyond the face to the trunk and shoulders, following directly from the observation that the movement is not confined to the head. And combine head movement 'with other behavioral biomarkers such as gaze, facial dynamics, and response to name' toward a multimodal digital phenotyping tool - which is the group's programmatic direction and is supported here by the demonstration that a single behavioural channel reaches AUC 0.85 in a prevalence-realistic sample.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Five directions, four of them well grounded. Larger samples covering both sexes and wider age ranges. Comprehensive language-ability assessment for group matching, with the mechanism stated. Extension to further typological classes, with named candidates chosen for their position relative to the two languages studied - German and Dutch as rhythmically similar to English, Japanese as distant from both. Neurophysiological investigation of prosody production across language groups, building on existing findings of increased right inferior frontal gyrus and right caudate activation during prosody comprehension in autism, with the observation that such findings 'would be particularly compelling if replicated in individuals with ASD who are speakers of languages other than English'. The fifth is a proposal to examine the ASPM gene as a marker for prosodic differences, on the basis that most Han Chinese people carry a T allele favouring linguistic pitch processing which 'may implicate a role of genetic factors in contributing to cross-linguistic differences of ASD phenotypes'. This last is speculation built on a population-genetic association applied to a null classification result, with no genetic data collected in the study, and it is the one place where the paper's interpretive discipline lapses - it offers an ancestry-based genetic explanation for a language-based finding when the language explanation the authors themselves give (that lexical tone constrains f0) is sufficient.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Six directions, each following from a stated limitation. Larger samples permitting stratification by age, sex and IQ. Inclusion of non-spectrum and other psychiatric groups. Other narrative contexts, with the specific prediction that less structured elicitation may behave differently. Model explanation techniques applied to word-level contributions, with the goal that 'giving meaning to collections of important words may lead to discovering new dimensions of language relevant to ASD' - which frames explainability as a route to linguistic discovery rather than only to trust. Combination of text with speech and extra-linguistic features, citing Asgari and colleagues and Fusaroli and colleagues. And automatic speech-to-text to eliminate the transcription bottleneck. The authors also express a clear preference between their own representations for translational purposes: 'the single vector approach, rather than the pages approach, seems to have the greatest possible clinical utility', because page segmentation is ambiguous and manual whereas the single vector 'enables full automation and objectification of the measurement' - choosing the marginally worse-performing option on deployability grounds, which is the right kind of reasoning and rare in this corpus.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Five directions, the first two substantive. Recruit a developmental-delay comparison group alongside autistic and typically developing children - the specificity test that the paradigm currently cannot support, and which matters particularly for a preferential-viewing task since developmental delay would be expected to affect social attention. Test at true population prevalence rather than balanced classes, to establish deployment performance. Characterise the symptom profiles of false-negative children, on the hypothesis that the 12.5% miss rate reflects clinical heterogeneity - though this requires severity data the study did not collect. Address the sex imbalance with reference to the established prevalence gap. And develop the system into 'an off-the-shelf and ready-to-use software package'. The last sits uneasily against the preceding four: a system that has not been tested at realistic prevalence, against developmental delay, or with characterised failure modes is not ready for packaging, and the paper does not sequence these.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Five directions, tightly tied to the stated limitations. Validate on independent datasets. Recruit 'a broad spectrum of the ASD and non-ASD participants' to address spectrum bias - the direct remedy for the acknowledged overestimation. Add developmental assessment alongside chronological age. Resolve the biological motion inconsistency, where their toddler comparison group failed to show a preference that prior work reports, with the authors noting that 'the age range for our study is between 1.5 and 3, while the previous study focused only on 2-year-olds, so we cannot exclude the possibility that the discrepancy is due to age range difference'. And exploit the age-specific paradigm rankings: 'elucidating the role of different paradigms in ASD classification across different stages may shed light on developing paradigms for earlier ASD detection, particularly for toddlers between 1.5 and 3 years old or even younger' - which is the concrete translational implication of the study's central finding.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Six directions, all operationally concrete. Reduce dependence on human video analysts in future algorithm generations - the scalability bottleneck. Determine what training primary care clinicians need to use the Device confidently in practice, which is a human-factors question the trial did not address since it used a study protocol rather than routine deployment. Run a registrational study monitoring the stability of Device results against diagnosis over time, 'including establishing a diagnosis later in children who at the time of initial evaluation did not meet diagnostic criteria for ASD' - the follow-up that would establish whether indeterminate and negative outputs remain correct as children develop, and the single most important missing evidence for a tool used at 18-72 months. Power future studies for demographic subgroups. Confirm performance across intellectual levels. And obtain cost and reimbursement data to establish whether deployment would be equitable, with explicit reference to Medicaid sustainability and to families without smartphones or insurance.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Five directions, of which two are unusually well targeted. Redesign the recording process so that intensity and pitch can be analysed at all, with the concrete specification that all participants should wear a microphone at a fixed mouth distance - the authors note this must be balanced against 'the necessity of maintaining some environmental comforts for the patients in a clinical condition', which correctly identifies the tension between naturalistic elicitation and acoustic control. Adopt common feature sets across studies so results are comparable across languages, citing De La Fuente and colleagues - a standardisation argument that this review's cross-linguistic study (Lau and colleagues) makes in a different form. The remaining three are larger datasets with feature-subset comparison to build a standard acoustic set for autism; investigation of how voice features relate to speaker age, sex and height; and testing whether the jitter and shimmer pattern seen here in children and reported by Kissine and Geelhand in adults persists across the lifespan, which the authors suggest would be 'a turning point in the early diagnosis'.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: One direction: 'to extract features using CNN models and combine them with features extracted by LBP and GLCM algorithms into a single feature vector for each image and classify it using all three ANN, FFNN and SVM algorithms.' This proposes more feature concatenation on the same 547 images with the same split, and addresses none of the study's substantive weaknesses. No proposal is made to group by participant, obtain demographic or diagnostic metadata, validate externally, interpret the features behaviourally, or test on an independent dataset.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Four directions, of which two are unusually practical. Expand the population and correct the class imbalance by augmentation. Analyse additional motion features such as limb movements and coordination, which the charades format would support naturally since the child is acting out prompts with their whole body. And - the most substantive - 'performing qualitative human-centered investigations or pragmatic randomized controlled trials to evaluate clinical usability' and 'evaluating the real-world diagnostic capabilities of our approach across diverse environmental settings'. Proposing a pragmatic randomised trial and human-centred usability work as the next step, rather than a larger dataset or a better architecture, is a translational rather than technical research agenda and is rare in this corpus.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Four directions. The first follows directly from the stated limitation and is the right one: obtain a dataset of single trials from a large group rather than multiple images from few participants. The second concerns collection quality - ensuring attention to the tracker and a distraction-free environment. The third proposes electrooculography as an alternative signal. The fourth is a deployment proposal that outruns the evidence considerably: 'a mobile app with an incorporated DNN-based ASD classifier and an extensive ET dataset of children aged 6 to 24 months may assist parents in independently screening their toddlers for ASD using a mobile device' - proposed for an age band entirely outside the analysed data, using a modality that requires an eye tracker, on the basis of a participant-level sensitivity of 58.62%.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Four directions, two of which would directly test the study's own weaknesses. Reproducing the paradigm with an examiner who is neither the parent nor informed of the diagnosis would isolate the child's contribution to the duration measure from the parent's and would blind the labeller - addressing the confound and the unblinding in a single design change, and it is the right experiment. Expanding recruitment to permit demographic subgroup validation follows directly from the equity framing that motivates the study, since a tool proposed to reduce disparities must be shown not to perform differentially across the groups it is meant to serve. The remaining two are extending prompts beyond CAFE images to video, and investigating how the parent-child dyadic relationship shapes the signal - the latter framed as scientific rather than merely methodological.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: One direction: 'One of our main tasks in future is to further enrich the dataset', motivated by the observation that the CNN needs more labelled data than are available. No proposal is made to group by child, characterise the participants, document the diagnostic procedure, describe the recording configuration, or validate on independent data.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: No dedicated future-work section, but both stated limitations imply directions and one is developed comparatively. Improving acquisition - the authors' contrast with a four-microphone beamforming setup indicates that better signal-to-noise ratio is the obvious lever, though it would trade against the deployability that a single-microphone setup buys. And relaxing the 20-second, 50-vocalisation minimum, which is framed as a constraint of the deep-learning architecture and which currently excludes the least verbal children. The paper also positions its result against two prior severity-estimation studies - one on Japanese-speaking adolescents using support vector regression and one on English-speaking children achieving a correlation of 0.634 in 33 children - and notes that it achieves 'a similar correlation value (0.606) while using a larger dataset of 132 children', which implicitly frames sample size as the axis along which the field should progress.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Improve and further develop the game scenarios in close cooperation with target users, explicitly including children alongside psychiatrists, psychologists and therapists; identify scenarios attractive to children; and extend toward a human-robot-interaction-enabled system that supports differentiation of autism symptoms beyond turn-taking. The inclusion of children themselves among the users to be consulted is the only participatory-design commitment in this corpus. The obvious additional steps, not proposed, are blinded rating, a larger sample, a developmental-level covariate, and test-retest assessment.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
