answers.answer: Fuse oculomotor with visual fixation features, since the authors' own earlier work on the same children reached 84.62% from fixation alone and 92.31% with fixation plus conversational length; build a representative ASD oculomotor template on the model of Eraslan et al.'s scan-path trend analysis and classify by similarity to it; pursue the neural basis of gaze irregularity; push the age range down towards the 43-month mean diagnostic age, motivated by evidence of atypical oculomotor behaviour in infants later diagnosed; test against developmental delay and ADHD rather than TD alone; extend to children with more severe presentations and a balanced sex ratio; and separate inherent oculomotor function from visual-attention allocation in unconstrained settings. The last of these is the most interesting, because it is an admission that the paper's central conceptual claim - that it measures oculomotor behaviour rather than attention - is not established by its own data.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Three concrete directions, the first two of which address real gaps. Test on a wider population and on a variety of cognitive deficits to determine whether the device can differentiate autism from other conditions rather than only from typical development - which is precisely what the four excluded CP and fragile X children could have begun to address. Investigate how the toy car's size, shape and colour affect children's engagement with it and therefore the extracted features - a design-sensitivity question rarely raised in this literature and directly relevant to whether a play-based screen generalises across devices. And position the device as one component of a larger multimodal screening system rather than standalone, on the argument that different autistic children present different symptoms so a single modality will always miss some.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Four directions. Enlarge the dataset in both size and feature relevance so that the latent space organises without supervision, which is the authors' stated ambition and would remove their reliance on clinical labels as ground truth. Generate as many candidate features as possible so a globally optimal feature set for autism identification can be determined, citing Zhao et al. (2021). Collect more clinical data so the latent space is more densely covered and new participants are less likely to fall into unvisited regions - a coverage argument that follows directly from their decision to classify by fitted density rather than by the predictor network. And combine these kinematic measures with traditional behavioural and cognitive scales into a multimodal risk indicator supporting clinicians rather than replacing them. Absent from the list, and more pressing than any of these, are participant-level validation, an independent cohort, a clinical comparison group, and test-retest reliability for the features proposed as clinical thresholds.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: No future-work section is provided. The conclusion's forward-looking claims are about deployment rather than research: that the method reduces the professional-knowledge requirement for assessment, provides efficient and objective computer-aided screening, and could support early autism screening in remote areas with underdeveloped medical care. Judged against the evidence, the research steps that would need to come first are clear and unstated: evaluation on children not used to train the detector; a balanced sample containing a meaningful number of non-autistic children so that the item score's discriminative value can be assessed; a second, blinded clinician rater with reported reliability so the reference standard is not one person's judgement; chance-corrected agreement statistics appropriate to an ordinal score; and threshold selection on a development set separate from the evaluation set. The wider point this study raises for the review, and does not itself pursue, is whether automating individual ADOS-2 items one at a time is a viable route to instrument automation - it is the only paper in this corpus attempting it, and the answer depends on error rates the paper cannot currently estimate.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Three directions are stated. Enrich the feature set derived from the eye-tracking graph in order to improve precision and accuracy - a reasonable ambition, and one the study has itself left unexploited, since the introduction develops a graph-theoretic framing of fixations as vertices and saccades as edges but no graph metric is ever computed. Extend the classifier to include conditions that overlap with autism so that differential diagnosis becomes possible - the most valuable of the three, and an acknowledgement that separating autistic children from unscreened schoolchildren does not establish clinical utility. And note that a system trained on children will not transfer to adults without retraining. Not mentioned, and more pressing: participant-level validation, reporting held-out rather than pooled performance, an independent cohort, culturally matched stimuli, inclusion of girls, and any cognitive covariate.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Five directions, all following directly from what the study found. Examine which behaviours drive a predicted diagnosis, framed not as a nicety but as a precondition for clinical use - 'clinicians should understand how the AI algorithm makes a prediction before taking this prediction into account' - and requiring more granular expression models than the current localised basis provides. Extend to younger participants, since early diagnosis is where the developmental benefit lies. Move from monadic to dyadic analysis by incorporating the confederate's behaviour, which the recording setup already captures and the paradigm's interactive nature makes theoretically apt. Test on neurodiverse samples rather than autism-versus-neurotypical, the authors' own diagnosis of their key external-validity gap. And conduct user research to determine whether clinician decisions actually improve when AI assistance is available - the step that would convert a demonstrated non-overlap of errors into demonstrated clinical value. Absent from the list: raising sensitivity, external validation on an independent cohort, and analysis of the bored condition.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Four directions, all substantive. Collect data from other age bands both to extend the model beyond 3-6 years and to characterise how dynamic viewing patterns change developmentally. Investigate diversity and individuality within the autistic group through subcategory classification and, notably, through explicit comparison of children who have and have not undergone rehabilitation training - which would convert the study's incidental finding about trained attention into a proper analysis. Predict stimulus discriminability directly with deep models, so that screening image sets can be designed rather than curated, building on the study's own demonstration that 60 well-chosen images match the full 82 while 60 random ones do not. And fuse gaze with fMRI, EEG, facial expression and observation-scale scores, described as an important and understudied challenge. What is missing from the list is the step that would matter most for the stated purpose: prospective evaluation in an unselected community population at realistic prevalence, with a described diagnostic reference standard.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: Two directions, both narrow: tune BERT's hyperparameters, since it was deliberately left at defaults and might improve further; and train additional deep and classical models 'to ensure that no high-performing models are overlooked'. Both extend the leaderboard rather than test the finding. The steps that would matter are absent from the list: splitting by user rather than by tweet, masking autism-related vocabulary to separate topic from style, describing and expanding the comparison group, reporting user-level performance, and obtaining any form of clinical validation for the label. So is any consideration of research ethics or of engagement with the community whose posts constitute the dataset.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Four directions, each following from a specific gap. Study complexity and coordination of facial dynamics during live interpersonal interaction rather than passive viewing, motivated by evidence that autistic people have difficulty with affect coordination in social exchange - the natural extension of a measure built on temporal predictability. Apply the same complexity analysis to head motion as an index of postural control, exploiting data the pipeline already produces. Pursue the preliminary supplementary finding that integrated entropy may separate autism from developmental or language delay, which is the differential-diagnosis question most of this corpus avoids. And combine the facial-complexity biomarker with gaze indices, response to name, motor signatures and other measures before any automated decision tool is deployed - stated as a precondition rather than an aspiration. Absent from the list, and worth adding: test-retest reliability, prospective external validation, and the relationship between entropy and ADOS-T severity.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Three directions, each tied to a specific finding. Collect more data to establish validity, the standard response to a small sample. Develop a method that works for participants whose gaze barely moves - which follows directly from the error analysis and is a real methodological problem rather than a generic wish, since a gaze-based classifier that fails on 17% of children because they use peripheral vision has a systematic blind spot that more data alone will not close. And obtain actual IQ values and other individual characteristics so that the relationship between the model and the heterogeneity of the conditions can be examined - an acknowledgement that a high-functioning sample of 15 cannot speak for a spectrum. Not proposed, and worth noting: a direct autism-versus-schizophrenia classifier, which the dataset already supports and which would be the natural differential-diagnosis test; and validation on an independent cohort.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: Three directions, all in the conclusion and all reasonable. Examine the stability of predictions over time - the obvious next step for a dataset spanning two and a half years that is currently analysed cross-sectionally. Predict quantitative traits of clinical relevance such as adaptive skills and the severity of the autism presentation, which acknowledges that the present labels are binary and unverified. And develop 'next generation digital markers and fingerprints for understanding change, variation, and opportunities for growth' - a framing oriented towards monitoring and personalisation rather than diagnosis, which is the more defensible use of this kind of data. Not proposed, and more pressing: obtaining any clinically verified labels, adjusting for or matching on age, reporting user-level rather than window-level performance, evaluating without pseudo-labelling, and addressing the ethical basis for research use of the telemetry.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: External validation in larger, IQ-matched cohorts is named as the priority and is the correct one. Beyond that, the authors propose that the standardised video acquisition setup could support large-scale collection of behavioural biomarker datasets 'applicable to a wide range of neuropsychiatric conditions', and offer a concrete protocol recommendation derived from their compliance analysis - that a joint attention-driven model should be trained on the first five to ten repetitions of a task, since both groups habituate beyond that point. Not proposed, and needed: a clinical comparison group so that autism-specificity can be separated from general developmental difference; a within-autism-only severity analysis using the K-ADOS-2 calibrated severity scores the study already holds; reporting of specificity; and test-retest assessment for a system intended to track severity.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: Two directions, both aimed at the sample-size constraint the authors identify: use data augmentation, specifically generative adversarial networks, to synthesise additional scanpath images, and expand the dataset itself. The first should be flagged as a hazard rather than a solution in this specific setting - generating synthetic scanpath images from a 547-image corpus and then evaluating on an image-level split would compound rather than mitigate the dependence between training and test data, and would do so invisibly. Expanding the dataset is the sound recommendation. Not proposed: splitting by participant, reporting participant-level accuracy, characterising the children, or examining what the models learn.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: Two directions, both apt: identify autism severity from speech, and explore differential diagnosis using speech-based analysis. The second is the more important and is unusually actionable, because the Eigsti corpus the study already uses contains a developmental delay group alongside autism and typical development. Distinguishing autistic children from children with developmental delay on pragmatic features - rather than from typically developing children on measures dominated by general language level - is the clinically meaningful version of this study's claim, and the material for it was in hand. Not proposed, and needed: leave-one-corpus-out validation, which the three-corpus structure makes available and which would test whether the model generalises across settings rather than learning corpus identity; adjustment for age and language level; and nesting of feature selection.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: No future-work section. The conclusion restates the finding that velocity-infused spatio-temporal scan-paths capture patterns associated with age, sex and their interaction, framed as progress on the heterogeneity problem. The steps the study's own results most clearly call for are absent from the paper: subject-disjoint evaluation, augmentation applied only within training folds, and - most importantly - a diagnosis classifier stratified or matched on age and sex, since the paper has itself established that both are strongly encoded in the representation and both differ substantially between its diagnostic groups.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: No dedicated future-work content in the retrieved text beyond the conclusion's framing that early-detection tools should be 'brief, easily understandable for parents, and easy to administer by healthcare professionals' and that eye tracking suits that purpose. Absent, and needed: reconciliation of the reported metrics, participant-level cross-validation, a held-out confirmation of the selected hyperparameter configuration, a majority-class baseline, and use of the available CARS scores to test whether classification tracks severity.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Five directions, all specific and all following from a stated limitation. Model each child's milestone performance pattern over time rather than collapsing to binary attainment, which would restore the delay-trajectory information the current representation discards. Add early signs not currently in the national protocol, with three concrete candidates named. Incorporate paternal age and family history of autism, both known risk factors absent from routine collection. Replicate with a later and more stable outcome label to reduce the label noise the authors quantify. And conduct direct cross-cultural validation before transferring the approach, covering not only sign expression but 'parental recognition, interpretation, and reporting levels' - an acknowledgement that a model built on parent-reported concern and clinician recording is embedded in a particular culture of help-seeking and documentation. The list is notable for containing no proposal to improve the algorithm.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: None is proposed. The introduction states an intention to test the model on images of children below 36 months 'to assess its efficacy in early detection', and no such analysis is reported. The conclusion contains no future-work content beyond restating the results.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: The paper proposes validation on larger multi-site datasets under different partitioning schemes. The more informative next steps, all available within ABIDE-I: refit with the ADOS, ADI-R and SRS fields removed, which would establish what the imaging and demographic streams contribute on their own; run leave-one-site-out evaluation to quantify the site confound; report an age-and-IQ-only baseline; and correlate the model's output probability with ADOS severity rather than consuming severity as input. The first of these would convert the study from a demonstration of circularity into a genuine test of multimodal fusion, and the architecture is well built enough to make that test worth running.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Larger samples with a balanced sex ratio and a wider severity range. The discussion adds a deployment argument rather than a research direction, positioning the approach as economic, contactless and calibration-free and therefore suited to early objective identification. Not proposed, and needed given the study's own results: nesting the feature construction within the cross-validation to establish whether the derived-feature gain survives, adjusting for the IQ and age differences, relating coordination to severity dimensionally, and directly reconciling the cross wavelet result with the group's own null complexity-matching finding on the same recordings.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Three directions, all concrete. Comprehensive verification with a substantially larger and more diverse participant pool, with the logistical difficulty of achieving this acknowledged rather than waved away. Improvement of the automatic annotation system, particularly for te-clauses, either by sharpening category definitions or by expanding training data - a specific and testable target derived from the study's own error analysis. And extension to other languages through transfer comparison, the same method used to build the Japanese system network, which the authors argue makes the annotation scheme 'applicable to any language'. That last is an unusually ambitious but well-grounded claim, since it rests on a documented linguistic methodology rather than on an assumption that features transfer. Not proposed, and needed: cognitive assessment of the comparison group, and analysis relating model output to the SRS-2, AQ, Vineland-II and ADOS-2 data already collected.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: None proposed. The conclusion restates the method and the comparison without identifying any next step.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: None stated. The directions the study most needs are evident from its own framing: evaluate on autistic participants, evaluate on spontaneous rather than posed expression, and test whether a model optimised on posed adult faces transfers to autistic children's faces at all - the last being a question another study in this review answers negatively for a comparable pipeline.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: Four directions, all concrete and following from stated limitations. Expand the sample and observe it longitudinally, to establish predictive capacity over time. Move beyond a single tablet as the tracking device, on the reasoning that richer data collection would improve analysis even from raw coordinates. Coordinate complementary measures, specifically manual and ocular movement data together, to characterise hand-eye patterns - a well-targeted proposal given that the drag-and-drop task is inherently visuomotor and the study measures only the manual half. And cross-validate against other diagnostic tools. Not proposed, and needed: participant-level validation, developmental assessment of both groups, and relating model output to the severity range the autistic sample is said to span.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: None stated.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None separately stated. The most useful next step is available from the data already held: refit with the A1-A10 items and the 'result' field removed, which would establish whether the registration metadata - age, gender, ethnicity, jaundice, family history, country - carry any independent information about screening outcome. That experiment would convert the study from a demonstration of arithmetic into a substantive one, and the architecture and optimisation machinery already built would serve it without modification.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Six directions, all specific. Develop a continuous SRS score prediction model rather than a dichotomous classifier - the most valuable of them, since it would convert a threshold decision into a trait estimate and is already supported by the observed correlation between SRS-2 and predicted probability. Integrate clinical assessments or standardised behavioural tests alongside the SRS-2 to strengthen the reference standard. Obtain a larger and more balanced sample above the threshold. Compare the SVM against random forests or deep learning. Validate on external datasets from different regions or institutions. And incorporate a broader range of balance cues. Not proposed, and needed: reporting whether feature selection was nested, and computing positive predictive value at the observed population prevalence.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: Two directions are named: clinical validation of the Grad-CAM heatmaps by psychiatrists or autism specialists, which is the right next step for the interpretability claim; and reduction of the computational cost for real-time use. Not proposed, and needed before any of the reported figures could support the paper's clinical claims: evaluation on a cohort with documented diagnoses, reporting of the demographic composition of each class, a test of whether the model's output survives matching on age and sex, and an assessment of whether the classifier's decisions track image provenance rather than facial phenotype.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: None stated. The steps this study most needs are participant-disjoint evaluation with the scheme reported, a stated majority-class baseline, feature-importance analysis over the eleven descriptors, and a comparison group larger than four.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: Six directions, each tied to a named limitation. Lengthen the free play session and create opportunities for child-initiated interaction, so that social communication and repetitive behaviours can actually be observed. Recruit a sex-balanced sample and analyse behavioural features by gender. Include children with subtler or atypical presentations rather than restricting to CARS-2 at or above 30, to make the model applicable where screening is hardest. Collect more data and formally evaluate the reliability and validity of both the coding scheme and the model, including across age groups and language levels. Add non-autistic clinical comparison groups, particularly intellectual developmental disorder, since that is the discrimination that real clinical practice requires. And use the coding scheme as a training substrate for automatic behaviour recognition - the paper is explicit that the count, duration and proportion indexes were designed to suit 'future application scenarios of machine learning automation'. Not proposed, and needed: an optimism-corrected or externally validated performance estimate, and predictive values recomputed at a realistic screening prevalence.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: External validation of the six-item model on independent data is stated as the explicit requirement and follows directly from the holdout result. The discussion also opens a mechanistic direction: since the ADOS-2's apparent autism signal in schizophrenia tracks negative symptoms, and since negative symptoms and autistic social-communication features may both reflect deficits in social cognition supported by overlapping brain regions, the two may be partly the same construct measured under different diagnostic labels. Not proposed, and needed if the model is to progress: blinded administration, item-level inter-rater reliability, a sample that includes the diagnostically ambiguous and comorbid cases the model is intended for, comparable cognitive measurement across groups, and predictive values computed for realistic clinical mixes.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Four directions are named: stratified sampling to distribute class imbalance evenly across folds; generative adversarial networks for minority-class synthesis, argued to be more representative of real data than SMOTE or ADASYN; extension to children younger than four and to pre-linguistic vocalisations, which the authors argue is supported by their use of non-speech vocalisations from De-Enigma; and continued fairness work given the gender disparities. Not proposed, and needed before the binary result can be interpreted: acoustic normalisation or channel compensation to address the clinic-versus-school recording split, reporting of the number of children per diagnostic class, age distributions by group, and evaluation on a corpus in which both classes were recorded under matched conditions.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: The technical directions named are clinical or crowdsourced annotation to replace hashtag labels, extension beyond English, and use of the retained network metadata. But the direction the paper actually advocates is procedural: 'a more inclusive approach during the model development process that involves the autistic community directly in the ideation and consent processes', supported by research-community work to 'find ways to support large-scale consent procedures' and by 'a regulatory framework for social media data mining'. The paper closes by keeping itself 'as a case study of what is currently possible with publicly available' data rather than proposing a successor system. No other study in this review proposes participatory governance as its principal future work, and none argues against the further development of its own method.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: More sophisticated fusion architectures that better exploit the complementary strengths of the two modalities - motivated directly by the finding that simple late fusion did not improve accuracy despite the networks failing together on only 8.75% of cases, which is exactly the pattern that a better combination rule should be able to exploit. Beyond that: additional modalities; identification of autism subtypes from behavioural patterns, which the ADOS-item analysis makes plausible; and extension to home settings without specialised equipment. Not proposed, and needed: confidence intervals and a larger test sample; predictive values at realistic prevalence; sex-stratified evaluation; a non-autistic clinical comparison group; and an explicit statement of whether the ADOS recordings used as input contributed to the diagnoses used as labels.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: Three directions, each tied to an identified weakness. Move from visual-only to audio-visual models. Replace the simple averaging of annotator ratings with a neural multi-label learning approach capable of handling disagreement and reaction-time lag - a direct response to the authors' own critique of their ground truth. And incorporate the subjects' gestures into both tasks, which is the most interesting of the three: the corpus is defined by gestural stereotypy, and cropping to the face discards exactly the behaviour that identifies the children. Not proposed, and prerequisite to interpreting the classification result: documenting the composition and source of the non-autistic class, and evaluating whether the classifier separates children or corpora.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Five directions are listed: larger and more diverse samples, additional modalities including speech and genetic information, ensemble models, longitudinal designs to track change over time, and evaluation in real-world clinical settings. The fourth and fifth are the ones the framework actually requires, and their inclusion is a tacit admission that a system proposed for continuous longitudinal monitoring and medication adjustment has been evaluated neither longitudinally nor clinically. Not proposed, and prerequisite to any of the above: participant-disjoint evaluation, disclosure of how severity labels were obtained, per-setting analysis to separate thermal environment from physiological signal, recording of current medication, inclusion of girls, and ethics review.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Clinical validation is named as necessary for adoption, which is the right requirement. No other direction appears in the retrieved text. Needed and not proposed: reporting of the demographic composition of each class, evaluation on a cohort with documented diagnoses, and any test of whether the classifier's decisions track facial phenotype rather than the collection route of the image.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: Larger and more varied datasets; better preprocessing to reduce transcription noise; and, implied by the mean-word-length finding, lexical complexity measured in phonemes or morphemes rather than characters. Not proposed, and needed: an independent language measure to separate delay from autism; reporting of age and sex composition by diagnostic group; model evaluation stratified by sex, given the interaction the paper itself reports; and reinstatement of the developmentally delayed children as a third class, since the source corpus contains them and the resulting three-way discrimination is what clinical practice requires.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Lightweight architectures to make dual-stream inference tractable in real time; improved augmentation and pre-training; and multimodal extension combining audio and visual data with skeleton. Not proposed, and needed: participant-level partitioning for DREAM; sensitivity and specificity alongside accuracy; demographic reporting and age-stratified analysis; use of all ten walking trials per child rather than one clinician-selected trial, which would both remove the outcome-informed selection and make within-child movement variability available as a feature; and joint-level attribution, which skeleton data make straightforward and which would connect model behaviour to describable gait characteristics.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: The authors propose larger and more culturally diverse samples, age-specific models to accommodate developmental change in cry acoustics, refined diagnostic methodology, and real-world testing and integration - adding that implementation 'would require clinician training and addressing ethical considerations', which is an appropriate acknowledgement from a commercially sponsored group. Not proposed, and prerequisite to interpreting the classification result: a held-out test partition, participant-level splitting, and a model-selection rule that does not maximise over the evaluation set. Also needed and readily available: a stratified analysis by recording setting, an age-adjusted group comparison, and a correlation between the acoustic features and the GARS-2 scores already collected.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: Incorporate diverse datasets to improve generalisability across populations, and explore deep learning and transfer learning. The more informative step, available from the data in hand, would be to refit with 'result' and the A1-A10 items removed and report what the registration metadata alone achieve - which would separate any genuine association from the arithmetic recovery of the label.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: Four directions are named: a larger parameter set, deeper architectures, a larger dataset, and optimisation for real-time performance. All are engineering extensions. Not proposed, and prerequisite to interpreting the present result: a sex-stratified or sex-adjusted analysis, which is the single most informative check the existing data would support; an ablation across the three landmark streams, which would show whether the signal lies in facial geometry, posture or hand movement and therefore how exposed it is to the sex confound; documentation of how autism was ascertained in the 50 children; an independent held-out evaluation; and ethics and consent documentation.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: Five directions, well matched to the acknowledged limitations: expand and diversify the dataset with a demographically varied sample of children with and without autism and gelotophobia; validate on independent cohorts from multiple institutions; try ResNet-50, EfficientNet-B4 and MobileNet-V3; integrate eye tracking, speech prosody and body language to capture dynamic signals; and build a real-time prototype. The first of these - actually collecting data from children assessed for both conditions - is what the study would have needed to support any of its gelotophobia claims, and its appearance as future work is an implicit acknowledgement that no such data underlie the present paper. Not proposed: obtaining a diagnostic reference standard for autism, participant-level splitting, or reporting per-class performance.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Collaboration with others in the field, per the conclusion. The steps the study most needs are participant-level splitting with the number of distinct children reported, a stated validation scheme, per-class metrics, and - given the frozen-extractor architecture - a coefficient analysis showing which embedding dimensions carry the signal, which would at least locate the discriminative information.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: Multimodal inputs and explainable-AI methods are proposed in the abstract, and the limitations section implies five more: demographic diversity, larger datasets, dynamic rather than static analysis, external clinical validation, and GPU-based training. All are reasonable. The step the study most needs and does not propose is reconciliation of its own metric table, followed by participant-level splitting with the number of distinct children reported.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: None separately stated. The step this study most needs is a source-held-out evaluation - training on Kaggle images and testing on Semarang images, or the reverse - which its own mixed corpus makes available and which would establish directly whether the models detect a facial phenotype or the character of an image source. Reporting the source-by-class breakdown would be the prerequisite.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Two directions: incorporating attention mechanisms into the deep learning models so the model focuses on the most relevant features, and extending to multimodal data combining eye-tracking with other behavioural or physiological signals. Neither addresses the validity problems in the present design; both propose adding capacity to a pipeline whose reported ceiling is already 99.78%.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Compare other AUTOML libraries; benchmark the model on public datasets such as the UCI ASD screening data to test robustness across populations. Both are reasonable and directly address the stated limitation, but neither touches the circular label that governs the entire result.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: Multimodal extension (3D scans plus voice analysis, eye tracking and movement data); explainability to improve clinical trust and transparency; real-world deployment in classrooms and social interactions on mobile or edge devices; robustness to lighting, expression and morphological variation. The classroom-deployment proposal is worth flagging - it would place automated facial ASD screening in schools, applied to children who have not consented and on the basis of a model trained on web-scraped photographs with no diagnostic labels.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Weight DTW by fixation duration to improve scanpath alignment; address calibration precision and data-integrity problems in eye-tracking to improve reliability and accessibility for screening; and evaluate on an independent dataset to assess generalizability and precision. The last is stated in the abstract itself, which is an unusually forthright acknowledgement that the reported figures are not yet generalisation estimates.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: None. There is no future-work section. The paper closes on the claim of superiority over existing methods.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: A single paragraph proposing Physical Neural Networks based on stacked intelligent metasurfaces to process multimodal sensory data at the hardware level, reducing computational overhead and enhancing privacy through localised data handling. Computational overhead is not a difficulty encountered anywhere in a study that fits shallow networks to 44 rows, and the proposal addresses none of the study's actual weaknesses.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: A single sentence proposing augmentation technologies to generate larger and more diverse datasets, plus unspecified additional techniques. Given that the study's own contribution is a dataset built to address representativeness, proposing synthetic augmentation as the route to further diversity moves away from the recruitment-based solution the paper has just demonstrated.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: External validation on larger and more heterogeneous cohorts, and integration of genetic or neuroimaging modalities. The first directly addresses the stated limitation; the second proposes adding expensive modalities to a pipeline whose reported ceiling is already 100%, which is the characteristic move of this literature - scaling up inputs rather than questioning the estimand.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: None stated. There is no future-work section.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Not available - the extracted text ends mid-discussion and contains no conclusion or future-work section.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: Include clinician-confirmed diagnoses and observational measures of camouflaging alongside self-report; replace criterion-based screeners with dimensional continuous scales for anxiety and depression to reduce scatter; and, before any clinical implementation, cross-validate extensively against health-record data. Each future direction addresses a specific stated limitation, which is rare in this corpus.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: Hybrid vision transformers and adaptive learning as a direction for future research in ASD classification and medical imaging, and validation on larger, more diverse datasets. The second addresses the study's real gap; the first proposes more of what was just done.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: None. There is no future-work section; the paper ends on the claim of higher accuracy with reduced model complexity.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: A single direction: migrate from R to Python for access to more advanced machine-learning libraries and better collaboration with the childcare research community. This is a tooling preference rather than a scientific direction, and it addresses none of the study's own identified concerns - not the overfitting the authors flag, not external validation, and not the missing clinical ground truth.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Add further explainable algorithms such as gradient boosting trees and explainable boosting machines, and integrate multimodal data combining eye tracking with behavioural, cognitive or neurophysiological measures to improve robustness and clinical applicability. Both are proportionate to the study's own findings.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: None. There is no future-work section; the paper closes on the claim that healthcare professionals can use these classifiers to enhance the accuracy rate of ASD diagnosis.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: Enhance preprocessing techniques, improve the efficiency of feature selection, and ensure the model's adaptability across diverse datasets. The last is the only one that addresses a genuine gap, and it is stated without reference to any external dataset.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Employ a range of shapes across the angular-frequency spectrum rather than only ellipses or spirals; investigate kinematic features for early screening in conjunction with clinical assessments; and separate clinically driven movement decline from normal ageing, a need the study itself establishes by demonstrating age effects on several kinematic features.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: External validation against independently clinician-annotated severity datasets - named as necessary rather than desirable - plus multimodal fusion (prosody, eye-gaze dynamics), federated learning validation, and prospective clinical trials to enhance sensitivity and ensure fairness across populations. The first directly addresses the study's own stated boundary; the fairness objective is undercut by the removal of ethnicity and country of residence during preprocessing.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: Not separately developed beyond the deployment limitations. The paper closes on the claim that the framework improved interpretability and diagnostic reliability.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: Announced in the paper's structure but not developed in the extracted text.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Sequential models that exploit the temporal structure of AOI fixations rather than aggregating them into summary features; larger cross-linguistic cohorts to assess bilingual exposure; and cost-benefit analysis of false positives to define what performance threshold would count as meaningful in low-stakes screening. The last of these is a form of future work no other study in this review proposes - defining the target rather than raising the number.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: Not captured in the extracted text.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Use feature ranking to remove uninformative measures and shorten the battery; design manipulations that accentuate reaction-time differences in the most sensitive domains, since certain emotional categories and stimulus types are harder to categorise and leave more room for RT differences; and test whether the sensitive measures differ across age groups.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: Validation on larger and more diverse datasets, and integration into an end-to-end screening platform. Both follow directly from the stated limitation.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: None stated.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: Assessment on demographically different and stable datasets to evaluate fairness and generalisability - proportionate to the stated limitation and the only future direction offered.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Collect real Kinect-derived severe-ASD data with a stated minimum sample of 20 to 50; test generalisation across age groups, genders and cultural backgrounds on larger datasets from multiple institutions; and run longitudinal studies of how motor biomarkers track severity change, framed as a way to evaluate intervention effectiveness. Each addresses a specific stated limitation.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Broader age ranges, more diverse environments and dialects, transfer learning from larger speech corpora, features capturing developmental-delay-specific nuances, conversational agents or robotic assistants for scalable screening, and a multimodal extension adding limited prosodic cues while preserving the privacy advantage of text. The last is a considered trade-off rather than a generic call for more modalities.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: Longitudinal protocols with additional collections at different time points to assess response stability and tool robustness; larger and more diverse samples to address the convenience-sampling limitation; and training for education professionals as a condition of deployment. Each addresses a stated threat.

questions.question_text: Which behaviours are targeted?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Speech/voice: pre-verbal vocalisations (babble, cry, squeal, laugh, whine, yell, single words) - acoustic and prosodic properties, not linguistic content.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Motor behavior: 3D upper-limb kinematics (velocity, acceleration, deceleration profiles, movement units, movement duration and wrist orientation) during a goal-directed reach-grasp-drop action.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: Behavioral task performance in response to facial-expression stimuli: response correctness and response latency. This is recorded behavior in a perceptual task rather than a directly sensed modality such as gaze, speech or motion.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Gaze: fixation coordinates during face viewing, aggregated as spatial frequency distributions. Temporal/scanpath information was deliberately excluded because cross-region transitions were too sparse in the training data.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Language: lexical/semantic content of elicited descriptive sentences about social relations. No acoustic, prosodic, gaze or motor data - this is one of the few purely linguistic-content studies in the corpus.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Motor behavior in two forms: gesture kinematics and form from the touch screen (velocity, area, height, duration, tap counts) and contact/angular forces from inertial sensors (accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer). No gaze, speech or facial data.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Motor behavior: 3D hand kinematics during imitation - velocity, acceleration and deceleration profiles and their timings, jerk, horizontal and vertical amplitudes, and movement duration. Single-point finger tracking rather than full-body pose.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: Facial expression (FACS action units and Kinect animation units), head pose in 3D, head-motion speed and cumulative head displacement, plus response latency to spoken questions. Voice is recorded for the answers but no acoustic or linguistic analysis of it is performed - only the time taken to respond is used.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Speech/voice: pre-linguistic infant vocalisations (babbling and other non-vegetative vocal breathing groups) characterised by spectral, energy and frequency-related acoustic parameters. No linguistic content, since the infants are pre-verbal. Parental voice is present in the recordings but is not analysed.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Speech: spontaneous child vocal production analysed paralinguistically through prosodic, spectral, cepstral and voice-quality descriptors. The introduction explicitly argues that linguistic markers may be unreliable because language skills vary across spectrum subtypes, and that paralinguistic cues are better suited to automatic detection - so linguistic content is deliberately excluded.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Motor behavior: ground reaction forces during walking - the kinetic rather than kinematic aspect of gait, measuring the forces generated against the ground in three directions rather than limb trajectories or joint angles.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Spatial/locomotor behaviour: the child's physical position and dwell time relative to a social robot, derived from overhead video tracking. Facial video is captured but not analysed. This is proxemic and approach behaviour rather than gaze, speech or fine motor kinematics.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Gaze: fixation duration on predefined facial and body regions during passive viewing of a speaking face. Aggregate dwell time per region rather than scanpath, saccade dynamics or pupillometry.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Speech and language jointly: acoustic/paralinguistic properties (voice quality, spectral envelope, harmonic phase distortion, F0) and linguistic content derived from ASR transcripts (LIWC categories, vocabulary size, repetition, reading accuracy, words per second). The explicit joint acoustic-linguistic framing is unusual in this corpus, where most speech studies are purely paralinguistic.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Gaze: fixation timing, duration, count and revisit behaviour within areas of interest during naturalistic web interaction. Distinctively, the stimuli are real web pages rather than faces or social scenes, so the measured construct is general attention allocation and search strategy rather than social attention.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Motor behavior captured as raw video: the kinematics of a reach-to-grasp movement, with visual appearance deliberately degraded by Gaussian smoothing so that only movement information remains available to the model. No markers, no motion capture, no handcrafted kinematic parameters - the paper positions this freedom from 'invasive sensory devices (e.g., MRI, microphones, eye tracker, Motion Capture landmarks)' as its central practical advantage.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Gaze: binocular fixation sequences with duration and order, encoded relative to automatically detected facial landmarks. The distinguishing feature is that temporal ordering is preserved and made the object of analysis, whereas the corpus's other gaze studies aggregate into dwell times or fixation counts that discard sequence.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Motor behavior: one-dimensional hand kinematics, specifically the statistical distributions of oscillation amplitude, velocity and acceleration rather than their means. The construct measured is behavioural variability/complexity rather than speed, accuracy or coordination - a different target from every other motor study in this corpus.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Speech and language jointly: acoustic-phonetic properties (voicing probability, pitch, jitter, shimmer, HNR, energy, MFCCs, zero-crossing rate and their deltas) and lexical/discourse properties (pause and overlap metrics, turn metrics, speaking rate, word complexity, LIWC psycholinguistic categories, lexical entropy and diversity, parts of speech, formality, polarity). Distinctively, all of these are computed for both the child and the adult conversation partner.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Three streams: gaze (fixation location, timing, duration, frequency, saccade amplitude), behavioural task performance (response latency and recognition accuracy), and the visual content of what was fixated (deep embeddings of the face region at each fixation). The third is unusual - most corpus gaze studies use predefined anatomical areas of interest, whereas here the stimulus content at the point of gaze is encoded by a deep network without any manual region annotation.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Behavioural observation mediated by human rating rather than direct sensing: 31 categorical judgements of autism-relevant behaviours (eye contact, social participation, stereotyped speech, sensory seeking, stereotyped interests and actions, and others) made by watching short video. This is the only approach in the corpus where the 'features' are human perceptual judgements of behaviour rather than automatically extracted signals - which is deliberate, since it removes any need for specialised sensing hardware in the deployment setting.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Gaze: fixation coordinates, durations and derived saccadic amplitudes during natural-scene viewing. Uniquely in this corpus, gaze features are combined with computed properties of the stimulus itself - detected object regions and a bottom-up saliency map - so the representation is jointly behavioural and stimulus-derived rather than purely behavioural.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Social-interaction behaviour observed as discrete cues: eye contact, vocalisations, imitation and gestures, each tracked in specified tasks. These are categorical behavioural events rather than continuously sensed signals, and in this study they were largely human-coded (in real time by the operator for critical observations, offline from video for the rest) rather than automatically detected.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Gaze: fixation durations within predefined regions of interest during viewing of visual stimuli. Aggregate dwell time only - no scanpath, saccade, pupillometric or temporal-sequence information.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Motor behavior: 3D index-finger kinematics during repetitive pointing (velocity, acceleration, deceleration, jerk, amplitude and their timings) together with spatial endpoint accuracy derived from where the finger contacted the table.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Gaze: raw point-of-regard coordinates over time, from which velocity, acceleration and jerk are derived and encoded chromatically. Distinctively, the representation preserves the full spatiotemporal trajectory rather than aggregating into area-of-interest dwell times, which is the dominant approach elsewhere in the corpus.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Motor behavior: whole-body non-verbal movement captured as frame-differencing motion energy in head and body regions, converted into intrapersonal synchrony - the temporal coordination between a person's own head and body movement. This is a distinctive construct in the corpus: not movement quantity, speed or trajectory, but the internal temporal coupling of one's own body segments during social interaction.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Motor pattern during gameplay, chosen deliberately in preference to social and emotional variables - the protocol lists as a strength that 'a computational analysis of motor pattern variables, rather than social and emotional variables, is employed', grounded in the hypothesis that 'an underlying movement disruption may be a core component of autism spectrum disorder and a new, accessible early biomarker'. The measurement is sub-second: touch-screen contact kinematics and triaxial inertial signals sampled while a child plays. Three properties make this construct choice significant for the synthesis. Motor control is measurable without any social demand, so it does not require the child to engage with a person, which is both an advantage in accessibility and a limitation in construct coverage. It is measurable without language, reaching the pre-verbal and minimally verbal children that the transcript- and conversation-based measures in this review cannot assess. And it is measurable without human rating, so the entire chain from behaviour to classification is instrumented - the protocol notes that in the pilot 'the result of the assessment was purely statistical; no subjective coding was required'. The motor hypothesis aligns with the one-legged-standing and skeleton-movement studies charted elsewhere here, which target postural and gait control on similar reasoning.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Gaze: fixation coordinates and durations during free viewing of natural scenes. The distinguishing conceptual move is that gaze is not analysed in isolation but relative to a computationally simulated typical scanpath, so the measured quantity is deviation from a modelled norm rather than an absolute gaze property.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Motor behavior: full-body pose, represented as the trajectories of 15 skeletal keypoints over 10-second windows. The authors position this explicitly against the field's focus on faces and eyes, noting that prior work has concentrated on 'analyzing RGB frames and pertaining high level information from the video as well as focusing on specific body parts of children (e.g. face)', whereas 'none of them focused on studying full body pose movement over time as an indicator of atypical behaviors'.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: Joint attention, specified with more precision than anywhere else in this review. The construct is decomposed into its three established subtypes - initiation of joint attention, responding to joint attention bids, and initiation of request behaviour - and the measured cues are enumerated: looking toward an object, toward the robot and toward the therapist, pointing, responding to a prompt from either mediator, and self-occlusion. The reported finding is subtype-specific rather than aggregate: initiation of joint attention appeared toward the therapist, across the mediator transition, and toward the robot in all three typically developing children, but only toward the therapist during the transition in the at-risk children. Whatever the sample's limitations, that is a claim about which form of joint attention differs and toward which partner, which is the level of specificity that makes a behavioural finding clinically usable. The paper also notes that the same infrastructure could measure eye contact, stereotyped head movements, concentration and excessive interest in objects, and that joint attention was chosen as this study's scope - so the construct restriction is deliberate.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Gaze: fixation locations and durations during image viewing. As with Wu et al. on the same benchmark, gaze is not analysed in isolation but relative to a computational model of typical viewing - here by sampling a predicted saliency map at each fixation, so the representation encodes how salient the fixated locations were to a general-population saliency model rather than where the child looked in absolute coordinates.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: Turn-taking, decomposed into two forms - and the decomposition is the study's substantive contribution to the review. Behaviour performed in response to an explicit robot instruction is treated as intentional turn-taking; behaviour performed spontaneously, imitating the robot without being told to, is treated as automatic turn-taking. Each is expressed as a proportion of the behaviours required of the child in that game, so the two are directly comparable within a child. The finding is that autistic children reliably do what they are asked and rarely do it unprompted, which the authors read as a specific deficit in automatic rather than intentional turn-taking. Two things make this valuable for the synthesis. It is a within-construct dissociation rather than a level difference, so it says something about the structure of the difficulty rather than only its presence - which almost no other included study attempts. And it identifies a measurement principle with wide application: a paradigm that separates prompted from unprompted performance can distinguish capacity from spontaneous deployment, a distinction that most behavioural measures in this corpus collapse.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Dyadic social-interaction behaviour: eye contact, social smiling, non-social smiling, protest behaviour and active social engagement, each measured as both duration and frequency. Uniquely in the corpus, behaviour is measured relationally - against a caregiver whose responsiveness is experimentally manipulated - rather than as a property of the child alone, and the manipulation is what generates the discriminative signal.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Two modalities: hand movement kinematics (velocity, acceleration, deceleration profiles with their timings, amplitudes, jerk) and eye movement behaviour during the same imitation task. Measuring gaze and movement concurrently during imitation is distinctive - it captures both what the participant looked at while observing the model and how they subsequently moved.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: A single modality - facial expression, captured as still images during prompted imitation of seven categories (angry, disgust, fear, happy, sad, surprise, neutral). The behaviour targeted is expression production on demand rather than spontaneous expression or expression recognition ability, although the paper's motivating literature concerns autistic people's difficulty recognising others' expressions, which is a different construct from the one measured.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Motor behavior: kinetic postural control, specifically centre-of-pressure excursion during quiet standing, capturing both the magnitude of sway (displacement, path length, area) and its temporal regularity (sample entropy). This is the only study in the corpus to measure static postural control with a force plate, complementing the gait, reach and imitation studies in the motor strand.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Two behavioral streams from video: upper-body movement (characterised through Laban weight, space and time features intended to capture movement intent) and facial configuration (68 keypoints from the nose and eye regions). Notably the facial keypoints are geometric landmark positions rather than expression classifications, so the model sees face shape and pose rather than interpreted emotion.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Motor behavior: whole-body 3D joint trajectories during imitation, evaluated for both spatial fidelity to a model and temporal synchrony with it. The construct measured is specifically imitation ability - the correspondence between the child's movement and a target - rather than movement quality in the abstract, which the authors argue distinguishes their approach from prior motor classifiers.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: Infant vocalisation captured passively during clinical assessment - one syllable utterances, canonical babbling, non-syllabic babbling, first words, and atypical voice including screaming and crying. Uniquely in the corpus, the vocalisations are categorised by developmental stage before modelling, so the acoustic analysis sits on top of an explicit linguistic-development taxonomy rather than treating all speech as homogeneous.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Walking gait, reduced to the temporal structure of the gait cycle: step time, stance time, swing time and step-to-step interval, each measured separately for the left and right leg. Only timing is used - no kinematics, no joint angles, no ground reaction forces, and no spatial measures - which makes the feature set narrow but exceptionally well specified.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: Child speech during clinical interaction, analysed along three distinct behavioural dimensions: prosody and voice quality (pitch, formants, spectral slope, jitter), acoustic energy dynamics (normalised energy and its derivatives, zero crossing rate), and conversational behaviour (vocalisation rate, segment durations, turn-taking latency and rate, total vocalisation count). The turn-taking features are what distinguish this from purely acoustic work - they measure the child's behaviour in relation to the clinician's, requiring the whole session and both speakers, and they turn out to be the features that track social affect specifically.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: Visual attention during naturalistic information-seeking - fixation behaviour across web-page regions during free browsing, targeted search and inferential synthesis. This is a distinctive behavioural target for the corpus: not social attention to faces or eyes, but general visual-information-processing strategy on non-social stimuli. The paper argues this is a feature rather than a limitation, since 'atypical visual-attention patterns reflect higher-order differences in information processing', and it sidesteps the dependence on social stimuli that characterises most gaze work here.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: Visual attention during free viewing, targeted specifically at its dynamic structure - the sequence of and transitions between fixations rather than where or how long the eye rests. This is the paper's defining choice and its stated critique of the field: existing methods 'tend to analyze the indicators based on individual static fixation, such as the fixation location and fixation duration. However, the actual eye movement is a dynamic process. The relationship between fixations also contains important information in visual attention.' Ironically, in operationalising the dynamic view the model discards fixation duration entirely, which the authors recognise and list as future work.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Whole-body movement during imitation, decomposed anatomically into head, trunk, arms, legs and feet, and measured as mean inter-frame joint displacement. The behavioural target is repetitive and stereotyped motor behaviour - the DSM criterion domain the paper argues is under-studied relative to social communication - operationalised as movement magnitude under graded sensory provocation rather than as counts of identified stereotypies. Uniquely in the corpus, the behaviour is elicited by a designed sensory manipulation rather than merely observed.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: Responsive social smiling - whether a toddler produces a clear smile in response to a specific social overture, across five humour mechanisms plus a parent-delivered greeting. The behaviour is deliberately chosen because it is the hard case: unlike response to name or joint attention it 'is evaluated by emotion description that usually remains an ambiguous classification result', so it is the element of screening where automation has the most to offer and where a defensible ground truth is hardest to obtain. That the paper builds a three-clinician consensus for exactly this reason is a considered response to the problem.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: Passive visual attention across six distinct social-cognitive constructs, decomposed into oculomotor mechanics (fixation counts and durations, saccade durations, first-saccade timing, exploration order), region-of-interest allocation (bodies, heads, eyes, mouths, activities, distractors), event-locked response latency, and data-quality measures (percentage of gaze on screen, missing data, proportion of events meeting quality requirements). Including quality metrics as candidate features rather than as exclusion criteria is a distinctive choice, and it pays off - one such feature appears third in the SHAP ranking, which the authors interpret as non-compliance during socially oriented content being itself informative.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: Two behavioural-adjacent targets of different kinds. The behavioural measure proper is visual attention allocation during face viewing, decomposed across eight regions from whole-face down to individual eyes, and manipulated by face race. The EEG measure is neurophysiological rather than behavioural - resting-state cortical rhythm power - and the paper interprets it in behavioural terms, linking theta to working memory encoding and retrieval, beta to alertness and motor behaviour, and gamma to sensory processing, working memory, attention and arousal.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Two behaviours measured simultaneously and by design: visual attention allocation between a central social stimulus and flanking nonsocial distractors, and emotion recognition accuracy and error structure. The distraction ratio - proportion of gaze frames on distractors rather than the face - is the primary behavioural measure, with a variant excluding frames coded 'nowhere in particular' to give a more direct face-versus-distractor comparison. Emotion responses are captured both as a 7 x 7 confusion matrix and as a per-face correct/incorrect sequence preserving performance over time.
