answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: Three behavioural channels measured simultaneously during a single interaction: facial expression (action unit occurrence and intensity, and critically mimicry - the time-shifted correlation between the actress's and participant's expression time series), gaze (angle, deviation from personal median, speed and acceleration), and voice (fundamental frequency, jitter, shimmer, energy, harmonics-to-noise ratio and MFCCs). Measuring mimicry rather than expression alone is the distinctive choice: it captures a dyadic property that requires both partners' behaviour, and it is only possible because the partner's behaviour is identical for every participant.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: Saccadic eye movement - specifically latency, accuracy (absolute error), amplitude, peak velocity, acceleration and the trial-to-trial variability of each, measured under gap and overlap conditions, together with fixation-proportion and pupil-area measures carried in the dataset. The rationale offered for targeting saccades rather than social gaze is worth noting and is not made elsewhere in this corpus in quite these terms: sensorimotor abnormalities are said to be detectable 'prior to the identification of social and cognitive deficits', so an oculomotor marker could in principle precede the social behaviours on which clinical diagnosis depends.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: Two behaviours, both DSM-relevant core impairments: joint attention, operationalised as the delay before establishing eye contact with a robot and the duration for which it is sustained under escalating cue support; and imitation, operationalised as the proportion of four gross motor actions correctly reproduced. Measuring both within a single interaction, and gating one on the other, is the design's distinctive feature - most robot studies in this corpus measure a single behaviour.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Anticipatory and referential gaze during joint attention - specifically whether and when the participant's gaze arrives at, dwells on and returns from the regions a therapist's gaze or gesture directs it toward. The construct targeted is more specific than the social-attention measures elsewhere in the corpus: not how much a child looks at faces, but whether the gaze tracks a referential sequence in time, including whether it arrives before the referent appears. The anticipation feature, which permits negative first-visit times computed against records from the preceding segment, is the direct operationalisation of that.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: Distribution of visual attention across three semantic region types in an immersive scene - human figures, an animal and landscape - characterised in three ways: total occupancy, continuity of occupancy, and transitions between region pairs. Including both total and continuous occupancy is the design's most productive choice, since the continuity features turned out to be the most important and total occupancy was not, which distinguishes sustained engagement from repeated brief glances - a distinction most gaze studies in this corpus collapse.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Visual orienting - shifting and sustaining attention toward a target indicated by a directional cue - decomposed across four cue types spanning a social-content gradient from arrow through pointing finger and cartoon gaze to human gaze. Four behavioural quantities are measured: success rate, latency to disengage from the cue, and dwell time in the target, confound and uninformative regions. The social gradient is what makes the study theoretically informative rather than merely predictive: it permits the question of whether the deficit is social-specific, and the answer is that it is not.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Visual attention to point-light biological motion, decomposed three ways: where on the screen gaze falls across six regions and five animation stages, whether head and eye move together, and whether the child anticipates a repeated action. The head-eye co-movement measure is distinctive in this corpus - most eye-tracking studies discard head movement as a nuisance to be minimised, whereas here it is treated as a behavioural signal in its own right, hypothesised to index stereotyped head-shaking. That the hypothesis was refuted does not diminish the value of measuring it.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: Gaze allocation across seven distinct social-viewing paradigms - own-race and other-race unfamiliar faces, joint attention, gaze following and social interaction - each reduced to a cumulative fixation duration measure within areas of interest. The behavioural coverage is broader than any other single study in the corpus, and the per-paradigm t-tests make it possible to see which constructs actually discriminate: unfamiliar own-race faces and social interaction do, joint attention and one of the two gaze-following tests do not.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Visual attention during competition between social and geometric content, analysed not as how much is looked at but as what predicts where gaze lands. The unit of analysis is the pixel: for each pixel, a 27-dimensional feature vector describing its image properties at pixel, object and semantic levels, with the model learning which properties predict fixation for each severity group. This reframes the behavioural question from a preference measure to an attentional-guidance measure, which is what allows the top-down versus bottom-up interpretation.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Two behavioural channels from a single live interaction. Gaze allocation to a real conversational partner across four regions - eyes, mouth, whole face, whole body - and interaction duration, measured as the time taken to complete a fixed number of conversational exchanges. The second is not a gaze measure at all but an outcome of the interaction, and treating it as a feature alongside gaze is the design's most productive decision. The four-session structure adds a temporal dimension, since each feature is computed per session, allowing the analysis to show that group differences in mouth and face fixation are strong in the early sessions and attenuate later.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: Voice quality during sustained phonation - specifically phonatory stability (jitter, shimmer), noise content of the glottal source (harmonics-to-noise, glottal-to-noise excitation and signal-to-noise ratios) and vocal tract spectral shape (MFCC, RASTA-PLP). This is the narrowest behavioural sample in the corpus: a single sustained vowel captures voice source and resonance properties but no prosody, no interaction, no linguistic content and no temporal structure of speech.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: Gaze trajectory and its dynamics across a heterogeneous battery spanning joint attention initiation, gaze following with head-plus-eye versus eye-only cues, static face-and-object viewing, and emotionally contingent versus non-contingent cartoon scenes. Rather than reducing these to fixation counts or dwell proportions, the study preserves the whole scanpath as a spatial object with velocity written into its colour - so the behavioural unit analysed is the shape of looking over time rather than any summary statistic of it.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Visual attention during competition between biological and geometric motion, analysed not as dwell proportions but as a mapping from image properties to fixation probability. The behavioural quantity modelled is which visual features attract a group's gaze, decomposed across low-level saliency (steerable pyramids, colour, intensity, orientation), semantic content (faces, people, skin, horizon), spatial position (distance to screen and scene centres) and motion (optical flow magnitude, biological versus geometric scene membership).

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: Visual attention to social and non-social content during free exploration of a rich environment, decomposed hierarchically: people versus items versus background; within people, the main interacting avatar versus other characters, adults versus children, faces versus bodies; within items, dynamic versus static. Because features are computed both globally and per scene, the analysis can locate where in the 16-scene sequence group differences arise - and the significant differences cluster in the hall, the electronics shop and the game centre rather than being distributed evenly, which is information a whole-session summary would lose.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Head movement during conversational gesture, decomposed into three rotational axes - pitch for nodding, yaw for shaking, roll for lateral inclination - and characterised along two independent dimensions: extremity of rotation (range) and quantity of rotation per unit time. The behavioural target is therefore the manner of gesture execution rather than its occurrence, which is what allows the study to separate gesture use from gesture kinematics. Head gesture is also, unusually for this corpus, a communicative act rather than an incidental behaviour - nodding and shaking carry propositional content in a yes-no exchange.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: Inherited from the source dataset: visual scanning behaviour rendered as a spatial trace. This paper adds no behavioural analysis of its own and does not characterise the target behaviour beyond the assertion in its introduction that autistic children show reduced attention to social content.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Upper-limb reaching and grasping, analysed at two levels. Conventional kinematics capture the surface properties of movement - speed, velocity-profile shape, endpoint variability. The synergy analysis captures something different in kind: how tightly the nine joint angles covary, indexed by how much of their joint variance three principal components can absorb. That second level is the paper's contribution, and it targets a construct - co-control of redundant degrees of freedom - that no other study in this corpus measures.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: Attention and engagement, decomposed into three operationally defined components with explicit rules. Face attention: orientation toward the robot's chest display, detected by Haar cascade, scoring +5 when the face is detected and -1 when it is not. Joint attention: a head turn matching the robot's directed gaze, detected through left or right ear detection, scoring +15 - the largest weight in the system, and appropriately so, since joint attention is the more specific construct. Sound response: latency from prompt to vocal response, converted by a fixed linear formula. The construct choice is well matched to the clinical purpose the paper sets out, which is not diagnosis but therapy targeting: the authors argue that 'one of the most important preconditions for the success of these interventions is the knowledge and availability of the kinds of stimuli that usually draw the attention of the child and increase his or her engagement over time'. Attention is what a therapist needs to know moment by moment to steer a session, and it is the quantity the system measures and feeds back. The weakness is the operationalisation of face detection as attention, which equates orienting with attending and will misclassify a child who listens without looking.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: No behaviour is observed. Six of 21 items concern the child's behaviour as recalled by a caregiver - crib rocking, suspected deafness, insistence on particular music, reaction to bright lights, colours or unusual sounds, age of walking and age of first words - which together sample early sensory reactivity, repetitive movement and developmental milestone timing. The remaining fifteen items are perinatal, familial and parental variables that are not behavioural at all. This composition is the principal reason the record sits at the boundary of the review's scope and should be distinguished in the per-group analysis from directly instrumented behavioural studies.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: Prosody during naturalistic conversation about emotions and social relationships, decomposed into pitch, cycle-to-cycle frequency perturbation (jitter), cycle-to-cycle amplitude perturbation (shimmer), harmonics-to-noise ratio and loudness, plus articulation indexed by cepstral coefficients and spectral entropy, and fluency indexed by voiced and unvoiced segment durations and counts. The behavioural target is the modulation of voice rather than its content, and the conversational rather than task-based elicitation means the speech is spontaneous.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Visual attention during free viewing, operationalised at three levels: what is looked at relative to image content (fixations on detected objects versus non-object regions, coverage, saliency-weighted fixation), how looking is temporally and spatially structured (fixation counts and durations, saccadic amplitudes, refixation, ROI clusters), and where looking is anchored spatially (distance of fixations and ROI centres from the image centre). Each family operationalises a specific published behavioural claim, so the feature set is a set of testable hypotheses rather than an undirected dump - which is what makes the error analysis interpretable when most of them turn out not to carry the result.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Visual attention during free viewing, represented at the level of the raw fixation sequence - coordinates, durations and their temporal order - rather than through hand-engineered behavioural constructs. Three encodings of the same behaviour are compared: a flat 99-dimensional vector, a 33-channel spatial fixation map preserving temporal order across channels, and a recurrent sequence. The comparison is informative in itself: the multi-channel encoding beat the single-channel version because it preserves ordering (66.06% versus 63.96% on validation), confirming that fixation sequence, not just fixation distribution, carries signal. The behavioural quantity that ultimately dominates, however, is the simplest - total scanpath duration.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Non-verbal social interaction taken as a global pattern rather than as an inventory of separable behaviours - the study's central conceptual commitment. The stated target is 'global patterns of atypical postures and movements, fewer gestures used and often decoupled from visual contact, facial affect, speech', with the emphasis on decoupling: the claim is that autistic non-verbal behaviour differs less in the presence or absence of individual acts than in how gesture, gaze, posture and affect are coordinated with one another and with the partner. That is a behavioural construct which single-behaviour paradigms cannot in principle capture, and it justifies both the whole-assessment input and the temporal modelling. The post-hoc symptom analysis supports the framing empirically: the items that tracked model output most strongly were integration of gaze with other behaviours (0.591), pointing (0.540) and unusual eye contact (0.500) - coordination items rather than frequency items.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: The kinematics of goal-directed dragging - how a finger travels from a card to a placeholder - decomposed into how fast (mean, max, min and SD of speed), how the speed changes (the same four for acceleration), how directly (STH straightness), how consistently in direction (DC and sdDC) and in how many separate pieces (MeanLength). The behaviour is not social and not autism-specific in its surface form; the claim is that autism manifests in the microstructure of any goal-directed movement because prospective motor control is impaired, which is why an arbitrary cognitive task can serve as the probe. The theoretical grounding is more developed than in most of this corpus, running from Kanner's original identification of disrupted movement patterns through Leary and Hill on motor-symptom links, the enactive mind account, Friston's predictive coding and Sinha's proposal that stereotypies are a response to an unpredictably 'magical' world - and the motor findings are read back into that frame as over- and under-compensation from interrupted feedforward control.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: The behavioural target is social visual attention: where a preschooler looks while watching a child and an adult interact, resolved to eight regions that separate the two people, separate eyes from mouth from body within each, and add an explicit joint-attention region. The six statistics per region capture both what was attended (fixation count, total and mean fixation duration, visit count) and the priority of attention (time to first fixation, number of fixations before first entering the region) - the latter pair encoding attentional precedence rather than mere allocation, which is the more theoretically pointed measure. The paired EEG modality is not behavioural at all, being eyes-open resting state with no task, so what the fusion combines is a behavioural response to social content with a task-free measure of intrinsic brain dynamics.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: A single, precisely defined social behaviour: initiation of joint attention, operationalised as the triadic gaze - 'a triadic gaze where the child shifts their gaze from the object at hand to the person they wish to interact with and back to the object, or from the person to the object and back to the person', sometimes accompanied by a point. This is the narrowest behavioural target in the corpus and the choice is deliberate and defended: joint attention is described as 'a high-level social skill and a valid indicator of social brain development', develops early in typical children, and is measured by a validated manual (ESCS). The contrast with the rest of this literature is instructive - where most studies extract many features from an unconstrained behaviour stream and let a model find what discriminates, this study constructs a paradigm to elicit one behaviour that clinicians already regard as diagnostic, then asks whether a model can see it. That inverts the usual relationship between the computational method and the clinical construct.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Two behavioural constructs, each operationalised in a way that departs from convention. Social attention allocation is measured not by fixation on hand-drawn regions of interest but by the distribution of fixations across K-means clusters discovered from the data - so the analysis asks where gaze concentrates without the experimenter deciding in advance what counts as a region. This removes one source of investigator judgement and is defensible when a stimulus has no clean object boundaries, but it also severs the link between a feature and any interpretable content: a cluster is a screen location, so a group difference cannot be reported as 'less looking at the comedian's face'. That is why the paper reports no directional gaze findings at all. Facial expression is operationalised as imitation rather than as expression: the expression displayed in the stimulus is defined as the target, and the feature is the count of frames in each 40-frame window in which the child displays that same expression - so the measure is expression contagion or mirroring in response to a specific social display, motivated by prior work suggesting 'spontaneous expression imitation could be used as a behavioral marker'. This is a sharper construct than generic expression frequency and one of the few instances in this corpus of a behavioural feature defined relative to what the stimulus is doing at that moment.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Nominally gaze during free viewing, but the behavioural construct is entirely lost in the representation. The source dataset encodes gaze coordinates together with their first, second and third derivatives - velocity, acceleration and jerk - as RGB colour gradients in a plot of the scanpath. This paper converts those images to grayscale, which discards the colour channel and hence the derivative information, then downsamples from 640x480 to 28x28, leaving 784 luminance values. What the classifier sees is a coarse silhouette of where the trace fell on the screen, with no fixation, saccade, duration or velocity quantity recoverable. The authors' own concluding observation that 'the amount of information in the images and the use of space in the x and y coordinates are essential factors' confirms this: the discriminative property is how much of the frame the trace covers, which is a plot-density statistic. No behavioural finding is reported and, given the representation, none could be.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Social visual attention during naturalistic viewing, resolved into a hierarchy of automatically detected regions: faces, eyes within faces, mouth, hands, non-head body parts, and non-social content, plus two global measures - total on-screen gaze time and the correlation of a participant's moment-by-moment gaze heatmap with a group reference. The heatmap measure is the conceptually distinctive one, since it captures moment-to-moment conformity with what other viewers looked at rather than aggregate time in a region, and it produced the largest group effects (d = 0.820 and 0.692). Its use also generates the paper's most consequential single analysis: constructing a reference heatmap from the autistic group and finding that it correlates at r = 0.966 with the control reference, while autistic individuals nonetheless match it less well than controls do. That result establishes directly that there is no shared autistic pattern of looking - the average autistic viewer looks where the average control viewer looks, and individual autistic viewers depart from that average in individually different directions.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Nominally prosody. The introduction rests its case entirely on prosodic abnormality, citing 'echolalia, monotonous intonation, and atypical pitch and linguistic stress patterns' as 'among the most notable signs of autism', and this is the paper's justification for looking at speech at all. What is actually modelled is broader and less specific: the random forest uses a generic speech-recognition feature set - MFCCs, chroma, RMS energy, spectral centroid, bandwidth and rolloff, zero-crossing rate - containing no pitch, intonation contour, stress or rhythm measure whatsoever, while the CNN and wav2vec models learn unconstrained representations from spectrograms and waveforms. The behavioural target is therefore 'whatever in the acoustic signal separates these two groups of children', which given the sample composition includes vocal-tract size, fundamental frequency range and articulatory maturity - all direct functions of the age and sex on which the groups differ. Because no acoustic finding is reported, the paper cannot say whether anything prosodic was involved. The contrast with Asgari and colleagues elsewhere in this corpus is instructive: that study modelled pitch, jitter, shimmer and harmonics-to-noise ratio explicitly, reduced to two interpretable features, and correlated them with independently rated severity.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Two distinct behavioural constructs measured from the same recording. Language targets expressive complexity and pragmatic function through mean length of utterance, lexical diversity, disfluency structure, rate of production, intelligibility and echoic repetition of the examiner's immediately preceding words - the last of these operationalising a specifically autism-relevant behaviour. The um-versus-uh proportion is the subtlest measure and reflects a well-established finding that the two filled pauses signal different planning difficulties. Voice targets paralinguistic production: pitch, cycle-to-cycle frequency and amplitude perturbation, harmonics-to-noise ratio as a hoarseness index, H1H2 as a breathiness index, spectral envelope and entropy, and RMS loudness. The paper's central empirical claim about these constructs is that they are separable in the participants they identify - the language measures track language ability, the voice measures do not, and the voice measures therefore capture 'paralinguistic features (e.g., prosody, loudness) that are truly independent of language level and output'.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Head movement dynamics during passive viewing, decomposed into three levels: how much the head moves (rate), how sharply that movement changes (acceleration, motivated as relating 'to the magnitude of the instantaneous forces involved in head movement'), and how predictable the movement time series is across temporal scales (multiscale entropy, indexing 'the level of predictability and stability'). The complexity measure is the study's conceptual contribution and is well chosen: rate and acceleration are magnitude measures that could be produced by any source of extra motion, whereas entropy captures the structure of the movement over time and licenses the specific claim that autistic toddlers' movements were 'less predictable and less stable'. The behaviour is explicitly sensorimotor rather than social, and the paper situates it in a substantial literature on motor differences in autism - stereotypies, fine and gross motor impairment, motor planning and coordination, asymmetry in home-video studies of infants later diagnosed, and difficulties in gait, balance, postural control, movement accuracy, manual dexterity and praxis. The authors' own inspection finding, that trunk and shoulders move too, suggests the underlying construct is postural rather than cephalic.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Prosody decomposed into its two canonical components and operationalised as multivariate structure rather than summary statistics. Rhythm is captured through the amplitude envelope - its spectrum, its intrinsic mode functions and its temporal modulation spectrum - with a neurobiological rationale that envelope rhythmicity in the 2-8 Hz band 'is crucial in the neural processing of intelligible speech as it aligns with brain areas in the spoken language processing pathway that oscillate at a similar rate'. Intonation is captured as the full time-normalised f0 contour across each utterance, on the argument that the contour 'encompasses the dynamicity of speech intonation which varies across time within the most fundamental utterance-sized linguistic unit known as the intonational phrase'. The theoretical framing distinguishes affective prosody, which expresses emotion and intent and is broadly recognisable across cultures with possible evolutionary homologies in other mammals, from linguistic prosody, which encodes lexical and grammatical structure and varies drastically across languages - and this distinction predicts the study's result, since rhythm carries more affective and less linguistic load than pitch does in a tone language.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Narrative discourse as linguistic content, deliberately abstracted from acoustics. What is modelled is the semantic and syntactic structure of what the participant said, encoded by language models pre-trained on general Polish text - so the target is pragmatic and structural narrative ability rather than prosody or voice quality. The literature review specifies the constructs at stake: conveying the gist of a story, appropriate use of referential devices, coherence and causal connection, avoidance of irrelevant components, lexical diversity, and internal state language describing characters' perceptions, emotions and cognitive states. None of these is measured directly; the embeddings are expected to capture them implicitly, which is the study's bet and also the source of its interpretability gap. The complement to this design is Asgari and colleagues elsewhere in this corpus, who model the acoustics of the same kind of ADOS-derived speech while discarding the content, and MacFarlane and colleagues, who show that the two channels detect different participants.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Competitive social attention - specifically, how a toddler allocates looking when social interaction and an attractive non-social alternative are visible simultaneously. This is a stronger operationalisation than measuring attention to social content alone, because it makes the measurement relative rather than absolute and therefore less sensitive to overall engagement or tracking success. The theoretical framing is explicitly two-sided, distinguishing 'diminished' from 'superior' processing and noting that autistic attention 'is captivated by non-social stimuli such as objects, lights, and geometric shapes' - so the target behaviour is a preference rather than only a deficit. The thirteen area-of-interest metrics then decompose that preference into how long (dwell time, net dwell time, fixation time), how often (fixation count, glances count, revisits, appearance count), how quickly (time to first appearance, entry time), how sustained per visit (average fixation duration, first fixation duration, glance duration) and how the eye leaves (diversion duration). That last dimension is the one the authors highlight as novel, and it captures something the others do not - the temporal cost of disengaging from an area, which connects to the attention-disengagement literature in early autism that the introduction reviews.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Visual attention allocation, operationalised as the proportion of stimulus time spent fixating each of ten predefined regions. The construct is deliberately layered across paradigms, moving from face parts (eyes versus mouth), through configural biological motion (upright versus inverted point-light figures), to social-versus-geometric competition (mouthing face versus moving dot), to non-social object tracking (duck, helicopter), to static social-versus-object preference (infant face versus fan). That gradation is what makes the age-comparison informative, since it can localise which level of social content is discriminative at which age. The finding that reduction appears at nearly every level, including for an abstract moving dot and an electric fan, is the study's most consequential result for construct validity and is left uninterpreted: a child who fixates less on the fan as well as less on the baby face is not showing selective social disinterest, and the measure may be indexing how much of the stimulus period was spent fixating anything at all.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Behaviour is captured through three complementary observational vantage points rather than a single measurement channel, and the design rationale is explicitly clinical rather than technical. Caregiver report captures behaviour across settings and time; home video captures 'rich insight into the child's natural behavior outside of the clinic setting'; and the clinician questionnaire captures structured professional observation within a visit. The constructs probed are enumerated in full and are recognisably the constructs of a clinical autism evaluation - joint attention, integration of communication forms, reciprocal communication, quality of social responses and overtures, directed and responsive smiling, eye contact appropriateness, pretend and creative play alone and with others, imitation, shared interests, offering comfort, repetitive mannerisms, sensory interests, unusual interests - rather than proxy signals such as gaze coordinates or acoustic features. This is the one study in the corpus where the computational input is the same behavioural vocabulary a clinician would use, which is why its outputs can be interpreted directly and why its false positives can be characterised as children with other conditions that would benefit from similar intervention.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Paralinguistic voice production during narrative, decomposed into four theoretically motivated families rather than treated as an undifferentiated feature vector. Frequency-related parameters index intonation and vocal-tract configuration; voice quality parameters (jitter, shimmer, harmonics-to-noise ratio) index the regularity of vocal fold vibration and are framed as measuring 'the difficulty in controlling the vocal fold vibrations, transforming the production into hoarseness, breathiness, and creaky voice'; loudness indexes intensity and, via its variability, 'the dynamic intonation of autistic speech production'; and spectral parameters index energy distribution. The theoretical grounding distinguishes pragmatic or linguistic prosody, carrying illocutionary force and sentence type, from affective prosody, carrying emotional state - the same distinction Lau and colleagues make - and locates the autism-relevant impairment in the affective channel, with consequences for both production and comprehension. The construct is coherent and the discussion of each family is genuinely scholarly; what it cannot survive is that all four families are equally functions of the recording apparatus.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Nominally visual attention, but no behavioural construct survives the pipeline. The source dataset encodes gaze coordinates and their derivatives as a rendered plot; this study then applies average filtering, Laplacian edge enhancement, active contour segmentation of the trace region, morphological hole-filling, and finally local binary pattern and grey-level co-occurrence texture descriptors. What reaches the classifier is a 216-dimensional summary of the local texture statistics of a processed image of a line drawing. No fixation, saccade, dwell time, area of interest, coverage measure or any other quantity with a gaze interpretation is computed at any stage, and consequently the paper reports no group difference in viewing behaviour, no effect direction and no interpretation. The introduction's extensive discussion of social versus non-social orientation, social attention deficits and visual biomarkers has no connection to anything the method actually measures - a gap of several sections between the stated construct and the operationalisation.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Two constructs drawn deliberately from clinical instruments: gaze fixation, 'which represent[s] regions of an individual's visual focus', and visual scanning, 'which refer[s] to the ways in which individuals scan their surrounding environment', both described as 'included in standard clinical diagnostic instruments'. The theoretical grounding is specific - fixation on the eyes signals communicative intent in dyadic interaction, and autistic individuals are reported to fixate instead on the mouth or other regions; scanning is grounded in Pelphrey's finding that neurotypical viewers transition between core facial features while autistic viewers scan non-feature areas such as the forehead and cheeks. Both constructs are then operationalised in a coordinate frame that cannot distinguish eyes from forehead from background, which the authors concede. The scanning analysis is nonetheless the more original contribution: modelling gaze shifts as a weighted graph and comparing adjacency matrices captures the sequential structure of looking rather than only its aggregate distribution, and it is what yields the interpretable finding that comparison children move between two adjacent central regions 13% of the time against 9.4% for autistic children.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Nominally atypical visual preference, with the introduction grounding this in the claim that autistic individuals 'pay less attention to faces and other social stimuli such as the human voice and hand gestures when compared to nonsocial stimuli' and that 'this unique pattern of eye movements appears in autistic children well before behavioral symptoms of ASD start showing'. Nothing of this construct survives into the analysis. The images are converted to greyscale - discarding the colour channel through which the source dataset encodes velocity, acceleration and jerk - resized to 100x100, and either flattened into pixel vectors for principal component analysis or passed through convolutional layers. No fixation, saccade, dwell time or area-of-interest quantity is computed at any stage, and no group difference in looking behaviour is reported anywhere. The construct discussed in the introduction and the quantity modelled in the methods are unconnected.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Emotion recognition, targeted through a compound behaviour whose composite nature the authors are unusually careful about. The stated construct is grounded in prior work showing that autistic and neurotypical children differ both in 'the ability to correctly identify an emotion and the reaction time required to do so', and the two feature families map onto exactly those two components. But the measured behaviour is not the child's recognition alone: it is the child recognising the emotion, planning and executing an enactment, and the parent interpreting that enactment and responding. The paper states this rather than eliding it, describing the process as 'a complex interaction between child performance and parent interpretation' and noting that treating it as a proxy for emotion recognition risks 'an oversimplified understanding', since it 'likely captures components of theory of mind, metacognition and many other phenomena, as well'. That is the right level of caution for a construct that no single measurement isolates, and it is rarer in this corpus than it should be.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Nominally the acoustic properties of autistic children's speech, but the construct is defined by a generative assumption rather than by any behavioural theory. The paper's model is that an autistic child's utterance equals a neurotypical utterance convolved with a filter bank representing 'all the dysfunctional factors', plus noise - so the target is whatever linear transfer function distinguishes the two groups' vocal production, treated as a property of 'the vocal system' rather than of prosody, articulation, phonation or pragmatics. Nothing in the analysis identifies which acoustic dimension is involved, and no group difference in any interpretable quantity is reported. The paper opens with a figure asserting 'noticeable distinctions' between an autistic and a comparison child's waveform, spectrum and spectrogram for the same content, but this is a single illustrative pair with no quantification. Compared with the other speech studies in this corpus - which measure pitch, jitter, shimmer, harmonics-to-noise ratio, rhythm or disfluency and report directions of effect - this study contributes no characterisation of speech at all.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: Prosodic and acoustic properties of spontaneous child speech during clinical assessment, grounded in a specific prior literature that the introduction summarises accurately: autistic children have been reported to show 'strange prosody', 'increased pitch variability and pitch range', 'slower speech rate, and prolonged word production', with the observation that 'these studies used manual annotation and inspection of the audio recordings' - which is precisely the dependency the present work is designed to remove. The 48 features are named only in part (pitch, formants, zero-crossing rate, duration), so the operationalisation cannot be fully evaluated from this paper. The construct that the model actually targets, though, is not an acoustic property but a clinical score: the system predicts ADOS raw scores, which aggregate social affect and restricted repetitive behaviour ratings across a 45-minute observation, most of which concerns behaviour the microphone cannot capture. That the model recovers 37% of the variance in such a score from speech acoustics alone is the substantive finding, and it is also the reason the result is hard to interpret mechanistically.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Turn-taking, treated as a specific and theoretically motivated construct rather than as a generic behavioural signal - and this is the study's main contribution to the review. Most included studies collect a rich behavioural stream and ask a model what separates the groups; this one names a single element of reciprocal social interaction, designs two contrasting scenarios to elicit it, defines the observable positions that constitute it in a published appendix, and tests whether the groups differ. Two secondary constructs are also measured on 0-5 severity scales: interest in the robot, and additional movements, the latter capturing motor behaviour that the authors treat as stereotypy-adjacent. The finding that autistic children produced significantly fewer turn-taking behaviours in both scenarios is consistent with the free-play study charted elsewhere in this review, which found the social-communication dimension separable in a brief structured sample while the restricted-repetitive dimension was not - here the additional-movements subscale did differ, which is worth noting since it suggests that a robot-mediated task may elicit motor behaviours that a 90-second free-play sample does not.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Gaze allocation during live social interaction, reduced to two constructs: regularity, measured as Shannon entropy of the spatial distribution of raw gaze points over 10 px bins (x-axis, y-axis and the 20,736-cell x-y grid), and spatial extent, measured as the maximum distance between the two most remote gaze points on each axis and in the plane. Crucially the representation is deliberately atemporal - gaze allocation 'captured how gaze behavior was mapped spatially without taking into account the temporal information', so no scan path, no fixation/saccade parsing, no dwell time and no areas of interest. The behavioural claim being tested is that autistic children spread gaze more diffusely and less predictably across the visual field during conversation. The results support this for entropy at every window length and for range only at short windows. Two further behaviours are measured but not modelled: conversational duration (191 s versus 110 s, p < .01), which the authors interpret as social-processing difficulty, and, implicitly, the willingness to wear glasses and converse for several minutes, which the sample was selected to guarantee.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Two behavioural constructs, both explicitly named as autism symptoms and both operationalised through the child's manipulation of a single object. First, interest in rotating objects and attention to parts rather than wholes, captured by the wheels-only play state: the encoder registers wheel rotation while the accelerometer shows the car body stationary, meaning the child is spinning the wheels and watching them rather than driving the car. The design was prompted by direct observation with version 1 that autistic children spent a great deal of time rotating the wheels and watching them while TD children did so much less. Second, movement and repetitive-play patterns, captured by the triaxial acceleration signature of the car being driven - its spectral content, energy, inter-axis correlation, jolt count and tilt dynamics. The four-state decomposition (not playing, wheels only, on the floor, in the air) is the behavioural core of the paper and yields an interpretable budget of how a child spends a play session. A third behaviour enters the model implicitly and without acknowledgement: engagement with the toy itself, via the not-playing ratio, which is dominated by the five autistic children who ignored the car completely against a TD group in which every child was 'very interested'.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Fine motor control during goal-directed touchscreen dragging - specifically the kinematic profile of moving a finger from a card to a target placeholder, characterised along three dimensions. Speed: mean, maximum, minimum and standard deviation. Acceleration: mean, maximum, minimum and standard deviation. Path geometry: STH (straightness, the ratio of start-to-end distance to actual path length, an index of linearity), DC (directional change over time, an index of nonlinearity), sdDC (its standard deviation, a measure of irregularity), and MeanLength (the number of finite trajectories drawn per task). The behavioural hypothesis, grounded in embodied cognition and predictive coding, is that impaired active perception in autism produces abnormalities in planning and in serial and prospective coordination, which should surface as measurably different movement kinematics even in a simple drag. The group's earlier descriptive work had found autistic trajectories to show low linearity, high maximum speed and acceleration, and low minimum speed and acceleration, but without significant group separation; the present analysis partly reverses the speed direction, finding that lower MaxSpeed increases ASD probability while higher MaxAcceleration does. Note what is not modelled: no social behaviour, no gaze, no language, no gross motor activity - this is one of the most narrowly motoric behavioural targets in the corpus, and deliberately so.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: One behaviour, examined more closely than any other single behaviour in this corpus: response to one's own name. The clinical definition adopted is precise - the child should turn and face the caller with eye contact rather than glance to the side - and the paper's decomposition of it into measurable components is the substantive contribution. Torso orientation is captured as the angle between the left-right shoulder vector at each frame and the same vector at the first frame after the call, so the measurement is relative to the child's own starting posture rather than to an absolute frame. Head orientation is captured as the yaw Euler angle from facial landmarks, with the mere detection of a face by the rear camera also serving as evidence that the child turned towards the caller. Response latency is captured by the ordinal 0-5 score, which encodes how many calls and reinforcements were needed. The authors are explicit about why body pose is needed alongside head pose, and the reasoning is behavioural rather than technical: prior work used head pose and gaze only, but some responsive children turn only the head with little shoulder movement, while some unresponsive children rotate slightly while manipulating toys, so neither channel alone separates response from non-response. What is not measured, despite being in the clinical definition, is eye contact itself - gaze is approximated by head direction on the stated assumption that the two agree, an approximation that is reasonable in general but is exactly the point at which a glance to the side, which the protocol says does not count as a response, becomes indistinguishable from a genuine orienting response.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Visual attention during face recognition and facial-expression matching, operationalised entirely spatially. For each defined region of the display - on each of the three candidate figures, on the reference figure, around each of these, and in two regions outside them - two quantities are computed: the number of fixation nodes falling there and the total fixation time spent there. The behavioural hypothesis is the standard one for eye tracking in autism, that autistic and non-autistic children distribute gaze differently when required to compare faces and match expressions, with the paper's own framing that 'the recorded data on eye movements suggest a clear difference between the eye fixation patterns of normal subjects and subjects with autism spectrum disorders'. Two aspects of the operationalisation are worth noting for the synthesis. The regions are defined by task structure (which figure) rather than by facial anatomy - there are no eye, mouth or face-interior areas of interest - so the classic autism finding of reduced eye-region fixation cannot be tested by this feature set at all; what is measured is which stimulus the child compared and how long they dwelt on it, which is closer to a matching-strategy measure than to a social-attention measure. And the distinction between 'on' and 'around' a figure is the study's one attempt to capture a qualitative gaze property, on the implicit reasoning that fixating adjacent to rather than on a face is itself informative; the ablation shows neither subset alone outperforms their union.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Facial movement and head movement during spontaneous conversation, and specifically their temporal coordination. The behavioural target is defined broadly and deliberately: the authors reject restricting analysis to the six basic emotions on the grounds that 'other kinds of facial movements (e.g., communicative expressions, speech-related mouth movements) are also important for diagnosing autism', and so quantify all observable facial motion via a morphable model rather than an emotion taxonomy. The coordination framing is grounded in the diagnostic instrument itself: the paper notes that ADOS criteria evaluate how an individual combines speech with gestures and eye contact with facial expression, and reasons by analogy that coordination within the facial channel - across regions, and between face and head - should be similarly informative. Empirically this is borne out. Head-pose-to-pose correlations carry the greatest average classifier weight, pose-eye correlations feature prominently in the top 10, and mouth-related correlations account for six of the top 10 including three mouth-mouth pairs; relative to their share of the 6,272-feature pool, pose features are about 2.5 times over-represented in the top 10 and mouth features about 1.6 times. The authors connect these to established findings on blinking and nodding as conversational signals and on head and eye movement as indices of social attention. Two behaviours present in the recording are excluded by design: speech, because audio was removed to keep the human comparison fair, and the confederate's behaviour, because the analysis is monadic.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Visual attention during passive free viewing, reconceived as a temporally ordered process rather than a spatial distribution. The paper's construct - the dynamic viewing pattern - encompasses where each fixation lands, in what order, for how long, and with what saccade amplitude and direction connecting it to the next, across all 82 stimuli. The descriptive analysis identifies the component behaviours: autistic children make fewer fixations with larger saccade amplitudes; they fixate faces less than typically developing children, with the largest between-group difference of any region appearing in facial areas; they fixate other salient objects less across food, animals, toys, gazed objects and touched objects; they are slower to notice most object types; and they spend more time on background regions and on the inter-stimulus grey mask. The mechanistic account offered is information-theoretic rather than social-motivational: typically developing children are described as fixating regions of continuous salient information under an information-maximisation principle, while autistic children are 'passive in the information exploration process'. The temporal analysis locates the difference at the extremes of each trial - autistic children's first fixation is often random or outside the image while typically developing children's lands near salient objects, the middle of the trial shows convergence, and the final stage diverges again as autistic children drift to non-salient background. One measured behaviour deserves separate flagging because the authors identify it as a top-three driver of model scores: whether the fixation pattern stays on the image or moves to the grey mask. This is as much a measure of task engagement as of visual preference, and the paper's own age analysis shows the same behaviour arising in typically developing 3-4 year olds from ordinary inattention.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: Written language produced spontaneously on social media - the only study in this corpus whose behavioural sample is entirely self-initiated public communication rather than behaviour elicited under a protocol. That is genuinely interesting as a modality: it is ecologically valid in a way no laboratory task can be, it is longitudinal by default (five years per user), it costs nothing to collect at scale, and it captures communication in its natural social context with real audiences and real stakes. But the study does nothing to characterise the behaviour it collects. No linguistic construct is named or measured - not lexical diversity, sentence length, pronoun use, sentiment, pragmatic markers, disfluency, figurative language or any of the features the autism-language literature has examined - and no analysis reports how the two corpora differ. The introduction gestures at 'linguistic patterns, emotional expressions, and communication styles' but nothing in the method operationalises any of these. The result is a study in which the behavioural target is left entirely to the classifier to define, with no account of what it found. Given that the positive class was assembled by searching for autism keywords and that no autism vocabulary was removed from the tweets, the behaviour actually being detected may be talking about autism rather than any property of autistic communication.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Spontaneous facial movement, characterised by its temporal predictability rather than its content - which is the study's conceptual contribution and distinguishes it from the affect-recognition tradition. Two regions were prespecified with stated rationales: the eyebrows, following the group's earlier finding about eyebrow raising in this cohort and the possibility that it indexes attentional engagement; and the mouth, on the basis of literature linking atypical vocalisation and mouth movement to autism. For each region the landmark points are averaged into a one-dimensional signal, head motion having first been removed by affine normalisation so that what remains is facial deformation rather than head movement. Multiscale entropy then quantifies how unpredictable that signal is across temporal scales. The authors are careful to explain what this does and does not capture, and the explanation is worth stating precisely because the distinction is often blurred elsewhere: a signal with large but highly periodic excursions gives low entropy, and so does a nearly stable signal with small excursions, while only irregular non-periodic movement gives high entropy. So the measure is not amplitude, not frequency and not variability, but predictability - and the paper backs this up empirically by showing that integrated entropy correlates only weakly (0.2-0.42) with landmark variation. The finding is that autistic toddlers' facial movement is less predictable in both regions, that the difference is amplified by social content, and that their responsiveness also varies more across different movies. The interpretation offered is that typically developing toddlers respond more predictably because they share an understanding of the movies' social meaning while autistic toddlers respond more idiosyncratically - explicitly labelled as speculation.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Visual attention during facial emotion recognition, measured in three ways and analysed separately for each emotion presented. Fixation counts within anatomically defined areas of interest - the eyes region extending up to the eyebrows, the nose and the mouth - index where attention is allocated on the face. Saccade counts index how often gaze shifts. Scan-path length, defined as the mean displacement between consecutive gaze samples, indexes how far and how restlessly the eyes travel. The paper's behavioural hypothesis is the one the field takes for granted, that autistic people look less at the eyes; its finding is that this holds much more clearly for schizophrenia than for autism in these data. In adults, fixation at the eyes separated the schizophrenia group from controls for all seven emotions with p values from .0001 to .01, but separated the autistic group from controls for only two of seven (anger and neutral). What did separate autistic adults from controls, across six of seven emotions, was scan-path length - they moved their gaze further per sample. Fixation at the mouth separated autism from controls for five of seven emotions but never separated schizophrenia from controls. So the two conditions produce distinguishable gaze signatures: schizophrenia is characterised by uniformly reduced eye-region fixation, autism by increased mouth fixation and longer scan paths that vary with the expression shown. In children, almost nothing reached significance - only eye fixation for anger. A secondary behaviour is measured and turns out to be null: emotion recognition accuracy, which was essentially identical across all groups in both datasets, so the gaze differences occur without any difference in task success.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: Interaction with a speech-generating communication device, treated as a behavioural signal in its own right rather than as a means to an end. Three representations of that behaviour are constructed and compared. Sequential modelling captures which keys are pressed in what order, encoded as a stream of numeric identifiers whose ranges preserve category membership - normal keys, complex keys, normal app events, complex app events - so that the encoding is 'pseudo-semantic' rather than arbitrary. Temporal modelling replaces the identifiers with inter-press intervals in milliseconds, capturing the rhythm of interaction independent of content. Spectral modelling counts how often each key or key category is pressed within a session, discarding order entirely. Spatial modelling is considered and rejected on the well-reasoned grounds that user customisation makes screen positions incomparable across people. What is measured, then, is the pattern of a person's attempts to communicate: how they sequence icons into utterances, how quickly they move between selections, and which parts of their vocabulary they use. Descriptively the paper reports that autistic users accessed the app most frequently and used a considerably higher number of unique words than most other groups, and that the commonest phrases across all users concerned food, sleep, sport and greetings. This is the only study in the corpus whose behavioural sample consists of real communicative acts serving real purposes - and also the only one where the behaviour is fully confounded with how the device happened to be configured, by whom, and for what.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Joint attention, taken as an established clinical construct and instrumented rather than rediscovered - which distinguishes this study from most in the corpus, where the behavioural target is whatever a model finds discriminative. Three forms are elicited and modelled separately. Initiation of joint attention indexes the child's motivation to share attention with another person and is behaviourally realised as a triadic gaze pattern shifting from an object to the partner and back. Low-level response to joint attention is the ability to follow and sustain attention on an object indicated near the child. High-level response requires following an indication to an object across the room, so the child must physically turn. The interpretability analysis then characterises what the model responded to in exactly these terms, and the descriptions are specific enough to be checked against the construct: comparison children showed the triadic shift in IJA while autistic children fixated neither toy nor examiner; comparison children sustained gaze on the indicated toy in low-level RJA while autistic children glanced briefly then looked away; comparison children turned immediately to the distant poster in high-level RJA and then back to the examiner as if seeking approval, while autistic children responded slowly or not at all. Two secondary behaviours are also measured. Task compliance across repeated trials, from which the authors establish that both groups habituate and that autistic children specifically disengage at the start of RJA tasks. And, implicitly, gaze itself - the Grad-CAM heatmaps localise to face and eyes - measured from ordinary video without an eye tracker, which is the study's quiet technical achievement.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: Visual scanning behaviour, encoded as a picture. A scanpath is defined correctly in the paper as a spatiotemporal representation of consecutive fixations and saccades that may overlap, and the input to every model is a rendered image of that trajectory. The behavioural claim motivating the work is the standard eye-tracking account of autism - that autistic children look away from eyes and mouths and towards background, with the widely cited 2008 observation about a 15-month-old attending more to the mouth than the eyes given as the example. But the study cannot test that claim, because it never reports what the children were looking at and never inspects what the models attend to. What is actually modelled is the appearance of a line drawing, and the properties of that drawing that a convolutional network could exploit include several that are only indirectly behavioural: the total extent of the plotted region, the density of overplotting, the number of line crossings, the aspect ratio of the traversed area. Some of these are informative about looking behaviour; others would follow from a child simply producing more or fewer gaze samples. The representation makes them indistinguishable, and no analysis in the paper separates them.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: Conversational language, targeted at the pragmatic and semantic level rather than the acoustic or syntactic one, and specified against a clinical instrument rather than by exploration. The design principle is stated plainly: features were extracted 'following the standard diagnostic tool for ASD - Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule', and the resulting measures map onto behaviours ADOS actually rates - echolalia, the ability to sustain back-and-forth interchange, asking questions, building upon statements, use of pronouns. Operationally this yields nine semantic-pragmatic measures: mean length of utterance in morphemes, number of distinct word roots, questions initiated by the child, immediate phrase repetition, coherence between the child's own consecutive utterances, coherence between the partner's and the child's utterances, echolalia as immediate repetition of the partner's bigrams, proportion of unintelligible units, and unexpected word use. Two design decisions are worth noting. Echolalia and child-partner coherence are inherently dyadic, defined by the relationship between what the partner said and what the child said next - so unlike almost every other behavioural measure in this corpus, these features encode interaction rather than individual output. And unintelligibility is retained as a feature rather than discarded as noise, which is behaviourally defensible since articulation and intelligibility are clinically relevant, though it also means transcription-quality differences across corpora enter the model.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: Social attention, decomposed into four constructs with distinct developmental and clinical significance rather than treated as a single quantity. Activity monitoring - attending to what others are doing together - is targeted with deliberate irrelevant distractors present. Dyadic bid sensitivity - responsiveness to another person's overture for engagement - is targeted with two built-in controls that distinguish genuine responsiveness from mere gaze-following and from mouth-movement salience. Social referencing - seeking clarifying information from others' faces in uncertain situations - is targeted with escalating stressful episodes containing a discrete critical event. Theory of mind - spontaneous processing of another's beliefs - is targeted with a naturalistic false-belief scenario. The measured behaviour is where and when the child looks within these scenes, rendered as a trajectory image. Two further behavioural findings emerge from the analysis rather than the design. Discrimination is strongest in the first three seconds of a clip and declines steadily thereafter, suggesting that the initial orienting response carries more diagnostic information than sustained viewing. And gaze velocity, added as colour, improves discrimination substantially over position alone in the same time window (71.74% to 80.25%), indicating that how fast the eyes move between points carries information the trajectory shape does not.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: Visual attention during video viewing, encoded as a drawn trajectory. The behavioural rationale offered is the standard one - that autistic children show atypical visual attention, particularly towards human faces - and the introduction develops it further than most reuses of this dataset, discussing atypical preference for geometric images as a marker of a more severely affected subtype and noting that children with both autism and ADHD show shorter fixation durations on faces than children with autism alone. None of this is operationalised: no areas of interest, no fixation durations, no face-versus-object contrast is computed, because the input is a picture of a path and the model receives nothing else. The source protocol's inclusion of a live host directing the child's attention means the recorded behaviour also reflects responsiveness to verbal social direction, which the paper does not discuss. As with the other scan-path-image studies in this corpus, the representation makes behavioural properties (where the child looked) and incidental graphical properties (how much of the canvas the drawing covers, how dense the overplotting is) indistinguishable to the model, and no analysis separates them.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Developmental milestone attainment across four domains, observed and recorded by trained nurses in routine practice, together with parent-reported concern. This is behavioural data of a different kind from the rest of the review - clinician-mediated, coarse, binary and administratively recorded rather than sensor-derived - and it is worth being explicit that the review includes it at the boundary of its modality scope. What the study demonstrates is how far that coarse behavioural signal goes. The seven most important milestone predictors are all things a nurse can observe in a two-minute interaction: whether a two-year-old has more than ten words, builds a tower from cubes, gives a kiss, eats independently with a spoon, knows a body part, composes two-word sentences, says 2-3 words. Four are language, two personal-social, one fine motor, all falling between 12 and 24 months, and all differ between groups at p < 0.001 on independent testing. The domain distribution is itself informative: language dominates, which is consistent with the wider literature on early markers but also raises the untested possibility that the model preferentially detects autistic children with co-occurring language delay. Parent-reported concern is a further behavioural channel and emerges as a key predictor, which is a finding about the informativeness of parental observation rather than about the child. Notably absent from the recorded protocol, and named by the authors as missed opportunities, are the subtler social behaviours that dominate the rest of this corpus - social reciprocity, social smile, eye contact - which the paper observes 'can be easily missed by a healthcare provider during a short checkup visit due to their gradual deviation or subtlety'.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: The autism classification component does not target behaviour at all - it targets facial morphology, on the stated premise that autistic children have an 'expanded upper face and a truncated mid-facial region' and 'differences in both the arrangement and dimensions of facial landmarks'. That is a claim about anatomy, not about what a child does, and it places this study outside the behavioural framing that organises the rest of this review. The expression recognition component does target behaviour - emotional facial expression - but it is trained on AffectNet, a general-population emotion dataset with no autism labels, and its output is never connected to the autism classification. So the paper's title claim to identify 'emotional and facial symptoms' rests on two modules that address different constructs on different data and are never integrated. For the review, the study is best understood as marking a boundary: the point at which automated autism detection stops analysing behaviour and begins inferring diagnosis from appearance.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: None observed. The study contains no behavioural measurement in the sense the rest of this review uses - no gaze, speech, movement, facial dynamics, play, telemetry or written language. What it calls behavioural data are scored summaries of clinician-administered assessments: ADOS communication and severity scores, ADI-R social and verbal domain totals, SRS raw totals. These are judgements about a person rather than records of what a person did, and the distinction is the one the review applies when admitting nurse-recorded milestone attainment or app telemetry as behavioural while treating instrument totals otherwise. The imaging stream targets neuroanatomy - voxel-level structure and Harvard-Oxford region relationships - which is a different construct again. The study is therefore charted here as the corpus's representative of a parallel literature rather than as a contribution to the behavioural evidence base, and its value to the synthesis lies in what it reveals about that parallel literature's reporting norms.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Interpersonal motor coordination during spontaneous conversation - the extent to which a child's whole-body movement synchronises with the interviewer's, resolved by frequency. This is the most genuinely dyadic behavioural target in the review: coherence cannot be computed from one person's data, the measurement is symmetric across the two parties, and the surrogate control is constructed precisely by breaking the dyad. The construct is developed carefully in the introduction, distinguishing unintentional coordination (limb synchronisation in side-by-side walking, group clapping, mimicry, turn-taking) from intentional coordination (rowing, choral singing), and grounding its social significance in evidence that coordination establishes rapport, enhances affiliation and promotes prosocial behaviour. The empirical finding is frequency-specific: coordination was reduced in the autistic group at the faster time scales (0.1-0.9 s), corresponding to rapid movement adjustments, while slower-scale coordination did not differ. Both groups exceeded the pseudo-pair chance level, so the finding is a difference in degree of real coordination rather than its presence or absence - a distinction the surrogate control makes possible and that a study without such a control could not draw. The measure's principal ambiguity is that half the signal belongs to the interviewer, so reduced coherence could reflect the child coordinating less, the adult coordinating differently with autistic children, or both, and nothing in the design separates these.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Lexicogrammatical choice - which options a speaker selects from the grammatical resources their language offers - as an operationalisation of pragmatic impairment. The theoretical grounding is Systemic Functional Linguistics, in which language is a system network of choices and meaning is made by selecting among them, and the clinical construct is defined with care as difficulty in 'adapting language formality based on the situation, interpreting non-literal language (such as idioms, metaphors, irony, and sarcasm), and understanding the nuances of language that affect interpersonal interactions... rather than with the basic structural or grammatical components'. The annotation scheme operationalises this across multiple lexicogrammatical systems, of which the paper details several: modality, where prior work by the first author found autistic individuals less likely to use probability expressions (must, will, may) and evidentiality expressions (seems, looks like, likely, is said, according to) and connected this to inferential reasoning; te-clauses with eight functional subtypes; negotiating particles, comprising twelve Japanese sentence-final and medial particles such as kana, ne, yo and yone that mark attitudinal stance toward a proposition and signal the speaker's claim on the information; and explanative mood.
