Two features distinguish this target from the rest of the corpus. It is language-specific in a principled way - the particles carrying much of the signal have no English equivalent and were identified through a system network built for Japanese - which is the opposite of the usual practice of applying an English-derived feature set across languages. And the empirical result localises the signal to socially interactive language: interview transcripts discriminated better than narrative recounting in every configuration tested, which is what a pragmatic account predicts and a purely structural account does not.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: None is measured. The paper's framing is behavioural - emotion, facial expression, distinctive patterns shown by autistic children - and its method is not. HOG captures gradient orientation distributions, LBP captures local texture, ORB captures keypoints and their descriptors, PHASH computes a perceptual fingerprint of the whole image, SIFT detects scale-invariant local features, and the three backbones supply generic ImageNet activations. None of these is a measure of expression, movement or any behaviour, and no expression labels exist in the dataset. For the review this study marks the far end of a boundary the companion paper already approached: automated autism detection that has left behaviour behind entirely while retaining behavioural vocabulary.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: Prototypical posed emotion in adult volunteers - anger, fear, joy, sadness, surprise and disgust - captured at peak intensity. The construct the paper claims to address is different and considerably harder: the atypical, low-intensity, idiosyncratic facial signalling that autistic people may produce and that conventional recognition systems misread. The paper states that problem clearly and does not test it. For this review the distinction matters because the two constructs have opposite difficulty profiles: posed peak-frame expression is the benchmark case on which affect recognition has long achieved very high accuracy, whereas spontaneous atypical expression in autistic children is where every reported system in this corpus degrades. A 99.8% figure on the first tells a reader nothing about the second.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: Fine motor control during goal-directed touchscreen dragging, represented as a full temporal sequence rather than as summary statistics. The behavioural claim is that motor differences in autism are prevalent, early-appearing - present 'even before the onset of language and social interaction difficulties' - and clinically neglected, with the paper stating that despite their relevance 'currently there are no adequate tools available to accurately assess motor function in children with autism'. The theoretical grounding is embodied cognition: how a person moves shapes how they learn from and explore the environment, so motor patterns are informative about cognition rather than peripheral to it. Empirically the study localises the signal to acceleration: synthetic trajectories with higher average acceleration are more likely to be classified as autistic, with correlations of 0.69 and 0.82 for the two models. That is a specific, directional and testable behavioural claim - faster or more abruptly accelerating dragging movements are associated with autism in this sample - and it is arrived at by manipulation rather than by correlation with observed data. Two things the representation does not capture: the visual half of the visuomotor task, since only finger position is recorded and gaze is not, which the authors identify as the priority extension; and any measure of task success beyond the requirement that a drag reach its target.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: Nominally facial emotional expression, reduced to seven probability values per individual across angry, disgust, fear, happy, neutral, sad and surprise, plus derived positive and negative emotion aggregates. But no elicitation condition, stimulus, recording apparatus or expression-recognition method is described, so it is unknown what produced these probabilities or what the individuals were expressing about. Two physiological variables sit alongside them, and the paper's framing does not distinguish behaviour from physiology at any point - facial expressions and 'sensory data of heart rate and body temperature' are treated as interchangeable inputs to a detection model. The theoretical discussion also concerns recognition of emotions in others ('impaired identification of sad and fearful expressions', 'facial affect identification deficiency'), which is a perceptual capacity, while the measured variables are expression production; the paper does not note the distinction.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None observed. The A1-A10 fields record whether a respondent endorsed each of ten statements about a person's social-communication characteristics - the person's own answers in the adult band, and a parent's, relative's or professional's answers about a child in the younger bands. These are judgements about behaviour, and the review's line is that a record of behaviour a person produced counts as behavioural data while a respondent's characterisation of that person does not. The remaining fields are administrative: age, gender, ethnicity, jaundice at birth, family history of autism, country of residence, prior app use and who completed the test. Nothing in the dataset is a measurement of anything anyone did. The contrast with the review's other administratively recorded data is instructive: nurse-recorded developmental milestone attainment counts as behaviour because it records whether a child performed an action, whereas a ten-item checklist total records what an informant concluded.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Postural control during single-leg stance, decomposed into three families with a clear theoretical rationale. The conventional family follows prior work: centre-of-pressure path length, mean speed, entropy and convex-hull area, together with the duration of the longest stand, capturing how much and how variably the base of support moves. The proposed family is the study's contribution and captures something different - the correlation between centre-of-pressure movement and the angle of each of ten joints (neck, shoulder, both elbows, both trunk sides, both hips, both knees), plus the difference between centre-of-mass and centre-of-pressure. These measure not how much the child sways but how the body's segments move in relation to the sway, which is a coordination rather than a magnitude construct. The empirical result supports the distinction: the conventional sway variables alone performed less well, while the proposed correlation variables achieved perfect separation, and SHAP attribution identified shoulder, hip and trunk as the dominant contributors. The authors' reading - that upper-body and waist coordination with the base of support is what differentiates children with high autistic traits - is a specific, mechanistically interpretable claim about anticipatory and compensatory postural control rather than about balance ability in general. The paper also flags the transition from two-legged to one-legged stance as a feed-forward process worth examining separately, which is a construct-level insight most balance studies do not articulate.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: Nominally facial morphology and expression; operationally, whatever separates two sets of internet images. The motivating literature is specific - intercanthal distance, facial midline height, facial asymmetry, facial masculinity, and increased complexity of eyebrow and lip movement in autistic infants - but none of it is operationalised. The representation is a raw RGB face crop, so no morphometric measurement is extracted, no landmark geometry is computed, and no temporal information is retained, which rules out expression dynamics entirely. What the network can key on is unconstrained: craniofacial shape, but equally facial expression at the captured instant, head pose, apparent age, ancestry, image resolution, compression artefacts, illumination, background and crop convention. The paper's leakage analysis inadvertently demonstrates how much non-diagnostic structure the images carry - a maximum training-test cosine similarity of 0.9714 in a pretrained ResNet-50 feature space, on a corpus that supposedly contains different children.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: None. No behaviour is observed, elicited or measured at any point: the recordings capture spontaneous cortical electrical activity while participants rest. The construct is neurophysiological - spectral power, signal complexity, fractal and entropy characteristics of the resting EEG - and the paper's motivating premise is that 'individuals with ASD exhibit atypical neural activity patterns'. For the review this places the study in a parallel evidence stream: it addresses the same clinical problem as the behavioural work and answers it with a different kind of measurement, one that is more direct physiologically and further from anything a clinician, parent or teacher observes. The related-work section shows the branch's feature vocabulary clearly - recurrence quantification analysis, power spectrum, wavelet transform, fast Fourier transform, fractal dimension, correlation dimension, Lyapunov exponent, entropy, detrended fluctuation analysis and synchronisation likelihood - none of which corresponds to an observable behaviour.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: The broadest behavioural coverage of any single task in this review. Nineteen behaviours were coded and expanded into 81 quantitative indicators of count, duration and proportion, spanning functional play, imaginative or symbolic play, eye contact, facial expression, vocalisations and verbalisations with a socially oriented subclass and a word-use subclass, stereotyped use of language, unusual and repetitive hand, body and limb movements, unusual restricted and stereotyped behaviours, and unusual sensory seeking. Play was further resolved by object category - miniature or representational toys, cause-and-effect toys, construction toys - so that play duration could be attributed to the kind of play the toy affords, and functional and imaginative play alone generated 18 of the 81 indicators. Behaviour form and function were coded alongside occurrence, and the timeline representation records overlap so that simultaneous behaviours can be identified. Two results from this breadth matter for the review. Only two behavioural families entered the final model - socially oriented speech and functional play with objects - so the informative signal is narrower than the coding scheme. And the restricted-repetitive indicators are statistically degenerate, with odds ratios in the millions and confidence intervals from zero to infinity, because these behaviours essentially did not occur in 90 seconds. That is a clean demonstration, made against a pre-registered prediction, that a brief structured play sample accesses the social-communication and play dimensions of the phenotype while leaving the restricted-repetitive dimension unobserved - a boundary that applies to every short-observation study in this corpus and is rarely made visible.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: The full 32-item behavioural repertoire of ADOS-2 Module 4, spanning communication (spoken language level, speech abnormalities, echolalia, stereotyped word use, offering and asking for information, reporting of events, conversation, descriptive gestures, emphatic gestures) and reciprocal social interaction (unusual eye contact, facial expressions directed to the examiner, language production linked with nonverbal communication, shared enjoyment, communication of own affect, comments on others' emotions or empathy, insight into social situations and relationships, responsibility, quality and amount of social overtures, quality of social response), plus imagination and restricted repetitive behaviour items. The item-level table is the study's richest contribution to this review's behavioural synthesis, because it shows that both conditions produce social-communication atypicality but of distinguishable kinds. The autism group scored non-zero more often on asking for information (90.0% against 50.0%), emphatic or emotional gestures (74.0% against 40.0%), unusual eye contact (72.0% against 22.5%), language production linked to nonverbal communication (90.0% against 55.0%) and quality of social overtures (88.0% against 47.5%). The schizophrenia group scored non-zero more often on reporting of events (60.0% against 24.0%), conversation (57.5% against 32.0%), communication of own affect (80.0% against 54.0%) and comments on others' emotions or empathy (75.0% against 34.0%). Roughly speaking, the autistic profile concentrates in the mechanics of nonverbal social exchange - gaze, gesture, the coordination of speech with nonverbal behaviour, the initiation of overtures - while the schizophrenia profile concentrates in the content and organisation of discourse and in affective and empathic commentary. The finding that matters for every behavioural study in this review is that a measure sensitive to social-communication atypicality in general will flag both groups, and that separating them requires attending to which atypicalities are present rather than how many.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Vocalisation and speech, with the target construct stated as prosodic. The motivating account is specific: autistic speech is monotonous and 'lacks the typical variations in pitch, intonation, and expressive elements that are commonly observed in the speech of typically developing children', a pattern reported to persist into school age. Both speech and non-speech vocalisations are used from De-Enigma, and the authors defend that choice on communicative grounds - 'non-verbal vocalisations are a form of speech and hold communicative value' - and argue it extends the approach toward pre-linguistic assessment in younger children. What the study cannot establish is whether its models respond to that construct. The representation is a learned embedding of the raw waveform, no acoustic analysis or attribution is performed, and prosody is not measured directly at any point, so the models' 94.8% could rest on fundamental-frequency variability, on vocal-tract length, on speaking rate, on the language spoken, on the age of the speaker, or on the reverberation of the room. The four-class task is more informative about the construct than the binary one, because separating autism from dysphasia requires something more specific than general atypicality of speech - and it is precisely there that performance falls to 60.9%, below the baseline of 62.4%.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: Written language produced in unconstrained public communication - the only such behaviour in the review, and the largest behavioural record it contains. Three analytic layers were applied: sentiment polarity via VADER, computed on both the raw corpus and a profanity-censored version with the two found to be almost identical; topic analysis for qualitative insight; and lexical-distributional modelling through TF-IDF and word2vec for classification. What the study cannot say is which linguistic properties distinguish the groups, because no feature analysis or attribution is reported for the classifiers. The behaviour targeted is therefore best described as 'written register' rather than any specific construct, and the ambiguity between two candidate constructs - autistic language production on the one hand, and participation in an advocacy discourse on the other - is the study's central unresolved question. It is worth noting against this that the authors' preprocessing removes a sixteen-item vocabulary specifically to prevent the second construct from being trivially detectable, which is more than most studies in this corpus do about their own confounds even when they name them.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: Two behavioural channels selected to be complementary, and the study's own analysis of what each captures is the most informative such account in the review. The video channel targets whole-body movement and gestural interaction within the child-examiner dyad, and its confidence relates most strongly to initiation of joint attention, quality of social overtures, unusual eye contact and pointing gestures - a coherent nonverbal social-communication cluster, and exactly what one would predict for a model of interactive body motion. The audio channel targets the full acoustic band without diarisation, so it contains child vocalisation, examiner speech and ambient sound from object manipulation - and its confidence relates most strongly to showing behaviour, pointing gesture, unusual sensory exploration and hand mannerisms, which are not vocal constructs at all. The authors draw the correct inference: the audio model is probably keying substantially on non-vocal sound produced by the child's interaction with objects, with sensory interests the single most correlated item, and possibly also on the examiner's prosodic adaptation to the child. This is a rare and important result for the review. It shows that a modality label ('audio') does not determine the construct measured, that a model can succeed by detecting the acoustic signature of behaviour rather than of speech, and that when a recording captures a dyad the model may be measuring the wrong member of it. Any study in this corpus using undiarised interaction audio inherits both possibilities, and none of the others examines them.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: Two constructs, only one of which the pipeline is well matched to. The classifier targets facial appearance in crops taken from videos whose defining content is self-stimulatory movement - spinning, head banging, arm flapping - so the behaviour that identifies the corpus is cropped away before modelling, leaving whatever differs in the face. The authors recognise this obliquely by proposing gesture analysis as future work. The affect regressor targets emotional expression in the continuous arousal-valence plane, and here the construct choice is well argued: the paper notes that affective computing has concentrated on discrete emotion categories, that 'conventional methods of estimating or quantifying affect in neurotypical individuals are not effective for individuals with mental health disorders', and that no dataset of continuous affect labels for autistic children existed - which the authors then set out to remedy. The resulting demonstration that a neurotypical-trained affect model transfers poorly to autistic faces is a substantive statement about the construct itself: emotional expression in autistic children is not the same measurement problem as in neurotypical adults, and models built on the latter do not simply generalise.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Two constructs from one sensor, and the choice is better motivated than most in this review. Facial mood is classified into five categories - neutral, anger, sadness, fear and happiness - and skin temperature is measured directly, on the physiological rationale that pulsating blood flow drives the largest facial temperature variations and that emotional change produces detectable thermal change in facial skin. The target is therefore emotional state and autonomic arousal rather than social communication, gaze or motor stereotypy, which distinguishes this study from nearly all of the corpus and connects it plausibly to the clinical problem it addresses: the medications at issue are prescribed largely for irritability and agitation, so a continuous measure of affective state and arousal is the right construct for titrating them. Three problems attach to the execution. The mood labels for thermal images of these particular children must have been assigned by someone, and the paper never says who or how - so a five-category emotional ground truth exists with no stated provenance, in a population whose facial expression is itself atypical. Skin temperature is confounded with ambient conditions and exertion across four physically different capture settings with no compensation. And no feature importance is reported for the severity classifiers, so whether the discriminative information lies in mood or in temperature - a question with entirely different clinical implications - is unknown.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Nominally craniofacial morphology; operationally, whatever separates an autism-labelled image folder from a folder of web-search results. The motivating claims are specific and measurable - broader upper faces, wider eyes, shorter nasal bridges, narrower cheeks - but nothing in the pipeline measures any of them: no landmarks are detected, no distances or ratios computed, and the models receive whole RGB images. What the networks can key on is unconstrained and includes apparent age, sex, ancestry, expression, pose, resolution, compression, lighting and background, all of which are free to differ between two folders built by different routes. The paper's third stated contribution was to analyse which facial features drive detection, which would have been the direct test of its own premise; that analysis does not appear.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: Structural and quantitative properties of spontaneous speech, operationalised as six standard psycholinguistic descriptors: mean length of utterance, mean length of turn, mean word length, number of utterances, total number of words and number of different words. Two design decisions distinguish this from a generic bag-of-features approach. Each feature was computed both for the child alone and as a ratio to the investigator's value in the same session, and the two versions were compared empirically to see which carried more information - a construct-level question about whether autistic children's speech differs absolutely or relative to their conversational partner's. And the count-based features were used only in ratio form to normalise for transcript length. The results locate the discriminative information in utterance and turn length and in the child's output relative to the adult's, with typically developing children higher on cMLU, rMLU, rMLT, rUtts and rTNW - a coherent picture of shorter utterances, shorter turns and proportionally less talk. Mean word length carried no signal, and the paper draws the right conclusion, that characters are a poor proxy for lexical complexity and that phonemes or morphemes would be the correct unit. The construct that this cannot separate from autism is expressive language level, of which MLU is a canonical index.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Whole-body movement kinematics, and the construct argument is one of the better ones in this review. Gait and gesture are presented as 'prominent behavioural markers' that can be 'efficiently and non-intrusively captured', and the case for preferring them to language-based assessment is made explicitly: diagnosis 'often requires speech-based tests', yet at the early detection stage 'many young children may not yet be able to speak'. That identifies a genuine coverage gap - the transcript-based and conversational measures charted elsewhere in this review are inapplicable to non-speaking and pre-verbal children, who are precisely the population early detection targets. The operationalisation is only partly matched to the argument. In the Gait dataset the construct is walking, measured across 25 full-body joints, which is the right instrument for the claim. In DREAM only 10 upper-body joints are available and the movements arise from therapy interaction, so gait is not measurable and the second experiment addresses a different construct under the same label. And no interpretability analysis connects the models to any nameable movement characteristic, so what aspect of gait the 95.4% reflects - stride variability, arm swing, postural sway, turning - is unknown, despite skeleton data making such an analysis unusually accessible.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Cry acoustics, and specifically voice quality rather than cry structure. Three perturbation measures were analysed - jitter, shimmer and harmonics-to-noise ratio - selected because of their established clinical use in voice assessment. The construct choice is the study's strongest conceptual contribution and is unique in this review: cry is available before any language develops, is produced by every child regardless of cognitive or verbal level, requires no cooperation, no task compliance and no social engagement, and directly reflects neuromuscular control of the larynx and respiratory system. The paper's formulation is apt - 'infant cries provide a unique window into the neurological and physiological state of the infant' - and it identifies prior work reporting atypical cry acoustics in autistic toddlers under 18 months, which is younger than any other behavioural measure charted here can reach. The findings are physiologically legible: higher jitter and shimmer mean greater cycle-to-cycle instability in the frequency and amplitude of vocal fold vibration, and lower harmonics-to-noise ratio means a greater proportion of aperiodic energy, so the composite picture is of less stable phonatory control. Two constructs are conspicuously not addressed: the temporal and prosodic structure of the cry, which prior work also implicates, and the communicative function of crying, which is discarded when only 'pure crying sounds' are retained.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: None observed. The A1-A10 fields are a respondent's answers to ten statements about their own social-communication characteristics, and the remaining fields are registration metadata. These are self-characterisations rather than records of behaviour produced, which is the distinction this review applies when admitting app telemetry, written language or nurse-recorded milestone attainment as behavioural data.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: The broadest simultaneous behavioural coverage from a single camera in this review: facial configuration and expression through a 468-point face mesh, whole-body posture through 33 pose points, and manual gesture through 21 points per hand, all captured at 30 frames per second and reduced to a 1,639-value vector per frame. Two derived measures add interpretable structure. The mouth aspect ratio - the ratio of vertical to horizontal lip distance - is a compact index of mouth opening that relates to both expression and vocalisation. Motion energy, defined as the mean Euclidean displacement of landmark coordinates between consecutive frames and computed separately for the face, the pose and each hand, is a clean measure of how much each body region moves per unit time, and its per-region computation means motor activity can be localised rather than aggregated. The stated behavioural targets - reduced eye contact, atypical emotional expression, and repetitive stereotypical movement - map reasonably onto these streams, though gaze itself is not measured directly and stereotypy is not identified as such, only as elevated hand motion energy. The visualisations reported (heat maps and movement-energy graphs) show group differences in motor activity and facial expression, but no ablation determines which stream the classifier uses, which leaves the construct claim unresolved.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: Two constructs of very different tractability. For autism, static facial appearance and expression, with the usual consequence that the model receives everything an uncontrolled photograph contains - morphology, expression at the captured instant, pose, apparent age, ancestry, resolution and image provenance - and no analysis identifies which of these it uses. For gelotophobia, the paper proposes to read a dispositional social fear from a still facial image. This is the weakest construct mapping in the review and its weakness is structural rather than a matter of execution: gelotophobia is defined by how a person interprets laughter directed at them, it is measured by self-report for that reason, and no laughter, social interaction or ridicule appears anywhere in the data. The paper's own finding that DeepFace 'was insufficient' for ambiguous facial cues, and its observation that fear and disgust involve minimal facial muscle movement, both point toward the same conclusion without stating it - that the construct is not visible in a photograph. The fallback offered is the GELOPH<15> self-report, which is the appropriate instrument and which the study did not administer.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Nominally craniofacial morphology and operationally whatever separates two internet image folders. The motivating claims are unusually specific - wider eyes, larger mouth, shorter mid-face, broader upper face, pronounced philtrum, shorter nose - and none is measured: no landmarks are detected, no distances or ratios computed, and the models receive whole preprocessed face crops. The three preprocessing configurations do bear on this indirectly and constitute the study's most interesting technical choice: greyscale conversion removes colour and therefore skin tone, and CLAHE normalises local contrast, so the greyscale-plus-CLAHE configuration strips two of the appearance cues most likely to differ between image sources. Comparing configurations that differ in exactly which appearance information is retained is the right instinct for this problem, and a systematic report of accuracy across the three would have been informative about how much of the signal survives when colour and illumination are removed. That comparison is set up and its results are not broken out in the retrieved text.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: Two constructs, of very different tractability. The autism task targets facial morphology, on the premise that autistic children 'show morphological differences within their face' - a physiognomic claim, unmeasured here, with the models receiving whole face images so that expression, pose, apparent age, ancestry and image provenance are all equally available. The emotion task targets six-way facial expression in autistic children specifically, and the construct argument for it is the paper's strongest contribution: general-population emotion models are 'primarily trained for healthy ones and consequently missing abnormal facial movements'. That correctly identifies a real gap, and the resulting 73.33% is instructive precisely because it is modest - emotion recognition on posed neurotypical adult faces reaches 98-99% in the benchmark literature charted elsewhere in this review, so a drop to the low seventies on autistic children's faces is consistent with the independent finding that affect models transfer poorly across this population. Read together with that study, this one supplies a second data point for the same conclusion.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: Facial appearance, described more honestly than in most of this branch. Rather than asserting a specific craniofacial phenotype, the paper says the network finds 'important patterns in the image, such as the shape of the face, the expression on it, and the texture of the skin'. That enumeration is accurate about what a whole-image CNN actually receives, and it names two properties - expression and skin texture - that are not morphological and would vary with photographic circumstance rather than with the child. Naming skin texture as a used feature is particularly pointed in a corpus mixing an internationally scraped collection with photographs from an Indonesian clinic, since skin appearance in an image is jointly determined by ancestry, lighting and camera. No landmark geometry or morphometric quantity is computed anywhere.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Visual attention allocation during free viewing - fixation position (point of regard, left and right eye), gaze direction vectors in three dimensions, and the categorical annotation of what was being looked at (Category_Right, Category_Left) alongside stimulus identity. The behavioural construct is therefore where the child looks, sampled instantaneously, with no aggregation into fixations, saccades, dwell times or AOI proportions.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Early social-communication behaviours as reported by a caregiver: response to name, ease of eye contact, requesting gestures, declarative pointing, pretend play, gaze following, comforting a distressed family member, early speech quality, conventional gestures such as waving goodbye, and prolonged purposeless staring. After correlation-based deletion only five of these (A3 requesting gestures, A4 pointing, A5 pretend play, A7 comforting, A10 staring) remain as predictors.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: Static facial morphology rather than behaviour: inter-landmark geometry and facial asymmetry, operationalised as upper-face breadth, eye spacing, mid-face length and jawline shape, over landmarks at the eye corners, eyebrows, nose tip, mouth corners and jaw outline. The theoretical warrant offered is that discrepancies in facial landmarks between those with ASD and those without indicate underlying variances in brain development.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Visual attention during viewing of a speaking face, decomposed into fixation position (x, y), fixation duration and inter-fixation velocity, and into scanpath shape compared by DTW and MultiMatch. The behavioural claims that emerge are specific and testable: attention duration and vertical gaze distribution differ most across severity levels, velocity least, and children with ASD show highly individualised rather than merely reduced gaze patterns.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: None. No behaviour is observed, elicited or measured. The target is static facial appearance - edges, contours and textures at multiple Gabor orientations and scales, described as capturing intricate details of face characteristics including the eyes, nose and mouth.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Movement kinematics and eye-movement behaviour, split into general and attention-specific variants: 120 kinematic features and 48 observational-behavioural features per instructional segment, with the attention-specific eye subset described as covering fixation and saccade characteristics. Because no task is described and no feature is ever named, the behavioural content of the study is opaque - the reader cannot identify a single behaviour that distinguishes the groups.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: Posed facial expression - flat, smiling and sad - and, implicitly, static facial appearance. Because expressions are pooled before classification, the study cannot say whether the model distinguishes groups by how the children produce expressions or by how their faces look, and the paper does not raise the distinction.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Parent-reported early social-communication behaviours drawn from Q-CHAT-10. The SHAP analysis names three specifically: joint attention (does your child follow where you are looking), use of simple gestures, and empathy-related behaviours. These are clinically sensible early markers, and the paper notes correctly that they correspond to established clinical markers - but their prominence in the model is a property of how the label was constructed, not independent evidence about them.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Parent-reported early social-communication behaviours from Q-CHAT-10 - response to name, eye contact, gestures, pointing, pretend play, gaze following, comforting, early speech, staring. No behaviour is observed, and the physical and verbal performance invoked in the Phase II framing does not exist in the data.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Parent-reported early social-communication behaviours from the Q-CHAT: response to name, ease of eye contact, pointing to express desires, and the remaining seven items, each mapped to a DSM-5 behavioural domain. The item-level analysis produces a consistent ordering - Q9, Q6 and Q5 most informative, Q8 and Q10 least - which is the paper's substantive behavioural claim.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: Camouflaging behaviour, decomposed into compensation (copying others' behaviours, preparing scripts for social situations), masking (controlling and adjusting facial and bodily expression to fit in) and assimilation (effortful engagement and pretending to be normal in social situations). The outcomes are dimensional autistic traits - aloof personality, pragmatic language, rigid personality - and depressive and anxious symptoms. The behaviour of interest is therefore an active social strategy rather than a deficit, and the study is the only one in the corpus to treat an autistic behaviour as adaptive rather than symptomatic.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: None. The classification target is static facial appearance. The paper's own account of what the model attends to - periocular regions, eye gaze, mouth movements, asymmetric facial movements - describes dynamic behaviours that a single photograph cannot contain, so the stated biomarker rationale and the actual input are mismatched.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: None. No behaviour is observed, elicited or measured. The target is static facial appearance recovered from deblurring and denoising.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Autistic traits as captured by the ten AQ-10 items, characterised in the XAI discussion as communication patterns, repetitive actions and frequency of eye contact. All behaviour is second-hand and questionnaire-mediated, reported by a family member, healthcare professional or unspecified other.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Social attention during simultaneous presentation of social and non-social stimuli: preferential looking to faces versus objects, indexed by fixation duration, fixation count, visit duration and latency to first fixation, across areas of interest from whole-stimulus categories down to eyes and mouth and across three emotional expressions. The substantive behavioural finding is about objects rather than faces - mean duration of visits to objects discriminates, which the authors interpret as difficulty disengaging attention from objects rather than as reduced interest in faces.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: Visual scanning behaviour, encoded as a rendered scanpath image showing the geometric trace of fixations and saccades. Because the images are treated as pictures rather than as sequences, no fixation duration, saccade amplitude, area-of-interest dwell or temporal ordering is extracted or reported - the behavioural content of the data is entirely implicit in the picture.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: Parent-reported early social-communication behaviour, entirely unspecified - the article names the Q-CHAT-10 instrument and describes its scoring rule but never states or discusses a single item, so no behaviour is identified anywhere in the paper.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Fine motor kinematics during constrained tracing: speed, acceleration, jerk, minimum and maximum speed, number of sub-movements, speed modulation (how sharply speed adapts to trajectory curvature), smoothness via SPARC, and tracing error, plus simple reaction time. The discriminating features are specific and directional - autistic participants showed greater speed modulation and more sub-movements than both other groups, and differed from PD in reaction time - and the paper is careful about mechanism, noting that reported increases in jerk in autism may be epiphenomenal on speed differences because the two quantities are mathematically linked.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: Screening-item behaviours from the A1-A10 instruments, organised into three domains - social communication difficulties, repetitive behaviour and a cognitive assessment component - which supply the weighted terms of the constructed severity index. The correlation analysis relates the composite Q_SCORE to social communication difficulties (r 0.64-0.67) and repetitive behaviour (r 0.45-0.63) and reports moderate inter-item correlations (r 0.10-0.46), read as each item adding unique variance.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: Developmental screening behaviours as captured by ASQ, CSBS, PEDS, M-CHAT and STAT items - communication through eye movements and repetitive hand and finger movements are the only behaviours described concretely - together with imaging and physiological modalities named but not characterised.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: Self-stimulatory motor behaviour observed in natural settings: arm flapping, head banging and spinning, against a fourth class of non-stereotyped movement. This is the corpus's clearest instance of behaviour being observed directly rather than inferred from a photograph, a checklist or a questionnaire - the behaviours are the ones clinicians actually watch for, recorded where they actually occur. The confusion-matrix analysis adds a substantive behavioural observation: errors concentrate between spinning and the two repetitive classes, attributed to overlap in motion dynamics, and normal behaviour is moderately confused with the repetitive classes in the held-out test.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Social attention to a speaking face, decomposed by facial region and by time relative to speech onset: fixation count, average fixation duration, dwell-time and fixation-time percentages, normalised dwell coverage and revisits, for the eyes, mouth and nose separately. The substantive behavioural findings are specific and testable - eye revisits and mouth fixation count rank highest in importance, mouth fixation time and cross-AOI revisits emerge as candidate biomarkers under both attribution methods, and the audio-visual advantage is concentrated in the pre-speech phase, which the authors read as anticipatory attention to the mouth before speech begins.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: Dataset 1: screening-questionnaire responses and comorbidity flags, none of them examined individually. Dataset 2: the most behaviourally specific description in the paper - velocity, acceleration, jerk, movement range, coordination and repetitive behavioural patterns from body keypoints, alongside voice quality and autonomic arousal - describing exactly the kind of multimodal behavioural measurement this literature needs, for a dataset whose existence the paper does not evidence.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Neuropsychological performance across three domains rather than a single behavioural marker: multisensory perceptual integration, emotion recognition (with accuracy and reaction time varying by emotional category and stimulus type), and executive function. The substantive behavioural findings are specific - reaction-time variables consistently ranked high in predictive value, and executive function emerged as informative in this adult sample - and the paper is careful that the ranking is sample-dependent.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: Visual scanning behaviour reduced to nine interpretable descriptors: number of fixations, mean and maximum and first fixation duration, total fixation duration, total path length, mean saccade amplitude, spatial dispersion of fixations, and fixation-duration entropy as a measure of irregularity in gaze allocation. Operating on these rather than on rendered scanpath images is the paper's central methodological claim, and it is a defensible one - the features are inspectable and the permutation analysis can name which of them matter.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: None. No behaviour is observed or measured; the target is static facial appearance, described in terms of symmetry, eye spacing, philtrum width and face shape.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: None. No behaviour is observed or measured. The targets are static facial features enhanced by Gabor filtering, with the paper referring to facial cues relevant to ASD and to expression patterns and facial morphology without identifying any specific feature.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Motor function measured directly in three dimensions: inter-joint distances, range of motion, gait speed, step length and cycle time, and temporal characteristics, over 25 skeletal joints. The behavioural claims arising from SHAP are anatomically specific - wrist movements, knee trajectories and elbow-to-foot distances - and are related to motor impairments reported in the prior ASD literature rather than presented as novel discoveries. A structural pattern is also reported: Y-axis features decline (30% to 10% to 0%) and X-axis features increase (70% to 90% to 100%) with increasing severity, though the severe end of that gradient is synthetic.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Expressive language and conversational participation in spontaneous interaction. The two leading features are behaviourally specific and directionally interpretable: Mean Length of Utterance, where lower values indicate shorter and simpler utterances and are associated with higher ASD likelihood, and Mean Length of Turn Ratio, the child's turn length relative to the adult's, where lower values indicate that the child contributes less to conversational exchange. Both correspond to well-established clinical observations, and the paper relates them accordingly rather than presenting them as discoveries.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: Executive function as elicited by three purpose-built games - planning, cognitive flexibility, inhibitory control, working memory and performance monitoring - captured through session-level telemetry including duration and task-performance fields. This is behaviour observed during a designed task rather than reported on a checklist or inferred from an appearance, and the construct is theoretically motivated rather than chosen for convenience. What the paper does not do is say which behaviours distinguished the groups: no feature importance is reported, so the executive-function framing that justifies the whole design is never connected to a result.

questions.question_text: How are multiple behavioural modalities fused, if at all?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion. No combination with clinical scores or demographics.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion across behavioral modalities. IQ and chronological age are used as ANCOVA covariates in the group comparison but are not combined with kinematics in the classifier.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: Two behavioral streams (correctness and latency) are combined by simple feature concatenation (RC&RT) and compared against each separately - an early-fusion feature-level combination. No integration with clinical scores, demographics or parent report.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion is performed. The discussion explicitly proposes future multimodal fusion with physiological, speech, motion and facial-expression measures. Within the modality, image-level decisions are fused to a participant-level decision by averaging confidence scores - a late/decision-level fusion across stimuli rather than across modalities.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Single modality. Positive and negative descriptions are analysed both combined and separately (the network difference loses significance when split, which the authors attribute to reduced power). Demographic and cognitive variables (age, gender, verbal IQ, vocabulary, WMS) are added to the classifier as covariates and do not improve performance - an integration attempt that is reported as null rather than omitted.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Two behavioral data streams from the same device - touch and inertial - are combined by feature concatenation into a single 247-dimensional vector (early/feature-level fusion). Predictions from the two games are additionally averaged per child, a decision-level fusion across tasks that produced the best AUC (0.932) - higher than either game alone. Age and gender are included as features in ET, RF and RGF, and deliberately excluded in RGF2, which performed best, showing the result does not depend on demographic inputs.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion across behavioral modalities. Within the modality there is a form of condition-level fusion: features from the two best conditions (No-Target Fast and No-Target Elevated) are combined into a joint 40-feature vector, which raised Naive Bayes accuracy from 70.0% and 66.7% individually to 83.3% jointly - an explicit demonstration that combining task conditions helps. IQ and age are used as matching variables, not as model inputs.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: Six behavioral feature families are combined by concatenation into a single normalised vector before classification - early/feature-level fusion - with temporal structure preserved by computing each family separately per story segment and concatenating across the 12 segments, which the authors describe as trading a twelvefold dimensionality increase for retained temporal information. No integration with clinical scores or demographics.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion. Video was recorded but used only for segmentation and annotation, not as a modelling input - a notable choice given that the same recordings could have supported gaze or motor analysis. Within the modality, per-vocalisation decisions are aggregated into a subject-level judgement by computing an ASD ratio and thresholding it, which is a late/decision-level fusion across utterances.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion. Two acoustic feature sets are compared rather than combined, and no combination with clinical, cognitive or demographic data is performed. The future-work section proposes extending the approach to video and physiological signals, but no multimodal work is done here.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Single modality, but with a form of within-modality fusion: features from all three orthogonal GRF components (medial-lateral, anterior-posterior, vertical) are pooled into one candidate set, and the three surviving features happen to come one from each component - so the discriminative signal is genuinely distributed across all three force directions. No combination with clinical, cognitive or demographic data.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Two feature families derived from the same modality - similarity of time-weighted spatial occupancy patterns, and the presence ratio in the robot-facing cell - are each fed to separate first-layer classifiers whose outputs are combined by a second-layer classifier. The authors describe this explicitly as a form of sensor fusion, though both inputs come from one sensor; it is decision-level fusion across feature views. Notably the fusion helped only the SVM (75% and 75% to 81.3%) and hurt the other four classifiers (dropping to 68.8%). No integration with clinical scores, demographics or parent report.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion. Within the modality, ten regional fixation times plus three derived ratios are supplied jointly to the SVM, which is feature-level combination across regions. Gaze data are separately correlated with Gesell developmental subscores using age and gender as covariates - an integration with clinical measures for interpretation rather than for prediction.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Fusion is the paper's central methodological claim and is done at two levels. Across modalities: acoustic and linguistic features are extracted separately and concatenated. Across sources: features from four structured tests plus passive monitoring plus usage pattern are all concatenated into one 1330-dimensional vector, with missing sources explicitly encoded as -1 so the model can handle non-participation rather than requiring imputation. The benefit is quantified by ablation - every single source scored 0.47-0.77 alone against 0.87 fused - and confirmed by CFS selecting at least one feature from each source, which the authors correctly note implies the sources are complementary rather than redundant given CFS's redundancy penalty. No integration with clinical scores or demographics, deliberately.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Single modality. Gaze features are combined at feature level with non-gaze contextual variables (page identity, AOI identity, correct-answer location, gender, visual complexity), and the paper reports that these additions generally reduced accuracy relative to gaze features alone - a negative fusion result reported plainly. Behaviour-level predictions are aggregated to a participant-level decision by majority vote, a late fusion across observations. The discussion proposes future fusion with non-gaze interaction data (mouse clicks, operation logs) as a route to eye-tracker-free deployment.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Single modality, no fusion. There is a form of temporal-spatial integration internal to the model - the LSTM's learned attention map weights spatial CNN features at each time step based on its accumulated hidden state, so spatial and temporal information are combined adaptively rather than by fixed pooling. Frame-level probabilities are averaged into a per-subject decision, a late fusion across frames and clips. No combination with clinical scores, IQ or demographics, despite those being available.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Single modality, but with an unusual internal contrast: spatial-only and spatial-plus-temporal representations of the same data are constructed through identical pipelines and compared, which is a form of ablation rather than fusion. Left and right eye representations are kept separate and both included as features, motivated by a possible lateral offset with each eye directed slightly toward its own side of the face. Face emotion, gender, age and task type were tested as additional predictors and reported as not significantly improving either model.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Single modality; no fusion. Within the modality, three kinematic quantities (amplitude, velocity, acceleration) are each summarised by two complexity measures (entropy and 95% range) and three cross-trial aggregates (min, median, max), giving an 18-feature grid, and the selected model combines amplitude-range and velocity-range/entropy features - so the fusion is across kinematic derivatives and trial aggregates. The discussion proposes future integration with genetic, neuroimaging and psychological data.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Two-way fusion. Across modality: 352 acoustic and 272 text features are concatenated into a single 624-dimensional vector, then reduced by correlation filtering and PCA - so acoustic and lexical information are combined at feature level. Across speaker: features from the child and the confederate are both included, and the results show confederate features were selected in all 70 folds for several jitter and HNR measures, making interlocutor behaviour an explicit part of the model. Demographic and clinical variables were tested as additional inputs and reported as unhelpful (age and sex) or harmful (IQ), which the authors correctly attribute to prior matching - a negative fusion result reported rather than omitted.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Feature-level fusion across the three families into a single per-fixation vector, and the contribution of each is ablated separately at fixation, trial and subject level - so the complementarity claim is directly evidenced. The clearest demonstration is that task features alone reach 81.0% subject-level accuracy but only 56.5% sensitivity, while adding gaze and face features raises sensitivity to 91.3% at similar accuracy. Predictions are additionally fused across observations by soft voting from fixations to trials to subjects, with accuracy rising monotonically (72.5% to 75.6% to 86.2%) as the aggregation unit widens.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Fusion occurs across annotators rather than across modalities, and this is the paper's methodological contribution. Each rater's annotations train a separate random forest, and predictions are combined by a softmax-weighted ensemble whose weights reflect each rater's model accuracy relative to a majority-vote baseline. The authors argue this lets the ensemble exploit each rater's strengths (one may rate eye contact well, another language ability) while discounting their weaknesses, and note it permits distributed annotation where each rater sees only a subset of videos without requiring imputation. A second form of composition is the stacked two-layer architecture, where layer one's atypical classifications feed layer two.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Single behavioural modality, but with genuine cross-source integration: three feature families (image content, fixation behaviour, centre bias) are concatenated for the classifier, and two of them require fusing gaze data with image-analysis outputs (YOLO object masks and SDSP saliency maps). This gaze-plus-stimulus-content fusion is a distinctive design in the corpus, though its contribution is never ablated so the value of each family is unknown. No integration with clinical, cognitive or demographic data - the latter being impossible given the dataset.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Multiple cue types are combined within each task's observation set and jointly update a shared belief over child condition, engagement and verbal activity - so eye contact, utterances, imitation and gestures fuse probabilistically into one latent state estimate. The hierarchical structure adds a second fusion level: each task's terminal belief is discretised into a partition index that becomes an observation for the protocol-level model, so information accumulates across tasks. This belief-space-partitioning interface is the paper's central technical contribution and is a genuinely different fusion mechanism from the feature concatenation used everywhere else in the corpus.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Single modality, no fusion. Per-ROI mean fixation durations are concatenated into a single feature vector per participant, described as capturing the time distribution of visual attention across regions - a within-modality spatial aggregation rather than multimodal fusion. No integration with clinical scores, demographics or the medical-history data the workflow collects.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Single modality, but with two distinct feature families combined - movement kinematics and endpoint accuracy - which is what allows the speed-accuracy trade-off to emerge. Features from dominant and non-dominant hands are pooled into means and standard deviations, a form of within-modality aggregation. No integration with clinical, cognitive or demographic data.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Single modality, but with an internal fusion of four kinematic quantities into one image: spatial path as line geometry, velocity as the red channel, acceleration as green and jerk as blue. This packs position and its first three temporal derivatives into a single representation that a generic image classifier can consume - an elegant encoding, though the subsequent grayscale conversion collapses the three colour channels back into a single luminance value, discarding the channel separation the encoding created.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Single modality in this analysis. The parent study measured interpersonal coordination between dyad members, but this classification uses intrapersonal synchrony only. Features from four separate interaction tasks are aggregated per participant, a form of fusion across contexts. The future-work section explicitly proposes multimodal fusion with eye-gaze, facial expression and clinical questionnaire data, and Box 1 lists 'combination of objective variables and standard diagnostic measures as input features' as a minimum requirement for reliable clinical application.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Two synchronous sensor streams from a single consumer device - touch-screen contact patterns and triaxial accelerometer plus gyroscope - capturing both what the child does to the screen and how the device moves while they do it. The fusion is inherent to the platform rather than engineered, which is part of the design's practical appeal: no synchronisation, no calibration and no additional hardware is required to obtain two complementary views of the same motor behaviour.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Two forms of fusion. In the synthetic saccade approach, real and synthetic scanpaths are aligned by dynamic time warping and concatenated along with aggregate duration statistics and three trajectory distance measures - fusing observed behaviour with a model-generated reference. In the image-based approach, a two-branch architecture separately encodes the stimulus image (frozen pretrained ResNet-18) and the fixation channels (ResNet-18 with a 33-channel input layer), concatenating their 512-dimensional outputs into a 1024-dimensional vector - fusing stimulus content with gaze behaviour. Both are stimulus-plus-behaviour fusions rather than multi-behavioural fusions.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Single modality in this work. Within it, the PoTion representation performs a spatiotemporal fusion: keypoint heatmaps from up to 301 frames are colourised by body region and by relative time, then aggregated into one image, so a 10-second motion sequence is compressed into a single static RGB frame that a standard convolutional classifier can consume. The colour channels carry body-region identity and the intensity gradient carries temporal order, which is an elegant encoding of three information types into three channels. Future fusion with RGB appearance and audio is proposed.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: Spatial rather than modal fusion, and it is the architecture's central idea. Multiple RGBD cameras each estimate head pose and gaze independently and publish them as ROS odometry messages; a fusion node performs asynchronous matching across all local estimates and computes a single visual focus of attention through a Hidden Markov Model, published with a timestamp and the name of the attention target. Fusing viewpoints to recover a gaze target is a direct answer to the occlusion problem that limits single-camera gaze measurement with moving children - the paper reports occlusion 'by hair, hands and the robot' as encountered in practice - and the HMM adds temporal smoothing so that the attention target is inferred from a sequence rather than frame by frame. No other study in this review builds comparable measurement infrastructure, and the fact that it is assembled from open-source components on ROS makes it reproducible in principle.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Fusion of behavioural and stimulus-derived information at two levels. Per fixation, a 1024-dimensional CNN encoding of the saliency-map patch is concatenated with the fixation duration, giving a 1025-dimensional vector that combines spatial-saliency context with temporal information. Across fixations, a two-layer LSTM integrates the sequence, explicitly to capture 'the temporal information and sequential dependency of the scanpaths'. No fusion across behavioural modalities and no integration with clinical or demographic data - the latter being impossible given the dataset.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: None. A single video stream coded by human raters, with the robot's own sensors unused for measurement. The paper's engineering framing points toward using them - it is explicitly gathering requirements for an 'interaction diagnosis system' - but no automated sensing is implemented here.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion. All features come from a single modality (video-coded social behaviour). The study's structural comparison is instead across conditions of the same modality: the still-face episode versus the free-interaction episode, and the still-face episode won for every classifier (83.35 vs 81.18 for SVM, 83.13 vs 80.72 for random forest, 82.35 vs 80.54 for naive Bayes). This is a useful counterpoint to the corpus's fusion studies - here the gain comes from choosing a better elicitation condition rather than adding a sensor.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Explicit multimodal fusion with quantified benefit: kinematic features alone gave 73%, eye movement features alone 70%, and combined features 78%. The authors state that the modalities 'provided complementary information for predictions', and the 5-point gain over the better single modality is one of the clearest quantified fusion benefits in the corpus, obtained under independent testing rather than internal cross-validation. Features are combined at feature level before selection and classification.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion. Adding recognition of children's physical movement to achieve 'diagnosis of autism from multiple perspectives' is named as future work. There is a nominal model-level combination - VGG-19 and ResNet-18 are said to be trained and then 'synthesised' - but no mechanism, weighting or comparative result is given for either model separately, so the combination cannot be evaluated.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Single modality, but with a designed within-modality manipulation: the same six COP variables are measured under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions and both sets are supplied jointly to the classifiers, giving 12 features. This effectively fuses two sensory conditions, allowing the models to exploit how each child's sway changes when visual input is removed. No integration with clinical, cognitive or demographic data, though anthropometrics were collected.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Feature-level fusion of the two modalities: 3 Laban movement features are concatenated with 68 facial keypoints into a single 71-dimensional vector per 1-second window, so movement and facial information are combined before classification. There is no ablation isolating either modality's contribution, so their relative value is unknown. The discussion proposes future fusion with physiological, eye gaze and vocal data.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: Single modality, with a designed internal fusion: spatial distance and two temporal asynchrony measures (lag and advance) are combined by learned linear weights into one continuous score, so spatial and temporal aspects of imitation are integrated rather than treated separately. The authors argue this integration is necessary 'given the importance of timing in social coordination and in characterizing autism-specific imitation impairments'. Separately, the CAMI score is validated against and correlated with independent clinical instruments (ADOS-2, SRS-2, MABC-2), which is convergent validation rather than fusion.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion - audio only, and the paper notes that video recordings existed but only their audio was used. The structural comparison it does make is across feature representations of the same modality: raw eGeMAPS-88, statistically selected eGeMAPS-54, and learned auto-encoder bottleneck features. Extension to linguistic features alongside acoustic ones for older children is named as future work.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion. A single modality throughout. The paper's structural comparison is instead between two aggregation levels of the same modality - the gait cycle and the walking trial - which is a distinct axis from the sensor-fusion comparisons elsewhere in the corpus and arguably a more fundamental one, since it concerns what a data point is rather than what it contains.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion - audio only. But there is a meaningful within-modality fusion result with a clear cost: the conversational features cannot be computed on short sub-groups of segments because they require the entire recording, so FC-DNN models 2 and 3 and the CNN use only the 48 acoustic and prosodic features. The best models therefore discard exactly the feature family that correlates most strongly with social affect symptoms, and still outperform the 60-feature vector model - which suggests the gain from many sub-samples outweighs the loss of conversational information, and implies an architecture that could use both would do better still.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion. Gaze only, with non-gaze metadata (AOI identity, media identity, correct-answer indicator, page visual complexity, participant gender) tested as additional variables and found in almost every case to reduce accuracy. That systematic negative result is itself the paper's fusion finding: on this data, adding non-gaze information hurt.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. There is within-modality feature fusion between learned CNN representations and handcrafted multi-level saliency features, and the ablation quantifies each family's contribution: removing CNN features costs 8.6 accuracy points, high-level semantic features 5.7, low-level 4.0 and mid-level 2.3. The paper closes by expressing the hope that the work 'can contribute to the development of multimodal approaches in the early detection and diagnosis of ASD', positioning gaze as one future component rather than a complete solution.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Multimodality here is in the stimulus rather than the sensing: a single depth camera captures movement, while visual, auditory and olfactory channels are added cumulatively to the environment. The results are informative and partly counterintuitive. For whole-body movement, discrimination is best under visual stimulation alone (89.36%) and degrades as modalities accumulate (74.47%, then 70.21%). For the head alone the pattern reverses, improving from 80.85% to 82.98% to 89.36% as sensory load rises. And pooling everything - all joints across all conditions - gives the worst result of any model at 70.21% with 45.45% sensitivity.
