The lesson transferable to the corpus's sensor-fusion studies is that indiscriminate aggregation across conditions and channels can destroy a localised signal.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: Genuinely multimodal, but with the modalities serving different functions rather than being fused as parallel evidence: audio drives temporal segmentation (locating each stimulus onset from its scripted keyword) while video drives measurement (detecting the face and classifying the expression). This division is the framework's structural idea - speech tells the system when to look, vision tells it what it sees - and it is what allows an unsegmented clinical recording to be parsed automatically. Within the vision branch there is a second fusion, between a 3D-CNN capturing temporal dynamics and a 2D-CNN capturing spatial detail, concatenated to 1024 dimensions before classification. No accuracy comparison between the branches is reported, so the contribution of each is unquantified.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion; the study is gaze-only. What it does instead is the inverse of fusion and arguably more useful: it asks how much of a large multi-paradigm battery can be discarded. The result is that 89.9% of stimuli can be removed with modest accuracy loss, and the paradigm-level analysis shows the retained signal concentrates in Dyadic Bids and Theory of Mind, both of which include visual response latency features, while Biomotion also has latency features but lacks discrete ROI measures on heads, faces, eyes and bodies. The authors hypothesise that Dyadic Bids and Theory of Mind features subsume information available in the other paradigms - a redundancy argument that is the mirror image of the fusion arguments elsewhere in this corpus.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: The clearest and most cleanly reported fusion result in the corpus, precisely because both single-modality baselines are given: EEG alone 68%, gaze alone 75.89%, fused 85.44% with AUC rising from 0.865 to 0.93. That is close to a 10-point gain over the better single modality, and the authors' rationale for expecting it is specific rather than generic - EEG abnormalities are inconsistent across the autism spectrum, particularly in high-functioning presentations, whereas 'atypical face processing' has been found 'for all types of ASD', so the modalities should fail on different subgroups. There is a second, within-modality fusion as well: own-race faces alone gave 72.33% and other-race faces 66.67%, but combining both face types gave 75.89%, better than either. The caveat is that with no validation scheme and feature selection over a much larger EEG feature pool, the size of the fusion gain cannot be taken at face value, and the identity of the 32 selected features is not disclosed so complementarity cannot be verified.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: The fusion result is negative and instructive. Gaze features alone gave the best behavioural performance (83.9% on trial 1 and on all trials), emotion confusion matrices alone performed at or below chance in two of three trials (6.5% and 35.5%), and combining all feature blocks gave 71.0% - worse than gaze alone. Adding emotion features to gaze reduced accuracy in most cells of the ablation grid. This is a rare demonstration in the corpus that multimodal combination can degrade rather than improve performance when one modality carries little signal and the feature-to-participant ratio is extreme. The critical comparison, though, is not between modalities but against the metadata baseline: age and gender alone reached 71.0% with P = .04, the same accuracy as the full model with a marginally better P value, so no combination of behavioural features demonstrably beat two demographic variables.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: A clean modality comparison with an informative asymmetry. Voice alone reached AUC 0.77, facial expression 0.74 with all 17 action units and 0.65 with the domain-selected subset, gaze 0.63, and all three combined 0.78 - so fusion added essentially nothing over voice alone, and the combined result is carried by the two strong modalities. The gaze failure is diagnosed rather than glossed: appearance-based estimation from a webcam is judged insufficiently precise for the subtle differences reported in the eye-tracking literature, and the authors explicitly recommend state-of-the-art eye trackers to test whether gaze carries information in this paradigm. The comparison between domain-selected facial features (0.65) and all available action units (0.74) is also instructive - constraining features for interpretability cost about 9 AUC points, a trade-off the authors accepted deliberately for 'transparent and explainable diagnostic decisions'.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion - a single modality throughout, and no within-modality condition comparison is exploited either. The gap and overlap blocks are described and their latency difference noted, but the paradigm's defining contrast is never used as a feature or analysed as a group-by-condition interaction, which is the main analytic opportunity the design offers and the paper leaves unused.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: Two behavioural channels are combined, but through a probabilistic model rather than a learned fusion: the posterior for each severity category is computed as the product of P(category | joint attention) and P(category | imitation). No single-channel baseline is reported, so the contribution of combining them cannot be assessed, and no ablation is performed. More problematically, the product form assumes the two observables are conditionally independent given severity - an assumption the study's own architecture violates, since the imitation module only activates once the child has sustained gaze on a robot for five seconds, making imitation performance conditional on joint attention performance by construction. There are also two sensing modalities (robot camera gaze and Kinect depth), but these map one-to-one onto the two behaviours rather than being fused.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. The combination that does occur is across time and across regions: nine segment-specific classifiers are ensembled, and the finding is that the whole is greater than any part, with every individual segment classifier below 75% while the best three-segment combination reaches it. This is a temporal rather than sensory fusion result, and it carries a clear message for the corpus's video-based studies - that a joint attention response is a sequence and that classifying any single moment of it underperforms classifying the sequence. The authors' own reading is that segments 1, 3 and 8 'present three fundamental stages of JA' and that 'the complete action process is necessary', though this identification comes from an exhaustive search rather than an a priori hypothesis.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion. What is combined is models rather than modalities: seven classifiers ensembled by probability averaging and majority voting, with the stated rationale that 'the best model that matches the pattern of this group of data well does not mean that it can be generalized to fit another group of data', so combining reduces variance and improves generalisation. That reasoning is sound and is borne out empirically - the ensemble's recall held at 0.81 then 0.77 across the two experiments while individual models swung from 0.81 to 0.55 (gradient boosting) or 0.44 to 0.00 (logistic regression). This is the corpus's clearest demonstration that ensembling buys stability under population shift, even though the underlying task here is not what the paper claims.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. The condition-level analysis serves the analogous purpose and yields a clear result: three-class accuracy falls from 81.08% to 78.4% using gaze cues alone and to 77.0% using non-gaze cues alone, so both cue families carry non-redundant information and the full set is better than either. This supports the paper's substantive claim that visual-orienting deficits in autism 'are not only tied to social cues but appear to be domain-general'. The behavioural analysis reinforces it: all three groups found face cues harder than arrow and finger cues, but the high-functioning group showed a cue-type effect on target dwell time that the low-functioning group did not, whose 'poor performance did not depend on the amount of social information contained in the cue picture'.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion, but a within-session combination of eye and head channels from a single device, which is closer to fusion than most gaze studies here attempt. No ablation isolates the contribution of the head channel, though the correlation analysis identifies head-eye features among the most label-correlated, alongside the area0 gaze features. The temporal decomposition into five stages is a second axis of combination - features are computed per stage and pooled - but no analysis compares stages, so which phase of the animation carries the signal is not established despite the stage structure being built into the design.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: The corpus's most architecturally ambitious fusion, and the ablation is properly constructed. Single-modality baselines using identical features and pipeline give 0.7368 for EEG and 0.7895 for gaze, against 0.9500 fused - a gain of over 15 points on the better single modality. Two comparators isolate the mechanism: a conventional pipeline concatenating features with mRMR selection and SVM reaches 0.8100, and a ResNet18 over concatenated features reaches only 0.7000 despite far greater capacity, which the authors read as showing that 'simply and rudely cascading EEG and eye-tracking recordings cannot make good use of multi-modality information'. The graph formulation itself is the contribution: features are nodes, thresholded covariances are edges, so convolution operates over discovered inter-feature structure rather than over a flat concatenation. The interpretive payoff is the cross-modal edge analysis, which identifies EEG synchronisation as related to exotic face, joint attention and gaze-following features, and entropy measures as related to face, joint attention and social interaction features - relationships that exist despite the two signals being recorded at different times. The caveat is that all of this rests on an accuracy figure whose validation unit is not stated and appears not to be the participant.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion - gaze only. The combination that matters is across levels of image representation, and the design makes this an explicit test rather than an implicit one. The three feature levels map onto the two mechanisms the paper is interested in: pixel-level features index bottom-up attention driven by image statistics, semantic-level features index top-down attention driven by prior knowledge, and object-level features sit between. The finding that the two semantic features survive selection only in the non-severe group, while pixel-level features survive in both, is a direct within-modality dissociation supporting the hypothesis that severity impairs top-down more than bottom-up attentional guidance.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: A clean and well-quantified fusion result, with both single-modality baselines reported: fixation features alone reach 84.62%, session length features alone reach 84.62%, and combined they reach 92.31% - roughly an 8-point gain. What makes it more informative than most fusion claims in the corpus is that the two feature families are conceptually distinct rather than two views of the same signal: one measures where the child looked, the other how long the interaction took. The best three-feature model draws on both, taking total session length plus two fixation features. The finding that session length alone reaches 79.49% is the most consequential single number in the paper, since it implies most of the discriminative information is available without an eye tracker at all.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: The fusion result is clearly negative and is reported without spin, which makes it useful. Combining feature families reduced performance in nearly every condition: for autism detection MFCC plus RASTA-PLP fell to 80.7% from 100% for either alone, and HNR plus SNR fell to 53.2%; for Down syndrome detection MFCC plus RASTA-PLP fell to 78.3%. The single exception is HNR plus GNE reaching 100% for autism-versus-Down-syndrome discrimination. The authors state the conclusion plainly: 'the combined feature set provides less performance when compared to the individual features, for most of the cases'. Given the sample size this is more likely a dimensionality effect than a substantive finding, but it stands in useful contrast to the widespread assumption elsewhere in this corpus that combining features or modalities helps.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion. What is fused is spatial and temporal information within a single representation: the scanpath image simultaneously carries where gaze travelled and how fast, with velocity encoded as greyscale gradient along each line. This is a genuinely different answer to the multimodality problem from the feature-concatenation approaches elsewhere in the corpus - the two information types are combined at the representation level before any learning occurs, and the MIC analysis is offered as evidence that the velocity channel carries real signal, since velocity correlates with CARS at 0.79 and is exactly what the colour encodes.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion. The combination is across feature families within a single modality, and the genetic algorithm's per-group selection is what makes it interpretable: the two models retain overlapping but non-identical feature sets, with distance-to-centre and biological-movement indicators appearing only in the autistic model and colour appearing only in the typically developing model. The authors' explanation for the biological-movement asymmetry is subtle and worth recording - the feature covers the whole region containing biological movement, and since typically developing attention 'is specifically more focused on the regions with people and faces' which are already captured by dedicated features, the broader region adds nothing for that group. That is a redundancy argument rather than an absence-of-effect argument, and it distinguishes a feature being uninformative from being subsumed.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion of sensor streams, but the stimulus is genuinely multisensory - visual, auditory and olfactory channels are synchronised, with odour presence and intensity under programmatic control. The analytic combination is across feature families, and the hypothesis-contrast approach makes it systematic: eight predefined families are modelled separately so their discriminative value can be compared. The resulting ordering is informative. Coarse social-versus-non-social contrasts perform best - people versus items at 84%, adults versus items at 83%, children versus items at 82% - while fine-grained within-social contrasts perform worst, with adults' faces versus bodies reaching only 66% and kappa 0.25. The authors draw the correct conclusion, that macro-area definitions capture the signal but cannot resolve face-internal patterns, and recommend adding eye and mouth areas.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion; a single modality analysed across three axes. What the design does combine is two measurement approaches to the same behaviour - human coding of whether gestures occurred and automated kinematic measurement of how they were executed - and the divergence between them is the paper's most valuable result. Blind human coders found no group difference in gesture frequency; automated tracking found significant differences in every kinematic measure. The authors generalise this appropriately: the 'human perceptual system is good at detecting specific patterns of movement (e.g., head nodding, smiling), but it is not good at giving precise metric measures of movement', so pose tracking has 'an advantage over behavioral coding techniques - finding motor patterns that might be difficult to spot through human observations'. That is a specific, testable claim about what automation adds, and it is demonstrated within a single study.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion. The only combination performed is unsupervised partitioning followed by supervised classification, which is a pipeline rather than a fusion. The result - higher accuracy within one cluster than on the pooled data - is presented as evidence that clustering helps, but no cluster is characterised, no analysis explains what makes cluster 1 different, and the improvement is a maximum over 36 cluster-by-classifier combinations, so it cannot be distinguished from selection across the grid.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion. What the study combines is levels of description within a single modality, and it does so to informative effect: the 17 classifier features include both conventional kinematics and the three synergy measures, and the per-participant feature importance analysis finds that spatial displacement measures and the cumulative variance accounted for by three components both contribute. The authors note that this 'substantially confirmed the results obtained with univariate statistics', so the classifier's internal weighting agrees with the group-level analysis - a convergence that few studies in the corpus check and that here supports treating the classification as reflecting the same phenomenon as the hypothesis test rather than an unrelated pattern.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: Three streams combined into one running score - face detection, ear-based head orientation, and speech-response latency - fused by weighted accumulation with operator-set constants rather than by a learned combiner. The weights encode a clinical judgement about relative importance (joint attention worth three times face attention, non-attention penalised lightly), which is transparent and adjustable but not empirically derived. No ablation examines what each stream contributes to the 82.4% agreement, which would have been informative about whether the joint-attention component - the most clinically specific and the hardest to detect from ear cascades - is carrying its weight.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion. What the study does combine is heterogeneous variable types within one questionnaire - child behaviour, perinatal history, family history and parental lifestyle - but no analysis separates their contributions, no feature importances are reported, and the retained feature sets under each selection scheme are never disclosed. Since the design's stated purpose is to identify which factors matter, this omission removes the paper's principal claimed contribution: a reader cannot tell whether classification rests on the developmental items, on demographics such as sex and birth order, or on parental background variables.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: The fusion result is negative and cleanly reported: prosodic features alone gave 82.23% AUC, articulation alone 67.98%, and the two combined 78.52% - worse than prosody alone. The authors attribute this to articulation's poorer specificity dragging down the combination, and respond by using prosody alone for all subsequent analyses. A second combination test concerns sampling context rather than feature type: the best single conversational activity (83.04%) matched or exceeded every combination of two, three or four activities, so concatenating more speech did not help. Both results run against the assumption that more data or more feature families improve performance, and both are acted on rather than merely noted.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Single-modality: eye tracking only. The paper nonetheless performs a fusion of a different kind - combining stimulus-derived features with observer-derived features - and this is its stated contribution. The comparison against competitors is argued in exactly these terms: the SP-ASDNET entries are said to fail because they 'do not consider the correlation between fixations and the corresponding image content', and the UCK entries because they discard the first fixation of each subject, which the authors argue is informative. The fusion is nonetheless only weakly supported by the results, since the best-performing competitor (TU, 0.59) matched RM3ASD exactly and also used a random forest over combined image and fixation features, while the error analysis attributes the model's success to a single fixation-duration feature that requires no image content at all.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Single-modality eye tracking, but the paper performs and systematically ablates two distinct fusions, and both fail in ways that matter. The first fuses the child's real scanpath with a model-generated neurotypical reference scanpath, on the reasonable premise that deviation from a normative scanning pattern should be more diagnostic than the raw pattern; across four paired comparisons the synthetic saccade never helped, and the authors identify its removal as one of the two changes that produced their post-challenge improvement. The second fuses scanpath with stimulus image, on the premise that autistic viewing differs specifically in response to social content; scanpath-only matched or beat the fused model in three of four comparisons. Taken together the two negative fusion results carry more weight than the positive headline: the information the classifier uses is neither the deviation from normative scanning nor the interaction with image content, but something intrinsic to the scanpath itself - which the authors correctly suspect is subject identity.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Single-modality by design, and the design is an argument. Sound is discarded, faces are discarded, appearance and scene are discarded, and what remains is 2D skeletal motion alone. The authors' case is that this isolates the non-verbal channel cleanly, and it is strengthened by the symptom analysis: of 27 ADOS items, the 15 that tracked model output were predominantly non-verbal, while the lowest-loading items on the PLS-C latent component were the verbal ones - immediate echolalia and stereotyped language - which the authors correctly attribute to a largely pre-verbal sample rather than to a modelling failure. Their handling of intonation, the one vocal item that loaded highly on a model that cannot hear, is the most careful piece of reasoning in the paper: rather than claiming the network recovered prosody, they explain that atypical intonation occurs in more severely affected, minimally verbal children who simultaneously score higher on atypical social overtures, atypical social response and undirected vocalisation, so the correlation runs through severity rather than through sound. Multi-person fusion is present but unexamined - skeletons of child, examiner and caregiver enter the same input without separation.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Single-modality: touchscreen kinematics only. The paper nonetheless performs a within-modality combination that is worth noting - the network receives twelve kinematic features together with five one-hot task-identity variables, so movement is interpreted conditional on cognitive context rather than pooled across it, and the task variables 'were always provided to the ANN' and were never subject to the removal analysis. This is a defensible design given that different Leiter-3 subtests impose different spatial demands, but it has an unexamined consequence: because task identity is always available, the model can learn task-specific kinematic norms, and since the feature vectors are per-child per-task averages, the combination of task identity plus habitual movement dynamics is close to a subject fingerprint. No cross-modality fusion is attempted, and none is claimed.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: The most carefully argued fusion analysis in the corpus, and one of very few where the mechanism of the fusion benefit is demonstrated rather than assumed. Four models are trained on identical data and folds: EEG alone, gaze alone, naive concatenation of raw features, and the proposed two-stage latent fusion. The ordering is informative at every step. Both fusion variants beat both unimodal models, so combining helps. Two-stage fusion beats naive concatenation, so the benefit comes from combining learned high-level representations rather than merely from having 221 features instead of 96 or 125 - the control that distinguishes a fusion architecture claim from a dimensionality claim. And the confusion matrices identify why: EEG classifies autistic children better (82.5% versus 77.7%) while gaze classifies typically developing children far better (94% versus 80%), so the modalities err in opposite directions and fusion recovers both strengths, reaching 92.5% and 98%. That asymmetry is a substantive finding in its own right and is the kind of evidence that most multimodal papers in this literature substitute an accuracy delta for. The t-SNE panels add a visual account, showing the fused representation separating classes where raw and concatenated features overlap. Two caveats: the paper does not test partial fusion (for instance gaze plus a single EEG family) so the minimum useful combination is unknown, and the behavioural modality alone at 86.67% already exceeds the EEG modality, which bears directly on cost-benefit given that eye tracking is far cheaper and faster to acquire than a 128-channel net in a preschooler.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Single modality - 2D RGB video only, with no audio, depth, gaze tracking or motion capture. No fusion is attempted or claimed. Within the modality the paper does run a preprocessing comparison that functions like an ablation: training, validation and test set #2 used semantically segmented video with the foreground human isolated so that 'most of the background noise (color of wallpaper, color of child's clothes, etc.) was reduced', while test set #1 was left raw. Accuracy was 0.918 on the segmented test set and 0.916 on the raw one, with autistic-class accuracy 94.5% versus 92.1%. Because the model was trained only on segmented video, its near-equivalent performance on raw video is a domain-shift result rather than a like-for-like comparison, and it constitutes direct evidence that the classifier is not depending on room or clothing cues - the confound that the skeletonisation approach elsewhere in this corpus removes by construction. The authors read the small drop as expected background distraction, which is a reasonable interpretation.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: The corpus's most explicit study of fusion architecture, with three design choices argued rather than assumed. First, fusion is hybrid rather than purely early or late: the two behavioural streams are fused at feature level, because they are homogeneous enough that concatenation exploits their correlation, while the physiological stream is fused at decision level with the behavioural subdecision, because feature-level fusion across such different data types would not work - the paper states hybrid fusion 'utilizes the merits of feature fusion and decision fusion and overcomes their disadvantages'. Second, the decision combiner is not plain naive Bayes but an attribute-weighted variant, on the explicit reasoning that 'the naive Bayes algorithm assumes that each attribute has the same influence on the classification result; in fact, they are different', with weights derived from training-set co-occurrence counts and constructed so they cannot vanish. Third, and most valuably, the paper demonstrates why fusion works rather than merely that it does: confusion matrices and pairwise confusion graphs show EEG achieving 90.0% on autistic children but only 77.5% on typical ones while facial expression achieves 92.5% on typical children but only 72.5% on autistic ones, with eye fixation missing 37.5% of autistic children - so the modalities err in opposite directions and the fused model recovers 85.0% and 90.0%. This is the same mechanism-level demonstration Han et al. provide, arrived at independently and with three modalities rather than two, and the convergence between the two studies on the finding that neurophysiological and behavioural streams fail in opposite directions is worth carrying into the synthesis. The one deflating observation is that the two behavioural modalities together (85.00%) essentially match EEG alone (83.75%), and the full fusion adds only 2.5 points over the behavioural pair - so on a cost-benefit view the EEG headset buys very little over a camera and an eye tracker.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Single modality throughout, and no fusion is attempted. The paper's comparative apparatus is entirely internal to the optimisation problem: six metaheuristics searching the same two-dimensional hyperparameter space, and four classifier families on the same features. The most informative comparison for a reader of this review is the classifier table rather than the optimiser table. On identical augmented inputs, a multilayer perceptron reached 0.8179 accuracy with AUC 79.17, naive Bayes 0.7306 and logistic regression 0.7243 with AUC 66.55, against 0.9881 and AUC 98.18 for the tuned KELM. A 17-point accuracy gap and a 19-point AUC gap between a tuned kernel machine and a neural network on the same 784 pixel features is not what one expects if the features carry a robust class signal; it is what one expects if two kernel hyperparameters are being optimised against the evaluation data. The authors read the table as evidence of their method's superiority and do not consider this alternative reading.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Single modality by design, and the paper is explicit that this is a limitation of its interpretation rather than a methodological choice to be defended: other measures 'would have revealed higher variability in ASD' is entertained as a live possibility. No fusion is attempted. The paper does perform an internal combination that is informative for the fusion literature elsewhere in this corpus: fingerprinting with all eight gaze features and with a reduced set of four gave nearly identical identification accuracy (32.6% versus 35.4% for the autistic group), because the removed features were highly correlated with the retained ones - non-social, non-head-body and hand gaze with face gaze, and mouth with eyes. That redundancy check, performed and reported rather than assumed, is the discipline missing from studies that report improvements from adding correlated features.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Single modality - audio only - with no fusion attempted, though multimodal extension is proposed as future work. The paper does run a genuine three-way representation comparison on identical child-disjoint folds, which is more informative than most single-modality studies here and yields two transferable observations. First, learned representations beat hand-engineered ones by roughly ten points (79.3% and 76.9% against 69.7%), and the gap is largest in AUROC (0.822 and 0.815 against 0.740), suggesting that whatever separates the classes is not well captured by the conventional descriptor set. Second, the two transfer-learning results point in opposite directions and the authors interpret both correctly: an ImageNet-pretrained Inception v3 with 33 million parameters lost to a purpose-built 8.7-million-parameter CNN, attributed to 'the irrelevance of ImageNet features to spectrograms', while a self-supervised audio transformer transferred usefully, justified by prior evidence of wav2vec's utility 'for suprasegmental tasks such as emotion prediction'. Domain-matched pretraining helped; domain-mismatched pretraining hurt, even at four times the parameter count.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: The best-evidenced fusion result in the corpus, on three counts. The improvement is statistically tested rather than asserted: DeLong's test for correlated ROC curves gives p < 0.001 against the voice model and p = 0.033 against the language model, with 95% confidence intervals on all three AUCs (0.7800, 0.8748, 0.9205). The improvement's structure is diagnosed: the combined model's specificity is identical to the language model's (0.8286) while sensitivity rises from 0.7727 to 0.8977, so the voice features recovered autistic participants the language model missed without importing the voice model's false-positive tendency - which is exactly the asymmetric gain one would predict if the modalities are complementary rather than redundant, and the authors note it explicitly. And the mechanism is established at participant level rather than inferred from the numbers: children detected by the language model had significantly lower CCC-2 structural and pragmatic scores and less output, while for the voice model 'the CCC-2 scores and the Friends task indices did not differentiate correctly or incorrectly classified participants', which is the direct evidence that the acoustic channel indexes something orthogonal to language level. The clinical implication the authors draw follows properly from that evidence: voice analysis is needed 'to detect communication differences among subjects with ASD who have achieved high language skills', concurring with the observation that voice atypicalities persist in individuals with otherwise typical outcomes. Compared with Han et al. and Liao et al., who also demonstrate complementary failure directions via confusion matrices, this study goes further by characterising the complementarity in terms of participant clinical profiles rather than class labels.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Single modality, with the fusion result confined to combining features within it - and that result is a clean negative. Two features (acceleration, entropy) across four movies gives an eight-dimensional space and AUC 0.73, worse than either feature alone combined across the same four movies (0.85 and 0.80). The authors report this plainly and explain it correctly as the expected behaviour of a moderate-sized dataset as dimensionality grows. Two aspects make the negative result more useful than most. The two features are moderately correlated (r = 0.4-0.5), so combining them adds dimensionality without much independent information - which is the situation in which such degradation is predicted, and the authors report the correlation that makes it interpretable. And combining a single feature across movies did help substantially, lifting acceleration from around 0.68-0.71 on individual movies to 0.85 across four - so aggregation over stimuli was worth far more than aggregation over feature types. The paper's stated future direction is genuine multimodal fusion with gaze, facial dynamics and response to name, which is the group's programme; this study establishes what one channel contributes.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: Not multimodal, but the study performs the corpus's most informative feature-class comparison, which serves an analogous function. Two feature classes representing the two components of prosody are tested on identical participants and identical utterances, within each language and combined, giving six models whose pattern is interpretable as a whole. The result is a dissociation rather than a fusion gain: rhythm classifies in both languages and survives pooling, intonation classifies in one language and collapses on pooling. Crucially the authors do not attempt to combine the two feature classes into a single model - which would have been the obvious accuracy-maximising move and would have obscured the dissociation. That restraint is what makes the study informative: the purpose is to determine which prosodic dimension is cross-linguistically robust, and combining them would have answered a different and less useful question. A supplementary analysis reported in the paper demonstrates that the rhythm features do contain systematic cross-linguistic differences, which is the necessary check that the successful combined-language model is separating diagnosis rather than exploiting language as a proxy - though with the two languages recruited at different sites through different routes, that check carries real weight and would ideally have appeared in the main text.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Single modality - text only, with no acoustic or extra-linguistic input, and combination with speech features named as future work. Within the modality the study performs a systematic representation comparison that functions as its main experimental variable: two encoders crossed with three representation schemes, reported as six configurations. The pattern is informative. Page-level representation with zero vectors beat whole-narration representation for both encoders, which the authors attribute to information loss in aggregation - 'the aggregation that occurs in the single vector approach for the whole narration causes some key information to be lost' - and to the possibility that particular pages matter more than others. The zero-vector scheme also beat masking, which is the more interesting of the two comparisons: masking tells the model to ignore pages the participant skipped, while zero vectors leave a marked absence, and the better performance of the latter supports the authors' reading that 'even missing out certain pages may provide clues to identify ASD participants'. Silence is treated as signal rather than as missing data. And the two encoders reaching identical top scores despite one being a bidirectional LSTM and the other a transformer suggests the architecture is not the limiting factor at this sample size.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Single modality, and no cross-modal fusion is attempted. Two within-modality combinations are studied instead, and both are informative. The first is the stimulus comparison: two competitor classes tested as separate datasets so that toys and animations can be compared directly, with animations winning on both raw looking times and classification. The second is a feature-combination test structured as a genuine ablation - net dwell time alone, the single most consistently selected feature, was used to classify and reached 70.67% and 79.17% on the two datasets, against 78.12% and 84.37% for the multivariate selected sets, and the authors report having 'made similar observations for all other single features as well'. That comparison establishes that the multivariate combination contributes real information beyond the best individual metric, which is the check that distinguishes a feature-selection claim from a dimensionality claim and which most studies here omit. What is not tested is combining the two stimulus sets, so whether toys and animations elicit complementary information from different children remains open.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Single modality with no cross-modal fusion, but two forms of within-modality combination are examined and both are informative. The first is combining the ten areas into a single classifier versus using each alone: the full ten-area model reached 80% and 71% while individual areas ranged from significant to indistinguishable from chance under permutation testing, and critically the set of areas exceeding chance differs between cohorts. The second is the within-paradigm pairing, where each social area sits opposite a size-matched non-social competitor in the same display, so the design supports comparing relative preference rather than absolute looking. The biological motion paradigm is analysed this way explicitly, with paired t-tests comparing upright against inverted within each of the four groups - and the result is a clean negative for three of them, with only preschool comparison children showing the expected preference. That the paper runs and reports this within-subject preference analysis, rather than only the between-group percentage comparison, is what allows it to engage substantively with the prior biological motion literature and to identify where it does not replicate.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: The most consequential fusion result in the corpus, though the fusion itself is inherited from prior work: 'previously published analysis of earlier algorithm iterations demonstrated that combining inputs significantly improved the performance of the algorithm'. What this trial adds is not a demonstration that fusion helps but a demonstration of what fusion plus abstention achieves under prospective conditions on the clinically relevant population. Two properties of the fusion deserve note. The three inputs are mutually blinded, so no channel is contaminated by another - the caregiver does not know what the clinician said, the video analyst does not know either, and none sees the output. And the channels are deliberately heterogeneous in vantage point rather than in modality, combining retrospective caregiver knowledge, naturalistic home observation and structured clinical observation, which is a different fusion logic from the modality-combining designs elsewhere in this review and is justified by reference to diagnostic guidelines rather than to information theory. The trial does not report per-input performance, so the marginal contribution of each channel in this cohort cannot be assessed - a gap relative to the fusion ablations reported by MacFarlane, Han and Liao.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Single modality with no fusion. The paper's comparative work is instead across classifiers, and the reporting of it is better than the headline suggests. Four methods are run ten times each and both the best model and the ten-run mean with standard deviation are given, which makes the instability visible: the decision tree's best model reaches 83% accuracy and 100% recall on the test set but its ten-run mean is 68.2% with a standard deviation of 16.40, and the authors read this correctly as overfitting - 'half of the ten best models of all the ones trained for DT are good in the classification task, but the others tend to decrease their performances drastically from the train to the test sets'. SVM is identified as most consistent (mean 79.8%, SD 6.75) and preferred on that basis rather than on peak performance, with the reasoning that linear SVM 'is the best to use when dealing with small datasets'. Choosing a model for stability over peak accuracy, and reporting the distribution that justifies it, is the right instinct and is rare in this corpus.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Single modality with no cross-modal fusion. Two within-pipeline combinations are performed. The first concatenates LBP and GLCM outputs into a single 216-dimensional vector, justified on the general ground that 'extracting the features from several methods and combining them are two of the most important recent methods that have an effect on accurate diagnosis' - an assertion rather than an argument, with no ablation showing what either family contributes alone. The second replaces each CNN's classification head with an SVM operating on its deep feature maps. That second comparison is the more informative because it is properly controlled: the same features are classified two ways, and the result is mixed - the SVM head improves GoogleNet from 93.6% to 95.5% but degrades ResNet-18 from 97.6% to 94.5%. The paper reports both directions without comment. Across all six configurations the pattern that hand-engineered texture beats learned representation is presented as the headline conclusion but never examined, though it is the observation most consistent with the discriminative signal residing in low-level plot morphology rather than in anything a pretrained visual network would find semantically salient.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Single modality, and no fusion is attempted, though the companion speech study from the same group and app processes audio from the same recordings - so the two papers together represent an unexploited multimodal opportunity on a shared corpus, which neither notes. Within the modality, two representations of the same annotation are compared: a static fixation profile and a dynamic transition graph. Both yield exactly one significant finding after correction, and interestingly they converge on the same location - fixation differs at region BC and the significant transition is between BB and BC - which is a form of internal corroboration the paper does not draw attention to. Only the fixation representation is carried into the classifier; the transition matrices, which encode sequence and might plausibly carry more information, are used only descriptively.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Single modality with no fusion. The paper's comparative structure is instead across model families and, more importantly, across data conditions, and the second of these is the study's real contribution. Running the same convolutional network across three data conditions - original, rotation-augmented, and one image per participant - constitutes an ablation over validation design rather than over features, and it is the only such experiment in the corpus. The model-family comparison is also informative as an internal control: deep SVM on principal components of the same images reached AUC 51.50% on the original data, indistinguishable from chance, and decision jungle 60.40%, so the conventional pipeline extracts essentially nothing. That places whatever signal exists in the convolutional representation and simultaneously indicates that the pixel statistics captured by principal components carry no class information - a useful negative result that the authors note but do not pursue.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Single modality with no fusion, but the feature-family comparison functions as a well-executed ablation and yields the study's clearest finding. Two families of seventeen features each - accuracy and duration - are compared in three ways: by model-derived importance across all 28 cross-validation iterations for all four classifiers, by a statistical test of the difference in mean importance (t = 5.15, p = 1e-5), and by retraining on the duration subset alone. All three converge: duration dominates, and removing accuracy improves or maintains performance in three of four classifiers, with XGBoost the only exception. The diagnosis of why is equally clean - accuracy scores cluster at ceiling in both groups, so the feature carries no variance to exploit - and the authors offer two candidate explanations, lenient parental labelling or a game too easy for most children, either of which would be actionable in redesign. This is what a feature ablation should look like, and it is more informative than the several fusion claims elsewhere in this corpus that rest on an accuracy delta alone.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Single modality with no fusion, but the three-method comparison is the paper's structure and its internal inconsistency is the most informative thing in it. Methods 1 and 2 are two views of the same computation: the ICA produces an unmixing matrix, which is applied to the observations to produce separated components. Method 1 uses the matrix, Method 2 uses its outputs. The reported results are 98.51% and 59.71%. If the separation were extracting genuinely different vocal sources for the two groups, the separated signals should carry that difference, yet they classify barely above chance even after the most favourable of 256 frequency sequences is selected. Method 3, which reconstructs time-domain speech from those same separated components and extracts standard cepstral features, then recovers 91-93% - which suggests the discriminative information is present in the reconstructed audio but not in the individual frequency-point sequences, and is consistent with ordinary speaker- and speech-level acoustic differences. Taken together the three results do not form a coherent picture, and the paper's explanation - that the unmixing matrix captures 'the essential distinctions between the two types of children's speech' - does not address why the separation those same matrices perform yields near-chance signals.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion, but the study performs a well-designed three-way comparison of segmentation inputs feeding an identical downstream model - manual annotation, MFCC-plus-pitch diarization, and x-vector diarization - which isolates the contribution of the segmentation stage cleanly. The result is the paper's most interesting finding and runs against expectation in two ways. Automatic diarization matched or slightly beat manual annotation (R 0.606 and 0.581 against 0.567), which the authors explain rather than merely report: 'the manual segmentation is not perfectly accurate, especially for the child segments. The child speech is often quiet and is sometimes masked by noises, especially when using a distant microphone in a reverberant environment.' And the more sophisticated representation lost: 512-dimensional x-vectors achieved better child-segment accuracy (89.84%) than MFCC plus pitch, yet produced worse downstream severity estimation - so segment-classification accuracy and downstream utility diverge, and optimising the intermediate metric would have selected the worse system. That dissociation between an intermediate objective and the end-to-end outcome is a transferable lesson for any pipeline architecture.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: None. A single video-recorded interaction stream, coded by human raters. The robot's own sensors - microphones, cameras, sonar, tactile sensors - are all present in the NAO platform and none is used for measurement, which is the study's clearest missed opportunity and the direction its own future-work section points toward. A robot that both elicits and records the interaction would supply exactly the standardised multimodal stream that several other studies in this review construct with far more improvised equipment.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: No fusion in this study - a single modality, six features, and the best model uses exactly one of them. The paper is nonetheless one of the more informative in the corpus about fusion, because the authors have a directly comparable prior study on the identical 39 children: Zhao et al. (2021a) reached 84.62% with visual fixation features alone and 92.31% by adding a single non-eye-tracking feature, conversational length. Set beside the present 87.18% from oculomotor features alone, this gives an unusually clean within-sample comparison of three feature families on the same participants - and it also shows how much of the gain in the earlier fusion result came from conversational length, a variable that is essentially a direct measure of the group difference in task duration reported here (191 s versus 110 s). That is worth flagging as a caution about multimodal gains: a fused feature that is itself a near-proxy for group membership will raise accuracy without adding behavioural insight. The authors' recommendation is to fuse oculomotor with fixation features, and, in the longer term, eye tracking with EEG, neuroimaging and kinematics, arguing that segmentation is the enabling technique because it preserves participants who would otherwise be dropped for data loss in any one stream.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Genuine two-stream fusion within a single physical device, and one of the cleaner ablation designs in the corpus. Streams: triaxial acceleration of the car body (movement pattern) and dual wheel shaft encoders (rotation). Fusion is early - after two rounds of backward elimination, first within each modality using inter-feature correlation and then across modalities, the selected features from both streams are concatenated into one vector for training. The ablation is fully reported and interpretable: 71.11% for acceleration alone, 78.61% for acceleration plus encoders, 75.83% for acceleration plus the new roll/pitch features, and 85.56% for all three sets, showing that each addition contributes and that the two contributions are partly complementary rather than redundant. The complementarity has a physical basis rather than a statistical one: the two sensors disambiguate states that either alone would confuse, since a stationary car with spinning wheels and a car carried through the air with static wheels are distinguishable only by looking at both signals together, and the new roll/pitch features are themselves derived by short-time Fourier transform of the accelerometer specifically to characterise what the body is doing during wheel play. The caution is that the ablation shares the sample and the feature-selection procedure with the final model, so the gains are measured under the same optimistic conditions as the headline accuracy; and that the largest single-feature contributor from the encoder side may be the not-playing ratio, which indexes engagement rather than rotation interest.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: None - a single modality with 12 features from one sensor stream. The study is nonetheless relevant to the fusion question in two ways. First, the authors' explicit future direction is to combine these kinematic measures with 'the traditional behavioural and cognitive scale' into a multimodal risk measure - a clinician-facing rather than sensor-facing conception of fusion, in which the computational signal supplements standardised assessment rather than being fused with another sensor. Second, and more interestingly, the design already contains an implicit two-channel structure that goes unexploited: the tablet records both what the child does cognitively (which cards go where, and whether the answer is correct) and how the child moves while doing it. The paper deliberately discards the first channel, analysing only correctly performed tasks so that cognitive errors do not contaminate the motor signal. Since Leiter-3 performance is itself diagnostically informative and the two groups' IQ ranges differ, the discarded channel is not noise but a second modality that the design chose to suppress rather than fuse.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Three-stream fusion with a clearly reported ablation, and the fusion architecture is a hand-written cascade rather than a learned combination. Audio and video are fused at the segmentation stage: the ASR stream supplies timestamps for each name call, which cut the video into 3 s response windows, and the authors note that this removes the manual-annotation error that would otherwise attach to onset marking. Body pose and head pose are then fused at the decision stage in a three-branch rule: shoulder rotation above 90 degrees for more than 10 frames gives a positive response outright; shoulder rotation below 20 degrees on every frame gives a negative response outright; and only in the ambiguous 20-90 degree band does head yaw adjudicate, with more than 8 frames of detected yaw giving a positive response. The ablation is reported for the two visual streams and is the paper's central quantitative claim: pose alone gives 83.3% of participants and 95.4% of events, pose plus head pose gives 93.3% and 98.2%. In participant terms that is three additional children correctly scored out of 30, so the confidence interval on the improvement is wide even though the direction is plausible. Two features of this fusion design are worth carrying into the synthesis. It is complementary by explicit behavioural argument rather than by empirical search - each stream is introduced to cover a named failure mode of the other - which is a more defensible basis for multimodality than the accuracy-chasing seen in several other studies here. And the multi-view arrangement is itself a form of fusion driven by the clinical protocol: two rear cameras are required because the caller may stand on either side, so which camera contributes the head-pose evidence depends on the geometry of the assessment rather than on a fixed sensor assignment.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: No fusion. A single modality with 18 features from one sensor, and the four reported conditions are nested subsets of that same feature set rather than distinct modalities. One near-miss is worth recording: the discussion states that 'the children's verbal responses to the observed game were also recorded during the test' and that 'the results indicate the significant matching of the provided responses to the recorded eye-tracking patterns'. A second behavioural channel - whether the child correctly identified the target, and what they said - was therefore captured and would have been straightforward to fuse with gaze, all the more so because the task has an objectively correct answer on every one of 240 trials, so accuracy, latency and error patterns were available at no additional cost. None of it is quantified, analysed or entered into the model; the claimed correspondence between speech and gaze is asserted without a single supporting number. This is the same pattern seen in the tablet-based motor study charted elsewhere in this review, where the cognitive-performance channel was deliberately discarded to isolate the motor signal: a second modality present in the raw data and suppressed rather than fused.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion - a single camera stream - but the study is one of the most informative in this corpus about fusion of a different kind, because its entire feature construction is a within-modality coordination analysis. The 56 time series (53 localised facial expression components plus yaw, pitch and roll) are combined pairwise by windowed cross-correlation with directional lag, producing 6,272 features that encode not what the face did but how its parts moved together in time. The results locate the discriminative signal squarely in the cross-channel pairs: the highest-weighted features on average are pose-pose, and pose-eye combinations appear among the top individual features - so the signal is in how head movement coordinates with itself and with eye-region movement, not in either channel alone. This is a concrete demonstration that the useful information in multimodal behaviour can lie in the coordination structure rather than in the constituent signals, which is a stronger and more testable claim than the generic 'fusion improved accuracy' reported by most multimodal studies here. Two limits are stated by the authors. Feature count grows quadratically in the number of time series, which is why Facial Action Coding System units were not added and why nose and cheek components were dropped - a rare instance of a paper declining extra features on principled dimensionality grounds rather than adding everything available. And the analysis is monadic: the confederate's synchronised video was recorded by the same device and discarded, so interpersonal synchrony, which is the natural extension of a within-person coordination analysis and is theoretically central to conversation, remains untested and is named as future work.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion - a single eye tracker - but two feature families are combined within the modality and their contributions are separately quantified, which is more than most multimodal papers here achieve. The semantic stream encodes what the child is looking at, by locating each fixation in a SLIC superpixel and passing that region through an autoencoder pretrained on MS COCO to yield a compressed code; the low-level stream encodes the mechanics of looking - position, duration, saccade amplitude and saccade orientation. The ablation is clean and reported in the discussion: semantic features alone give 94.85% accuracy with 97.14% sensitivity and 93.16% specificity, low-level features alone 93.33% with 90.71% and 95.26%, and the combination 96.73% with 96.85% and 96.63%. The two are therefore complementary in a specific and interpretable way - semantic content drives sensitivity while movement mechanics drive specificity - and combining them raises both rather than trading one against the other. That is a more informative fusion result than the usual report of a single accuracy gain. A second, structural form of integration operates at the stimulus level: 82 per-stimulus scores are aggregated into one subject decision, and the paper shows both that individual stimulus scores are unreliable (Fig. 9(a) shows typically developing children scoring high on particular images) and that between-group separation grows with the number of stimuli pooled, so multi-scene aggregation is doing work analogous to multimodal fusion. On genuine cross-modality, the authors list fMRI, EEG, facial expression and observation-scale scores as future work and describe the problem of relating data across modalities as important and understudied.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: No fusion, and no possibility of it in this design - text alone, one tweet at a time. Two structural forms of integration that the data support were also not used. The first is user-level aggregation: 252 users each contribute hundreds or thousands of tweets, and pooling per-tweet predictions into a per-user decision would be the natural analogue of the multi-stimulus aggregation used to good effect by several eye-tracking studies in this corpus, and is the only form in which a screening application could work, since no one would be assessed on a single tweet. It is neither performed nor discussed, and no user-level metric appears. The second is metadata: the Twitter API returns posting time, reply and thread structure, follower and following counts, engagement figures and interaction partners, all of which are behavioural signals about social communication and all of which are discarded in favour of raw text. The paper's own framing - that social media offers insight into 'the social experiences and challenges faced by individuals with ASD' - points directly at interaction structure, which is precisely what is thrown away.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion, but the paper contains the corpus's cleanest test of whether two measures from the same modality carry redundant information, and the test is designed as discriminant validity rather than as an accuracy chase. The comparison measure is the group's own previously published affect analysis - the energy of the first derivative of neutral, positive and negative affect probability time series, computed as a 10-frame moving average of the rate of change followed by cumulative sum. Three lines of evidence are brought to bear. Correlation: Spearman r between integrated entropy and positive-affect energy is moderate for Blowing Bubbles (.49 eyebrows, .60 mouth) and Mechanical Puppy (.41, .49) but negligible for the other four movies (.01-.15), and the mouth correlates more strongly than the eyebrows, which the authors note is expected because smiling is a mouth event. Classification: decision trees using entropy alone reach 76.6-78.3% accuracy, using affect alone 61.6-75.0%, and using both 63.3-79.5% - so adding affect does not help and in two of four movies hurts, while AUCs compared by DeLong's method favour entropy alone in three of four movies. Logistic regression: entropy gives odds ratios up to 1.8 while affect gives 0.8, i.e. below unity. The conclusion that the two measures are largely independent and that entropy is the stronger is therefore supported by three convergent analyses rather than by a single accuracy comparison. The general lesson for the review is that a partially correlated second measure can be genuinely non-redundant, and that testing for redundancy explicitly - rather than reporting that fusion improved accuracy - is the more informative design.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion, but two forms of within-study integration are central to the design. The first is the CNN's dual input: the gaze heat map is presented alongside the stimulus image, so the network can 'explicitly learn the facial regions and expressions' rather than treating gaze positions as coordinates divorced from what was at those coordinates. Since the same 21 or 32 images are shown to every participant, the image channel functions as a conditioning signal identifying which trial the heat map came from. The second, and the paper's actual contribution, is the aggregation layer: each of the 21 or 32 trials is classified independently and the per-trial decisions are then combined either by unweighted hard voting or by a random forest that learns which stimuli to trust. That is a form of stimulus-level fusion, and unlike most fusion claims in this corpus it is tested against its own ablation across three separate problems with informative results - weighting adds 10 points for autistic adults and 16.7 for autistic children but nothing for schizophrenia. The differential outcome is explained mechanistically rather than left as a number: weighting helps precisely when group differences are selective across stimuli, and is useless when they are uniform. That is a more transferable finding about when multi-stimulus aggregation should be weighted than any of the accuracy comparisons in this review.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: No fusion. The three usage-pattern representations are alternatives compared against one another rather than channels combined, and the results across them are informative in their own right: sequential modelling peaked at 58% in the prior analysis, temporal at 60% and spectral at 61%, so all three views performed near chance individually, and no attempt is made to combine them. That is a missed opportunity of exactly the kind this review has seen elsewhere, since content (what was said), timing (how fluently) and frequency (which vocabulary) are plausibly complementary rather than redundant descriptions of the same behaviour, and the paper's own results give no reason to prefer any one of them. Two further channels present in the data are also unused. The survey captured age, which is the single most obvious covariate and is reported descriptively but never entered into any model or adjustment. And the app logged what users actually said - the phrase and unique-word analyses in the descriptive section demonstrate that the content is recoverable and interpretable - yet the classification pipeline reduces every key press to a category-preserving integer, discarding lexical content entirely. Given that the paper reports a large descriptive difference in unique-word count between diagnostic groups, the decision not to model content is a substantive choice left unexplained.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion; a single camera. Two forms of internal integration are central. Architecturally, spatial features from a CNN are combined with temporal modelling by an LSTM and an attention mechanism over frames, so the system represents both what is in each frame and when in the sequence it matters - and the interpretability analysis exploits this composition directly, using attention weights to find the informative time points and Grad-CAM to localise within them, which is a genuinely joint spatial-temporal explanation rather than two separate ones. Conceptually, three separate task-specific models are built rather than one fused model, and the comparison across them is where the study's substantive findings lie: all three tasks detect autism near-perfectly, but only IJA carries severity information, and high-level RJA improves with age. Treating the three joint attention subtypes as separate models and comparing them, rather than pooling all video into one classifier, is what allows the paper to say something about which behaviour matters for which question - a design choice more informative than a fusion gain would have been. The unexploited channel is the compliance score, which is computed for every trial, shown to differ between groups in a diagnostically interesting way, and then used only descriptively rather than as a model input or covariate.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: None. A single modality rendered as a single image type, with no fusion, no auxiliary features and no metadata. The three reported models are alternatives compared against each other rather than channels combined. What the comparison does establish, usefully, is a difference in error profile rather than merely in accuracy: the end-to-end CNN is heavily skewed towards the majority class (recall 0.88 versus 0.48) while the ImageNet-pretrained feature extractor plus a simple classifier is balanced (0.85 versus 0.74 for the MLP). That is a real observation about small-sample deep learning - a network trained from scratch on 382 images collapses towards the majority class, while generic pretrained features generalise better - and it is the study's most transferable finding, though the paper frames it in terms of accuracy rather than of what it reveals about training regime.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: No cross-modal fusion, and the absence is conspicuous for a paper at a speech-signal-processing venue: the introduction cites acoustic findings on pitch range and variability in autistic children, the abstract refers to 'diagnostic predictions made using speech signals', and the title names speech features - yet the study operates entirely on transcripts and computes nothing acoustic. What it does instead is a careful within-modality fusion across three linguistic levels, and reports the ablation in full: syntactic complexity alone 70%, part-of-speech frequencies alone 82%, semantic-pragmatic features alone 82.3%, the last two combined 88.2%, and all three 94.1%. That progression is the study's real contribution and is more informative than a single accuracy figure, because it establishes that the semantic-pragmatic family carries as much signal alone as the lexical family and that the three are complementary rather than overlapping - the specific question the authors identified as unanswered in the prior literature. The caution is that the ablation shares its data, its unnested feature selection and its 17-item test set with the headline result, so the ordering is more reliable than the individual numbers.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion, but the paper is one of the more informative in this corpus about fusing information types within a single modality, and it reports the ablation cleanly. Three representations are compared on the same data. Spatial scan-paths encode position only and give 74.4% for diagnosis. Spatio-temporal scan-paths encode position within bounded time windows, which allows the temporal locus of discrimination to be identified (76.3% in the first three seconds, declining to 70.2% by 12-15 seconds) but does not by itself improve peak performance. Velocity-infused spatio-temporal scan-paths encode position, time window and speed simultaneously by using velocity as the colour channel, and raise the 3-6 second window from 71.74% to 80.25% with AUC improving from 0.790 to 0.839 - a gain of 8.5 accuracy points from adding a derivative of the same underlying signal. That is a well-controlled demonstration that a rendered-image representation can be enriched with dynamics rather than discarding them, and it addresses head-on the central weakness of scan-path-image approaches, which is that drawing a trajectory throws away time. The caveat is that all three representations were evaluated under the same image-level splitting and the same whole-dataset augmentation, so the ordering is more trustworthy than the absolute values.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: No fusion of any kind - a single modality rendered as a single image type, classified by a single network. The only representational variation tested is greyscale versus colour, with greyscale giving marginally better results (95.59% versus 94.69%). The paper's related-work section notes that others have combined eye tracking with kinematic data to gain 5-8 accuracy points, and that gaze features combined with demographic descriptors such as age improved classification with the observation that 'the average classification accuracy decreased when age was excluded as a feature in all tested classifiers' - a finding it reports without recognising its implication for its own work, namely that gaze-based classifiers in this literature draw part of their performance from age information. Since the present study's dataset carries age and CARS at the participant level and uses neither, both a fusion experiment and a confound check were available and not attempted.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Genuine multi-source fusion, and the only study in the review to combine behavioural observation with biological, familial and perinatal data in one model.
