Five families are integrated: developmental milestone attainment across four domains; birth parameters including gestational age, birth weight and delivery mode; post-natal growth percentiles; familial variables including maternal age, country of birth and nursing status; and parent-reported developmental concern. The rationale for fusion is stated as a scientific argument rather than an accuracy claim: 'prematurity, like other factors, interacts with additional ASD risk factors, such as cesarean delivery, parental age, and birth complications; therefore, there is a need for an integrative/cumulative approach to risk estimation', and these non-linear interactions are what machine learning on large data is expected to capture. The SHAP analysis confirms that the final model draws on all five families, with seven of the top twenty features being milestones and the remainder spanning sex, parent concern, nursing, maternal age, gestational age and growth. The finding that undercuts the fusion rationale is the method comparison: logistic regression, which cannot represent the interactions the argument invokes, achieves an identical AUC of 0.86 with slightly better sensitivity. So the integration of heterogeneous data sources demonstrably helps, while the non-linear modelling that was supposed to exploit their interactions demonstrably does not.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: Claimed but not performed. The paper states that it combines 'facial expression recognition with autism classification, thus providing a more complete picture of a child's condition', but the two components are trained on different datasets for different label spaces, evaluated with different metrics in separate tables, and never joined, compared or shown to inform one another. No fusion architecture, joint training, feature sharing or ablation is described. The claim to combine them is a description of the software containing two modules, not of any analysis relating them.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: The most architecturally developed fusion in the review. Rather than concatenating features, the design produces a separate embedding from each modality - an interpretable additive probability from GAMI-Net for the tabular stream, and a CNN-GNN representation for the imaging stream that preserves both local voxel structure and inter-region relationships - then compresses both into a shared 32-dimensional latent space through an autoencoder, and finally uses a hypernetwork to generate subject-specific classifier weights so that the decision function adapts per individual. Each stage has a stated rationale and the ablation studies test the components. As a fusion methodology this is more sophisticated than anything else charted here, including the studies whose data are sound. Its evidential yield is nonetheless nil, because a fusion architecture cannot be assessed when one of the streams it fuses already determines the outcome: no ablation reported can distinguish a genuine multimodal gain from the phenotype stream carrying the label. Removing ADOS, ADI-R and SRS and repeating the ablation would make this the review's most informative fusion experiment.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion. The paper is nonetheless informative for the review's treatment of fusion in two ways, one architectural and one cautionary. Architecturally, the measure is intrinsically two-stream: two movement time series, one per person, combined by cross wavelet coherence, so the 'fusion' is between people rather than between sensors - a form of integration no other study in this corpus attempts except in the dyadic language features of the speech study. Cautionarily, the derived-feature construction is presented as a general recommendation for feature combination - 'creating novel features based on statistically significant features could help improve classification performance' - and it is the clearest example in the review of a feature-engineering step that raises accuracy by importing label information rather than by capturing additional signal. The 57 derived features are sums of coherences already known to differ between groups; summing correlated significant features raises effect sizes arithmetically, and the reported Cohen's d improvement is a consequence of the selection rather than independent evidence for it. The recommendation should not be carried forward as a fusion technique.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Two representations of the same speech are fused and their contributions separately established. The tag stream encodes the linguistic-theoretical description - which lexicogrammatical options were selected - while the text stream encodes the words themselves, and the combined model concatenates tag and word embeddings at each time step so the Bi-LSTM sees both simultaneously. The ablation is reported across four configurations, two tasks and two annotation methods, and its result is instructive precisely because it is modest: on interviews the tag-only linear model reached 0.78, the tag-only Bi-LSTM 0.80, the text-only Bi-LSTM 0.80 and the combined model 0.80-0.82, with McNemar tests finding no significant differences between them. So the theoretically motivated tag representation and the raw word sequence carry largely overlapping information, and combining them adds at most a point or two. The authors report this honestly rather than claiming a fusion benefit, and note that 'the text-DNN and text+tag-DNN models performed almost the same, with the text+tag-DNN model being marginally higher'. That is a more useful contribution to the review's treatment of multimodality than a claimed gain would have been: it shows that an expensive, theory-driven annotation layer can be approximately recovered from surface text by a sequence model, while remaining far more interpretable - which is why the authors retain it.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Fusion within a single modality and across feature families, systematically ablated. Three feature vectors are constructed, each concatenating the same 315 handcrafted features with one backbone's 3,000 deep features, and results are reported for the handcrafted set alone and for each fused vector across five classifiers. The ablation shows a consistent gain from adding deep features - best accuracy rising from 84.5% with handcrafted features alone to 90.2% with ResNet and 94.6% with Inception - which is a clean comparison and is the paper's only methodological contribution. Its interpretability is destroyed by the absence of an evaluation protocol: without knowing how the accuracies were computed, the gain cannot be attributed to better representation rather than to greater capacity to fit the data.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: None. A single static image modality throughout. The recurring references to encoding 'physiological signal characteristics' and 'physiological signal properties' in quaternion space describe the optimiser's original application domain rather than anything in this study, where no physiological signal is acquired.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: No cross-sensor fusion. The study's ablation is between two representations of the same signal - raw coordinates alone versus coordinates plus velocity and acceleration - and its result is more interesting than a simple fusion gain. The four-feature model outperforms the two-feature model substantially (0.90 versus 0.76), which would ordinarily be read as the derived features adding information. But the simulation analysis shows that acceleration correlates with the two-feature model's predictions at r = 0.69 even though that model never receives acceleration as an input, so the information is already present in the raw coordinate sequence and is being recovered from it. The 14-point accuracy difference therefore reflects how easily a network of this size and training regime can extract a derivative from a 20 Hz position sequence, not what information the sequence contains. That is a genuinely useful distinction for the review's treatment of feature engineering: it shows a case where explicit derived features improve performance without adding information, which is the opposite of the usual assumption and is established by manipulation rather than asserted. The authors' own conclusion follows this reading, noting that raw data analysis has potential while the four-feature model excels.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: Three data sources are concatenated - emotion probabilities, heart rate and body temperature - with no ablation isolating their contributions, no rationale for combining state physiology with expression measures, and no reporting of which features the optimisation stage selected. Since the selected feature subset is the explicit output of the paper's central algorithmic contribution, its omission is the study's most conspicuous reporting gap: the method is designed to identify essential features and never says which they were. The one available clue is Table 2, where the physiological variables separate the two label groups cleanly and the emotion probabilities do not obviously do so.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None. A single tabular modality throughout.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Genuine two-sensor fusion, and the fusion is constitutive rather than additive. A pressure sensor supplies centre of pressure and a webcam supplies joint angles via pose estimation, synchronised at 20 Hz - and the study's proposed variables are precisely the correlations between the two streams, so neither sensor alone could produce them. The ablation is reported across three configurations and is informative: conventional variables derived from the pressure sensor alone gave the weakest accuracy and sensitivity, the proposed cross-sensor correlation variables reached perfect scores on their own, and the combined set also reached perfect scores. That ordering says that the information distinguishing the groups lies in the relationship between body movement and base-of-support movement rather than in either measured separately, which is a more specific and more mechanistically meaningful fusion result than the accuracy gains reported by most multimodal studies in this corpus. The caveat is that all three configurations share the same feature-selection procedure and the same evaluation, so the ordering is more trustworthy than the absolute values - and with two of the three reaching exactly 1.000, the comparison has no headroom to discriminate further.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: None in the sense this review uses the term. The paper's 'multiscale fusion' combines feature maps at different spatial resolutions within a single network operating on a single image modality, and the abstract's reference to 'both facial and multimodal datasets' is not borne out by the methods - both corpora are collections of still images. The multiscale ablation is nonetheless informative and is reported honestly: without the hyperparameter search, adding multiscale fusion lowered accuracy from 0.89 to 0.85, and the authors state that 'adding multi-scale fusion may not have yielded better results'. Only in combination with white shark optimisation does the fuller architecture win, which means the architectural contribution and the search contribution are not separable in the reported comparison.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: None. A single electrophysiological modality throughout, with no behavioural, imaging or clinical data fused. The eleven features span time and frequency domains, which is within-modality diversity rather than fusion.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: No sensor fusion - a single camera supplies everything. But the final model combines information across behavioural channels rather than within one: duration of socially oriented vocalisations from the communication channel together with four measures of functional play from the object-manipulation channel, one of them a count and three of them durations resolved by toy type. That cross-channel structure is meaningful. It says that neither the social nor the play dimension alone accounted for the group difference in the stepwise selection, and it aligns with the clinical description of autism better than a single-channel model would. The play predictors also carry an internal ordering worth noting: total counts of functional play has by far the strongest odds ratio (0.639), while the three toy-specific durations sit close to 1 per unit of time (0.985, 0.973, 0.958), so the discriminative work is done mainly by how often a child engages in functional play at all rather than by how long any particular episode lasts.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: None in the sensor sense - a single observational instrument supplies everything. But the retained six-item model is cross-channel in the same way that the free-play model charted elsewhere is: it combines a discourse-content item (reporting of events), a gesture item (emphatic or emotional gestures), a gaze item (unusual eye contact) and three social-reciprocity items (comments on others' emotions or empathy, responsibility, quality of social overtures). No single channel would have sufficed, and the directions differ by channel - gaze, gesture and overture atypicality point toward autism while discourse and empathic-commentary atypicality point toward schizophrenia. That opposition of signs within one model is what allows a six-item combination to reach an apparent AUC of 0.938 where the algorithm totals, which simply add atypicality across channels, reach 0.56. It is a clean demonstration that summing behavioural abnormality destroys the information needed for differential diagnosis, and it should temper the widespread practice in this corpus of building composite atypicality scores.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: None. A single audio modality throughout, with no fusion across sensors, channels or annotation types. The transfer in this study is across datasets and tasks rather than across modalities - discriminative fine-tuning transfers from one child-vocalisation corpus to another, and Wav2Vec 2.0 transfers from 960 hours of unlabelled adult speech to child clinical speech. The comparison between these two transfer sources is the study's clearest methodological result and is worth recording for the review: pre-training on a small, closely related corpus of child autistic vocalisations (D-FT) outperformed pre-training on a vastly larger but unrelated adult speech corpus (W2V2-FT) on both tasks, by 3.3 points on typicality and 6.6 points on diagnosis. Domain proximity beat scale. The caveat is that D-FT's advantage may partly reflect its exposure to De-Enigma's autistic vocalisations, which are class-informative in a way the unlabelled adult corpus is not.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: None modelled, though the opportunity was substantial and deliberately declined. The curated corpus retains account creation date, friend count, follower count, tweet timestamp, reply count, retweet count, like count, hashtag lists and posting source, and the authors observe that 'other supporting metadata could be used in the future for network analysis or statistical studies'. Fusing behavioural text with network position and engagement metrics would be a natural extension and would plausibly improve discrimination - which is precisely why not doing it, in a paper that concludes such models should not be built without consent, is consistent rather than an oversight.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: Late fusion of two independently trained networks, with three combination rules compared and all results reported. The honest headline is that fusion did not improve accuracy materially: 82.5% for the confidence-gated ensemble against 80.0% for video alone and 78.8% for audio alone, a gain of two children out of eighty, and the authors name this as an important limitation rather than presenting the ensemble as a success. What fusion does deliver is two things worth recording. First, genuine error complementarity - both networks were simultaneously wrong on only 8.75% of test cases, meaning that roughly 90% of the errors made by one model were correctable in principle by the other, which is precisely the condition under which a better fusion rule should help and is the strongest argument for the authors' own proposed future work. Second, operating-point control: the OR rule yields sensitivity 0.90 at specificity 0.75 and the AND rule yields specificity 0.925 at sensitivity 0.60, so the same two models can be configured for a high-recall screening role or a high-precision confirmatory one. Presenting this as tunability rather than as a single best number is the correct framing for a screening application and is not done elsewhere in this corpus. The interpretability analysis further shows that the two modalities index partly different clinical constructs, which is the substantive justification for combining them at all.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: None implemented. Audio-visual fusion is stated as an aim in the introduction - 'audio-visual cues will also be used to extract emotional features' - and appears in the conclusion as future work, so the paper announces a fusion approach it does not deliver. The related-work section reports a prior audio-visual study reaching about 72%, with the observation that 'the facial expression part shows less accuracy because the features are less discriminative in comparison to the features used for the audio part (screaming and shouting)'. That observation is worth recording alongside the Geneva multimodal study charted elsewhere in this review, which found by a different route that its audio channel's predictive power came largely from non-vocal sound rather than speech: two independent studies pointing to acoustic events accompanying behaviour, rather than facial or vocal expression as such, as the carrier of the signal in in-the-wild recordings.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Two feature families from a single thermal sensor - learned mood categories and measured temperature - concatenated for severity classification. This is within-modality fusion rather than multi-sensor fusion, and no ablation separates the two contributions, which is the analysis that would give the result whatever interpretive content it might have. The omission is notable because it was free: Random Forest supplies feature importances by default and the paper reports Random Forest results without them. Without that decomposition, an accuracy of 98.33% is consistent with the model reading affective state, with it reading ambient temperature at the moment of capture, and with it reading individual identity across an image-level split - and the study provides no means of distinguishing them.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: None. A single image modality throughout, with no fusion of any kind.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: None across modalities - text only, with no acoustic, prosodic or visual information. The ratio features constitute a form of dyadic fusion in that they combine the child's output with the investigator's within a session, which is conceptually similar to the interaction-level modelling in the pose-based studies charted elsewhere in this review and is more than most transcript-based work attempts. Its vulnerability is that the investigator's behaviour is not standardised across the four source corpora, so the denominator of every ratio feature varies by protocol.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Two representational streams over one sensor, aligned by a pairwise Euclidean distance loss during training and then tested separately. Stream one encodes skeleton sequences as Skepxels for an image backbone; stream two embeds relative joint angles and applies MSG3D, combining graph convolution over the skeletal topology with temporal convolution over time. The design rationale is stated clearly - the loss 'minimises the distance between the Skepxel embedding, which captures spatiotemporal features, and the GCN embedding, which models structural joint relationships', promoting co-learning of complementary representations - and the ablation supports the graph component, with a Stack Transformer substitution lowering accuracy. This is representational rather than sensor fusion, but it is a coherent idea coherently tested. What is missing is a decomposition of how much each stream contributes to the final figure, which would be the natural complement to the architecture ablation that is reported.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: None. A single acoustic modality, with two analysis routes over the same signal - Praat-derived perturbation measures for the statistical comparison and spectrogram images for the network. The two routes are never joined: the paper does not test whether the network's confidence relates to jitter, shimmer or harmonics-to-noise ratio, which would have connected its interpretable finding to its opaque one and is the single most useful additional analysis the existing data would support.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: None. A single tabular modality.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: Three landmark streams from one camera, concatenated at the feature level and modelled jointly - within-camera multimodal fusion rather than multi-sensor fusion. The breadth is a genuine advantage: face, posture and hands are rarely combined in one model in this literature, and doing so at 30 frames per second with temporal modelling gives the network access to how expression, posture and gesture co-vary. The paper argues this explicitly, proposing a model that 'simultaneously analyzes facial expressions, head movements, hand gestures, and posture over time, combining spatial and temporal learning'. What is missing is any decomposition: no ablation reports performance with each stream removed, so the relative contribution of face, pose and hands is unknown. That omission is more costly here than usual, because the three streams carry very different confound exposure - facial mesh geometry is strongly sex-linked, hand motion energy much less so - and the study's 32-point sex imbalance between groups makes the distinction decisive for interpreting the result.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: None empirically. The proposed architecture is a two-stage fusion of facial expression analysis with questionnaire response, with the questionnaire invoked when facial cues are ambiguous - a sensible design in principle, since it routes the hard cases to the instrument actually validated for the construct. But the questionnaire was never administered to any person, so no fusion occurred on any data, and the claim that 'incorporating the GELOPH<15> questionnaire improved diagnostic reliability and consistency' describes an expected property of the design rather than an observed result.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: None. A single image modality throughout.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: Architectural rather than modal fusion. The autism model combines ResNet50V2 and InceptionV3 at the feature level, with the rationale that single-network approaches fail to obtain 'hierarchical features with fine grains'. Combining backbones whose receptive-field structures differ - residual depth against inception-module width - is a coherent argument for multi-granularity feature capture, and it is stated rather than assumed. No ablation isolates what each backbone contributes, so whether the hybrid outperforms its components is not established, and given the inconsistency in the reported metric set the comparison could not be evaluated in any case.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: Decision-level ensembling rather than modality fusion. Two CNNs classify independently and their outputs are combined by probability averaging or majority voting, with the stated rationale that this 'makes the system more reliable and accurate by lowering the chance of errors from a single model and making it better at generalizing new data'. Five pairings are compared, which gives real architectural breadth, and the pairings deliberately combine a lightweight backbone with an EfficientNet variant of differing scale. No ablation reports single-model performance against the ensembles, so the claimed ensembling gain is asserted rather than demonstrated.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: No fusion of behavioural modalities - eye tracking only. There is, however, an undeclared fusion of a different kind: the clinical instrument score (CARS) is concatenated with the behavioural features into a single input vector. That is not multimodal behavioural fusion; it is the insertion of the outcome's own measurement instrument into the predictor set. Multimodal work is named as future rather than present.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: No fusion - a single questionnaire modality, augmented by four static fields (age, sex, jaundice, family history). The study belongs to the corpus's questionnaire-tabular branch alongside local_8253c2ec and local_a0d73248 rather than to any sensor-based branch.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: No fusion - a single image modality. The architecture stacks several representations of the same photograph (CNN features, shape-appearance model, landmark graph, boosted trees), which the paper presents as integrating multiple facial features but which is pipeline depth rather than multimodality. Genuine multimodal fusion with voice, gaze and movement is deferred to future work.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion - eye tracking alone. There is a within-modality fusion of two representations of the same recording (scanpath sequences for the RNN path, cropped eye images for the CNN path), which is what the hybrid designation refers to. The Gesell Developmental Scale was collected and could have supported a genuine behavioural-clinical fusion, but no GDS result is reported.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: No fusion of modalities - a single image source. What the paper calls an ensemble is three classifiers (LSTM, DBN, HKELM) over one shared MobileNetV2 feature vector from one photograph. The LSTM's inclusion is unexplained: there is no temporal or sequential structure in a single still image for a recurrent model to exploit, and the paper never addresses this.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: This is one of the few charted studies with genuine cross-modal structure, and its fusion design is worth recording precisely. Two local models operate on separate files, one specialising in kinematic features and one in eye-movement features; their outputs are merged and passed to a global model with its own dense layers and dropout. That is late fusion at the model level, in contrast to the feature-concatenation fusion used elsewhere in the corpus. The design is sound in outline. What it cannot support is inference: with 44 examples divided among three clients and evaluated on nine cases, no comparison between the unimodal and fused configurations is distinguishable from noise, and the paper never makes that comparison explicitly in any case.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion - a single photographic modality. The introduction reviews thermal-imaging work at length (ResNet-50 on facial skin temperature across emotional states) and a thermal branch would have been a natural pairing with this acquisition setup, given that the protocol already controls room temperature and includes a body-temperature acclimation period. Only RGB photographs are collected.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: No fusion - a single questionnaire modality plus static demographic covariates. Multimodal extension with genetic and neuroimaging data is proposed as future work only.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: No modality fusion. The only fusion is the merging of two questionnaire datasets from different regions, which is dataset pooling rather than multimodal integration - and, as noted, the regional structure created by that merge is then discarded rather than used for cross-cohort validation.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: No fusion - a single questionnaire modality with demographic covariates. The systematic subset comparison is a study of feature configurations within one modality, not multimodal integration.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: No modality fusion - a single self-report modality throughout. The nearest analogue is the input-configuration comparison, which tests whether adding gender and/or autism diagnosis to the CAT-Q-ES items improves prediction and finds that it does not. The authors themselves identify observational measurement of camouflaging as the modality this study lacks and recommend adding it.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: No fusion of modalities. The hybrid designation refers to combining two vision backbones (ResNet and ViT) over the same image. The introduction reviews multimodal neuroimaging and EEG-plus-eye-tracking work and dismisses both on cost and complexity grounds.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: No fusion of modalities - a single image source. The pipeline stacks three processing stages (deblurring, denoising, classification) over one photograph, which is depth rather than multimodality.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: No modality fusion - a single tabular source. There is, however, a fusion of instrument types within the feature vector that is the study's defining characteristic: AQ-10 item responses, an AQ-10 total, a Q-CHAT-10 total, an SRS score and a CARS severity rating all sit in the same 19-variable input alongside the ASD_traits label they are designed to determine.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: No multimodal fusion - eye tracking alone. What the study does instead is a granularity comparison within one modality: four nested feature sets ranging from 24 broad variables to 158 fine-grained ones. The result is a clean negative finding that broad social/non-social area-of-interest variables carry the discriminative information while adding specific facial features and emotion categories does not improve accuracy. Multimodal extension with behavioural, cognitive or neurophysiological measures is named as the next step.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: No fusion of modalities - one image source. The hybrid model combines two ImageNet backbones over the same image, which is architectural ensembling rather than multimodality.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: No fusion - a single questionnaire modality. The hybrid designation refers to combining two convolutional architectures over the same tabular input.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Genuine and declared multimodal fusion, and the study's most useful applied finding. Kinematic features and self-report questionnaire scores are combined in an explicit grid of predictor configurations - kinematics alone, questionnaires alone (ASD, PD, or both) and their combinations - and the combination outperforms either alone for both classification problems (0.73 clinical versus non-clinical; 0.93 ASD versus PD). Because the questionnaire sets are named and separated, the contribution of each modality is visible rather than buried, and the finding that both trait questionnaires together beat either individually is directly interpretable.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: No fusion - a single questionnaire modality. What the study does perform is dataset harmonisation across four age cohorts into a common 15-attribute schema with stratified merging, which is cross-cohort integration rather than multimodal fusion. Multimodal extension with prosody and gaze is named as future work, and the absence of such cues is acknowledged as a constraint of the current data.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: Multimodal fusion is the framework's structural claim: each modality is partitioned, processed by per-partition CNNs, aggregated into a modality representation, and fused into a single feature vector for a softmax classifier. The claim cannot be evaluated. The modality set differs between sections (MRI, video, audio, text and EEG versus MRI, video and text); no dataset is characterised well enough to know what any modality contains; the fused feature vectors are printed as illustrative example numbers; and no ablation isolates any modality's contribution except a reference to an MRI-only ablation whose results are not shown in the extracted text.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: No fusion - video only. The CNN-GRU combination is spatial-plus-temporal modelling within one modality, and the architectural rationale is stated properly: convolutional layers extract spatial features from single frames while autism-related behaviour is a temporal phenomenon requiring sequence modelling across frames. That is a correct justification for a recurrent component, unlike the several studies in this corpus that apply LSTMs to single static inputs.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Modality is manipulated experimentally rather than fused computationally, which is a different and arguably more informative use of the term. By presenting the same storytelling task audio-only and audio-visually and comparing gaze features across the two, the study isolates what the visual speech channel contributes to group discrimination - and finds that it contributes most before speech onset. That is a designed contrast producing an interpretable answer, in contrast to the corpus's several studies that concatenate modalities and report only the combined figure.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: Dataset 2 is presented as genuine four-modality fusion - image, audio, motion and physiological features concatenated into a 4,220-dimensional vector - and the ablation attributes the final gain from 97.80% to 98.2% to multimodal integration. Three things make that uninterpretable. There are 4,220 features for 400 samples, of which only 100 are original. The 400 include augmented copies split across training and test, so the multimodal gain is measured on partly duplicated data. And no modality-level attribution is reported: SHAP and LIME are applied to Dataset 1 only, so the paper cannot say what any modality contributed. A 0.4-point accuracy gain on a 40-sample test set is a single case reclassified.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Genuine, declared and quantified multimodal fusion, and the study's central result. Objective task measures and the AQ questionnaire are evaluated separately and together on the same matched sample: 74% for tasks alone, 83% for the AQ alone, 92% combined. Because each configuration is reported, the increment attributable to fusion is visible (9 points over the questionnaire alone), and because the feature-importance profile is very similar with and without the AQ, the authors can argue that the two data types contribute information in different ways rather than merely duplicating each other. This is the only study in the charted corpus to report all three configurations and thereby make the fusion claim checkable.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: No modality fusion - eye tracking alone. What is fused is classifiers rather than data: bagging, boosting and stacking are combined within one architecture, with base learners selected by a stated diversity criterion to promote complementary decision boundaries.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: No fusion - a single image modality. The paper's own literature table lists no multimodal analysis as a limitation of a cited prior study and does not apply it to itself.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: No modality fusion - a single image source. The paper's fusion is across three ImageNet backbones (VGG16, DenseNet-121, XceptionNet) applied to the same photograph, which is representational concatenation rather than multimodality, and no ablation isolates any backbone's contribution.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: No modality fusion - 3D skeletal motion alone. The study's most interesting observation is instead about modality availability: the severe-ASD group could not be captured with the same sensor as the other two, so the modality itself is unavailable for the group whose severity the study most wants to classify. That is a genuine finding about the deployability of depth-sensor assessment and it applies well beyond this paper.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: No modality fusion - text alone, deliberately. The paper's argument is that excluding audio and video is the point, since transcripts avoid identifiable biometric data, and it acknowledges the cost: prosodic features indicative of atypical speech cannot be captured in text. Its future-work proposal to add limited prosodic cues while preserving text-level privacy is an explicit privacy-information trade-off, which no other study in this corpus formulates.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: No modality fusion - game telemetry alone. The behavioural anamnesis questionnaire completed by guardians is collected and not used as a predictor, which keeps the model's inputs clean of parent-report information but also leaves an available modality unexploited.

questions.question_text: Which model paradigms are used?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithms: support vector machine with RBF kernel, and probabilistic neural network (Parzen-window Bayes network).

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithm: linear-kernel support vector machine, with Fisher discriminant ratio feature ranking as the selection step.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithms: decision tree, random forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbour and AdaBoost, each evaluated with and without ReliefF feature selection across eight class-grouping definitions.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithm: RBF-kernel support vector machine, preceded by unsupervised K-means clustering used purely as a quantisation/feature-construction step.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Supervised learning with unsupervised dimensionality reduction. Algorithms: linear discriminant, quadratic discriminant and RBF-kernel SVM; latent semantic indexing (an SVD-based technique related to PCA) provides the representation. Graph-theoretic network analysis (local clustering coefficient) is used descriptively alongside the classifiers.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Supervised learning with decision-tree ensembles: ExtraTrees, Random Forest and Regularized Greedy Forest (plus an RGF variant without demographics). The authors explicitly rejected SVMs and gradient boosting machines as overfitting-prone given more features than observations and strong inter-feature correlations - a deliberate model-selection rationale that is rare in this corpus.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Supervised learning, with unsupervised PCA used only for feature selection. Algorithms: Naive Bayes, SVM with linear and RBF kernels, decision tree C4.5 and random forest. The choice of Naive Bayes first is explicitly motivated by anticipated SVM overfitting given 40 features and 30 samples, and the paper reports the informative finding that Naive Bayes performed comparably to SVM even on a quarter of the features, speculating that the independence assumption may genuinely hold for these kinematic parameters.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: Supervised learning. The diagnostic classifier is an RBF-kernel SVM with greedy forward feature selection. A deep CNN (a modified dynamic deep-learning AU architecture) is used upstream as a pre-trained facial action unit detector. The authors explicitly reject end-to-end deep learning on raw pixels because the small training set would cause severe overfitting - a deliberate and well-reasoned choice to use deep learning for representation but not for diagnosis.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithms: linear-kernel SVM (Weka SMO) as the baseline, chosen for robustness and insensitivity to feature overfitting, and a one-layer bidirectional LSTM neural network with eight cells as the deep-learning alternative. The comparison is reported as effectively a tie, which the authors attribute to sample size rather than to the architectures.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Unsupervised deep representation learning combined with supervised classification. Algorithms: a generative adversarial network whose discriminator acts as a non-linear feature extractor, with hidden-layer activations fed to a linear-kernel SVM. Baselines: linear SVM, RBF-kernel SVM and a four-hidden-layer multilayer perceptron. Notably the GAN is used purely for representation learning, not for the data augmentation that the introduction motivates - the generator's synthetic samples are never used to enlarge the training set.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithms: a three-layer feed-forward artificial neural network trained by scaled conjugate gradient backpropagation, and support vector machines with linear, polynomial and RBF kernels. Stepwise discriminant analysis serves as a statistical feature-selection stage. The authors note that comparative studies often favour SVM, which makes their ANN result a departure from expectation.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithms: decision tree, k-nearest neighbours, Gaussian-kernel SVM, linear discriminant analysis and logistic regression, each evaluated on both feature families and on the stacked combination. Gaussian SVM was selected as the final model. Statistical hypothesis testing (t-test, ANOVA) is used alongside classification to establish that the features carry group information.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Supervised learning with a single algorithm: support vector machine, described as discriminant analysis. No comparison against alternative classifiers, which is unusual for this corpus and arguably a strength - it removes the best-of-many selection optimism that inflates other studies here.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithm: binary SVM optimised by stochastic gradient descent with a hinge loss objective, preceded by correlation-based feature subset selection. No deep learning, and no comparison against alternative classifiers - the paper's contribution is the data collection and fusion scheme rather than the model.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithm: logistic regression in R, chosen after testing several classification algorithms. The deliberate choice of a simple linear model with a small feature set, rather than a high-capacity model on 30 participants, is consistent with the paper's general conservatism about overfitting.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Supervised deep learning: a pre-trained GoogLeNet CNN as frame feature extractor feeding a recurrent LSTM with a learned soft spatial attention mechanism and a binary softmax classifier. A handcrafted alternative (dense trajectories with HOG/HOF and VLAD encoding) is included specifically as a baseline and is reported to perform at chance - an informative negative comparison that most corpus studies omit.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: Supervised learning with unsupervised embedding: gradient boosted decision trees (LightGBM) over t-SNE embeddings of a ScanMatch similarity matrix. The Needleman-Wunsch sequence alignment underlying ScanMatch is a classical bioinformatics algorithm repurposed for gaze. A benchmark condition substitutes Levenshtein distance and Kruskal's non-metric multidimensional scaling for the ScanMatch/t-SNE pair.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Supervised learning with a broad classifier comparison: SVM, linear discriminant analysis, decision tree, random forest and k-nearest neighbour with k in {1,3,5,7}. KNN with k=1 - effectively a nearest-neighbour lookup, the highest-variance choice available - gave the best result, which on 43 participants with four selected features warrants caution the paper does not express.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Supervised learning: a Gradient Boosting Classifier from scikit-learn. Principal Component Analysis is used unsupervised for dimensionality reduction. No comparison against alternative classifiers, which removes best-of-many selection optimism but also leaves the algorithm choice unjustified empirically.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Supervised learning: random forest with bootstrap sampling, majority voting and balanced class weights. A pre-trained deep convolutional network (OpenFace, 37 layers in 8 Inception blocks) is used upstream as a frozen feature extractor without fine-tuning, on the stated grounds that the LFW training set is sufficiently general.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Random forests per rater with softmax ensemble weighting for the main classification; logistic regression with elastic net regularisation and balanced class weights for the cross-cultural transfer analysis. The choice of a two-layer stack is motivated conceptually - layer one optimised for sensitivity so no atypical case is missed, layer two optimised for both sensitivity and specificity to separate ASD from other delays - which links model design to intended clinical use more explicitly than most of the corpus.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithm: random forest via MATLAB TreeBagger with 128 trees and bootstrap aggregation, selected on the stated grounds that it performs well on all-numeric feature sets with a numeric class label. Mean-shift clustering is used unsupervised as a feature-construction step. No alternative classifiers are compared.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Not machine learning in the supervised sense. The method is probabilistic sequential decision-making: a hierarchical POMDP with task-level and protocol-level models, solved by the SARSOP point-based value iteration solver. Model parameters are specified rather than learned - transition matrices for child states are identity (robot actions cannot change the child's condition, and no data existed on their effect on engagement or verbal activity), and observation probabilities were elicited from a clinician survey. The authors themselves note that comparison against trained classifiers is not yet possible for lack of data.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithm: support vector machine only, selected because it is used in the cited literature and is a capable binary classifier. No paradigm comparison, no alternative algorithms, and no kernel specification.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Supervised learning. Algorithm: SVM with RBF kernel, with C and gamma grid-searched. Four feature-selection strategies are compared as complete pipelines: SVM recursive feature elimination (embedded), two-sample t-test (filter), ReliefF (filter with neighbour interactions) and mRMR (filter with redundancy penalty). The finding that the two simplest filters outperformed the two more sophisticated methods is reported without embellishment.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: Supervised learning, with the problem deliberately recast as image classification. Conventional baselines (Naive Bayes, logistic regression, SVM, random forests) are compared against feed-forward artificial neural networks of increasing capacity (single layer with 50, 200 or 500 neurons; two layers of 80 and 40), trained with 100 epochs and 20% dropout. PCA provides unsupervised dimensionality reduction. Notably no convolutional architecture is used despite the image framing, since PCA-compressed grayscale vectors are fed to fully connected layers.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Supervised learning: linear-kernel support vector machine, with PCA used unsupervised for dimensionality reduction. A single algorithm with no best-of-many comparison, consistent with the paper's methodological conservatism.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: A commercial third-party classifier, Play.Care, described as an adaptation of the algorithm developed and published from the pilot study. Its internals are not restated in the protocol, and for the trial's purposes this is by design: the point of a phase III evaluation is that the instrument is locked and applied unchanged to new data, so the algorithm's specification belongs to the development phase rather than to the evaluation. The trade-off is that the trial can establish whether the instrument works without establishing what it measures - a limitation the protocol does not name.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Supervised deep learning throughout. Fully connected networks of two capacities for the synthetic saccade approach, and a dual-branch convolutional architecture built on pretrained ResNet-18 for the image-based approach. STAR-FC, a computational saliency and saccade generation model, is used upstream as a reference generator rather than as a classifier. No conventional machine-learning comparators are included.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: Supervised deep learning throughout, in a three-stage pipeline: a retrained Mask R-CNN detector for pose estimation, a classical particle filter for state estimation of missing keypoints, and a convolutional binary classifier over the resulting motion images. A conventional video-classification approach (Inception V3 on single frames with majority voting) serves as a baseline, which is a genuine comparator rather than a strawman since it represents standard practice.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: No model is trained on the study's own data. The neural components are pretrained and used as instruments: Dlib's CNN face detector and ResNet face recogniser, and OpenFace's CLNF landmark and gaze estimator, integrated into ROS nodes with the neural model made an attribute of the node class and evaluated on each topic callback. The only inference component developed here is the Hidden Markov Model for visual focus of attention, which infers the attention target from the fused pose and gaze sequence. For a review of computational approaches this is the measurement-infrastructure end of the field: the machine learning does the perceptual work that a human coder would otherwise do frame by frame, and the clinical inference remains with the therapist. The paper's stated purpose supports this reading - automated video coding is intended to 'help the clinicians to reduce the delay of ASD diagnosis' by removing the manual coding burden, not to produce a diagnosis.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: Supervised deep learning combining convolutional and recurrent architectures: shallow CNNs for per-patch visual encoding and a two-layer LSTM for sequence modelling, with a pretrained generative adversarial saliency model (SalGAN) used upstream as a frozen feature source. No conventional machine-learning comparators are included, and no ablation isolates the contribution of the saliency map versus the raw image.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: None. No computational or machine-learning model is fitted. The analysis is a Wilcoxon signed-rank test on paired within-subject proportions, which is the correct choice for small-sample paired ordinal data and is used appropriately. For a review of computation-based approaches, the study sits immediately upstream of the modelling work: it establishes that a robot-delivered paradigm produces a measurable and theoretically interpretable behavioural dissociation, which is the finding that a subsequent automated system would need to reproduce.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Three classical supervised classifiers compared on identical tabular features: support vector machine, Gaussian naive Bayes and random forest, all from scikit-learn. No deep learning, which is appropriate at n = 83 with 10 features. The three algorithms perform within about three percentage points of each other, which is itself informative: with this feature set the choice of classifier matters far less than the choice of elicitation episode.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Supervised learning with SVM-RBF as the fixed classifier, so that the experimental variable is feature selection rather than model family. Four established selectors are benchmarked (t-test filter, SVM-RFE, ReliefF, mRMR) and three variants developed (ensemble, bagging, wrapped t-test). Holding the classifier constant while varying selection is a clean design that isolates the contribution the paper is actually studying.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: Deep supervised learning: VGG-19 and ResNet-18 convolutional neural networks for seven-way facial expression classification. The paper argues explicitly for deep over traditional approaches, on the grounds that handcrafted features (oriented gradient histograms, Gabor filters, local directional patterns, enhanced local binary patterns) are 'artificial design, time-consuming and laborious' and work well only on small image sets, whereas end-to-end deep models combine feature extraction and classification. Critically, neither network is trained on an autism label - the diagnostic layer is a hand-set threshold on classification agreement, not a learned model.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Supervised learning with an unusually broad comparison: discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbour, naive Bayes, decision trees, support vector machine and random forest, each briefly explained with a citation. The rationale is stated explicitly - because features, sample sizes and data structures differ, 'no one algorithm works best for every dataset', so researchers usually implement several and explore the best. The authors also note that basic supervised algorithms are chosen because they are 'computationally efficient and relevant to small sample sizes'.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Supervised learning with a deliberate depth comparison: a 1D convolutional neural network chosen for its suitability to ordered temporal data, benchmarked against random forest and k-nearest neighbour, which the authors describe as having 'simpler structures than a deep CNN with fewer hyperparameters that require fine-tuning'. Reporting a null result from this comparison - that all three perform equivalently - is a strength.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: A hybrid of classical algorithm and learning: dynamic time warping provides temporal alignment, metric learning determines how the three derived features combine, and a support vector machine performs diagnostic classification. The design rationale is stated explicitly - the authors deliberately impose structure to reduce learnable parameters using expert-derived guidance, arguing that 'using expert knowledge to guide the features improved CAMI's interpretability, while deviance from HOC as a result of automatized learning processes improved CAMI's diagnostic discriminative ability'.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: Four models compared on identical data: a linear-kernel SVM baseline, a vanilla eight-cell BLSTM on 88 features, the same BLSTM on 54 statistically selected features, and a stacked auto-encoder jointly optimised with the BLSTM. The auto-encoder is semi-supervised, carrying an auxiliary binary ASD/TD softmax head on its latent layer so that the representation is shaped by the diagnostic target rather than by reconstruction alone. Joint optimisation of representation and classifier is the paper's actual contribution, and holding the BLSTM fixed at eight cells across conditions is what isolates it.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Four classical supervised classifiers held as the experimental variable: SVM, KNN, random forest and decision tree, each optimised by grid search so that comparisons are between best-configured models rather than arbitrary defaults. The selection rationale is stated per classifier - KNN as a simple baseline suited to small data, SVM as the field's default for small datasets and for autism classification specifically, and random forest and decision tree for their handling of non-linearly separable data. No deep learning, appropriately for 105 or 278 data points with eight features.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: Six models spanning linear regression, kernel regression and three deep architectures, all on identical data, which makes the comparison genuinely informative. The decisive variable turns out to be input structure rather than model family: the same 100 x 48 matrix input produces the two best models (FC-DNN 3 and CNN) while the same sub-sampled features presented as independent 48-vectors (FC-DNN 2) produce the worst model of all six. The authors draw the right conclusion - that architectures exploiting multiple simultaneous samples of a child's speech have a large advantage, and that the non-linear models' margin over linear regression and SVR shows 'the optimal ADOS prediction model is not likely to be linear'.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: Logistic regression, chosen after testing a set of standard classification algorithms in R with the comparison deposited publicly. A deliberately simple model, appropriate at 30-38 participants, and consistent with the paper's emphasis on characterising the signal and the data representation rather than on architecture. The experimental variables are the task, the AOI definition and the feature set, not the learner.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: A hybrid: a pretrained two-stream CNN as a fixed feature extractor (not fine-tuned on this data), scale-specific SVM regression models via LIBSVM, and Otsu thresholding for the final decision. Using a frozen pretrained CNN is a sensible response to 74 participants, avoiding the overfitting that end-to-end deep training would invite, and the SVM stage operates on a much larger effective sample because each child contributes many scanpath pieces. The multi-scale design - one model per piece length from 1 to 5 fixations - is the architectural contribution, and is explicitly contrasted with the alternative of zero-padding variable-length scanpaths to a fixed size.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: A conventional and appropriately conservative pipeline for 47 participants: PCA at 95% variance retention, then C-SVM with a Gaussian kernel, with nonlinear SVM-RFE including correlation bias reduction as a wrapper inside each training fold. No deep learning is used for classification - OpenPose supplies the deep component as a fixed, externally trained pose estimator, which is the right division of labour at this sample size. Hyperparameters were searched over seven logarithmically spaced values of cost and gamma between 0.1 and 1000.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: A cascade rather than a single model: pretrained ASR, pretrained face detection, a fine-tuned two-branch expression network, and a shallow classifier over six binary scores. The design is well matched to the data regime - deep components are trained on large external corpora (AISHELL-2, Oulu-CASIA, and the purpose-built 15,000-clip children's database) while the only model fitted to the 41-child cohort is a decision tree over six features. Four classifiers are compared, with the decision tree best by a wide margin (80.49% against 70.73% for SVM), which for a six-dimensional binary feature space is plausible.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: Three sparsity-inducing methods compared on identical splits - lasso, group lasso and the paper's SGIN - against a panel of non-sparse baselines (linear and RBF SVM, decision tree, random forest, linear and logistic regression) run 100 times each. SGIN extends group l1 regularisation to a multi-layer non-linear network by penalising the Frobenius norm of the parameter block connecting each input group to all first-hidden-layer neurons, and introduces a Stochastic Blockwise Coordinated Gradient Descent optimiser that converges faster and finds more sparse groups than plain SGD. The comparison is informative precisely because the winner is not the most accurate model: non-sparse linear baselines reach about 84% accuracy against SGIN's 78-80%, but they remove nothing, so they cannot shorten the battery at all.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: A single linear SVM throughout, preceded by mRMR feature selection based on mutual information, chosen for jointly maximising relevance to the class label and minimising redundancy among features. No model comparison is performed - the experimental variable is the modality and the number of selected features, not the learner. This is a defensible focus given the paper's question, but it means there is no evidence about whether the linear SVM is the right choice for these features.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: Elastic net as the primary classifier, chosen explicitly for the data regime: 219 features per trial against 33 participants means 'regularization was important to prevent model overfitting', and elastic net combines lasso and ridge penalties. Logistic regression with grid-searched l1 or l2 regularisation serves as an ablation comparator, included on the technical grounds that elastic net optimisers can be unstable at the edge cases where one penalty vanishes. Elastic net outperformed logistic regression in most tasks, which the authors read as confirming 'a need for regularization in this dataset'. No deep learning, correctly - the discussion notes that a larger, more balanced corpus 'would also enable the use of more complex statistical models, such as artificial neural networks', which is a statement of what the data cannot currently support.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: A single random forest of 1,000 trees with maximum depth and minimum samples per leaf tuned over seven values each, applied identically to each modality and to the combination. Model choice is deliberately conservative given 80 participants, and an earlier conference paper by the same group compared alternative approaches. The more consequential modelling decision is what enters the model: features were restricted 'strictly to features based on domain-knowledge or on the EMG preparatory study' for the primary analyses, which is a principled constraint that sacrifices accuracy for interpretability and is quantified by the parallel all-action-unit result.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: A Two-Class Boosted Decision Tree, selected after comparing linear regression, logistic regression, multiclass neural networks, support vector algorithms and quantile regression models within Azure ML Studio. The stated justification - that ensemble boosting suits small tabular data better than the bagging of random forests or the hierarchical structure of neural networks - is reasonable in outline, and choosing a shallow tabular model over deep learning at n = 108 is the right instinct. But no performance figure is given for any comparator, so the selection cannot be assessed, and including linear and quantile regression in a binary classification comparison indicates the model set was not well matched to the task.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: A two-state Hidden Markov Model with the severity level as the hidden state and the two binned behavioural categories as observables. The choice is defensible for an intrinsically sequential intervention series with a latent clinical state, and the model is inherently interpretable. But the temporal structure that motivates an HMM is not actually exploited - sessions are treated as independent observations rather than as a sequence within child, no state transitions over the course of therapy are examined, and the reported posterior computation is a static Bayes calculation over two conditionals rather than a sequential inference. In effect the model functions as a naive Bayes classifier over nine input cells, with the HMM framing adding formalism rather than capability.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Random forests, one per video segment, combined into an ensemble by weighted voting - a design that mirrors the temporal structure of the stimulus rather than flattening it. Three combination strategies are compared systematically, and the exhaustive variant testing all 511 subsets is thorough as an exploration but constitutes a very large selection space when evaluated on the same cross-validation used for reporting. No deep learning, which is appropriate at 86 participants, and no single-model baseline over concatenated features is reported, so the benefit of the segment-wise decomposition itself is not isolated.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: Seven classical classifiers plus an ensemble, with each model's assumptions and their consequences discussed individually - PCA applied before logistic regression because of multicollinearity and before naive Bayes because of its independence assumption, normalisation before KNN because distance is scale-sensitive, standardisation before SVM for convergence. This model-by-model reasoning is more careful than most of the corpus. The ensemble is then justified on generalisation rather than accuracy grounds, which is the right argument and is the one the test experiment supports.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: k-nearest neighbours, deliberately simple, chosen for the low intrinsic dimensionality of gaze coordinates, for tolerance of overlapping class distributions and for small-sample performance. The single hyperparameter k was fixed by piloting on a different published dataset rather than tuned on the present data - so the entire model specification is set outside the evaluation, which removes the model-selection optimism that affects most of the corpus. No comparison against alternative classifiers is reported, which is a minor gap, but the choice is consistent with a paper whose stated aim is to avoid optimising anything on the evaluation data.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Three classical classifiers compared on identical features: KNN with Euclidean distance, Gaussian naive Bayes and a cubic-kernel SVM. The choice is appropriate for 83 samples and 43 features, and the paper's stated rationale for the whole approach - preferring structured interpretable features over unstructured deep learning inputs - is coherent and is followed through. The cubic kernel is an unusual choice, more prone to overfitting than the standard RBF at this sample size, and no justification for the polynomial degree is given.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: A graph convolutional network over a feature graph, with random forest for upstream gaze feature selection, compared against an SVM-based feature-engineering pipeline and a ResNet18. The GCN choice is well matched to the stated problem - modelling relationships between features across modalities where no explicit correlation exists between the raw signals - and using features rather than subjects as graph nodes is an unusual and defensible formulation. That the much deeper ResNet18 performs worst supports the argument that architecture matched to the fusion problem matters more than capacity at this sample size.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: An unusual architecture for this corpus: rather than training one discriminative classifier on participant-level features, the paper trains one small generative model per severity group - each a ten-neuron single-hidden-layer network with Bayesian regularisation, predicting whether a pixel was fixated by that group - and then classifies a new participant by which group's saliency map their own fixation map more closely resembles. This is a nearest-prototype scheme in saliency space. It has two consequences worth noting: the model is small enough to be well conditioned on the available data, and the comparison of the two fitted models is itself the scientific output, which is why the feature-selection difference is reported as the main finding rather than as an ablation.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Four classical classifiers - SVM, linear discriminant analysis, decision tree and random forest - each wrapped in forward feature selection, with the paper giving a short rationale for each including the observation that decision trees offer 'strong interpretability, but it is prone to overfitting'.
