The model comparison is informative in one respect: random forest needed sixteen features to reach 84.62% while SVM reached 92.31% with three, which speaks to how concentrated the signal is. The wrapper design is also what creates the study's main methodological weakness, since the selection criterion is the reported metric.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: A single-hidden-layer feed-forward network trained by scaled conjugate gradient, chosen for its lack of user-dependent parameters and avoidance of line search, compared against RBF-kernel SVM and naive Bayes on identical features. The comparison is systematic and the network wins in every condition, though the margins - 100% against 78.5% for SVM and 91.2% for naive Bayes on the same MFCC features for autism detection - are large enough to be suspicious, since a shallow network and an RBF SVM on the same low-dimensional features would not normally diverge this far unless one is exploiting something the other is not.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: A convolutional network with four convolutional layers, four pooling layers, two fully connected layers and dropout, trained for three epochs. The architectural choice follows directly from the representation decision: having converted gaze to images, the natural learner is a CNN, and the authors describe the whole approach as recasting diagnosis as 'a typical task of image classification'. No comparison against alternative classifiers or against engineered-feature baselines is reported, though the authors note this study builds on their own earlier work using fixation and saccade event features.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Two small neural networks, one per group, each acting as a generative model of where that group looks, plus a similarity-vote decision rule - the same architecture as the severity study from the same laboratory but applied to diagnosis. SVM was tested as an alternative learner and performed worse (0.775 against 0.818 without selection). The comparison table across six classifier-and-selection combinations is genuinely informative: genetic algorithm selection raised the network's mean AUC only from 0.818 to 0.822 but cut its standard deviation from 0.053 to 0.015, while the same selection dropped the SVM from 0.775 to 0.695. Reporting a case where feature selection helps stability rather than accuracy, and helps one learner while harming another, is more nuanced than most of the corpus manages.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: Five classifiers - naive Bayes, XGBoost, kNN, random forest and SVM - trained on each of ten datasets, with the best per dataset reported. Default hyperparameters were used throughout, a decision the authors justify explicitly as avoiding an additional layer of search complexity. That is defensible and unusually candid, though it means the algorithm comparison reflects default behaviour rather than tuned potential, and different algorithms win on different datasets (SVM on two, kNN on two, naive Bayes on two, random forest and XGBoost on one each), which is what one would expect when nothing is tuned and sample sizes are small.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Five classifiers compared on identical features, each with a short rationale and stated weaknesses, including the acknowledgement that decision trees are 'prone to overfitting' and that random forest 'could well address the overfitting problem of the DT algorithm' - which makes it notable that the decision tree nonetheless produced the highest accuracy, a pattern consistent with the exhaustive search finding a favourable split on a small sample. Reporting that all five classifiers exceeded 81% with three features or fewer is more informative than the single maximum, since it shows the signal is not classifier-specific.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: Nine classifiers spanning trees, ensembles, kernel methods, neural networks and probabilistic models, applied uniformly across all five datasets. Breadth is the only principle - no rationale is given for any individual choice, no hyperparameters are reported, and the winning algorithm differs by cluster (multilayer perceptron in cluster 1, random forest in clusters 3 and 4, three classifiers tied in cluster 2), which at these sample sizes is consistent with noise rather than with any property of the clusters.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: A single radial-basis-function SVM with hyperparameters grid-searched at each leave-one-subject-out iteration. No model comparison is reported, which is appropriate given that classification is explicitly secondary to the mechanistic question and the paper makes no claim about optimal architecture. The design decision that matters is aggregation: the classifier operates on trials, and subject-level inference is obtained by taking each participant's proportion of positive trial responses as an estimate of diagnosis probability, from which the ROC is built.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: No model is trained. The system is rule-based throughout: off-the-shelf Haar cascade classifiers perform face and ear detection as measurement infrastructure, and the attention score is accumulated by hand-specified increments with operator-adjustable constants. There is no training set, test set, cross-validation or fitted parameter anywhere. For a review of computational approaches this is a useful boundary case, because it shows what can be achieved without learning: a transparent, adjustable, real-time measure that tracks a clinician's judgement on 82.4% of sessions and closes a therapy loop. The corresponding limitation is that the constants are asserted rather than derived, so the score's calibration rests on the operator's judgement rather than on evidence.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Nine classifiers spanning probabilistic, instance-based, linear, tree, ensemble and kernel families, each described in a sentence with no rationale for inclusion and no hyperparameters. Breadth substitutes for justification. That six of the 27 cells reach 95% while the rest cluster between 90% and 92.5% - a spread of two test cases - indicates the comparison is not resolving real differences between algorithms.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: A single linear SVM with L1 regularisation, chosen after the non-linear variant underperformed and justified by L1's property of zeroing uninformative coefficients - appropriate for a high-dimensional feature space built by summarising frame measures across statistics, regions and activities. The more important modelling decision is the inclusion of an explicit chance classifier that randomly assigns participants, run through the same pipeline and reported in every results table at 49.90% AUC with its own confidence interval. That baseline is what converts the reported figures from numbers into evidence, and its presence distinguishes this study from most of the corpus.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: A bagged decision-tree ensemble over 30 hand-engineered features - deliberately classical rather than deep, and justified by the comparison table showing that no classifier family separated meaningfully from any other. The spread across all 23 candidates is 59.3% (fine KNN) to 68.5% (TreeBagger), roughly nine points across decision trees, discriminant analysis, logistic regression, naive Bayes, six SVM kernels, five nearest-neighbour variants and five ensembles. That flatness is itself an informative negative result: when every model family lands within a few points of every other, the limiting factor is the feature representation and the data, not the learner - which supports the authors' focus on features and undercuts any claim that a deeper model would help.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Five architectures compared directly on the same data: baseline MLP, branched multi-encoder MLP, CNN over fixation maps, ResNet18/ResNet50 two-branch image models, and a 5-layer LSTM. The spread on the blind test set is 52.53% (CNN-SP-STAR) to 62.13% (ResNet50) - about ten points across shallow and deep, feedforward, convolutional and recurrent families - and the two best (62.13% and 61.39%) come from opposite ends of that range, a deep image model and a shallow MLP on raw coordinates. As in the companion paper on the same benchmark, the flatness across architecture families indicates that the limiting factor is the data rather than model capacity. The authors also note a specific failure mode with a plausible cause: the CNN over fixation maps performed worst, which they attribute to 'the mismatch between the fixation image maps and the CNN networked pretrained on natural images' - a sparse synthetic input passed through an ImageNet backbone.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: A CNN-LSTM action-recognition architecture - VGG16 for per-frame spatial encoding, a 512-unit LSTM for temporal dependency within 5-second windows - selected because it 'previously showed a good performance in video-based action classification'. The choice matches the construct: if what distinguishes the groups is the temporal coordination of non-verbal behaviours rather than their static configuration, a model without temporal structure could not capture it. The authors report that the final architecture 'was obtained upon testing various configurations', with the alternatives shown in supplementary Figure S2, and that 5-second segments beat 10- and 15-second segments on validation loss - so architecture and segment length were both selected on the internal validation split rather than on the held-out children, which is the correct separation.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: A single small feedforward network - 17 inputs, one hidden layer of five tanh units, two softmax outputs - chosen for the stated reason that neural networks handle 'complex and nonlinear relationships between variables', which matches the paper's explicit epistemic position that no individual movement variable need differ between groups and that what is categorisable is 'the dynamic interaction of these features'. That position is argued rather than assumed, with a citation to Yarkoni and Westfall on prediction versus explanation, and it justifies choosing a predictive framework over group-difference testing. Model selection was equally restrained: a descending grid search from 10 hidden units found comparable accuracy down to 5 and degradation below, and 5 was chosen on the explicit principle that fewer hidden units reduce overfitting. Deliberate simplicity of this kind is rare in this corpus and is the right instinct for a 60-participant dataset; the difficulty is that it was verified against a cross-validation that does not hold participants out.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Stacked denoising autoencoders used hierarchically - two for unimodal representation learning, a third for fusion - with greedy layer-wise unsupervised pre-training followed by supervised fine-tuning. The choice is well matched to the problem: 221 hand-engineered features from 90 children is a regime where supervised deep learning would overfit immediately, and unsupervised pre-training exploits the input data without consuming label information, while the denoising objective with zero-masking corruption prevents the identity mapping and encourages robustness. The paper justifies the choice by precedent in Alzheimer's diagnosis, ADHD classification and machinery fault diagnosis. The architecture is also deliberately shallow - two hidden layers per model, compressing 125 to 50 and 96 to 50 - which is appropriate for the sample size, though the t-SNE analysis reveals a cost the authors acknowledge: learned EEG features separate the classes less well than raw ones in the visualisation, which they attribute to dimension reduction discarding useful information.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: CNN-LSTM with soft attention over raw video - a standard action-recognition architecture, applied without modification and without comparison to alternatives. Only one model is reported: no baseline, no ablation over architecture, no simpler comparator such as a frame-averaged CNN or a hand-engineered gaze-shift detector, and no chance or trivial baseline. The architectural choices are nonetheless well reasoned for the task. The last convolutional layer of VGG-16 is retained specifically because it 'preserves the spatial information' as a 7x7 grid of 512-dimensional vectors rather than a globally pooled summary, which matters when the discriminative event is a head turn at a particular image location. The LSTM supplies temporal structure, necessary because the target behaviour is a sequence - object, then person, then object - not a static configuration. And the attention module is included not for performance but for inspectability, which is how it is actually used.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Deliberately conventional classifiers - random forest, SVM and K-nearest neighbour - with all three applied to every modality, and both best and average accuracy reported. Running the full grid rather than reporting one model is informative: the spread on EEG features runs from 65.00% (SVM) to 83.75% (random forest), an 18-point range on identical inputs, and SVM is the weakest learner on all three modalities. That variability is a caution about single-classifier results generally, and its reporting here is more transparent than the corpus norm. The modelling novelty sits in the combiner rather than the base learners: an attribute-weighted naive Bayes whose weights are computed from training-set counts, with the formula given and its zero-avoidance property noted. No deep model is used for classification, which is appropriate given 80 participants, though a CNN is used upstream for facial expression recognition.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: A Kernel Extreme Learning Machine - a single-hidden-layer feedforward network with randomly assigned input weights and an analytically computed output layer, kernelised with an RBF - chosen for computational economy over deep models, with the paper explicitly excluding deep learning from comparison 'since they require many computational resources and time for training'. The KELM has exactly two tunable parameters, C and gamma, and the entire modelling contribution is how they are chosen. The Giza Pyramids Construction algorithm searches that two-dimensional space via a metaphor of workers pushing stone blocks up a ramp, with gravity, ramp angle, kinetic friction and a worker-substitution probability as parameters. It is worth stating plainly that a two-parameter search over a grid of powers of two from 2^-7 to 2^7 does not require a population-based metaheuristic - exhaustive enumeration of 225 combinations would be cheaper than 10 iterations of a 10-member population - so the algorithmic apparatus considerably exceeds the difficulty of the problem it is applied to. The convergence result reported (optimal values found by iteration six) reflects this.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: The modelling is deliberately simple and the choice is argued: a Gaussian naive Bayes classifier on four features, because the study's question is whether diagnostic information exists in the gaze data at all, not how much a flexible model can extract from 153 participants. The complementary unsupervised analysis uses a variational Bayesian Gaussian mixture model, which learns the number of clusters from the data rather than being told it - an important property here, since forcing two clusters would have guaranteed a partition that could be compared against diagnosis, whereas learning the number allows the data to indicate no meaningful split. It returned predominantly two clusters (25 of 33 windows) and was robust to initialisation at 5, 10 or 20 components. Pairing a supervised classifier with an unsupervised clustering that asks the same question from the opposite direction, and finding that both fail to recover diagnosis, is stronger evidence than either alone.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Three families compared on identical folds - an ensemble tree model on hand-engineered features, a convolutional network on spectrograms, and a fine-tuned self-supervised transformer on raw waveforms - which spans the realistic design space for a small audio classification problem. The comparison is conducted honestly: alternatives that lost are named rather than omitted (logistic regression, Gaussian naive Bayes, AdaBoost for the shallow family; Inception v3 for the deep one), and the winning CNN is the smallest deep model tried. Full hyperparameters are given for the random forest and described as 'manually chosen', with no tuning procedure stated - which leaves open whether the shallow model was tuned as carefully as the deep ones and hence whether the ten-point gap partly reflects unequal effort. The fold-to-fold correlation across all three models is the most thoughtful analytic observation in the paper: 'each model appears to perform well on fold 2 while performing relatively poorly on fold 3. This suggests that the data in each fold may be too limited', which correctly attributes the variance to the data partition rather than to model instability.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Linear-kernel SVMs throughout, chosen deliberately over more flexible alternatives and justified by prior use in speech-and-autism work. Non-linear SVMs and formal hyperparameter tuning were run and relegated to supplementary material with the linear configuration reported in the main text - which is the correct ordering when the goal is validating interpretable measures rather than maximising accuracy, though it does mean the reported soft-margin constants (C = 10, 1 and 100 for the three models) were selected on performance. The restraint is consistent with the study's stated purpose: 17 interpretable features, a linear classifier, and an emphasis on which participants are detected rather than on how high the number can be pushed. The mSVM-RFE analysis then delivers a genuinely useful negative result - the optimal eight-feature subset (0.9344) did not significantly outperform the full 17-feature model (0.9235, p = 0.1592), so feature selection bought nothing, and the authors report this rather than promoting the higher figure as their headline.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: A single SVM with RBF kernel on two or three interpretable features, chosen because it 'is popular when used on relatively smaller datasets' and paired with leave-one-out cross-validation explicitly 'to minimize the risk of overoptimistic classification', citing Vabalas et al. (2019) - one of only two studies in this corpus to cite the methodological literature on validation bias directly. The modelling is deliberately subordinate to the statistical analysis: the paper's primary evidence is a set of mixed ANOVAs, Mann-Whitney and Wilcoxon tests with effect sizes and ANCOVA covariate control, and classification is used to answer a specific supplementary question - whether the measures 'can be integrated to distinguish autistic and neurotypical toddlers'. That ordering is appropriate for a study whose contribution is a behavioural finding rather than a screening product, and it is unusual in this corpus, where classification accuracy is typically the primary and often the only evidence. Classifier configurations are compared by a formal variance-based true-difference criterion, so the claim that combining across movies beats single movies is tested rather than asserted.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: A single linear-kernel SVM applied consistently across all six configurations, with the kernel choice argued from the structure of the problem rather than selected empirically: linear kernels are 'preferable to non-linear kernels because theoretically it is always possible to find a linear decision boundary that separates data, in spite of high data dimensionality and small sample size', with precedent cited in neuroimaging and gene expression, where features routinely outnumber samples. Holding the model fixed across all six configurations is the right design for a study whose question is about features rather than about learners - any performance difference between rhythm and intonation, or between English and Cantonese, is attributable to the data rather than to differential model tuning. No alternative classifier is compared, which is appropriate given that no classification-performance claim is being made against competing methods.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Frozen pre-trained encoders feeding conventional classifiers, rather than end-to-end fine-tuning - the appropriate choice for 50 participants and roughly 300 words each, and justified on exactly those grounds: 'Thanks to the properties of embedding vectors, classification algorithms can successfully learn from relatively small labelled data sets.' Three classifier families were tried (XGBoost, SVM with two kernels, and a single dense layer with a 27-point hyperparameter grid), and a footnote records that recurrent classifiers were also tested and performed substantially worse. Reporting the failed recurrent experiments is good practice. The problem is the reporting rule for the successful ones: 'For each input combination we only report the results of the best performing classifier', so each of the six reported figures is the maximum over at least three classifier configurations and, for the masking rows, over a 27-point grid - all selected on the same leave-one-out folds used for reporting, with no held-out estimate of the selection cost.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Four conventional classifiers spanning distinct inductive biases - a decision tree, naive Bayes, random forest and SVM - each run on each of three feature-selection outputs for each of two datasets, giving 24 configurations all of which are reported. Running the full grid and publishing all of it is good practice and exposes the spread: accuracy ranges from 67.5% to 87.5%, an 20-point range on the same participants, and no single classifier dominates across configurations (naive Bayes wins on the toys dataset, random forest and SVM on the animation dataset). The authors read this correctly as indicating that decision trees overfit small data while noting the tree's compensating virtue - it 'can be visualized' and traversed by a clinician, which they illustrate with a worked example walking through the split on social interaction fixation time at 5,879 ms. Choosing conventional classifiers over deep models is appropriate at this sample size. No hyperparameters are stated for any of the four, so the comparison cannot be assessed for equal tuning effort.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: A support vector machine on ten interpretable percentages, fitted separately for each age cohort. Modelling is subordinate to the statistical analysis throughout: the paper's primary evidence is a set of ANCOVAs with covariates, variance-assumption testing, post-hoc correction and effect sizes, and classification is used to answer the supplementary question of whether the measures combine usefully and which paradigms contribute at which age. That ordering suits a study whose contribution is a developmental finding rather than a screening product. Fitting the cohorts separately rather than pooling with an age covariate is the decision that makes the age-specific feature rankings possible and is the right one given that the entire hypothesis concerns differential patterns. The classifier itself is under-specified - no kernel, no hyperparameters, no implementation named - which matters less here than it would in a study whose headline was the accuracy, but which prevents replication of the classification component.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: A gradient boosted decision tree, chosen for a regulated diagnostic aid over deep architectures, and locked before the trial. The model's provenance is described across seven years of prior development: initially trained 'using patient record data from thousands of children with diverse conditions, presentations, and comorbidities' with labels from standardised diagnostic tools, then 'iteratively improved, supplemented with ASD-expert input, and prospectively validated for 7 years prior to this study'. The abstention mechanism is the modelling contribution and is handled with unusual explicitness: thresholds were tuned by cross-validation on training and testing data to hold PPV above 65% and NPV above 85% - floors agreed with the FDA in advance - while minimising the abstention rate. The justification for abstaining rather than always deciding is stated in three parts: it 'provides a safeguard against known machine-learning failure modes, fosters clinician trust through model transparency, and helps flag cases where additional human expertise or data may be needed'. That framing - abstention as a transparency and triage mechanism rather than a performance trick - is the right one, and the paper earns it by quantifying the alternative.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Four conventional classifiers - decision tree, K-nearest neighbours, random forest and SVM - run ten times each on 16 preselected features. The classification is explicitly instrumental rather than the contribution: 'the final aim of these implementations is to test whether these acoustic features are typical in the speech production of Italian-speaking children with ASD. Good results in the performances of the classifiers would confirm this assumption.' That framing is coherent but it does not escape the underlying problem, since features selected for significance on the same 28 samples will by construction classify those samples well regardless of what produced the difference. No hyperparameters are reported for any method, so the comparison across classifiers cannot be assessed for equal tuning effort, and no baseline of any kind is provided - not a chance level, not a demographic comparator, not the unselected 88-feature set, which would have been the most informative control given the authors' own citation of Luz and colleagues showing that performance 'drop[s] consistently if applied to the same dataset without performing the feature selection'.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Six configurations spanning three families, all reported, which is a reasonable comparative design in itself. The shallow networks use 216 input neurons and 10 hidden layers, an unusually deep configuration for a fully connected network on 216 features and 547 samples, with no justification, no hidden-layer widths and no regularisation described. The CNN training is more conventionally specified with full hyperparameters for both networks. The SVM is unspecified as to kernel or parameters. What is missing throughout is any baseline: no chance level, no permutation test, no simple comparator such as image mean intensity or trace pixel count, and no repetition across splits - so a 6.2-point spread between the best and worst configuration is reported without any means of judging whether it exceeds split-to-split variation on 109 test images.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: An LSTM chosen to exploit temporal structure, with the architecture kept minimal - w cells each taking a 16-dimensional one-hot vector, a single fully connected output and a sigmoid - and a weighted binary cross-entropy loss to handle the class imbalance. Only window size and shift are varied, explored across 50 to 500 frames and 10 to 100 respectively on the validation set, with the three best carried to the held-out test set. No alternative architecture, no baseline classifier and no chance comparator is reported, which is the main gap: given the imbalance, a majority-class predictor and a permutation null are both necessary to interpret a macro-averaged recall of 0.598, and neither is provided. The restraint in model complexity is appropriate for 95 children, but the absence of any comparator makes the modest result harder to situate than the group-difference analysis, where permutation testing does exactly that job.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Four algorithms across two families. The three conventional models were run in a graphical cloud environment with 'minimal settings, making them lightweight and suited for low-power computers', which is a deployment argument rather than a methodological one. The convolutional network was arrived at by iterative search - 'we continued modifying configurations of the above model, such as various combinations of convolutional, pooling, and dense layers until we found an optimal model' - and its hyperparameters likewise tuned 'until the model produced the highest score', so both architecture and hyperparameters were selected on performance with no held-out confirmation of that selection. The authors do report an honest interim observation, that 'we found that all models were overfitting, which could be due to two factors: model complexity or the limited size of the dataset', and their response - augmenting the data - is a reasonable inference that turns out to have created a worse problem, which they then diagnose correctly.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Four classifier families selected on three reasoned criteria rather than by convention: no a priori assumption about linearity, so both linear and non-linear families are tested; the small sample, motivating families 'that offered considerable flexibility to prevent overfitting through regularization'; and interpretability, 'to gain insight into the specific aspects of gameplay that predict ASD'. The hyperparameter grids are tabulated in full and were deliberately restricted 'to include hyperparameters that would lead to more regularization and less overfitting' - so the search space itself was biased against complexity because of n = 49, which is a considered decision rather than a default. The spread across families is informative: tree-based methods reach AU-ROC 0.73-0.75 while linear methods reach 0.67-0.71, and linear SVM achieves the highest precision at 0.70 while tree methods achieve the highest recall, so the choice among them is a genuine operating-point decision. Model selection is stated as 'the simplest model resulting in the highest average of AU-ROC and Recall', a criterion declared before the comparison rather than fitted to it.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Two classifiers applied uniformly across all three feature methods, which makes the method comparison interpretable in that respect. The SVM is specified - radial basis function kernel with C and gamma selected by cross-validation, with the search surface plotted - and justified on small-sample grounds, that it 'still has good generalization ability under finite small samples'. The CNN is not specified at all: no layer count, filter sizes, depth, optimiser, learning rate, batch size or epoch count appears, only the general claim that convolution 'provides translation invariant convolution in time and space'. It underperforms the SVM under every one of the six conditions, by margins from 2.9 to 5.6 percentage points, which the authors attribute to insufficient training data. No baseline, chance level or permutation test is reported for any condition, which matters most for Method 2 where 59.71% needs to be judged against both chance and the 256-way selection that produced it.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: Two networks in sequence, each matched to its task. Diarization uses a fully connected network with two stacked softmax layers, the second added on cited grounds that it improves final classification, followed by Viterbi decoding to impose temporal coherence on the frame-level outputs - a sensible structure for a sequence-labelling problem. Severity estimation uses a convolutional network with a linear output for regression, trained with RMSprop and hyperparameters selected by random search under five-fold cross-validation, with the selected values reported separately for each segmentation condition. Reporting per-condition hyperparameters is a small but meaningful detail: it shows the comparison between segmentation methods was made with each given its own tuned configuration rather than one set imposed across all three. Neither architecture is described in enough depth to reimplement, with details deferred to a prior publication.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: None. No computational or machine-learning model is fitted at any point, and no automated measurement is performed. The analysis is non-parametric group comparison - Mann-Whitney, Kruskal-Wallis and chi-squared - which is the appropriate choice for ordinal ratings from five children per group and is used correctly. For a review of computation-based approaches this study occupies the position immediately upstream of the modelling work: it establishes that a robot-delivered paradigm elicits a measurable group difference on a defined construct, which is the prerequisite for any subsequent automation, and it does not attempt the automation itself.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Classical machine learning in two stages. Stage one is a support vector machine classifying individual gaze behaviour segments as ASD-like or TD-like, chosen because 'SVM has been often used in ML studies in the field of ASD' - a popularity rather than a suitability argument, with no comparison against any other classifier. Stage two is a threshold classifier: count the proportion of a child's segments labelled ASD-like and call the child autistic if it exceeds a cut-off tuned to maximise accuracy (46% at the optimal 7 s window). No deep learning, no ensemble, no probabilistic model. The two-stage design - weak per-segment classifier plus aggregation to a strong per-participant decision - is the same multiple-instance shape used by Kojovic et al. in this corpus, and it is a sound idea; the difference is that Kojovic partitioned children before generating segments and this study did not, which is precisely what separates a legitimate aggregation gain from an inflated one.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Classical machine learning throughout, with three algorithms compared: a linear-kernel SVM as the primary model, a random forest, and a multilayer perceptron trained with unspecified data augmentation. The SVM was retained because it outperformed the others on overall accuracy, and the linear kernel was chosen after testing three kernel types. No deep learning, no sequence model, no probabilistic or Bayesian approach; the whole session is collapsed to one fixed-length feature vector per child before any model sees it. The choice is defensible at n = 46 and the authors implicitly acknowledge the sample-size constraint by noting that 'the size of the training set is small compared to the size of the feature vector' as the motivation for aggressive feature reduction. The most interesting modelling observation in the paper is the discussion of the SVM/random forest trade-off: the random forest is 4.7 points worse on accuracy but better on both sensitivity and specificity, and the authors state plainly that a user may prefer it because it would miss fewer autistic children and mislabel fewer typically developing ones - an error-profile argument that most studies in this corpus never make.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: A variational autoencoder with an attached supervised predictor - the only VAE in this corpus and one of few genuinely generative models here. The encoder maps the 12 features to the parameters (mean and standard deviation) of a diagonal Gaussian latent distribution; a latent vector is sampled and passed both to a symmetric decoder that reconstructs the input and to a predictor MLP with a tanh intermediate layer and a softmax output over the two classes. The composite loss has three equally weighted terms: mean squared reconstruction error, the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the learned latent distribution and a zero-mean unit-variance diagonal Gaussian, and binary cross-entropy on the prediction. The architectural rationale is stated clearly and is the paper's conceptual contribution: the KL regularisation forces a well-behaved latent geometry, and the predictor loss forces the two classes into separable regions of it, because if the class-conditional latent distributions overlap too much the stochastic sampling makes the prediction loss stagnate. The result is a latent space in which classification and generative description coexist. At inference the predictor is then set aside in favour of two fitted bivariate Gaussians over the latent points, on the explicit grounds that density-based assignment is more conservative for inputs that land in unvisited regions - a deliberate outlier-aware design choice that is unusual and clinically sensible.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: A hybrid that is unusual in this corpus: four deep neural networks are used as perception front ends, but no model is trained on the behaviour and the decision itself is a hand-written rule. The deep components are YOLOv3 for person detection (retrained on the study's own images rather than using COCO weights, on accuracy grounds), HRNet for top-down 2-D pose estimation (selected for its high-resolution feature maintenance and repeated multi-scale fusion), OSNet re-identification for multi-object tracking (necessary because the scene contains the child, the clinician and a variable number of parents, so the child's skeleton must be identified and followed), OpenFace for facial landmarks and 3-D head Euler angles, and a commercial deep fully-convolutional ASR for name-call timestamps. Above these sits a three-branch threshold cascade with five hand-set constants. The architectural choice is defensible for the task - the clinical scoring rule is itself a deterministic decision tree over observable orienting behaviour, so encoding it directly rather than learning it from 109 examples is the right call at this sample size, and it makes every judgement auditable. The cost is that nothing adapts: the thresholds cannot accommodate a child whose habitual posture or motor control differs, the paper's own two error cases are both threshold-boundary failures, and there is no probability or confidence attached to any judgement, so no case can be flagged as uncertain and referred back to the clinician - which is precisely what an assistive scoring tool ought to do.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: A single shallow multilayer perceptron, trained by error backpropagation using the scaled conjugate gradient algorithm, with hyperbolic tangent activation in the hidden layer and sigmoid activation at the output, implemented in MATLAB R2020b. No alternative classifier was evaluated - no SVM, random forest, logistic regression or even a linear baseline - despite the introduction surveying several such methods, so there is no evidence that the neural network is better suited to 18 features and 240 rows than a simpler model would be. Nor is the network itself specified: the paper devotes a paragraph to explaining that the number of hidden layers and nodes is problem-dependent and then never states what was used, and the iteration count and learning coefficient are described as optimised by MSE without saying on which partition. For a dataset of 240 rows and 18 features, a shallow MLP is a defensible choice and overfitting is the expected risk; the reported train-to-test gaps of roughly 20 points in every configuration are consistent with that risk having materialised.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: A linear support vector machine at the default regularisation C = 1, over 6,272 engineered coordination features. The choice of a simple model is argued rather than defaulted: deep learning was rejected because 'the sample size is insufficient for reliably training deep learning models from scratch', and transfer learning was rejected because, to the authors' knowledge, no publicly available pre-trained model is directly applicable to the problem, so fine-tuning a classification head was also unavailable. Leaving C at its default further shrinks the search space, so the entire modelling procedure has exactly one tuned quantity - the cross-correlation window - and that is tuned inside a nested loop. The result is a pipeline with very few researcher degrees of freedom, which is the main reason its 80.5% is more credible than several higher figures elsewhere in this corpus. The intellectual weight of the paper sits in the representation rather than the classifier: the modelling contribution is the 3DMM-based identity-removed localised expression basis and the directional cross-correlation feature construction, with the SVM as a deliberately transparent read-out.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: A three-stage deep pipeline with an unsupervised front end, a weakly supervised middle and an unsupervised decision rule. Stage one is a deep autoencoder used purely as a nonlinear dimensionality reducer, trained layer-wise then fine-tuned globally with cross-entropy reconstruction loss on 10,000 MS COCO images - so the semantic encoder never sees participant data, which is a clean separation and removes one potential leakage path. Stage two is an LSTM over the per-fixation feature sequence for each stimulus, chosen for its capacity to model sequential dependence and to avoid the vanishing-gradient problems of plain recurrent networks, ending in a fully connected layer and a single-neuron regression head that scores the pattern. Stage three aggregates the 82 stimulus scores into a subject average and binarises it with Otsu's maximum between-class variance threshold. The weak supervision is explicit and correctly reasoned: the authors note that an autistic child's viewing will be atypical on only some stimuli but that labels for which specific stimuli are unavailable, so each child's diagnostic label is propagated to all 82 of their patterns and the aggregation step is relied upon to recover the subject-level decision from noisy per-stimulus targets. This is the appropriate formulation for the problem and is stated as such rather than adopted implicitly. Two baselines are reimplemented for comparison - a fixation-count histogram with SVM and stacked deep features of up to 10 fixations with SVM - and both underperform, which is the study's evidence that sequence structure, not merely deep features, carries the signal.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: Four models compared: a decision tree, XGBoost, k-nearest neighbours with k = 1, and BERT-base-multilingual-cased. The comparison is framed as a deliberate test - the three classical models were hyperparameter-tuned by grid search while BERT was left entirely at defaults, 'to see if the DL model just with the basic model gives more accurate results than ML models that have been optimised' - and BERT won by 13 accuracy points over the best classical model. Setting up an asymmetric comparison and reporting it transparently is a reasonable framing, but the comparison is not interpretable as stated, because the text representation given to the classical models is never described. BERT builds its own contextual representation from subword tokens; the decision tree, XGBoost and k-nearest neighbours must have been given something, and what that was is unstated. If it was a sparse bag-of-words vector, then the finding is about representation rather than model family, and the paper cannot tell the two apart. Two of the classical results also look near-degenerate rather than merely weak: k = 1 nearest neighbours over a high-dimensional text representation is close to a memorisation baseline, and the decision tree assigned nearly everything to the positive class. Neither observation is drawn out.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Deliberately simple, and the simplicity is appropriate to the claim. The primary analyses are conventional non-parametric statistics: Mann-Whitney U for between-group comparison, Wilcoxon signed-rank for within-group, with effect size r reported for every significant test, and ANCOVA to adjust for two prespecified confounds. The modelling contribution is not a classifier but the entropy estimator itself - a modification of multiscale entropy that handles partially missing time series by admitting only fully observed embedding vectors into the coefficient counts, and that normalises per participant so complexity can be compared across people. The authors flag the second point sharply, noting in a footnote that despite MSE's popularity in health research the across-subject comparison problem 'has never been addressed before, and often authors report lower MSE for data that is clearly more complex and vice-versa'. The classification component is a secondary demonstration using a decision tree with Gini splitting and leave-one-out cross-validation, plus logistic regression for odds ratios. No deep learning appears anywhere. Given 40 autistic participants and two features, this is the right choice, and the paper does not pretend otherwise - the classifier is presented as evidence of feasibility rather than as the result.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Deliberately small models with a classical aggregation layer, and the modesty is justified rather than incidental. The per-trial classifiers are a three-hidden-layer multilayer perceptron with five neurons per layer, taking three scalar gaze features, and a two-convolutional-layer CNN with 3 x 3 kernels and 8 and 16 channels plus one fully connected layer, taking a 34 x 34 greyscale heat map and the stimulus image. The authors describe a three-step strategy adopted explicitly because the dataset is small: downscale the images to 34 x 34 greyscale after centre-cropping, reduce the CNN to two layers plus one fully connected layer, and use leave-one-participant-out cross-validation to maximise training data. Above the per-trial classifier sits the paper's contribution, an aggregation over the 21 or 32 per-trial decisions by either hard voting or a random forest, the latter learning which stimuli should count. Training used Adam with cross-entropy loss, a 300-epoch cap and early stopping after 15 epochs without validation improvement, with the learning rate optimised inside the nested cross-validation. The authors also justify not using a support vector machine, on the grounds that the per-fold sample size of 630 or 651 trials is adequate relative to a cited prior study - an argument about sample adequacy rather than an unexamined preference for deep learning.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: A wide but shallow model comparison. The classical arm comprises radial-basis and polynomial-kernel SVMs, a probabilistic neural network, logistic regression, LogitBoost and bagging; the deep arm comprises stacked autoencoders with one, two and three encoder layers and deep belief networks with two and three layers. The framing is a straightforward representation-learning argument, stated in the discussion: 'feature manipulations and transformations that are being performed in inner layers of deep learning methods such as DBN and SAE are likely to better position such classifiers to stratify usage patterns to expected classes compared to standard classifiers such as SVM and logistic regression'. Two features of the comparison undercut it. Tuning effort was uneven, and the authors say so - the deep belief network was tuned specifically for the 20-key-press window and its weaker results elsewhere are attributed to that, which means the model ranking partly reflects how much attention each classifier received. And the comparison spans two different experiments with different validation schemes and, crucially, different label sets: the 47-61% figures come from the 180 self-reported cases while the 70% and 82% figures come from the pseudo-labelled corpus, so the apparent progression from classical to deep methods is confounded with the change in what was being predicted. The most consequential algorithmic choice is not a classifier at all but the k-means step that generated labels for roughly 5,192 users, which converts a supervised problem on 180 people into a largely self-supervised one on 5,372.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: A single custom architecture combining a convolutional neural network for spatial features, a long short-term memory network for temporal sequence modelling, and an attention mechanism over frames, applied end-to-end to raw video with no hand-crafted features, pose estimation or gaze tracking. The rationale for each component is given: the CNN for frame-level spatial content, the LSTM because it 'was developed to better process sequential data' and the video is time-dependent, and attention to make it possible 'to access and visualize the attention weights across each video sequence according to which frames or video time points contributed most to the model's decision-making' - so the attention mechanism is included at least partly for interpretability rather than purely for performance, which is a defensible and unusual justification. Three separate models are trained, one per joint attention task, with input dimensions matched to task duration (300 frames for the 10-second IJA clips, 150 for the 5-second RJA clips). No alternative architectures or baselines are compared, and no ablation of the CNN, LSTM or attention components is reported, so the contribution of each is unestablished. Grad-CAM, attention plots and agglomerative hierarchical clustering complete the analysis pipeline.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: Two contrasting approaches. The proposed pipeline uses ImageNet-pretrained InceptionV3 as a fixed feature extractor, taking the 2048-dimensional output of the last convolutional layer before global average pooling on the stated principle that layers close to the classifier head carry the most distinctive representations, and feeds these to either logistic regression or a two-hidden-layer MLP (200 and 100 neurons). The baseline is a custom five-level CNN trained from scratch (16, 32, 64 and 128 3x3 filters, ReLU, 2x2 max pooling at each level, flatten to 2048, dense 256, dense 128, sigmoid output) with Adam at learning rate 0.001, binary cross-entropy, batch size 64 and 15 epochs. The choice is appropriate to the data volume and the result vindicates it: with 382 training images, transfer learning outperforms training from scratch by 9 percentage points and, more importantly, produces a balanced rather than a majority-collapsed classifier. The paper describes InceptionV3 as 'fine-tuned' in one place while describing features as extracted from a fixed layer in another, an ambiguity about whether any weights were updated that is not resolved.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: Six classifier families compared by an AutoML tool - majority baseline, k-nearest neighbours, logistic regression, random forest, gradient boosting and support vector machine - with an RBF-kernel SVM retained on the basis of best accuracy and its C and gamma tuned by grid search with 5-fold cross-validation. The choice of simple, interpretable models is appropriate to 76 samples and 63 features and is consistent with the paper's stated priority of interpretability over raw performance. Two aspects of the comparison need stating. Selecting the best of six families on the same small evaluation set means the reported 94.1% is the maximum of a search, and the spread across families is wide (64.7% to 94.1%), so the choice is doing real work. And SHAP serves a dual role - as the feature-elimination criterion reducing 77 features to 63, and as the post-hoc attribution method interpreting the final model - which is efficient but means the interpretation is being read off a feature set that SHAP itself selected on the full data.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: A dense neural network and a convolutional neural network, compared throughout at two dropout rates (0.2, 0.5) and two epoch counts (50, 100), with both reported and the better bolded in each table. No classical baseline, no majority classifier, and no architecture search beyond dropout and epochs; the networks are shown only as a schematic figure. The modelling is deliberately simple and the paper's intellectual investment sits in the input representation rather than the classifier, which is a reasonable division for a study whose claimed contributions are representational. The consistent pattern across every table is diagnostic of the setup rather than of the models: training accuracy reaches 100% or 99.9% almost everywhere while test accuracy sits between 67% and 81%, so both architectures memorise the training images completely at every setting tried, and dropout at either level does not prevent it.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: A network the paper calls T-CNN-ASD, described as a convolutional deep neural network but parameterised and reported entirely in terms of hidden-layer neuron counts, from a single layer of 50-600 neurons up to two layers of 500 and 250. The characterisation is internally confused: kernel size, stride and pooling are swept as hyperparameters, which implies convolution, yet the preprocessing explicitly flattens the 100 x 100 image 'from 3D to 1D' before the model, which removes the two-dimensional adjacency structure convolution operates on, and no layer diagram or channel specification is given. The comparison set is four classical classifiers - k-nearest neighbours, decision tree, random forest and multilayer perceptron - of which the multilayer perceptron reaches 94.69%, within one point of the proposed model, suggesting that whatever is driving performance is available to a plain feed-forward network on flattened pixels. The most informative modelling result is the optimiser sweep: Adam gives 95.59% and Nadam 95.07%, but SGD and Adadelta collapse to 56-62% across every architecture tried. A 35-point dependence on optimiser choice, on a fixed dataset with a fixed architecture family, indicates a result that is a property of the optimisation trajectory as much as of the data.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Gradient boosted decision trees as the primary model, with the mechanism explained in the text - successive trees fitted to the errors of their predecessors, combined stage-wise rather than in parallel - and three comparators: logistic regression, random forest and naive Bayes. Risk stratification used the Youden threshold, defined as the cutoff optimising the balance of sensitivity and specificity. The modelling is deliberately conventional and the paper makes no architectural claim; the contribution is the data and the design. The comparison across methods is the most useful modelling result in the study and cuts against the assumption running through this corpus: logistic regression matched gradient boosting exactly at AUC 0.86 while achieving marginally higher sensitivity (0.77 versus 0.75), with random forest at 0.84 and naive Bayes at 0.83, so the entire spread across four methods is 0.03 AUC. On a genuine population dataset with 59 clinically chosen features, the choice of algorithm is close to irrelevant - which suggests that the very large algorithm-driven performance differences reported elsewhere in this review are more likely properties of small samples and leaky validation than of modelling power.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: Three ImageNet-pretrained networks - MobileNet, Xception and InceptionV3 - used as fixed feature extractors with two dense layers appended (1,024 neurons with ReLU and L2 regularisation at 0.015, dropout 0.4, softmax output), trained with RMSprop under early stopping on validation loss with patience ten. Separately, five YOLOv8 classification variants plus a proposed 11.2-million-parameter model for facial expression recognition. The architectural choices are conventional and appropriate to a small image dataset; the paper notes candidly that batch normalisation and dropout 'didn't notably enhance the models' performance' and that early stopping proved more effective. That candour is worth noting because it is the only self-critical observation in the paper. The reported 100% training accuracy alongside 95% validation accuracy is left without comment.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: Four components, each chosen for a stated reason. GAMI-Net models tabular clinical data through feature-wise subnetworks with pairwise interaction layers and sparse regularisation, giving an interpretable additive decomposition rather than a black-box embedding - the right choice for clinical variables and a deliberate answer to the interpretability problem that dominates this branch. A CNN captures volumetric structure and a GNN models relationships between Harvard-Oxford regions. An autoencoder fuses the two embeddings. A hypernetwork generates per-subject MLP weights, which is an unusual and interesting device for accommodating heterogeneity. Comparison against TabNet, CNN, LSTM and Bi-LSTM baselines and a component ablation are both reported. The methodology is well constructed throughout; the difficulty lies entirely upstream in what the tabular stream contains.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Four conventional classifiers - support vector machine, linear discriminant analysis, decision tree and random forest - chosen on the stated grounds that they have performed well in prior autism classification work, with forward feature selection and an early-stopping rule capping the model at fifteen features 'to avoid the potential overfitting problem caused by too many features'. The best result in the original-feature condition came from an unspecified classifier with five features, and in the derived-feature condition from a decision tree with three. The modelling is deliberately simple and appropriate to 41 participants, and the explicit feature cap shows awareness of the dimensionality problem. The intellectual content sits in the signal processing rather than the classifier: motion energy analysis to extract movement without markers or tracking, cross wavelet analysis to decompose coordination by frequency, and the surrogate-pair construction to establish a chance level. That the best model uses a decision tree with three features is worth noting - the discriminative structure is simple enough that a small tree captures it, which is consistent with the features having been pre-selected for group difference.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Four configurations spanning two model families, with the trade-off between them argued rather than resolved by accuracy. Logistic regression on normalised tag frequencies serves as the interpretable model, retained explicitly because 'in the medical context, interpretability is crucial because we are dealing with human lives' and because it 'allowed us to identify tags that impacted the outputs and quantify these effects'. Bi-LSTM models serve as the performance-oriented alternative, in three variants: tags only, text only, and tags plus text concatenated at each time step. A fifth model, a separate Bi-LSTM sequence labeller, performs automatic annotation and is retrained within each cross-validation fold. Two aspects of the modelling deserve particular credit. Hyperparameters were adopted from standard values and deliberately not searched, on the stated basis that preliminary work showed the search had little impact - which removes a large source of optimism on a 135-participant dataset. And the authors decline to declare a winner: after observing that the linear model was less precise, they write that 'it is not possible to make an unconditional judgment of which model is better', because interpretability and accuracy are not commensurable in a clinical setting. No other study in this corpus refuses to rank its models by accuracy.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Three ImageNet-pretrained backbones used as fixed feature extractors with fully connected layers excluded, and five classical classifiers - random forest, k-nearest neighbours, decision tree, SVM and logistic regression - applied to each of four feature conditions, giving twenty reported model-condition combinations of which eighteen are tabulated. The design is a systematic grid rather than a single proposed model, which is reasonable for a comparison study. No hyperparameters are reported for any classifier, and no rationale is given for the choice of backbones or descriptors beyond their being commonly used.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: A hybrid of Weighted Quantum Particle Swarm Optimisation with a Fast Mask Recurrent Convolutional Neural Network. The optimiser's distinguishing feature is that it encodes the swarm in quaternion rather than Euclidean space, and the quaternion algebra is set out explicitly through Hamilton's relations, on the stated rationale that this concentrates the search on more productive regions. Comparison against CNN, linear SVM and k-nearest-neighbour baselines with significance tests is more than many papers in this branch offer. What is not reported is the optimiser's own configuration - population size, iteration count, inertia and weighting parameters - or the network's hyperparameters, so the mechanism credited with the improvement cannot be reproduced.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: Two artificial neural networks trained on sequential data, differing only in input dimensionality - two features (rotated x and y coordinates) versus four (adding velocity and acceleration). No architecture details, layer counts, activation functions, optimiser or training hyperparameters are given in the retrieved text, which is the study's main reporting gap and is conspicuous against the exceptional specification of the task, the preprocessing and the simulation procedure. No alternative model families are compared and no baseline classifier is reported. The modelling is deliberately minimal because the study's question is representational rather than architectural: whether raw trajectories suffice. Given 20 children, keeping the model simple is the right choice, but the absence of any specification means the comparison between the two models cannot be checked for confounds such as differing capacity or training duration.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: A metaheuristic contribution presented as a detection model. DF-ABHBO hybridises artificial bee colony with the honey badger algorithm, motivated by the observation that the former suffers from local optima and slows under sequential processing while the latter offers dynamic and global search, and switching between them according to an adaptive density factor thresholded at 0.5. This tunes the hidden neuron count and weights of a deep neural network, and the weights and epoch count of a recurrent network, which together form HWODNRN. The comparison against PSO, WOA, ABC and HBO variants of the same architecture is the appropriate ablation for an optimisation contribution and shows differences under one percentage point, while the comparison against decision tree, ANN, RNN and ensemble learning shows ten-point differences - so the architecture rather than the optimiser accounts for most of the reported advantage, a reading the paper does not draw.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: One-dimensional convolutional networks fitted separately per age band, with a baseline configuration and a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator-optimised version. The methodological argument for the optimiser is the paper's best contribution and is correctly reasoned: prior work on these datasets used predefined hyperparameters or exhaustive grid search, and an adaptive Bayesian method that concentrates sampling in promising regions is both cheaper and more likely to find good configurations. Fitting a separate model per age band is also appropriate, since Q-CHAT-10 and AQ-10 are distinct age-calibrated instruments. The difficulty is that neither choice can be evaluated on this task: when the label is a deterministic function of the features, an optimiser that reaches 100% and a baseline that does not are distinguishable only in how efficiently they discover a summation rule, which is not what the comparison is presented as measuring.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: A linear-kernel support vector machine, with the cost parameter reported (0.01 for the two best models) and between three and five variables selected from sixteen per configuration. The choice of a linear SVM on interpretable biomechanical features is well matched to 126 participants with 19 positives, and the reported model equations - high autistic trait group as a function of named variables - make each fitted model fully transparent. Only one algorithm family was tried, which the authors identify as a limitation and propose remedying by comparison against random forests or deep learning. The more consequential modelling detail is that feature selection and hyperparameter optimisation were performed jointly in a single procedure described in one sentence, with the stated purpose of improving 'performance and generalization of all SVM classification models' - so the search is doing substantial work, reducing sixteen candidates to three to five while also fixing the regularisation, and its relationship to the cross-validation loop is not specified.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: Deep convolutional networks with channel attention and multiscale feature fusion, in four configurations - SE-CNN and SE-MSF-CNN, each with and without white shark optimisation. White shark optimisation is a swarm metaheuristic that adjusts learning rate, layer widths, batch size, depth and kernel size against a fitness combining accuracy, F1 and loss. The reported configuration is ten agents over two iterations, roughly twenty fitness evaluations, which is a very shallow search for a six-dimensional space - and the tabulated dimension of 3 does not match the six ranges given. The evaluation partition for the fitness function is not stated, which matters: if fitness was computed on the test partition, the reported test performance is a selection maximum rather than a held-out estimate. Comparison across configurations is supported by McNemar's test and paired t-tests with p below 0.01, more statistical care than is usual in this branch, applied to a comparison whose foundation - the labels - is the unexamined part.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: Four architectures compared on a common feature set: a convolutional network, a three-layer dense network (128 ReLU, 64 ReLU, single sigmoid, with the layer equations written out explicitly), an LSTM, and a custom design. Presenting four architectures with their formulations, and reporting the weakest alongside the strongest, is more even-handed than much of this corpus. The comparison's informativeness is limited by the spread being small - 89.02% to 94.02%, five points across four quite different architectures - which on a 17-participant sample is well within the range that resampling variation alone would produce, and by no hyperparameter or training detail being reported. The pattern nonetheless matches the one found in the skeleton-movement study charted elsewhere in this review, where six architectures spanned two percentage points on one dataset: in this literature the data determine the result and the architecture rarely does.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: Univariate logistic regression for candidate screening followed by stepwise logistic regression for model construction, with the result presented as a nomogram. No machine learning algorithm is used and none is needed - with 246 children, 123 events and 81 candidate predictors, a regularised or stepwise regression is the statistically appropriate choice, and the transparency it buys is substantial: five interpretable coefficients with odds ratios and confidence intervals, displayed in a form a clinician can read off a chart. The model is accompanied by a Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test (chi-square 15.329, p = 0.053), a bootstrap procedure and a calibration curve. This is prediction-model methodology as the clinical literature practises it, and it is markedly better matched to the data than the deep architectures applied to smaller samples elsewhere in this corpus. The methodological gap is not the algorithm but the evaluation: stepwise selection from 81 candidates, on the sample that then supplies the performance estimate, without an optimism-corrected figure.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: Logistic regression throughout, at three levels: domain scores from each published algorithm as predictors of clinical diagnosis; per-item regressions on dichotomised non-zero indicators to identify predictive items; and a combined six-item model. A further logistic regression within the schizophrenia group predicted ADOS-2 cut-off positivity from the clinical variables that differed between cut-off-positive and cut-off-negative subgroups, returning the PANSS negative scale alone. ROC curves were compared by DeLong's test. With 90 participants and a differential-diagnosis question, regression is the correct tool and no machine learning is attempted or needed - the value of the analysis lies in what the coefficients say, not in maximising a discrimination statistic. The one modelling weakness is the size of the search: six items were chosen from 32 candidates on 90 participants by seeking 'the combination of assessment items with the highest diagnostic predictive accuracy', which is an unregularised selection over a large space, and the holdout result confirms the cost.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Two transfer-learning approaches compared head to head. Discriminative fine-tuning pre-trains on De-Enigma child vocalisations and fine-tunes on CPSD - the first application of this technique to autism recognition from speech, according to the authors. Wav2Vec 2.0 fine-tuning uses self-supervised representations pre-trained on 960 hours of unlabelled speech, with the quantisation step removed so that context representations derive solely from the input signal, feeding a BLSTM classifier. Both are appropriate to the data-scarcity problem the study sets out to address, and the comparison is fairly constructed - identical folds for both models and both tasks, a separate development partition, and evaluation on the same test sets. The finding that the smaller, domain-matched pre-training corpus outperforms the much larger unrelated one is the substantive modelling result. Minority-class upsampling was applied in training only, with development and test distributions left intact - a deliberate choice, correctly explained, and one that this review has found in strikingly few papers, since rebalancing the evaluation set is a common and usually silent source of inflation.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: A sensible staged progression rather than a single architecture. TF-IDF features were first passed through four classical algorithms - support vector machines, naive Bayes, logistic regression and XGBoost - with 5-fold cross-validation on accuracy used to select the best; word2vec representations were then trained with the selected algorithm and evaluated on a fuller metric set; and an attention-based bidirectional LSTM over a self-trained embedding layer was used for the user-level task, with padding and an unknown token to handle variable tweet lengths. The final tweet-level result comes from word2vec with logistic regression, and the profile-level result from the BiLSTM. The modelling is proportionate: a corpus of 6.5 million tweets can support a deep sequence model, and the authors escalate to one only for the aggregated user-document task where sequence structure and attention have a plausible role.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: Two architectures matched to their data. For video, an ImageNet-pretrained VGG16 with its dense layers removed extracts per-frame features from 5-second segments, feeding a 512-unit LSTM, then 512 fully connected ReLU units and a softmax; segment predictions are filtered at 90% confidence and averaged across the session, with the child classified autistic if the mean exceeds 0.5. For audio, five Librosa feature families averaged along the time axis into a one-dimensional vector feed two 1D convolutional layers, max pooling, a third convolutional layer, dropout 0.5, flattening, 512 dense units and a softmax, trained with categorical cross-entropy and Adam at batch size 512 for 30 epochs. Both are conventional and appropriately sized for 160 children; the authors report that larger batch sizes and epoch counts increased validation loss, which indicates that capacity was actively constrained rather than maximised. Fusion is by simple rules rather than a learned combiner - which is both why it underperforms and why the authors identify better fusion as the obvious next step.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: Three architectures compared across four datasets and two task types, which is a broader and more systematic comparison than most of this branch attempts.
