A Perceiver transformer was chosen for autism classification on the grounds of image-classification performance and cross-instance weight sharing; an ImageNet-pretrained Inception v3 emerged as the best affect regressor; a CNN-WGAN was included for its discriminator's sensitivity to image authenticity. The authors report negative tuning results honestly - varying the Perceiver's latent dimension, head count and learning rate produced no improvement over the original paper's configuration - and they explain the Perceiver's poor regression performance mechanistically, attributing it to 'the absence of temporal information'. Comparison against published methods is included for every experiment, and the study's own models lose in several of them, which is reported without softening.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: A three-stage pipeline, competently constructed at each stage. Viola-Jones face detection, then denoising by a non-decimated wavelet transform combined with a DnCNN, then the DN-FME network - eleven convolutional layers and three dense layers, 5x5 and 3x3 kernels, batch normalisation in blocks conv3 to conv5, 14 million parameters, 160x160 input - and finally Random Forest, SVM and KNN for three-class severity. Model sizing is reasoned rather than assumed: the authors explain that a smaller input resolution and limited data made a dropout of 0.5 counterproductive because it 'resulted in dropping useful information necessary for learning features', and they demonstrate the point with a monotonic table of validation accuracy across seven dropout values. Choosing classical classifiers for the final stage is also appropriate to 30 children. The gap is at that final stage: no hyperparameters are reported for any of the three classifiers, and no tuning procedure is described - so the stage carrying the paper's headline result is the least documented.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Three ImageNet-pretrained architectures - ResNet50, Inception-V3 and VGG-19 - fine-tuned with categorical cross-entropy and SGD for up to 25 epochs. Transfer learning from ImageNet is a reasonable default for a 2,940-image corpus, and comparing three families is more informative than reporting one. Two problems attach. The training curves show Inception-V3 reaching 0.9992 training accuracy against 0.9779 validation, and VGG-19 exceeding 0.9854 in training before 'a significant decline in accuracy from epochs 24-25', both of which are signs of fitting to the training set that the paper reports without interpreting. And the introduction's statement that 'VGG16' was among the architectures compared, and that VGG19 achieved the best 98%, contradicts both the abstract and the results tables - an inconsistency about the study's own central claim.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: A systematic seven-model comparison spanning logistic regression, Gaussian naive Bayes, random forests, k-nearest neighbours, support vector machines, a multilayer perceptron and a small convolutional network. Comparing classical against neural models on the same features is the paper's stated purpose and is executed evenly - same features, same splits, same metrics. The scale is appropriate for 64 children and twelve features, and the classical models are the ones such data can support. The conclusion drawn from the comparison, however, exceeds it: a 5-to-10-point advantage for neural models on 64 children, with test folds of sixteen and no confidence intervals, is not a stable basis for the recommendation to use deep learning clinically, and the one-to-two-point margin between the multilayer perceptron and the convolutional network is certainly not.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: A dual-stream architecture derived from a prior design, with two deliberate substitutions tested: ConvNeXt-Base replacing the original ViT-B in the image stream to assess whether CNN backbones capture gesture features effectively, and a Stack Transformer trialled against MSG3D in the sequence stream. Six image backbones were compared in total - ViT-B, ConvNeXt-Base, Swin-V2-B, ShuffleNetV2-X2, ResNet-152 and MaxViT-T - spanning transformer, convolutional and hybrid families. The comparison is even-handed and the reference implementation is reported alongside the alternatives rather than only the winner. Its most valuable outcome is a negative one: across six architectures the accuracy spread is 2.2 points on one dataset and 1.3 on the other, against a 25-point gap between the datasets, so architectural choice is nearly irrelevant to performance here. For a literature in which most papers are organised around a new architecture, that is a finding worth propagating.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: A recurrent convolutional network trained from scratch, combining three convolutional layers (kernel size 3, 32 output channels) for spatial feature extraction from spectrograms with LSTM layers for temporal structure - a standard and well-motivated architecture for audio, and the paper justifies the hybrid by reference to its success in video and speech recognition. Regularisation is taken seriously: dropout at 0.2 in each LSTM layer, and frequency masking and time masking augmentation applied specifically to the training split, which is the correct restriction. Optimisation used Adam with a cyclic learning rate between 1e-6 and 1e-5 and batch size 16. All of this is competently specified. The problem is not the model but the selection rule: training ran for 2,000 epochs and 'the model exhibiting superior validation accuracy being designated as the final trained classifier', so the reported figure is the maximum of 2,000 validation-accuracy draws, reported from the partition on which the maximum was taken.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: A Random Forest with hyperparameters tuned by Bayesian optimisation, evaluated by 5-fold cross-validation. Ensemble trees are a sensible default for a small mixed-type tabular dataset, cross-validation is appropriate at 704 rows, and Bayesian optimisation is a reasonable alternative to grid search. The methodology is proportionate to the data; the difficulty is entirely in what the data contain.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: A hybrid CNN+LSTM: convolutional layers for spatial feature extraction from the per-frame landmark vector, then an LSTM(64, return sequences) and an LSTM(32) for temporal dependency, then dense(16, ReLU) and dense(1, sigmoid), trained with binary cross-entropy and Adam. The architecture is standard, appropriately sized for 100 participants, and compared against configurations using either component alone, with the hybrid winning at p < 0.05 by paired t-tests across folds. Regularisation is unusually well specified - early stopping at patience 10 on validation loss, dropout 0.5, L2 at 0.001 and per-epoch batch shuffling - and each control is given with its parameter rather than merely named. The gap is that no hyperparameter search is described and the layer sizes are stated without justification, so it is unclear whether the configuration was tuned on the same folds that supply the reported figures.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: DeepFace supplies 100,352 features per image, which a multilayer perceptron then classifies, with several other machine learning models compared and the perceptron reported as best on testing accuracy. Ten-fold cross-validation was applied within the training portion, which is the correct arrangement when a separate test partition exists. Two modelling concerns. The feature count exceeds the image count by a factor of about 34, with no dimensionality reduction or feature selection described, which is an extreme ratio for a shallow classifier and is not commented on. And DeepFace's principal representation is a face-recognition embedding optimised to encode individual identity - so the features are, by design, maximally informative about which person a face belongs to, which is exactly the information an image-level split makes exploitable when multiple images of the same child are present.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Five ImageNet-pretrained networks used as frozen feature extractors with logistic regression as the binary classifier - a deliberate capacity restriction and the study's most defensible modelling decision. A linear classifier on frozen embeddings estimates only as many parameters as there are embedding dimensions, against the millions fitted by the end-to-end networks used on this same corpus elsewhere in the review, so it has far less scope to memorise individual images. Comparing five extractors also gives the architectural breadth that single-model papers lack. The corresponding limitation is that frozen ImageNet embeddings encode general visual appearance rather than anything face-specific or autism-specific, so the representation carries every source-dependent property of the photograph.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: A hybrid ResNet50V2 plus InceptionV3 for autism classification, and an enhanced MobileNet - MobileNet layers followed by global average pooling and fully connected layers - for six-way emotion recognition, each compared against baseline architectures including VGG16 with Random Forest. Choosing MobileNet for the emotion task is sensible given CPU-only training, and the baseline comparisons with confusion matrices give the emotion result more support than the autism result receives. The hybrid's motivation is argued rather than asserted, which is more than most of this branch offers.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: Five ensemble pairings of pretrained convolutional networks, combined at the decision level by averaging or voting. The selection criterion is explicitly computational: lightweight architectures using depthwise separable convolutions and compound scaling, chosen for fast inference on constrained hardware. That is an appropriate design goal for a low-resource deployment context and is argued rather than assumed. Comparing five pairings with learning curves for each is more architectural breadth than most single-model papers in this branch offer, and the authors' reading of those curves for stability - identifying which pairings learn smoothly and which fluctuate - is a legitimate diagnostic use rather than a decorative one.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Supervised deep learning for binary classification: a standalone LSTM (64 units, dropout, sigmoid) and a hybrid 1-D CNN plus LSTM. The recurrent framing is nominal - the input tensor has exactly one timestep, so the LSTM has no sequence to traverse and reduces to a gated dense transformation of a 16-dimensional vector. The paper says this explicitly (even though the input consisted of only a single timestep) without recognising that it removes the entire justification for the architecture.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Automated machine learning by genetic programming: TPOT searched pipelines over classical estimators and returned an ensemble of BernoulliNB and RandomForestClassifier. Six manually specified baselines (SVM, KNN, naive Bayes, logistic regression, decision tree, random forest) were fitted for comparison. No deep learning.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: A four-stage hybrid: CNN with Active Shape Appearance Model for landmark localisation; a Euclidean graph over the landmarks encoded by graph encoder convolutional networks; Randomized Trees for feature importance; XGBoost for the final binary decision. Each stage is motivated by a stated deficiency of prior work, in the now-standard architecture-stacking rhetoric of this literature, but no ablation isolates any stage's contribution.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Supervised sequence classification. Primary model is a hybrid CNN-RNN combining convolutional feature extraction with GRU and LSTM recurrence; comparators are GRU, a two-layer LSTM, BiLSTM, random forest and XGBoost. LSTM layers use 128 hidden units into a fully connected softmax; batch size 64, cross-entropy loss, learning rate 0.0001. The classification section describes the output as softmax regression for class probability prediction in binary classification although the task is four-class throughout.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: A four-stage pipeline: Gabor filtering, MobileNetV2 feature extraction, a heterogeneous ensemble of LSTM, deep belief network and hybrid-kernel extreme learning machine, and metaheuristic hyperparameter selection by the Crested Porcupine Optimizer. This is the corpus's most elaborate architecture stack applied to its simplest and least trustworthy data. Only one component's contribution is actually tested (Gabor filtering); the others are argued for in the conditional - removing MobileNetV2 may result in diminished performance, evaluating individual classifiers against the ensemble might reveal improvements - without those experiments being run.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Supervised deep learning in a simulated federated architecture: two local DNNs per client (a shallow dense network for binary classification, and a five-hidden-layer network described as multi-class), three clients, three communication rounds, FedAvg aggregation into a global model. XGBoost with SHAP serves as a separate feature-ranking model. No classical baseline is fitted for comparison.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: A convolutional neural network with a sigmoid output, trained end to end. The architecture is never described. The introduction promises the design of custom layers to optimise detection of ASD-specific visual characteristics, and no custom layer, or indeed any layer, is ever specified. Prior architectures (VGG-19, ShuffleNet, MobileNet, ResNet-18/34/50, AlexNet, VGG16) are discussed only as literature figures.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Six classical supervised learners - LightGBM, Extra Trees, Decision Tree, KNN, RBF-kernel SVM and a four-layer MLP - each evaluated with the full feature set and with a chi-square-selected subset, all tuned by Bayesian hyperparameter optimisation with cross-validation inside the training data. No deep learning on raw signals; no ensemble of the six.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Seven classical classifiers - random forest, decision tree, logistic regression, KNN, SVM, gradient boosting, XGBoost - plus an RF-XG voting ensemble presented as the novel contribution. Three feature-selection techniques (Bi-Directional Elimination, Boruta, ML-based selection) are compared. No hyperparameter is reported for any model.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Four supervised learners: logistic regression, k-nearest neighbours, a feed-forward artificial neural network, and a soft LR-KNN ensemble presented as the contribution. No tree-based or boosted classifier is used for prediction, though RF and Extra Trees are used for feature ranking.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: Fifty supervised regression algorithms compared under a common protocol - support vector regression, neural networks, linear and regularised linear regressors, decision trees, random forests, boosting ensembles, k-nearest neighbours and Gaussian processes among others. Different algorithms won for different outcomes (SGD for Aloofness, SVR for Pragmatics, Ridge for Rigidity, KNN for Depression, boosted trees for Anxiety), and the winners are simple regularised or instance-based methods rather than deep networks. This is regression to continuous scores rather than the binary classification that dominates the corpus, which removes the threshold and prevalence problems that make most of the charted accuracy figures uninterpretable.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: A three-stage architecture: a ConvBlock in which a pre-trained ResNet produces a 512-dimensional feature vector that is projected by a 1x1 convolution to three channels and interpolated back to 224x224; a TransformerBlock applying a pre-trained ViT-base with a residual ReAttention mechanism; and global average pooling into a linear classifier. The intermediate step is unusual and unexplained - ResNet features are collapsed to a three-channel image-shaped tensor purely so that a pre-trained ViT's input interface can consume them, which discards most of the convolutional representation before the transformer sees it. No ablation tests whether the ConvBlock, the ReAttention module or the ABAL contributes anything.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: A two-stage pipeline: DeepDeblur, a convolution/deconvolution network learning a blurred-to-sharp mapping, followed by DOCNN, a CNN in which one layer set denoises and the next classifies, with a Fire Hawk Optimizer tuning parameters. Three separable components are each claimed as a contribution and none is ablated, so the reader cannot tell whether the deblurring stage, the denoising branch or the metaheuristic contributes anything to the classification result.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Eight classical classifiers compared under a common protocol - random forest, SVM, gradient boosting machine, XGBoost, C5.0, a neural network, k-nearest neighbours and logistic regression - with grid-search tuning in caret and formal statistical comparison by Wilcoxon signed-rank and Friedman tests. No deep learning on raw signals; the comparison is fair in form and the statistical apparatus is more rigorous than anything else in the charted corpus.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Interpretable classical classifiers selected for explainability rather than capacity, with naive Bayes and logistic model trees performing best. No deep learning. The algorithm choice follows from the stated aim - to identify which eye-tracking variables discriminate, in a form clinicians can inspect - rather than from a search for maximum accuracy, and this is one of the few studies in the corpus where the modelling choice is subordinated to the scientific question.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: Four transfer-learning classifiers: MobileNet, VGG19, DenseNet169 and a VGG19+MobileNet hybrid, each with ImageNet weights, the top layers removed, a pooling layer, dense layers with ReLU and dropout, and a two-unit softmax output.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: MEResNeXt, combining the Moments Embedding Network with ResNeXt. Both are convolutional architectures designed for images: MoNet's contribution is a bilinear second-order moment embedding with a sub-matrix square-root layer developed for fine-grained visual recognition, and ResNeXt's is the aggregated residual transformation with cardinality developed for ImageNet classification. Applying them to a short tabular vector of binary questionnaire responses is never justified, and neither the spatial structure that motivates convolution nor the fine-grained texture statistics that motivate moment embedding exists in the data.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Three standard classifiers - KNN, random forest and linear-kernel SVM - selected on the explicit ground that these three have been used together in comparably sized studies of parkinsonian movement. No deep learning and no novel architecture; results are reported for all three separately and as a mean, so no single algorithm's best run stands in for the finding.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: A bidirectional LSTM as a high-capacity representation learner over static questionnaire attributes, trained with a chaotic optimiser that applies controlled chaotic perturbations to diversify gradient updates, described as an alternative to deterministic optimisers such as Adam or RMSProp. Baselines fitted by the authors under identical preprocessing and validation: SVM, random forest, logistic regression, MLP and unidirectional LSTM. The ablation reports a clean monotone progression from 0.932 to 0.987.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: MUXAI-ASDBD, described as a partitioning-based explainable CNN framework with layer-wise explainability and a machine-unlearning mechanism at the summation layer, using ResNet-50 or InceptionV3 as per-partition feature extractors. Baselines named are CNN, GNN, ACNN, SVM, LSTM and a proposed FCNN-LSTM - a list that does not match the framework the paper is proposing, since the title framework is a partitioned CNN and the proposed baseline is a fully connected LSTM.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: A custom CNN-GRU hybrid, with GRU selected over LSTM on the stated grounds of simpler gating, fewer parameters, greater training stability and less overfitting under repeated k-fold retraining. Four comparators - VGG16, MobileNet, EfficientNet-B7 and 3D-CNN+LSTM - were fitted by the authors on the same data under identical hyperparameters, which makes this one of the few architecture comparisons in the corpus that is actually controlled.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Six classical interpretable classifiers - SVM (linear kernel only, chosen deliberately to preserve interpretability), logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost and a shallow MLP among them - selected explicitly because the study prioritises explainability over capacity. SVM was most consistent across conditions; logistic regression gave the single best result. No deep sequence model is used, and the authors give the reason: the corpus is small and the features are lightweight.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: Five base learners (random forest, XGBoost, gradient boosting, SVM, logistic regression), soft-voting and stacking ensembles with a logistic-regression meta-learner, and two neural networks - a regularised MLP with L2, batch normalisation and dropout, and a deeper variant with early stopping and adaptive learning-rate scheduling. Predictions are combined by ensemble weighting proportional to validation performance.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Random forest, selected with reasons given: capacity to detect sparse signals in high-dimensional data, provision of feature-importance rankings usable for battery optimisation, and the property of being difference-focused rather than deficit-focused. No deep learning and no architecture competition - the modelling is subordinated to the scientific question.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: A three-strategy ensemble - bagging, boosting and stacking - over five base learners (decision tree, random forest, KNN k=3, AdaBoost, gradient boosting) with a stacking meta-learner. The base-learner set is chosen by an explicit diversity-aware strategy rather than assembled arbitrarily, and every constituent's performance is reported separately so the ensemble's increment is visible: the best base learner reaches 0.9267 accuracy and the stack 0.9600, a gain of about 3.3 points.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: YOLOv8n and YOLOv9c, single-stage object detectors, applied to a whole-image binary classification problem. The architectural choice is consequential and unexamined: an object detector localises instances within a scene and scores them against a Background class, so the confusion matrices contain Autistic, Non-Autistic and Background categories, and the reported mAP is a localisation-plus-classification measure rather than a diagnostic accuracy. Nothing in the task requires detection - each image contains one face - so the apparatus adds a spatial estimation problem and a third class to a two-class question.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: A four-stage pipeline: Gaussian Gabor filtering, concatenated features from three pretrained CNNs, a wavelet neural network classifier, and chimp-optimisation parameter tuning, with Grad-CAM++ appended for visualisation. Each stage is named as a contribution and none is ablated, so the reader cannot tell whether the Gabor stage, the three-way fusion, the wavelet classifier or the metaheuristic contributes anything to the reported figure.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Random forest, chosen for performance, flexibility and compatibility with SHAP-based interpretation. No architecture competition, no metaheuristic and no deep learning - the modelling is subordinated to the interpretability aim.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Three classifiers - logistic regression, random forest at maximum depth 2, and TabNet - with logistic regression selected for the interpretability analysis on the basis of its performance. The depth-2 random forest is an appropriate constraint for 38-48 cases and is reported rather than left implicit.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: Seven algorithms under a single protocol - random forest, MLP, deep MLP, KNN, logistic regression, SVM and naive Bayes - with the full grid search published. The comparison is genuinely controlled and the spread it produces (96% down to 82% and lower) is informative in itself.

questions.question_text: Which input representations are used?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: Handcrafted acoustic-prosodic features computed per 25 ms frame and summarised per vocalisation instance as mean, standard deviation and range (three nested feature combinations FC1-FC3).

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Handcrafted kinematic summary features - 17 scalar measures derived from segmented sub-movements (durations, movement units, peak velocity/acceleration/deceleration and their timings, wrist-angle change), not raw time series.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: Symbolic/event-based per-stimulus features: a 40-dimensional vector of binary correctness values and a 40-dimensional vector of millisecond latencies, indexed by image identity, plus their concatenation. No raw time series, embeddings or images are fed to the models.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: Data-driven histogram (bag-of-locations) representation: fixation coordinates are quantised to K K-means cell centroids over the face image and counted, then normalised by total fixation count, giving one K-dimensional histogram per viewed face. Explicitly orderless - no raw time series, scanpath sequence or deep embedding.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Handcrafted symbolic representation: each description is a word-frequency vector over a 1161-word vocabulary, reduced to a low-dimensional LSI projection (six dimensions capture 96% of variance). Word ordering, phrases and higher-order correlations are explicitly omitted. Separately, a word-word co-occurrence graph is built and summarised by its mean local clustering coefficient.

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: Handcrafted statistical features over sensor streams: touch data are segmented into atomic gestures and summarised by kinematic and form variables; inertial data are summarised across the session by statistical moments, zero-crossing counts and inter-axis correlations. All per-feature values are reduced to their session mean before modelling. No raw time series, images or learned embeddings.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: Handcrafted kinematic summary features: 20 scalar parameters per trial, aggregated per participant per condition into means and standard deviations across 8 trials, giving 40 features per condition. Critically, the discriminative signal turned out to lie entirely in the standard deviations rather than the means - i.e. in trial-to-trial variability rather than in average movement form. No raw time series, images or learned embeddings.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: Histogram-based aggregation of frame-level descriptors: AU intensities, animation-unit intensities, head-pose angles and head speeds are each binned into per-segment histograms; cumulative distance and response times enter as scalars; everything is length-normalised by frame count and Z-scored. This is a handcrafted statistical representation built on top of deep-learned per-frame features rather than a learned embedding of the video.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: Handcrafted standardised acoustic features: the 88-parameter eGeMAPS set of statistical functionals computed over 25 smoothed low-level descriptors per vocalisation. The BLSTM additionally consumes the descriptors on 10 ms time steps, so the deep model sees a frame-level time series while the SVM sees utterance-level functionals - a representation difference the paper does not foreground.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: Two-stage representation: hand-crafted acoustic functionals (eGeMAPS 88-dimensional, or ComParE 6373-dimensional) computed per utterance, then transformed into deep embeddings by taking the activations of one of four GAN discriminator hidden layers (256 units each). The comparison across layers is itself a study of representation depth, and yields different optima for the compact and the brute-forced feature set.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: Handcrafted time-series parameterisation: each GRF waveform is reduced to its local peaks, minima and the relative times at which they occur, with amplitudes normalised to percentage body weight and times to percentage of stance phase. This yields 20 scalar features, reduced to three by feature selection. No raw waveforms, time series or learned representations are used.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: Symbolic/spatial-occupancy representation: continuous tracked position is discretised onto a 4x4 grid and summarised either as a 16-bit binary occupancy vector or a 16-dimensional dwell-time proportion vector, then converted into pairwise cosine similarities between children. The classification features are therefore relational - how similar this child's spatial pattern is to others' - rather than absolute, which is an unusual representation choice in this corpus and one that makes the features dependent on the composition of the sample.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: Handcrafted region-aggregated features: total fixation time per area of interest over the 10-second clip, plus three normalising ratios. Extremely low-dimensional - ten AOIs and three ratios against 74 children - which is a far healthier feature-to-sample ratio than most studies in this corpus and materially reduces overfitting risk.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: Handcrafted features at two levels of abstraction: acoustic functionals (mean, max, min over 74 COVAREP descriptors sampled at 10 ms, giving 222 dimensions per recording, then averaged across recordings) and symbolic linguistic features from ASR transcripts (LIWC psycholinguistic categories, plus task-performance counts such as correct, irrelevant and repeated word ratios and word error rate). Notably the task-specific features are designed to be robust to the real-world failure mode observed - a parent prompting the child - by counting irrelevant and repeated words rather than only correct ones.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: Handcrafted per-AOI gaze summary features - time to first view, total and percentage viewing time, fixation count and revisit count - computed under two alternative AOI definitions (VIPS-derived page elements versus a generic 2x2 grid), plus categorical contextual variables. No raw scanpaths, time series or learned embeddings. The AOI-definition comparison effectively treats the representation itself as an experimental variable, which is unusual and produces one of the paper's most useful findings.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Learned deep embeddings over raw video, with no handcrafted features at all: 7x7x1024 convolutional feature maps per frame from GoogLeNet, adaptively pooled by a learned 7x7 attention map into a 1024-dimensional vector, then consumed recursively by a 128-dimensional LSTM. Videos are split into 15-frame clips for training, with each clip treated independently and probabilities averaged across frames at test time. This is one of the few genuinely end-to-end representations in the corpus.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: A distinctive three-stage representation: fixation sequences are first converted to character strings where each AOI symbol is repeated proportionally to fixation duration (one character per 50 ms), so that duration is encoded in string length; pairwise ScanMatch alignment then produces a similarity matrix incorporating spatial proximity and anatomical group membership through a purpose-built substitution matrix; and t-SNE finally embeds each scanpath as a point in two dimensions. This converts an inherently pairwise, non-vector representation into per-item coordinates that can be tested statistically - which is exactly the barrier the paper sets out to solve.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: Handcrafted distributional features: Shannon entropy over a 101-bin normalised histogram and the central 95% range, computed for amplitude, velocity and acceleration and aggregated across three trials by minimum, median and maximum. This is a distribution-shape representation rather than the point-statistic representation (peak velocity, duration, jerk) used by other motor studies in the corpus, and is well matched to the construct of restrictedness.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: Handcrafted features at two levels: frame-level acoustic descriptors summarised per speaker per conversation by four statistical functionals, and text-derived lexical, syntactic and discourse counts. These are then projected onto 10 principal components for modelling, so the classifier operates on a learned low-dimensional linear subspace of handcrafted features rather than on the features directly.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: Hybrid representation: handcrafted scalar features for task performance and gaze dynamics, combined with a 640-dimensional learned embedding of the fixated face region taken from an intermediate convolutional layer. This is a distinctive design in the corpus - it replaces manually annotated areas of interest with a learned encoding of stimulus content at the point of gaze, which the authors explicitly present as avoiding reliance on annotated AOIs.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: Categorical human ratings as features: 31 multiple-choice responses per video per rater. No signal-level representation of the video is used at all. The authors note in future work that a sufficiently large annotated corpus would allow convolutional and recurrent networks to learn features directly from raw video and audio - explicitly positioning the current human-rating approach as a bootstrapping stage.

answers.title: Exploiting Visual Behaviour for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification
answers.answer: Handcrafted numeric features - 30 scalar statistics per scanpath spanning content-relative fixation allocation, fixation and saccade dynamics, spatial coverage and refixation, saliency-weighted attention, and centre-proximity measures. No raw scanpath sequences, images or learned embeddings are fed to the classifier, though deep models (YOLO) and a saliency model are used upstream to define the regions the features are computed against.

answers.title: Hierarchical POMDP Framework for a Robot-Assisted ASD Diagnostic Protocol
answers.answer: Behaviour is represented as discrete observation symbols drawn from a defined set per task, and the child is represented as a probability distribution (belief) over a factored latent state space of condition, engagement and verbal activity. Between hierarchy levels, a continuous belief simplex is discretised into 16 partitions whose centroids define observation probabilities. There are no feature vectors, embeddings or time series.

answers.title: Intelligent Gaze-Based Screening System for Autism
answers.answer: Handcrafted low-dimensional features: mean fixation duration per region of interest, assembled into one feature vector per participant. The paper describes this as incorporating both temporal and spatial information, since duration is temporal and ROI identity is spatial. No raw scanpaths, images or learned embeddings.

answers.title: Kinematic features of a simple and short movement task to predict autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Handcrafted kinematic summary features: 20 scalar movement measures per pointing movement plus spatial accuracy measures, aggregated to 60 features as means and standard deviations pooled across hands, then z-score normalised. No raw time series, images or learned embeddings.

answers.title: Learning to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder based on the Visual
answers.answer: A two-stage engineered-then-learned representation: scanpaths are first rendered into RGB images encoding position and its derivatives via colour gradients, then compressed by rescaling to 100x100, grayscale conversion, and PCA from 10,000 dimensions to 50 components. The classifier therefore operates on a 50-dimensional linear projection of a grayscale rendering rather than on the image directly, which is a significant loss of the spatial structure the rendering was designed to create.

answers.title: Machine Learning to Study Social Interaction Difficulties in ASD
answers.answer: Automatically computed high-dimensional synchrony representation: 1004 lagged cross-correlations per window between head and body motion energy time series, z-standardised and aggregated across four interaction conditions into 4016 features per participant, then projected onto principal components explaining 80% of variance within each inner fold. No handcrafted kinematic parameters and no manual behavioural coding.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: Sub-second touch-screen and inertial time series from two five-minute gameplay sessions per child. The feature set derived from these is not enumerated, being internal to the commercial product.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: Two contrasting representations tested side by side. First, handcrafted: aligned coordinate pairs plus duration statistics plus three trajectory distances, in 7- and 47-dimensional variants. Second, learned: each fixation rendered as a sparse image channel carrying its duration at its location, Gaussian-smoothed to counter sparsity, with 33 channels stacked in temporal order - an unusual encoding that preserves both fixation order (by channel index) and duration (by value) while letting a convolutional network read spatial position directly rather than from coordinates.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: An engineered spatiotemporal image representation consumed by a learned classifier. The PoTion encoding is the distinctive element: rather than feeding a frame sequence to a recurrent or 3D convolutional model, it collapses the entire episode into a single 256x256x3 image where spatial position encodes keypoint location, colour hue encodes body region, and colour intensity encodes time within the episode. This makes a temporal classification problem tractable with a standard 2D convolutional network.

answers.title: Robot-Assisted Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnostic Based on Artificial Reasoning
answers.answer: Per-camera head pose and gaze vectors published as ROS navigation messages, fused asynchronously and reduced to a timestamped visual-focus-of-attention estimate naming the target the child is looking at. The representation is intentionally semantic rather than raw - the pipeline's output is 'the child is looking at the robot' rather than a feature vector - which is why the analysis can be conducted in the vocabulary of joint-attention subtypes.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths
answers.answer: A distinctive representation: rather than encoding fixation coordinates directly, each fixation is represented by the local neighbourhood of a predicted saliency map, so the model sees the saliency context of what was fixated. Duration is appended per fixation, and the sequence is processed recurrently with zero-padding to fixed length 40 and max-pooling over LSTM outputs. This preserves fixation order and duration while abstracting away absolute position.

answers.title: Social robot in diagnosis of autism among preschool children
answers.answer: Proportions of required behaviours performed, computed separately for instructed and spontaneous conditions in each game. Normalising by the number of behaviours the game required of the child is the right construction, since it removes differences in game length and in how many opportunities each scenario afforded, and it makes the two conditions commensurable within a child.

answers.title: Application of the Still-Face Paradigm in Early Screening for High-Risk Autism Spectrum Disorder in Infants and Toddlers
answers.answer: Ten hand-defined behavioural statistics per child: duration and frequency of eye contact, active social engagement and social smiling in the FF episode, and duration and frequency of eye contact and active social engagement in the SF episode. All are produced by human coders in Observer XT 12, not by automated sensing - so the representation is interpretable and clinically legible, but the pipeline is not automatable and the home self-screening application the paper envisages would require replacing this stage entirely.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Kinematic and Eye Movement Features of a Movement Imitation Task to Predict Autism Diagnosis
answers.answer: Handcrafted kinematic and gaze summary features, structured hierarchically: 20 kinematic parameters computed as means and standard deviations for each of three movement conditions within each of two instruction blocks, plus 24 gaze means and 24 gaze standard deviations per block. This produces a feature space far larger than the 30-participant development sample, which is precisely the small-sample high-dimensional regime the paper's methodology is designed to handle.

answers.title: Research and Design of Autism Smart Diagnosis Information System Based on Chinese Children's Facial Expression Data and Deep Convolution Neural Network
answers.answer: Raw facial images processed end-to-end, with learned convolutional features persisted as HDF5 feature files for reuse and incremental retraining. Training data are FER2013 (35,887 low-resolution 48x48 images), CK+ (593 sequences from 123 people at 640x480), and 112 images from 16 Chinese children aged 5-8. The mismatch between the training distribution - largely adult, largely posed, mostly non-Chinese - and the target population of 3-6 year old autistic children is the input-representation problem the paper's supplementary collection was meant to address but at 112 images cannot.

answers.title: Automated identification of postural control for children with autism spectrum disorder using a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Handcrafted low-dimensional biomechanical features: 12 scalar summaries of centre-of-pressure behaviour per child, spanning two theoretically distinct constructs - sway magnitude and sway complexity. The 12-features-to-50-participants ratio is among the healthiest in the corpus and materially reduces overfitting risk relative to the high-dimensional representations used elsewhere.

answers.title: Behavior-based Risk Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through
answers.answer: Handcrafted temporal features over a sliding window: Laban movement analysis converts pose trajectories into three interpretable movement-quality dimensions (weight, space, time) computed over 1-second windows, concatenated with raw facial keypoint coordinates. The representation is therefore partly interpretable in principle - Laban features have established meanings in movement analysis - though no interpretation is pursued.

answers.title: Computerized Assessment of Motor Imitation as a Scalable Method for Distinguishing Children With Autism
answers.answer: A three-dimensional interpretable representation derived from 20-joint 3D trajectories: a joint-importance-weighted DTW distance capturing spatial fidelity, and two durations capturing how long the child lagged and led the model. Producing a continuous score in [0,1] rather than a categorical judgement is an explicit design goal, argued as necessary for populations with high behavioural variability where 'categorical outputs can only capture relatively large variations'. This is one of the lowest-dimensional and most interpretable representations in the corpus.

answers.title: Deep-Learning-Based Detection of Infants with Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Auto-Encoder Feature Representation
answers.answer: eGeMAPS - all 88 parameters, per 25 ms frame with 10 ms overlap, normalised using training-set statistics and grouped into blocks of five consecutive frames so the BLSTM sees local temporal context; the SVM receives the same five frames flattened into a 440-dimensional vector. The auto-encoder compresses 88 to 54 dimensions, matched deliberately to the 54-feature statistical subset so the two dimensionality-reduction strategies are directly comparable. That comparison is the paper's cleanest result: learned compression beat statistical selection, and statistical selection was worse than no reduction at all.

answers.title: Effects of Intra-Subject Variation in Gait Analysis on ASD Classification Performance in Machine Learning Models
answers.answer: Eight temporal gait-phase durations per gait cycle, computed as frame-count differences at 250 Hz between detected foot strike and foot off events, then L2-normalised per feature vector to equalise phases of naturally different duration. The two representations compared are the raw per-cycle vector (Dataset A) and its mean across all cycles within a trial (Dataset B). The averaging is the intervention under study, and the paper demonstrates its effect directly by plotting the same two features before and after for six subjects.

answers.title: Estimating Autism Severity in Young Children From Speech Signals Using a Deep Neural Network
answers.answer: Sixty handcrafted features across seven families, fully enumerated, computed over automatically detected vocal segments within manually labelled speaker intervals. Three input arrangements are compared: one 60-feature vector per child; 100 independent 48-feature vectors per child, each from 10 sequential vocal segments; and those same 100 vectors stacked into a 100 x 48 matrix per child. The sub-sampling is a deliberate data-augmentation strategy for a 72-child dataset, raising training samples from 51 to 5100 in model 2 - and the finding that this hurt while stacking the same samples into a matrix helped is one of the more useful negative-plus-positive results in the corpus.

answers.title: Detecting High-Functioning Autism in Adults Using Eye Tracking and Machine Learning
answers.answer: AOI-level gaze feature vectors: one row per AOI per page per participant, under three AOI definitions - VIPS page-specific elements at the fifth hierarchical level, a 2 x 2 grid, and a 4 x 4 grid. The AOI comparison is the paper's most transferable methodological result. Page-specific AOIs suit Search tasks, where areas have differing task relevance; grid AOIs lose less for Browse tasks, where all elements are equally relevant; the coarse 2 x 2 grid is always worst; and the finer page-specific segmentation in Study 2 (26.6 AOIs per page against 18.6 in Study 1) may have added noise rather than information, since the 4 x 4 grid outperformed it for Synthesis. The authors conclude there is 'a trade-off between having sufficiently detailed AOIs and not introducing too much noise' and that the optimal number 'is best defined empirically'. Grid AOIs have the additional property that no fixation is lost.

answers.title: Identification of Autism Spectrum Disorder via an Eye-Tracking Based
answers.answer: Scanpath pieces of one to five consecutive fixations, each fixation represented by two-stream CNN features over centre and surround image patches concatenated with 33 saliency features spanning low-level (orientation subbands, colour, Itti conspicuity, colour histograms, Oliva-Torralba saliency), mid-level gist (distance to centre, horizon line) and high-level semantic (face, person and car detector responses) tiers. Crucially, features describe what was looked at - the image content at each fixation - rather than the gaze coordinates themselves, so the representation encodes the semantics of visual attention rather than its geometry. Fixation duration is deliberately excluded and its omission acknowledged.

answers.title: Machine Learning and Virtual Reality on Body Movements' Behaviors to Classify Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Mean inter-frame Euclidean displacement per joint, aggregated by body region and stimulus condition into a 24-cell factorial of datasets, each reduced by PCA then by RFE to three or fewer retained features. The representation is deliberately minimal - a single scalar per joint per condition - which is defensible at this sample size but discards everything about the temporal structure, rhythmicity or repetitiveness of the movement, despite repetitive behaviour being the construct the study is about. The paper's own terminology reflects the gap: it calls the measure 'frequency' throughout, but nothing in the pipeline computes a rate or a period.

answers.title: Responsive Social Smile: A Machine-Learning Based Multimodal Behavior Assessment Framework towards Early Stage Autism Screening
answers.answer: A six-dimensional binary vector, one element per stimulus. This is a deliberately clinical representation - it mirrors exactly what a clinician records on a screening sheet, so the classifier's input is inspectable and the system's intermediate output is directly usable by a human even if the final classification is ignored. The cost is that all temporal, intensity and latency information about the smile is collapsed to a single bit per stimulus, and missing stimuli are mean-imputed within the child, which for a binary feature produces values the classifier was not otherwise trained on.

answers.title: Selection of Eye-Tracking Stimuli for Prediction by Sparsely Grouped Input Variables for Neural Networks: towards Biomarker Refinement for Autism
answers.answer: 9,647 features organised into 109 groups, one per stimulus - the grouping is the methodological point, since acquisition cost is incurred per stimulus and not per derived variable, so selection must respect that structure. Group sizes are unequal by paradigm (41 to 177 features per stimulus) and group lasso's square-root-of-group-size weighting accounts for this. The regime is p >> k > n, with 9,647 features and 109 groups against 64 participants, which the paper states explicitly as the reason standard variable selection is inapplicable. Missing values imputed by unsupervised Expectation-Maximization.

answers.title: The identification of children with autism spectrum disorder by SVM approach on EEG and eye-tracking data
answers.answer: Two feature families of very unequal size. EEG contributes relative power in five bands across 62 electrodes - potentially over 300 features, though the paper reports an EEG-only classification 'using the five frequency bands' relative power', suggesting channel-averaged values were used there. Eye tracking contributes 16 features (eight AOIs by two face races) as fixation-time proportions. The relative power formulation is a considered choice, expressing each band as a share of total spectral power to expose 'abnormalities in the rhythmic fluctuations' independent of overall amplitude. The 60 ms fixation threshold on the gaze side is a similarly considered detail, excluding gaze too brief to be conscious. The asymmetry in pool size between modalities is not addressed and matters for interpreting which features the mRMR selection favoured.

answers.title: Toward Continuous Social Phenotyping: Analyzing Gaze Patterns in an Emotion Recognition Task for Children With Autism Through Wearable Smart Glasses
answers.answer: 219 features per trial in four clearly separated blocks, which is what makes the ablation grid possible: a row-normalised 7 x 7 emotion confusion matrix flattened to 49 features; a per-face binary correctness sequence of 41 or 42 features preserving temporal structure; three gaze features per face (proportion of frames on the face rather than a distractor, proportion of fixation changes directed to the face, and frames elapsed before first looking at the face) giving 123 or 126; and two metadata features, age and gender. Including metadata as an explicit feature block rather than as covariates is the design decision that makes the paper's central finding visible.

answers.title: Towards the automatic detection of social biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: introducing the simulated interaction task (SIT)
answers.answer: Primary features chosen a priori from theory and from an independent EMG study, then expanded into secondary summary statistics (mean, standard deviation, minimum, maximum, time of maximum, skewness, kurtosis) computed separately for each of the seven conversation parts - yielding 715 facial, 85 gaze and 58 voice features. Segment-wise computation preserves the paradigm's designed structure, so the representation encodes not just how much a participant smiled but when relative to the emotional content of the conversation. Each participant contributes exactly one feature vector, which the authors state explicitly rules out nested repeated measures. Gender is included as a feature throughout so that the model can weight sex-dependent voice features appropriately.

answers.title: Utilizing Artificial Intelligence to Diagnose Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Tracking Saccades
answers.answer: Nineteen tabular attributes reduced to sixteen by dropping ethnicity, blood type and eye colour, then to six by mutual-information filtering. The features arrive pre-computed, so no representation design was performed here. Two observations about the feature set are worth recording: the presence of blood type and eye colour in a saccade dataset is unexplained and suggests the source was not well understood; and dropping ethnicity as 'unrelated to tracking eye movement' removes the one variable that would have permitted any check on demographic confounding, which given the total absence of participant characteristics is a consequential deletion.

answers.title: An Experimental Trial: Multi-Robot Therapy for Categorization of Autism Level Using Hidden Markov Model
answers.answer: Two continuous session-level percentages, each collapsed into three ordinal bands at 50% and 80% thresholds - so the entire model input for a session is one of nine discrete combinations. This is by far the coarsest representation in the corpus. The thresholds were 'deduced in discussion with the therapist and according to the child's performance', which gives them clinical meaning but also means they were chosen with sight of the data by the same source that supplied the labels. The per-child averages in Table 2 show how much is discarded: joint attention values from 43.43% to 85.46% and imitation from 59.9% to 92.19% collapse into a handful of cells.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis Based on Trajectories of Eye Tracking Data
answers.answer: Fifteen trajectory and timing features per region per segment, giving nine feature vectors of 15 x R dimensions per participant. Three aspects are distinctive. First, distance-to-centre features (mean, standard deviation, coefficient of variation) capture how tightly gaze is held on a region rather than merely whether it was there. Second, ordinal features (order of longest visit, order of longest fixation) encode sequence position within a segment. Third, the anticipation features permit negative values by searching gaze records from the preceding segment, so a participant whose gaze arrives before the referent appears is distinguished from one who arrives promptly. Missing values, arising when a region was never visited or fixated, are imputed as the segment's final time or order multiplied by an empirically chosen constant of 4 - a defensible encoding of 'never' as an extreme value, though the constant was tuned rather than derived.

answers.title: Autistic spectrum traits detection and early screening: A machine learning based eye movement study
answers.answer: Nine gaze features plus age and sex. The gaze features are proportions rather than counts, which normalises for exposure length, and the three-way split into total, continuous and transition proportions gives a compact description of both where attention rests and how it moves. Whole-sample means show the landscape dominating at 76% of gaze points against 17% for figures and 7% for the animal. The inclusion of age and sex as predictors is the consequential decision: it improves fit within a homogeneous adult sample but makes the model's behaviour on a demographically different test population uninterpretable, since the classifiers may be responding to the demographic features rather than the gaze features.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Sixty-eight distributional statistics computed from raw gaze samples - eight moments and order statistics for x and y in each of four regions, plus sample counts per region - used in full without selection. Two design details matter. Samples were stacked across all trials within a condition, justified by the verified absence of a learning effect between the first and last 10 trials in any group or condition. And because targets and confounds appeared at random positions, gaze samples in those regions were converted to local coordinates while cue and other regions retained global coordinates, so that the distributional statistics describe gaze relative to the object rather than relative to the screen. The stated principle - features 'arbitrarily specified without a prior assumption' and used without selection - is the direct methodological answer to the selection-inflation problem the paper identifies in the literature.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: Forty-three features, every one traceable to one of three stated behavioural hypotheses, with a systematic naming convention (area-n-N for region n in stage N, plus per-region means). The representation is genuinely interpretable - each feature is a rate with a plain-language meaning - which serves the paper's clinical-support framing. Two design decisions bear scrutiny. Area0 is defined as an eye deviation angle of exactly zero, taken to mean gaze that 'cannot be tracked by the device', so a measurement artefact is promoted to a behavioural feature; this may capture real inattention but cannot distinguish it from tracker dropout, off-axis head position or non-compliance. And the region assignment depends on a single angular tolerance epsilon set to 2.25 by unspecified means, so the entire spatial feature family rests on one tuned constant.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: Fourteen features total - seven EEG spanning time domain, time-frequency, synchronisation and four complexity measures, and seven gaze features corresponding one-to-one with the seven viewing tests. This is an extremely compact representation, and the one-feature-per-paradigm structure on the gaze side means each node carries the summary of an entire experimental condition, which is what makes the covariance edges interpretable as relationships between constructs rather than between arbitrary statistics. The corresponding cost is that all spatial detail within each gaze paradigm - which areas of interest were fixated - is collapsed, and 120 of 128 EEG channels are discarded.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Twenty-seven image features at three levels of abstraction, computed per pixel, reduced by ReliefF to 15 for the non-severe model and 12 for the severe model. The representation describes the stimulus rather than the participant, with the participant entering only through which pixels they fixated - an inversion of the usual arrangement in this corpus, where features describe gaze behaviour directly. Frame reduction from 1,590 to 135 groups by a 33% pixel-difference criterion is a sensible efficiency measure for 54 seconds of video, and discarding the ten frames either side of each video transition removes the change-detection artefacts that would otherwise dominate.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Twenty-one features: sixteen fixation percentages (four areas of interest by four sessions) and five durations (four sessions plus total). The representation is compact, interpretable and clinically legible - every feature is a proportion of looking at a named body region during a named conversational activity, or a duration. Computing features per session rather than pooling across the conversation is what allows the temporal pattern to emerge, showing group differences concentrated in the earlier sessions. The authors note the representation's narrowness themselves, observing that fixation counts, entropy, revisits and oculomotor features were all available and unexploited.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: Three feature families with an explicitly argued progression. Perturbation measures are introduced first and their limitation stated: 'a high degree of jitter consequences in a voice with roughness... Besides, it is very difficult to measure fundamental frequency, in the case of a pathological voice'. Noise energy measures follow, with their limitation likewise stated: they 'depend on the voice recording environment'. Spectral-cepstral features are then introduced to overcome both, with MFCC justified because it 'analyze the vocal tract independently of the vocal folds that can be injured due to voice pathologies' and RASTA-PLP because its bandpass filtering removes channel effects. This is a coherent and well-referenced design rationale, and the empirical ordering of results matches it. Each family is summarised to a fixed-length vector by statistical moments across frames.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: The representation is the contribution. Scanpath images at 256 x 256 after cropping and rescaling, with three deliberate design decisions documented: a cap of 200 consecutive drawn points, selected empirically after finding that 100-150 'turned out to poorly discriminate the 2 classes' while higher values produced clutter; a velocity bound at a quarter of the screen diagonal on the grounds that faster movement 'would not be normal given the scenarios used'; and vertical mirroring to correct for the coordinate origin. Augmentation generated five synthetic variants per image. The heterogeneous stimulus battery is what yields an average of 9.27 images per child, which is simultaneously what makes the dataset large enough to train a CNN and what creates the leakage risk the paper then measures.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Twenty-eight pixel-level image features reduced to 15 per group by genetic algorithm, computed by averaging feature values across the frames aggregated into each group. The aggregation procedure is the paper's more distinctive representational contribution: because individual video frames contain too few fixations to support learning, consecutive frames are merged wherever mean optical-flow motion falls below 0.33, a threshold derived by visual inspection of when successive frames were nearly identical, and explicitly flagged as needing revision for any different stimulus. Training pixels are then sampled as the 350 most-fixated coordinates against 350 randomly chosen zero-fixation coordinates, giving a balanced 700 per map.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: 144 frame-count features spanning general, background, area-of-interest, person and item families, each computed globally and per scene, plus explicitly constructed difference features contrasting faces against bodies, children against adults, avatar against other characters, dynamic against static items, and people against items. Building the contrasts directly into the feature set rather than leaving them for the model to discover is a sensible choice at this sample size. The unit throughout is the number of frames in which something was seen, which measures how much of the session was spent looking at a category but discards fixation structure, dwell duration and sequence - a limitation the authors partly recognise in calling for finer area definitions.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Six features only - rotation range and amount of rotation per minute in each of pitch, yaw and roll. This is the most parsimonious representation in the corpus relative to sample size, and it is arrived at by design rather than by reduction: the two measures are chosen to separate the amplitude of movement from its quantity, and the per-minute normalisation explicitly corrects for participants taking different amounts of time. Spline interpolation is applied to smooth the raw series before computation. The small feature count is what makes exhaustive subset search feasible and also what limits overfitting risk.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: Raw 128 x 128 greyscale pixels with brightness increased - 16,384 features per image, with no engineered representation, no dimensionality reduction and no convolutional structure. Applying classifiers such as naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbours and logistic regression directly to raw pixels of spatially structured images is a poor match of method to data, and is likely why the pooled results plateau around 74%: none of these models can exploit spatial locality. The source study used a convolutional network on the same images for exactly this reason.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Seventeen trial-level features, each defined explicitly in a table, spanning movement timing, peak dynamics and their relative timing, spatial displacement at both peak velocity and movement offset, trajectory length, and the three cumulative variance-accounted-for measures. The representation is compact, physically interpretable and includes the theoretically motivated coordination variables alongside the descriptive ones. The PCA preprocessing is carefully specified - trial-wise application after time-normalisation to 200 points and per-trial z-scoring, the latter adopted specifically to account for the differing ranges of motion across joints, with the choice of three components justified by reference to prior work on three-dimensional movement.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: A scalar attention score accumulated at approximately 1 Hz across a session, with session-level trends used both for the agreement analysis and for adapting the next session's scenario. Every increment is traceable to a detection event and a stated constant.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Twenty-one questionnaire items binary- or one-hot-encoded, reduced by three alternative selection schemes. The representation is transparent and the questionnaire is fully documented, which makes it reproducible as an instrument even though the analysis is not. The critical gap is that the outcome of selection is never reported: SelectKBest retained 17 of the features, but which 17 is not stated, and the variance-threshold and model-based schemes likewise report no retained sets.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: A three-level cascade producing a fixed-dimension subject vector from variable-length speech: frame measures at 100 per second, summarised by five distributional statistics separately for voiced and unvoiced regions and augmented with duration statistics, then summarised again per conversational activity, then concatenated across four activities. The separation of voiced from unvoiced regions is a considered choice - 'features extracted from voiced regions tend to differ in nature compared to those from unvoiced regions' - and the per-activity structure is what enables the sampling-context comparison. Recursive elimination then reduces the prosodic set to two interpretable quantities, pitch and loudness.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: One fixed-length 30-dimensional vector per subject-image pair, computed by summarising the scanpath against the image. The representation choice determines the unit of analysis: because features are per subject-image, each child contributes one labelled instance per image, and the model classifies scanpaths rather than children. Nothing aggregates the multiple scanpaths belonging to the same child into a single participant-level prediction, and the reported metrics are means over per-image scanpath classifications.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: The most thorough exploration of input representation in the corpus. Scanpaths were encoded as (i) a zero-padded 99-dimensional flat vector of normalised coordinates and durations, (ii) a 33-channel image where each channel places one fixation's duration at its location, with two densification schemes (Gaussian sigma = 20 versus replication to a 30-pixel radius) and two channel schemes (one channel per fixation versus all collapsed into one), and (iii) a sequence fed to an LSTM alongside a 49-dimensional image feature taken from the ResNet 7x7 map before global pooling. The ablation over these choices is reported cleanly: separated channels beat collapsed channels because temporal order is preserved, and Gaussian spreading beat replication. Two representational decisions are also documented as corrections of earlier error - the original challenge entry had aligned real to synthetic scanpaths with dynamic time warping, which 'completely ignores the duration of each fixation point because no duration information is provided by the STAR-FC model' and thereby 'introduces distortion and omission to the real scan-path'; abandoning the warping and using raw 33-point scanpaths with durations was one of the two sources of the improvement.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: The most consequential representational decision in the corpus: rendered skeletons on a black background, with the background removed entirely. This forecloses whole classes of confound that demonstrably affect other studies here - clinic decor, lighting, camera model, image resolution, clothing, and the facial appearance that group-specific recording conditions can encode. It simultaneously delivers de-identification, which the authors name as a co-equal motivation. Two further choices support generalisation: features are computed from rendered image output rather than raw keypoint coordinates, explicitly 'to obtain feature vectors invariant to a rigid body and affine transformations', so a child positioned differently relative to the camera is not thereby a different input; and downsampling to 320x240 keeps the representation coarse. The residual limitation is that the rendering includes every person OpenPose detects, so the representation is of the interaction scene rather than of the child.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: One 17-dimensional vector per child per task: twelve kinematic features averaged over all finite trajectories in that task, plus five one-hot task indicators, yielding 60 x 25 = 1,500 rows. Two aspects of this construction determine what the results can mean. Averaging within task discards within-task variability and produces a stable per-child descriptor - which is exactly what makes each row informative about the individual as well as the group. And because every child contributes 25 such rows that share their individual movement characteristics, rows are strongly clustered within children; treating the 1,500 rows as exchangeable for the purpose of fold assignment is the analytic decision that undermines the headline figure. A representation of one vector per child would have given 60 rows and a much harder, but interpretable, problem.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: A three-level representation. Level one is hand-engineered and theory-driven: EEG features chosen to test published claims about spectral power, signal complexity and network topology in autism, and gaze features chosen to test claims about social attention allocation.
