Level two compresses each modality to a 50-dimensional latent code via its own autoencoder. Level three concatenates the two 50-dimensional codes into a 100-dimensional vector and compresses again to 20 before classification. Two design points matter. Fusion occurs after each modality has been separately abstracted, so the fusion network operates on comparable representations rather than on raw features of wildly different scale and character - which is the paper's explanation for why it beats naive concatenation. And normalisation is fitted on training data only and applied to test data, a discipline stated explicitly and observed by very few studies in this corpus. The unit throughout is one vector per child, which is why the cross-validation can be genuinely subject-independent.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Raw video reduced only by clip trimming and, for three of four partitions, foreground segmentation. There is no hand-engineered representation at all: no head pose, no gaze vector, no skeleton, no facial landmarks. This is a meaningful methodological position given that the target behaviour is a gaze shift, which the pose-estimation literature would extract explicitly. The tradeoff is visible in the results - the model works, but nothing about the representation is inspectable, and interpretability has to be recovered afterwards through the attention weights. The temporal unit is fixed at 10 seconds from toy placement, which encodes an assumption that a genuine initiation will occur within that window; the paradigm's 30-second wait before each trial makes that assumption defensible but it is not tested.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: One feature vector per child per modality, so the unit is the participant throughout - which is what permits genuine leave-one-out cross-validation. The gaze representation is the most distinctive: rather than manually delineating areas of interest, K-means partitions the fixation space and cluster occupancy frequencies become the features, with K tested at 8, 12, 16 and 20. The approach adapts the region structure to where children actually looked, but it carries two costs the paper does not discuss - the clusters are fitted to the pooled data of both groups, and the choice of K was made on the basis of classification results. The expression representation is a time series of target-expression counts per 40-frame window, preserving some temporal structure. The EEG representation is 12 scalar band powers, reduced from 30 candidate region-band combinations by significance testing.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: 784 grayscale pixel intensities from a 28x28 downsample of a 640x480 gaze-path plot, contrast-stretched to [0,1] and flattened into CSV rows. The paper describes this resizing as its dimensionality reduction and states explicitly that 'the entire DR process is also the feature selection used in the proposed method' - so there is no feature engineering, no domain representation and no learned encoding, only downsampling. Two consequences follow. The colour encoding of velocity, acceleration and jerk that the source dataset was constructed to carry is destroyed by the grayscale conversion, so the very information that made the images more than plots of position is discarded before modelling. And at 28x28 the trace is a coarse blob, meaning the retained signal is essentially spatial coverage and density. Augmentation by horizontal flipping is also questionable for this representation: mirroring a scanpath about the vertical axis produces an image that no eye could have generated on the original stimulus, so the synthetic examples are not merely redundant but physically impossible.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Eight, then four, interpretable scalar features per participant per epoch - each a percentage of gaze time to an automatically detected region, or a correlation with a reference heatmap. Two representational decisions carry substantial methodological weight. Areas of interest were generated frame by frame by pretrained computer vision models rather than hand-drawn, removing experimenter judgement about what counts as a face or a hand and making the approach applicable to arbitrary naturalistic video; detection rates are reported (96.2% of 61,724 frames containing a person; 94.9% with face parts) and the automatic segmentations were manually verified by watching reconstructed overlay videos. And gaze-time percentages to each region were normalised by the number of frames with successful on-screen gaze rather than by total frames, explicitly so that individual differences in tracking success could not bias the region-specific measures - the direct remedy for the data-quality-as-signal pattern that recurs throughout this corpus, where tracking failure rates differ by group and can masquerade as behaviour. A partial correlation analysis then verified that the reliability findings were not explained by on-screen gaze time alone.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Three representations of the same 850 clips. Hand-engineered acoustic descriptors for the random forest; Librosa-generated mel spectrograms treated as images for the CNN; and raw waveforms for wav2vec 2.0. The unit throughout is the clip, not the child, and this is the study's one residual validation gap: the folds are child-disjoint, which correctly prevents a child's clips appearing on both sides, but the metrics are averaged over clips, so the reported figures aggregate 850 correlated observations from 58 people. A child who contributes 21 clips influences the accuracy twenty-one times over, and no per-child prediction or per-child accuracy is reported. Since clip counts differ systematically by group - roughly 21 per autistic child against 11 per comparison child - the clip-level metrics also weight the two classes' children unequally.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: One 17-dimensional vector per participant, produced by averaging frame-level acoustic measures across the task and computing transcript-level language measures over the same interval, then normalising all features to [0,1]. The unit is therefore the participant throughout, which is what makes leave-one-subject-out cross-validation meaningful. One representational property is worth noting because the authors use it defensively and correctly: almost every measure is length-normalised, being either an average over frames or c-units or a proportion computable on any sample length, the sole exception being number of distinct word roots. This lets them rebut the objection that the nine missed autistic participants escaped because their unusually long transcripts broke the measures - 'it is highly unlikely that the measures did not perform well for high language output, and more likely that high IQ and older children had fewer communication difficulties, making them harder to detect'. That is an argument about measurement invariance made from the construction of the features rather than from post hoc testing.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: One scalar per feature per movie per child, so the unit of analysis is the participant throughout and no segment-level inflation is possible. Three representational decisions do substantial confound-neutralising work. Displacement is normalised by a running average of inter-eye distance, removing the effect of a lap-held toddler moving toward or away from the camera, which would otherwise dominate the raw landmark displacement signal. The entropy tolerance uses the population-wide standard deviation rather than each child's own, so a child with more variable movement is not scored against a correspondingly wider tolerance and thereby made to appear more regular - a subtle and correct choice, with a prior paper cited for its detailed justification. And analysis is restricted to segments where the child is attending, established by two independent criteria: a head-yaw threshold justified by central-bias theory for gaze estimation, and an automatic gaze estimation algorithm confirming the child was looking at the screen. That restriction is what allows the authors to argue that the differences 'do not appear to reflect the degree of attention to the movies', and it is reinforced by the near-equal attention rates of 95% and 93%.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: One feature vector per participant, formed by concatenating measures across the 20 selected utterances - so the unit of analysis is the participant and there is no possibility of the utterance-level leakage that would arise if each utterance were treated as an independent sample. Given 8,640 rhythm features against 66 English or 48 Cantonese participants, dimensionality reduction is unavoidable, and the handling is the correct one: principal component analysis is performed inside each cross-validation training fold rather than once on the full dataset, so the components are not informed by test-fold participants. The representational commitment that distinguishes the study is retaining trajectories rather than summaries - a full f0 contour instead of mean and range, an envelope spectrum instead of a speech rate. The cost is interpretability, since no directional statement about any acoustic quantity can be recovered from a principal component of an envelope spectrum, and the paper accordingly reports no group means or effect sizes for any feature. That is a defensible trade for a study whose question is about generalisation across languages rather than about characterising a difference.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: One feature vector per participant in every configuration, so the unit is the person and leave-one-out cross-validation is genuinely participant-level. The representation question is the study's actual experiment, and it is framed as a trade-off rather than an optimisation. The page-level scheme carries far more information - 15,360 dimensions for ELMo against 1024 for the single vector - and performs marginally better, but requires manually segmenting the narrative by book page, which the authors describe as 'sometimes ambiguous, especially when a participant skips one of the pages during storytelling' and which they were only able to resolve because they had video recordings; with audio alone it 'may require arbitrary decisions whether the utterance should be assigned to one page or the next'. They then recommend the single-vector approach for clinical use despite its slightly lower scores, because it is fully automatable. That is a deployability argument overriding a performance argument, made explicitly, and it is the kind of reasoning almost absent from the rest of this corpus.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: One value per feature per area of interest per participant, averaged across the three videos within each stimulus set - so 26 values per participant per dataset, and the unit of analysis is the child. Features were min-max normalised to [0,1]. Averaging across the three videos within a set discards between-video variability, which is defensible for a screening measure but means the paradigm's internal consistency is never examined. Computing every metric for both the social and the non-social area of interest is the representational choice that makes the design work: it lets the classifier use the relationship between the two halves of the display rather than absolute looking at either, which is what a preferential paradigm is for. The two stimulus sets are kept as separate datasets throughout, so no participant contributes to a combined model.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Ten scalar percentages per child, so the unit is unambiguously the participant and leave-one-out cross-validation is genuinely participant-level. Two representational choices deserve note. Averaging the position-switched replicates before analysis removes lateral bias but also discards the only within-child replication in the design, so no reliability estimate is available. And normalising by stimulus duration rather than by on-screen looking time is the choice that produces the study's interpretive ambiguity: because the denominator is total presentation time rather than valid tracked time, a child who looks away, blinks, or loses tracking accrues a lower percentage on every area simultaneously. That is consistent with the observed pattern of reduction across nine of ten areas including non-social ones, and it is precisely the normalisation that Keles and colleagues explicitly avoid by dividing by frames with successful on-screen gaze specifically 'to control for possible individual differences between participants in their total on-screen gaze time'. The contrast between the two studies on this single methodological point is instructive.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Three input vectors combined into a single mathematical representation, with 64 questionnaire items per child spread across the channels. The representation is entirely in the vocabulary of clinical behavioural observation rather than in derived signal features, which is what allows the outputs to be audited clinically - the paper can report which comorbidities and which severity levels are associated with each output because the inputs are commensurable with the reference standard's own constructs. The age-banded versions are a considered detail: item content differs slightly between 18-47 and 48-71 months 'in order to best capture the ASD phenotype among children based on developmental trajectories', with the classifier trained to perform equivalently across both, and the trial then reports performance separately by age band and finds a genuine difference in determinate rate and specificity. That is representation design responding to a developmental fact, and it is validated rather than assumed.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: One feature vector per child, so the unit is the participant and there is no within-subject leakage. The representational contribution is the argued choice of eGeMAPS: ComParE was rejected on an explicit dimensionality argument relative to sample size, and eGeMAPS chosen over GeMAPS on grounds of psychological interpretability, with the whole parameter set tabulated and defined. Using a published standard parameter set rather than a bespoke feature collection is also what makes the study's cross-language comparison possible - the authors compare their selected features directly against those reported by Pokorny and colleagues using the same set and find agreement on unvoiced spectral slope in the 0-500 Hz range - and it is the basis of their recommendation that the field standardise on common feature sets. That is a genuine methodological contribution independent of this study's data.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: The representational chain is the study's core and its central problem. Four preprocessing stages precede feature extraction - average filtering, Laplacian enhancement, active contour segmentation, morphological cleaning - each documented with equations and each progressively removing information that might have carried gaze meaning. Segmentation isolates 'the eye-tracking path region', converting a trajectory into a binary or near-binary shape; morphological cleaning then modifies that shape further. LBP and GLCM are then computed over the result. Local binary patterns encode the relative intensity of a pixel against its neighbours and were developed for texture and face recognition; grey-level co-occurrence matrices summarise second-order intensity statistics. Neither has any relationship to where a child looked. The consequence is visible in the paper's own output: 27 pages containing six accuracy tables, multiple confusion matrices and ROC curves, and not one statement about what distinguishes autistic children's scanning from that of their peers.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: The representation is where the study's tradeoff is concentrated. Frame-level gaze is discretised from continuous (x, y) direction estimates into a 4x4 grid, then one-hot encoded and windowed. Discretisation is defensible given noisy estimates from uncalibrated phone video, and the sliding window with shift smaller than window generates overlapping samples, which multiplies the effective training set from 449 videos into many thousands of sequences - a legitimate augmentation given that the split is child-disjoint so the overlap cannot cross the partition. The decisive property, however, is the coordinate frame: gaze is expressed relative to the camera, which sits on the parent's forehead and moves with them. A region in this space is a direction, not a target, and the authors state that it cannot be matched to facial anatomy. The consequence is that the representation supports detecting that gaze distributions differ but not saying what they differ about - which is precisely the distinction between a signal and a behavioural finding, and the paper is clear about which it has.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Two representations of the same images, both stripped of behavioural content. For the conventional models: greyscale conversion by equal channel weighting, resizing to 100x100, flattening to a 10,000-element vector, then principal component analysis retaining 500 components (1,750 after augmentation). For the network: the same greyscale 100x100 image passed through four convolutional stages producing 4,608 features. The greyscale step is the most consequential and passes without comment: the source dataset's distinguishing property is that gaze velocity, acceleration and jerk are encoded as colour gradients, and averaging the three channels equally discards precisely that information, leaving a monochrome trace of position only. Both this study and Gaspar and colleagues make the same conversion on the same images, so the two independent reuses of this dataset both destroy the derivative encoding it was constructed to carry.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Thirty-four scalar features per child, derived directly from four event fields with no signal processing, feature learning or dimensionality reduction. The representation is maximally interpretable - each feature is 'percent correct on the disgust prompt' or 'mean response duration on the surprise prompt' - which is what makes the feature-importance analysis meaningful and what allows the finding to be stated in behavioural terms. Restricting to the 17 most commonly presented prompts 'in order to minimize missing-data imputation' is a sensible data-quality decision that is stated and justified. The one unresolved representational question is aggregation: features are described as computed 'for a single session of gameplay' while the sample is 49 children, and the paper does not state whether a child playing several sessions contributes several rows. If it does, the nested cross-validation would not be child-disjoint and the estimates would inherit the within-subject leakage that the paper is otherwise careful to avoid.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Three representations of the same recordings, differing in where they intercept the ICA pipeline, and the choice among them is the paper's contribution. Method 1's representation is the unusual one and the one carrying the headline: the coefficients of the 2x2 unmixing matrix at each of 256 frequency points, concatenated. These are not properties of the child's voice in any direct sense - they are the parameters of a linear demixing operator estimated from the observation channels - and their interpretation depends entirely on what those channels are, which the paper does not establish. Method 2's representation is the separated component sequences, one per frequency point, of which the single best-performing was reported. Method 3's is conventional: MFCC, LPCC and PLP computed on reconstructed audio, and the authors note that separation 'eliminates the influence of certain noises and makes the speech data more pure', while sensibly cautioning that speech processing 'need not overly pursue the complete elimination of noise' since aggressive denoising distorts speech.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: The representation choice is the study's most considered technical decision. Rather than reducing each recording to a single averaged feature vector - which is what most speech studies in this corpus do - the system builds a 100x48 matrix per child, where each row summarises 48 features over a randomly drawn run of 10 sequential vocalisations. This preserves within-session variability, which matters for a construct like prosodic atypicality that is expressed as inconsistency rather than as a shifted mean, and it supplies a two-dimensional input that a convolutional architecture can exploit. Because the matrix is the input and one prediction is produced per recording, the unit of analysis remains the child despite the internal resampling, so no leakage arises from the 100 correlated rows. The design also implicitly handles variable session length: a child with more vocalisations contributes more distinct draws, but every child yields the same fixed-size matrix.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Rater-assigned counts of movement activities and 0-5 severity scores per defined position, aggregated into turn-taking indicators for each game. Every value is traceable to a named behaviour with a published definition, so the representation is fully auditable - the opposite end of the interpretability spectrum from the 100,352 DeepFace features or 1,639 landmark values used elsewhere in this review, and a reminder that the constructs those studies attempt to learn were originally defined by exactly this kind of manual specification.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Six hand-crafted scalar features per fixed-length window of the raw gaze coordinate stream: entropy_x, entropy_y, entropy_xy, range_x, range_y, range_xy. The window length is itself a modelled hyperparameter, swept from 1 to 10 s. The binning that defines the entropy is spatial and fixed to the scene camera resolution (10 px cells), which means the features are defined in the wearer's own head-centred frame rather than in a world or face-referenced frame - an appropriate choice given head-mounted tracking, but one that makes the features depend on the geometry of where the interviewer sat. No normalisation, standardisation or per-participant centring is described, so between-child differences in absolute gaze spread enter the model directly - the same property that makes segment-level pooling risky.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: A single 54-dimensional hand-crafted feature vector per child, reduced to 10 by feature selection. The 44 inherited acceleration features are per-axis means, variances, the five dominant frequencies and their amplitudes, signal energies, pairwise inter-axis correlations, a jolt count and the playing-time duration - i.e. a mix of time-domain statistics and coarse spectral descriptors computed over the whole session. The 10 new features are of two kinds: seven state-occupancy ratios derived from the joint encoder/accelerometer signature (fractions of total and of interactive playtime spent not playing, on wheels only, on the ground and in the air) plus the total wheel turn rate, and two tilt-count features (about X and about Y) obtained by short-time Fourier transform of the acceleration signal to recover the car's roll and pitch during wheel play. The representation is therefore entirely aggregate: no temporal ordering, no sequence, no windowing, and no per-episode analysis, so a child who spins the wheels once for ninety seconds and one who spins them thirty times for three seconds each are indistinguishable. The final selected set was seven acceleration features (Y-direction jolt, tilt about Y, X-direction energy, X-Y acceleration correlation, the fourth-highest X frequency, the fifth-highest Z frequency, and the relative amplitude of the highest Y frequency) and three encoder features (wheels-only play ratio, not-playing ratio, total wheel turn rate).

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Twelve hand-crafted scalar features per task observation: four speed statistics (mean, max, min, SD), four acceleration statistics (mean, max, min, SD), and four path-geometry descriptors (STH straightness, DC directional change, sdDC directional-change variability, MeanLength). Features are computed per trajectory - one dragging movement from first tap to finger lift - using the R traj package, then averaged across the trajectories within a task, giving one 12-vector per child per task and 1,500 rows overall. The 40 Hz raw coordinate stream is therefore reduced twice before the network sees anything: once to per-trajectory summary statistics, once again by averaging across trajectories. No sequence model, no raw-signal input, no learned front end, and no representation of within-task variability across trajectories except through the SD features. The bottleneck is 10 latent dimensions at training, reduced to 2 for analysis after PCA showed the first two components carried 95% of the latent variance - so the effective representation of a child's movement on a task is a point in a plane.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Two scalar angle time series per 3 s response window, each sampled at 25 fps and therefore up to 75 frames long, reduced to threshold-crossing frame counts before the decision. The shoulder rotation series is computed frame by frame as theta_t = arccos(v_0 . v_t / |v_0||v_t|) converted to degrees, where v_t is the vector from the right to the left shoulder joint at frame t and v_0 is the same vector at the first frame after the name call - so the measurement is self-referenced to the child's posture at call onset rather than to any absolute frame, which is a sensible choice that removes dependence on how the child happened to be sitting. The head series is the OpenFace yaw Euler angle, accompanied by an implicit binary of whether a face was detected at all by the relevant rear camera. Both series are then summarised only by counting frames that satisfy a threshold, so the representation discards the shape of the movement entirely: peak angular velocity, smoothness, whether the turn was completed or aborted, and whether the child returned to the toys are all invisible. Nothing is learned from the raw joint coordinates, and no representation of the temporal profile of orienting survives into the decision.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: An 18-dimensional vector of region-based fixation statistics per observation. The stimulus space, 1024 x 768, was augmented beyond its true extent to accommodate out-of-range gaze samples, then partitioned into named regions: on FIG 1, FIG 2 and FIG 3; on the Reference FIG; around each of these; and two OUT regions below the outer figures. Fixations were clustered by location of node aggregation and two quantities extracted per region - the number of fixation nodes and the fixation time. Four nested subsets of this matrix were evaluated separately: around the figures, on the figures, on and around the figures, and all features. The representation carries no temporal information: no scan-path order, no saccade amplitudes or directions, no transition probabilities between regions, no within-trial dynamics, and no trial-to-trial evolution across the 240 images. This is a notable gap given the introduction's extended development of a graph-theoretic view in which fixations are vertices and saccades are edges - Fig. 6 even displays such a graph for one autistic child - because every quantity that graph representation would naturally yield (degree distribution, edge weights, path structure, transition entropy) is left uncomputed, and the model receives only vertex-region tallies.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: A single 6,272-dimensional vector per participant, built in three steps. First, frame-wise 3D morphable model fitting via 3DI, which jointly models identity, pose and expression so that the person's facial identity is estimated and removed rather than left to confound the expression signal - the authors cite identity bias explicitly, and this is one of very few studies in this corpus that treats individual identity as something to be subtracted rather than as an accidental source of accuracy. Second, replacement of the model's default PCA expression basis with 60 purpose-built localised components, of which 53 are retained (nose and cheek discarded), so that each dimension corresponds to a nameable facial region; concatenated with yaw, pitch and roll, this gives a 56 x T matrix per video. Third, windowed cross-correlation on every ordered pair of the 56 series, using 50% overlapping windows of length Tw and permitting only forward lag on the second series so that direction is preserved and the (i,j) pair differs from (j,i); each pair contributes the mean and standard deviation of its maximal cross-correlation across windows. The representation is therefore about temporal relationships rather than about static or averaged expression content, and it deliberately discards absolute expression magnitude, which is exactly the quantity most vulnerable to identity and recording differences. The dimensionality - 6,272 features for 42 participants - is extreme, mitigated by a linear model, fixed regularisation, no feature selection and participant-level nested cross-validation.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Per fixation: a c-bit semantic code obtained by locating the fixation's SLIC superpixel, resizing that superpixel's bounding box to d x d and passing it through the pretrained autoencoder, concatenated with four low-level descriptors - normalised position, duration, saccade amplitude and saccade orientation. A viewing pattern of m+1 fixations on one stimulus becomes a length-m sequence of these vectors, and each child yields 82 such sequences. The defining property is that no aggregation precedes the model: sequences enter the LSTM in their original order and length, in deliberate contrast to the histogram baseline (which discards order entirely) and the stacked-feature baseline (which fixes the fixation count at 10 by zero-padding or truncation). The authors' analysis of the minLength parameter is a good illustration of how carefully this was handled - raising the minimum sequence length from 2 to 4 fixations improves nothing and causes 'significant data loss in the ASD group', because autistic children produce fewer fixations, so filtering by pattern length would systematically discard the very participants the model must detect. Recognising that a preprocessing threshold interacts with the group difference it is meant to measure is a subtlety absent from most of this corpus. One reported negative result adds to the representation's credibility: using a fixed patch at each superpixel's centre performed worse than the resized full bounding box.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: For BERT, subword tokens and contextual embeddings from the multilingual cased checkpoint, applied to one tweet at a time. For the three classical models, unspecified - the paper says natural language processing techniques were used but names no tokenisation, vectorisation or feature scheme, so the representation those models consumed is unknown. In every case the unit is a single tweet treated independently: no thread context, no reply structure, no temporal ordering, no user-level aggregation, and no metadata. The maximum sequence length is not stated, which matters because tweets in the 2017-2022 window span both the 140- and 280-character limits. Nothing was masked or normalised beyond the four corpus-cleaning steps, so hashtags, mentions, URLs, emoji and autism-related vocabulary all remain in the text the models see - the last of these being the reason the results cannot be read as evidence about communication style.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Two scalar features per participant per movie: integrated entropy of the eyebrow region and of the mouth region, each being the cumulative sum of sample entropy across the first 20 coarse-grained scales of the landmark time series. The pipeline that produces them is where the work sits. Forty-nine landmarks are tracked at 30 fps; the child's face is isolated from those of caregiver, siblings and clinicians by facial embedding; eye-corner and nose landmarks drive an affine transform to a canonical face so that head motion is removed rather than confounded with expression; head-pose angles are estimated separately; signal above 15 Hz is filtered as noise on the physiologically motivated grounds that a facial expression takes at least 260 ms; non-attending intervals are excised; and the remaining landmark points within each region are averaged into a single time series. Sample entropy uses m = 2 and r = 0.15 sigma, both taken from prior literature with an appendix showing insensitivity to the choice. The missing-data rule is stated with a worked numerical example: only embedding vectors free of missing points contribute to the counts, because concatenating across gaps would inflate Cm without inflating Cm+1 and so bias the entropy. A minimum 40% valid-data requirement per movie applies. The representation deliberately discards expression identity, amplitude and timing, retaining only predictability - which is what makes it complementary to the affect measure rather than a variant of it.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Two parallel representations, compared directly. The baseline uses three interpretable scalars per trial: number of fixations, number of saccades and scan-path length. The CNN uses a spatial representation: gaze sample positions are set to 1 in an otherwise zero image, blurred with a Gaussian kernel of sigma 10, centre-cropped and downscaled to 34 x 34 greyscale, then paired with the stimulus image so the model sees both where the person looked and what was there. Two observations about this representation. It discards temporal order entirely - a heat map is a spatial density, so the sequence in which regions were visited, which the paper's own scan-path measure partly captures, is unavailable to the CNN. And the aggressive downscaling to 34 x 34 from a 1920 x 1080 display means each pixel spans roughly 56 x 32 display pixels, so the representation can distinguish eyes from mouth but not, say, one eye from the other or the pupil from the eyelid; this is a reasonable trade for a dataset of this size but bounds what the model can learn. One reporting inconsistency: fixation counts of 200-300 in a five-second trial exceed the number of possible fixation events at 120 Hz, so these are gaze samples classified as fixation rather than discrete fixation events, and the label is used loosely throughout.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: Fixed-length windows over a pseudo-semantic numeric encoding of the key-press stream. All events and keys across the corpus were enumerated - 69 unique ones despite users being able to add vocabulary - and partitioned into normal keys, complex keys, normal app events and complex app events, with each category assigned a non-overlapping range of integer identifiers so that a value's category is recoverable from its magnitude. That design is a genuine thought: it gives an otherwise arbitrary integer encoding a coarse semantic structure that a model can exploit. The stream is then cut into non-overlapping windows of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 or 100 consecutive presses, each becoming a pseudo-sample; overlapping windows were tested and gave 'no tangible improvement'. Temporal modelling substitutes inter-press intervals for identifiers, and spectral modelling replaces windows with per-session frequency counts. Two properties of this representation matter for interpretation. Users contribute pseudo-samples in proportion to how much they used the app, so heavy users dominate and the effective sample size is never reported. And lexical content is discarded: what a person said is reduced to a category-preserving integer, even though the paper's descriptive analysis shows content to be both recoverable and group-discriminating.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Raw RGB video frames at 224 x 224, in sequences of 300 (IJA) or 150 (RJA) - a fully end-to-end representation with no intermediate abstraction whatsoever. This is a stronger commitment to learned representation than any other study in this corpus, most of which extract landmarks, poses, gaze coordinates or hand-crafted statistics before modelling. It has two consequences that pull in opposite directions. It removes an entire class of failure - no landmark detector to fail on a child who turns away, no gaze estimator to calibrate, no feature engineering to bias - and it is what allows the same pipeline to work on a task where the child physically turns around, which a face-based method could not handle. But it also means the model has access to everything in the frame: the child's appearance, clothing, posture, the examiner, the room, and anything that co-varies with recruitment site. With autistic children recruited exclusively from one hospital clinic and comparison children from day care centres, and with a 44-50 point IQ difference between groups, an end-to-end model on raw frames has many routes to near-perfect separation that have nothing to do with joint attention. The Grad-CAM analysis is the study's answer to this, and it is a good one as far as it goes - the heatmaps localise to faces and eyes and the described behaviours match the constructs - but it is illustrative rather than systematic, and no quantitative check on background or appearance confounds is reported.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: A rendered scanpath image, resized either to 100x100 greyscale (custom CNN) or 299x299 RGB with pixel values normalised to [-1, 1] (InceptionV3). The greyscale conversion for the CNN is described candidly as an empirical choice: RGB training was slow and 'converting the images to grayscale proved to significantly reduce the training time and an improvement in classification accuracy was also noticed'. That is honest reporting of a decision made partly on observed accuracy, and it is worth noting that if the source rendering used colour to encode anything - fixation order, duration, or which eye - greyscale conversion would discard it, and the paper cannot say whether it did, because the rendering scheme is never described. The deeper representational point is that all temporal information in the original gaze data survives only as visual geometry: sequence order, fixation duration and saccade velocity are recoverable from a drawing only to the extent the renderer encoded them, and the model receives no time series at all.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: One fixed-length vector per child summarising an entire conversational session, comprising 45 part-of-speech tag frequencies, 23 syntactic complexity measures and 9 semantic-pragmatic measures, reduced from 77 to 63 by SHAP-guided elimination that removed non-informative tags such as SYM and MD and an um-propagation artefact. Count-based features - echolalia, unintelligible units, unexpected words - are normalised over conversation length, which is a necessary and correctly applied step given that source sessions range from about 10 to 30 minutes. Two of the features are computed with contextual embeddings rather than surface statistics: child-child and child-partner discourse coherence are cosine similarities between BERT representations of consecutive sentences, which is a reasonable operationalisation of topic maintenance and is more sensitive than lexical overlap would be. The representation discards temporal structure beyond that local coherence, so trajectory across a session - whether a child warms up, disengages, or shifts topic progressively - is not represented.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: A 100 x 100 image per participant per video clip, produced by drawing the gaze trajectory on a 1680 x 1050 black background and downsampling. The downsampling is aggressive - each output pixel spans roughly 17 x 11 input pixels - so fine spatial structure such as whether gaze fell on an eye or a cheek is not preserved, and what survives is the coarse geometry of the trajectory: its extent, its density, how many times it crosses itself. Three enrichments are then tested. Temporal restriction to 3-second or 1-second windows, which encodes time by segmentation rather than within the image. Velocity colour coding, which maps average speed between consecutive points - Euclidean distance over time interval - onto a colour scale with stated thresholds. And rotation-based augmentation, which generates additional images and is applied at three levels in one experiment. Two properties of this representation matter for interpretation. Because the image is a drawing, incidental graphical characteristics such as total ink and plotted extent are available to the network alongside behavioural ones, and no analysis distinguishes them. And because velocity depends on sampling rate, which is never stated, the velocity encoding cannot be reproduced or compared across studies.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: A 100 x 100 greyscale image flattened to a 10,000-element vector, with a parallel colour variant. Three transformations separate the raw gaze data from the model input, each discarding information: rendering the coordinate time series as a static drawing removes temporal order, fixation duration and saccade velocity; downscaling from 640 x 480 to 100 x 100 means each output pixel spans roughly 6 x 5 source pixels, so fine spatial resolution of where on a face gaze landed is lost; and flattening removes spatial adjacency. What survives is the coarse geometry and density of the drawn path. The greyscale conversion is reported to work slightly better than colour, which is consistent with colour carrying no information in these renderings - but the rendering scheme is not described, so whether colour originally encoded anything (order, duration, which eye) cannot be determined.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: A tabular feature vector per child, built from 100 candidate variables reduced to 59 on clinical-relevance grounds before any modelling - a reduction made a priori rather than by data-driven selection, which the paper states explicitly and which removes a source of optimism that data-driven feature selection would introduce. The central representational decision concerns milestones, and it is reasoned carefully. Records vary in the timing of checkups and contain multiple entries per milestone per child, so each milestone was reduced to a binary of 'ever passed' versus 'only failed', chosen specifically 'to avoid attributing a-priori developmental assumptions' to never-tested and late-tested records. The cost is stated in the same paragraph: children who passed after several attempts cannot be distinguished from those who passed immediately, so the pattern of delay - arguably the most diagnostically informative aspect of milestone data - is discarded. Stating a representational trade-off, its motivation and its cost in three sentences is better practice than anything comparable in this corpus. Longitudinal structure within a child is otherwise collapsed, and modelling performance patterns over time is named as the first priority for future work.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: Cropped facial photographs, resized (to 96 x 96 in one passage and 224 x 224 x 3 in another) and rescaled to [0, 1], with an extensive augmentation list: rotation, horizontal and vertical flipping, zooming and cropping, brightness and contrast adjustment, noise injection, shearing and scaling. Two elements deserve comment. Vertical flipping produces upside-down faces, which has no rationale for a task premised on facial landmark geometry and would be excluded by anyone reasoning about the construct rather than reaching for a standard augmentation set. And brightness, contrast and noise augmentation are described as helping the model generalise across imaging conditions - which is the right instinct but addresses only the appearance of the problem, since systematic imaging differences between the two source collections would remain available through resolution, compression and framing regardless.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: Voxel volumes and Harvard-Oxford region graphs for imaging; approximately 65-70 tabular clinical fields for the phenotype stream; a 32-dimensional fused latent vector. The phenotype representation is where the study's problem is located and where its transparency is greatest - because GAMI-Net decomposes contributions feature by feature, the paper is able to report exactly which fields drive the prediction, and it does so honestly. The top ten are ADOS_TOTAL, ADI_R_SOCIAL_TOTAL_A, FIQ, AGE_AT_SCAN, SRS_RAW_TOTAL, ADOS_COMM, ADOS_GOTHAM_SEVERITY, VIQ, PIQ and ADI_R_VERBAL_TOTAL_BV - six diagnostic-instrument scores, three IQ measures and age. Not one is a measurement of behaviour, and six of the ten are the assessment whose result is the label.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: A 41 x 23 matrix: one row per participant, one column per time scale of cross wavelet coherence, with scales spanning 0.1 s to 10 s. Each value is the coherence between the child's and the interviewer's whole-body movement time series at that scale, computed from motion energy analysis of a single side-view video. Two properties are worth recording. The representation is inherently relational - no value describes the child alone - and it is inherently frequency-resolved, which is what allowed the group difference to be localised to the fast scales where a summary measure had found nothing. A second representation of 57 derived features was then built by summing subsets of the six significant coherences: all 15 pairs, 20 triples, 15 quadruples, 6 quintuples and the single six-way sum. These are transparent linear combinations of the originals and add no new information about movement, only a re-weighting chosen with reference to the group difference.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Two representations, both derived from the same transcripts. Tags come from a Systemic Functional Linguistics annotation scheme built for Japanese through transfer comparison, comprising four system networks and eleven or more lexicogrammatical headings each with multiple tag types - modality, te-clauses with eight subtypes, twelve negotiating particles, explanative mood and others. For the linear model the input is a tag-frequency vector normalised by total word count, which discards order. For the Bi-LSTM variants the input is the ordered sequence of tag sets, with each word represented by the sum of the embedding vectors of its tags, giving 300-dimensional tag embeddings; the text model uses 300-dimensional word embeddings; and the combined model concatenates the two at each time step. Annotation was performed both manually and automatically, with both evaluated in parallel throughout, and the automatic annotator achieving a mean F of 0.88 against manual - so the study reports both the ceiling achievable with perfect annotation and the performance obtainable in a setting where manual annotation is impossible.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: A 3,315-dimensional concatenation per image: 3,000 activations from one backbone plus 100 HOG, 50 LBP, 50 ORB, 65 PHASH and 50 SIFT features. The handcrafted component is worth characterising because it determines what a source-provenance confound would look like. HOG encodes gradient distributions, which depend on image sharpness; LBP encodes local texture, which depends on resolution and compression; PHASH is a whole-image fingerprint, which encodes global tone and layout; SIFT and ORB encode keypoint structure, which depends on contrast and focus. Every one of these is a property of the photograph rather than of the face, and all differ systematically between images collected from different sources. That this feature set alone achieves 84.5% is therefore the paper's most diagnostic result, and it is reported without comment.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: Grayscale cropped faces at 120x110 for Gabor filtering and 100x100 for convolutional processing, after normalisation, histogram equalisation, face detection and realignment. KDEF images are additionally pre-standardised by the corpus creators so that eyes and lips occupy fixed coordinates, which removes pose and scale variation entirely - a property that raises accuracy and reduces the relevance of the result to any uncontrolled setting.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: A rotation-normalised sequence of 20-69 points per trajectory. The rotation step is the representational contribution and is worked out carefully: because targets sit at eight positions 45 degrees apart, raw trajectories to different targets are not comparable, so the angle between consecutive points relative to the origin is computed with atan2, mapped from the atan2 range into 0-360 degrees, and applied as a rotation - with all three steps written out as numbered equations and the resulting endpoint coordinates given. This makes trajectories to any target directly comparable while preserving their shape, and it is the kind of preprocessing that reflects thought about the construct rather than convention. The two-feature model then receives only these rotated coordinates and the four-feature model adds velocity and acceleration. Crucially, unlike the group's companion study on a different sample - which averaged twelve kinematic features across a task to give one vector per child - this study preserves the full temporal sequence, so the model sees the unfolding of the movement rather than its summary. The 20-69 point length window standardises comparability at the cost of discarding both very brief and very extended drags.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: A tabular vector of eleven variables per individual, reduced by the optimisation-based selection stage to an unnamed subset. The fitness function combines correlation, data variance and inter- and intra-class cosine similarity, which is a reasonable multi-objective formulation for filter-style selection but depends on class labels and is therefore a candidate leakage route if applied outside training folds - a question the paper does not address. No temporal, sequential or image representation is used, so whatever dynamics the underlying facial or physiological recordings contained are absent from the model input.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: A 17-dimensional tabular vector per respondent, retained from 19 or 21 available fields after dropping two judged irrelevant. Ten of the seventeen are the binary screening item responses. The critical structural fact is that the outcome is computed from those ten by summation and thresholding, and that the sum is itself present among the fields in these datasets - so the representation contains the answer twice over, once implicitly across the items and once explicitly in the total.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: A 16-dimensional summary vector per child. Time-series pressure and pose data are compressed into scalar descriptors: path length, mean speed, entropy and convex-hull area for centre-of-pressure; longest-trial duration for overall balance; and ten joint-wise correlations plus the centre-of-mass to centre-of-pressure difference for the body-pressure relationship. This is aggregation rather than sequence modelling, so the temporal unfolding of a stance is not represented except insofar as entropy and correlation capture it. The correlation features are nonetheless well chosen for the construct: a correlation between a joint angle and centre-of-pressure position is inherently relational and cannot be computed from either stream alone, and it summarises coordination in a single interpretable number. Every variable is named, categorised and explained, with the rationale and calculation method for each given in supplementary material.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: RGB face crops, normalised to [0, 1], obtained by third-party cropping in dataset 1 and by MTCNN detection with alignment, cropping and resizing in dataset 2. No landmark coordinates, no morphometric derivations, no temporal sequence. The representation therefore cannot express any of the specific craniofacial or expression-dynamic constructs the introduction invokes, and it retains every source-dependent property of the image - resolution, compression, illumination, pose, background - that is free to vary with class given how the two classes were harvested.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: An eleven-dimensional vector of linear and non-linear time- and frequency-domain descriptors per EEG segment. The features are individually interpretable and have an established electrophysiological literature, which makes the absence of any feature-importance analysis a real loss - identifying which descriptors and which electrode positions separate the groups would have produced a transferable finding independent of the classification accuracy. The number and duration of segments and their distribution across participants are not reported, which is the missing information needed to judge the sample structure.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: An 81-dimensional vector per child of counts, durations and proportions, derived arithmetically from human coding of a 90-second video with onset and offset times on a timeline. Every element is directly interpretable and directly auditable - a coder's judgement about a named behaviour, aggregated by a stated rule. The final representation is five numbers: one speech duration and four play quantities. The proportion indicators are a thoughtful design element, since normalising socially oriented vocalisations by total vocalisations, or word-use vocalisations by total vocalisations, separates the social direction of speech from the amount of speech - and indeed the proportional versions had the strongest univariate odds ratios in the vocalisation family (0.367 and 0.345). It is notable that stepwise selection nonetheless retained the raw duration measure rather than a proportion, which leaves the model's strongest predictor confounded with how much the child spoke at all, and thus with expressive language level, which was never measured.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: Two representations, compared directly. The instrument's own algorithm domain scores - communication and reciprocal social interaction under the original algorithm, social affect and restricted repetitive behaviour under the revised - which aggregate item ratings into totals against published cut-offs. And a binary per-item vector recording whether each of the 32 items received a non-zero score. The dichotomisation is the more interesting choice and is justified on psychometric rather than convenience grounds: for several items a higher rating denotes a different presentation rather than a more severe one, and the paper works through item B11, quality of social response, where a rating of 1 describes limited, awkward or inconsistent reactions and a rating of 2 describes odd, stereotyped or contextually inappropriate ones - 'there was no clear difference between scores 1 and 2 regarding the severity of ASD symptoms, and the differences were considered to be limited to phenotypic differences in symptoms'. Treating such a scale as ordinal and summing it is exactly what the algorithms do, and the collapse to presence-or-absence of atypicality is part of why the item-level analysis recovers information the totals lose.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Raw waveform segments per vocalisation, encoded by learned representations - either the discriminatively fine-tuned model's features or Wav2Vec 2.0 context representations. No hand-crafted acoustic descriptors are used in the study's own models, though the ComParE feature set is discussed as background. Sample durations are not stated but can be inferred at roughly 1.3 seconds for De-Enigma and 2.2 seconds for CPSD from the reported totals. Short segments are a real constraint on a prosodic claim: intonation contour, pitch range and expressive variation are properties of utterances and turns rather than of one- to two-second fragments, so the representation may not span the timescale on which the hypothesised difference lives.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: TF-IDF vectors and word2vec embeddings at tweet level; a self-trained embedding layer feeding an attention-based BiLSTM over a concatenation of all of a user's preprocessed tweets at profile level, restricted to users with at least five tweets. The representation is the product of aggressive normalisation - profanity masking, removal of non-alphanumerics, links, mentions and HTML, lowercasing, stop-word removal, stemming and lemmatisation - which strips much of the paralinguistic texture of social media writing (capitalisation, punctuation, emoji, elongation) that might itself carry the signal of interest. The most consequential representational decision is the removal of sixteen autism-related tokens including the hashtag that defines the label, on the explicit ground that they 'could introduce bias and lead to model overfitting'. That is a target-leakage control, correctly reasoned, and it is the same failure mode this review documents in the questionnaire-item studies where the label is an arithmetic function of the features - handled here rather than left in place.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: The video representation is the study's most important technical decision and functions as a designed confound control. Rather than modelling raw frames, the authors apply OpenPose and plot the resulting skeletal keypoints over a plain black background at 320x240, 'hence preserving a visual gist of the social interaction between the examiner and the child'. This removes face, expression, clothing, body habitus, skin tone, room, furniture, lighting and every other appearance cue - so a classifier operating on it cannot be exploiting the identity and setting confounds that this review has documented throughout the image-based branch, where models trained on photographs may be recognising where an image came from rather than who is in it. Here the confound is architecturally excluded, not merely unmeasured. It also makes partial data sharing possible, which is why a de-identified pose subsample could be deposited on Zenodo when the raw video could not. The audio representation is the mirror image: the full band with no diarisation, retaining child voice, examiner voice and ambient sound, summarised as time-averaged MFCCs, Mel spectrogram, chromagram, spectral contrast and tonal centroid over 10-second windows. Time-averaging discards temporal structure within each window, so prosodic contour is only weakly represented - consistent with the finding that the audio model's predictive items are gestural and sensory rather than vocal.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: RGB face crops produced by a Haar cascade, with only frames in which the child's face is observable retained and the number of frames per video varying accordingly. No landmark geometry, no morphometric derivation, no body pose and no temporal sequence for the classifier. Two consequences. Cropping to the face discards the stereotypies that define the corpus, so the classifier cannot use the behaviour that identified these children as autistic in the first place - which the authors implicitly acknowledge by proposing gesture analysis as future work. And retaining only frames with a visible face introduces a selection that could differ systematically between classes, since a child spinning or flapping presents their face to a home camera less consistently than a child photographed for a curated corpus would.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Denoised thermal face images at 160x160 for the mood network, and a concatenation of learned mood output with measured skin temperature for the severity classifiers, whose dimensionality is never stated. Two representational points matter. Absolute skin temperature is only meaningful relative to ambient conditions, and no normalisation or ambient reference is applied, so the same child at the same physiological state would yield different feature values outdoors and indoors. And each image is treated as an independent observation despite 50 coming from each child, so the representation carries no notion of within-child variation - which is exactly what a continuous-monitoring framework should model and what the paper's own critique of the 15-minute ABC assessment implies it should measure.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: RGB face images at 224x224x3 with pixel values rescaled to [0, 1], augmented by 10% shear, 10% zoom and horizontal flip. No landmark geometry and no morphometric derivation, so the craniofacial constructs invoked as motivation are not represented at all, and every source-dependent property of the image is retained.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: A vector of at most twelve interpretable linguistic values per child, reduced after a first round comparing the child-alone and ratio forms of each feature. This is the most parsimonious representation in the review and is well matched to the sample: every dimension is a quantity with a published psycholinguistic literature, computed by documented rules from a public archive, so the representation is auditable end to end. Its limitation is that transcript-level aggregation discards everything about how the speech unfolded - no sequence, no timing, no prosody - so constructs such as turn-taking latency or intonation, which the wider literature associates with autistic speech, are outside its reach.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Three-dimensional joint coordinate sequences, re-expressed two ways - as Skepxel images and as angle-augmented graph sequences. The skeleton representation functions as a designed confound control of the same kind used by the Geneva pose study charted elsewhere in this review: face, expression, clothing, body habitus, room, lighting and background are all absent by construction, so a classifier operating on it cannot exploit the appearance and setting confounds that dominate the photograph branch. It also carries the privacy property the paper argues for, since joint coordinates do not identify a child by appearance. The limitation is coverage: 25 full-body joints in one corpus against 10 upper-body joints in the other, so the two experiments do not measure the same thing, and the paper's own figure contrasting the joint layouts makes this visible without drawing the inference for the 25-point performance gap.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Two representations. For the statistical analysis, Praat-derived scalar features per cry pattern - jitter as the mean absolute difference between consecutive pitch periods, shimmer as the amplitude analogue, and harmonics-to-noise ratio - each with a clinical interpretation and an established literature. For the classification, 128x128 single-channel spectrogram images per cry instance. The spectrogram representation retains time-frequency structure that the scalar perturbation measures discard, which is the right complement in principle; but because each cry instance is treated as an independent observation and roughly six come from each child, the representation also carries whatever is idiosyncratic to an individual voice, which is what an instance-level split allows the model to exploit.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: A tabular vector per respondent drawn from 21 fields, with the retained subset unspecified after a feature-engineering stage. The decisive representational fact is that both the ten AQ-10 items and their summed total appear in the enumerated field list, and no removal of the total is described.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: A per-frame vector of 1,639 values comprising a timestamp, 99 pose landmark coordinates, 63 coordinates for each hand, facial mesh coordinates, the mouth aspect ratio and per-region motion energy, formed into sequences for temporal modelling. Reducing video to landmark coordinates before any learning is a deliberate confound control of the same kind used by the pose-based studies elsewhere in this review: skin tone, clothing, background, lighting and room are all discarded, so none can drive the classification, and this is a substantive advantage over the whole-image approaches in the photograph branch. The residual exposure is facial mesh geometry, which retains craniofacial morphology and therefore retains the sex- and age-linked variation that the sample does not control.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: A 100,352-dimensional DeepFace feature vector per image. Whole-image transfer through a pretrained face model retains every source-dependent property of the photograph, and the identity-encoding character of the embedding makes the representation particularly ill-suited to a corpus split at image level with an unreported number of distinct children. No landmark geometry, morphometric measurement or temporal information is used, so no specific facial construct is operationalised.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Preprocessed face crops in one of three configurations - resize plus normalisation; resize plus normalisation plus CLAHE; resize plus normalisation plus greyscale plus CLAHE - encoded as pretrained CNN embeddings, with augmentation by zoom (1.0 to 1.2) and brightness (0.7 to 1.3). The augmentation parameters are explained rather than merely listed, which is good reporting; the concern is that zoom and brightness variants of one photograph are near-duplicates, so if augmentation preceded splitting the evaluation is compromised, and the paper does not say which order was used.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: Normalised and augmented face images, filtered to require a visible frontal face with eyes, nose and mouth. The quality filter is a genuine and unusual step for this branch, since web-scraped corpora contain profile shots, partial faces and heavy occlusion that add noise without adding signal - but it also selects a subset whose class balance is unreported, and if image quality differs systematically between two folders drawn from different online sources then the filter itself could shift the composition.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: Resized and normalised face images augmented by rotation, flipping and contrast adjustment. Contrast adjustment is worth noting because it partially normalises a property that would differ systematically between image sources; whether it is sufficient to remove a source signal is untested, and no source-wise analysis is performed.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: A 16-element tabular vector per gaze sample: trial and stimulus identifiers, Tracking_Ratio, Point_of_Regard right/left X and Y, six gaze-vector components, Category_Right, Category_Left, #Stimulus, and CARS_Score. Min-max scaled to [0,1], reshaped to (1,16). Two of these deserve separate note. CARS_Score is a clinician-administered autism severity instrument: within this dataset it is effectively a monotone function of the label, so its inclusion is direct target leakage and by itself can account for a near-perfect result. Tracking_Ratio is a signal-quality index that plausibly differs systematically between groups for reasons of compliance rather than social attention. Stimulus and trial identifiers encode session structure.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: A nine-field tabular row per child: five binary Q-CHAT items plus age in months, binary sex, binary jaundice and binary family history. The feature-selection step is the analytically decisive move and it runs in an unexpected direction. Items A1, A2, A6, A8 and A9 were removed because they correlated highly with the Q-CHAT-10 score - but the Q-CHAT-10 score is the sum of exactly those items, so high correlation is arithmetic necessity, not redundancy. Deleting them does not remove noise; it removes half of the summands that define the label. The reported 0.83 is thus an estimate of how well five items reconstruct the threshold on all ten, which is why this study lands in the low 80s while local_8253c2ec and local_a0d73248, which retained all items, reach 100%.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: Nominally a 3D landmark graph; actually a 2D landmark configuration from Dlib applied to 224x224 web photographs, with rotation and scaling augmentation. The depth channel that the entire introduction argues is essential does not exist in the data. This mismatch propagates into the results: the reported landmark localisation error falling from 2.5 mm at 100 epochs to 0.9 mm at 500 epochs is a physical measurement that no part of the input can support, since the images have neither metric calibration nor ground-truth 3D landmark positions.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Two representations. (i) Variable-length scanpath sequences over four features - x, y, fixation duration d, velocity v - padded to maximum length with a masking mechanism, evaluated in four combinations. (ii) 4,000 cropped eye images at 416x416, fifty frames per child times left and right eye, each labelled with subject ID, frame number, severity band and eye side. The image-level representation is what the 70:15:15 split partitions, and it is where the validity problem originates: with a fixed 100 images per child, the split cannot separate participants even in principle.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: Gabor-filtered RGB face crops at an unstated resolution, passed through MTCNN detection, median denoising and Z-score channel normalisation, then encoded as MobileNetV2 features. Augmentation adds rotation, horizontal flip, cropping and brightness variation, described as a preprocessing stage rather than as a training-time operation. Class weighting is applied on the stated grounds of imbalance, although the source Kaggle corpus is balanced by construction and the paper's own confusion matrices imply near-equal class sizes.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Tabular vectors of 120 kinematic or 48 behavioural/eye features per instructional segment, organised into four named subsets (K_General, K_Attention, L_General, L_Attention). Preprocessing includes one step that deserves separate note: missing values and anomalies were replaced with the mean value of each respective class - imputation conditioned on the outcome label, computed over the whole dataset before any split. Where a feature has missing values at different rates in the two groups, that step writes the label into the feature matrix directly, and it is a sufficient mechanism to produce a nine-of-nine result on its own.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: 224x224 RGB face crops at 1:1 aspect ratio, rescaled to [0,1], with training-time augmentation by rotation to 20 degrees, width and height shifts to 0.2, shear 0.2, zoom 0.2 and horizontal flip. Noise removal and contrast enhancement are mentioned without method. The conclusion treats the 1:1 ratio and 224x224 size as the study's principal finding, which places a preprocessing convention where an empirical result should be.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: A tabular row per toddler: ten binary Q-CHAT-10 items plus sex, ethnicity, jaundice, family history, region, respondent and age, label-encoded and min-max scaled. Two features of this representation matter. First, the ten items are the constituents of the Q-CHAT-10 score whose threshold defines the label, so the predictor set arithmetically determines the outcome - the same structure as local_8253c2ec and local_a0d73248 (which reach 100% on six metrics) and the inverse of local_8ff20c48 (which deleted five of the ten items and consequently fell to 0.83). Second, ethnicity and region are nominal categories converted to ordered integers by label encoding, imposing an artificial ordering that the paper does not remark on.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Tabular rows of ten binary Q-CHAT-10 items plus demographic and history fields, SMOTE-augmented and feature-selected. The ten items are the constituents of the Q-CHAT-10 total whose threshold defines the Phase I label and whose bands define the Phase II label, so in both phases the predictor set arithmetically determines the outcome.
