Rather than presenting an attention heatmap and asserting that it looks sensible, the authors used the soft attention weights as a testable hypothesis about mechanism: they plotted the alpha values across all 300 frames for every clip and then checked each plot against the corresponding video to see whether a rise coincided with a specific social gesture. The finding is stated with appropriate precision - for typically developing children a distinct rise to at least twice baseline was 'invariably noted' somewhere in the sequence, though its onset and duration varied between children, while for autistic children attention weights 'did not change significantly throughout the duration of the video clip'. Crucially both directions are checked: every attention peak in a typically developing child coincided with an observed IJA behaviour, and across the whole dataset fewer than 1% of autistic children showed both an IJA behaviour and a corresponding peak. That establishes correspondence rather than mere plausibility, and it means the model's decision can be traced to the occurrence or non-occurrence of the clinically defined behaviour the protocol was designed to elicit - which is exactly the claim most deep-learning studies in this corpus make without evidence. The illustrative figure showing frames 80, 140, 180 and 240 for one child from each group makes the mechanism concrete. What is not done: attention is temporal only, with no spatial attribution showing which part of the frame is used, so it cannot be verified that the model is watching the child rather than the contingently responding examiner.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Interpretability is strongest for EEG and absent for the behavioural modalities. The EEG t-test table is complete - all 30 region-band combinations with F, t, p, mean difference and standard error - and the directions and interpretations are given: theta power significantly higher in the autistic group in five of six regions with the largest effect at left frontal (t = 5.82), and interpretations offered for each band ('theta waves mainly reflect the emotional experience of individuals', 'the low-beta band is related to the capacity for concentration', gamma 'related to the abilities of learning, memory, and information processing'). Those band-to-function attributions are loose and would not survive scrutiny in the EEG literature, but the underlying statistics are fully reported and the theta finding is placed in the context of prior work. For gaze and facial expression there is nothing: no group means, no directions, no effect sizes, no indication of which clusters or which time windows differ. This asymmetry follows from the representations - clusters and frame counts have no semantic content to report - and it means the study, despite recording two behavioural modalities, contributes no behavioural finding beyond classification accuracy. The confusion-graph analysis is a genuine interpretability contribution at modality level, showing exactly which class each modality handles and which it fails.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: None, and none is possible. There is no feature importance, attribution, saliency map or ablation, and the representation - individual pixels of a 28x28 downsampled plot - admits no behavioural interpretation even if attribution were computed. The paper offers no group difference, no effect direction and no descriptive statistic about gaze. Its one interpretive sentence, that 'the amount of information in the images and the use of space in the x and y coordinates are essential factors when classifying ASD', is a statement about how much of the frame the trace fills. Placed against the rest of this corpus, that is a meaningful observation in an unintended way: it is consistent with the classifier keying on trace density, which is a property of how much usable gaze data the tracker captured, and hence potentially on data quality rather than on viewing behaviour - the pattern seen in Li 2020's SHAP quality feature, Fang 2021's untracked-gaze 'area0' and Zhao 2021's differential OpenFace failure rates.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Interpretability is pursued through study design rather than through model attribution, and is stronger for it. Four analyses jointly characterise what the gaze data contain. The effect-size profile across areas of interest, with bootstrap confidence intervals in both episodes, shows where the group differences lie and that they replicate. The reference-heatmap comparison establishes that the autistic and control group averages are nearly identical (r = 0.966) while individual autistic participants depart from both - which localises the phenomenon at the individual rather than group level. The fingerprinting analysis quantifies how much individually distinctive information the same features carry, and the four-versus-eight-feature comparison shows the information is distributed rather than concentrated. And the per-participant classification and clustering frequencies show which individuals the group-level model can and cannot place. The authors summarise the feature-level picture honestly as 'a rather distributed effect over heatmaps and facial features, with no single feature driving the effect', and note the caveat that their features were intercorrelated and their videos always contained people. The absence of a correlation between any gaze feature and ADOS severity is also reported, and is an important negative: the measures separate groups on average without indexing individual severity.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: None. No feature importance, attribution, saliency, spectral analysis or group comparison of any acoustic quantity is reported, and no interpretation is offered of what distinguishes the classes. This is a substantial gap given that the paper's entire motivation is a specific set of prosodic claims - echolalia, monotonous intonation, atypical pitch, irregular stress - none of which is tested, measured or discussed after the introduction. The random forest's feature set would have supported at least a permutation-importance analysis at no cost, and mel spectrograms admit standard saliency methods. The consequence is that the study yields three accuracy figures and no knowledge about autistic children's speech, so it cannot be evaluated for construct validity: there is no way to tell whether the models are keying on prosody, on vocal-tract size, on recording distance, or on utterance length. The authors do gesture at interpretability as a future goal, proposing that combining audio features with computer-vision measures 'could possibly result in interpretable models', which acknowledges the present absence.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Interpretability is built into the design rather than added afterwards, and it operates at three levels. The features are individually meaningful by construction - mean length of utterance, filled-pause ratio, disfluency proportion, F0, shimmer, loudness - so any model weight is directly interpretable, in contrast to the learned representations used by the deep-learning speech studies elsewhere in this corpus. mSVM-RFE ranks them and identifies an optimal eight, evenly split between modalities, though the selection is honestly reported as producing no significant gain. And the misclassification analysis functions as the deepest interpretive layer, answering not 'which features matter' but 'which children does this measure see', which is the question that determines clinical utility. Its findings are specific and consequential: the language model is biased toward younger children with poorer language and less output; the voice model is unbiased with respect to language level; the residual misses have the highest IQ and most language output; and neither ADOS severity nor IQ predicts misclassification in any model - from which the authors draw the appropriately hedged conclusion that 'if replicated, this result could confirm that our voice and language measurement methodology specifically taps aspects of communication skills that are not confounded by autism severity or developmental delay'.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Interpretability is pursued through the design of the measures rather than through model attribution, and the analysis that carries most weight is the within-group contrast. Because the measures are three physically meaningful quantities, the finding can be stated directly in behavioural terms. The decisive analysis compares social against nonsocial movies within each group: neurotypical toddlers moved more, faster and less predictably during social content (r = 0.47, 0.62, 0.51), while autistic toddlers showed no content-dependent difference at all. That single contrast does three things a between-group difference cannot. It shows the effect is not simply 'autistic children move more' but that neurotypical children modulate movement by content and autistic children do not. It adjudicates directly against Martin and colleagues' published interpretation that increased head movement in autism serves to modulate perception of social stimuli, since on that account the difference should be confined to social content, and here it is not. And it rules out the reading that the measure indexes social engagement, since the group difference persists for nonsocial content. The paper then engages seriously with alternative mechanisms - general sensory modulation, postural control under multisensory demand, a regulatory function analogous to repetitive behaviour - rather than settling on one. The Mullen correlation analysis is the interpretively weakest element and contains an internal contradiction: the Results report positive correlations between Early Learning Composite and all three movement measures during social movies (r = .36, .39, .34), implying higher cognitive ability accompanied more movement, while the Discussion asserts that 'autistic children with lower cognitive abilities showed higher levels of head movement rate, acceleration, and complexity' and builds an interpretation on that reading.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: No feature-level interpretability, and none is possible given principal components of 8,640-dimensional envelope representations - the paper reports no group means, no effect sizes and no directional statements. What it provides instead is interpretability at the level of theoretical construct, which is the level its question operates at. The rhythm-versus-intonation contrast is itself the interpretive result, and the authors connect it to the existing descriptive literature ('the ML algorithms identified in this study appeared to capture patterns from acoustic features that were representative of these prosodic characteristics, paralleling such descriptive observations by clinicians and researchers') and to prior objective measures of speech rate, lexical stress and cross-syllabic durational variability. The Cantonese intonation failure is then given a mechanistic account grounded in phonology - pitch carries lexical meaning in tone languages, so f0 is under phonological constraint - and used to reconcile conflicting prior findings across English, Thai and Japanese. That is a stronger form of interpretation than a feature-importance ranking would have provided, because it generates a testable prediction: intonational differences in autism should be attenuated in tone-language speakers generally. The one interpretive overreach is the ASPM allele speculation, which substitutes a population-genetic explanation for a linguistic one that the paper has already established.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: None, and the authors treat this as the study's principal scientific shortcoming rather than a minor gap: 'Neural network encoders followed by classifiers can take into account a wide variety of utterance characteristics but does not help to identify which particular aspects of language are crucial.' They frame the remedy as a route to discovery rather than to trust, proposing LIME-style word-level attribution so that 'giving meaning to collections of important words may lead to discovering new dimensions of language relevant to ASD', and connecting it to their own prior work identifying sentiment and language abstraction as relevant dimensions - while noting 'it is very likely that this list is not exhaustive'. That framing is correct: for a study whose motivating literature is entirely about specific narrative constructs (coherence, causal connection, referential devices, internal state language), a classifier that cannot say which of these it is using contributes no linguistic knowledge. The one indirect interpretive finding is that skipped pages carry signal, inferred from zero-vector representation outperforming masking.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Interpretability is pursued at two levels and both are useful. At feature level, the selections of all three algorithms are tabulated feature by feature and area by area for both datasets, with agreement across algorithms used as the criterion for calling a feature discriminative - a more conservative approach than trusting any single ranking. The resulting claim is specific and checkable: net dwell time, diversion duration and first fixation duration on the social area were selected by all three algorithms in both stimulus sets. The authors then situate this against their own published systematic review of eye-tracking features in autism, noting that fixation count, fixation time, average fixation duration and dwell time dominate the literature while diversion duration is essentially absent - so the finding is that the field's default feature set may not contain its most discriminative member. At model level, the decision tree is reproduced with its thresholds and its traversal explained in clinical terms, presented as a transparency argument rather than a performance one. What is absent is any link between model output and clinical characteristics: no severity measure was collected, so the authors' own proposal to examine the symptom profiles of false negatives cannot be executed on these data.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Interpretability is inherent in the design rather than added afterwards, since each feature is a named percentage on a named region and every group difference is reported with its direction and effect size. The per-area classification analysis then functions as a formal importance ranking, tested against permutation rather than asserted, and the finding that the rankings differ substantially between cohorts is the study's central claim. The eye-area result is the clearest example and is properly interpreted: comparison children's eye-looking rises from 17.6% at toddler age to 29.2% at preschool age while autistic children's stays flat at 15.4% and 15.1%, so the group difference emerges developmentally rather than being present from the outset. The authors offer a mechanistic account - that toddlers with typical development use visual mouth information for language acquisition, reducing eye attention, and that as language becomes more auditorily meaningful preschool attention shifts to the eyes - which is testable and which explains both the mouth and eye interactions coherently. Against this, the paper offers no interpretation at all of the finding that fixation is reduced on non-social areas, which is the observation most in tension with the social-attention framing it works within.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: No feature-level interpretability, and the algorithm and code are proprietary - so at the level of mechanism the Device is opaque. What the paper offers instead is case-level interpretability, and it is more clinically useful than a feature ranking would be. The indeterminate group is characterised diagnostically: 91.0% had at least one neurodevelopmental disorder, 71.0% were autism-negative with another condition, 20.0% were autism-positive and 9.0% had no developmental diagnosis - so the abstentions concentrate on the genuinely ambiguous rather than falling randomly. Output is cross-tabulated against DSM-5 severity, showing a clear gradient from 44 of 65 Level 3 children classified positive to 1 of 5 Level 1 children. Output is cross-tabulated against every comorbidity, showing for example that phonological disorder yields abstention 82.4% of the time. And specialist certainty is compared between cases the Device classified and cases it declined - 71% versus 64% completely certain, p = 0.40 - testing whether the Device abstains where clinicians are also uncertain, and finding no significant difference. Taken together these establish what the Device is doing at the level a clinician needs, even though they say nothing about how.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: The strongest part of the paper, and the reason it is worth charting despite its data problems. Every one of the 16 selected features is reported with group means, standard deviations, outlier counts and exact p-values, and then discussed individually against named prior work - with contradictory findings reported rather than suppressed. The pitch literature is described as containing 'opposite findings'; a proposed link between pitch excursions and 'motherese' speech is cited and then noted to have been 'disprove[n]' by later work; the loudness literature is enumerated as containing higher values, lower values, null results, and studies that avoided intensity entirely 'to avoid the risk of obtaining unclear results'; and the spectral findings are flagged as lacking comparators, with the authors stating plainly that 'we did not find any other relevant studies to confirm the importance of spectral features to detect ASD'. The jitter-shimmer-HNR discussion is the most substantive, correctly identifying the expected inverse relationship between jitter and harmonics-to-noise ratio, verifying it in their own data, and connecting it to the voice-pathology literature on breathiness and hoarseness. The interpretive irony is that this same literature supplies the reason to doubt the finding: harmonics-to-noise ratio is a signal-to-noise measure, and the two groups' signals were acquired through different chains.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: None, and none is possible. There is no feature importance, attribution, saliency or ablation, and the representation - texture codes over a segmented, morphologically cleaned rendering of a gaze trace - admits no behavioural interpretation even in principle. No group means, effect sizes, directions or descriptive statistics about viewing behaviour appear anywhere. The paper therefore contributes six accuracy figures and no knowledge about autism, gaze or visual attention, despite an introduction devoting several pages to social orientation, attention biomarkers and the clinical significance of atypical visual attention. That disconnection between the stated motivation and the delivered content is the study's defining characteristic.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Interpretability is pursued through the design of the analysis rather than through model attribution, and the outcome is honest about its own limits. The two group-comparison analyses are fully interpretable in their own terms - which regions, which transitions, what percentages - and the graph representation adds a sequential dimension that a fixation profile alone would miss. The reported effect is concrete: 13% of comparison children's gaze shifts occur between two adjacent central regions against 9.4% for autistic children. What is missing, and is conceded, is the mapping from those regions to anything in the world. Because the phone moves with the parent's head, region BC is a direction relative to a moving camera, not the parent's eyes or mouth, so the finding cannot be connected to eye contact, mouth-looking, or the Pelphrey and Chawarska results the introduction builds on. The LSTM receives no attribution analysis at all. The net position is that the study establishes a difference exists without being able to characterise it, and says so.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: No feature-level interpretability of any kind, and none possible given that the features are principal components of pixel arrays or convolutional activations over a rendered plot. No group means, effect sizes, directions or descriptive statistics about gaze appear anywhere. What the paper offers instead is interpretability at the level of experimental design: by running the same model across three data conditions it makes visible what each condition contributes, which is a more useful form of insight for this review than a saliency map would be. The discussion also contains speculation not supported by anything done here - that 'by leveraging the capabilities of complex CNN-based algorithms, ML models could quantify heterogeneities in ASD symptoms, allowing for accurate ASD severity grading using ET data' - which is notable because the source dataset contains CARS-based severity labels that would have permitted a direct test.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: The most thorough feature-importance analysis in the corpus relative to the size of the study. Importances are extracted from the best model at each of the 28 cross-validation iterations for each of the four classifier families and displayed as per-iteration heatmaps, so stability across folds is directly visible rather than asserted from a single fit. The two feature families are then compared statistically, yielding a large and significant separation (t = 5.15, p = 1e-5), and importances are aggregated by emotion category to give an interpretable ranking. The finding that disgust prompts carry the most importance, followed by surprise and sadness, is then connected to independent evidence that 'younger children are worse at discriminating facial expressions of disgust and surprise when images of these expressions are presented alongside specific other emotions', suggesting these emotions require more cognitive development to process - a mechanistic account that generates a testable prediction rather than a post hoc rationalisation. The authors immediately temper it, warning against 'an oversimplified understanding of these features'. The one weakness is that no direction of effect is reported: it is not stated whether autistic children took longer or shorter on disgust prompts, so the finding is that the feature discriminates without saying how.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: None. No feature importance, attribution, group comparison, effect size or acoustic characterisation appears anywhere, and Method 1's representation admits none in principle - an unmixing-matrix coefficient at frequency point k has no interpretation as a property of a child's voice. The one interpretive claim offered is theoretical rather than empirical: that because autistic speech is modelled as neurotypical speech convolved with dysfunction filters, 'the unmixing matrix can be regarded as the inverse matrix of these filter banks', so extracting it 'is equivalent to extracting the inherent distinguishing features representing the vocal system of both, reflecting the essential distinctions between the two types of children's speech'. This is an argument from the assumed generative model to the meaning of the features, not evidence that the features mean what is claimed, and it is not tested. Method 3, using standard cepstral features, would have supported conventional acoustic interpretation and none is attempted.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: No feature-level interpretability: the 48 features are not individually reported, no importance analysis is performed, and no acoustic characterisation of severity is offered, so the study contributes a prediction system rather than a finding about how autistic children's speech varies with symptom level. The interpretability that is present operates at the level of the pipeline. The three-way segmentation comparison establishes which stage contributes what, and the finding that automatic diarization outperforms manual annotation is given a mechanistic account grounded in the recording conditions. The dissociation between x-vectors' better segment accuracy and their worse severity estimate is reported without explanation, but it is reported, and it is the kind of intermediate-versus-final metric divergence that a paper optimising only for diarization performance would never have surfaced.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Complete, because nothing is opaque. Every measurement is a named behaviour scored against a definition published in an appendix, so any result can be traced to an observable event and independently re-scored - which is precisely what the six-rater reliability analysis does. The conclusion states the intended use in human terms: 'If a specialist has a sense of how a typical child plays with NAO, then they will be able to see possible deficits in the turn-taking of a child with autism by observing him/her.' That formulation is worth recording for the review because it describes an alternative to automation that most of this corpus does not consider - a standardised elicitation device that improves a clinician's calibration, rather than a model that replaces the clinician's judgement.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Good by the standards of this corpus, and honest about the limits of its own interpretation. Forward feature selection produces an explicit ranking, and Table 3 shows the striking result that a single feature - entropy of gaze allocation in the x-y plane - achieves the maximum 74.15% and that adding any of the other five slightly reduces accuracy. Table 2 gives group means, SDs and t-tests for all six features at all ten window lengths, letting a reader see that entropy separates the groups at every scale while range does not beyond 4 s. The discussion then supplies a mechanistic account rather than a post-hoc story: higher entropy in the ASD group follows from gaze being distributed more evenly between social and irrelevant regions instead of concentrating on face and body, referencing the authors' own fixation analysis of the same children. And they close by conceding the interpretive cost - 'the atypical oculomotor performance in the children with ASD was inseparable from visual attention in our study' - which is a rare admission that a paper's headline construct is confounded with the one it set out to distinguish itself from. The model is not interrogated at the individual level: no per-child probabilities, no error analysis, no examination of which five children were misclassified.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Good, and grounded in physics rather than post-hoc attribution. Every feature is a named, humanly meaningful quantity, and the four play states are defined by an explicit and checkable sensor logic: encoder moving with accelerometer static means wheel spinning; accelerometer moving with encoder static means the car is airborne; both moving means floor play; neither means no play. The selected 10 features are listed individually so a reader can see exactly what the model uses, and the three encoder features that survived - wheels-only ratio, not-playing ratio, total wheel turn rate - map directly onto the behavioural hypothesis that motivated the hardware change. The mechanism itself came from observation of children playing with version 1, not from a literature-driven guess, which is a legitimate and transparent route to a feature. What is absent is any quantitative feature-level analysis: no group means or effect sizes for the wheels-only ratio or any other feature, no statistical test that autistic children actually spin the wheels more, no feature importances or coefficients, and no error analysis. So the paper can say which features the classifier used but cannot say by how much the groups differ on them, which is why the not-playing-ratio confound cannot be assessed from the reported results.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: The best interpretability work in this corpus, and it is not an add-on but the paper's purpose. Three techniques are layered. First, the latent space is made analytically tractable by construction: the VAE's KL term drives it towards a diagonal Gaussian, so two-dimensional class-conditional Gaussians can be fitted to the ASD and TD point clouds and a genuine probability density function evaluated for any point rather than a black-box score. Second, feature influence is measured causally within the model rather than by correlation: for each participant, each of the 12 features is resampled 100 times from a Gaussian while the other 11 are held fixed, and the resulting displacement of that participant's latent projection is tracked, identifying not only which features move a subject but at which values the class assignment flips. Figure 5 aggregates this into per-feature density maps over the latent space and Figure 6 into class-probability curves against raw feature values. Third, the outputs are expressed in clinically usable form: signed, feature-specific rules (higher MaxAcceleration and sdAcceleration, lower MaxSpeed and MinAcceleration increase ASD probability) explicitly offered as candidate threshold values for joint use by clinicians. The design also embeds an interpretability-motivated safety property, replacing the predictor with density evaluation at inference so a participant in an unpopulated region is not confidently misassigned. The caveats are that no uncertainty is attached to any of these feature effects, no group-level statistics on the features themselves are reported (the earlier descriptive paper failed to find significant differences, which is the stated motivation for this analysis), and the whole latent geometry was learned on data containing the test observations, so the thresholds are in-sample.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Fully interpretable by construction, and this is the study's clearest methodological strength. Every judgement reduces to two physically meaningful quantities - degrees of shoulder rotation relative to the child's posture when their name was called, and degrees of head yaw - together with counts of how many of the 75 frames satisfied a stated threshold. Figures 6 and 7 plot both series for worked examples against their thresholds, so a clinician or auditor can replay any decision frame by frame against the video and see exactly why it came out as it did. The design rationale is also explained in behavioural terms rather than defended by performance: shoulder rotation alone fails in two named directions, missing responsive children who turn only the head and falsely flagging unresponsive children who shift slightly while playing with toys, and head pose is introduced specifically to adjudicate that band. Even the duration constant is argued from evidence rather than tuned, being derived from the observation that gaze fixation during concentration lasts at least 0.2 s and then doubled to 0.4 s to allow for timing error in children's rotation. Three interpretability limits remain. Nothing quantifies how close a judgement was to its threshold, so no case can be surfaced as borderline. The perception layer beneath the rule is entirely opaque and unevaluated on this population, so a wrong answer caused by a tracking identity switch would look identical to one caused by a genuine behavioural boundary case. And eye contact, which the clinical definition requires, is never measured - head direction stands in for gaze on an assumption stated but not tested.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Limited but honest. The features are individually meaningful - counts and durations of looking at specified places - and the region diagram makes each one concrete. The four-subset comparison functions as a coarse importance analysis, showing that the full set outperforms either the figure regions or their surroundings alone, and the paper's interpretation of this is straightforward and reasonable: more regions provide more detail. A single-child worked example traces the fixation points and times for one trial and shows the child concentrating on the target and the matching candidate before answering correctly, which usefully demonstrates that the raw data are behaviourally interpretable. Against this, no group-level feature analysis is reported at all - no means, no distributions, no effect sizes, no statistical comparison of where the two groups looked - so the paper never states, and cannot state, what visual behaviour distinguishes autistic from comparison children in its own data. It reports only that a network reached a certain accuracy. For a study whose stated purpose is to support specialist decision-making, the absence of any description of the discriminative behaviour is a substantive gap: a clinician can act on 'autistic children fixated less on the reference face' but not on 'an unspecified MLP scored 73.8% pooled across partitions'.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: Interpretability is treated as a design constraint rather than a post-hoc report, and the study is the clearest example in this corpus of a modelling choice being made to preserve semantic traceability. The authors note that the 3DI method's PCA expression basis 'limits the interpretability as PCA components are not localized - we cannot associate any PCA component with a specific facial region', and therefore rebuild the basis with 60 localised components before any modelling occurs. The linear SVM then makes weights directly readable. The importance analysis is done at two levels and, critically, against the right baseline: individual top-10 features are named, and the four anatomical categories are compared with their proportion of the full 6,272-feature pool, so the conclusion that mouth features matter is not an artefact of there being many mouth features (25.5% of the pool, 40% of the top 10) and the pose finding is stronger than it looks (5.3% of the pool, 13.3% of the top 10). Findings are then related to independent literature on blinking, nodding, social orienting and backchannel feedback rather than left as bare weights. The authors are equally explicit about the ceiling: they cannot distinguish upper lip from mouth corner, a fuller account would require 3D versions of localised bases, and 'further analysis to uncover why these features are important is beyond the scope of this study'. Finally, the discussion argues that interpretability is a precondition for the assistive use case the paper proposes - a clinician cannot rationally weigh a dissenting AI opinion without knowing which behaviours produced it - which correctly makes explanation a functional requirement rather than a courtesy.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: The paper does substantial interpretive work, but almost none of it is attribution on the trained model. Three strands. First, an extensive pre-modelling descriptive analysis with low-level and semantic gaze features, region-of-interest labelling, first-fixation timing and object-category breakdowns, which establishes the expected group differences and then concludes candidly that they are 'not sufficiently significant to directly use these hand-crafted features for classification' - an honest admission that the interpretable features do not do the work. Second, and most distinctive, a quantitative analysis of separability itself using time-delay embedding to compute Hausdorff and mean-minimal distances, showing how between-group distance and within-group variability change as a function of how much temporal context and how many stimuli are used. The finding that with pattern sections shorter than five fixations the within-autism variability exceeds the between-group difference is a genuinely useful result about the structure of the problem, and it turns the paper's architectural choices into consequences of measurement rather than assertions. Third, qualitative inspection of model scores, from which three drivers are named: whether the pattern stays on the image or drifts to the grey mask, whether fixations on salient objects are missing, and whether fixation order and duration are reasonable - each illustrated with worked successful and failed cases against the two baselines. The gap is that no attribution method is applied to the LSTM: there is no saliency analysis, no gate inspection, no per-fixation contribution, and no way to say for an individual child which of their 82 patterns or which fixations produced their score. For a system proposed as an aid to non-specialists in remote clinics, per-child explanation is exactly what would be needed, and the paper's own emphasis on an 'AI-marker' makes its absence more noticeable.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: None. No feature importance for the tree-based models, despite decision trees and XGBoost both supporting it natively and both having been fitted; no attention or probing analysis for BERT; no error analysis; no inspection of misclassified examples; no lexical comparison between the two corpora; no topic modelling. The paper's entire interpretive content is the observation that BERT 'utilizes neural networks to recognize intricate patterns within the input data' and that this 'demonstrates the potential of deep learning models to extract relevant patterns'. The absence is not merely a missed opportunity but the reason the study's central claim cannot be assessed: the difference between a classifier that has learned something about autistic communication and one that has learned that certain accounts discuss autism, or that has memorised 31 people's writing styles, would be visible in even a cursory look at the most predictive tokens, and no such look is reported.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Interpretability is structural rather than added afterwards, because the feature is a single quantity with a stated physical meaning. The paper explains precisely what integrated entropy measures and, importantly, what it does not: not amplitude, not variability, not frequency, but predictability, with the specific consequence that both a highly periodic large-excursion signal and a nearly stable small-excursion signal yield low entropy. That distinction is then tested rather than asserted, through the weak correlation (0.2-0.42) between integrated entropy and landmark variation, and through ANCOVA adjustment for variation as a covariate. Region selection was hypothesis-driven and prespecified with citations, so the analysis is confirmatory rather than exploratory in its choice of features. The social/non-social contrast functions as an interpretive control, showing that the effect is amplified by social content but present without it. The redundancy analysis against affect is itself an interpretability exercise - establishing that the measure is not simply detecting smiles. And the substantive interpretation offered is clearly labelled as speculation and is symmetrical rather than deficit-framed. What is missing is individual-level explanation: no error analysis, no examination of which children were misclassified, and no link between entropy and ADOS-T severity, which would have been the strongest available evidence that the measure tracks the construct it claims to index.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Interpretability is built into the aggregation design and is then cross-checked against independent evidence, which is the part that distinguishes it. The random forest that weights the 21 or 32 per-image decisions yields an importance per stimulus, averaged over cross-validation folds, and a table maps each face number to its emotion so the importances can be read semantically. The authors then test each importance ranking against the separate statistical analysis. For autistic adults the two highest-weighted images are neutral faces, and the statistics independently show all three gaze features differing significantly on neutral trials - a convergence the authors relate to documented difficulty with subtle expressions, since neutral is the least prototypical stimulus in the set. For autistic children the highest weights fall on surprise and two anger images, and anger is the single emotion showing a significant gaze difference in that dataset. For schizophrenia the top-weighted images are disgust and anger, and here the authors decline to interpret: 'we do not think that feature importance has any particular significance', because the statistics show eye-region fixation differing for every emotion, so no image is distinctive and the ranking is noise. Refusing to build a story around an importance ranking that the underlying statistics do not support is a discipline absent elsewhere in this corpus, and it makes the two interpretations that are offered more credible. The error analysis adds a second layer of interpretability at the individual level, identifying the specific participants the models could not classify and diagnosing why.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: Essentially absent at the model level and moderately good at the data level. No feature importance, saliency, attention, latent-space inspection, error analysis or example-level examination is performed for any classifier, so the paper cannot say what distinguishes autistic from non-autistic usage patterns - only that a stacked autoencoder can tell them apart 82% of the time on a largely pseudo-labelled corpus. This is a particularly costly gap because the alternative explanation is so readily available: with a comparison group dominated by acquired adult-onset conditions and an autism group dominated by young children, the most parsimonious account of the classification is age, and a single look at what the model responds to would have addressed it. What interpretive content exists is descriptive and is genuinely useful for understanding AAC use: usage frequency and duration by age band, average time in app by diagnostic category, the top 14 phrases across the corpus, and unique-word counts by diagnosis showing autistic and stroke users producing considerably more distinct vocabulary than other groups. The pseudo-semantic identifier scheme is designed to make the numeric encoding interpretable, and the rejection of spatial modelling is well argued - but neither is followed through into any analysis of what the models learned.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: The most thorough interpretability work in this review, and unusually it is used to verify the model's reasoning against an independent clinical account rather than to generate a post-hoc narrative. Three techniques operate in sequence. Attention weights across the frame sequence identify which time points drove the decision, plotted per participant. Grad-CAM is then applied specifically at those attention peaks, localising the spatially informative regions within the frames that mattered - so the spatial and temporal explanations are coupled rather than independent. Agglomerative hierarchical clustering of attention-weight trajectories across the test set, displayed as dendrograms with participant identifiers alongside the heatmaps, tests whether the model's temporal decision patterns cluster by class at the dataset level rather than only in selected examples. The results are behaviourally specific and, crucially, match the constructs the tasks were designed to elicit: triadic gaze shifting in IJA, sustained versus fleeting gaze on the indicated object in low-level RJA, and immediate turning with a return to the examiner in high-level RJA. The authors' claim that the system 'made predictions based on salient behavioral differences... in the same way trained specialists diagnose ASD' is therefore supported by evidence rather than asserted. The cluster maps also corroborate the quantitative severity finding independently, showing IJA separating the three severity classes more cleanly than the RJA tasks. Two limits remain. Grad-CAM and attention illustrations are presented for selected participants and time points, so they demonstrate that the model can attend to the right things without establishing that it always does. And no quantitative test rules out appearance, background or site confounds, which an end-to-end model on raw frames from differently recruited groups is exposed to.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: None. No class activation mapping, saliency analysis, feature visualisation, error analysis or inspection of misclassified images is reported for any of the three models. The methods section instead provides several paragraphs of general exposition on how convolutional layers, pooling variants and InceptionV3's factorisation techniques work - accurate but generic. The absence is more consequential here than in studies that model interpretable features, because the input is a picture of a behaviour rather than the behaviour itself, so there is a genuine open question about whether the models respond to where the gaze went or to incidental graphical properties such as ink density, plotted extent or line crossing count. A single class activation map over a handful of correctly and incorrectly classified scanpaths would have addressed it directly and would have been the most informative addition the paper could have made.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: The study's strongest dimension, and interpretability is treated as the objective rather than as a diagnostic afterthought. Three layers support it. The feature set is specified against ADOS, so every measure has a clinical referent and the model's inputs are quantities a clinician would recognise - echolalia, discourse coherence, initiative in asking questions, vocabulary extent - rather than embeddings or spectral coefficients. The feature-family ablation quantifies what each level of linguistic description contributes, which is itself an interpretive result: semantic-pragmatic features alone reach 82.3%, matching part-of-speech features, and the families combine additively to 94.1%. And SHAP attribution identifies which individual features drive predictions, with the findings then checked against independent literature rather than asserted - the number of distinct word roots emerges as the largest contributor and is linked to prior work on vocabulary extent in autistic children, while the prominence of unexpected words and of both discourse-coherence measures is connected to evidence that autistic children show reduced global coherence in conversation. The authors' claim that these features are 'coherent and understandable to non-experts as well' is defensible. Two limits: no error analysis or per-child examination is performed, and no check is made on whether the top features differ systematically across the three source corpora - which, given that one corpus supplies only autistic children, is the analysis that would distinguish a linguistic finding from a corpus artefact.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: No model interpretability whatsoever - no saliency, class activation, filter visualisation or error analysis is applied to either network, so the study cannot say what feature of a scan-path image produces a prediction. Its interpretive work is entirely at the input level and is systematic: individual video clips are removed one at a time and the models retrained, ranking each clip's contribution and showing that Theory of Mind and Dyadic Bid clips matter most while one Social Referencing clip matters least; scan-paths are restricted to successive temporal windows to locate when in a trial the discriminative information lies; and velocity encoding is added and removed to test whether dynamics contribute beyond position. These ablations yield findings a clinician could act on - that the first three seconds carry the most signal, that certain stimulus types are more informative than others - and are more useful than a saliency map would have been for stimulus design. But they say nothing about whether the network is responding to where the child looked or to how much of the canvas the drawing covers, which is the question a scan-path-image method most needs to answer.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: None. No saliency map, class activation, filter visualisation, error analysis or example inspection is performed for any model. The discussion's account of why the proposed model outperforms the alternatives is entirely generic and borrowed from the image-processing literature - that convolutional networks are 'successfully used for image denoising' and that convolution 'reduces the high dimensionality of images without losing its information' - with no reference to anything observed in these scan-paths. The absence is compounded by the flattening step, which means the model is not exploiting spatial structure in the way that explanation assumes. For a study whose entire input is a picture of a behaviour, and where incidental graphical properties are as available to the network as behavioural ones, a single class activation map over correctly and incorrectly classified scan-paths would have been the most informative addition possible.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: SHAP attribution applied within each of the three folds, with fold-to-fold stability quantified explicitly - 15 of 24 unique top-20 features appeared in all three folds, 6 in two and 3 in one. Reporting the stability of an importance ranking across resamples, rather than presenting a single ranking as though it were a property of the data, is a discipline almost absent from this corpus and it materially changes how much weight the ranking can bear. The seven milestone predictors surfaced by SHAP were then tested independently with Fisher's exact tests, all significant at p < 0.001, so the attribution is corroborated by conventional statistics rather than standing alone. The resulting features are directly interpretable and directly actionable by the clinician who would use the model: a nurse can check whether a two-year-old has more than ten words or builds a tower from cubes. Summary and distribution plots for a representative fold appear in the paper with the remaining folds in supplementary material. The one interpretive question left open is whether the model's reliance on language milestones means it preferentially detects autistic children with co-occurring language delay - a question the data could address and the paper does not.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: None, and the absence is the study's central evidential gap rather than a peripheral omission. The paper asserts that its networks work by 'capturing facial features, creating distinctive facial patterns, and evaluating the distances between facial landmarks', and includes a figure of facial landmarks, but no landmark extraction appears in the method and no evidence connects the models' decisions to facial geometry. Given that the two image classes were assembled from different internet sources, the alternative explanation - that the models distinguish autism-website photographs from general internet photographs by their imaging characteristics - is at least as plausible as the stated one, and a single class activation map over correctly and incorrectly classified images would have addressed it directly. No such analysis appears anywhere.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: The most thoroughly interpretable model in the review, and the interpretability is what makes the study diagnostically useful to this synthesis. GAMI-Net is transparent by construction: each behavioural feature passes through its own subnetwork so its marginal contribution is isolated, pairwise interaction layers capture second-order relationships such as ADOS_Total by Age, and sparse regularisation prunes redundant inputs. The paper states the intended clinical benefit directly - the decomposition allows clinicians 'to directly visualize how an increase in, say, ADOS-Gotham_Total or ADI_R_RRB_Total_C, elevates the predicted ASD probability'. SHAP extends the analysis to the imaging and fused stages and t-SNE visualises the latent space. The machinery functions exactly as designed, and what it reports is that the model's dominant predictor is the ADOS score. The authors present this as evidence that the model aligns with clinical knowledge; it is better read as the interpretability apparatus correctly identifying that the model is reading the answer off its own input. That a transparent architecture surfaces this where a black-box model would have hidden it is a genuine argument for interpretable design, and the strongest positive lesson the study offers.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: Interpretable by construction and mechanistically grounded, with one gap. Every feature is a coherence at a nameable time scale, so the finding translates directly into a physical statement: autistic children's whole-body movement was less synchronised with their conversation partner's at time scales below one second, while synchrony at slower scales was comparable. The pseudo-pair surrogate makes the interpretation secure in a way that a bare group comparison would not, by establishing that both groups' coherence exceeds what two non-interacting people produce - so the difference is in the degree of genuine coordination rather than in some artefact of shared periodicity. The derived features remain interpretable as explicit sums of named coherences. What is missing is any individual-level analysis: no examination of which children were misclassified, no relation between a child's coherence profile and their IQ or age, and no dimensional analysis relating coordination to autistic traits - the last being the natural next question given the introduction's claim that coordination correlates with social cognition and autistic traits, and given that no severity measure was collected to test it.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: Interpretability is a design constraint, an argument and a reported finding rather than a post-hoc gloss. The features are categories from an explicit linguistic theory, so a model contribution attaches to a nameable grammatical choice - a modality expression, a particular sentence-final particle, a te-clause subtype - rather than to an embedding dimension, and the linear model is retained specifically so those contributions can be identified and quantified. The authors' refusal to declare the deep model superior on accuracy grounds, on the reasoning that interpretability matters differently when 'we are dealing with human lives', is the clearest statement of that principle in the corpus. Group differences in tag frequencies are tabulated in supplementary material. The annotation system's own errors are analysed rather than assumed away, with an overall F of 0.88 and the te-clause identified as the dominant error source together with an explanation of why - it subdivides into eight classifications whose boundaries are hard to define. What is missing is the individual level: no error analysis identifies which participants were misclassified, and no analysis relates model output to the SRS-2, AQ, Vineland-II or ADOS-2 scores the study holds, which would have tested whether the linguistic signal tracks clinical severity.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: None. No feature importance, saliency map, activation visualisation, error analysis or example inspection appears for any of the eighteen combinations. The absence is decisive rather than incidental in this design, because the study's own results contain the material for an interpretability check it does not perform: handcrafted descriptors sensitive to image quality reach 84.5% alone, and a single analysis of which descriptors carry that performance - or a single visualisation of what distinguishes the two classes - would establish whether the model responds to faces or to photographs.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: None. No attribution, saliency, feature-importance or error analysis is reported for the classifier. The quaternion formulation is presented in mathematical detail but is a search-space construct, not an explanation of what the network responds to, and the associated claim that it captures physiological signal properties has no referent in the data.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: The strongest element of the study, and methodologically distinctive. Rather than applying a post-hoc attribution method, the authors manipulate the input: synthetic trajectories are generated with average acceleration systematically varied between -5 and +5 cm/s squared, and the models' predictions are measured as a function of that variation, yielding correlations of r = 0.69 and r = 0.82 with a stated direction - higher acceleration increases the probability of an autism prediction. This is causal rather than correlational evidence about the model's decision function, it is quantified, and it is directional. A second robustness analysis simplifies trajectories at seven rates from 35% to 90% and re-tests, with generated trajectories under 20 points excluded. And the analysis produces an informative incidental finding: the two-feature model, which has no acceleration input, still correlates with acceleration at 0.69, showing that the raw sequence carries the information. What is absent is any individual-level interpretation - no error analysis, no examination of which children were misclassified, and no relation between predictions and the severity range the autistic group reportedly spans.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: None. No feature importance, attribution or error analysis is reported. The omission is particularly consequential here because the paper's central algorithmic claim is that its optimiser identifies 'the most essential features', and the identity of those features is never disclosed - so the one output that would connect the computational contribution to any clinical or behavioural interpretation is withheld. Given that the paper's only displayed data show the label tracking body temperature and heart rate rather than emotion probabilities, naming the selected features would have been directly informative about what the model detects.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: None. No feature-importance, attribution or ablation analysis is reported. The omission is the single most consequential methodological gap in the study, because the one experiment that would have distinguished a real finding from an arithmetic one - refitting without the A1-A10 items and the summed result - requires nothing that the study has not already built.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Strong, and directed at the study's substantive question rather than at post-hoc justification. Every one of the sixteen variables is a named biomechanical quantity with its rationale and calculation given in supplementary material, so an attribution is interpretable without further translation. SHAP values are computed for each of the three variable sets and displayed across all participants, and the variables selected by each model are named in the results table - so a reader can see not only which features mattered but which entered each fitted model. The convergent finding across SHAP and model selection, that shoulder, hip and trunk correlations dominate, supports a specific claim about where in the body the difference lies. Most valuable is the continuous check: predicted probability is correlated with SRS-2 total score for each variable set, testing whether the model tracks the underlying trait dimension or merely reproduces the imposed threshold, with a positive relationship reported in every case. That analysis is the one this review has repeatedly noted as absent elsewhere, and it is performed here on the study's own severity variable. What is missing is per-participant error analysis - though with perfect classification there are no errors to analyse, which is itself a reason for scepticism about the perfect scores.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: Grad-CAM heatmaps are computed over the attention-generated feature maps and presented as ensuring 'transparency and reliability in decision-making'. The authors then add the qualification that distinguishes this paper from others in the branch: the heatmaps were never shown to clinicians, so their diagnostic meaning is unassessed, and collaboration with psychiatrists or autism specialists is recommended to establish whether the highlighted regions are informative. That is the correct caveat and it is stated in the authors' own voice. Its limits should be clear, though. Saliency identifies where in the image the model looked, not what property it responded to, and every candidate explanation for the result - craniofacial shape, expression, apparent age, ancestry, image resolution, crop convention - is located in the same face region. A heatmap centred on the eyes and mouth is therefore equally consistent with a facial phenotype and with the model having learned to recognise the photographic style of images that appear on autism support pages. The conclusion nevertheless instructs clinicians that they 'must recognize these facial traits or regions, as they indicate the condition', which asserts precisely what the heatmaps cannot establish.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: None. No feature-importance, attribution, spectral-band or electrode-localisation analysis is reported. In a study whose features are interpretable physiological quantities and whose electrodes have known anatomical correspondences, this is the clearest missed opportunity: a ranking of the eleven descriptors, or a topographic map of discriminative channels, would have been comparable across the branch's literature and would have survived any subsequent revision of the accuracy figure.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: Intrinsic and complete, with no post-hoc machinery needed. The model is five logistic coefficients over directly observable quantities, each reported with an odds ratio and confidence interval, and displayed as a nomogram that a clinician can use by hand. Calibration between predicted and observed probability is plotted rather than asserted, density plots show the underlying distributions, and the full univariate-to-multivariate progression is tabulated so that a reader can see which candidates were considered and which survived. The substantive interpretation is coherent and clinically recognisable: reduced frequency of functional object play, reduced play time across all three toy categories, and less socially directed speech. This is one of the few models in the review whose output could be discussed with a family in ordinary language. Two interpretive gaps remain, both concerning what the coefficients might be measuring other than autism. Predicted probability is never related to CARS-2, so whether the model tracks severity or only group membership is untested on data already collected. And no age term appears in the model, although four of five predictors are quantities of object play in a sample spanning 1 to 6 years, where those quantities rise steeply with development and where the two groups' age distributions differ in spread even after matching on the mean.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: Fully interpretable by construction and, unusually, the interpretation is the point rather than a supplement to it. The six predictors are named ADOS-2 items with published behavioural definitions, each reported with an odds ratio, confidence interval and direction, so the model reads as a clinical statement: atypicality in eye contact (OR 34.29), quality of social overtures (OR 10.84) and emphatic or emotional gestures (OR 6.49) points toward autism, while atypicality in reporting of events (OR 0.05), responsibility (OR 0.06) and comments on others' emotions or empathy (OR 0.14) points toward schizophrenia. The complete 32-item table with non-zero proportions and tests lets a reader see the whole profile rather than only the selected six, and the profiles are coherent enough to be taught. The study also performs the construct-validity analysis that this review has repeatedly noted as absent elsewhere: rather than accepting that the ADOS-2 measures autism, it asks what the instrument is measuring in the schizophrenia group and answers with evidence - correlations across all domains with the PANSS negative scale, higher negative-symptom scores in cut-off-positive patients, and cut-off positivity predicted by the negative scale alone. Establishing what a positive score means in a population where it is wrong is a stronger form of interpretability than any saliency map in this corpus.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: None attempted. No saliency, attribution, acoustic analysis or characterisation of the learned representations is presented, and none is claimed - the models are evaluated purely as classifiers. The only window onto behaviour is the confusion matrices, which the authors do interpret, observing that both models predict typically developing more successfully than atypically developing and attributing this to the class distribution. For a study whose motivating hypothesis is specific and acoustically measurable - reduced variation in pitch, intonation and expressive elements - the absence of any analysis connecting model decisions to prosody is the clearest missed opportunity in the paper, because it is the analysis that would distinguish a model responding to speech from one responding to the acoustics of a clinic room. The fairness analysis partially compensates by revealing something about the models that no saliency map would have: that their apparent competence does not extend to girls.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: Limited at the model level and thoughtful at the corpus level. Sentiment and topic analyses were run before classification to develop qualitative understanding of the data, and the comparison of sentiment polarity between raw and profanity-censored versions is a genuine methodological check - it establishes that any polarity difference between groups is not simply a difference in swearing. But no attribution, coefficient inspection, attention visualisation or error analysis is reported for either classifier, so what the models responded to is unknown. This is the study's clearest missed opportunity, because inspecting the highest-weighted terms in the word2vec logistic regression would have spoken directly to the interpretive question the paper leaves open - whether 73% reflects something about autistic language or about the vocabulary of a self-advocacy community - and because the prior removal of sixteen autism-related tokens means the answer would have been informative rather than circular.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: The most substantive interpretability work in the review, and the only instance of a study explaining its models in the vocabulary of the clinical construct rather than in the vocabulary of the input. Random regression forests were fitted with all 27 ADOS-2 items as predictors and each network's prediction confidence as the outcome; importance was assessed through three metrics simultaneously - percentage increase in mean squared error, increase in node purity, and p-value - and a third normalising forest was calibrated on the averaged confidence of both networks so that importances from the two separate models could be placed on a common scale and compared. The design of this analysis is careful in a way that saliency maps elsewhere in this corpus are not, because it produces claims that can be checked against clinical knowledge. The video result is coherent and expected: joint attention initiation, quality of social overtures, unusual eye contact and pointing gestures, a nonverbal social-communication cluster that a model of dyadic body motion should be sensitive to. The audio result is coherent and unexpected: showing behaviour, pointing gesture, unusual sensory exploration and hand mannerisms, none of which is a vocal construct. The authors follow this where it leads rather than around it, proposing that non-vocal ambient sound from object manipulation drove part of the classification and noting that sensory interests was the single most correlated item, and separately raising the possibility that the examiner's prosodic adaptation to the child contributes. An analysis that tells the authors their audio model is probably not listening to speech, reported as such, is worth more to this review than any number of attention heatmaps.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: None for the models. No saliency, attribution or feature analysis is reported for the classifier or the regressor, so what distinguishes the two image classes is never examined - which matters especially here, since the undocumented composition of the negative class means an attribution analysis is the only way a reader could tell whether the model responds to children or to corpora. The one transparency contribution is at the measurement layer: an inter-annotator correlation matrix showing each rater's agreement with the mean annotation, accompanied by the authors' own critique of the averaging procedure. That is honest reporting of label quality rather than model interpretability, but in a study whose labels are the weakest link it is arguably the more useful of the two.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Present for the mood model at the level of its outputs - five named, clinically legible emotion categories, with two ablations documenting the architectural choices and their numeric effects - and entirely absent for the severity classifiers, which is where a system recommending medication dosages most needs it. No feature importance is reported despite Random Forest providing it without additional work, so it is unknown whether the model responds to skin temperature or to facial mood, to which mood categories, or to which facial regions. Nothing links a severity prediction to any observable property of a child that a clinician could inspect, challenge or corroborate. The paper's own framing makes this gap sharper than usual: it proposes replacing a 58-item instrument, whose items are explicit and auditable, with a classifier whose basis is not reported, and it presents the substitution as an improvement in precision.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Claimed and absent. The third listed contribution is 'Analysis of the specific facial features that contribute most significantly to accurate ASD detection', and the paper contains no such analysis - no saliency map, no attribution, no landmark or region analysis, no feature ranking. This is the one omission that most directly affects the paper's own argument: having asserted specific morphometric differences as the biological basis for the approach, the study had both the motive and the standard tools to test whether its models respond to those regions, and did neither. In their absence, the 98% is compatible with a facial phenotype and equally compatible with the model having learned the photographic character of images that appear in autism-related online collections - and this review has recorded four other studies on this corpus where saliency evidence, where offered, could not distinguish the two either.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: Among the better-handled in the review, because the features are interpretable by construction and the interpretation is pursued rather than asserted. Feature-importance plots are given for logistic regression and random forests; mean length of utterance emerges as the top predictor in both; and the finding is compared explicitly against prior literature, confirming one study's MLU result and contradicting another's conclusion that total number of words does not differ. The stratified analysis goes beyond importance to describe how each feature behaves across diagnosis, age band and sex, producing the specific and testable claims recorded above. And the negative result on mean word length is interpreted correctly rather than ignored - characters are the wrong unit for lexical complexity, and phonemes or morphemes would be better. What interpretability cannot settle here is the identity of the underlying construct: MLU is a developmental language index and no independent measure of language ability exists in the data, so the models' leading signal is compatible with autism-specific pragmatic difference and with generic expressive language delay, and the paper does not raise the distinction.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: None attempted, and the omission is more notable here than in most of this review because the modality invites it. Skeleton data are inherently interpretable: joints have names, angles have physical meaning, and time is explicit, so a joint-level or phase-level attribution would map directly onto describable gait characteristics - stride variability, arm swing amplitude and asymmetry, trunk sway, turning smoothness - which are the terms in which the clinical motor literature the paper cites is written. The Geneva pose study charted elsewhere in this review shows what such an analysis yields when its model confidences are regressed on clinical item scores. Here nothing connects the 95.4% to any nameable property of how the children walked, so the study establishes that a classifier can separate the groups and contributes nothing to understanding what it separates them on. Given that no demographic data exist either, the possibility that the models respond to age- or sex-related gait maturation rather than to autism cannot be examined from any direction.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Split between a well-interpreted feature analysis and an uninterpreted model. The three perturbation measures are clinical voice-quality metrics with direct physiological meaning, so the statistical result translates into a specific and evaluable claim about phonatory stability, and the paper articulates it correctly.
