There is no repetition over alternative splits, no confidence intervals and no independent replication.

answers.title: Automatic classification of children with autism spectrum disorder by using a computerized visual‐orienting task
answers.answer: Subject-wise leave-one-out cross-validation with no feature selection and a hyperparameter fixed from external data - about as clean an internal validation as this sample size permits, and argued for explicitly against record-wise alternatives with citation to the methodological literature on accuracy inflation. Beyond that, the two cross-group tests constitute a genuine generalisation experiment rarely attempted in this corpus: an entire group is withheld from training and used as an unseen population. The resulting asymmetry - 100% correct on unseen low-functioning children from a model trained on typically developing versus high-functioning, against 53.85% on unseen high-functioning children from a model trained on typically developing versus low-functioning - is interpreted correctly as showing that 'a model trained with more similar groups can perform well with test data from a disparate group, and a model trained with data from more different groups will underperform with test data from an intermediate group'. What remains absent is an independent cohort, an external site and any replication.

answers.title: Auxiliary Diagnostic Method for Early Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye Movement Data Analysis
answers.answer: The weakest element. A single random split of 83 children into 43 training and 40 testing, with no cross-validation, no repetition over alternative splits, no held-out tuning set and no independent cohort. The two feature hyperparameters were set empirically with no procedure stated and an explicit acknowledgement that other values could improve performance, and the correlation analysis used to justify the feature design was computed across the entire dataset including the test half - so the features whose relevance is demonstrated on all 83 children are the same features evaluated on 40 of them. With a 40-child test set, the reported accuracies carry sampling uncertainty of roughly plus or minus 8 percentage points that is never quantified.

answers.title: Children ASD Evaluation Through Joint Analysis of EEG and Eye-Tracking Recordings With Graph Convolution Network
answers.answer: The weakest element and the one that governs how the headline should be read. A single 8:2 split with no cross-validation, no repetition and no held-out tuning set. The unit of splitting is never stated, and the reported figures indicate it is not the participant: 42 children split 80/20 gives roughly 8 test children, on which 0.9500, 0.7368 and 0.7895 are unattainable, whereas they correspond precisely to 19/20, 14/19 and 15/19 samples. With EEG divided into 4-second epochs yielding roughly 90 segments per child, sample-level splitting would place segments from the same child on both sides of the boundary. Additionally, the t-tests and the covariance thresholding that determines the graph's edge structure were computed across the entire dataset, so the graph topology the network convolves over was constructed using test-sample information. There is no independent cohort, no external site and no replication.

answers.title: Classification of Autism Spectrum Disorder Severity Using Eye Tracking Data Based on Visual Attention Model
answers.answer: Five-fold cross-validation with splitting stated explicitly at the subject level, which is the correct unit and is clearly described. Folds were proportionally balanced. Two elements fall outside the loop. ReliefF feature selection is described once, per group, with no statement that it was repeated within folds - and since the group-specific feature sets are the paper's principal scientific claim, whether they were derived using all 88 participants or only training-fold participants materially affects their status. The 20-frame decision threshold was chosen by the Youden index applied to the ROC curve, which is the same curve used to characterise performance, so the operating point is fitted to the evaluation. There is no independent cohort, no external site and no held-out replication.

answers.title: Classification of Children With Autism and Typical Development Using Eye-Tracking Data From Face-to-Face Conversations: Machine Learning Model Development and Performance Evaluation
answers.answer: Leave-one-out cross-validation at the participant level, explicitly motivated as overfitting protection. The defect is that forward feature selection evaluates candidate features by their classification accuracy, and that accuracy is the leave-one-out estimate itself, so features were chosen to maximise the number subsequently reported. Compounding this, results are reported for every feature count from 1 to 21 across four classifiers and three feature sets - 252 cells - and the maximum is quoted as the headline. There is no outer validation loop, no held-out cohort and no repetition. The saving grace is that the paper prints the entire selection trajectory, so a reader can see that accuracy plateaus at 92.31% from three features through eleven and that the single-feature result is 79.49%, which makes the shape of the result assessable even though the peak is optimistic.

answers.title: Combined Signal Processing Based Techniques and Feed Forward Neural Networks for Pathological Voice Detection and Classification
answers.answer: The decisive weakness. Partitioning is 70/15/15 with six-fold cross-validation, but over 255 voice samples drawn from only 19 children - roughly 13 phonations each - with no statement that a child's samples were confined to one partition. Repeated sustained vowels from one speaker constitute a speaker-identification problem, and MFCC, RASTA-PLP, jitter, shimmer and HNR are the standard feature set for exactly that task, so a classifier can achieve near-perfect accuracy by recognising individuals and mapping them to their known group. Six of 33 reported conditions achieve exactly 100% accuracy with AUC 1, which is what speaker-level leakage produces and which is otherwise implausible for a clinical classification from a single vowel. Additionally, the hidden neuron count was chosen by trial to maximise accuracy separately for each feature set and task, so every figure is a maximum over that search. There is no independent cohort, no external validation and no held-out speaker test.

answers.title: Computer-Aided Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Eye-Tracking Study Using Data Visualization and Deep Learning
answers.answer: The paper's most important element and the reason it matters to this review. Three-fold cross-validation is run twice on the same model and data under two splitting units. Pooling the 547 images regardless of origin gives approximately 90% accuracy. Splitting the 59 participants first and then assigning their images by ID - so that no child appears on both sides - gives approximately 71%. The authors describe the second explicitly as a further examination of model performance and note the decline as expected. With an average of 9.27 images per child, this constitutes a direct within-study quantification of segment-level inflation: roughly 19 accuracy points, on a design where images from one child are highly correlated. Residual issues: augmented samples presumably inherit their source image's participant, so the image-level figure may be further inflated; only accuracy is reported for the participant-level condition; three epochs is very few; and there is no independent cohort or external site.

answers.title: Computer-aided autism diagnosis based on visual attention models using eye tracking
answers.answer: Five-fold cross-validation over subjects, stated explicitly and unambiguously - 'no information of subjects used for testing is used in the learning phase, once the cross-validation was performed over the subjects' - which is the correct unit and is rarely stated this plainly. A second partition operates over frames, with 50 held out from model learning for diagnosis only, deliberately simulating stimulus independence. The authors also pre-empt and address the same-video contamination objection. Two elements nonetheless sit outside the loop: the genetic algorithm feature selection is presented as a single result per group with no indication it was repeated per fold, and the 28-vote decision threshold was chosen by Youden index on the cross-validated ROC. There is no independent cohort or external site.

answers.title: Eye gaze as a biomarker in the recognition of autism spectrum disorder using virtual reality and machine learning: A proof of concept for diagnosis
answers.answer: Five-fold cross-validation repeated four times with means and standard deviations reported, which is better practice than single-split evaluation and gives some sense of variability. The limitation is stated by the authors themselves - no independent sample exists and all participants contributed to validation - and compounded by the fact that both the feature subset and the model were selected on that same repeated cross-validation, across five algorithms and ten datasets. The reported per-dataset maxima are therefore optimistically biased, and the general-approach figure of 0.86 is the best of roughly fifty fits. The ten-feature cap on selection is a sensible guard against overfitting given 144 candidates and 55 participants, and using default hyperparameters removes one further source of selection. There is no external site, no independent cohort and no held-out replication.

answers.title: Identifying Autism with Head Movement Features by Implementing Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Leave-one-out cross-validation at the participant level, correctly implemented and explicitly motivated as overfitting protection. The weakness is the search: the random feature combination approach deliberately tests every subset of the six features, and the authors justify it on the grounds that exhaustive search 'typically yields equal or higher classification accuracy simply owing to the fact that all features and feature combinations could be tested' - which is precisely the property that makes the resulting maximum optimistic. Sixty-three subsets across five classifiers gives 315 fits, all scored on the same leave-one-out estimate, with no outer loop and no held-out set. The mixed-effects feature screening also used all participants, though since all six features passed and all were retained, this contributed no additional selection. There is no independent cohort or external replication.

answers.title: Machine Learning Model To Predict Autism Investigating Eye-Tracking Dataset
answers.answer: The decisive weakness, and unusually well documented because the source study performed the missing check. Ten-fold cross-validation is applied over 547 scanpath images drawn from 59 children, with no statement that a child's images were confined to a single fold. The study that released these images ran both configurations and reported approximately 90% accuracy pooling images against approximately 71% holding out participants - so the inflation attributable to image-level splitting on this exact dataset is known and is roughly 19 points. This reanalysis does not repeat that check. Separately, k-means clustering used the entire image set, so the partition determining each model's training and test pool was fitted on data including the test images. There is no held-out set, no participant-level analysis, no confidence intervals and no independent cohort.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Leave-one-subject-out, correctly implemented and explicitly motivated as simulating 'the diagnosis of a new patient in everyday life clinical settings'. Normalisation is fitted on training folds and applied to test data using training statistics, and hyperparameters are grid-searched at each iteration rather than fixed globally. Two robustness analyses extend the validation usefully - varying the number of trials available in the test set, and restricting features to those derivable from the ulnar marker alone - both framed around deployment constraints rather than as statistical exercises. The residual issues are that the ROC operating point is chosen on the evaluation curve, and that no independent cohort or external site is tested, which the small sample precludes.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: Not applicable in the classification sense - no model is trained, no individual is assigned a class, and no autism prediction is attempted. The relevant validation question is whether the automated attention measure tracks the construct it claims to measure, and the study answers it with concurrent validation against an independent human standard: agreement with the treating therapist's 0-100 attention ratings on 28 of 34 sessions, reported as 82.4%. That is the right design for the claim and it is described accurately, with the conclusion stating that the system matches 'over 80% of therapist assessments' rather than presenting the figure as diagnostic performance. Four qualifications bound it. The 34 sessions come from 6 children and are therefore clustered, with no adjustment reported, so the effective sample is closer to 6 than to 34. No chance-corrected agreement statistic is given, so how much of the 82.4% reflects the marginal distribution of the therapist's ratings is unknown. No reliability estimate exists for those ratings, so the ceiling on achievable agreement is unknown - and a measure agreeing 82.4% with a standard of unknown reliability could be tracking either the construct or that particular therapist. And the scoring constants are operator-adjustable per child, which is clinically sensible but means the score is not a fixed instrument and its agreement with a clinician may partly reflect tuning. The separate longitudinal claim - that attention rose across seven weeks - has no control condition at all, so it cannot be separated from familiarisation with a novel robot, practice on a repeated task, maturation, or the attention of being in a study; and with 5 of 11 children not completing and no reason given, the trend is computed on a self-selected subgroup. The authors label the causal claim a hypothesis, which is the correct standing for it.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: The weakest element. A single 80/20 split of 200 children gives a 40-child test set, with no cross-validation, no repetition across splits and no separate tuning set. SelectKBest's k was chosen as 17 'as it gave the best results', which tunes a selection parameter against the reported evaluation. Twenty-seven algorithm-by-selection combinations were evaluated and the maximum quoted in the abstract. There is no independent cohort, no external validation and no confidence interval, so the reported 95% cannot be distinguished from the 90% cells by anything the paper provides.

answers.title: Quantifying Voice Characteristics for Detecting Autism
answers.answer: Five-fold cross-validation with training, development and test sets rotated and an explicit statement that model parameters were learned only from training examples and were 'totally blinded from the test examples'. Class imbalance is handled by iterative undersampling to 28 per class, repeated until scores converged at around 100 iterations - a substantially more rigorous treatment than a single balanced draw, since it averages away the randomness of which majority-class participants are selected. Confidence intervals are computed on every AUC. The IQ-matched subsample analysis functions as an internal replication under a controlled confound and returns a higher AUC (88.27%) than the main analysis, which is strong evidence that IQ was not driving the result. What remains: RFECV and the best-activity selection were both performed across the same cross-validation used for reporting, with no outer loop; and no independent cohort or external site was tested.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: The benchmark's fixed 300/100 image split, with hyperparameters tuned by out-of-bag error on the training portion. Three weaknesses. The split partitions stimuli, not participants: all 28 children appear on both sides, so the model can learn subject-specific viewing idiosyncrasies from a child's training-image scanpaths and apply them to that same child's test-image scanpaths - the segment-level leakage pattern that recurs throughout this corpus, although here the low absolute performance suggests little was gained from it. Second, 23 classifiers plus a three-parameter grid were evaluated before one was chosen, and the resulting optimism is directly visible: the selection table reports 68.5% for TreeBagger while the test set returns 0.59, a nine-point gap that the paper presents without reconciling the two numbers. Third, no repeated splits, no cross-validation over participants, no confidence intervals and no significance test against the 0.59 competitor, so the claimed tie for first place rests on a single comparison of two point estimates on 100 images.

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: The strongest external evaluation arrangement in the corpus paired with the weakest partitioning principle. On the strong side: the test labels were withheld by the ICME 2019 organisers and all test performance was computed by them, so no amount of iteration could tune to the test set - the only genuinely third-party-scored evaluation here - and validation results are averaged over repeated runs with standard deviations reported. On the weak side: the partition is over images (240 train / 60 validation / 100 test), not over children, so all 28 participants appear in all three sets, and a model that learns a child's characteristic viewing tempo from their training scanpaths can apply it to their test scanpaths. The authors identify this mechanism themselves as the explanation for scanpath-only parity, which makes it the corpus's only self-diagnosed instance of the leakage pattern - but they do not draw the consequence that it bounds the 62.13%. The benchmark's fixed splits preclude re-partitioning without forfeiting the blind test, which is a real constraint rather than an oversight; the appropriate response would have been to state the resulting ceiling explicitly. A further diagnostic sits unremarked in the tables: validation-optimal and test-optimal configurations differ in both pipelines (LSTM 67.23% on validation but 60.40% on test; BrMLP-SP-F best on validation, BrMLP-SP on test), which the authors attribute to training and validation being 'more similar to each other than to the test dataset' without noting that this makes the validation set unfit for model selection.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: The corpus's reference implementation of correct validation for a segment-generating modality. Three properties matter. Participant-wise partition: the 136 children are split 68/68 into training and Testing Set 1, matched on diagnosis, age, gender and ADOS module, so no child's frames appear on both sides - and matching the partitions on covariates, not merely the groups, is a refinement almost nothing else here applies. Participant-level aggregation: the network trains and predicts on 5-second segments (~505 per video, ~34,000 in training), but every segment prediction within a video is averaged into one ASD probability per child before any metric is computed, so the reported 80.9% is over 68 children and not over 34,000 clips. This is precisely the correction that Cilia had to apply retrospectively, watching image-level accuracy of ~90% fall to ~71% at participant level, and applying it by construction is what makes this figure comparable to a clinical one. Hyperparameter selection is confined to an 80-20 split inside the training set, with the least-validation-loss checkpoint carried forward. Two limits persist. Testing Set 2, though larger, contains only autistic children and comes from the same cohort, so it estimates sensitivity in a slightly older sample rather than replicating externally - no independent site or cohort is tested. And the covariate matching does not extend to cognitive level: best-estimate IQ is measured, differs between a typically developing and an autistic group as a matter of course, and correlates with the model's output at -0.283, so some portion of the separation may reflect general developmental level rather than autism specifically. No leave-one-site-out or examiner-held-out analysis addresses the parallel possibility that examiner behaviour contributes.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: The study's decisive weakness, and the reason its numbers are not comparable to participant-level results elsewhere in this corpus. The dataset is 1,500 samples formed as 60 subjects x 25 tasks, explicitly 'randomized between subjects and tasks', and the folds are drawn so that 'for each fold, we take the 10% of the samples for testing and the remaining 90% for training, regardless of the number of ASD or TD subjects in the test or training set'. Every child therefore has roughly 22 or 23 of their 25 vectors in training whenever the remaining two or three are tested. Because each vector is an average of that child's habitual movement dynamics within a task, the network can identify the individual from their kinematic signature and recover the diagnosis from that identification rather than from any group-general motor property - the same mechanism Liaqat et al. diagnose explicitly in their own eye-tracking data and that Cilia quantified as a fall from ~90% to ~71% when the unit was corrected. No participant-held-out analysis is reported anywhere, so the magnitude of the inflation here is unknown. A second, independent issue concerns which number is reported: ten-fold cross-validation with five repetitions returned 88 +/- 3%, and the paper then states that 'for the successive analysis, we used the best trained model across the 10-fold', from which the 93% accuracy, 0.87 sensitivity, 0.98 specificity, ROC curve and complete feature-importance ordering are all derived. The best of ten is a maximum, not an estimate, and it is the figure carried into the abstract, the Discussion and the Conclusion while the cross-validated 88 +/- 3% appears once. Hidden-layer width was additionally selected on the same cross-validation. The compounded effect is that the reported operating characteristics come from a model chosen for performing best on data structurally related to what it was trained on.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: Done correctly, and stated in terms that leave no ambiguity: 'we perform a 10-fold subject-independent cross-validation to evaluate the performance of the proposed model, where each subject is regarded as a sample', with stratified sampling to preserve the class ratio in every fold, each fold tested exactly once, and the average across folds reported with standard deviations. Because every child contributes exactly one feature vector - EEG features are averaged across that child's clean segments, gaze features aggregated across their two trials - there is no possibility of the segment-level leakage that inflates results throughout this corpus, and the 95.56% is a genuine participant-level figure. Feature normalisation is also fitted on training data only. Two gaps remain. The three network geometries, the noise level, both learning rates and both iteration counts are stated as given, with no description of how they were arrived at, so selection optimism cannot be excluded and may be substantial across four compared architectures. And there is no external validation - no second site, no held-out cohort, no replication sample - so the estimate, though internally sound, rests entirely on 90 children from two institutions in one city. The correct comparison for this study's 95.56% is therefore not the segment-level 90%-plus figures elsewhere in the corpus but the small set of participant-level results, against which it stands as one of the highest and, on validation design, one of the better supported.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Correct in its most important respect and incomplete in a secondary one. The partition is subject-disjoint: 40 children in training and validation (16+16 and 4+4), 36 in test set #1, 18 in test set #2, accounting for all 94 participants with no child in more than one partition. This forecloses the identity-leakage route that inflates several other studies here, and it is the reason 0.916 can be compared to Kojovic's 80.9% and Han's 95.56% rather than to segment-level figures. Two independent test sets rather than one is a further strength, and making them differ in preprocessing turns the second into a domain-shift check rather than a redundant repetition. What is incomplete: the reported test metrics are clip-level, computed over 416 and 184 clips rather than over 36 and 18 children, so within-child correlation inflates the apparent precision even though it does not bias the point estimate; the paper describes per-subject probability averaging for training and validation but not for testing, and no per-child accuracy appears. There is also no cross-validation - a single fixed split with 32 training children - so the estimate carries no measure of split-to-split variability, and no external cohort or site. Finally, whatever architecture and hyperparameter selection occurred is undocumented, so it cannot be established that the validation set was used only once.

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Leave-one-out cross-validation over 80 children with the participant as the unit - structurally the right design, and it forecloses the within-subject leakage that inflates Simeoli, Liaqat, Mazumdar and Akter. But two selection steps precede it and contaminate it. The EEG feature set was determined by running independent-samples t-tests on band power across all 80 children and retaining the 12 region-band combinations reaching significance; only then was classification with leave-one-out cross-validation performed on those features. Every held-out child therefore contributed their label to the choice of features used to classify them - the classic selection-bias pattern, and one that inflates the EEG modality specifically, which is the modality the paper concludes is most discriminative and which anchors its central claim. Second, the number of gaze clusters was tested at four values and 'the final value of K was determined from the experimental results', so a preprocessing hyperparameter was also chosen on classification performance across the full sample. A third, milder issue is that the headline 87.50% is the best of three classifiers; the paper reports averages for single modalities but not for the fusion. There is no external validation, no independent cohort and no repeated-split estimate of variability. The correct reading is that the participant-level design is sound but that the reported figures - particularly for EEG and for the fusion that depends on it - are optimistic by an unmeasured margin.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: The corpus's weakest evaluation design, and the weakness is threefold. First, no train/test split, cross-validation scheme, held-out set or partition of any kind is described anywhere in the paper; the only replication is 30 reruns of the optimiser. Second, augmentation preceded whatever evaluation occurred, and the authors state their purpose plainly: 'We included a data augmentation step to generate synthetic samples to enlarge the training and testing data.' Flips, translations and blurs of a source image are near-duplicates of it, so populating a test set with them guarantees that the model has effectively seen every test instance. Third, and independently of augmentation, the 547 source images come from a small number of children contributing roughly nine images each, and no participant identifiers exist in the released image set, so images from the same child necessarily span any partition. Layered on top, the metaheuristic optimises C and gamma against the KELM's mean squared error with the accuracy-versus-iteration curve in Figure 4 rising monotonically over ten iterations, which indicates the search is scored on the same predictions that are reported. The instructive comparison is with Cilia and colleagues, who built this dataset and reported that image-level accuracy near 90% fell to approximately 71% when computed per child. This paper reports 98.8% on the same images, cannot compute a per-child figure because it records no participants, and does not cite the correction. The gap between 71% and 98.8% is the measure of what these three compounding decisions add.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: The reference standard for this corpus, and the source of its most transferable methodological lesson. The classification procedure holds out a third of each group, samples a 10-minute epoch at random from the combined 43-minute dataset, trains on the remainder and repeats 10,000 times - so the estimate is not a single split and every participant is held out repeatedly. Decisively, the chance level is derived empirically from a null distribution and comes to 0.607 rather than the 0.500 that an imbalanced 48/105 design might naively suggest; the observed 0.618 therefore exceeds chance by about one percentage point at p = 0.039, which the authors correctly describe as 'only slightly greater than would be expected by chance' and as confirming that heterogeneity 'precludes diagnostically robust classification'. Had the same number been compared against 50%, it would have been reported as a 12-point improvement. Beyond classification, the validation apparatus includes: leave-one-participant-out construction of every reference heatmap 'to eliminate bias'; normalisation of area-specific gaze by successful on-screen frames so that tracking quality cannot leak into the behavioural measures; a partial correlation control confirming reliability is not driven by on-screen time; measurement of stimulus familiarity and verification that it affects no result; replication of every analysis across two distinct stimuli and across epoch durations from 10 minutes down to seconds; bootstrap confidence intervals on all effect sizes; permutation testing for fingerprinting; FDR correction throughout; and two independent sites with site membership displayed rather than pooled. The single most important output for this review is the fingerprinting result itself: gaze identifies an individual out of 153 at five to ten times chance from 2 minutes of data. That is a direct measurement of the individual-identity signal that any train/test split failing to separate participants will allow a classifier to exploit, and it explains quantitatively why studies here that split by image, segment, task or augmented copy report accuracies far above what participant-level designs achieve.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: Correct on the dimension that matters most in this corpus and incomplete on a secondary one. The fold constraint is stated explicitly and reasoned exactly right: 'all clips spliced from a given child's video had to be included in the same fold to prevent models from learning from child-specific recording idiosyncrasies, including environmental background noise and audio quality'. That names both the mechanism and its two concrete forms, and it is the discipline missing from Cilia's image-level folds, Simeoli's task-level folds, Liaqat's image-wise splits and Gaspar's augmented copies. Fold composition is tabulated so the balance can be checked, all three models are evaluated on the same folds, and metrics are averaged with standard deviations. Three gaps remain. Metrics are clip-level rather than child-level, so 850 correlated observations from 58 children are treated as the effective sample and no per-child accuracy is available. There is no held-out test set beyond cross-validation, and the random forest's hyperparameters were 'manually chosen' with no procedure described, so some selection optimism is unquantified. And most importantly, no analysis addresses whether the classifier is separating diagnosis or separating age and sex - there is no age-matched subsample, no covariate adjustment, and no age-only or sex-only baseline, despite both variables differing markedly between groups and both directly determining child vocal acoustics. The validation protocol is therefore sound against leakage and silent on confounding.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Leave-one-subject-out cross-validation, and uniquely in this corpus the choice is justified by citation to the methodological literature on exactly this issue - Saeb et al. (2017) on subject-wise versus record-wise validation - with the rationale that it approximates 'the clinically relevant use-case of diagnosis in unseen participants'. Because each participant contributes a single averaged feature vector, there is no possibility of the within-subject leakage that inflates results throughout this review. Robustness was checked against 10-fold cross-validation, giving 0.9235 against 0.9205 with p = 0.9219, confirming the estimate is not an artefact of the resampling scheme. Comparisons between models use DeLong's test rather than informal inspection. Sex-stratified models were fitted to test whether the sex imbalance drove the result. The confounding variables were tested rather than acknowledged. What remains: the soft-margin constants were chosen per model on performance and the linear configuration was selected for reporting over tuned non-linear alternatives, so some selection optimism is present though bounded by the small hyperparameter space; feature selection was performed under 10-fold rather than leave-one-out for software reasons; and there is no independent replication cohort - the sample is a single site and overlaps with the two prior papers whose findings are being replicated, so the 'replication' is of models rather than of data. The authors' own framing is appropriately cautious about all of this, describing the results as 'preliminary but very encouraging'.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Sound in every respect that this corpus commonly gets wrong, with the residual weakness being confounding rather than leakage. The unit is the participant, since all features are per-child summaries; leave-one-out cross-validation is used and justified by citation to Vabalas et al. on overoptimistic classification; AUCs carry Hanley-McNeil confidence intervals; and classifier configurations are compared by a formal criterion rather than by inspecting point estimates. Two further design properties strengthen the estimate beyond what the cross-validation alone provides. The class ratio of 41:416 approximates real screening prevalence, so the AUC is not estimated under an artificially balanced design - a distinction that matters enormously for translation, since the same AUC implies very different positive predictive value at 9% prevalence than at 50%. And diagnosis followed rather than preceded enrolment, so the sample is not conditioned on already being diagnosed, removing the referral filter that shapes almost every other study here. What remains unaddressed: age and missing data were covaried but sex was not, on stated power grounds; ethnicity and caregiver education differ significantly and are never revisited; cognitive ability differs and cannot be adjusted because Mullen data exist only for the autistic group; the 12 children with non-autism diagnoses were excluded, so the discrimination tested is against typical development rather than against developmental concern; and there is no independent replication cohort, though this study is itself a replication and extension of the group's earlier rate-only finding in a larger sample with redesigned stimuli.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: The strongest aspect of the study, and stated in the terms that matter: 'Several procedures were performed in the classification pipeline to further avoid overfitting and optimistic bias due to limited sample size and the high-dimensionality of data'. Three properties follow. Repeated 10-fold cross-validation is used rather than a single split. Dimensionality reduction into principal components and hyperparameter tuning are both performed 'in a nested fashion' inside the cross-validation, so neither the components nor the hyperparameters are informed by held-out data - the single most common source of optimistic bias in high-dimensional small-sample classification, and one that Liao and colleagues elsewhere in this corpus violate directly by selecting features on the full sample before cross-validating. Significance is established by permutation rather than assumed from a nominal chance level, with 5,001 iterations, and the resulting p values are what license the paper's negative claims. The unit is the participant throughout. What remains: no independent replication cohort, though the two-language design provides a form of internal generalisation test that is arguably stronger for the question at hand; no confidence intervals on the AUCs; no formal test comparing feature classes; and the unexplained 40% attrition from the English autistic sample, which is a selection concern that no amount of validation discipline can address. The combined-language model's validity also rests on the supplementary demonstration that language differences in the rhythm features do not account for the classification, a check that is performed but reported outside the main text.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: Leave-one-out cross-validation with the participant as the held-out unit, chosen deliberately for small-sample efficiency, and correctly described. Because each participant is represented by a single vector there is no possibility of utterance-level leakage. What is not controlled is selection: only the best classifier per input combination is reported, across three families and, for the masking configurations, a 27-point hyperparameter grid, all evaluated on the same folds that produce the reported numbers. With 50 participants and six reported configurations each maximised over several classifiers, the optimism is unquantified and could plausibly account for a substantial part of the 12-point gap between the best models (0.72) and the human raters (0.60). No permutation test, confidence interval or AUC is reported to bound this. Set against that, the study's benchmarking design provides a form of validation that internal resampling cannot: the human raters constitute an empirical performance floor obtained on identical input, and the standardised instruments an empirical ceiling obtained on identical participants, both of which anchor the model figures in a way no single-model study can achieve. The authors themselves qualify the ceiling, noting that their instruments exceeded their own published validation figures because the sample was selected for clear-cut cases while the validation sample included non-spectrum clinical participants.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: Two claims are made and both are the right ones to make, but neither can be verified from what is reported. The cross-validation is stated to be participant-based - 'the data is divided into ten subsets based on participants... ensuring that all participants' data appeared either in the training or test set' - which forecloses within-participant leakage, though since each child contributes a single feature vector the safeguard is structural rather than earned. Feature selection is stated to use training data only. Against these, three issues remain. The analysed sample cannot be reconciled with the 133 recruited: the accuracy grid across all six results tables is consistent with roughly 20 per class and inconsistent with 61 and 72, and the balancing statement acknowledges that classes were equalised without saying how or how much was discarded. The Wrapper feature-selection method is by definition driven by classification accuracy, and while WEKA's attribute-selection mode can be run under cross-validation, the description does not establish that selection was refitted inside each classification fold rather than performed once and then used throughout - a distinction that determines whether the reported figures carry selection optimism. And the headline 87.5% is the maximum over 24 reported configurations, with no correction, no confidence interval and no held-out confirmation. The public data posting is the mitigating factor: it is the only route by which an external reader could resolve the sample question.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Participant-level leave-one-out cross-validation, described in enough detail to confirm that each held-out child's classifier was 'determined using only the data from the other subjects, omitting the one predicted'. Cohorts were modelled separately, so no information crosses between them. Single-area classifications were tested against non-parametric permutation, which is what establishes that several areas do not exceed chance rather than leaving weak accuracies to be read as weak positives. The statistical analyses are protected by covariate adjustment, variance-assumption testing with an appropriate substitution, Tukey correction and multivariate-t adjustment for the interaction contrasts. Three gaps remain. There is no independent validation cohort, acknowledged. The two quality-control exclusions - calibration failure and off-screen fixation - are described but their counts are not reported, and both plausibly operate differentially by group, so the analysed sample is a compliant subset of unknown size and composition. And the reference standard is DSM-5 plus CARS without observational confirmation, which bounds what any validation can establish. The most valuable validation-adjacent contribution, though, is not internal: by calculating that 80% sensitivity and 82% specificity yields a 4.2% positive predictive value at 1% prevalence, the paper supplies the translation step that converts a cross-validated accuracy into a statement about deployment, and it is the only study in the corpus to do so numerically.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: The validation design is the study's principal contribution to this review and differs in kind from everything else charted here. Rather than resampling within a dataset, the model was locked with thresholds fixed on prior training and testing data, and then evaluated prospectively on consecutively enrolled children whose diagnoses were established afterwards by an independent blinded specialist consensus. All three Device inputs were blinded from one another and from the output; the specialists were blinded to the Device. The trial was registered before initiation, so the endpoints - PPV and NPV with FDA-agreed floors - were pre-specified rather than selected post hoc. Participant flow is fully documented with attrition causes including the COVID-19 disruption quantified. The two features that make this the corpus's benchmark are the population and the disclosure. The population is the referral cohort the tool is meant for, with 28.7% prevalence and only 9.4% neurotypical, so predictive values are directly deployable rather than requiring prevalence correction - the calculation Kong and colleagues perform hypothetically is here unnecessary because the design supplies it directly. The disclosure is the counterfactual: sensitivity 51.6% and specificity 18.5% without abstention, against 98.4% and 78.9% with it. No other paper in this corpus reports what its performance would be under a less favourable operating decision. What remains open is the temporal question the authors themselves identify - whether children given indeterminate or negative outputs at 18-72 months go on to receive autism diagnoses later - which the planned registrational study is designed to address and without which the NPV of 98.3% is a cross-sectional rather than a prognostic figure.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: The weakest dimension, and the authors say so more clearly than most. Feature selection by Mann-Whitney test was performed across all 28 samples before any split, so the 16 retained features are those that best separate the very children on whom the classifiers are then evaluated. The consequence is stated in advance and with a supporting citation: 'the feature selection operated on clinical recorded data can lead to high performances of the classifier, which are not reproducible on new data considering all the speech production. This aspect produces a bias in the results obtained by the classifier when used to create a tool able to distinguish the speech productions of the disease. For instance, while performing the same task on people with Alzheimer Dementia's speech, Luz et al. (2020) report that the performance evaluation metrics drop consistently if applied to the same dataset without performing the feature selection.' The scope is then narrowed accordingly - 'this work aims to test the feature extraction effectiveness and not automatically classify ASD from new speech data' - which is the right response to a known bias, though it does not remove it from the reported numbers. Three further limits compound it: an 80/20 split leaves six test samples; ten runs per method were performed with the best reported alongside the means; and there is no independent validation, no permutation test, no confidence interval and no baseline. The single most important validity threat, however, is not statistical at all: features selected for their ability to separate two groups recorded on different equipment will select for the equipment difference, and no amount of validation discipline within the dataset can detect that.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Two distinct problems, one shared with several studies in this corpus and one specific to this paper. The shared problem is the unit of analysis: 547 images come from 59 children at roughly 9.3 images each, and the 80/20 partition is by image with no participant grouping described, so images from the same child appear in both training and test. Cilia and colleagues, who produced this dataset, measured the consequence directly, reporting image-level accuracy near 90% falling to approximately 71% when recomputed per child; that correction is neither cited nor applied here. The specific problem is that the headline figure pools phases: the abstract and conclusion report 99.8% while the results text states the same model achieved 100% in training and validation and 98.7% in testing, and describes 99.8% as 'the overall accuracy'. One element is handled correctly and deserves credit - augmentation by flipping, rotation, displacement and shearing was applied only to the training and validation partitions, expanding them from 175 and 262 to 1,750 and 1,834 images, while the test set remained unaugmented at 44 and 66. This is the correct discipline and is precisely what Gaspar and colleagues violated on the same dataset by augmenting the testing data as well. Against that, there is a single fixed split with no repetition, no cross-validation, no confidence intervals and no external validation, so the reported differences among six configurations rest on one partition of 109 test images.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: The split is child-disjoint and stated as such, which is the single most important property and is applied correctly even under a feature construction that generates heavily overlapping windows: 324 videos to training, 71 to validation and 54 to a held-out test set, 'ensuring that all videos corresponding to a single child were assigned to the same set'. Hyperparameters were selected on validation and only the three best configurations evaluated on the test set, so the held-out estimate is not tuned. Group comparisons are protected by permutation testing with Bonferroni correction across both feature families. Three limits remain. There is no independent cohort. There is no baseline or null for the classification results, which matters acutely given a test set of 43 autistic and 11 comparison videos where the majority-class weighted-average recall of roughly 0.80 exceeds the reported 0.656 - a comparison the paper does not make. And the split is by video within child rather than being balanced on any covariate, so with an unreported age span of 2 to 15 years the training and test partitions could differ substantially in age composition without this being detectable. The overall picture is a study that validates its statistical claims rigorously and its predictive claim only loosely, while describing the latter as mild.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: This is simultaneously the study's weakest and its most valuable dimension, because it fails and then measures its own failure. Three separate contaminations affect the headline analyses. Rotation augmentation was applied to all 547 images before partitioning, so rotated copies of the same source image appear in training and test. Principal component analysis was fitted on the complete 547x10,001 array (and later the 2,566x10,000 array) before splitting, so the components for the conventional models are informed by test images. And images from the same child span the partition regardless of augmentation, at roughly 9.3 per participant. The authors identify the first of these explicitly - 'possible data contamination as similar replicates are entered into the training set, as seen in the testing dataset' - and respond by constructing a one-image-per-participant subset evaluated by leave-one-out cross-validation, which removes both the augmentation and the within-child duplication. The result is 72.88% accuracy with 58.62% sensitivity, against 97.00% AUC in the contaminated condition. That within-study drop of roughly 24 points, produced by the same architecture on the same source images, is the cleanest quantification of validation-induced inflation available in this review, and its close agreement with the approximately 71% Cilia and colleagues obtained by the same correction on the same data amounts to an independent replication of the corrected figure. The remaining weakness is that the participant-level analysis itself is thin - 59 samples, one arbitrarily selected image per child, leave-one-out, no confidence interval - so 72.88% is 43 correct classifications and carries a wide interval.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Among the best-handled in the corpus on the dimensions the paper controls. Leakage is named explicitly and designed against: 'To avoid incorporating information from the distribution of the training data into the test set (i.e., data leakage), we carried out the following preprocessing steps separately for each test-train split of the data' - covering outlier removal, k-nearest-neighbour imputation, standardisation and SMOTE upsampling. Performing imputation and resampling inside the fold rather than on the full dataset is the correct handling and is violated by several studies here, including Liao and colleagues who select features on the whole sample and Kanhirakadavath and colleagues who fit principal components before splitting. The validation structure is genuine nested cross-validation - inner four-fold grid search selecting hyperparameters by AU-ROC, outer held-out fold estimating performance, repeated seven times for 28 estimates - so hyperparameter selection cannot contaminate the reported figures. Two residual issues. Feature selection was performed by inspecting importances across the 28 iterations and then retraining on the duration subset, so that selection used information from all folds; the effect is likely small since the selection is a binary family choice made on a large and statistically tested difference, but it is not nested. And the unit of analysis is not stated, so whether the folds are child-disjoint cannot be confirmed. Set against the corpus, the reported AU-ROC of 0.745 is modest precisely because these controls are in place, and the paper presents it as feasibility rather than accuracy.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: The weakest dimension, with three compounding problems. The split is by recording: 408 autistic and 428 comparison recordings train, the remainder test, described as randomly selected from 511 and 506 recordings originating in more than 80 and more than 60 children - so approximately six utterances per child are randomly assigned between the two sets and utterances from the same child appear on both sides. For one-second single-word samples from the same speaker in the same session, this approaches speaker identification rather than group classification, and it is the same failure that Kanhirakadavath and colleagues quantified on gaze images as a fall from 97% to 73% when the unit was corrected. There is no cross-validation of the classifier, no repetition and no confidence interval, so the reported figures come from one partition of 181 test recordings. And Method 2's headline of 59.71% is the best of 256 frequency sequences, chosen after inspecting all of them, with no correction and no report of the distribution across the other 255. Layered over all of this is the unresolved question of what the two ICA observation channels are: if the equations mean what they say, each unmixing matrix is estimated from a paired autistic and comparison utterance, so Method 1's features would be functions of a label-dependent pairing and the 98.51% would not measure classification at all. The paper provides no information with which to exclude that reading.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: Among the better-designed validations in the corpus for a regression problem, with one important limitation that is interpretive rather than procedural. The split is by child and repeated 50 times, and - distinctively - each split is constructed so that the ADOS score distribution matches the full sample on four moments: 'we divided the children into training and testing datasets while balancing the distribution of ADOS scores (mean, standard deviation, kurtosis, and skewness) in each dataset'. Matching skewness and kurtosis as well as mean and variance is the right control for a bimodally distributed target, since an unlucky split could otherwise place most of the low-scoring comparison children on one side and inflate or deflate the correlation. Reporting means and standard deviations across the 50 repetitions rather than a single split follows properly. Hyperparameters were tuned by random search under five-fold cross-validation, though whether that tuning sat inside the 50 outer splits or was performed once beforehand is not stated - which leaves some selection optimism unquantified. The substantive limitation is what the correlation measures rather than how it was estimated: computed across a sample where the autistic group averages ADOS 14.6 and the comparison group 3.2, R = 0.606 conflates between-group separation with within-group severity grading, and no within-autism correlation is reported. That is the analysis that would distinguish a severity estimator from a diagnostic classifier expressed on a continuous scale, and it is the same conflation this review has flagged in Kojovic and colleagues.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Not applicable in the machine-learning sense, since no model is fitted and no individual receives a predicted class - and the corresponding measurement-validation work is done properly. Six independent raters scored the same video material against definitions published in an appendix, inter-rater reliability was assessed with Kendall's W and reported at 0.65 (p < 0.001), and the Additional movements subscale returned an internal-consistency alpha of 0.77. Non-parametric tests appropriate to small ordinal samples were used throughout. The binding limitation is statistical power: with five children per group, only large effects are detectable, no confidence interval or effect size is reported, and nothing in the design supports individual-level inference - which is consistent with the study's own claims, since it asserts a group difference and a paradigm, not a classifier. Two internal-validity issues are unaddressed. Rater blinding to diagnosis is nowhere discussed, and since diagnoses were held in kindergarten records and every measurement is a human judgement, this is the study's main risk of bias. And no cognitive or language measure was obtained, so reduced turn-taking in a game requiring the child to understand the game cannot be separated from general developmental level. Set against the modelling studies in this review, however, the study has one structural advantage that no amount of downstream methodology can substitute for: its measurement instrument is published, its reliability is quantified, and its construct is named in advance.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: This is the paper's weak point and the reason its two headline numbers should be read very differently from each other. Segment level: tenfold cross-validation with random partition of segments. The text is unambiguous that the unit is the segment ('all behavior samples were randomly partitioned into 10 subsamples'), and there is no statement anywhere that a child's segments were kept together. With 19 + 20 children each contributing tens to hundreds of windows from one continuous recording, adjacent segments from one child are near-duplicates in feature space, and the classifier can exploit stable individual gaze idiosyncrasies - the exact leakage that Keles et al. in this corpus quantified directly by identifying individuals from gaze at 35.4% against 6.2% chance. So 74.15% is not an estimate of performance on an unseen child. Participant level: the aggregation is applied to those already-leaky segment labels, and then two further quantities are optimised on the same 39 children - the window length (10 candidates, Table 4 shows accuracies 0.77 to 0.87) and the threshold (a sweep whose grid is not specified, optimal values 0.40 to 0.56). Reporting the maximum of that joint search as the study's accuracy is best-of-many reporting; the median of Table 4 is 0.78. Feature selection is likewise unnested, run once on all data with the chosen subset reused in every fold. What the study does do right is the segment-level chance floor: the majority-class baseline is computed and plotted at every window length precisely because the class imbalance is group-linked, and the SVM beats it throughout. That is more care about chance than most studies here take, which makes the absence of the corresponding participant-level baseline or permutation test more conspicuous. A corrected design would partition the 39 children into folds, generate segments within folds, run forward feature selection inside each training fold, and select the window length and threshold on training children only - and would very likely report a materially lower number, as Cilia et al. found when they moved from image-level to participant-level evaluation of the same data.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Better than most on the split unit, weaker on everything downstream. The unit of splitting is the child - one aggregate feature vector per participant - so the segment-level leakage that inflates results throughout this corpus is impossible here by construction, and the paper deserves credit for that even though it is a consequence of the aggregate representation rather than a deliberate safeguard. The reported scheme is an 80/20 division with 5-fold cross-validation rotating which 20% is held out, giving fold test sets of about 9 children and averaged metrics. The problems lie elsewhere. First, feature selection: two consecutive rounds of backward elimination were run over the feature set, described in a section that precedes the results and with the surviving 10 features named as a fixed outcome, with no indication that the procedure was repeated within each training fold. Selecting 10 of 54 features on all 46 children and then cross-validating the chosen subset is a well-characterised source of optimism, and it is most severe exactly in this regime of many features and few samples - the regime the authors themselves identify as the reason feature reduction was needed. Second, model selection: three algorithms, three SVM kernels and four feature configurations were evaluated on the same 46 children, and the maximum of that grid is the abstract's claim. Third, no chance baseline: the majority class alone gives 60.9%, and no permutation test or confidence interval is reported, so with roughly 9 children per test fold a single child's label moves fold accuracy by 11 percentage points and the difference between the 78.61% and 85.56% configurations is a handful of children. Fourth, prevalence: 61% autism in the modelled sample against a population rate near 1-2%, with no prevalence-adjusted metric. The corrective design is straightforward and worth stating for the synthesis - move both backward-elimination rounds and the kernel/algorithm choice inside the training folds, report the mean and spread across folds rather than the best cell of the grid, add a majority-class and a permutation baseline, and retain the CP and fragile X children as a differential-diagnosis check.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: The critical weakness, and it is unacknowledged. The dataset is stated plainly: 60 participants x 25 tasks = 1,500 observations of 12 features, with a parallel 1,500-element label vector repeating each child's diagnosis 25 times. Cross-validation is 10-fold over that observation set, giving 91.2% +/- 5.6%. There is no statement that a child's 25 rows were assigned to a single fold, and the description ('we used the k-fold cross-validation with k = 10 and returning the average accuracy', applied to 'the collected dataset') implies observation-level partitioning. Under that scheme every test observation has roughly 22-23 siblings from the same child, same session and same hand in the training data, differing only in Leiter-3 subtest and difficulty level. Movement kinematics are strongly individual - speed and acceleration profiles are close to a motor signature - so a 12-input, 2-latent model can separate children rather than groups and score highly, exactly the leakage Keles et al. quantified directly elsewhere in this corpus by identifying individuals from behaviour at many times chance. Two internal signals support this reading: the authors themselves note that the clustering is 'even more evident' when participants are plotted as the mean of their tasks than task by task, which is what one expects when within-child consistency is high; and they never compute the participant-level accuracy that this observation invites. Secondary issues compound it. The choice of two latent dimensions was made from PCA on a latent space learned from the entire dataset. The class-conditional Gaussians used for the interpretability analysis and proposed as clinical thresholds are fitted to all 1,500 points. Only accuracy is reported. And the balanced 50/50 design, while making chance interpretable, is 25-50 times the population prevalence at which the proposed screening support would operate. The corrective is straightforward and would be a genuinely valuable result: split the 60 children into folds, train on one set of children and test on unseen children, report participant-level sensitivity and specificity as well as accuracy, and refit the latent Gaussians within training folds only. Given 60 children and a well-specified reference standard including ADOS-2, that study is within reach of this dataset.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: There is no validation strategy, and this is the study's decisive methodological gap. No training/test split, no cross-validation, no development set, no held-out participants: the five decision constants were set by hand and are reported on the same 30 children and 109 calls used to define them, and the single trained component, YOLOv3, was retrained on more than 1,700 images drawn from those same 30 subjects, so the person detector has seen every child it is subsequently evaluated on. Nothing in the paper estimates how the pipeline would behave on a child it has never encountered. Compounding this, no chance-agreement floor is computed although the data make one essential: with 17 of 30 children scoring 5 and each of those children contributing five non-response events, a trivial always-predict-non-response rule would already agree with the clinician on well over half the participants and on a substantially larger share of the 109 calls, so the 98.2% event-level figure is being reported against an unstated and high baseline. For an ordinal agreement problem the correct summary is a weighted kappa or ICC; accuracy without chance correction systematically overstates agreement in exactly this configuration. The 109 events are also treated as independent although they cluster within 30 children and are serially dependent by the protocol's own logic. Finally, the reference standard against which all of this is measured is a single unblinded clinician with no second rater, so even a perfectly validated system could only be shown to reproduce one person's uncorroborated judgements. The corrective study is well within reach of this group and would be worth more than the current numbers: fix the thresholds on a development subset, evaluate on children whose images never entered detector training, add a second blinded rater and report inter-rater reliability, and report weighted kappa alongside accuracy at both aggregation levels.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: The weakest element, and it fails on two counts that compound one another. First, the reported performance is not held-out. The abstract, results narrative and conclusion all quote 76.6% precision and 73.8% accuracy, which Table 5 identifies as the TOTAL column - the pooled figure across training, validation and test. The test column of the same table reads 66.7% precision and 58.3% accuracy, with sensitivity 57.1% and specificity 60.0%. The same pattern holds for every feature subset: total accuracies of 65.0-73.8% against test accuracies of 52.8-58.3%, with training accuracies of 67.9-78.6%. A roughly 20-point train-to-test gap in all four configurations is the signature of overfitting on a small dataset, and it is neither reported nor discussed. Second, the split is over observations rather than children. The paper says only that '70 percent of data ... were used for training and the remaining 30 percent for tests and validation', but the reported percentages determine the arithmetic exactly: with 240 rows split 168/36/36 in the MATLAB Neural Network Toolbox default proportions, 78.6% of 168 is 132, 66.7% of 36 is 24, 58.3% of 36 is 21, and (132 + 24 + 21)/240 = 73.75%, reproducing the reported total to the decimal, and the same reconstruction works for the other three subsets. Forty children therefore contribute six rows each, randomly scattered, so every test row has five siblings from the same child in the training set. Because the features are per-region fixation counts and durations - quantities that are highly stable within an individual and reflect that person's habitual looking style as much as their diagnosis - this is a direct channel for identity leakage, and it means even the 58.3% test figure is optimistic relative to a genuinely unseen child. Two further issues: four feature subsets were compared on the same data and the best reported, and no chance baseline, permutation test or confidence interval accompanies any figure, although the balanced design makes chance exactly 50% and the test partition is small enough that three observations separate the reported result from it. The corrective is available and would be worth doing: partition the 40 children, generate observations within partitions, tune the network on training children only, choose the feature subset on a development set, and report test-column figures with confidence intervals as the study's result.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: The strongest validation design encountered so far in this review, with one important caveat about how the result should be read. Each participant contributes exactly one feature vector, so the unit of splitting is the person by construction and the segment-level leakage that inflates most studies in this corpus is structurally impossible. Validation is nested cross-validation with a single tuned hyperparameter, the correlation window Tw over four candidate values, optimised inside the inner loop; the SVM's regularisation is left at its default rather than tuned, further reducing researcher degrees of freedom; and no feature selection is performed at all, so selection bias cannot arise despite 6,272 features. The outer evaluation is 10-fold cross-validation repeated 100 times with participant order shuffled between repetitions, which addresses fold-assignment variance - a source of instability that very few studies here even acknowledge. The identity-modelling step deserves separate credit as leakage control of a different kind: because the 3DMM estimates and removes facial identity, the representation is explicitly stripped of the individual-appearance information that, elsewhere in this corpus, silently drives high accuracy. The caveat is the base rate and the operating point. At 15 autistic and 27 neurotypical participants, majority-class prediction yields 64.3%, so 80.5% is a 16-point improvement rather than the 30 points a reader assuming balance might infer, and no permutation test or confidence interval is offered. The class imbalance also shapes the classifier: at sensitivity 0.55 and specificity 0.95 the model has learned to be conservative, so its accuracy is carried disproportionately by correctly identifying neurotypical participants. None of this undermines the study's actual claim - which concerns the non-overlap of AI and human errors, evaluated per participant - but it does mean the headline accuracy should not be read as evidence of a strong autism detector.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: Among the stronger validation designs in this corpus at the level of splitting, with two specific weaknesses further down the pipeline. The split unit is the subject: 50% of the 333 children are held out, so all 82 stimulus-based patterns from a child stay together and within-child leakage is structurally impossible - which matters here more than usual, because the model scores individual stimuli and a naive pattern-level split would have placed 41 of each test child's own patterns in training. The procedure is repeated over five random permutations with the minimum reported (95.76%), addressing split-assignment variance. The semantic autoencoder is trained on MS COCO rather than on participant data, so the representation learning introduces no leakage. Two ablation baselines are implemented on the same data rather than cited from other papers. Against this: first, the decision threshold is fitted transductively. The paper states that subject average scores were computed 'for each subject in training and testing' and the Otsu maximum between-class variance threshold selected on that combined distribution, and the same is described for the stimulus-level threshold. Otsu does not use labels, so this is not label leakage, but the operating point is nonetheless chosen with sight of the test subjects' score distribution, and in a deployment where children arrive one at a time no such distribution exists - the threshold would have to be fixed in advance from training data alone, and no result is reported under that constraint. Second, several choices were compared on the evaluation data with no separate development set: LSTM hidden units and fully connected size, epoch count, mini-batch size, learning rate, and the minLength lower bound, all reported in a single results table with the best configuration carried forward. The stimulus-discriminability ranking used to argue that 60 images suffice was likewise computed on the same data, so the proposed shortened protocol is selected in-sample. Third, no majority-class floor (57.6%) or confidence interval is given. None of these undermine the subject-level split, which is the hard part and is done correctly; they mean the 96.73% is a mildly optimistic estimate under a transductively chosen threshold rather than a fully prospective one.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: The weakest validation design in the corpus, and the failure is structural rather than marginal. A single random 75/25 split was applied to 90,000 tweets, with the tweet as the unit. Those tweets come from 252 users, so every user is represented on both sides of the split, and the imbalance makes this acute for the negative class: 31 comparison users supply all 45,000 non-autistic tweets, roughly 1,450 each, of which about 1,090 land in training and 360 in test. A model needs only to recognise those 31 writing styles - vocabulary, topics, habitual phrasings, recurring names, professional jargon, regional idiom - to classify the negative test set almost perfectly, and BERT is exactly the kind of model that will do so. The positive class is less concentrated at roughly 200 tweets per user but is leaky by the same mechanism. Nothing in the paper estimates performance on a writer the model has never seen, which is the only quantity relevant to the stated application. Compounding this: there is no cross-validation and no repeated split, so the single reported figure carries no stability estimate; hyperparameters were grid-searched with no validation set distinct from the test set; no chance baseline or confidence interval is given; and no user-level aggregation is performed, so the study never reports the metric its own use case requires. The corrective is simple and would be a genuinely informative experiment: hold out entire users, expand the comparison group well beyond 31 people, mask autism-related vocabulary, and report user-level sensitivity and specificity. On the current design, the 84.3% cannot be interpreted as evidence about autism at all.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Sound at the level that matters most and loose at the margins. The classifier uses leave-one-out cross-validation over participants, so the split unit is the child and no within-participant leakage is possible - though this is easier to achieve here than elsewhere because each participant contributes a single feature vector per movie rather than many segments. More importantly, the paper's primary claims are not predictive at all: they are group comparisons with effect sizes, supported by ANCOVA adjustment for two prespecified confounds and by an internal control condition (non-social movies), which is a design where cross-validation is not the relevant safeguard and where the reported statistics carry their own uncertainty. Three looser points. The classification analysis was restricted to the four social movies because the group comparisons on the same data had shown larger effect sizes there, so that restriction is in-sample; the effect is modest, since the choice was made on a prespecified social/non-social distinction rather than by searching over movies individually, but it should be stated. No class handling is described for the decision tree, and reported precision near 70% with recall near 89% cannot be produced from 40 autistic against 396 typically developing participants - so an undisclosed balancing or subsampling step exists, and without knowing it the accuracy figures cannot be placed against the correct baseline. And no majority-class baseline is given, which at 9.2% prevalence would be about 91%, so the reported 76-79% accuracies would be below trivial on the unbalanced sample and are only meaningful under whatever balancing was applied. None of this affects the study's principal finding, which rests on non-parametric group comparisons with large effect sizes, confound adjustment and an internal control - a design that is more robust than a cross-validated accuracy figure and that this corpus contains too few of.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: One of the two or three soundest validation designs in this review.
