The instructive point for the synthesis is that this inconsistency is detectable only because the study reported specificity and AUC alongside accuracy; the seven other studies charted here on the same corpus report accuracy alone or accuracy with precision and recall, and an identical internal contradiction in any of them would be invisible. If the specificity is the accurate figure, the model is below chance at identifying non-autistic children, and the paper's 95% headline conceals a result that would substantially undercut the branch's claims. The provenance confound in the corpus is untouched by any of this, since a model recognising autism-related web imagery would succeed on any partition.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: An 80:20 image-level split with no cross-validation, no separately described validation partition, and no participant-level partitioning; the number of distinct children behind 2,936 images is never stated. Augmentation by rotation, flipping and contrast adjustment is applied without specifying whether it preceded the split, and such variants of a single photograph are near-duplicates rather than independent observations. These are the standard weaknesses of this branch. What is distinctive here is a confound the mixed corpus introduces and the paper leaves entirely unexamined. The images come from two sources - Kaggle and an autism centre in Semarang - and neither the proportion from each nor their distribution across the two classes is reported. If the clinic supplied predominantly autistic images while the comparison class came predominantly from the international web collection, the classes would be separable by ancestry, camera, lighting and photographic convention without any facial phenotype being involved, and the reported 0.8299 would measure source rather than diagnosis. The paper's own account of what the network extracts - face shape, expression and skin texture - is consistent with that reading. The remedy is available and unused: with two identifiable sources in hand, a source-held-out evaluation, or simply a source-by-class table, would settle the question directly. Two elements of the analysis nonetheless stand above the branch norm: the learning curves are interpreted for stability and overfitting rather than displayed without comment, and the precision-recall trade-off across pairings is read in screening terms, with a high-precision low-recall model correctly judged 'less useful for finding all ASD cases'.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Stratified 5-fold cross-validation on 1,048,575 gaze-sample rows, stratified by class only. This is the review's clearest instance of within-participant leakage at the finest possible granularity: with 59 children and roughly 17,800 rows each, every test fold is virtually guaranteed to contain samples drawn from the same recording session, the same child and the same stimulus presentation as the training rows, differing by fractions of a second. A model can reach 99.78% by recognising individual children rather than autism. Three further defects compound it. First, mutual-information feature selection was run on the whole dataset before cross-validation, so the folds were chosen using their own test labels. Second, mean imputation of missing values was likewise computed over the whole dataset. Third, early stopping restores the weights that minimise loss on the same partition whose accuracy is then reported. The 0.11% standard deviation across folds is presented as evidence of stability; it is better read as confirmation that the five folds are near-identical resamples of one recording set. No participant-level split, no external cohort, and no held-out site is attempted anywhere in the paper.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: A single random 80/20 split: 593 training, 149 test. No cross-validation of the final model, no repeats, no seed, no stratification statement, no interval estimate. TPOT's internal search cross-validates within the training portion, so the pipeline choice is not directly contaminated by the test rows - a cleaner arrangement than most of this corpus - and the manual re-fit with the reported parameters confirms the pipeline is what it claims to be. Two problems dominate nonetheless. First, the validation design cannot address the label's circularity: no split scheme can turn the reconstruction of a checklist threshold into diagnostic accuracy. Second, the test set is 71.1% positive and the paper never states the majority-class baseline, even though it prints it - the SVM comparator's recall of 1.000 at precision 0.718 and accuracy 0.71 is the all-positive classifier, sitting unremarked in the comparison table as though it were a genuine competitor. Read against that baseline, the AUTOML pipeline's contribution is about 12 accuracy points, and the non-autistic recall of 0.53 shows where its errors fall - on precisely the children a screening tool exists to reassure.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: An 80-20 stratified image-level split (2,020 / 506) with 5-fold cross-validation inside the training portion. The cross-validation placement is correct in principle and better than most of this branch. Four problems undo it. First, the split is image-level, not child-level, on a corpus known to contain repeated faces, so the same child can appear on both sides. Second, augmentation by rotation and scaling is described as part of preprocessing rather than as applied within training folds only. Third, and most serious, the headline numbers do not come from the 506-image test set at all: 200 images (100 ASD, 100 non-ASD) were selected from the test set for the final evaluation, with no selection rule stated, which is the definition of a hand-picked evaluation subset - and the accompanying confusion matrix nonetheless totals 300. Fourth, every reported metric is presented as a monotone function of epoch count with the maximum always at the largest value tried (500), and no criterion determined where to stop, so the reported figures are the best point on a curve rather than the output of a prespecified procedure. The cross-validation folds, having been run, are never reported as a mean and standard deviation.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: The design is a 70:15:15 partition of 4,000 eye images derived from 40 children at exactly 100 images per child (50 frames, left and right eye). Because the per-child image count is constant and the split is at the image level, every participant is present in the training, validation and test subsets simultaneously; more finely still, the left and right eye of the same video frame - two crops of one instant of one recording - can land on opposite sides. This is frame-level leakage of the same kind documented in the video, EEG-epoch, thermal, cry and facial-image branches, and it is sufficient to explain a 97% four-class result from 40 children. Three further weaknesses compound it. Augmentation by rotation and shearing is described as a dataset-preparation step applied before partitioning. Cross-validation is asserted four separate times as ensuring robustness, but no fold count, no per-fold result and no variance is ever reported, so it cannot be assessed and may not have been run on the final model. And the external comparison in Table 7 places this study's four-class severity accuracies (95.93%, 97.95%) beside Saliency4ASD entries (74.22%, 65.41%, 61.62%) that solve a different, binary ASD-versus-TD task on different data - the numbers are not commensurable, and the higher figure is not evidence of a better method. To the authors' credit, the abstract itself concedes that further evaluation on an independent dataset will assess the generalizability and precision of the model, which is the correct reading of their own result.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: The validation account is internally contradictory, and this is the study's central defect. The experimental section reports confusion matrices at five epoch settings whose correct-classification counts - 1,338 normal plus 1,362 autism at 1,000 epochs, and comparable figures at the other settings - account for essentially the entire stated dataset. No train-test division is described anywhere in that section. If those matrices are computed over all available images, then every reported metric is a resubstitution figure on the training data. Separately and much later, the comparison discussion asserts that 5-fold cross-validation was applied with 80% training and 20% testing per fold, and that the model consistently attained elevated accuracy and F1 scores across all folds, exhibiting minimal variance - yet not one per-fold number, mean or standard deviation is given, so the claim cannot be checked and does not reconcile with the confusion-matrix counts. On top of that: the reported headline is the best of five epoch settings with no selection criterion or held-out basis; the Crested Porcupine Optimizer searched hyperparameters against an unstated objective on an unstated partition; augmentation is described before any split; and the split, whatever it is, is at the image rather than the child level on a corpus known to repeat faces. The comparison in Table 3 sets this study's figure against seven baselines taken from other publications on unstated data and protocols, which is a comparison of numbers rather than of methods.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: This is the review's clearest case of a metric grid resting on almost nothing. The entire empirical base is 44 examples. Those are divided among three simulated federated clients by a rule that is never stated, and each client's reported accuracy is computed on nine test cases - a number that appears nowhere in the text and must be reconstructed from the confusion matrices (6+2+1+0 = 9; 6+3 = 9) and from the quantisation of every tabulated accuracy to multiples of one ninth. On nine cases the standard error of an accuracy estimate is roughly 17 percentage points, so the difference between the paper's best result (1.00, reported as 99.99%) and its worst (0.11) is barely more than sampling noise, and the four-subset by three-client by two-scenario by two-model grid amounts to dozens of comparisons among estimates that cannot be distinguished from each other. Three further problems compound it. Class-conditional mean imputation was applied across the full dataset, writing outcome information into the predictor matrix. SHAP-based feature selection was likewise performed on the whole dataset before the federated runs. And no split ratio, seed, cross-validation or repetition is reported, so none of the figures carries a variance estimate. Finally, the headline itself is unstable across the paper: the abstract credits 99.99% to Client 2 and 88% to Client 1, the contributions list credits 88% to Client 3, and the results section reports the best configuration as accuracy 1.00 - three descriptions of the same experiment. The framing of nine correct classifications out of nine as flawless classification performance and as high diagnostic accuracy suitable for healthcare applications is not supportable at any sample size this study has.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: A single 70/20/10 division at the image level - 369, 105 and 51 images per class - applied to 1,050 photographs from 70 children at exactly 15 photographs each. Participant separation is therefore impossible: five near-identical shots of the same child pulling the same expression, taken minutes apart under fixed lighting at a fixed one-metre distance with the same camera settings, are distributed across training, validation and test. This is the same frame-level leakage documented across the video, EEG-epoch, thermal, cry and facial-image branches of this review, and it is the study's decisive methodological failure - the more so because the acquisition protocol is so tightly controlled that the only systematic variation left between images of different children is the children themselves. Three further points. The split is unrepeated and unseeded, with no cross-validation and no interval on any figure. Training and validation accuracy are reported as reaching nearly 100% within the first few epochs with loss near zero, described as optimal and stable performance without signs of overfitting, while held-out accuracy is 90% - a gap the paper reads as success rather than as evidence about the split. And group membership is perfectly confounded with institution, since all autistic children were photographed at a special school and all comparison children at a state school, so any residual site difference in setup, operator or child preparation is available to the classifier. What would have rescued the design is available and unused: with 70 children, a participant-level split holding out, say, 7 autistic and 7 typically developing children entirely would have cost nothing and produced an interpretable, if less impressive, number.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: The validation section is, in most respects, the most carefully constructed in this review's questionnaire branch. A stratified 70/10/20 split is used, the roles of the three partitions are stated explicitly (fitting, hyperparameter tuning and model selection, final reporting), Bayesian optimisation is cross-validated inside the training data only, the test set is described as never used during training or tuning, and the author pre-empts the overfitting objection directly, listing four mitigations. Two problems defeat all of that care. The first is ordering: SVM-SMOTE was applied to the whole 1,054-case dataset before partitioning, expanding it to 1,456 instances, and only then was the balanced dataset randomly partitioned. Synthetic minority instances are interpolations between real minority cases, so synthetic rows in the training set are constructed from real rows that ended up in the test set, and synthetic rows in the test set are constructed from real training rows. The hold-out is therefore not independent, and this alone can produce near-perfect minority-class recall. The second is the estimand: the label Class/ASD_Traits is the Q-CHAT-10 outcome, a deterministic threshold on the sum of ten items that are supplied as features. No split scheme can make the reconstruction of that threshold into a diagnostic accuracy. Together these explain a result that the paper instead attributes to methodological quality - 292 of 292 test cases correct, zero false positives and zero false negatives, reported as 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity and as confirming suitability for reliable clinical screening. The external comparison in Table III compounds this by ranking the 100% against literature figures of 97.15%, 97.82% and 93.69% from other datasets and protocols, presenting the gap as a methodological advance.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Phase I follows the familiar pattern: an 80:20 split plus 10-fold cross-validation over data whose label is a threshold on the summed predictors, with SMOTE applied at an unstated point relative to the split and feature selection of unstated nesting. Row counts are absent at every stage, so no reported figure can be located to a sample. That much places the study alongside local_ed30e24c, local_8253c2ec and local_a0d73248 in the circular-label group. Phase II is a different and more serious matter, and it is the reason this record exists. The teaching-method target did not come from any school, therapist, assessment or record: the paper states that a new column named Teaching Method was added to the dataset using the numpy library, containing integers 1 to 6 for six specialised teaching methods plus 0 for no special education needed, and that these were assigned on the basis of severity as analysed from the Q-CHAT-10 score, which is the count of the A1-A10 values. The models are then trained to predict that manufactured column from the other columns - including A1 to A10 themselves. The reported 0.9917 accuracy therefore measures how well a classifier reproduces an arithmetic rule that the authors wrote, applied to the very features they wrote it from. It is not an estimate of anything about children, education or autism; a lookup table would score 1.00. Compounding this, the mapping from severity band to intervention (Pivotal Response Training for high-level, technology-aided instruction for moderate-to-high, PECS for moderate, task analysis for low-to-moderate, Intensive Behavioral Intervention for low) is asserted with no evidence base, no clinical input and no citation, and it inverts the usual intensity gradient by assigning the most intensive intervention to the least affected group. The results are then offered to educators and professionals as a basis for informed decisions about teaching methods that can have a significant impact on the children's learning and development. The merged two-region design offered a genuine external-validation opportunity - train on one cohort, test on the other - and it is not taken.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: The validation design is under-reported - no split proportions, no value of k, no per-fold results, no statement of whether feature selection and tuning were nested inside the training partition, and a passage stating that the manually tuned model is then trained and evaluated on the dataset to ensure generalization, which describes tuning and evaluating on the same data. The confusion matrices imply a 317-record test partition but disagree on its class composition across models (105/212 for three of them, 110/207 for the ANN). Underneath that, the estimand is the branch's usual one: Class/ASD traits is the Q-CHAT-10 outcome and Q1-Q10 are its summands, so predicting the former from the latter is arithmetic recovery. What makes this study analytically valuable to the review is that its own feature-subset experiment maps the circularity almost completely without naming it. Subsets 3 and 4 retain the Qchat-10-Score and discard the items; Q1-Q10 retains the items and discards the total; Subset 2 retains both, and the author observes that this could sometimes mislead the model results. Every configuration containing either the total or its summands performs well, and the reported conclusion - that Q1-Q10 alone gives optimal performance with 41% fewer features - is a statement about which encoding of the label's own arithmetic is most compact. The single most revealing number in the paper is in the iterative analysis: with only the two least significant features, age and sex, sensitivity was 99.5%. With 69.1% of records positive, that is what a near-all-positive classifier produces, and the surrounding text treats it as a baseline from which adding Q1 (sensitivity 97.6%) and Q2-Q4 (92.8%, 91.3%) represents degradation. Read correctly it demonstrates that sensitivity alone is uninformative on this dataset and that the majority-class baseline is 69.1% accuracy - neither point is made, and no chance level appears anywhere in the article.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: The validation design is the most rigorous in the charted corpus and is reported operationally rather than by name. Two-layer 4-fold cross-validation: 601 participants divided into four partitions that are disjoint at the participant level and stratified so that each spans the full score range; in each of four trials, two partitions train, one validates and one tests, with roles rotating so that every partition serves as test exactly once; for models with tunable hyperparameters, candidates are fitted on the training partitions, selected by MAE on the validation partition, then refitted on training plus validation before a single prediction on the untouched test partition; the four test MAEs are averaged. Hyperparameter selection therefore never sees the test data, the analysis unit is the person, and no participant contributes to both sides of any split - the three failures that account for most of the inflated figures elsewhere in this review are all absent here. Two real limitations remain. The first is the one the paper does not name: predictors and outcomes are self-report questionnaires completed by the same person in the same sitting, so the correlations are inflated by common-method variance, and there is direct construct overlap between camouflaging items (which describe effortful management of social interaction) and the BAPQ Aloofness and Pragmatic Language subscales (which measure social and pragmatic difficulty). The R=.85 for Aloofness should be read as agreement between two overlapping self-descriptions of social experience, not as prediction of an independently ascertained trait - which is precisely why the anxiety and depression models, whose outcomes are less conceptually adjacent to camouflaging, drop to .54 and .58. The authors explain that gap through instrument structure; construct proximity is at least as plausible. The second is that no external cohort is tested, which the paper itself insists on before any clinical use. Set against the corpus, this study is the reference point: a properly nested, participant-level, model-selection-clean design applied to a genuinely dimensional target yields R=.85 at best and .54 at worst, with only 36% of individual predictions landing within 5% of the truth - the realistic ceiling against which the 99% and 100% figures elsewhere in this review should be read.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: A single image-level split of 2,926 images into 2,526 training, 200 validation and 200 test, with no cross-validation, no repetition, no seed and no description of how the split was drawn. Three problems follow. First, the corpus is the widely reused web-scraped autism face collection, which contains duplicate and near-duplicate images of the same individuals; the paper demonstrates awareness of exactly this, noting that a cited study cleaned duplicates from the dataset using the MD5 hash algorithm, and then does not deduplicate, so images of the same child can sit on both sides of the split. Second, the test set is 200 images, giving a 95% confidence interval around 91% of roughly 86-95% - wide enough to contain the great majority of the comparison entries the paper ranks itself above, including MobileNet-V1 at 90.67 and Xception at 92.01, so the reported ordering is not supported. Third, validation accuracy is 4.5 points below test accuracy on partitions of equal size, an inversion that normally indicates split variance rather than generalisation and is reported without remark. Underneath all three sits the problem the whole benchmark line shares and this paper states approvingly: the models being compared have a solid common foundation because they use the same dataset - a dataset with no diagnostic labels, no provenance and no demographic information. A common foundation of that kind makes the numbers comparable to each other and to nothing else.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: This study's decisive problem is that the reported result does not come from its stated evaluation design. The methods define an image-level split of 2,940 images into 2,540 for training and 400 for testing, balanced within each. The results section then states that out of 2,940 images used for evaluation the model correctly classified 1,430 autism images and 1,420 non-autism images, 2,850 correct with 90 misclassified - and 2,850/2,940 is precisely 96.94%, the headline accuracy carried into the abstract and the comparison table. The reported performance is therefore a resubstitution figure computed over the whole dataset, with 86% of the evaluated images having been used to fit the model. The 400-image test set is defined and never used to produce a number. Three further issues compound this. The corpus is the web-scraped autism face collection that repeats individuals, so even a correctly executed image-level split would not separate children. The Fire Hawk Optimizer tuned unspecified parameters against an unspecified objective on an unspecified partition. And the comparison table ranks 96.94% against five literature figures spanning 92.0% to 96.63% obtained on different image counts (2,636 to 3,014) under unstated protocols, with the paper asserting that the comparisons are done under the same conditions used in the existing methods to ensure fair comparison - a claim that cannot hold when this study's own figure is a training-set score.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: On the axes that defeat most of this literature, the design is sound. The analysis unit is the child, the folds partition children, there is no within-participant leakage, hyperparameters are grid-searched, per-fold results are published, model differences are tested with Wilcoxon signed-rank and Friedman statistics rather than eyeballed, and the k-NN sweep is reported. The authors then did what almost no one in this corpus does: they distrusted their own result. Concerned about the potential for overfitting given exceptionally high metrics, they re-ran the full comparison at 2, 4 and 5 folds, observed that the neural network scored perfectly at 4 and 5 folds but fell to 0.8691 at 2, and noted that this indicates a potential risk of overfitting to specific data characteristics. That is the right instinct pointed at the wrong object. Varying the fold count tests partition sensitivity; it cannot detect leakage that lives in the feature set. Here the feature set contains four separate instrument measurements of the target condition - CARS, SRS, AQ10 and Q-CHAT-10 - plus the item-level constituents of the AQ-10 total, all predicting a binary ASD_traits label. Under those conditions accuracy 1.0000 is not overfitting; it is the model reading the answer off the input, and no resampling scheme will change it. Two further issues compound this. The preprocessing removed 68% of the records and a third of the variables through expert identification of inconsistencies and erroneous data, performed on the whole dataset before cross-validation and with no stated criterion, no per-class counts and no indication of outcome blinding - a step credited in the abstract with improving generalizability. And the class balance is never reported, so neither a majority-class baseline nor a prAUC reference exists, and the perfect scores cannot be positioned against anything. The abstract's claim that rigorous preprocessing improved real-world applicability across diverse clinical datasets is made from a single dataset with no external cohort.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: The validation is participant-level and structurally correct: stratified 5-fold cross-validation over 93 children, one row per child, no within-participant duplication, and no clinical instrument score anywhere in the feature set. Three caveats qualify the numbers rather than invalidate them. First, dimensionality - the full dataset carries 158 variables for 93 children, and even the smallest carries 24, so the models operate in a regime where cross-validated estimates over five folds are noisy; no interval or fold variance is reported. Second, selection - the headline figures are the best over four feature sets crossed with several algorithms and four group comparisons, with no correction and no held-out cohort, so they are optimistic by an unquantified margin. Third, confounding - the clinical groups are approximately 92% male against 50% in the TD group (chi-squared 20.15, p<0.01) and differ significantly in receptive vocabulary and basic attention, all of which are plausible correlates of gaze behaviour in a paired-preference task; none is adjusted for, so part of the 0.86 and 0.912 against TD may reflect sex and language ability rather than diagnosis. The result that survives all of this is the one the authors themselves foreground: ASD versus DLD reaches only F1 0.63, at nearly balanced class sizes, and they conclude that the approach is more effective as a screening tool than for differential diagnosis. That conclusion is the correct reading of their own data and is the most valuable single sentence in this part of the corpus, because the two comparisons are internally controlled - same task, same equipment, same pipeline, same analyst - so the gap between 0.86 against typical development and 0.63 against another neurodevelopmental condition isolates how much of the apparent signal is autism-specific rather than clinical-population-general.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: The preprocessing order is handled correctly - the dataset is split before augmentation, and augmentation is applied during training via ImageDataGenerator - which is better than several neighbours in this corpus. Everything else about the evaluation undercuts the result. The split is at the image level on a scanpath collection in which each child contributes multiple images, so images generated from the same child's viewing session sit on both sides of the partition; this is the same within-participant leakage documented across the video, EEG-epoch, thermal, cry and facial-image branches, and it is sufficient to explain a perfect score. The test partition holds 55 images, a figure the paper never states and that must be recovered from a support column, so every reported metric carries roughly plus or minus 11 to 13 percentage points of sampling noise; MobileNet's 100% means 55 of 55 correct. There is no cross-validation, no repetition and no seed, and the spread across four architectures trained identically on the same data - 100%, 92%, 78% and the hybrid - is itself evidence of how unstable a 55-image estimate is, though the paper reads it as a genuine ranking of methods. The comparison against three prior studies on the same dataset (87%, 90%, 79%) is attributed to a different preprocessing approach, when the more parsimonious explanation is that the earlier figures came from evaluations that were less permissive. Finally, the paper never describes the viewing task behind the scanpaths, so it cannot exclude that the classifier is recognising which stimulus produced a trace rather than who produced it.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: There is no validation design to assess. The article describes no train-test split, no cross-validation, no held-out set and no test-set size; it never states how many records the dataset contains or what its class balance is; and its results are presented as curves of accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and F1 against iteration count (20 to 80) and training percentage (70%, 80%), with the abstract's 95.3% / 96.5% / 94.8% taken from the best region of those curves. Reading performance off the maximum of a sweep is model selection on the reported quantity, and here there is not even a stated partition on which the sweep is evaluated. Underneath that sits the estimand: the label is a threshold on the sum of the ten Q-CHAT-10 items supplied as features, so the task is reconstruction of a checklist rule regardless of how the data are partitioned. The contrast with the rest of this branch is instructive. local_ed30e24c reached a flawless 292 of 292 with all items retained and pre-split SMOTE; local_14df790d reached 0.99 and mapped the mechanism through its feature-subset comparison; local_8ff20c48 fell to 0.83 after deleting five items. This study reports 95.3% after an unreported metaheuristic selection of an unreported number of features - a figure whose position in that range is determined by how much of the label's arithmetic the optimiser happened to retain, which the paper does not report and therefore cannot interpret.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: The validation design is participant-level and honestly reported, with three qualifications that the review should record rather than treat as disqualifying. The structure is correct: an 80/20 split of participants, with test accuracy computed on held-out people and reported for each of three algorithms and as their mean, and with the entire configuration grid published so that the reported maximum sits visibly among its alternatives, including two models at chance. The qualifications are, first, size - 63 participants in the ASD-versus-PD contrast and 94 in clinical-versus-non-clinical give test partitions of roughly 13 and 19 people, so a 0.93 mean accuracy corresponds to about 12 of 13 correct and carries a confidence interval running from roughly 0.66 to 1.00; no interval is reported. Second, selection - the discriminatory kinematic feature sets were defined by group-difference significance from mixed models fitted on all participants, so configurations using those sets saw the held-out participants' labels during feature selection and are optimistically biased; the all-kinematic-features configurations are unaffected, and the paper's own observation that variability was seen in whether discriminatory or all features yielded stronger accuracy is consistent with the selection buying less than it might. Third, no external cohort, which the authors acknowledge by describing the work as proof-of-concept. Set against the corpus, what makes this study valuable is not its accuracy figure but its structure: the negative result is the primary finding, it is supported by Bayesian evidence for the null rather than by absence of significance, and the classification is offered as a secondary demonstration rather than as a diagnostic claim.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: The evaluation is stratified 10-fold cross-validation at the record level with early stopping and class weighting, supported by three quantified sensitivity analyses - imputation method, severity thresholds perturbed by 5%, domain weights perturbed by 10% - showing macro-F1 stable within 0.6% and kappa within 0.03. That is more robustness checking than any other study in this branch performs. But the estimand is settled before any of it, and the paper states the conclusion itself: the severity labels are deterministically derived from the same behavioural attributes used as model inputs, so the task is function approximation and the accuracy figures are not diagnostic accuracy. Read that way, the results are internally coherent and even informative - a BiLSTM recovers a four-way threshold on a weighted sum of ten items with 97-99% accuracy, and simpler models recover it with 90-94%, which quantifies how much architectural capacity the reconstruction of a piecewise-linear scoring rule requires. Three residual issues qualify even that reading. The domain weights were calibrated on the full dataset by optimising kappa against expert labels before cross-validation, so the labelling function itself was fitted to the data the model is then evaluated on. SHAP-based feature pruning was likewise applied to the whole dataset and necessarily requires a fitted model. And the expert calibration - the only external anchor in the study - reports kappa 0.72 without stating how many records were expert-labelled, by whom, or with what instrument, so the one bridge between the constructed label and clinical severity is itself unspecified. Compared against the branch, the difference is not in the estimand but in the interpretation: local_ed30e24c reported 292 of 292 correct as confirming suitability for reliable clinical screening; local_b9de0d7f offered a numpy-generated teaching-method label at 0.9917 to educators; this study reports 99.10% and states in four separate places that it does not mean what it appears to mean.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: The validation section contains, in isolation, the most methodologically literate paragraph of any weak study in this review: a 70/15/15 partition with strict subject-level separation to avoid leakage across folds, stratified sampling to preserve class distribution, Youden-index thresholding on validation data, clinically meaningful metrics including PPV and NPV and calibration, paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, ablation of the MRI-only modality, runtime measurement with means and standard deviations, and a subject-level deletion threat model under which the unlearned model should remain statistically indistinguishable from one retrained without the deleted data, audited by removing specified subjects and validating forgetting against deletion audit sets. Every element of that is the right thing to do. None of it can be assessed, because the article does not report a single number from any of it and because the data description it would apply to is self-contradicting - 10,000 MRI samples yielding 25,000 positive cases, a 25,000-to-1,200 split called class balance, six partitions in one section and four in another, three mutually exclusive age ranges. The experiments are moreover described throughout as simulation results, and the only quantitative outputs shown are before-and-after bar charts binned into low, medium and high. The gap between the methodological vocabulary and the reported evidence is the finding here: this is the corpus's clearest instance of validation language functioning as a genre convention rather than as a description of work performed.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: The evaluation is better constructed than most in this corpus and still cannot support the claim the title makes. On the credit side: k-fold cross-validation with per-fold standard deviations reported for all five architectures, an independent test evaluation with its own confusion matrix, identical hyperparameters across models to make the comparison fair, and paired t-tests against every baseline at a corrected threshold. On the debit side, three things. First, the unit: 75 source videos are segmented into clips and the k-fold matrix covers 303 samples, with no video-level or child-level grouping described, so clips from the same recording - same child, same room, same camera, same clothing - fall on both sides of every fold. In naturalistic video this is the strongest available shortcut, because recording identity is far easier to learn than movement type. Second, the reported stability is read backwards: standard deviations below 0.004 across five different architectures are presented as robustness, whereas over clips from 75 videos they indicate that the folds contain much the same material. Third, and separately from any of this, the task is not the task claimed. Four-way discrimination among arm flapping, head banging, spinning and other movement, in videos of children who are all autistic, cannot yield screening for ASD, because no non-autistic person appears anywhere in the data - a screening claim requires a comparison the design does not contain. The paper's own hedge, that the system is intended as a clinical decision support system and not an independent diagnostic system, is the correct reading and sits uneasily beside a title placing the work in diagnoses of ASD and an abstract promising effective screening.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: This is the most rigorously validated study in the charted corpus, and its result is the corpus's most useful single number. The design is five-fold nested cross-validation with participant-independent splits, class balance preserved within folds, hyperparameter selection confined to the inner loop, retraining on the full training portion before a single outer-fold evaluation, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals on every estimate, and a per-fold majority-class baseline included specifically to test whether the features beat class distribution. Each child contributes multiple samples across stories, modalities and phases, and the participant-independent split is what prevents that from becoming the leakage that inflates most of this literature. The outcome is 64.1% F1 and 64.5% AUC at best and around 55% in most conditions - and the authors state plainly that this positions the work as a research exploration rather than a deployable diagnostic tool, given that benchmarks for clinical viability often exceed 80-90%. Two qualifications remain. The sample is 45 children, and the paper repeatedly notes that the limited number of observations prevents modality differences from reaching significance. And the ASD group's receptive vocabulary is markedly lower (PPVT-III 50.0 versus 67.3), which is measured and reported but not adjusted for in a task requiring comprehension of narrated stories - so part of the gaze difference may be a comprehension difference. Neither qualification changes the study's value to this review, which is calibrative: run with correct participant-level nesting, an explicit trivial baseline, confidence intervals and a purpose-designed social-attention paradigm, eye-tracking classification of autism in children reaches the low sixties.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: The two datasets require separate verdicts. On Dataset 1 the pipeline ordering is right and is unusually well documented: a stratified 60:20:20 split precedes SMOTE, SMOTE is applied only to the training portion and only when the class ratio falls below 0.8, and the paper states this explicitly as preventing data leakage - the ordering that local_ed30e24c got wrong and that most of this branch does not discuss. What the ordering cannot repair is the feature set, which contains the Autism Spectrum Quotient, the Social Responsiveness Scale, the Q-CHAT score and the Childhood Autism Rating Scale as predictors of a binary ASD-traits label. The same dataset produced accuracy 1.0000 for local_183eaef4; here it produces 97.60%, and the difference is attributable to preprocessing choices rather than to anything about autism. Dataset 2 is worse in kind. Its 100 original clinical samples were augmented fourfold to 400, and the stratified 80/10/10 split and 5-fold cross-validation were applied to the augmented set - so rotated, pitch-shifted, coordinate-scaled and noise-added copies of the same clinical sample sit on both sides of the split. The test partition therefore holds 40 samples, of which perhaps ten correspond to distinct originals, evaluated against a 4,220-dimensional feature vector. The reported 98.2% is roughly 39 of 40 correct on data the model has seen transformed versions of. It is also not a detection result: Dataset 2 contains four severity classes and no non-ASD class, so the abstract's presentation of 98.2% accuracy alongside the behavioural detection figure conflates a four-way severity task with binary ASD identification. Neither dataset carries a confidence interval, and the 63.28% majority-class baseline available in the paper's own Table 2 is never used.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: This is one of the two most rigorously evaluated studies in the charted corpus, and its distinctive contribution is the demographic-confounding analysis. The design uses a train/test split with 3-fold cross-validated grid search for hyperparameters and monitors overfitting by the train-test performance gap; adds a label-randomisation control that falls to chance, empirically establishing the baseline rather than assuming it; and declines to resample, stating that neither SMOTE nor undersampling was used. Its decisive move is to run the entire analysis twice - once on the full unbalanced sample and once on a subsample matched 100% on age and gender at 125 per group - and then to report the matched result as primary, stating that performance in the unmatched sample is inflated by the inclusion of age and gender as features given the disparity between groups in those factors. The difference is large: 81.8% unmatched against 74.0% matched, so roughly eight accuracy points in this study were attributable to demographic confounding alone. That number is directly relevant to the rest of this review, in which sex imbalances of 32 points (local_4ceee075) and 43 points (local_7432ffd7) between groups are reported and left unadjusted, and it is the only quantification of that effect anywhere in the corpus. Residual limitations: no confidence intervals or fold variance accompany the final estimates; the matched subsample is 250 people; diagnosis is self-reported rather than verified, albeit through a national register; and 407 of 959 recruited participants were excluded for missing data, which may not be at random. None of these undermines the study's central results, and the authors identify the most important of them themselves.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: The design gets the structural question right and is limited by size rather than by construction. Subject-wise aggregation and evaluation are adopted explicitly to prevent data leakage and to provide a more realistic estimate of generalisation in clinical settings, and this is listed as one of the paper's four stated contributions - a rare instance in the eye-tracking branch of participant-level splitting being treated as a design requirement rather than overlooked. Set against the branch, that choice is what separates this study's 0.96 on 28 people from local_44d3aef5's 1.00 on 55 scanpath images and local_bb4d1f7a's 0.97 on 100 eye crops per child. Three qualifications remain. First, size: 28 participants across five folds gives test sets of five or six, and the reported standard deviations (0.08 accuracy, 0.095 F1) reflect that directly - the estimate is not wrong, it is imprecise, and the paper says as much in calling the work a proof of concept. Second, the within-subject resampling: additional subject-level samples were generated by resampling scanpaths within each subject and recomputing the aggregated representation, described as occurring during model training; if that augmentation was performed before the fold split rather than inside it, several aggregated vectors derived from the same participant's scanpaths would cross the partition and the subject-wise protocol would be undermined by the very step intended to increase sample diversity. The paper's wording suggests the correct placement but does not state it unambiguously. Third, the source cohort is uncharacterised - no task, no equipment, no diagnostic procedure, no demographics - so what the classifier separates cannot be independently assessed.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: The evaluation is thinly described and internally inconsistent. The dataset is said to be divided into three groups for testing, validation and training, with the reasoning that such splitting reduces the bias and overfitting possibility - and no ratio, no partition size, no seed and no cross-validation follows. The split is at the image level on a corpus whose per-child composition is unknown, and whose 14,352 images most plausibly derive by augmentation from a much smaller set of underlying photographs, since Roboflow's augmentation was applied at export rather than during training; if so, transformed variants of the same photograph sit on both sides of the partition. Training and evaluation are said to have been carried out multiple times with highly consistent results, and no variance figure supports that claim. Most concretely, the two mAP figures cannot both be genuine: mAP@0.5:0.95 within 0.11 points of mAP@0.5 is arithmetically achievable only under near-perfect localisation at IoU 0.95, which is not attainable here. And the informal robustness probe demonstrates directly that the system's decision surface extends to objects that are not faces, which no reported metric captures.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: The evaluation rests on a single image-level partition of 2,940 photographs into 70% training and 30% testing, with no cross-validation, no repetition, no seed and no statement of how the split was drawn. The corpus repeats individuals, so an image-level split does not separate children, and the number of distinct children is unknown - the same defect documented across the other fifteen members of this branch. Two further features are specific to this paper. First, the accuracy inversion: the testing phase reports 98.42% against the training phase's 97.75%, and the learning curves show validation accuracy exceeding training accuracy, which the authors interpret as evidence of good generalisation. The more usual explanation on this corpus is that the partitions are not independent. Second, the chimp optimisation algorithm tuned the classifier's parameters against an unstated objective on an unstated partition, so the reported test figure may be the outcome of a search evaluated on the data it is then reported against. On top of this, the comparison against seven quoted literature figures (92.10% to 97.76%) is drawn from other papers under unknown protocols, and no component of the four-stage pipeline is ablated.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: The evaluation is competently constructed at the child level - 5-fold cross-validation with a fold standard deviation reported, plus two 20% held-out sets one of which is reserved solely for final validation, and an explicit statement that neither constitutes independent external validation because both are reserved subsets from the same data distribution with the same sensor, protocol and feature pipeline. Against most of this corpus that is exemplary. The decisive issue is the severe class, and the paper states it before any reader could raise it: because no Kinect recordings exist for the nine severe-ASD children, the severe class's feature vectors were created by averaging moderate ASD vectors and adding Gaussian noise. A classifier separating that construction from real moderate data is separating a smoothed, noise-perturbed version of one distribution from the distribution itself, which is a task with a known answer and no clinical content - and the author says so, writing that the 100% result reflects the ability to distinguish real moderate ASD motor data from an artificially constructed distribution, not true clinical severity levels. The 4-of-4 result carries a 95% confidence interval from 39.8% to 100.0%, which the author computes, reports and interprets. Two further qualifications apply to the real two-class portion: 463 features for 109 children is a high-dimensional regime with roughly 87 training cases, and the three-class majority baseline of about 45.9% is never stated against which 84.6% should be read. The study is nonetheless the corpus's clearest demonstration that a near-perfect number can be reported and simultaneously explained away by the person reporting it.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: The design is sound in structure and limited by two things the paper handles unevenly. Structurally: 5-fold stratified cross-validation at the child level, grid-searched hyperparameters under the same scheme, an explicit overfitting check reporting a train-validation gap of no more than 4% with the small sample sizes named as the reason for checking, SMOTE confined to the one imbalanced corpus and validated by Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests showing near-identical distributions, and six metrics reported for every configuration. That is careful work. Two problems remain. The first is confounding, and it is visible in the paper's own table: in the Nadig corpus the typically developing children average 29 and 34 months while the ASD children average 61 and 53 months - roughly a two-year gap - and the ASD group is 83% male against 58%. Age is then included as a feature and identified as one of the four that carry the signal. A classifier separating a four-year-old from a two-and-a-half-year-old on utterance length and vocabulary is doing developmental rather than diagnostic work, and the Nadig ROC-AUC of 0.93 cannot be separated from that. The Eigsti corpus is better matched (TD 40-45 months, ASD 55-56) and yields a lower 0.87. The second is the placement of SMOTE relative to the folds, which is not stated - though the distributional validation is more than most studies provide. Against these, the study's most valuable number is the one it foregrounds itself: 0.71 for the three-class task including developmental delay, against 0.87-0.93 for ASD versus typical development. The gap is internally controlled - same features, same corpus, same pipeline - and it quantifies how much of the binary performance is autism-specific rather than a general clinical-versus-typical distinction.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: The design is careful everywhere except the one place that determines the answer. Careful: three months of primary collection in the real deployment setting; age-matched groups organised into bands; enumerated inclusion and exclusion criteria for children and professionals; guardian and professional consent; a purpose-built task grounded in the executive-function literature; grid search with 5-fold cross-validation and the full search space published; seven algorithms under one protocol; learning curves inspected per model; code and data deposited; and a six-item threats section including the ethics of school-based screening. Decisive: the analysis unit is the game session. Six hundred and forty sessions from 12 children give roughly 53 sessions per child, and the partition into 20% validation and an 80/70/30 training-testing split - together with 5-fold cross-validation - is performed over sessions with no participant grouping described. Every fold therefore contains sessions from the same children as its training data, played on the same device in the same room with the same supervising professional, so a classifier can reach 96% by recognising individual children rather than autism. With six children per class, no session-level partition can produce a participant-level estimate. Two further points compound this. The learning curves showing high training and validation accuracy are read as suggesting a strong generalization capability, and the paper states elsewhere that the high accuracy observed in the models and the robust metrics reinforce the low likelihood of overfitting - inverting the inference, since under session-level splitting high validation accuracy is what leakage produces. And no feature importance is reported, so there is no evidence about what the 96% is built on. The remedy was available and cheap: with 12 children, leave-one-child-out validation would have given twelve honest folds.

answers.title: Phase 3 diagnostic evaluation of a smart
answers.answer: BMJ Open 2019;9:e026226, Protocol section, open access under CC BY-NC; received 6 September 2018, revised 26 March 2019, accepted 1 May 2019, first published 16 July 2019. A general medical journal with a dedicated protocol section, and the venue's requirements are visible throughout: STARD-based design, trial registration with status, a Strengths and Limitations box, tabulated participant allocation and eligibility criteria, explicit power calculations, named ethics committees, an itemised competing-interest statement distinguishing academic from commercial authors, and author contributions specifying individual roles. Publishing a diagnostic protocol before results exist is the practice that makes selective reporting detectable, and this is the only instance of it in the corpus.

answers.title: Predicting Autism Diagnosis using Image with Fixations and Synthetic Saccade Patterns
answers.answer: IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo Workshops (ICMEW) 2019, as an entry to the Saliency4ASD Grand Challenge - a multimedia and computer-vision venue, not an autism or clinical venue.

answers.title: Recognition Of Atypical Behavior In Autism Diagnosis From Video Using Pose Estimation Over Time
answers.answer: An IEEE conference (2019), venue name truncated in the source metadata - a signal-processing or computer-vision venue rather than an autism or clinical one, consistent with the paper's technical framing and industry collaboration.

The venue's orientation also accounts for the paper's most valuable contribution to this review, which is infrastructure rather than result.

answers.title: SP-ASDNet: CNN-LSTM Based ASD Classification Model using Observer ScanPaths

The venue explains both the paper's strengths, in its explicit treatment of the assessment problem as a joint psychology-engineering design task, and its omissions, since participant characteristics and diagnostic ascertainment would be expected in a clinical venue and are absent here.

answers.answer: Scientific Reports, 11, 10131 - a broad open-access multidisciplinary journal, with authorship spanning a computing school, a university psychiatry department and a bioinformatics postgraduate programme.

answers.answer: Autism Research, 15(1), 131-145 - the journal of the International Society for Autism Research, published open access under CC BY. answers.answer: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders, 52, 3038-3049 - a specialist autism journal rather than an engineering venue, which is consistent with the paper's substantive engagement with the motor-atypicality literature and its careful covariate handling.

answers.answer: 2021 2nd International Conference on Robotics, Electrical and Signal Processing Techniques (ICREST), pages 383-387 - a general engineering conference with no clinical or autism-specific remit.

answers.title: Motor synergies: Evidence for a novel motor signature in autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Cognition, 213, article 104652, published open access in a special issue honouring the journal's founding editor - a cognitive science venue rather than a clinical or engineering one, which explains the depth of theoretical development relative to the modelling.

answers.title: Personalized Robot Interventions for Autistic Children: An Automated Methodology for Attention Assessment
answers.answer: International Journal of Social Robotics 13:67-82, 2021; accepted 25 February 2020, published online 6 March 2020. A social robotics venue, and the article reads accordingly - the system engineering, the chest-mount mass distribution, the detector configuration and the scoring rules are all specified precisely, while the clinical evaluation carries no control condition, no chance-corrected agreement statistic and no account of attrition. The venue's orientation also explains the study's most valuable feature, the closed measurement-intervention loop, which is a robotics design idea rather than a clinical-trial one.

answers.title: Predictive Analysis of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using Machine Learning
answers.answer: 2021 International Conference on Frontiers of Information Technology (FIT), pages 305-309 - a general computing conference with no clinical remit.

answers.answer: Frontiers in Psychology, 12, article 665096, in the Psychology for Clinical Settings section - a psychology venue, with authorship spanning a paediatrics institute on development and disability and departments of psychiatry and paediatrics, which explains the depth of clinical characterisation relative to the modelling.

answers.title: Early detection of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder based on visual exploration of images
answers.answer: Signal Processing: Image Communication, volume 94, article 116184 (Elsevier), authored from Roma Tre University and the University of Padova. An image-processing journal with no clinical readership, and the paper is an extended write-up of an IEEE ICME 2019 Grand Challenge submission - a publication route that explains both its strengths (standardised data, common test set, direct comparison against seven other methods) and its weaknesses (no participant characterisation, no diagnostic provenance, no ethics statement, no clinical framing beyond the opening paragraphs).

answers.title: Predicting ASD Diagnosis in Children with Synthetic and Image-based Eye Gaze Data
answers.answer: Signal Processing: Image Communication, volume 94, article 116198 (Elsevier) - the same issue as the Mazumdar RM3ASD paper, which it cites and benchmarks against. Authorship spans the University of Kentucky and UC Davis and combines signal-processing and networking engineers with two autism researchers from the MIND Institute tradition, and the work is supported by NIMH R01MH121344-01. The engineering-clinical composition is visible in the framing (the introduction cites mean US age at diagnosis over 4 years, fewer than 25% before age 3, and characterises the delay as 'squandering years of potential intervention when the brain is most plastic') but not in the participant reporting, which remains that of a benchmark paper.

answers.title: Using 2D video-based pose estimation for automated prediction of autism spectrum disorders in young children
answers.answer: Scientific Reports 11:15069 (2021), doi 10.1038/s41598-021-94378-z - a broad-scope journal reaching both clinical and computational readerships. The authorship is genuinely interdisciplinary and the division of labour shows in the paper: the Psychiatry Department at the University of Geneva supplies the cohort, the gold-standard clinical measures and the ADOS-item interpretation; AIcrowd supplies the deep learning; and the Geneva School of Economics and Management and Citizen Cyber Lab supply the scalability framing. Two authors are marked as contributing equally, one clinical and one computational. That composition explains why this study alone in the corpus combines competent deep learning with full clinical characterisation, correct partitioning and Bonferroni-corrected multivariate validation - most papers here have one side of that expertise or the other.

answers.title: Using Technology to Identify Children With Autism Through Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: Frontiers in Psychology 12:635696 (2021), in the Health Psychology section, from the Department of Humanistic Studies at the University of Naples Federico II, the CNR Institute of Cognitive Sciences and Technologies, and the Neapolisanit rehabilitation centre. A psychology venue with a cognitive-science orientation rather than an engineering one, which is visible in the balance of the paper: the theoretical framing occupies more space than the model, the literature review traces motor abnormality in autism from Kanner forward, and the machine learning is deliberately modest. The clinical co-affiliation supplied the participants and the diagnostic pathway.

answers.title: A Multimodal Approach for Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorders in Children
answers.answer: IEEE Transactions on Neural Systems and Rehabilitation Engineering 30:2003-2011 (2022), a biomedical engineering venue. Authorship spans the School of Psychology at Capital Normal University, the School of Electrical Engineering at Yanshan University, and the State Key Laboratory of Cognitive Neuroscience and Learning at Beijing Normal University, with two first authors marked as contributing equally - one psychological, one engineering. Funded by three national and municipal Chinese grants. The psychology-engineering pairing explains the study's shape: rigorous signal acquisition and a validation design that respects subject independence, alongside an almost complete absence of clinical characterisation and of feature-level interpretation.

answers.title: AI-assisted Initiation to Joint Attention Evaluation for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: IEEE 3rd International Conference on Human-Machine Systems (ICHMS) 2022, DOI 10.1109/ICHMS56717.2022.9980778 - an engineering conference, four pages. The author list is genuinely clinical-computational: the Department of Biomedical Systems Informatics at Yonsei University College of Medicine, the Division of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry at Seoul National University College of Medicine, the Department of Child Development and Family Studies at Seoul National University, and one industry author. That composition explains the paper's characteristic shape - protocol design and diagnostic characterisation at journal standard, training details at conference standard. Funded by the Korean government's IITP programme (2022-0-00234).

answers.title: Application of Machine Learning Techniques to Detect the Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Journal of Healthcare Engineering, volume 2022, article 9340027, an open-access Hindawi title. Authorship is from the Department of Education at Pingdingshan University and the National Engineering Laboratory for Technology of Big Data Application in Education at Central China Normal University - an educational-technology rather than clinical or biomedical-engineering provenance, which explains the paper's shape: careful engineering of the fusion architecture and the stimulus selection, competent statistics on the EEG, and essentially no clinical characterisation of the participants. The review timeline is notably compressed (received 16 February 2022, revised 5 March, accepted 8 March, published 25 March - eleven days from submission to acceptance). Funded by Henan provincial science and social science programmes.

answers.title: An optimized Kernel Extreme Learning Machine for the classification of the autism spectrum disorder by using gaze tracking images
answers.answer: Applied Soft Computing, volume 120, article 108654 (Elsevier) - a computational intelligence journal with no clinical readership. Authorship is from the Division of Technologies for Cyber-Human Integration at Universidad de Guadalajara and the School of Engineering and Sciences at Tecnologico de Monterrey, with no clinical or psychological co-authorship. The venue and authorship together account for the paper's profile completely: rigorous treatment of the optimisation problem, six-metric reporting with non-parametric testing, full algorithmic specification, and no participants, no ethics statement, no diagnostic information and no validation protocol. Its related-work section surveys classifiers and data sources broadly and accurately but engages with no methodological literature on evaluation.

answers.title: Atypical gaze patterns in autistic adults are heterogeneous across but reliable within individuals
answers.answer: Molecular Autism 13:39 (2022), an autism-specific journal with a mechanistic and clinical readership, published open access. Authorship spans Caltech's Division of the Humanities and Social Sciences with computation and neural systems affiliations, the University of Iowa, Indiana University, Tampere University and a joint senior authorship shared between the two site leads. The group's prior work is cited as motivation and critiqued in the process - the paper explicitly identifies the limitation of its own earlier study as the gap it now addresses. Publishing a null classification result in an autism journal, framed as informative rather than as a failed experiment, is itself notable given that the corpus's positive-accuracy studies appear predominantly in engineering venues.

answers.title: Classifying Autism From Crowdsourced Semistructured Speech
answers.answer: JMIR Pediatrics and Parenting 5(2):e35406 (2022), an open-access digital-health journal for paediatric readers. Authorship spans Stanford's Division of Systems Medicine in Pediatrics, Bioengineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Data Science and Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, with the senior author's group having produced a substantial body of prior work on mobile autism screening, wearable social-cue delivery and crowdsourced annotation - much of it cited here. Funding is extensive, listing four NIH grants, an NSF award and numerous foundations. The senior author declares founding Cognoa, a company developing digital paediatric diagnostics, disclosed appropriately; the same company's FDA-authorised screening product is critiqued by name in the Ko et al. paper elsewhere in this corpus for feeding human ratings rather than raw video into its model - a critique that this study's raw-audio approach implicitly answers.

answers.title: Combining voice and language features improves automated autism detection
answers.answer: Autism Research 15(7):1288-1300 (2022), the journal of the International Society for Autism Research - a specialist autism venue with clinical and behavioural-science readership rather than an engineering one. Authorship spans OHSU's Department of Psychiatry, the Institute on Development and Disability and the Department of Pediatrics, with the senior author being a prominent autism epidemiologist and the two first authors marked as contributing equally, one from the language side and one from computation. Funding is from NIH and specifically the National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders. The venue and authorship explain the paper's balance: full clinical characterisation, careful terminology, statistical inference appropriate to a clinical audience (DeLong tests, confidence intervals, non-parametric group comparisons), and modelling that is deliberately conservative.

answers.title: Complexity analysis of head movements in autistic toddlers
answers.answer: Journal of Child Psychology and Psychiatry 64(1):156-166 (2023, published online 2022), a clinical child mental health journal rather than an engineering venue. Authorship spans Duke's Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Department of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, Center for Autism and Brain Development, Global Health Institute, Office of Information Technology, and Department of Biomedical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Sciences, with two co-senior authors - one clinical, one engineering. Funded by an NIH Autism Centers of Excellence award and two NIMH R01s, with additional support to the engineering authors from NSF, the Department of Defense and industry gifts. The genuinely joint clinical-engineering leadership is visible throughout: the statistical inference is what a clinical journal would require (effect sizes, mixed ANOVA, ANCOVA covariates, non-parametric tests), the measurement engineering is what a computer vision group would produce (landmark normalisation, population-wide entropy tolerance, dual attention criteria), and neither is subordinated to the other. The paper includes a 'Key points' box in the journal's clinical format.

answers.title: Cross-linguistic patterns of speech prosodic differences in autism: A machine learning study
answers.answer: PLOS ONE 17(6):e0269637 (2022), open access. Authorship spans the Roxelyn and Richard Pepper Department of Communication Sciences and Disorders at Northwestern University, the Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages and Brain and Mind Institute at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, Chongqing University, and St. John's University - a genuinely bi-national collaboration, which is what the design requires and which is unique in this corpus. Funding comes from NIH grants in the United States and the Health and Medical Research Fund and two private foundations in Hong Kong. The communication-sciences provenance is visible throughout: the theoretical framing of prosody, the choice of a standard narrative elicitation task, the distinction between affective and linguistic prosody, and the interpretation of results in phonological terms all reflect a speech-language rather than an engineering orientation.

answers.title: Detecting autism from picture book narratives using deep neural utterance embeddings
answers.answer: International Journal of Language and Communication Disorders 57(5):948-962 (2022), published on behalf of the Royal College of Speech and Language Therapists - a speech and language therapy journal, so the readership is clinical rather than computational. Authorship pairs the Institute of Computer Science of the Polish Academy of Sciences with the Faculty of Psychology at the University of Warsaw, with equal contribution declared, and the psychology author is an ADOS-2 trainer who supervised the assessments. That composition explains the study's shape: the clinical measurement is handled to research standards (research-reliable ADOS-2 administration, blind dual transcription with reliability, three-tier consent) while the computational work is competent but modest, and the interpretation is oriented toward what a speech and language therapist could use. The journal's format requires an explicit statement of clinical implications, which the authors use to state the supportive rather than replacement role of the method.

answers.title: Development of a visual attention based decision support system for autism spectrum disorder screening
answers.answer: International Journal of Psychophysiology 173:69-81 (2022), a psychophysiology journal with a methods-oriented readership. Authorship pairs two special education departments (Hacettepe and Gazi Universities) with two computer engineering departments (Pamukkale and Hacettepe), and the pairing shows in the paper's shape: the paradigm design, stimulus rationale, calibration discipline and literature critique are of special-education quality while the machine learning is competent but conventional and under-specified. Funded by the Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey. The authors' own prior systematic review of eye-tracking features in autism is cited and used substantively to position the diversion-duration finding.

answers.title: Different Eye Tracking Patterns in Autism Spectrum Disorder in Toddler and Preschool Children
answers.answer: Frontiers in Psychiatry 13:899521 (2022), in the Child and Adolescent Psychiatry section - a clinical psychiatry venue. Authorship spans the Athinoula A. Martinos Center for Biomedical Imaging and the Departments of Psychiatry and Medicine at Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School with the Department of Child Psychiatry and Rehabilitation at Shenzhen Maternity and Child Healthcare Hospital, with two co-first authors and two corresponding authors spanning the two sites. The inclusion of a biostatistician from MGH's Department of Medicine is visible in the analysis, which is more statistically careful than any comparable study in the corpus. Funded by Chinese national and provincial sources. The international collaboration also explains the diagnostic constraint being stated so directly: a US-based team publishing on a Chinese cohort has every reason to flag the absence of ADOS and to name its cause.

answers.title: Evaluation of an artificial intelligence-based medical device for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: npj Digital Medicine 5:57 (2022), a digital health journal published in partnership with Seoul National University Bundang Hospital. Authorship spans 20 affiliations including CHOC Children's, UC Irvine, Stanford, Nationwide Children's, Ohio State, University of Missouri, Arizona State, Children's National, and seven authors affiliated with Cognoa Inc., the device manufacturer, with the corresponding author reachable at a cognoa.com address and also holding a CHOC and UC Irvine appointment. The senior author list includes the Stanford investigator whose group also produced the crowdsourced speech study elsewhere in this corpus and who declares founding Cognoa there. The commercial relationship is transparent from the affiliations and the paper is framed as a regulatory submission, which explains both its methodological rigour - a pivotal trial must satisfy FDA review - and its limits, since the algorithm and code are proprietary and unavailable for independent scrutiny.

answers.title: Extraction and Classification of Acoustic Features from Italian Speaking Children with Autism Spectrum Disorders.
answers.answer: Proceedings of the RaPID-4 workshop at LREC 2022 (Resources and Processing of linguistic, para-linguistic and extra-linguistic Data from people with various forms of cognitive or psychiatric impairment), published by ELRA under CC-BY-NC. Authorship spans the Department of Classical Philology and Italian Studies at the University of Bologna and the Department of Swedish, Multilingualism, Language and Technology at the University of Gothenburg, with the first author a student. This is a computational linguistics workshop rather than a clinical or engineering venue, which explains the paper's profile precisely: the linguistic and acoustic scholarship is of a high standard, the engagement with the prosody literature is extensive and critical, and the clinical characterisation, ethics reporting and validation design are correspondingly thin. The clinical data were collected by a third party for a prior thesis, acknowledged by name.

answers.title: Eye Tracking-Based Diagnosis and Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques
answers.answer: Electronics 11(4):530 (2022), an MDPI open-access engineering journal.
