Authorship spans the Applied College at Najran University in Saudi Arabia, Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University in India, Bournemouth University in the UK and the University of Malaya in Malaysia, with no clinical, psychological or autism-research affiliation among the seven authors. The review timeline is compressed - received 15 January 2022, accepted 6 February, published 10 February, twenty-six days from submission to publication - and the paper contains no limitations section, no ethics statement and several internal inconsistencies in its reported metrics. Funded by the Najran University Scientific Research Deanship.

answers.title: Identification of Social Engagement Indicators Associated With
answers.answer: Journal of Medical Internet Research 24(2):e31830 (2022), a digital health venue. Authorship spans Stanford's Departments of Computer Science, Bioengineering, Pediatrics and Biomedical Data Science, and Neuroscience, from the same group that produced the crowdsourced speech study on the same GuessWhat corpus. Funding is extensive, listing four NIH grants, an NSF award and numerous foundations. The senior author declares founding Cognoa and a co-author declares part-time consulting for the same company - relevant context given that the corpus's FDA pivotal trial paper evaluates a Cognoa device, and that the present study's honest reporting of a weak result sits in a portfolio that also contains a regulated commercial product.

answers.title: Investigation of Eye-Tracking Scan Path as a Biomarker for Autism Screening Using Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: Diagnostics 12(2):518 (2022), an MDPI open-access clinical diagnostics journal. Authorship is from the Schools of Electronics and Electrical Engineering at Vellore Institute of Technology in India and the Department of Biomedical Engineering at Ajman University in the UAE, with no clinical or autism-research affiliation. The review timeline is compressed - received 27 January 2022, accepted 12 February, published 17 February, twenty-one days from submission to publication - and no ethics statement appears. The literature review is nonetheless the most substantive of the three studies reusing this dataset, summarising six prior works with their samples, equipment, stimuli and reported figures, and correctly identifying which prior study reported what.

answers.title: Machine learning models using mobile game play accurately classify children with autism
answers.answer: Intelligence-Based Medicine 6:100057 (2022), an Elsevier open-access journal. Authorship spans Stanford's Departments of Biomedical Data Science, Bioengineering, Pediatrics and Electrical Engineering, from the same group and the same GuessWhat platform as the crowdsourced speech study and the gaze study elsewhere in this corpus - three papers analysing three different data streams from one app. No competing-interest declaration appears in the extracted text, though the senior author declares founding Cognoa in both companion papers. The paper carries some marks of light editing, including a placeholder left in the methods ('need figure/graphic showing this') and a misspelling in the introduction.

answers.title: Speech Signal Analysis of Autistic Children Based on Time-Frequency Domain Distinguishing Feature Extraction
answers.answer: Proceedings of the 2022 IEEE 34th International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI), DOI 10.1109/ICTAI56018.2022.00164. All three authors are from the School of Computer Science and Technology at Anhui University, with no clinical, psychological or speech-science affiliation, though the data collection is credited to cooperation with Anhui Medical University, the Anhui Autism Association and special education schools. Funded by two Anhui provincial science programmes. The venue is an artificial intelligence tools conference, and the paper's profile matches: the signal-processing derivation is developed at length with full equations while the participants, the diagnostic basis, the recording configuration and the ethics are absent.

answers.title: The Impact of Speaker Diarization on DNN-based Autism Severity Estimation
answers.answer: Proceedings of the 2022 44th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC), DOI 10.1109/EMBC48229.2022.9871523. All authors are at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, spanning biomedical engineering and the Azrieli National Centre for Autism and Neurodevelopment Research, so signal-processing and clinical autism expertise are co-located in a single institution - which shows in the study's access to research-reliable ADOS administration and in the realism of its recording setup. Funded by the Israel Ministry of Science and Technology with a grant number. The work builds explicitly on the same group's prior publications for the vocalisation segmentation method, the 48-feature set and the CNN architecture, so this paper reports an increment - the substitution of automatic diarization for manual labelling - rather than a standalone system.

answers.title: The Use of Social Robots in the Diagnosis of Autism in Preschool Children
answers.answer: Applied Sciences 12(17):8399, MDPI, open access under CC BY; received 10 June 2022, accepted 17 August, published 23 August 2022. An applied-sciences venue with a robotics editorial team. The paper's clinical apparatus - multidisciplinary diagnosis, ethics approval, separate filming consent, inter-rater reliability, a published observational scale - is more complete than that of many papers in clinical venues charted in this review, which suggests the standard came from the authors rather than from the venue: the author list spans robotics, cognitive and applied psychology, psychology, and rehabilitation medicine across four Polish and two British institutions, with all seven authors noted as contributing equally.

answers.title: Use of Oculomotor Behavior to Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development: A Novel Implementation of the Machine Learning Approach
answers.answer: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders 53:934-946, an Original Paper - a clinically oriented specialist autism journal rather than an engineering or machine-learning venue. The venue choice shows in the reporting profile: participant characterisation, diagnostic procedure, task protocol and feature-level statistics with t-tests at every window length are all reported to clinical standards, while the computational specification (SVM kernel, regularisation, scaling, code) is thin and the cross-validation unit is left ambiguous. The paper was received in an earlier form, accepted 13 July 2022 and published online 1 August 2022 in the 2022 volume year with a 2023 issue assignment.

answers.title: A Sensorized Toy Car for Autism Screening Using Multi-Modal Features
answers.answer: Sustainability 15(10), article 7790, MDPI, in a section handled by an academic editor from the image-processing field. This is an open-access multidisciplinary sustainability journal rather than a clinical, autism-specialist or biomedical-engineering venue, and the fit is achieved through an explicit framing device: the paper argues that low-cost widespread screening advances the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by extending access to under-served and rural populations, and the argument recurs in the abstract, discussion and conclusion. That framing explains several features of the report - the emphasis on device cost and expert-independence, the comparison table of competing modalities by accessibility and cost, and the near-absence of clinical detail such as diagnostic criteria. Received 28 December 2022, revised 13 March 2023, accepted 25 April 2023, published 10 May 2023, CC BY.

answers.title: A deep learning latent variable model to identify children with autism through motor abnormalities
answers.answer: Frontiers in Psychology 14, article 1194760, Original Research, in a psychology rather than an engineering or clinical venue - which shows in the structure. Roughly two pages of the Methods are a textbook exposition of artificial neural networks and backpropagation aimed at a psychology readership, while the network actually used has no reported layer widths, learning rate, optimiser or epoch count; conversely the theoretical framing in embodied cognition and predictive coding is developed at length. Editorial and review handling is disclosed by name, as Frontiers requires. Received 27 March 2023, accepted 21 April 2023, published 18 May 2023 - a 25-day review turnaround - under CC BY.

answers.title: A multimodal discrimination method for the response to name behavior of autistic children based on human pose tracking and head pose estimation
answers.answer: Displays 76, article 102360, Elsevier - a display-technology and human-visual-interface journal, recommended for publication by a named handling editor. The venue is an unusual home for a clinical assessment study and explains the emphasis: camera geometry, multi-view capture, pose and landmark estimation and frame-level signal processing are described in detail, while the clinical apparatus around them - demographics, diagnostic scores, rater reliability, chance-corrected agreement - is thin or absent. Received 2 November 2022, revised 25 November 2022, accepted 18 December 2022, available online 5 January 2023.

answers.title: Classification of autistic and normal children using analysis of eye-tracking data from computer games
answers.answer: Signal, Image and Video Processing 17:4357-4365, Springer - a signal-processing engineering journal, published as an Original Paper. The venue accounts for the reporting balance: the metric tables are exhaustive and correctly disaggregated by training, validation and test partition, and ROC curves are plotted for every configuration, while the clinical apparatus is minimal (no diagnostic instrument, no cognitive measure, no screening of the comparison group) and the eye tracker is never identified. Received 30 March 2023, revised 25 May 2023, accepted 10 June 2023, published online 4 July 2023.

answers.title: Comparison of Human Experts and AI in Predicting Autism from Facial Behavior
answers.answer: CEUR Workshop Proceedings volume 3359, the ITAH (Intelligent Technologies for Assistive Healthcare) track of the Joint Proceedings of the ACM IUI 2023 Workshops, pages 48-57 - a workshop paper at a human-computer interaction venue rather than a clinical or machine-learning journal. The venue choice fits the contribution: the question of whether AI predictions add anything beyond human judgement is an interaction question, and the paper's framing around assistive rather than autonomous use is native to the IUI community. It also explains some of the reporting compression, since workshop papers are short. The article is deposited as an HHS Public Access author manuscript, reflecting the NIH funding, and is available under CC BY 4.0.

answers.title: Dynamic Viewing Pattern Analysis: Towards Large-Scale Screening of Children With ASD in Remote Areas
answers.answer: IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering 70(5):1622-1632, May 2023 - a high-profile biomedical engineering journal, submitted 17 June 2022, revised 15 October 2022, accepted 14 November 2022, published online 21 November 2022. The venue accounts for the paper's characteristic asymmetry: the signal-processing and machine-learning pipeline is specified to a standard that would permit reimplementation, complete with LSTM gate equations, a parameter sensitivity table, reimplemented baselines, ablations and a reported negative result, while the clinical apparatus that generated the labels is not described at all. Supplementary material comprising ten figures and three tables is hosted by the publisher. The paper adopts the journal's structured abstract format (Objective, Methods, Results, Conclusion, Significance), which is unusual in this corpus and enforces an explicit statement of clinical significance.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder through AI-Powered Analysis of Social Media Texts
answers.answer: 2023 IEEE 36th International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS), pages 235-238 - a four-page conference paper at a computer-science venue oriented to medical systems. The format explains some of the compression, though not the absence of an ethics statement, which conference length limits do not excuse. The venue also explains the paper's evaluative frame: the result is presented as a model comparison with a winner, in the idiom of a benchmark leaderboard, rather than as a clinical or linguistic finding. Two DOIs appear in the retrieved text (10.1109/CBMS58004.2023.00051 and .00223), an artefact of the proceedings metadata.

answers.title: Exploring Complexity of Facial Dynamics in Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: IEEE Transactions on Affective Computing 14(2):919-928, April-June 2023; manuscript received 30 April 2021, revised 4 September 2021, accepted 16 September 2021, published online 20 September 2021 - so the work predates its issue date by nearly two years. The venue is an affective-computing journal, and the paper is in part an argument against that field's dominant framing: rather than recognising emotions, it discards expression identity entirely and measures only the predictability of movement, then demonstrates that this carries information the affect pipeline misses. Five supplementary appendices are hosted with the article, containing the entropy-parameter sensitivity analysis, the across-subject normalisation discussion, the developmental-delay comparison, the head-motion analysis and the confound correlation values. The paper is unusually well supplied with methodological detail for its length, and the appendices carry material that would otherwise have been omitted.

answers.title: Eye-movement analysis on facial expression for identifying children and adults with neurodevelopmental disorders
answers.answer: Frontiers in Digital Health 5:952433, Digital Mental Health section, Original Research, CC BY. Received 25 May 2022, accepted 30 January 2023, published 16 February 2023 - an eight-month review, longer than the Frontiers norm, with two named reviewers and a handling editor from Duke University disclosed as the journal requires. The venue is a digital-health rather than an engineering or clinical-psychiatry journal, and the reporting reflects that mixed audience: clinical instruments and diagnostic procedure are described to psychiatric standards while model architectures, optimiser settings and cross-validation structure are tabulated to engineering standards, and both the statistical analysis and the machine learning are given roughly equal space. Supplementary materials hold the nose-fixation and saccade analyses.

answers.title: Large-scale Investigations of AAC Usage Patterns: Trends, Autism, and Stacked Autoencoders
answers.answer: 2023 IEEE 13th Annual Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference (CCWC), pages 851-857 - a seven-page general computing conference paper rather than a clinical, assistive-technology or machine-learning venue. The format accounts for some compression, though not for the absence of an ethics statement or of any metric beyond accuracy. The venue choice also explains the paper's structure: roughly half is a literature review of AAC efficacy research, followed by descriptive characterisation of the user base, with the classification experiments occupying comparatively little space and being presented partly as a replication and extension of the same group's earlier report on the same dataset.

answers.title: Development and Validation of a Joint Attention-Based Deep Learning System for Detection and Symptom Severity Assessment of Autism Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: JAMA Network Open 6(5):e2315174, published 25 May 2023, accepted 10 April 2023, open access under CC-BY, with a correction issued 7 July 2023 for an author contact detail. This is the highest-profile clinical venue of any study in the corpus and the venue standards are visible throughout: adherence to the STARD reporting guideline is declared, the participant table carries formal group comparisons with p values for every characteristic, every performance metric is reported with a 95% confidence interval computed by a named method, funder role and author contributions are itemised, competing interests including issued patents are disclosed in full, and a data sharing statement is provided. Two supplements carry the enrolment flow diagram, task and acquisition procedures, compliance metric, architecture diagram, training and validation performance, age-stratified results and all interpretability figures. The contrast with the conference-proceedings papers elsewhere in this corpus is instructive: the same underlying study reported at a workshop would have shown none of the participant characterisation that makes its IQ confound visible.

answers.title: Predicting autism in children at an early stage using eye tracking
answers.answer: 2023 2nd International Conference on Vision Towards Emerging Trends in Communication and Networking Technologies (ViTECoN), IEEE - a general communications and networking engineering conference, not a clinical, biomedical or machine-learning venue. That placement explains the paper's balance: substantial textbook exposition of convolutional networks and InceptionV3 architecture aimed at a non-specialist engineering audience, minimal clinical context, and no participant characterisation at all. It also explains the absence of ethics, funding and competing-interests statements, which such venues do not typically require. The paper is short and does not overreach; the reporting gaps are those of the format as much as of the authors.

answers.title: SPASHT: Semantic and Pragmatic Speech Features for Automatic Assessment of Autism
answers.answer: ICASSP 2023, the IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing - the principal venue for speech signal processing, and a slightly incongruous home for a study that performs no acoustic analysis at all. The paper operates entirely on transcripts, computing lexical, syntactic and semantic-pragmatic measures, while the abstract refers to 'diagnostic predictions made using speech signals' and the introduction reviews acoustic findings on pitch range and variability that the study does not build on. The four-page format accounts for the absence of a limitations section, an ethics statement and a competing-interests declaration, though not for the unexplained mismatch between the stated 90:10 split and the 17-item test set implied by the reported accuracies.

answers.title: Stratification of Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Fusion of Temporal Information in Eye-gaze Scan-Paths
answers.answer: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data 17(2), Article 25, published 20 February 2023; received 15 July 2021, accepted 8 May 2022, online 3 June 2022 - a ten-month review at a data-mining journal. The venue explains the paper's shape: twenty pages with fourteen results tables systematically varying representation, temporal window, stimulus subset and augmentation level, alongside almost no clinical reporting - no diagnostic procedure, no demographics beyond age band and sex, no ethics statement, no sensitivity or specificity. Open access support is provided by six institutions. The article had accumulated 18 citations and 2,645 downloads at retrieval.

answers.title: A Convolutional Deep Neural Network Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder Based on Eye-Tracking Scan Paths
answers.answer: Information 15(3), article 133, MDPI, open access under CC BY; received 22 January 2024, revised 21 February, accepted 26 February, published 28 February 2024 - a 37-day turnaround from submission to publication. The venue is a general information-science journal rather than a clinical, biomedical or specialist machine-learning one, which is consistent with the paper's shape: twelve tables of hyperparameter sweeps, extensive tutorial exposition of convolutional network components, and no limitations section, ethics statement of its own, funding declaration or competing-interests statement. The compressed review period is worth noting given that the paper's central results table contains an unreconciled arithmetic inconsistency between accuracy and the class-conditional metrics.

answers.title: A Prediction Model of Autism Spectrum Diagnosis from Well-Baby Electronic Data Using Machine Learning
answers.answer: Children 11(4), article 429, MDPI, open access under CC BY; received 12 March 2024, revised 28 March, accepted 29 March, published 3 April 2024. The venue is a paediatrics journal rather than a computational one, and the reporting reflects that: the cohort definition, case ascertainment, exclusion logic and group comparisons are described to epidemiological standards with effect sizes and a p-value threshold adjusted for sample size, while the modelling is reported adequately but without software versions or hyperparameters. Five supplementary tables and figures carry the full feature list, per-fold training performance, multi-threshold performance and two sensitivity models. The three-week review period is short, though the study's design and reporting do not show the marks of it.

answers.title: AI-Powered Human-Computer Interaction Assisting Early Identification of Emotional and Facial Symptoms of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children: “A Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Facial Feature Recognition System”
answers.answer: Proceedings of ICMISI 2024, the International Conference on Machine Intelligence and Smart Innovation, IEEE, pages 87-91 - a five-page general machine-intelligence conference paper with no clinical or biomedical scope. The format accounts for the brevity but not for the absence of an ethics statement, of a limitations section, or of any check on what the classifier responds to. The paper carries internal inconsistencies - two input sizes, a confusion matrix matching no stated partition, sensitivity written as a percentage of a proportion - that a substantive review would be expected to catch.

answers.title: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework for Multimodal Autism Diagnosis Using XAI GAMI-Net and Hypernetworks
answers.answer: Diagnostics 15(17):2232, MDPI, open access under CC BY; received 26 July 2025, revised 30 August, accepted 1 September, published 3 September 2025 - a 39-day cycle. A diagnostics journal, and the review appears to have engaged with the architecture rather than the inputs: a paper reporting 99.99% ROC-AUC for autism diagnosis, whose own explainability figures name the ADOS total as the leading predictor, was accepted with an internally inconsistent accuracy figure (99.40% against 96.4%), an internally inconsistent split description (70:30 against 20%), and a subject count for the held-out set matching neither. The supplied metadata dates the article to 2024 while the article itself is a 2025 publication.

answers.title: Interpersonal Motor Coordination in Children with Autism and the Establishment of Machine Learning Models to Objectively Classify Children with Autism and Typical Development
answers.answer: IRBM 45 (2024), article 100838, Elsevier - a biomedical engineering journal, published as an Original Article with a highlights list and graphical abstract. Received 22 February 2023, revised 15 January 2024, accepted 27 May 2024, available online 6 June 2024, so nearly sixteen months in review. The venue is a reasonable fit: the paper's substance is signal processing applied to a clinical question, and the reporting reflects that balance, with the motion energy and wavelet procedures specified carefully and the clinical apparatus - diagnostic procedure, demographics, ethics - reported to adequate but not detailed standards. The journal's declaration templates produce the unusual artefact of an animal-research statement in a study of children.

answers.title: Creating a diagnostic assessment model for autism spectrum disorder by differentiating lexicogrammatical choices through machine learning
answers.answer: PLOS ONE 19(9), article e0311209, published 27 September 2024; received 19 March 2024, accepted 15 September 2024, open access under CC BY, with a named academic editor. Twenty-nine pages, of which a substantial proportion is devoted to the linguistic theory, the annotation scheme and the interpretation of what the tags mean - so the balance is unusual for this corpus, with the machine learning occupying perhaps a quarter of the paper and the linguistic framework the rest. The venue's reporting requirements produce the data availability, funding and competing-interests statements, and the length permits the annotation scheme to be documented at a level that a conference paper could not accommodate. Two supplementary files carry the tag frequency comparisons between groups.

answers.title: Emotion-based Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection by Leveraging Transfer Learning and Machine Learning Algorithms
answers.answer: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications 15(5), 2024, pages 566 onwards - a general computer-science journal published by The Science and Information Organization, outside the clinical and biomedical literature. The venue accounts for the reporting profile: extensive procedural description of feature extraction, a large comparison grid, and no ethics, funding, competing-interests or limitations statement. It does not account for the absence of an evaluation protocol, which is a scientific rather than a formatting omission.

answers.title: Enhanced Autism Spectrum Disorder Facial Expression Recognition Using Hybrid Weighed
answers.answer: Traitement du Signal 41(6), IIETA, open access under CC BY, doi 10.18280/ts.410628; received 12 April 2024, revised 7 August, accepted 20 August, available online 31 December 2024. A signal-processing venue. The review process accepted a paper whose title and abstract promise autism facial expression recognition while its experiments use two general-population posed-expression corpora; whose class count differs across three locations in the text; whose architecture narrative refers repeatedly to physiological signals that are never collected; and which states no validation scheme of any kind.

answers.title: Enhancing early autism diagnosis through machine learning: Exploring raw motion data for classification
answers.answer: PLOS ONE 19(4), article e0302238, published 22 April 2024; received 9 January 2024, accepted 28 March 2024, open access under CC BY, with a named academic editor. The venue's requirements produce the data availability statement with its GitHub URL, the funder no-role statement and the competing-interests declaration - and the first of these is what makes this the only included study in the review with openly published data. Eighteen pages, with substantial space given to the theoretical framing, the task design and the preprocessing mathematics, and comparatively little to the model architecture, which is not specified.

answers.title: Hybrid weight optimized deep learning for autism and visual sensory processing disorder detection: A heuristic strategy on medical domain
answers.answer: Intelligent Decision Technologies 18(1):533-559, IOS Press, 2024; received 26 September 2022, accepted 28 October 2023 - a thirteen-month review at a decision-technologies journal outside the clinical and biomedical literature. Twenty-seven pages, of which the great majority document the optimisation algorithm, the network architecture and the metric definitions, with a single paragraph and one five-row table describing the data. The venue explains the balance and the absence of clinical reporting conventions; it does not explain the absence of a sample size, which no venue's norms would require to be omitted.

answers.title: Bayesian optimization of one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D CNN) for early diagnosis of Autistic Spectrum Disorder
answers.answer: Journal of Computational Mathematics and Data Science 13:100105, Elsevier, 2024. A computational mathematics venue, and the reviewing focus followed accordingly: the optimisation methodology, the architecture comparison, the class-distribution reporting and the metric set are all handled to a reasonable standard, while a paper reporting 100% on six metrics across four datasets - and deploying a public diagnostic tool on that basis - was accepted without the derivation of the class variable being examined.

answers.title: Machine learning’s effectiveness
answers.answer: Frontiers in Psychiatry 15:1464285, Original Research, open access under CC BY; received 13 July 2024, accepted 30 September 2024, published 17 October 2024. Editorial and review handling is disclosed by name as Frontiers requires, and the reviewers include a researcher whose own work on movement analysis in autism is cited in this review's corpus - an indication that the paper was assessed within the relevant specialist community. The venue's structure produces the ethics, funding, competing-interests and data-availability statements, and supplementary materials carry the per-variable rationale and calculation methods that would not fit the main text.

answers.title: Multiscale attention-based network to enhance detection and classification of autism spectrum disorders using convolutional neural network
answers.answer: PeerJ Computer Science 11:e3134, submitted 8 April 2025, accepted 29 July 2025, published 2 October 2025, open access under CC-BY 4.0, academic editor Davide Chicco, with subject areas listed as bioinformatics, algorithms, artificial intelligence and data science. The venue is a computer science journal, which shapes what the review process attended to: the paper's statistical comparison of model variants, its ablation design, its code archiving on Zenodo and its leakage analysis are all above the norm for this branch, while the absence of any ethics statement, any diagnostic reference standard and any demographic description passed without comment. PeerJ's declaration structure elicited funding, competing-interests, author-contribution and data-availability statements from these authors but has no field that would have prompted a human-subjects declaration. The bibliographic record also carries an inconsistency worth noting for the corpus: the supplied metadata dates the article to 2024 while the article itself is a 2025 publication.

answers.title: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Autism Detection Using EEG Data [REC04023]
answers.answer: Advances in Technology Innovation 9(4):287-300, 2024, doi 10.46604/aiti.2024.13951; received 1 July 2024, revised 31 July, accepted 2 August 2024 - a 32-day cycle. A technology-innovation venue, and the reviewing pattern is consistent with that: the acquisition chain, the feature families and the four architectures with their layer equations are all documented, while the complete absence of any validation scheme, of any majority-class baseline, of a limitations section and of any account of diagnostic ascertainment passed without comment, as did an ethics declaration stating in absolute terms that no human-rights statement or informed consent is required.

answers.title: Prediction for children with autism spectrum disorder based on digital behavioral features during free play
answers.answer: BMC Psychiatry 24:799, 2024, open access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; received 10 May 2024, accepted 30 September 2024, doi 10.1186/s12888-024-06129-9. A clinical psychiatry venue, and the difference from the engineering venues that dominate this corpus is visible throughout: the paper reports matching statistics and their tests, cites the psychometrics of its diagnostic instrument, describes coder training and inter-rater reliability, reports odds ratios with confidence intervals, tests calibration and goodness of fit, enumerates five limitations including its own selection bias, and supplies the full coding manual as supplementary material. It is comparably weak where clinical journals are typically weak: the statistical software is not named, the code is not available, the stepwise criterion is unstated and no optimism-corrected estimate is reported. The version under review is the blinded submission, with the recruiting hospital and ethics committee anonymised in the text.

answers.title: Predictive model using autism
answers.answer: Frontiers in Psychiatry 15:1493158, Original Research, open access under CC BY; received 13 September 2024, accepted 19 November 2024, published 18 December 2024. Editorial and review handling is disclosed by name as the venue requires. This is a clinical psychiatry journal and the paper reads accordingly: the diagnostic process is described in detail with the explicit exclusion of ADOS-2 and ADI-R from it, the full clinical battery is reported for each group, sample size is justified against a comparable prior study, significance thresholds are stated including a stricter alpha for correlations, AUC interpretive bands are prespecified, effect sizes carry confidence intervals throughout, and the limitations section names overfitting as the explanation for the study's own validation drop. What a computational venue would have added is missing - no code, no data deposit, no statement of the holdout procedure's details - and what a computational venue would have missed is present in full.

answers.title: The Noor Project: fair transformer transfer learning for autism spectrum disorder recognition from speech
answers.answer: Frontiers in Digital Health 7:1274675, Original Research, open access under CC BY; received 8 August 2023, accepted 28 May 2025, published 18 August 2025, with editor and reviewers disclosed by name. The near two-year interval between submission and acceptance is unusual. The venue is a digital-health rather than a clinical journal, and the paper reads accordingly: the partitioning, metrics, benchmarking and fairness analysis are handled to a good computational standard while the clinical description of the corpora - diagnostic procedures, ages, per-class participant counts, recording conditions - is left almost entirely to the source datasets and is internally inconsistent where it is given. The supplied bibliographic metadata dates the article to 2024 while the article itself is a 2025 publication.

answers.title: Using #ActuallyAutistic on Twitter for Precision Diagnosis of Autism
answers.answer: JMIR Formative Research 2024;8:e52660, Original Paper, open access. The record carries two notable annotations: the version retrieved is a corrected version, with the correction statement published at JMIR Formative Research 2024;8:e59349, and a formal comment on the article appears at JMIR Formative Research 2024;8:e59794. A published comment on a paper of this kind indicates that its approach was contested in the literature, which is itself part of the paper's significance for this review - it is the only included study whose ethics generated a documented scholarly exchange. JMIR's formative-research track is intended for feasibility and early-stage work, which fits a study whose conclusion is that the thing is possible and should not be done without consent. The venue's structure produced the ethical-considerations section with its IRB number, data-governance determination and description of measures taken beyond regulatory requirement - a section that has no counterpart anywhere else in this corpus.

answers.title: Video-audio neural network ensemble for comprehensive screening of autism spectrum disorder in young children
answers.answer: PLOS ONE 19(10):e0308388, Research Article, open access under CC BY; received 30 April 2024, accepted 12 July 2024, published 3 October 2024. PLOS ONE's structural requirements produced the data-availability statement, funding itemisation and competing-interests declaration, and the venue's data-sharing policy is visibly what prompted the considered middle position adopted here - raw recordings withheld because they contain faces and voices, a de-identified pose subsample deposited on Zenodo with a DOI, and training code published on GitHub. That is the policy working as intended, and it is worth noting for the review that the same policy which cannot compel raw sharing of identifiable child data did elicit a genuinely useful partial release, made possible by the study's own choice of a skeletal representation.

answers.title: Video-based continuous affect recognition of children with Autism Spectrum Disorder using deep learning
answers.answer: Biomedical Signal Processing and Control 89:105712, Elsevier; received 24 February 2023, revised 18 October 2023, accepted 5 November 2023, available online 8 November 2023, with a 2024 issue date. A signal-processing venue, and the fingerprints are visible in both directions: the architectural detail, the metric definitions, the four-dataset comparison and the careful argument about MSE versus CCC are all to a good engineering standard, while the absence of any ethics or consent statement for identifiable children's home videos, the undocumented comparison class and the absent demographics passed review without comment. The journal's structure elicited funding, competing-interests, author-contribution and data-availability declarations but has no field that would have prompted a human-subjects statement.

answers.title: A novel thermal imaging-based framework for continuous ASD classification and behavior analysis using facial mood and skin temperature features
answers.answer: Biomedical Signal Processing and Control 100:107009, Elsevier; received 25 November 2023, revised 8 August 2024, accepted 30 September 2024, online 10 October 2024, with a 2025 issue date. The same journal published another study charted in this review, and the pattern is consistent across both: signal-processing components are held to a reasonable standard - denoising evaluated against alternatives on PSNR and SSIM, architectural choices supported by ablation, hyperparameters tabulated - while the clinical apparatus passes without scrutiny. Here that meant an article proposing automated psychiatric medication dosing for children was published with the declaration 'Ethical Approval. Not required.', with no stated source for its outcome labels, with no participant-level validation, and with no limitations section. The journal's declaration structure elicited statements on ethics, funding, data availability and authorship, so the ethics field was completed - with a denial of applicability that went unqueried.

answers.title: Application of artificial intelligence in modern healthcare for diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: Frontiers in Medicine 12:1569464, Original Research, open access under CC BY; received 31 January 2025, accepted 16 April 2025, published 21 May 2025, with editor and three reviewers disclosed by name. The venue is a general medical journal rather than an engineering one, which makes the pattern of what passed review notable: a physiognomic premise asserted without measurement, a corpus whose comparison class is described in the paper's own methods as web-search results, no demographic information of any kind, results reported from a validation partition while a defined test partition goes unreported, support counts inconsistent with the stated split, a claimed feature-importance analysis that does not exist, and an introduction that contradicts the abstract and the results tables about which models were compared. The retrieved text ends mid-discussion at Table 8, so the declarations could not be assessed.

answers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using Linguistic Features
answers.answer: 2024 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Computing and Machine Intelligence (ICMI), doi 10.1109/ICMI60790.2024.10585946. A short computing-conference paper, single-authored by a student at The Harker School in San Jose - a secondary school - which is worth recording factually because it contextualises both the scale and the character of the work. The paper is careful where a beginner might not be: it splits by participant, justifies its repeated-split design with a stated stability criterion, documents its token-cleaning rules against TalkBank's transcription guide, plots ROC variability bands, compares its feature findings explicitly against three named prior studies including where it contradicts them, and reports modest accuracies without inflation. It is weaker on the clinical reasoning that a conference in computing and machine intelligence would not have prompted: no independent language measure, no age composition by group, a non-autistic clinical comparison deliberately discarded, and a recommendation about clinical model choice resting on a one-to-two-point margin. Set beside several journal papers in this review that report 98-100% from image-level splits on web-scraped corpora, its 84% from a participant-level split on a consented research archive is the more informative result.

answers.title: Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Skeleton-Based Body Movement Analysis via Dual-Stream Deep Learning
answers.answer: Electronics 14(11):2231, MDPI, open access under CC BY; received 26 April 2025, revised 21 May, accepted 26 May, published 30 May 2025 - a 34-day review cycle. An electronics and computing venue, and the profile matches: the software stack is versioned to nine packages, the hardware is specified, the cross-validation scheme is stated separately for each dataset with fold sizes and repetition counts, and every architecture is reported with mean, max, min and standard deviation. What a clinical venue would have required is absent: no sensitivity or specificity, no demographic composition, no examination of the outcome-informed trial selection quoted in the methods, and no discussion of what the 25-point gap between the two datasets implies about the construct being measured.

answers.title: Automatic Cry Analysis Deep Learning for Screening of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Early Childhood [REC01905]
answers.answer: Journal of Autism and Developmental Disorders, Brief Report, accepted 18 March 2025, open access under CC BY-NC-ND, doi 10.1007/s10803-025-06811-1. A clinical autism journal, and the venue's influence is visible in what is reported well: the four-stage diagnostic procedure with clinician qualifications, the explanation of why ADOS was unavailable in Farsi, the ethics and consent statements, the exclusion rules, the per-group recording-setting and cry-cause distributions, and above all a competing-interest declaration that itemises employment, founder status, equity holding and advisory compensation by individual. The brief-report format constrains length, but the omissions that matter are not length-related - a test partition, a participant-level split and a model-selection rule that does not maximise over the evaluation set are design decisions rather than reporting ones, and the same journal's structure that elicited an exemplary conflict declaration did not elicit any account of how the 90.28% was obtained.

answers.title: Enhancing Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder Using a Bayesian-Optimized Random Forest Algorithm
answers.answer: Procedia Computer Science 258:1576-1585, Elsevier, 2025, open access under CC BY-NC-ND, doi 10.1016/j.procs.2025.04.389, peer-reviewed under the scientific committee of the International Conference on Machine Learning and Data Engineering. A conference-proceedings venue with a short review cycle, and the reviewing engaged with the modelling rather than the data: a paper whose own methods section prints a feature list containing both the summed screening score and the thresholded outcome derived from it was accepted reporting 0.9890 accuracy without that relationship being examined.

answers.title: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics
answers.answer: Bulletin of Electrical Engineering and Informatics 14(5):3985-4000, October 2025, open access under CC BY-SA; received 20 March, revised 8 August, accepted 1 September 2025. An electrical engineering and informatics venue, and the profile of what was and was not scrutinised follows: the acquisition protocol, the feature construction, the validation strategy, the regularisation parameters and the architecture are all specified in detail, while the absence of any diagnostic ascertainment procedure and of any ethics or consent statement for a prospective study recording 100 children passed review without comment. The journal's structure elicited conflict-of-interest and data-availability declarations - the latter citing 'privacy and ethical considerations' - but has no field that would have prompted a human-subjects statement.

answers.title: Data Mining–Based Model for Computer-Aided Diagnosis of
answers.answer: JMIR Formative Research 9:e72115, 2025, Original Paper, with a companion article listed at formative.jmir.org/2026/1/e91833. The formative-research track is intended for early-stage and feasibility work, which fits a study proposing a diagnostic architecture ahead of collecting the data to evaluate it. The venue's structure produced the ethics, funding, data-availability and competing-interest declarations, and the ethics statement is more detailed than most in this branch - it is also the statement that reveals the contradiction with the abstract about whether the GELOPH<15> was administered. That a paper whose abstract, objective and conclusion all centre on gelotophobia detection was published while its own ethics section records that no gelotophobia assessment took place is a reviewing gap that the structured declarations made visible rather than concealed.

answers.title: Deep Learning-Based Feature Extraction from Children's Facial Images for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: Cognitive Models and Artificial Intelligence Conference (AICCONF '24), Istanbul, 25-26 May 2024, ACM, doi 10.1145/3660853.3660888; five pages. A short conference paper from an artificial-intelligence venue, and the profile follows: the preprocessing and augmentation are documented carefully, the software and hardware are versioned, and the five-extractor comparison is set up systematically, while no validation scheme, no class distribution, no per-configuration results, no ethics statement and no limitations section appear.

answers.title: Deep learning-based detection of autism spectrum disorder and emotion recognition in children
answers.answer: Pattern Recognition 173:112906, Elsevier; received 13 June 2025, revised 11 November 2025, accepted 8 December 2025, online 9 December 2025, with a 2026 volume date. A pattern-recognition venue, and the profile is characteristic: the partition sizes, stratification procedure, quality filter, architectures and metric tables are all documented, while a metric set that is arithmetically impossible on its own stated test set was published without reconciliation, alongside no ethics statement, no diagnostic ascertainment and no chance baseline. The limitations section is nonetheless one of the better ones in the branch, which suggests the shortfall is in verification rather than in candour.

answers.title: Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) Using Lightweight Ensemble CNN Based on Facial Images for Improved Diagnostic Accuracy
answers.answer: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications 16(7):229ff, 2025. An open-access computer science venue, and the profile follows: the ensemble pipeline, augmentation, split ratio and metric tables are documented, while the corpus's dual provenance is left unquantified, no ethics statement appears despite clinic-sourced images, no limitations section is provided, and the conclusion repeats the results paragraph verbatim. An unedited template placeholder survives in the keyword list.

answers.title: Diagnosing autism spectrum disorder based on eye tracking technology using deep learning models
answers.answer: Frontiers in Medicine 12:1690177 - an open-access general medical journal, not a computing venue. This matters for the review's venue analysis: the paper's audience is clinical, its abstract advises healthcare professionals, and no clinical reviewer flagged the absence of an ethics statement, the absence of a limitations section, or the use of a diagnostic instrument as a model input.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder Through Automated Machine Learning
answers.answer: Diagnostics 15(15):1859 (MDPI) - an open-access clinical diagnostics journal, with academic editors drawn from the biomedical signal-processing community. The venue's clinical framing did not surface the label circularity or the abstract/table accuracy mismatch in review.

answers.title: Enhanced ASD detection using 3D facial landmark localization with convolutional shape appearance model and graph-randomized XGBoost
answers.answer: Sadhana 51(1):30 - the Indian Academy of Sciences' general engineering-sciences journal, not a clinical or specialist vision venue. This is relevant to the review's venue analysis: the mismatch between a 2D Kaggle photo set and a paper about 3D scanning, the unsourced demographic table, the absent ethics statement and the internally inconsistent confusion matrix all survived a 324-day review cycle at a general engineering journal.

answers.title: Enhanced multilevel autism classification for children using eye-tracking and hybrid CNN-RNN deep learning models
answers.answer: Neural Computing and Applications 37(33):27631-27654, in a special issue drawn from the 2023 India International Congress on Computational Intelligence. Special-issue routing is relevant to the review's venue analysis: the impossible CARS bands, the absent TD group behind a TD claim in the abstract, the surviving x placeholder in the participant count, and a literature review containing building-energy and distributed-generation citations all passed review in 53 days.

answers.title: Ensemble of Deep Learning with Crested Porcupine Optimizer Based Autism
answers.answer: Computers, Materials & Continua 83(2) (Tech Science Press) - a broad-scope open-access computing journal covering materials, computing and engineering. This is the review's clearest venue-mismatch case: a diagnostic claim about children, resting on unlabelled web photographs and an explicit ethics exemption, published in a journal with no clinical review capacity, with no limitations section and no future work, in 81 days.

answers.title: Explainable and secure framework for autism prediction using multimodal eye tracking and kinematic data
answers.answer: Complex & Intelligent Systems 11:173 (Springer) - a computational-intelligence journal. Relevant to the review's venue analysis in a specific way: this is a privacy-and-governance paper by construction, invoking GDPR and HIPAA, published without an ethics statement of any kind, and its headline accuracy of 99.99% on nine test cases passed review over 126 days.

answers.title: Facial Images Dataset for Early Screening of Autism Children Using Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: 2025 10th International Conference on Computer and Communication Engineering (ICCCE), IEEE, pages 351-355. A short engineering conference paper. The venue explains but does not excuse the asymmetry between a fully specified acquisition protocol and a completely unspecified model, and the survival of unrelated stunting terminology in the workflow description.

answers.title: Improving Early Autism Detection with Chi-Square Feature Selection, Machine Learning, and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Engineering, Technology & Applied Science Research 15(5):27954-27959 - an open-access general engineering journal. A 100% diagnostic accuracy claim, a hold-out contaminated by pre-split synthetic oversampling, and a label that is a threshold on its own predictors passed review there in 48 days including a revision round.

answers.title: Novel Framework for Autism Spectrum Disorder Identification and Tailored Education With Effective Data Mining and Ensemble Learning Techniques
answers.answer: IEEE Access - a high-volume open-access multidisciplinary engineering journal. The published PDF is the unedited accepted version, retaining template placeholders in the header (Date of publication xxxx 00, 0000; DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2017.DOI) and a VOLUME 4, 2016 footer throughout. No reviewer questioned a fabricated educational-placement target, a 99.99% figure absent from the results, or the absence of any ethics statement in a paper recommending educational interventions for individual children.

answers.title: Predicting autism traits using Q-CHAT behavioral features: a machine learning approach
answers.answer: Engineering Research Express 7(2):025269 (IOP Publishing) - an open-access general engineering journal. A 132-day review including one revision round did not surface the mutually inconsistent confusion matrices, the missing split proportions and cross-validation k, the unstated chance level, or an ethics statement that treats absence of direct human interaction as constituting ethical approval.

answers.title: Predicting autistic traits, anxiety and depression symptoms using camouflaging autistic traits questionnaire (CAT-Q-ES): A machine learning study
answers.answer: Research in Autism 128:202712 (Elsevier) - a specialist autism research journal rather than an engineering or general-science venue, and the difference is visible throughout: dimensional outcomes, in-sample psychometrics, effect sizes with confidence intervals for group comparisons, a self-critical limitations section, an ethics analysis of algorithmic screening in mental health, and deposited code. It is the only paper in the corpus published in a venue whose reviewers are subject-matter specialists in autism, and it is also the only one to release code, report internal consistencies, or discuss stigma.

answers.title: A Computational Method for Early Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Deep Learning Approach
answers.answer: International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems 18(3):312-319 - an open-access computing journal. Review appears to have been rapid (received 17 January 2025, revised 4 February 2025) and did not surface the absent ethics statement, the unreported class counts, the 200-image test set behind a four-way ranking claim, or the mismatch between a movement-based biomarker rationale and a still-image input.

answers.title: Early Detection of ASD from Facial Images Using DeepDeblur and Denoising Optimized Convolutional Neural Network
answers.answer: International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems 18(4) - an open-access computing journal, the same venue as local_6e7174c0. Review did not surface the mismatch between the stated 400-image test set and the 2,940-image evaluation, the absent ethics statement, or the reporting of reference-dependent image-quality metrics for photographs that have no sharp reference.

answers.title: Reliable Autism Spectrum Disorder Diagnosis for Pediatrics Using Machine Learning and Explainable AI
answers.answer: Diagnostics 14(22):2504 (MDPI) - an open-access clinical diagnostics journal, with paediatric and psychiatric clinicians among the authors. The clinical involvement is real and shaped the feature selection; it did not surface that four instrument measurements of the target condition were sitting in the predictor set, which is precisely the observation clinical expertise is best placed to make. The paper cleared review in 40 days.

answers.title: Using explainable machine learning and eye-tracking for diagnosing autism spectrum and developmental language disorders in social attention tasks
answers.answer: Frontiers in Neuroscience 19:1558621 - an open-access neuroscience journal, with a 127-day review. The venue's disciplinary fit shows in the reporting: matched group characteristics with ANOVA and chi-squared tests, a standardised language measure, a pre-specified interpretive scale for F1, an ethics reference number, and a limitations paragraph that includes the provisionality of early diagnoses.

answers.title: Utilizing deep learning models in an intelligent eye-tracking system for autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
answers.answer: Frontiers in Medicine 11:1436646 - an open-access clinical journal, accepted in 44 days. A 100% diagnostic accuracy claim, an abstract that reports image counts as child counts, an absent ethics statement, an unstated test-set size and no limitations section all passed clinical review.

answers.title: A novel hybrid deep learning model using MEResNext for autism spectrum disorder detection
answers.answer: Computational Biology and Chemistry 120:108619 (Elsevier), 2026 issue. A computational-biology venue, and the mismatch shows: a paper with no sample size, no validation protocol, no reported class balance, two incorrect metric definitions, image architectures applied to binary questionnaire responses, and author statements referring to co-authors of a single-authored manuscript.

answers.title: An assessment of autistic and parkinsonian movement profiles to inform selective classification algorithms
answers.answer: Journal of Neurodevelopmental Disorders 18:8, a specialist neurodevelopmental journal, with a 180-day review - the longest among the charted 2026 studies. The disciplinary fit is visible throughout: formal group matching with equivalence tests, mixed models with appropriate random-effect structure, Bayesian evidence for the null, pre-specified interpretive thresholds, deposited data and scripts, complete ethics reporting including participant remuneration, and a limitations section that reasons about cohort effects in ascertainment.

answers.title: An explainable deep learning framework for screening level autism severity using behavioural data
answers.answer: Discover Applied Sciences 8(4):363 (Springer) - an open-access multidisciplinary applied-sciences journal. The venue is not clinical, yet the paper is the most careful in the branch about the boundary between computational and clinical claims, which suggests the discipline of the authors rather than of the reviewers is doing the work here.

answers.title: An explainable machine unlearning algorithm framework for early detection of autism spectrum disorder and brain disabilities in newborns
answers.answer: Alexandria Engineering Journal 145 (2026) 164-181 (Elsevier) - a general engineering journal. Review did not surface a sample description in which 25,000 positive cases are drawn from 10,000 samples and a 21-to-1 ratio is called balanced, three incompatible age ranges for the study population, partition counts differing between sections, a named metric set none of whose values are reported, cybersecurity vocabulary about malicious and fraudulent events in a paper about infants, or a surviving response-to-reviewers sentence in the body text.

answers.title: Deep learning based approach for Behavior classification in diagnoses of Autism Spectrum Disorder using naturalistic videos
answers.answer: Frontiers in Computational Neuroscience 20:1626315, with a 174-day review including a substantial revision. The review did not surface the absent ethics statement for reuse of identifiable children's home videos, the unreported number of distinct children, the absence of a non-autistic comparison behind a screening claim, or the reading of near-zero fold variance as robustness.

answers.title: Explainable Children Autism Detection using Gaze Features in Audio-Visual Speech Comprehension
answers.answer: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction 10(3), Article ETRA012, the ETRA eye-tracking venue. The disciplinary fit shows in the reporting: participant-independent nested cross-validation, bootstrap intervals, a majority-class lower bound, paired significance testing between conditions, fold-level attribution computation, and an explicit comparison of the achieved performance against published clinical-viability thresholds.

answers.title: Explainable Ensemble Learning Framework for Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder: Enhancing Trust, Interpretability and Reliability in AI-Driven Healthcare
answers.answer: Computer Modeling in Engineering & Sciences 146(1):41 (Tech Science Press), 55 days from submission to acceptance. A modelling and engineering venue; review did not surface an entirely unsourced clinical dataset carrying an IRB claim with no committee or institution, a split performed over augmented copies, a four-class severity result reported alongside a binary detection result, or four autism instruments sitting in the predictor set.

answers.title: Finding the forest in the trees: Using machine learning and online cognitive and perceptual measures to predict adult autism diagnosis
answers.answer: Translational Psychiatry 16:129 (Nature Portfolio) - a clinical and translational psychiatry journal, and the only such venue in the charted corpus. The disciplinary fit is evident throughout: matched-subsample analysis, Bonferroni-corrected group comparisons, a label-randomisation control, sensitivity and specificity reported separately, deposited analysis code, documented data-access procedures, an explicit language statement citing community preference, and a discussion that diagnoses the methodological failures of the prior literature it is compared against.

answers.title: Hybrid ensemble learning for Autism Spectrum Disorder screening using eye-tracking scanpath
answers.answer: Array 30 (2026) 100753 (Elsevier) - an open-access computer science journal. The author list spans engineering and clinical institutions including a psychiatric hospital, which makes the absence of any description of the source cohort's diagnosis or demographics more notable rather than less. The paper discloses an editorial conflict of interest for one author, which is good practice and uncommon in this corpus.

answers.title: Early Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Facial Images and AI-Based Deep Learning Models
answers.answer: Journal of Pioneering Medical Sciences 15(1):137-145, a medical sciences journal, 90 days from submission to acceptance. Clinical review did not surface the absent class counts and split ratios, the mAP inconsistency, or the reported finding that one of the two models labels a dog as autistic.

answers.title: Multimodal fusion of deep transfer learning with wavelet neural network for autism spectrum disorder detection using facial images
answers.answer: Multimedia Tools and Applications 85:300 (Springer), 218 days with a revision round. A multimedia and computing venue. Review did not surface an ethics declaration stating that no human participants were involved in a study of 2,940 children's photographs, a data-availability statement denying that any dataset was analysed, a test accuracy above training accuracy read as good generalisation, or the mismatch between the stated 50 epochs and the 25-epoch learning curves.

answers.title: SHAP-based explainable AI framework for autism severity classification using 3D motor biomarkers
answers.answer: Frontiers in Psychiatry 17:1751654, 107 days with a revision round. A psychiatry venue, and the fit shows in the reporting - confidence intervals on a small-sample result, an explicit statement that held-out sets are not external validation, full provenance for a secondary analysis, and a limitations discussion that identifies the study's own most striking result as uninterpretable. The revision round appears to have strengthened rather than softened these statements, since the synthetic-data caveat appears in the abstract itself.

answers.title: Screening autism spectrum
answers.answer: Scientific Reports 15(1):34134 (Nature Portfolio). A multidisciplinary venue. The reporting reflects it: demographic tables by group and sex, six metrics with stated rationales, a quantified overfitting check, KS validation of the oversampling, and a limitations section that names the information cost of the privacy choice.

answers.title: Towards screening of children students with autism spectrum disorder based on executive functions with serious game and machine learning approaches
answers.answer: Expert Systems With Applications 295 (2026) 128884 (Elsevier) - an applied AI journal. Review did not surface that 640 analysis rows come from 12 children with no participant-level partitioning, nor the Phishing keyword.

questions.question_text: What is the publication year, and how is the work framed?

answers.title: Very early detection of Autism Spectrum Disorders based on acoustic analysis of pre-verbal vocalizations of 18-month old toddlers
answers.answer: 2013 - the earliest study in this corpus. The paper characterises the field as having focused on verbal children over age three and positions itself as pushing the age range down to 18 months; it does not otherwise analyse field-level trends.

answers.title: Use of Machine Learning to Identify Children with Autism and Their Motor Abnormalities
answers.answer: 2015. The paper characterises prior pattern-classification work in ASD as dominated by neuroimaging (structural MRI, DTI) with only isolated behavioral examples (automated vocal analysis), and positions kinematics as a cheaper, less intrusive alternative - an explicit statement of the field's shift from neuroimaging toward behavioral signals.

answers.title: ADHD and ASD Classification Based on Emotion Recognition Data
answers.answer: 2016. The related-work section positions the study against neuroimaging-based ADHD classification and against kinematic ASD classification in 2-4 year-olds (Crippa et al.), explicitly noting that its own high-functioning, older ASD participants are harder to separate from controls - an early acknowledgement that sample severity drives reported accuracy across this literature.

answers.title: Identifying children with autism spectrum disorder based on their face processing abnormality: A machine learning framework
answers.answer: 2016. The paper characterises machine learning in autism research as so far dominated by feature selection to shorten diagnostic instruments (ADOS/ADOS-G item reduction) and by neuroimaging, with behavioral classification only just beginning (citing Crippa et al. 2015 as the motivating precedent) - documenting the field's pivot toward behavioral prediction that this corpus goes on to record.

answers.title: Semantic mapping reveals distinct patterns in descriptions of social relations in adults with autism spectrum disorder
answers.answer: 2016. The paper positions data mining of language production for psychopathology as previously proposed but never demonstrated quantitatively across diagnostic groups, presenting itself as a first step - an early marker of the linguistic-content strand that grows later in this corpus (social media text, picture-book narratives, conversation transcripts).

answers.title: Toward the Autism Motor Signature: Gesture patterns during smart tablet gameplay identify children with autism
answers.answer: 2016. The paper positions itself as the first to use smart-device serious games to study motor patterns in autism, and notes only one prior machine-learning study of autism-specific motor patterns (Crippa et al., optical motion capture, n=30) - which it critiques directly for SVM plus leave-one-out cross-validation being 'prone to over-fitting'. This is the corpus's clearest early example of methodological self-correction within the field, and it documents the shift from laboratory optical motion capture to consumer-device sensing.

answers.title: Applying machine learning to identify autistic adults using imitation: An exploratory study
answers.answer: 2017. The paper surveys the emergence of machine learning in autism research across neural markers, cognitive scores, diagnostic-instrument item reduction and pregnancy risk factors, and notes that 'to date, there have been few studies that have applied machine learning to autistic motor data', naming Crippa et al. (2015) as the only prior motor example. It positions itself as the first to apply machine learning to imitation kinematics and, unusually, contrasts its own design against that predecessor on specific methodological grounds - less constrained task, exploration of which test conditions discriminate, and adults rather than children where group differences should be smaller.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of ADHD and ASD from Expressive Behaviour in RGBD Data
answers.answer: 2017. The paper characterises computer vision for ADHD and ASD as 'still in its infancy', with prior work confined to detecting predefined behavioural markers (AOSI markers, self-stimulatory behaviour, social games, engagement) whose 'effectiveness in predicting the actual ADHD and ASD diagnosis still remains to be seen'. It positions itself as one of the first to pose diagnosis directly as a machine-learning problem and, unusually for this corpus, targets adults rather than children.

answers.title: Earlier identification of children with autism
answers.answer: 2017. The paper notes that early speech-language development in ASD has repeatedly been characterised as delayed and deviant but that only a few studies examine vocalisation specificities at the feature level, and that most of those assessed crying with single acoustic features such as fundamental frequency or duration. It positions itself as one of the first to explore ASD-related pre-linguistic vocalisation specificities across a wide standardised parameter set - documenting the shift from single hand-picked acoustic measures to standardised high-dimensional feature sets that characterises the speech strand of this corpus.

answers.title: Speech-based Diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Condition by Generative
answers.answer: 2017. The paper characterises the field as showing that 'high levels of accuracy can be achieved' for discriminating typically developing children from children with ASC, but immediately qualifies that these results come from 'rather small datasets, and may lead to potential confounds', naming corpus size as 'a major obstacle in the development of robust models which are sufficiently reliable for clinical practice'. It positions itself as the first application of GAN representation learning in computational paralinguistics. This is one of the corpus's most explicit internal critiques of its own literature's headline accuracies.

answers.title: ANN and SVM Classifiers in Identifying Autism Spectrum Disorder Gait Based on Three-Dimensional Ground Reaction Forces
answers.answer: 2018. The paper notes that machine learning has been proven effective for automated gait recognition in cerebral palsy, post-stroke and Parkinson's disease, but that 'research in the area of automated recognition of ASD gait using machine learning techniques based on GRFs gait features is less prevalent' - positioning autism gait analysis as lagging behind other clinical gait populations, and its own contribution as an incremental extension of the authors' prior KNN study on the same data.

answers.title: Analyzing Human-Robot Interaction Using Machine Vision for Autism screening
answers.answer: 2018. The paper situates itself against traditional questionnaire-and-expert screening (3DI, ASD-OC), noting clinical guidance that no questionnaire can be recommended as a diagnostic test and that a combination of direct behavioural observation and caregiver report is recommended instead - then frames robot-based screening as 'a new trend'. Its own contribution is explicitly the automation of a previously manual feature-extraction step in an existing robot protocol, illustrating the corpus-wide progression from manually coded behavioural observation to automated sensing of the same behaviour.

answers.title: Applying Eye Tracking to Identify Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children
answers.answer: 2018 (published online August 2018, in the 2019 volume). The paper documents the field's trajectory in some detail: eye tracking as 'one emerging objective tool increasingly being applied in ASD clinics and research', machine learning recently applied to behaviour, brain activity and eye tracking with 'encouraging results', and ASD biomarker research having 'grown exponentially' with integration into future risk assessment 'almost certain'. It also situates itself against three specific predecessors (Shic et al. on infants, Liu et al. on face-scanning machine learning, Fujioka et al. on adults), comparing accuracies directly - one of the more explicitly cumulative papers in the corpus.

answers.title: Automatic Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection Using Everyday
answers.answer: 2018. The paper characterises prior speech-based autism work as demonstrating that vocalisations contain usable biomarkers across infants, young children and teenagers, but criticises it on two specific grounds: recordings are 'mostly based on audio data obtained in very controlled environments' and are 'often manually reviewed, segmented, and processed by speech experts', which limits both practicality and recording length. It positions the emergence of affordable child-specific smart devices (Amazon Echo Kids Edition at $79, Xiaomi Kids Smartwatch at $45) as the enabling shift - documenting the corpus-wide movement from laboratory instrumentation toward consumer hardware and naturalistic settings, and framing it explicitly as a global health-equity argument.

answers.title: Detecting Autism Based on Eye-Tracking Data from Web Searching
answers.answer: 2018. The paper surveys autism classification from fMRI (71-86.7% across several studies) and EEG (94%), and argues that eye tracking 'has not been used to investigate whether it is suitable to detect autism by considering atypical visual attention patterns', claiming to be the first study to test gaze data for autism screening. It also documents an important methodological trend critically rather than approvingly - noting that several high-accuracy results in the literature rest on partitioning by data segment rather than by participant - and situates eye tracking as moving from research equipment into consumer hardware (Samsung Galaxy S4, Tobii gaming trackers, Acer notebooks), anticipating the consumer-device turn this corpus records.

answers.title: Video Gesture Analysis for Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
answers.answer: 2018. The paper surveys machine learning applied to autism across quotient-based diagnostic tools, MRI, kinematic data, eye tracking and language acoustics, and argues that these modalities are 'quite invasive or require specialized personnel, often affecting the behavior of the subjects under study', and that most rely on 'handcrafted features and simplified linear models that often fail to handle the complexity of human behaviors in less controlled settings'. It positions itself as the first to cast autism diagnosis as a video-based computational problem and as part of the shift toward deep learning - a shift this corpus documents accelerating sharply from 2018 onward.

answers.title: A Novel Eye Movement Data Transformation Technique that Preserves Temporal Information: A Demonstration in a Face Processing Task
answers.answer: 2019. The paper's field characterisation is methodological rather than clinical: it observes that 'most related studies rely on spatial information about which different areas of visual stimuli were looked at, without considering the order in which this occurred', and that 'even state-of-the-art analyses of this type are typically based on spatial but not temporal eye movement information'. It also criticises the prevailing stimulus convention - that existing studies 'typically use facial images with cropped peripheral regions... and such that the locations of the key facial regions are the same across images', which 'facilitates the analysis but can be seen as somewhat unrealistic'. Both observations identify structural simplifications in the gaze literature that this corpus otherwise leaves unexamined.

answers.title: Applying Machine Learning to Identify Autism With Restricted Kinematic Features
answers.answer: 2019. The paper characterises machine learning in autism as having concentrated on two things: shortening existing diagnostic instruments by removing redundant ADOS and ADI-R items (citing a claimed 100% accuracy from an 8-item ADOS subset, later above 95% on a larger sample), and classifying from neuroimaging, eye gaze and kinematic data - with only 'a handful' of kinematic studies, none of which targeted restricted and repetitive behaviour. Its closing argument that integrating genetic, neurological, psychological and kinematic features 'might pose a considerable challenge to the current diagnostic criteria of ASD' is one of the corpus's more ambitious claims about where the field is heading.

answers.title: Automatic Detection of Autism Spectrum Disorder in Children Using Acoustic and Text Features from Brief Natural Conversations
answers.answer: 2019. The paper characterises the speech-and-autism literature as drawing overwhelmingly on either highly structured elicitation (reading sentences or word lists) or semi-structured clinical interviews with an autism expert, chiefly ADOS evaluations, and argues these 'produce results that may not generalize to the everyday conversations that impact the lives of children on the autism spectrum'. It cites specific prior accuracies for calibration - roughly 74% from pitch features on 146 children, roughly 69% from speech rate and rhythm on 69 children - and identifies interlocutor speech features as an emerging and underused signal, noting prior findings that psychologists' speech predicted children's symptom severity better than the children's own features. This move from clinical-elicitation corpora toward naturalistic interaction is one of the clearest trend statements in the corpus.

answers.title: Classifying Individuals with ASD Through Facial Emotion Recognition and Eye-Tracking
answers.answer: 2019. The paper surveys the eye-tracking-plus-machine-learning literature specifically, citing SVM classification of children from face-recognition scanpaths, deep-learning extraction of fixated-region features achieving 92% in adults, and gaze-plus-demographics classification across ASD risk levels. Its critical observation is that 'these studies only considered the eye-tracking data, mainly what was looked at, without jointly taking into account the task performance', which it attributes to behavioural tasks being 'general but not specific enough' - identifying the integration of task performance with gaze as the field's next step. It also cites a systematic review noting that eye-tracking results have varied across studies and are sensitive to sample size, age, developmental level, IQ and stimulus variation.

answers.title: Detecting Developmental Delay and Autism Through Machine
answers.answer: 2019. The paper documents the field's cross-cultural blind spot directly: empirically validated tools like ADOS and ADI-R 'are not always used in different countries, particularly in developing countries, as these tools are expensive, require trained clinicians to administer, and may be limited by available translations and cultural adaptations', and it notes that global autism prevalence is 'largely unknown' with estimates of 0.15-0.8% in Bangladesh and around 3% in Dhaka, most cases in semiurban and rural areas going unnoticed.
